0c6f934e-a89f-5201-8884-4f5cd43e4cba.name: Turkish weights
0c6f934e-a89f-5201-8884-4f5cd43e4cba.description2: After Wallachia and Moldavia entered under Ottoman sovereignty and the Ottoman Empire became their main commercial partner, a series of Ottoman measures of mass and weight were adopted, such as the “oka” (1.282 kg) or the “kantar” (56.449 kg). When in 1864 the Romanian Ministry of Agriculture decreed the introduction in the United Principalities of the metric system, all the measures used in the past were abolished.

0ccfaeef-b75e-522c-ba46-eb30b18d6040.name: Pertevniyal Valide Sultan Mosque Complex
0ccfaeef-b75e-522c-ba46-eb30b18d6040.keywords: Women patrons; religious architecture; Orientalism; Gothic; mosque
0ccfaeef-b75e-522c-ba46-eb30b18d6040.description2: The complex was built by Pertevniyal Valide Sultan, wife of Sultan Mahmud II and mother of Sultan Abdülaziz, who was known for her charitable works. It comprises a mosque, a mausoleum, a *sabil* (water dispensary), a fountain, a clock-room and a school. The mosque reflects the characteristics of its period. The square prayer hall covered with a dome is extended with a wide arch to four sides. Mainly Oriental in style, the mosque is lavishly decorated. It was built with an eclectic taste bringing together elements from Gothic, Ottoman, Islamic and Indian arts.

0cd36a65-5e7b-5bb2-8525-edcaea12dea2.name: Omar al-Mukhtar (1861–1931), leader of anticolonial resistance in Libya
0cd36a65-5e7b-5bb2-8525-edcaea12dea2.author: Giulia Barrera
0cd36a65-5e7b-5bb2-8525-edcaea12dea2.description2:
In 1923, the head of the Senussi Muslim order Mohamed Idris charged Omar al-Mukhtār (1861-1931) with the task of leading Libyan anti-colonial resistance. Omar al-Mukhtār was leader of the Libyan anti-Italian guerrillas, until he was captured and executed by the Italians in 1931.  
In 1911-12, Italy successfully waged war against Turkey for the colonial conquest of Libya. However, during WWI Italy lost control of most of the Libyan territory. After the war, it took Italy about ten years to re-establish its hold on Libyan inland areas.  
Thanks to his military genius, to the wide popular support he enjoyed and the financial help provided by the Senussia, Omar al-Mukhtār was able to keep the Italians in check for years, even when the army of the invaders was ten times larger than the guerrilla forces. The Italians were able to capture him only after deporting part of the population of the Cyrenaica mountains (Gebel Akhda) in concentration camps on the coast.

en: Del Boca, Angelo, *Gli italiani in Libia*, Milan: Mondadori, 1993.

0cdaaac9-facc-525a-b1f1-756e4b6df842.name: Silvio Benigno Crespi and his family in the courtyard of Villa Pia (Villa Crespi), Orta San Giulio (Novara)
0cdaaac9-facc-525a-b1f1-756e4b6df842.author: Ignazio Galella
0cdaaac9-facc-525a-b1f1-756e4b6df842.description2:
Silvio Benigno Crespi was one of the children of Cristoforo Benigno Crespi, the industrialist who built a Moorish-style villa (known as villa Pia or villa Crespi) built on the lake d’Orta.  
This picture was taken in the courtyard of Villa Crespi. It shows Silvio Benigno Crespi (standing, on the right); sitting on the extreme left is his wife Teresa Ghiglieri; at the centre their first-born child Benigno and their other six children.  
The picture gives a hint of the lifestyle of this stock of cultivated, enlightened and successful industrialists.

0d4f3f4b-f17c-5cc6-86eb-8f3f56c416b7.name: Madrasa al-Bachiya
0d4f3f4b-f17c-5cc6-86eb-8f3f56c416b7.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
0d4f3f4b-f17c-5cc6-86eb-8f3f56c416b7.history: The *madrasa* was the accommodation building for the students of the Zaytuna University. The students lived in rooms resembling monastic cells around an open-air courtyard surrounded by covered porticos, and were able to both study and pray here.
0d4f3f4b-f17c-5cc6-86eb-8f3f56c416b7.description2: Located in the Suq des Libraires, this *madrasa* was built by 'Ali Pacha, the nephew Hussein ben 'Ali. It was built in the mid-18th century in the standard style of the time, distinguished only by its rich plaster décor and ceramic tiles, a *tourba* (funerary vault) for the builder and his family attached to the building, and a *sabil* (water fountain) for public use. Today, the *madrasa* has become a training centre for a crafts and apprenticeship college.

0db9b6f4-876c-52ec-9ce4-b7a1827400e3.name: Coat (*Attila*) for a commander of the Macedonian reform-gendarmerie
0db9b6f4-876c-52ec-9ce4-b7a1827400e3.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
0db9b6f4-876c-52ec-9ce4-b7a1827400e3.keywords: Macedonia; war; warfare; military object; military wear; Ottoman army
0db9b6f4-876c-52ec-9ce4-b7a1827400e3.description2: According to the agreements at Mürzsteg in 1903 between Austrian Emperor Francis Joseph I and the Tsar of Russian, the international community was sending police officers into the region of Macedonia in order to support and modernize the Macedonian police force. These officers submitted to the orders of the Sultan as the supreme commander of the Imperial Ottoman Army. Against the will of Russia, all international police officers wore a uniform in the Ottoman style: an *attila* like the one seen here. The official headwear was supposed to be the typical local fez, but officers from Austria, Russia and France adopted instead a *Kalpak* made of fur.

0dc23a30-fb0c-549b-b031-54f5fa9e9a23.name: The dormitory
0dc23a30-fb0c-549b-b031-54f5fa9e9a23.author: Hala Masri
0dc23a30-fb0c-549b-b031-54f5fa9e9a23.description2: Pictured here is the dormitory of 'Ayntura school, a large rectangular room with a high ceiling, supported by tall, thin columns. The room has several windows and is furnished with identical wooden beds.

0dc391d9-1f9b-5c22-91bf-a9670c98fa1b.name: Two Egyptian mummies
0dc391d9-1f9b-5c22-91bf-a9670c98fa1b.dates: Undated; 1906 (included in the National Museum of Antiquities collection)
0dc391d9-1f9b-5c22-91bf-a9670c98fa1b.description2: The National Museum of Antiquities was founded in Wallachia in 1834. According to a museum catalogue from 1906, a section of one exhibition room was dedicated to “Egyptian religious objects” (more than 120 items, among which small statues of various gods and goddesses, amulets, clay or bronze scarabs, cameos, a mummified hand). The museum also owned three mummies, exhibited in the “Trophy Room”, along with very varied objects of different epochs. Two of the mummies, belonging to a little boy and girl, were donated by a certain captain Horovitz (no information about him is known), who brought them from Cairo. He also offered the museum a mummified ibis and four mummified parrots.

0dd30a0a-1b26-5aa8-95ed-2abdad17a184.name: *Tercüman-ı Ahval* Newspaper
0dd30a0a-1b26-5aa8-95ed-2abdad17a184.description2: *Tercüman-ı Ahvâl* was the first private newspaper published in Istanbul. It was produced between 1860-1866 by Agah Efendi and Şinasi, men of letters of Tanzimat Era. Initially it was published only on Sundays, but starting from the 25th issue in 1861, it was published three times a week. Leading authors of the period such as Ahmed Vefik Paşa, Ziya Paşa and Refik Bey frequently wrote for it, discussing the reasons for the backwardness of Ottoman society and current events. In the paper, works of literature were also published. For instance the first Turkish theatre play, *Wedding/Marriage* of the Poet, by Şinasi (1860) was published as a series. The paper was closed for two weeks in 1861 after a very critical article probably written by Ziya Paşa. This is regarded as the first example of a ban in Turkish press. The paper was no longer published after 11 March 1866.

0dda7d39-b57f-5849-bcea-6897a0d0d4be.name: Amulet
0dda7d39-b57f-5849-bcea-6897a0d0d4be.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
0dda7d39-b57f-5849-bcea-6897a0d0d4be.description2: Throughout the 19th century in Macedonia, jewellery was not used only for adornment; it also served an apotropaic function. People used to wear various kinds of reliquaries for the purpose of personal protection from evil spirits. These protective items used to be worn in pockets or sewn to the garment. This amulet is made of silver using the techniques of hammering and engraving. The rectangular plate depicts the Virgin and Child flanked by two angels above them. The rings on the sides show that the amulet must have been worn suspended on a chain.

0df04b1e-0995-5f3a-a767-e848e62c8fbf.name: *The Bridge Carol I*
0df04b1e-0995-5f3a-a767-e848e62c8fbf.description2: The railroad bridge over the Danube that was built between 1890–1895 in South-Eastern Romania shortened the route of the Orient Express, a passenger train meant to connect Paris to Istanbul. The bridge made it possible for the Orient Express to reach Constanţa, a Black Sea port, from where ships went to Istanbul, whereas in the past the journey implied people being ferried on the Danube from Romania to Bulgaria, travelling by train to Varna (a Bulgarian Black Sea port) and then taking a ship to Istanbul. The “Carol I” bridge, which was designed by engineer Anghel Saligny and was at that time the longest in Europe, was inaugurated on 29 September 1895. In his inaugural speech, the king declared that “Romania is now owner of the shortest route between the northern seas and the countries of the Orient”.

0e467a26-3229-554d-8707-115f086aa0be.name: Portrait of Claudius Rich
0e467a26-3229-554d-8707-115f086aa0be.keywords: Bible; travelling; archaeology; archaeological excavation; exploration; collecting; collector; museums
0e467a26-3229-554d-8707-115f086aa0be.description2: Rich was the East India Company’s first Resident in Baghdad. He was a talented linguist. In his spare time he explored ancient sites, producing the first proper plans of Babylon and Nineveh. He hosted important travellers to Iraq, searching for sites of Biblical relevance. In 1821 he died during a cholera outbreak in Shiraz. His collection formed the nucleus of the British Museum’s collection.

0e6a50b3-2b5c-5608-aae5-77ecf66cfde2.name: *Sketch of Algeria, featuring the Roman occupation, the railway lines, roads suitable for mule and horse drawn vehicles, ports* \[…\] drawn from an archaeological point of view and dedicated to ...
0e6a50b3-2b5c-5608-aae5-77ecf66cfde2.second_name: Taken from *Revue Africaine: Journal des Travaux de la Société Historique Algérienne 78*
0e6a50b3-2b5c-5608-aae5-77ecf66cfde2.description2: Founded in 1856, the Société Historique Algérienne organised excavations, published a journal, and created maps and plans. This map helped facilitate research on the Roman occupation of Algeria, by indicating clearly the main sites, how to get there, and other elements which allow the reader to better understand the Roman presence (such as marble quarries and thermal baths).

0e7a0149-6b93-507e-b4df-dc55cdc5bd9f.name: Iron coffee roasting spoon
0e7a0149-6b93-507e-b4df-dc55cdc5bd9f.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
0e7a0149-6b93-507e-b4df-dc55cdc5bd9f.author: Huda Kilani
0e7a0149-6b93-507e-b4df-dc55cdc5bd9f.keywords: coffee; coffee roasting; coffee beans; domestic furnishing; domestic vessels
0e7a0149-6b93-507e-b4df-dc55cdc5bd9f.description2: Iron coffee roasting spoon used to turn coffee beans while roasting them. Coffee-drinking in a communal setting is an essential part of traditions in Bedouin communities to celebrate or mourn.

0e9e0841-ee1f-5aa8-8944-2225bf18b5d7.name: Coffee pot
0e9e0841-ee1f-5aa8-8944-2225bf18b5d7.holder: Sharjah Heritage Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
0e9e0841-ee1f-5aa8-8944-2225bf18b5d7.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
0e9e0841-ee1f-5aa8-8944-2225bf18b5d7.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
0e9e0841-ee1f-5aa8-8944-2225bf18b5d7.description2: This copper dallah goes back to a type allegedly first used in 17th-century Baghdad, By the 19th century, we know of several production centres in the Arabian peninsula. Its design reflects its functional needs. The broad base ensures stability on the fire or on the sand, the large beak prevents too much coffee sediment to reach the cup. The lid is weighted to avoid it opening during the pouring process.The quality and quantity of the coffee served indicated the wealth of the host and status of the guest. Throughout the Near and Middle East coffee lay at the heart of social ritual and hospitality, while providing sustenance during chats, debate and political discourse in the many coffeehouses in the region. In continental Europe, the fashion for coffee was at its height in the 17th and 18th centuries, with coffeehouses the preferred meeting places for intellectuals and artists. In Britain, meanwhile, tea soon overtook coffee in popularity, even though certain religious organisations tried to promote coffee houses for the poor in order to steer them away from pubs and bars.

0eb45a82-3f02-52db-8222-86625075ccdf.name: Bridal coat (*Klashenik*)
0eb45a82-3f02-52db-8222-86625075ccdf.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
0eb45a82-3f02-52db-8222-86625075ccdf.keywords: klashenik; broad cloth; textile; embroidery; geometric patterns; geometric motifs; costume; wedding; marriage
0eb45a82-3f02-52db-8222-86625075ccdf.materials: Thick woollen fabric, twill-weave, embroidery with *srma* and decoration with wool braids
0eb45a82-3f02-52db-8222-86625075ccdf.description2: A *klashenik* is a kind of over-garment women used to wear in winter. It is split in the front and made of thick woollen broadcloth called *klashna*. This piece is long to the hips. It is adorned with red braids along the hems. It is also decorated with embroidery of geometric patterns on the sleeves and at the breasts. Every ethnic area in Macedonia had distinct style of traditional costume, yet all of them show undeniable influence of Oriental art.

0ee9442b-fe87-5668-a98a-944398b82de9.name: *Egypt. Suez canal.*
0ee9442b-fe87-5668-a98a-944398b82de9.keywords: Suez canal; Egypt; Ferdinand de Lesseps
0ee9442b-fe87-5668-a98a-944398b82de9.second_name: Taken from the collection *Lithiographies Représentant L'isthme de Suez*
0ee9442b-fe87-5668-a98a-944398b82de9.description2: The inauguration of the Suez Canal saw spectacular celebrations, attended by many European royalties. This was a huge victory for Ferdinand de Lesseps, who had sincerely hoped it would be a memorable and historical event. On his request, the painter Édouard Riou (1833–1900) produced a series of watercolours which were later published in *L’Album de l’Impératrice : Voyage Pittoresque à travers l’Isthme de Suez*.

0ef1fad2-ddb0-571e-aa44-e858e5b159ac.name: *Die stadt Algier*
0ef1fad2-ddb0-571e-aa44-e858e5b159ac.author: Dalila Orfali
0ef1fad2-ddb0-571e-aa44-e858e5b159ac.description2: According to the historiographer Gabriel Esquer, this illustration was the most detailed view of Algiers available in the 17th century. The artist has accurately mapped out the streets and houses of the city.

0f088fa7-47b1-5825-9ada-f45bc3097162.name: The Italian Politeama Rossini theatre in Tunis, inaugurated in 1903
0f088fa7-47b1-5825-9ada-f45bc3097162.author: Giulia Barrera
0f088fa7-47b1-5825-9ada-f45bc3097162.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 67
0f088fa7-47b1-5825-9ada-f45bc3097162.description2:
The Politeama Rossini was built by the construction company of Giuseppe Di Vittorio (a Sicilian who had migrated to Tunisia in 1882); the architect was a Mr. Baron. It could house an audience of 2,500.  
The first Italian theatre in Tunis was the “Teatro Tapia” founded in 1826. Other Italian theatres (such as the “Teatro Italiano” and the “Teatro Paradiso”) and concert halls (“Gran Teatro”, “Teatro Cohen”, etc.) were created in Tunis the following decades.

0f0a80ba-ac59-5cc2-9963-b390e49608d0.name: *Kitchen of the Algerian Coffee Shop, at the Trocadero* \[Paris Exhibition 1878\]
0f0a80ba-ac59-5cc2-9963-b390e49608d0.author: Marina Minozzi
0f0a80ba-ac59-5cc2-9963-b390e49608d0.archival: *L'Esposizione di Parigi del 1878 illustrata*, Sonzogno Editore, 1878, p. 108
0f0a80ba-ac59-5cc2-9963-b390e49608d0.keywords: Exposition universelle de Paris; industrialisation; exhibition building; Moorish city; exhibitions and urban spaces; Moorish style; Islamic architecture; reinterpretation; exoticism; reproduction; model; magazine
0f0a80ba-ac59-5cc2-9963-b390e49608d0.copyright: Copyright image: Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale, Roma.
0f0a80ba-ac59-5cc2-9963-b390e49608d0.third_name: *La cucina del Caffè Algerino, al Trocadero*
0f0a80ba-ac59-5cc2-9963-b390e49608d0.description2: Within the International Exhibition in Paris, 1878, commercial activities typical of the colony were performed in the park next to Trocadero Pavilion. The scene shows the practice of making unfiltered coffee inside a kitchen decorated with *majolicas*, part of the reconstruction of a hypothetical neighbourhood in Algeria.

0f212b46-5c94-5a3d-875d-f50778a5c111.name: Request to the Bey of Tunis by Tunisian merchants in Istanbul
0f212b46-5c94-5a3d-875d-f50778a5c111.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
0f212b46-5c94-5a3d-875d-f50778a5c111.description2: This petition from the Jerbian merchants in Istanbul to the Bey of Tunis protests the behaviour of a Tunisian Jewish merchant.

0f2af30a-b903-5cfa-a52e-5a834629196d.name: *Sbeïtla. Attempt to reconstruct the façade of the three temples*
0f2af30a-b903-5cfa-a52e-5a834629196d.second_name: Description of the antiquities of the Tunisian regency: monuments from before the Arab conquest. Report on the 1882–83 mission.
0f2af30a-b903-5cfa-a52e-5a834629196d.description2: The French architect and winner of the Grand Prix de Rome, Henri Saladin, went on an archaeological campaign to Tunisia with the archaeologist René Cagnat between 1882 and 1883. He took many sketches in various archaeological sites, such as this drawing of Sbeïtla (the ancient Roman city in Sufetula). Upon his return he constructed a "Tunisian pavilion" for the 1889 Exposition Universelle (world fair) in Paris, which contained a mix of all the different architectural styles he had seen during his time in Tunisia.

0f8914a6-32b8-5c6c-8562-d748aa45552b.name: *Fountain of Sultan Ahmed III*
0f8914a6-32b8-5c6c-8562-d748aa45552b.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
0f8914a6-32b8-5c6c-8562-d748aa45552b.description2: Although essentially a realist painter, Şevket Dağ worked with free brush stokes in the style of Corot. He is celebrated for his paintings of the interiors of mosques. He took lessons from Osman Hamdi Bey, and followed his master in painting genre pictures reflecting various aspects of Ottoman life. In addition to mosque interiors he would also paint scenes in market places, still-life compositions and the interiors of houses. Over time, Şevket Dağ's work began to be appreciated abroad following exhibitions in European art centres such as Munich and Paris, and he was awarded a gold medal in the Munich International Exhibition of 1909. He later came under the influence of the impressionists.

0fa95d00-46ca-5bec-8348-9b86a0617d78.name: Ten Ottoman piasters
0fa95d00-46ca-5bec-8348-9b86a0617d78.author: Aida Naghawi
0fa95d00-46ca-5bec-8348-9b86a0617d78.description2: On obverse *tuğra* of sultan Abdul Hamid II, flower to right, denomination below: ١٠ ش “10 sh”, all within wreath with crossed quivers and unstrung bow at bottom, above seven stars, “W” below wreath tie. On reverse: within a wreath: “*duriba fi misr* 1293 22” (“22, struck in Misr, 1293”). Above 3 stars. It was issued in the year 22 (AH 1317 / AD 1896) of sultan Abdul Hamid II’s reign (Hegira 1293–1327 / AD 1876–1909).

0fb21836-e5e1-51dd-ab52-da180f9f90b6.name: Oud
0fb21836-e5e1-51dd-ab52-da180f9f90b6.holder: Lebanese National Higher Conservatory of Music
0fb21836-e5e1-51dd-ab52-da180f9f90b6.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
0fb21836-e5e1-51dd-ab52-da180f9f90b6.description2: The oud is the Arabic word for a lute, a pear-shaped instrument with a short fretted kneck and six sets of double strings. It is played with a plectrum, usually made of trimmed eagle feather, and has a deep, mellow sound. The word 'lute' in English comes from the Arabic "al-oud", via the Spanish word for the instrument, "laúd".

0fbf5343-64ee-545a-b2c8-56f70b18ca50.name: Samovar
0fbf5343-64ee-545a-b2c8-56f70b18ca50.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities
0fbf5343-64ee-545a-b2c8-56f70b18ca50.keywords: Russia; Eastern and Southern Europe; Middle East; metal container; tea drinking; domestic vessels
0fbf5343-64ee-545a-b2c8-56f70b18ca50.description2: Samovars are very common in Russia, Eastern Europe and in the Middle East. The samovar is a highly decorated metal container with a tap at the bottom and a pipe that runs vertically through it. By filling the pipe with coals, it will heat the water inside the container. A teapot kept on the top of the pipe will brew a strong concentration of tea that will be served after adding boiled water to it from the container. Samovars were brought to Jordan by various north Caucasian peoples, referred to as Circassians, who immigrated to the region during the last quarter of the 19th century.

0fca5a3a-17d8-542b-bada-abe14d89b5ed.name: Carved wooden chest
0fca5a3a-17d8-542b-bada-abe14d89b5ed.description: A carved wooden chest with painted geometric and floral decoration, it illustrates the decorative styles that began to appear in the 19th century and also how industrial colours, imported from Europe, were being used.
0fca5a3a-17d8-542b-bada-abe14d89b5ed.keywords: Craftsmanship; traditional craftsmanship; Moroccan craftsmen; woodwork; carving; trade; raw material; industrial colours; geometric decoration; floral decoration; geometric motifs; floral motifs; vegetal decoration; vegetal motifs; furniture

0fee6c38-84a6-5884-a476-0a33d319a555.name: Old Serail
0fee6c38-84a6-5884-a476-0a33d319a555.description: This Ottoman Serail was constructed in 1850, and is a mix of local and Ottoman architectural styles. The atrium contains an inner garden which is surrounded by arcades. Today, it serves as the city's town hall and is known as the 'Old Serail'.
0fee6c38-84a6-5884-a476-0a33d319a555.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
0fee6c38-84a6-5884-a476-0a33d319a555.history: The Serail was used as a prison in the past, which suffered of severe overcrowding. The prison was transferred to a larger site in 2009. Today, it functions as a town hall and houses the offices of the municipality, as well as a museum of the city's history.

1028751a-07f0-53c2-8d14-e1b298d6e008.name: Board
1028751a-07f0-53c2-8d14-e1b298d6e008.description: Qur'anic board used in the African *madrasas* (schools), places where the first verses of the Qur'an are learned, under the direction of the *marabout* (teacher). The learning method consists of copying and reciting the different verses of the Qur'an, in a process of memorisation, which allows the students to erase them and then to write the following verses. The *alluha* (table of wood), the reed, and the ink are the only available pedagogic materials of the Qur'anic schools in the rural areas. The Qur'anic boards turn into documents that preserve the written personality of those who used them, the irregularity of the letter, the crooked lines, the hesitations, the corrected mistakes, the erased lines that refuse to disappear, as a register of a period of effort and domain of skills typical of the school stage.

10420cae-bec5-5219-ac37-b2d0536040b3.name: Hindu Villa
10420cae-bec5-5219-ac37-b2d0536040b3.holder: Ministry of Antiquities; Ministry of Culture
10420cae-bec5-5219-ac37-b2d0536040b3.author: Ahmad al-Bindari
10420cae-bec5-5219-ac37-b2d0536040b3.history: Baron Empain had a passion for stylistic architecture from different parts of the world. The earlier buildings of Heliopolis were a melange of European and Arab architecture at a time when eclecticism was booming in Europe. His Hindu palace was and is still the crown jewel of the buildings of Heliopolis. The Baron Empain Palace was built using an innovative technique called the Hennebique system – named after the French engineer François Hennebique – wherein reinforced concrete was used for the first time. The varied external elements drawn by Marcel were cast in France via the Hennebique enterprise, then transported to Cairo and assembled on-site. The villa’s interior decorations were made by the French interior designer Georges-Louis Claude (1879–1963).
10420cae-bec5-5219-ac37-b2d0536040b3.keywords: Hindu Palace; Baron Empain Palace; Baron Palace; Cambodian Architecture in Cairo
10420cae-bec5-5219-ac37-b2d0536040b3.architects: Architect: Alexandre Marcel; interior designer: Georges-Louis Claude
10420cae-bec5-5219-ac37-b2d0536040b3.description2: The Hindu Villa of the Baron Empain (Edward Louis Joseph Empain, born on 20 September 1852 at Boleil-en-Hainaut, Belgium, died on 22 July 1929 at Waluwe-Saint-Pierre) is known today as the Baron Palace. The house was erected in 1906 following the plans of the French architect Alexandre Marcel (1860–1928), member at the Institut de France. The house reflects a mix of styles: Indian, Mongolian and Chinese, with some Islamic features. The eye-catching silhouette of the palace recalls the image of a Hindu temple. Marcel was already well-known for his exotic opera, in which he merged his masterpieces in a model titled “Panorama around the World: a Japanese Pagoda, Chinese Pavilion and an Indian Temple” that he made for the *Exposition Universelle* in Paris in 1900. This was Marcel’s inspiration for Empain’s residence.

104473a3-fc89-55f7-a3b9-20138dba554c.name: Plan of the city of Pompeii and the excavations there, pl. 2. Historical note
104473a3-fc89-55f7-a3b9-20138dba554c.second_name: Taken from *Dessins des Ruines de Pompéi*
104473a3-fc89-55f7-a3b9-20138dba554c.description2: The architect François Mazois (1783–1826) was appointed as Caroline Murat's official artist in 1809. He was allowed to set up in Pompeii to draw and measure the ruins, something unheard of at this time. His drawings and observations, published under the title *Les Ruines de Pompéi, Dessinées et Mesurées pendant les Années 1809 à 1811*, became a model for contemporary archaeologists and a source of inspiration for neo-Classical architecture.

1057c04c-dcfd-5f86-aac4-e464ef4ed226.name: Diploma awarded to the Vista Alegre factory
1057c04c-dcfd-5f86-aac4-e464ef4ed226.keywords: International Exhibitions; Portugal; Vista Alegre; Factory
1057c04c-dcfd-5f86-aac4-e464ef4ed226.description2: The participation in commercial exhibitions by the Vista Alegre Factory began in 1838, with the presentation of a glass and crystal collection in the Exhibition promoted by the Portuguese Industrial Society. In 1851 Vista Alegre took part in the Universal Exhibition, organized in London, and again in 1867 in Paris, having won the copper medal. In 1873 the factory received the Medal for Merit in the International Exhibition of Vienna, Austria. Universal Exhibitions represent in the 19th century an excellent medium for commercial and artistic exchanges, as well as a public stage for the competition between. This display arenas, with an international vocation, commercial exhibitions were ideal for the promotion of technical and artistic skills of European industries.

en: Arez, Ilda, *et al.*, *Vista Alegre Porcelanas*, Lisbon: Inapa, 1989.

109c897b-cb5d-5bc6-9360-7b2423876f34.name: Romanian coin – 10 bani 1867
109c897b-cb5d-5bc6-9360-7b2423876f34.description2: In October 1866, when the sultan recognized the reign of Carol I of Hohenzollern, the Principalities were given the right to struck national coins, but on one condition, namely that a sign symbolizing the Ottoman Empire, the Principalities’ suzerain, had to appear on the coins. Despite this, when the Romanian Parliament adopted the Law for the establishment of a Romanian monetary system and for the making of national coins (April 1867), it was decided that the coins would bear no inscription referring to the sovereign power. The first coins issued based on this monetary law were commissioned that same year to two British Mints, Heaton Mint and Watt & Comp. They were made of copper and their design belonged to British engraver Leonard Charles Wyon.

109ed34a-507a-5652-bb30-736569eca0ac.name: Drum
109ed34a-507a-5652-bb30-736569eca0ac.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities
109ed34a-507a-5652-bb30-736569eca0ac.author: Huda Kilani
109ed34a-507a-5652-bb30-736569eca0ac.keywords: drum; animals skin; linen rope; wooden stick; Ramadan; to wake up
109ed34a-507a-5652-bb30-736569eca0ac.description2: Small round drum, pointed on the bottom, covered on the top with leather, and fastened with a linen rope. It was played with a wooden stick to create special sounds of music, and it was used during the Muslim holy month of Ramadan to wake up people to eat (*suhur*) before sunrise. Some people used to volunteer to go around before dawn to wake people up during Holy Ramadan, reflecting community spirit.

10a5b375-34b0-5c68-bd08-21bc738e5e36.name: Lisbon Botanical Garden
10a5b375-34b0-5c68-bd08-21bc738e5e36.type: Botanical Garden; National Monument (Decree nº18/2010, DR, nº250  28  December 2010)
10a5b375-34b0-5c68-bd08-21bc738e5e36.holder: National Museum of Natural History and Science (MUHNAC) / Museums of the University of Lisbon
10a5b375-34b0-5c68-bd08-21bc738e5e36.dates: Starting of plantation: 1873; opened to the public: 1878; belongs to the University of Lisbon since 1911
10a5b375-34b0-5c68-bd08-21bc738e5e36.author: Catarina Teixeira (MUHNAC-UL), David Felismino (MUHNAC-UL)
10a5b375-34b0-5c68-bd08-21bc738e5e36.history: Since its creation in 1837, the Polytechnic School is committed to use  the Botanical Garden to support teaching and research in Botany. This purpose was firstly achieved at the Royal Botanical Garden at Ajuda, whose scientific and administrative supervision passed to the Polytechnic School in 1839. The installation of the new garden begins in 1873, on the initiative of Conde de Ficalho (1837–1903), and it opens to the public in 1878. In the 20th century, a new Herbarium building was added (1942) and, in 1962, a new Greenhouse replacing the original one, degraded by use and by the bombings of 1927. Topographically the Botanic Garden consists of two distinct parts – a flat area, dedicated to systematic botany and a gentle slope with the collection of trees and shrubs (Arboretum).
10a5b375-34b0-5c68-bd08-21bc738e5e36.keywords: Botanical Garden; Collections; National Museum of Natural History and Science; Polytechnic School
10a5b375-34b0-5c68-bd08-21bc738e5e36.architects: Ordered by Manuel Melo Breyner, Conde de Ficalho (1837–1903). Author of the design and arrangement of the Order Beds: German botanist Goeze Edmund (1838–1929), Arboretum: French botanist Jules Daveau (1852–1929)
10a5b375-34b0-5c68-bd08-21bc738e5e36.second_name: Botanical Garden of the University of Lisbon
10a5b375-34b0-5c68-bd08-21bc738e5e36.description2: The Garden holds more than 1,500 specimens over 4 acres, highlighting a remarkable diversity of palms and a unique collection of Cycadaceae, with exemplars only surviving in some parts of the world. It is also rich in species from New Zealand, Australia, China, Japan and South America, demonstrating the peculiarities of different microclimates created by its topography. The Garden fulfils also national requirements, both by the universality of its collection, and by the quality and quantity of the associated collections (herbaria, wood collections, seed bank). Furthermore, it includes relevant edified heritage, designed by important Portuguese architects from the 19th and 20th centuries.

10c5da68-3de4-54d1-9e73-5196e05c7ae8.name: *Description de L'Egypte: Antiquités Planches*
10c5da68-3de4-54d1-9e73-5196e05c7ae8.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. The *Description de l'Égypte* was a series of publications, appearing first in 1809 and continuing until the final volume in 1829, which offered a comprehensive scientific description of ancient and modern Egypt as well as its natural history. It is the collaborative work of about 160 civilian scholars and scientists, known popularly as the savants, who accompanied Napoleon's expedition to Egypt in 1798 to 1801 as part of the French Revolutionary Wars, as well as about 2000 artists and technicians, including 400 engravers, who would later compile it into a full work.

10e20816-215a-59c8-b59d-b15f4c933e82.name: Mahmud II Sultan of Turkey (1784–1839)
10e20816-215a-59c8-b59d-b15f4c933e82.keywords: Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey; Egypt; Janissary; Konya; Ibrahim Pasha; Muhammad Ali; Greece
10e20816-215a-59c8-b59d-b15f4c933e82.description2:
Portrait of Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey (1784–1839). In 1826 Mahmud II initiated the development of a modern army. This led to the uprising of the Janissary, which was quelled by massacring the rebellious troops. Under Mahmud II's reign, in 1821 the Greeks started their fight for freedom which was granted to them in the Peace of Adrianople in 1829.  
After the destruction of the Janissary, the Ottoman Empire under Sultan Mahmud II had only 35,000 badly trained regular soldiers in 1827. Due to the weakness of the Ottoman Empire, Ibrahim Pasha, the son of Muhammad 'Ali (ruler of Egypt), invaded Syria. On 20 February 1832, the Egyptian Army defeated the Ottoman Army at the Battle of Konya. This forced Mahmud II to sign the Peace of Kütahya and to cede Syria and Kilikia to Egypt.

10eff4e6-77c9-5f30-9f3f-98be6f9c668a.name: Yıldız Palace Island Kiosk
10eff4e6-77c9-5f30-9f3f-98be6f9c668a.notice: This is an unedited Database entry and may contain errors and inconsistencies in spelling. We are working to raise the funds required to complete the editing; should you wish to contribute please visit our [Support page](https://www.museumwnf.org/atrium_support.php).
10eff4e6-77c9-5f30-9f3f-98be6f9c668a.history:
Yildiz Palace, which is the last architectural example of Turkish Ottoman palace, is located on the Yildiz hill in the district of Besiktas. Sultan Ahmed I was the first to build a pavilion, over this land registered at the time to the Private treasury of the Ottoman Sultan as a hunting place sultans beginning during the reign of Suleiman the Magnificent (1520-1566).  
The main construction in the palace started in the period of Sultan Abdulhamid II (1876-1909) and it was called Saray-i Humayun (Central palace). During this period the palace comprised of buildings for private use of the sultan as well as buildings, allocated for the officials, repair shops and carpentry like repairing shop, carpenter’s shop and the buildings of culture and art such as theatre, museum and library. The Palace begun to serve as a museum under the name of “Directorate of the Museum of Yildiz Palace since 1993.
10eff4e6-77c9-5f30-9f3f-98be6f9c668a.description2: It is a residence that was built by Sultan Abdulhamid II for resting in Hasbahche. It is known that the mansion had been fenced around with wires, turned into a small zoo and the sultan used to watch the animals from there. The architectural structure of the kiosk represents Art Nouveau style and the design belongs to architect Raimondo D’Aronco.

11048de0-74f3-54a9-a02b-fa1ad1add1c1.name: Moroccan coins
11048de0-74f3-54a9-a02b-fa1ad1add1c1.description: Coin struck in 1936 under Sultan Mulay Yusuf (reigned twice, first in 1927-53 and then again in 1955-61) at the Paris mint. For a century (1800-1900) the ‘Alawid sultans struck coins in the workshops of Fez, but due to the economic crisis at the time, gold was unavailable so most coins were of silver, bronze or other common metals – although the technique remained the same, with the metal poured into moulds. The patterns on the face and on the back vary between the star with eight points (Solomon ring) and the indication of the place of mint.

113d81d8-ec2d-5435-9b8d-e7c59e9ff9fb.name: The Ghetto of Florence
113d81d8-ec2d-5435-9b8d-e7c59e9ff9fb.author: Marina Minozzi
113d81d8-ec2d-5435-9b8d-e7c59e9ff9fb.keywords: Macchiaioli; Italian painters; painting; artistic exchanges; Corot; landscape; cityscape; realism; unification of Italy; social history; social topics; Italian society; post-unitarian Italian society; Italian Jews; city; urban space; segregation; ghetto
113d81d8-ec2d-5435-9b8d-e7c59e9ff9fb.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
113d81d8-ec2d-5435-9b8d-e7c59e9ff9fb.description2: Telemaco Signorini was part of the group of artists known as The Macchiaioli Movement, a group drawn to colour and nature. After his studies at the Academy of Florence, he started painting from real life and spent some time in Paris, where he met Corot and the painters from the School of Barbizon. Back in Italy the artist went to Tuscany and Liguria. He also travelled frequently to France, England and Scotland, where he was well known. Signorini liked painting urban scenes and cityscapes. The artist developed urban themes with a unique emphasis, matching together vivid descriptions, social and humanitarian features and cultural issues.

11568132-d5af-54cf-9a3f-f663abfb4f5b.name: Winter jacket
11568132-d5af-54cf-9a3f-f663abfb4f5b.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
11568132-d5af-54cf-9a3f-f663abfb4f5b.author: Huda Kilani
11568132-d5af-54cf-9a3f-f663abfb4f5b.materials: Wool, cotton and silk; hand weaving and hand embroidered
11568132-d5af-54cf-9a3f-f663abfb4f5b.description2: Sleeveless jacket made of woollen fabric of red and black stripes, decorated with floral motifs of orange and purple colour with couching in silk threads on the shoulders and the bottom. This object illustrates the variegated population composition of the Jordanian territory in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, influenced by the local economy. The main activities were trade and crafts that influenced population movements and the coexistence of various local and foreign communities.

1182b4e7-198f-51a0-b819-4ec5360c27f8.name: Casket
1182b4e7-198f-51a0-b819-4ec5360c27f8.description: This casket was displayed in the exhibition about Islamic Art held in Munich in 1910. Afterwards it was acquired by Lázaro Galdiano, one of the most important Spanish art collectors. It is important to note Lazaro Galdiano's interest in and art appraisal of objects from the Spanish Muslim period. He was one of the earliest collectors of Arab art in Spain.
1182b4e7-198f-51a0-b819-4ec5360c27f8.dates: 1100–1199; exhibited in 1910 and then acquired by Lázaro Galdiano
1182b4e7-198f-51a0-b819-4ec5360c27f8.author: Ámparo López

11882e61-41ff-533d-8ba1-acb37292e9e4.name: The Rosetta Stone
11882e61-41ff-533d-8ba1-acb37292e9e4.keywords: archaeology; Egyptomania; exploration; collection; collecting; museums; inscription; Greek inscription; hieroglyph; Demotic; science
11882e61-41ff-533d-8ba1-acb37292e9e4.description2: An iconic image of decipherment, since the same text is inscribed in three different scripts, including Greek, the ‘stone’ is actually part of a grey and pink granodiorite stela bearing a priestly decree concerning Ptolemy V in three blocks of text: Hieroglyphic (14 lines), Demotic (32 lines) and Greek (54 lines).

11e4d236-bdc2-5339-827e-8d983887fbd6.name: The private carriage of Queen Maria Pia
11e4d236-bdc2-5339-827e-8d983887fbd6.description2: Private carriage of Queen Maria Pia, offered by her father, King Victor Emmanuel, when she married the Portuguese king D. Louis in 1862. The chariot is pulled by steam locomotive D. Luiz.

11ee08c6-3f50-5b88-b216-58be546fc86a.name: *Antonis Benakis at the Sporting Club in Alexandria*
11ee08c6-3f50-5b88-b216-58be546fc86a.author: Maria Dimitriadou
11ee08c6-3f50-5b88-b216-58be546fc86a.description2: A black and white photos from a photo album showing snapshots of a polo game at Alexandria Sporting Club and naming Antoni Benakis as the leading rider. Phototographer unknown.

1223f05d-519a-50c0-8c79-8e8c02636ede.name: Chandelier
1223f05d-519a-50c0-8c79-8e8c02636ede.holder: Shangri La, Doris Duke Foundation for Islamic Art
1223f05d-519a-50c0-8c79-8e8c02636ede.keywords: glass; chandelier; France; Baccarat; India; Salar Jung; collector; collection
1223f05d-519a-50c0-8c79-8e8c02636ede.description2: During the nineteenth century, a vogue developed in western and southern Asia for European glass. Manufacturers such as Baccarat in France responded to these markets by producing glassware with motifs and aesthetics that they believed would appeal to these new consumers. This chandelier is thought to have been made for export to India. Indeed, Doris Duke purchased the chandelier in 1966 from the estate of Salar Jung, a noted collector in Hyderabad, India.

123030ca-d6ea-5a9d-b948-0601ad74e192.description: Glazed, blue, terracotta dish, dated 1894 and made in Fez.
123030ca-d6ea-5a9d-b948-0601ad74e192.keywords: Applied arts; craftsmanship; Moroccan craftsmanship; kitchen ware; domestic ware; terracotta; earthenware; bleau de Fez; glaze; floral decoration; floral motifs; vegetal decoration; vegetal motifs

124efc2d-1a23-56df-83e7-543dbb950692.name: Port of Beirut
124efc2d-1a23-56df-83e7-543dbb950692.description: The Port of Beirut is the main port in Lebanon and it is one of the most beneficial commercial architecture in Lebanon that contributes the state’s revenue. It was founded in 1887 under the reign of the Ottomans and has since been the western-eastern link in the Middle East area. The Port of Beirut has a total area of 1,200,000 m2.
124efc2d-1a23-56df-83e7-543dbb950692.holder: Government of Lebanon; Gestation and exploitation of Port of Beirut (GEPB)
124efc2d-1a23-56df-83e7-543dbb950692.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Rita El Hachem, Julien El Khoury
124efc2d-1a23-56df-83e7-543dbb950692.history: Founded in 1887, the Port of Beirut is located on the eastern side of St Georges Bay, on Beirut's northern Mediterranean coast, west of the Beirut river. It is one of the largest and busiest ports of the Eastern Mediterranean. In early 90’s, a phase of development and reconstruction took place. The Port was rehabilitated and expanded to encompass 4 docks, 2 new quays (15 and 16) and new container terminal with 700,000 TEU/year capacities. The container terminal became operational in February 2005. It is equipped with 6 ship-to-shore gantry cranes (outreach 60m) and 18 rubbed tyred gantry cranes. The Port of Beirut has been selected as a transhipment hub for the 2nd and 3rd largest container shipping companies in the world.

12ae0ba0-fa77-59bd-a23f-763b7a6f9512.name: Four anklets
12ae0ba0-fa77-59bd-a23f-763b7a6f9512.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
12ae0ba0-fa77-59bd-a23f-763b7a6f9512.description2: Ankle bracelets - or "anklets" - were common accessories in various regions of the ancient Middle East. They were first worn by ancient Egyptian women, and were made of materials such as brass, gold, silver, iron, glass, or ivory. The Hebrew word for "ankle chain" and "step chains" both come from the root *tsa'adh'*, meaning "to take steps; to march". The Hebrew word *e'khes*, meaning "bangle; anklet" comes from the root *akhas*, meaning "to make a tinkling sound" or "shaking bangles". Indeed, many anklets were adorned with small bells and heavier anklets would have made a loud tinkling or ringing noise as the wearer walked along. These bells were usually fashioned by placing a small pebble in hollowed silver spheres. It is possible that heavier anklets would have been designed to restrict the woman's step, thus forcing her to walk slowly in a style perceived as feminine, or to attract attention as she walked. The anklets pictured here are made of silver and are adorned with small dangling silver bells.

138b0748-bba7-544a-afa4-6e44661538d4.name: *View of Constantinople*
138b0748-bba7-544a-afa4-6e44661538d4.author: Papastratos 1990, vol. 2, 578-79, figs. 617-18; Delivorrias, Fotopoulos 1997, 508-9, figs. 900-901
138b0748-bba7-544a-afa4-6e44661538d4.description2: Both this print and the *View of Smyrna* are based on earlier Western ones, which have been assimilated into the distinctive Athonite topographical style. They are exceptions to the corpus of Athonite prints, since they are of secular subjects. The printmaker was, indeed, active outside Athos, where he executed nonreligious commissions. The subjects relate to the tradition of topographical murals depicting important commercial and cultural centers of the day that decorated the mansions of wealthy merchants by the mid-eighteenth century. Kaldis aimed to supply a wider public with inexpensive works of a decorative nature. The activity of merchants from Lesbos at Smyrna, Constantinople, and the Black Sea on the one hand justified the choice of subject and, on the other, provided the appropriate network in which the multiple printed works could circulate. In order to attract the largest possible clientele, the view is coloured and annotated with explanatory comments in Greek and Turkish.

en: Delivorrias, Angelos, and Fotopoulos, Dionisis, *Greece at the Benaki Museum*, Athens: Benaki Museum, 1997.

139d89ef-83f7-5902-8e15-21a9ae45cbf2.name: Early collecting
139d89ef-83f7-5902-8e15-21a9ae45cbf2.description2: A colossal statue of Cypriot Bes was found near the agora of the ancient city of Amathus in 1863. The British government attempted to obtain it for the British Museum but it was sent to Constantinople on order of the Porte. This illustrates the beginnings of a more official policy to claim antiquities for the Ottoman state and to exhibit them in museums. The first Ottoman Law on antiquities was passed in 1869, followed by a more detailed one in 1874.

14597b52-b897-5eac-9ab6-b73b6fabbf11.name: House
14597b52-b897-5eac-9ab6-b73b6fabbf11.dates: End of 19th – beginning of the 20th century
14597b52-b897-5eac-9ab6-b73b6fabbf11.author: Prof. Petar Namichev (PhD)
14597b52-b897-5eac-9ab6-b73b6fabbf11.history: The first mention of the Debar-Reka art school in the sources was in the 10th century. The centre of the art school was in the village of Galichnik. Activities of the Debar-Galichnik art centre throughout the centuries have given rise to the development of diverse crafts related to construction and architectural decoration, as well as icon-painting, woodcarving, sculpture, etc. The male population of the Reka area was traditionally widely known for their construction skills. These native architects used to work in groups called *tajfas*. *Tajfas* consisted of around ten men, including builders, wood-carving masters and stone cutters. The leader of the *tajfa*, i.e. the person that used to organize the construction activities, was called *ustabashiya*.
14597b52-b897-5eac-9ab6-b73b6fabbf11.description2: The existence of structures with similar architectonic features in the Reka Area, the territory of Metochia, Albania, Greece, Bulgaria and Bosnia confirms the common concept of expression in dwellings of "tower" type in the traditional architecture of the Balkans. This three-storey house of symmetrical layout is built of stone. It shows some features of tower-houses with its very small windows built extremely high at the ground floor and symmetrically positioned bigger windows on upper stories. The house is distinguished by the interesting entrance portion.

14763417-a183-5949-ac5d-11f296d400e1.name: Hanging (*sitara*) for the Mosque of the Prophet, Medina al-Munawwarah
14763417-a183-5949-ac5d-11f296d400e1.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Authority
14763417-a183-5949-ac5d-11f296d400e1.dates: Hegira mid 13th century / AD mid 19th century
14763417-a183-5949-ac5d-11f296d400e1.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
14763417-a183-5949-ac5d-11f296d400e1.materials: Silk, cotton, silver and gilt silver thread
14763417-a183-5949-ac5d-11f296d400e1.description2: This hanging of red, yellow-golden and green silk is richly embroidered with silver and silver-gilt inscriptions and designs. Above, a lamp with invocations to Allah as the Opener or Judge (ya Fattah) appears suspended from an arched niche resting on two columns. Its spandrels display two roundels with the Islamic profession of Faith (shahada). Below, a quote from chapter 2 (Al-Baqarah), verse 197 of the Holy Qur’an appears: ‘…and the best provision is Al-Taqwa (piety, righteousness)’. In the lower half of the hanging, four roundels with the names of the rightly-guided caliphs surround the imperial Ottoman emblem or tughra of the sultan Abd al- Hamid II  (1293 H/1876 AD – 1327 H/1909 AD), who commissioned this curtain.. Hangings like this one may have been intended for the prayer niche of the Prophet’s mosque, as earlier examples of this type often include the inscription ‘this is the mihrab of the Prophet (pbuh)’.

147b289f-3d6e-58be-8aa0-db105cfb150f.name: *National Museum of Archaeology No. 9 (Arab Courtyard) Monuments and Epigraphy of Islamic Spain*

This room displayed different pieces such as the Alfajería arch, a copy of the fountain of the Lions and the bronze lamp from the Alhambra palace. This room was one of the first museum galleries focusing on Arab or Islamic pieces in Europe.

1488ab73-2672-5641-a84a-174c9bfb4fd8.name: Perpetual calendar
1488ab73-2672-5641-a84a-174c9bfb4fd8.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
1488ab73-2672-5641-a84a-174c9bfb4fd8.dimensions: Height 130 mm, width 70 mm, depth 33 mm
1488ab73-2672-5641-a84a-174c9bfb4fd8.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
1488ab73-2672-5641-a84a-174c9bfb4fd8.materials: Nielloed silver, copper alloy, iron, wood, printed paper, printed textile
1488ab73-2672-5641-a84a-174c9bfb4fd8.description2: This perpetual calendar is contained within a cylindrical silver casing with a rounded shoulder. Four lateral knobs, two on either side, move the calendar's paper and textile elements, giving the month, the date and probably the day (this section is damaged). Above, a circular medallion contains the start year of the calendar, 1327 H/ 1909 AD.  The calendar is decorated all over with delicate niello deccoration. The front, with three superposed and elongated cartouche-shaped openings, is ornamented with a lobed panel containing naturalistic flower sprays. Below, a panel with three loop extensions contains an Arabic inscription - taqweem da'imi - that identifies the object's function. In the Tanzimat period, and up to 1926, the Mailya or Rumi calendar was introduced, which was based on the Julian solar calendar but started in the year of the Prophet's (pbuh) move from Makkah to Madina in 1 H/ 622 AD. It used old Syrian names for the months and was intended to ease the annual tax and fiscal calculations and payments.

14d25094-56e3-5812-add7-3c7c717c6829.name: Mijwiz
14d25094-56e3-5812-add7-3c7c717c6829.holder: Lebanese National Higher Conservatory of Music

14d25094-56e3-5812-add7-3c7c717c6829.description2: The *mijwiz*, meaning "double" in Arabic, is a common instrument in traditional Lebanese music. It is a type of reed clarinet, played by breathing slowly through a circular aperture at the end of the instrument, and covering the holes down the body of the instrument with your fingers in order to create different notes.

14fdce8b-d60e-5d32-ad42-c489568e4c66.name: Collective housing
14fdce8b-d60e-5d32-ad42-c489568e4c66.description: This type of collective housing, which was popular until the mid-19th century, generally consisted of houses built in sandstone or limestone *ramleh*, covered by a cray terrace and reinforced concrete slabs. The plan of the house is built around a central courtyard.
14fdce8b-d60e-5d32-ad42-c489568e4c66.author: Jeff El-Msanne, David Andos
14fdce8b-d60e-5d32-ad42-c489568e4c66.history: A *hawsh* is a style of collective housing built around a *harat* (an Arabic term which literally means "lane"). It consists of several main buildings built around a common courtyard, which were usually occupied by families or relatives of similar geographical origins. Unlike the *dar* (another type of house built around a central courtyard), there is no hierarchy in the distribution of the buildings around the courtyard. In the suburb of Medwwar-Rmeil, Beirut, Beirut, an area which in the 19th century relied mostly on the agricultural sector, the *hawsh* was typically leased to the newly installed peasant families.

159f7828-e467-5f3d-b3ba-96aafc6f5b7c.name: Postcard: *Colonial Exhibition 1907, Tuareg caravan*
159f7828-e467-5f3d-b3ba-96aafc6f5b7c.description:
This postcard (not franked or used) is part of a collection donated by the anthropologist Manuel Antón.  
During the second half of the nineteenth century in Europe and America there were held countless ethnological and colonial exhibitions that showed groups of individuals from distant exotic territories, to make them public and available to anthropologists and scholars. They were put on show alongside exotic animals and recreations of the structures inhabited by these people in their places of origin.  
These exhibitions were a result of the intensification of colonial imperialism of the West and also the relative popularity of two young scientific disciplines (physical anthropology and ethnology) and the development of new and intense forms of consumerism among the European bourgeoisie. Actually these exhibitions got to transmit a sense of lower and "savage" status of the colonised people (Sánchez Gómez, L. “Espectáculos demasiado humanos”, 2008, 88-89).

16145c6c-e484-5568-ab55-c93317ec5964.name: Carol I, King of Romania (1839–1914) / Karl von Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen
16145c6c-e484-5568-ab55-c93317ec5964.keywords: Carol I, King of Romania; Karl von Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen
16145c6c-e484-5568-ab55-c93317ec5964.description2: Portrait of Carol I, King of Romania (1839–1914) in uniform with Karl von Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen. He was elected Prince of Romania on the recommendation of Napoleon III in 1866. In 1881, after achieving formal independence from the Ottoman Empire, Carol declared himself King of Romania.

161d25a6-f2f3-5bd7-9bce-84afb082e31e.name: The Hijaz Railway Delegations
161d25a6-f2f3-5bd7-9bce-84afb082e31e.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
161d25a6-f2f3-5bd7-9bce-84afb082e31e.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
161d25a6-f2f3-5bd7-9bce-84afb082e31e.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph The Hijaz Railways
161d25a6-f2f3-5bd7-9bce-84afb082e31e.description2: The Hijaz Railway ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. The main purpose of the railway was to establish a connection between the capital of the Ottoman Empire and the seat of the Islamic Caliphate, and Hijaz in Arabia, the site of the holiest shrines of Islam and the holy city of Mecca, the destination of the Hajj annual pilgrimage. Another important reason was to improve the economic and political integration of the distant Arabian provinces into the Ottoman state, and to facilitate the transportation of military forces.

16c4b489-744b-54ba-b2f9-e9d429647ac5.author: Marina Minozzi
16c4b489-744b-54ba-b2f9-e9d429647ac5.keywords: Revivalism; Egyptomania; Egyptian motifs; applied arts; jewellery; exploration; archaeology; excavation; scientific expedition; Campaign in Egypt; Campaign in Syria; Enlightenment; science; technique; Egyptology; Orientalism; travel; botany; epigraphy
16c4b489-744b-54ba-b2f9-e9d429647ac5.description2: This bracelet, owned by Princess Paolina Bonaparte (1780–1825), wife of Camillo Borghese, was made by one of the most famous goldsmiths in Paris, Jean Baptiste Claude Odiot, as identified by the trademark on the safety lock of the bracelet. The elegant Egyptian decoration made by hieroglyphics and triangles alternating with little palms is inspired to the book *Voyage dans le Basse et Haute Égypte*, written by Dominique Vivant Denon (1745–1825) during Napoleon’s campaign along the Nile river in 1798 and published between 1802 and 1810. The ancient Egyptian fashion, popular in Italy since the second half of the 18th century, influenced furniture design and works of art following publication of Denon’s book, which popularized a “retour d’Egypte”.

en: Costamagna, A., *La raffinatezza e il lusso: lo "stile" Borghese dal cardinale Scipione ai principi Camillo e Paolina in quattro piccoli "tesori" artistici*, Rome: Galleria Borghese, 2005: 23–27.

16e62e70-a7b1-5c81-b4f3-e37bfa439cad.name: Letter by Kenny Leveck to Odeh Goussous
16e62e70-a7b1-5c81-b4f3-e37bfa439cad.description: A unique document signed by Kenny Leveck. The document is dispatched to the attorney general Mr. Odeh-Goussous informing him that the president of the high council of Kerak's national government appointed him attorney general on 21 September, 1920, asking him to take up his position seriously and actively. At the end of the letter is the signature “chief of high council, British resident, Major Kenny Leveck,” then a stamp of Kenny Leveck in Arabic. To the right is the translation of the signature in English, "F.M Kenny leveck, A political officer and president of council, Kerak." (The letter A means Acting.) Kenny Leveck was in Kerak for a couple of weeks, where he headed the new administration formed from the Elders of the Kerak Tribes known as “the National Government of Moab”. It is not true what Sir Alec Seath Kirkbirde mentioned in his book *A Crackle of Thorns*, page 21-22, that he was elected by the council of Kerak and became head of the High Council of Kerak, or as he says on page 22, he “became head of a more less independent republic”.

171d0c66-d91f-50c5-9daf-466b883aab37.second_name: Taken from "Sénégalais", an album of 41 anthropological photographs from the  Exposition Universelle in Paris, 1889
171d0c66-d91f-50c5-9daf-466b883aab37.description2: The villages inhabited by African and Asian immigrants attracted a great deal of attention during the time of the European world fairs. Even the sciences (medicine, anthropology, etc.) showed much curiosity towards them, a curiosity whose justification as 'scientific' seems incongruous and dishonest to a modern audience.

171ffd50-c8dd-51b6-8ca7-e79ffd9de227.name: *The tourist's travelling equipment*
171ffd50-c8dd-51b6-8ca7-e79ffd9de227.description2: The rise of tourism saw the production of clothes and items suitable for varying climactic conditions, physical activity, and even potential dangers. This poster foregrounds an image of a hiker in an alpine setting, framed by depictions of many other types of tourism, such as seaside resorts and other more adventurous activities.

174a686d-d71c-5900-ac66-c2dba02914eb.name: Jug
174a686d-d71c-5900-ac66-c2dba02914eb.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
174a686d-d71c-5900-ac66-c2dba02914eb.description2: It is known that there were workshops producing glass vessels around Beykoz in Istanbul in the 19th century. The first glass workshop was founded by Mevlevi Dervish Mehmed Dede during the reign of Selim III (1789–1807). There were European glass craftsmen working in those workshops as well. Cups, bottles, jugs etc. made of colourful, colourless and opal glass were among Beykoz's productions. *Çeşm-i bulbul* is the name of the technique used to make this glass jug. In this technique, the glass bars are immerged into transparent glass. On the body of the jug we see spirally placed opaque white, opaque purple and blue glass bars immerged into colourless ground. It is of pear-shaped with a short neck and a lid. The handle was attached later. The lid handle is in the shape of a *Mevlevi sikke* (Mevlevi Sufi headwear).

176c309e-be45-54b8-81a1-917857d46338.name: Textile
176c309e-be45-54b8-81a1-917857d46338.description: This textile was displayed in the exhibition about Islamic Art held in Munich in 1910, as part of the Miquel i Badia collection. Afterwards it was acquired by Lázaro Galdiano, one of the most important Spanish art collectors. It is important to note Lazaro Galdiano's interest in and art appraisal of objects from the Spanish Muslim period. He was one of the earliest collectors of Arab art in Spain. The decoration is similar to the Golden Room of the Alhambra palace and it could be the Mohammad V period.
176c309e-be45-54b8-81a1-917857d46338.author: Ámparo López
176c309e-be45-54b8-81a1-917857d46338.keywords: Nasrid art; islamic influence; orientalism; collectionism
176c309e-be45-54b8-81a1-917857d46338.materials: Silk and metallic threads; lampas weave

17887320-c89a-503d-8231-40a84fa14975.name: *Revolution of 1830 (29 July). Building barricades.*
17887320-c89a-503d-8231-40a84fa14975.second_name: Dedicated to the citizens of Paris
17887320-c89a-503d-8231-40a84fa14975.description2: The revolutions of the first half of the 19th century are strongly associated with barricades, usually a pile up of furniture and other objects across streets, aimed at slowing down army troops. There were almost 4,000 barricades in Paris during the revolution of 1830.

178d2db5-fbc1-5e5a-8ce8-245dc22c7cea.name: Arabian *bisht*
178d2db5-fbc1-5e5a-8ce8-245dc22c7cea.description2: Arabian *bisht* made from black cloth and gold thread.

17926a9d-a6e5-5215-b39f-488c46d6e51c.name: *Firman*
17926a9d-a6e5-5215-b39f-488c46d6e51c.keywords: archaeology; exploration; Egyptomania; collection; collector; travel; traveller; museums; historical document; imperial symbols; Ottoman monograms
17926a9d-a6e5-5215-b39f-488c46d6e51c.description2: The official permit, or *firman*, confirming the appointment of Henry Salt to the post of British Consul in Egypt, dated 23 December 1815. The imperial cipher at the top is flanked by floral motifs. This is a fine manuscript with exquisite Arabic calligraphy and watercolour and gold floral decorations. When Salt arrived in Egypt in 1816 he obtained permission from the Pasha, Mohammed Ali, to collect antiquities for the British Museum.

179af9eb-b888-57e9-b30c-78f45dee8021.name: *Weapons Market Street*
179af9eb-b888-57e9-b30c-78f45dee8021.keywords: Weapons Market; Cairo Markets; Old Cairo
179af9eb-b888-57e9-b30c-78f45dee8021.description2: A rare photo of the weapons market street that goes back more than 700 years and is located in the Darb al-Ahmar area, to the North of Cairo. It was originally called “Al-`Izzi Market”, after a relative to Prince `Izz al-Din Bahdar, one of the Bahri Mamluks who was said to live there. With the passing of time, people started calling it “Suq al-Silah" street because of its many workshops and factories that made a variety of different weapons, including spears, swords and shields. The street provided weapons to the Citadel during the Mamluk era in Egypt.

179f9d9d-6b5a-52fc-8dea-c159da198fd5.name: *La Reine de Saba: 14 costume sketches*
179f9d9d-6b5a-52fc-8dea-c159da198fd5.description2: Charles Gounod turned to the librettists Jules Barbier and Michel Carré for advice when he was writing his great opera, and so they recommended him the legend of Hiram, the great tale narrated by Gérard de Nervale in his *Voyage en Orient*. The opera was put on in Paris in 1862. As this costume from the court of Suleiman shows, the models and costumes responded above all to the Orientalist stereotypes in vogue at the time.

17a114d9-989f-52a9-85d5-689485ba21f6.name: Icon *The Holy Seven Slav Teachers*
17a114d9-989f-52a9-85d5-689485ba21f6.author: Viktorija Popovska Korobar, art historian
17a114d9-989f-52a9-85d5-689485ba21f6.description2: This icon represents icon-painting in Macedonia in the 19th century. This painted variant of the motif of the seven Slav teachers was enriched by Dimitar Dicho Zograf with the romantic awareness of the Macedonian Revival. The style of the most popular and most productive Macedonian painter in the 19th century follows the experience of the painters from that period. It was commissioned by the Robev family for the church of St. Nicholas Gerakomia in Ohrid. It was painted on wood with oil. It represents the Slav missionaries Ss. Cyril and Methodius and their most prominent disciples Clement, Nahum, Gorazd, Sabbas and Angelariy, in a sole composition entitled as “Sedmochislenitzi” (The Seven Holy Teachers). The saints' names are inscribed in the Old Church Slavonic language.

17a2df03-43c9-5803-92e9-9cff69d81432.name: Mosque lamp
17a2df03-43c9-5803-92e9-9cff69d81432.keywords: Orientalism; Mamluk Revival; trade; calligraphy; inscription; glass; furniture; decorative arts
17a2df03-43c9-5803-92e9-9cff69d81432.description2: ‘Mosque lamp’ reproducing well known examples from the Middle East. Produced by Philippe-Joseph Brocard, Faubourg Saint-Honoré. Brocard was inspired by his collection of Mamluk glass.

17b041f8-8464-54a0-bfab-c18e51639102.name: A rare photo showing important guests at the inauguration of Luxor–Aswan Railway Line
17b041f8-8464-54a0-bfab-c18e51639102.description2: A group of guests at the inauguration of the Luxor–Aswan Railway Line upon disembarking at the Station of Aswan. One of the rare photos for the inauguration of the Luxor–Aswan railway line, with `Adli Yakan Pasha; Muhammad Najib al-Gharabli Pasha; Husayn Rushdi Pasha; Tharwat Pasha; Fathallah Barakat Pasha; Morkos Hanna Pasha; al-Dagwi Bek, director of Aswan; and Mahmud Shakir Bek, deputy undersecretary of the Ministry of Transportation in attendance, in 1926.

17e0e95e-14d7-5aeb-b21f-b18091757a69.name: *Mr. Byzantoine et son ex-libris*, by the Greek cartonist Kem
17e0e95e-14d7-5aeb-b21f-b18091757a69.author: Mina Moraitou
17e0e95e-14d7-5aeb-b21f-b18091757a69.description2: Antonis Benakis in Byzantine dress holds his ex-libris and golf clubs, with his dog Mangas and his boat at his feet; on the right, the Russian painter I. Bilibin, below, K. Synadinos, and, top left, ceramics glued together, probably from sherds. Kem’s drawing is a satire on the artistic and athletic interests of Benaki, in the style of Bilibin’s illustrations to Russian legends, for example *The Tale of the Tzar Saltan* (1905).

17ebadf5-f8b4-5fec-89b1-0d6719047eeb.name: Uadi-Merdùm [Wadi Merdum]. Count Sforza and the Interpreter Maffei Transcribe a Roman Inscription Brought to their Attention by 'Natives'
17ebadf5-f8b4-5fec-89b1-0d6719047eeb.author: Patrizia Pampana, Giulia Barrera
17ebadf5-f8b4-5fec-89b1-0d6719047eeb.third_name: *Uadi-Merdùm. Il conte Sforza e l’interprete Maffei trascrivono un’iscrizione romana segnalata dagli indigeni*
17ebadf5-f8b4-5fec-89b1-0d6719047eeb.second_name: The members of an Italian mission to Libya, aimed at assessing local mining resources, transcribe a Roman inscription
17ebadf5-f8b4-5fec-89b1-0d6719047eeb.description2:
In 1911, before the war broke out, Count Sforza and Ignazio Sanfilippo were touring Libya on a mission to assess local resources, sponsored by the Libyan branch of the Banco di Roma. Their parallel interest in Roman archaeology – testified by this photo – is meaningful for the connection between Italians’ claims of their Roman heritage and Italian colonial ambitions.  
In the opinion of Italian colonialists the discovery of Roman antiquities in Libya brought support to Italian argument that Italy had an historic right to rule over Libya.

18197caa-f988-5826-9a1d-d30e87a0bed4.name: Ottoman map of the period of Sultan Abdülhamid II
18197caa-f988-5826-9a1d-d30e87a0bed4.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
18197caa-f988-5826-9a1d-d30e87a0bed4.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph map
18197caa-f988-5826-9a1d-d30e87a0bed4.description2: One of the world's largest photo archives, Abdülhamid II's photo archives – knows as the Yildiz Albums – contain about 37 thousand pictures from that period of the Ottoman Empire. Abdülhamid II was the 34th Sultan of the Ottoman Empire and the last Sultan to exert effective autocratic control over the fracturing state. He oversaw a period of decline in the power and extent of the empire, including widespread pogroms and government massacres against the minorities of the empire (named the Hamidian massacres, after him) as well as an assassination attempt. He ruled from 31 August 1876 until he was deposed shortly after the 1908 Young Turk Revolution, on 27 April 1909.

183b1889-44b1-5781-a76f-71957bab4067.name: Muhammad ‘Ali Pasha (1769–1849)
183b1889-44b1-5781-a76f-71957bab4067.description2: Portrait of Muhammad 'Ali Pasha. Although born in Greece, he was the founder of modern Egypt. From Albanian origin, he came to Egypt as an Ottoman officer and began the modernisation of the Egyptian state.

184eef10-6e1e-5cd3-9d3c-79a146221593.name: Amelia del Valle y Serrano
184eef10-6e1e-5cd3-9d3c-79a146221593.description: The Marquis of Cerralbo (politician, historian, and collector of art and antiques) and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This albumen portrait of Amelia del Valle y Serrano is delicate and quiet, with outstanding deep chocolate colour which reveals the quality of the photographic technique and the good condition of the object.
184eef10-6e1e-5cd3-9d3c-79a146221593.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes

185ba5fa-c953-5b73-a895-436fd368117e.name: Ottoman Clothing Album
185ba5fa-c953-5b73-a895-436fd368117e.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
185ba5fa-c953-5b73-a895-436fd368117e.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
185ba5fa-c953-5b73-a895-436fd368117e.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
185ba5fa-c953-5b73-a895-436fd368117e.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

1867f5d4-3b17-57ea-bb1b-bff0861448b8.name: The gardens of Regaleira
1867f5d4-3b17-57ea-bb1b-bff0861448b8.holder: Sintra Parks Monte da Lua, Conservation Company
1867f5d4-3b17-57ea-bb1b-bff0861448b8.history: This Romantic estate formerly belonging to the Viscondessa of Regaleira, was acquired and enlarged by António Augusto Carvalho Monteiro (1848–1920) as his favourite country estate. His vast fortune earned him the nickname of Monteiro dos Milhões, (Moneybags Monteiro). He was inspired by the Garden of the Desert de Retz in Marly; Torrigiani Garden in Florence amongst others.
1867f5d4-3b17-57ea-bb1b-bff0861448b8.keywords: Neomanueline; Romanticism; Nature; Garden; Spirituality; Mistery; Alchemy
1867f5d4-3b17-57ea-bb1b-bff0861448b8.description2:
As an image of the Cosmos, the gardens of Regaleira are revealed to the visitors through the sucession of magic and mysterious places. A Paradise Lost coexists in these scenographic representations with a mundus inferus – a Dantesque underground world – through which the candidate is guided by his intuition. The various scenes offer a concrete representation of an initiation journey, like a pilgrimage through a symbolic garden in which one can feel the Harmony of the Spheres and the vertical alignment of the consciousness, in analogy with the Quest for the Supreme Being found in the great Epics.  
References abound in these realms to the worlds of classical mythology, to Virgil, Dante, Milton and Camões, to the Templar-like mission of the Order of Christ and to the enigmas of the alchemical Ars Magna.

189f6b52-96fc-5888-81ec-495e29fdd3fb.name: Image from Sibiu, a city that the emperor and his wife visited in 1817

18b5dc74-b4d3-5829-af1b-731448b5f7c5.name: Sagesse College
18b5dc74-b4d3-5829-af1b-731448b5f7c5.description: The College's old building consists of a stone building with roof tiles and arcades, whereas the new building is a mostly concrete and glass structure. The College first opened its doors to students in 1874, although its construction was not fully completed until 1878 with the addition of a Church. The college's plan is horseshoe shaped facing the sea, and supposedly cost "about thirty thousand pieces of gold, including the purchase of surrounding land".
18b5dc74-b4d3-5829-af1b-731448b5f7c5.author: Hala Masri
18b5dc74-b4d3-5829-af1b-731448b5f7c5.history: Educational institutions in Lebanon were based on religion, as all the religious sects or confessions in Lebanon were in competition in the attempt to spread their beliefs and principles. The Maronite Christians struggled to build this institution due to the Ottoman presence. It was finally inaugurated by Archbishop Yussef Debs in 1875, and was heavily funded by France and Belgium. The construction of the building began in 1874 and lasted four years and cost approximately 30,000 pounds.

18ce1dd3-9c8e-520a-add7-46441936d12f.name: *The impalement of heads of two trapped Austrian soldiers during the combat at Jaice, August 7th 1878*
18ce1dd3-9c8e-520a-add7-46441936d12f.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
18ce1dd3-9c8e-520a-add7-46441936d12f.description2: This painting depicts a brutal war crime that occurred during the Austro-Hungarian Army's occupation campaign in 1878. On the reverse side of the painting there is a contemporary inscription, which sheds light on the situation: “During the battle at Jaice, Master Corporal Grilec and Private Matko, members of the 53rd Infantry Regiment have been trapped and beheaded. Their heads have been impaled in front of the gate to the river Pliva.” This treatment of prisoners of war was unfortunately not rare during the first weeks of the campaign; it provided a glimpse into a difference in approaches to warfare that would be borne out during the upcoming wars in the Balkans, 1912–13.

18e02623-b9ad-5163-8ba9-d958a15a6f01.name: Dagger
18e02623-b9ad-5163-8ba9-d958a15a6f01.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
18e02623-b9ad-5163-8ba9-d958a15a6f01.dimensions: Length without sheath 28 cm, sheath length 19.5 cm
18e02623-b9ad-5163-8ba9-d958a15a6f01.author: Huda Kilani
18e02623-b9ad-5163-8ba9-d958a15a6f01.keywords: Thin silver; Hammering; sheath; geometric motifs; turquoise; arms; armours; metalwork; fashion; accessories
18e02623-b9ad-5163-8ba9-d958a15a6f01.materials: Thin silver, wood, metal; casting handmade
18e02623-b9ad-5163-8ba9-d958a15a6f01.description2: Wooden handled dagger with thin silver sheath; incurved geometric designs on the obverse side; inset with turquoise and black stones. The dagger was used by both Bedouins and villagers as part of men’s traditional garb. This object reflects the diverse population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It also demonstrates personal attire, fashion, local costumes and rites.

18fa1217-5885-554f-bf5c-aed5d4898cb0.name: Editorial. Inauguration of the Musée Gallo-Romain at the Château de Saint-Germain
18fa1217-5885-554f-bf5c-aed5d4898cb0.keywords: Gallo-roman antiquities; Musée de Sain-Germain en Laye
18fa1217-5885-554f-bf5c-aed5d4898cb0.description2: In March 1862, Emperor Napoléon III ordered the "creation of a museum for Celtic and Gallo-Roman antiquities at the Château de Saint-Germain-en-Laye". The castle was restored by Eugène Millet, student of Viollet-le-Duc, who chose to restore it to its condition under François I. A team of confirmed archaeologists were tasked with the organisation of the Museum. Napoléon III wanted a museum dedicated to the archaeology of the national lands (contrary to the collections at the Louvre), and methodically classified: the first curator, Alexandre Bertrand, introduced a chronological classification, breaking the tradition of thematically classified collections. The emperor chose to inaugurate the museum with a symbolically extravagant ceremony, while in Paris the Exposition Universelle (world fair) was in full swing (May 1867).

18fd68f6-0db6-5ad7-aa02-07fc4aa8572e.name: Bronze medal celebrating the Suez Canal
18fd68f6-0db6-5ad7-aa02-07fc4aa8572e.description2: This medal combines two of the great passions of the late 19th century: modern technology (here in the form of the magnificent new canal) and the captivating remains of ancient Egypt.

19148556-ea6b-5b21-8cbd-bc83909a1343.name: Binding/Book cover
19148556-ea6b-5b21-8cbd-bc83909a1343.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art
19148556-ea6b-5b21-8cbd-bc83909a1343.description2: Arabian leather binding bought for the Museum of Applied Arts in Vienna.
