1947528b-a97f-56af-b6c4-fe8372c9bdd5.name: *The Western Wall*
1947528b-a97f-56af-b6c4-fe8372c9bdd5.description2: The Western Wall of the Haram es-Sharif in Jerusalem, as depicted for the readers of the Illustrated London News by William ‘Crimea’ Simpson. Simpson’s sketches were turned into engravings for publication in the ILN, and were among the most important graphic depictions which helped to introduce western readers to the present-day appearance of Jerusalem and Jerusalemites.

1959666e-3460-5e95-bc55-a3706388cf52.name: Archaeological excavations
1959666e-3460-5e95-bc55-a3706388cf52.description2: This photograph documents the discovery and excavation of archaeological relics in the area of Saqqara in 1901. The original photograph was included in a specific collection of the German Archive.

1961e839-9c16-5779-a767-870149fec738.name: The Serious Unemployment Crisis in the Province of Ferrara [central Italy]: Women Preventing the Cavalry from Advancing against the Rioters
1961e839-9c16-5779-a767-870149fec738.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
1961e839-9c16-5779-a767-870149fec738.author: Giulia Barrera
1961e839-9c16-5779-a767-870149fec738.third_name: *La grave crisi della disoccupazione in provincia di Ferrara: donne che impediscono alla cavalleria di avanzare contro i tumultuanti*
1961e839-9c16-5779-a767-870149fec738.second_name: Clashes between people who are protesting against unemployment and the army
1961e839-9c16-5779-a767-870149fec738.description2:
Violent clashes in the province of Ferrara (Emilia Romagna, Italy) between people who protested against unemployment and the army. The women are in the front line, protecting their comrades from the attacks of the cavalry.  
In 1913, an economic crisis hit Italy. Unemployment grew considerably and so did emigration. In 1913, Italian migration abroad reached its peak: 870.000 Italians migrate abroad. Social tensions and conflicts ran high.

19a79dbf-5845-53ed-a137-ee4c74fd1299.name: Inkpot and blotter
19a79dbf-5845-53ed-a137-ee4c74fd1299.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
19a79dbf-5845-53ed-a137-ee4c74fd1299.description2: Dimitrija Chupovski (1878-1940) devoted his life to raising the awareness of Macedonians about their national identity. He worked actively on the recognition of Macedonian as distinct Slavic language and prepared the grammar of the modern Macedonian language. He also contributed to opening schools for children in Macedonia to learn in their native language.

19adb7d5-92bf-5c8a-8b63-f8d677d0e713.name: Danilo I, Prince of Montenegro (1871–1939)
19adb7d5-92bf-5c8a-8b63-f8d677d0e713.keywords: Danilo I, Prince of Montenegro; Jugoslavia; Vienna; Austria
19adb7d5-92bf-5c8a-8b63-f8d677d0e713.description2: Danilo I, Prince of Montenegro (1871–1939) was the eldest son of King Nicola I of Montenegro. He was married to Princess Jutta von Mecklenburg-Strelitz and had to leave Montenegro after it was integrated in the kingdom of Yugoslavia after WWI. He died in 1937 in Vienna, Austria – in exile.

19dba65f-a9fe-593e-8561-b4a20b42b083.name: *A British Ship Coral Fishing Near Algiers*
19dba65f-a9fe-593e-8561-b4a20b42b083.author: Rossana Spadaccini, Cristina Francioli
19dba65f-a9fe-593e-8561-b4a20b42b083.archival: ASNa, Ministero degli affari esteri, Piante, 7048
19dba65f-a9fe-593e-8561-b4a20b42b083.third_name: *Bastimento inglese esercitando la pesca del corallo*
19dba65f-a9fe-593e-8561-b4a20b42b083.description2: Coral fishing was an important economic activity in the Mediterranean. Algeria was the main fishing area for corals, especially after the depletion of Sardinian coral, and ships from different countries competed for this valuable resource. Torre del Greco, near Naples, was the most important port town for coral fishing in the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies, while Livorno was the most important port town for coral fishing in the Grand Duke of Tuscany. In 1864, Torre del Greco had 300 coral-fishing boats while Livorno had 60.

19f232dc-5ab5-59c1-9ebb-efa8da82d771.name: *Turkish woman at the hammam or baths*
19f232dc-5ab5-59c1-9ebb-efa8da82d771.keywords: costume; hammam; women; fashion; Orientalism; travel; traveller; Ottoman bath culture
19f232dc-5ab5-59c1-9ebb-efa8da82d771.description2: Sheet from *Costumes Turcs*, a lavish set of volumes produced in Turkey for a European audience. They present the appearance of people from different areas, with different jobs etc.

1a477c20-c077-5125-9fc1-9d8eb04e2681.name: *View in the Plain of Latakia, in Syria*
1a477c20-c077-5125-9fc1-9d8eb04e2681.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
1a477c20-c077-5125-9fc1-9d8eb04e2681.provenance: First published in Robert Brown, *The Countries of the World*, published by Cassell and Company Ltd, London and New York, 1876, p. 28
1a477c20-c077-5125-9fc1-9d8eb04e2681.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
1a477c20-c077-5125-9fc1-9d8eb04e2681.description2: This print, entitled 'View in the Plain of Latakia, Syria' was first published on page 28 of in Robert Brown''s 'The Countries of the World', published by Cassell and Company Ltd, London and New York in 1876. In the 19th century, Latakia was famous for its tobacco, grown in the plain behind the town and on the Ansarieh hills. Three main varieties of tobacco were produced: the lowest quality was dark in colour and strong in flavour; the best, grown in the districts of Diryus and Amamareh, was light and aromatic, exported mainly to Alexandria, Constantinople, Cyprus and directly to Europe.

1a6c2dab-593a-50ec-bd49-e8fe751754f3.name: Lebanese Bachelor degree diploma
1a6c2dab-593a-50ec-bd49-e8fe751754f3.holder: Ministry of Education and Fine Arts
1a6c2dab-593a-50ec-bd49-e8fe751754f3.author: Hala Masri
1a6c2dab-593a-50ec-bd49-e8fe751754f3.description2: Michel Yusuf Karam's high school diploma, dating to 1913.

1a906565-b92b-506c-8793-8e7de3c29e02.name: Medallion: primary education, national education (an teacher and two students).
1a906565-b92b-506c-8793-8e7de3c29e02.description2: The engraver Oscar Roty was famous for his image of "La Semeuse" (the sower), which was stamped on French coins.  This symbolic medallion, depicting two young students, pays tribute to Jules Ferry's education laws, which introduced free, secular and mandatory primary schooling for girls and boys.

1aa20f81-288f-5491-bfba-4d0a1e219f27.name: Qur’an
1aa20f81-288f-5491-bfba-4d0a1e219f27.holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts
1aa20f81-288f-5491-bfba-4d0a1e219f27.keywords: Floral decoration; religious objects; waqf; Qur’an; Turkish Baroque-Rococo
1aa20f81-288f-5491-bfba-4d0a1e219f27.description2: Illumination is a natural part of Qur'ans. Illuminators used naturalistic floral motifs influenced by Europe alongside classical elements to illuminate the Qur'ans during the AH 12th–13th / AD 18th–19th centuries.

1ac5c099-15f5-5bc0-b9bd-13a0de13ed0b.name: Al-Majidiyya Mosque
1ac5c099-15f5-5bc0-b9bd-13a0de13ed0b.description: Located by the coast, north of Beirut's downtown, al-Majidiyya Mosque was once an 18th century Ottoman defensive fort.
1ac5c099-15f5-5bc0-b9bd-13a0de13ed0b.author: Jeff El-Msanne
1ac5c099-15f5-5bc0-b9bd-13a0de13ed0b.history: In 1841, this ex-Ottoman fort was turned into a mosque and named after the Ottoman sultan 'Abd al-Majid I. The mosque was then enlarged and renovated in 1881 and in 1906. Its tall, pencil-shaped minaret is built in the typical Ottoman style, whereas the shorter minaret resembles the Beiruti-Mamluk style. The interior of the mosque has conserved the arches and vaulted ceilings of the Ottoman fort it once was.

1aee0242-efb1-5288-9004-18c010d1d030.name: *Raqqi Synagogue, Damascus*
1aee0242-efb1-5288-9004-18c010d1d030.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
1aee0242-efb1-5288-9004-18c010d1d030.author: Stefan Weber
1aee0242-efb1-5288-9004-18c010d1d030.second_name: Courtyard, demonstrating the architectural vicinity to dwellings
1aee0242-efb1-5288-9004-18c010d1d030.description2: The Raqqi Synagogue is a basalt construction from the late 19th century in Damascus. It was one of the several synagogues in the city, all of them built or rebuilt in the 19th century. Thus, the are relatively new in comparison to the long history of Jews in city. Its architectural style and decoration is very close to urban dwellings of the period. In 2011, extensive renovation plans for this important synagogue were passed.

1b1e3ef8-5e29-5178-ac83-8c4cb0d8ce8c.name: Invitation from Egyptian Sultan Fuad I to Joaquín Sorolla
1b1e3ef8-5e29-5178-ac83-8c4cb0d8ce8c.description: Sultan Fuad I’s letter was sent to Sorolla by Garcia Herreros. It is an invitation to spend one year with his family in the palaces of Cairo, where the painter could reside and work freely. All this is part of the artistic policy that was intended to attract well-known Western artists to the Egyptian sultan's court. Unfortunately, Sorolla was never able to take this trip, but from a letter to his wife we know the excitement that was caused by the idea of spending time in Egypt.
1b1e3ef8-5e29-5178-ac83-8c4cb0d8ce8c.author: Covadonga Pitarch
1b1e3ef8-5e29-5178-ac83-8c4cb0d8ce8c.third_name: Carta del Sultán de Egipto Fyad I

1b350001-5006-5f24-bc12-29f7589319af.name: *Country West of Algiers from the British Consul General's Garden*
1b350001-5006-5f24-bc12-29f7589319af.author: Houria Cherid
1b350001-5006-5f24-bc12-29f7589319af.third_name: *Country West of Algiers from the British Consul General's Garden*
1b350001-5006-5f24-bc12-29f7589319af.description2: A lithograph depicting the countryside to the west of Algiers, as seen from the garden of the British General Consul's garden.

1b553eb5-5ca4-5f1a-9027-ff3e00f54fe1.name: *Voyage de la Haute Egypte*
1b553eb5-5ca4-5f1a-9027-ff3e00f54fe1.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. Travelling in the 19th century became easier and more reliable due to the advent of steamships and trains. Westerners travelled to the East not only for touristic purposes, but also for scientific research, history, archaeology or for religious reasons. Western travellers told of their experiences and what they saw in eastern countries in their travel books and they even offer advice about the journey. Istanbul, where East and West meet, has been the subject of many a traveller's book.

1bb390d7-8753-553f-9174-6119a0f96ab1.name: *Exposition Universelle - Their Royal Imperial Majesties and the Viceroy of Egypt visit the Temple of Edfu*
1bb390d7-8753-553f-9174-6119a0f96ab1.artist: Artist: Filippo Liardo; illustrator: Gustave Janet
1bb390d7-8753-553f-9174-6119a0f96ab1.keywords: Archaeological excavations; Egyptomania; Egypt; World fairs
1bb390d7-8753-553f-9174-6119a0f96ab1.description2: Visitors to the 1867 Exposition Universelle (world fair) had the opportunity to explore a reconstruction of the Temple of Edfu in a "Parc Égyptien". This reconstruction (containing a mix of various different temples) was a response both to the fashion for ancient Egypt, and the desire for good diplomatic relations with modern Egypt. Indeed, we can see the imperial couple in this photograph standing with Isma'il Pasha, the viceroy of Egypt, who had come to see the exhibition. The Temple of Edfu had just been rediscovered by the famous Egyptologist Mariette.

1bf2807f-b480-5653-a4f4-e5a1183a5629.name: Dura'ah coat
1bf2807f-b480-5653-a4f4-e5a1183a5629.keywords: costume; cotton; silk; silk trade; Syria
1bf2807f-b480-5653-a4f4-e5a1183a5629.description2: Druze, Galilee. Most of this coat, apart from the brown cotton sleeves, is made from luxury fabrics imported from Syria or Europe: red satin and panels of  blue and silver brocade, which are attached with large red running stitches. The cord edging shows Ottoman influence.

1c205c93-bc85-56c7-bb96-3f280389af94.name: *Comares Courtyard at the Alhambra*
1c205c93-bc85-56c7-bb96-3f280389af94.description: The monument of the Alhambra, the last palace of the kingdom of Granada, fascinated travellers to Spain during the nineteenth century. Sorolla saw it for the first time in 1902 and in his successive trips to Granada during 1909, 1910 and 1917 he painted it, away from the Orientalist clichés, focusing on its corners, and especially in its gardens and fountains. In this view of the Patio de Comares, he highlights the reflection of the arches over the pond and a set of mirrors that is repeated in successive rooms of the palace.
1c205c93-bc85-56c7-bb96-3f280389af94.author: Covadonga Pitarch
1c205c93-bc85-56c7-bb96-3f280389af94.third_name: *El Patio de Comares, la Alhambra de Granada*

1c267ea2-0ed8-59a8-a801-5398707285eb.name: Balkans, exiled civilians on the move
1c267ea2-0ed8-59a8-a801-5398707285eb.description2: The First Balkan War (1912–1913) saw the Ottoman Empire at war with Serbia, Bulgaria and Greece. The violent nature of the conflict caused many populations to be displaced.

1c45a682-1820-5eee-b604-862620e6fcea.name: *The Tunisian post service*
1c45a682-1820-5eee-b604-862620e6fcea.holder: Musée des Postes, Télégraphes et Télécommunications
1c45a682-1820-5eee-b604-862620e6fcea.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
1c45a682-1820-5eee-b604-862620e6fcea.keywords: Post and telegraph office; Greco-Roman style
1c45a682-1820-5eee-b604-862620e6fcea.description2: This oil on canvas painting shows a scene from daily life at the Tunis post and telegraph office, built on the Rue d'Italie (now Rue Charles-de-Gaulle). One of the busiest rooms, the revenue office's great hall is, with its tremendously high ceilings, an impressive example of neo-classical architecture. Featuring elements of carved plaster and a map of Tunisia on a central marble panel, this painting faithfully reproduces the opulence of this historic building.

1c4b95a5-1ef1-50b3-a51a-bdc1148ce5c5.name: Archaeological excavations
1c4b95a5-1ef1-50b3-a51a-bdc1148ce5c5.description2: Photograph showing workers at the site of the excavations carried out in the area of Abusir in 1901, and the discovery of some archaeological pieces and columns. Photo taken by the German archaeological mission.

1c651cdc-3180-5289-952f-daeae5e69f65.name: Emigrants who immigrated to America
1c651cdc-3180-5289-952f-daeae5e69f65.holder: Population Exchange Museum (The Foundation of Lausanne Treaty Emigrants)
1c651cdc-3180-5289-952f-daeae5e69f65.description2: The 1923 population exchange between Greece and Turkey was based upon religious identity, and involved the Greek Orthodox citizens of Turkey and the Muslim citizens of Greece. The "Convention Concerning the Exchange of Greek and Turkish Populations" was signed at Lausanne, Switzerland, on 30 January 1923, by the governments of Greece and Turkey. This photo depicts some Muslim migrants who immigrated to America.

1c7eb8dd-c27a-55e4-b4bd-256860c07387.name: Types of Cairo
1c7eb8dd-c27a-55e4-b4bd-256860c07387.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
1c7eb8dd-c27a-55e4-b4bd-256860c07387.author: Vito Lattanzi, Marina Minozzi
1c7eb8dd-c27a-55e4-b4bd-256860c07387.keywords: Woman; photograph; anthropology; ethnology; geography; travel; exploration; scientific expedition; ethnography; museums; model; genre picture; portrait; representation of the other; costume; material culture; collection; Egypt
1c7eb8dd-c27a-55e4-b4bd-256860c07387.description2: The historical photos, belonging to Enrico H. Giglioli's collection, were collected by the Florentine naturalist during his travel around the world in 1865–68 on the Magenta's steam corvette, with the purpose to start diplomatic and commercial relations. The "genre" images seem to be created "ad hoc" to represent human diversity along the different ages. The ethnographic photographs in the Giglioli's collection are part of the historical archive of the Pigorini Museum, and are very important for the history of anthropological science and history of photography. The origins in terms of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome, can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

1ca3c828-bf7a-599e-a4f4-bc69d80d6a00.name: A photograph of the old building of the Berlin Stock Exchange
1ca3c828-bf7a-599e-a4f4-bc69d80d6a00.holder: Photo archives of the Prussian Heritage Foundation

1ca4ae5b-e753-59d1-a5de-423460efb5d1.name: Iconostasis in the Church of the Holy Saviour
1ca4ae5b-e753-59d1-a5de-423460efb5d1.type: Work of art executed in wood-carving; iconostasis
1ca4ae5b-e753-59d1-a5de-423460efb5d1.holder: The Church of the Holy Saviour
1ca4ae5b-e753-59d1-a5de-423460efb5d1.author: Nada Andonovska
1ca4ae5b-e753-59d1-a5de-423460efb5d1.artist: Petre Filipovski Garkata and his group of artisans from village Gari near Debar
1ca4ae5b-e753-59d1-a5de-423460efb5d1.description2: This iconostasis was created by one of the greatest Macedonian masters of woodcarving, Petre Filipovski Garka, who formed his own group of artisans and developed his outstanding style of wood-carving, which was widely recognizable in the Balkans in the early 19th century. This exquisite piece of wood-carving was made from walnut in the technique of high relief. The iconostasis depicts scenes from the Old and the New Testament in which biblical figures are rendered wearing traditional costumes worn in Macedonia. The detail shows the self-portraits of Petre Filipovski and his associate artisans.

1caa0741-193b-5ce9-9a9c-423846c3eeff.name: Small bucket
1caa0741-193b-5ce9-9a9c-423846c3eeff.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
1caa0741-193b-5ce9-9a9c-423846c3eeff.author: Marina Minozzi
1caa0741-193b-5ce9-9a9c-423846c3eeff.keywords: Applied arts; minor arts; manufacture;  craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; model; reproduction; decoration; motifs; collection; collector; glass; Murano glass; glasswork; gold leaf; cobalt-blue; crystal; zoomophysm; zoomorphic; eastern influence
1caa0741-193b-5ce9-9a9c-423846c3eeff.description2: M.A.I. was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, as part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. The small bucket in glass cobalt-blue is decorated with crystal animal-shaped applications and gold leaves recalling ancient eastern motifs. The object was made according to the 18th century taste and recalls 15th century models of aspersoriums, or holy water basins, from Venice dating from the 16th and 17th centuries. These objects were depicted in paintings by Veronese and Carpaccio.
1caa0741-193b-5ce9-9a9c-423846c3eeff.holding_institution_org: Museo Artistico Industriale presso la Galleria nazionale d’arte antica in Palazzo Barberini

en: Zaccagnini, M., *Arti decorative: Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini*, Rome: L'Erma di Bretschneider, 2011: 23.

1ccb2e38-9e35-5e04-be15-39d7faa20cc7.name: Bahiya Palace
1ccb2e38-9e35-5e04-be15-39d7faa20cc7.history: The site of the palace lies southeast of the Marrakesh *Medina*, close to the present royal palace. It was built in two phases by a father and son who served as grand viziers to two ‘Alawid sultans. The first part of the palace, known as Dar Si Musa ‒ the largest and most luxurious in Morocco at the time ‒ was built between 1866 and 1867 by Si Musa, grand vizier to Sultan Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman (reigned 1859-73). Between 1894 and 1900, the second phase of construction started under Si Musa’s son, Si Ahmad ibn Musa, grand vizier to two sultans Mulay al-Hasan I (1873-94) and Mulay ‘Abd al-‘Aziz (1894-1908), to designs by the architect Muhammad ibn Makki al-Misfiwi. During his reign, Ahmad ibn Musa enlarged the southern part of his father’s palace and subsequently developed a number of glamorously designed connecting houses. He lived on the grounds with four wives, a harem of 24 official concubines and their many children. Having built the palace for his favourite wife, Ahmad ibn Musa named it *Bahiya*, meaning “beautiful, brilliant”.
1ccb2e38-9e35-5e04-be15-39d7faa20cc7.keywords: Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic architecture in Morocco; Moroccan architects; traditional city; Islamic city; palace; royal palace; plan; urban planning; stucco; garden; patio; Islamic garden; zellij; ceramic; geometrical motifs; gardens and architecture
1ccb2e38-9e35-5e04-be15-39d7faa20cc7.description2: Covering an area of eight hectares, the palace consists of 150 rooms lavishly decorated with *mashrabiyya*, marble sculptures, paintings on beech and cedar, stuccowork and *zellige*. Built in two phases in the second half of the 19th century, the estate is comprised of structures built piecemeal, including outbuildings and ancillary structures: a Turkish bath, mosque and stables, and other annexed houses that are connected to each other, many of which are remarkable both in their structure and their ornamentation. Although the buildings are arranged disparately throughout the estate they are organised around several patios and green Islamic-style gardens (*al-agdal*), planted with orange, banana and cypress trees, as well as hibiscus and jasmine, and irrigated by *qanat*.

1d05a82c-6016-572a-b4ab-6100639104d3.name: Project for a steamship for the Sultan of Morocco, by the Fratelli Orlando shipyards (Livorno, Italy)
1d05a82c-6016-572a-b4ab-6100639104d3.author: Daniela Tazzi
1d05a82c-6016-572a-b4ab-6100639104d3.archival: ASLi, Cantiere Navale Luigi Orlando, busta 10M2
1d05a82c-6016-572a-b4ab-6100639104d3.description2:
Project drawn to a scale 1:100.  
In 1899, the Fratelli Orlando shipyards (Livorno, Italy) made a project of a screw steamer for the Sultan of Morocco. The steamer was to have two decks, two steam engines of 900 HP and harbour twelve passengers. The project, however, was never realised.  
The Fratelli Orlando shipyards built the cruiser Bascir for the Moroccan Navy and a yacht for the Khédivé of Egypt.

1d3af9a9-da3f-50ca-95c3-42bd8920651e.name: Medwakh Pipe
1d3af9a9-da3f-50ca-95c3-42bd8920651e.holder: Sharjah Heritage Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
1d3af9a9-da3f-50ca-95c3-42bd8920651e.dates: Hegira first half of the 14th century / AD first half of the 20th century
1d3af9a9-da3f-50ca-95c3-42bd8920651e.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
1d3af9a9-da3f-50ca-95c3-42bd8920651e.description2: This small pipe has a long tradition among the local sailors and seafarers in the Gulf region, who traditionally favoured Medwakh tobacco, a particular local blend mixed with herbs, spices and aromatic bark. It was produced locally and came in three strengths, from cold (barid) to warm (dafi) and hot (har). Unlike other tobaccos, dokha, as it is known as, is not harvested and cured, its vegetal ingredients simply dried in the sun. As the dokha mixtures were very potent, they were only ever smoked in very small pipes like the one illustrated here.

1d9d7d4e-2cb4-52c3-9914-92ee2a314c89.name: Giuseppe Verdi
1d9d7d4e-2cb4-52c3-9914-92ee2a314c89.archival: Fondo Galletti – Autografi – busta T-Z, fascicolo “Verdi Giuseppe”

1d9fdf68-a63f-5cd6-937f-9223edee8336.name: *Hebron*
1d9fdf68-a63f-5cd6-937f-9223edee8336.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
1d9fdf68-a63f-5cd6-937f-9223edee8336.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
1d9fdf68-a63f-5cd6-937f-9223edee8336.description2: This print is based on a watercolour by David Roberts entitled 'Hebron Mosque erected over the graves of Abraham and the Patriarchs' and completed in 1835. Apparently, this in turn was based on an initial sketch made at the Mosque by a Mrs Bracebridge. According to Jewish, Christian and Muslim tradition, the sanctuary at Hebron houses the graves of Abraham, his wife Sarah and their family. To Jews, it is the second holiest site after Jerusalem. Muslims revere the site because of its associations with Abraham and view the city of Hebron as one of the sacred cities of Islam. Formerly prosperous as a glass-manufacturing centre and hajj staging post, Hebron's fortunes declined in the 19th century due to cheap glass imports and the rerouting of the hajj caravan from Damascus to Transjordan.

1d9fdf68-a63f-5cd6-937f-9223edee8336.artist_deathplace: David Roberts: London; William Finder: London

1deb708b-ab5d-5f99-8702-421204b044cf.name: Berber woman (Nailiya) lying down
1deb708b-ab5d-5f99-8702-421204b044cf.description: The image depicts a Nailiya, a woman of the Berber tribe of the Ouled Naïl, in the south of Algeria. She is lying on her side like an odalisque, wearing a colourful silk dress and the rich jewels used to perform their traditional dance. The Nailiyat were independent women, free to marry men of their choosing. They moved to the cities in the North to earn money as dancers, in order to maintain their families in their community of origin. All this was not fully understood by Europeans. With the emergence of sex-tourism these women were forced to introduce sexual content in their originally hieratic performance, and finally they were even considered as prostitutes by the French administration, which in turn led to them being repudiated in their villages. Early photography contributed to forge this image of the Nailiyat in the European imagination.

1ded3dd3-7a23-59f6-a90a-327c278ea1a9.name: Portrait of Shaykh Qasim al-Kusty
1ded3dd3-7a23-59f6-a90a-327c278ea1a9.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
1ded3dd3-7a23-59f6-a90a-327c278ea1a9.description2: Shaykh Qasimal-Kusty was born in Beirut in 1840. He studied Arabic literature alongside great masters of his time, such as Shaykh Ibrahim al-Ahdab and Shaykh Yusuf al-Asir. He practiced teaching for a while, before publishing his first collection of poetry. He also assisted with theatrical productions. He died in 1909.

1df2efa8-09f6-56fe-b40d-5cff853bf496.name: Revolver
1df2efa8-09f6-56fe-b40d-5cff853bf496.description: A Belgian produced double action revolver, serial number 6647, with a five-shot cylinder. Fitted with chequered wooden grips, this revolver features some simple leaf and scroll pattern and border engraving of the frame and cylinder. The base of the cylindrical barrel, where it is attached to the cylinder, has a crowned “R”. The cylinder itself is decorated with a strand of small 6-pointed stars. On the left side of the revolver are the words "*Dassen Patent, Guss Stahl*".

1e12d773-b67f-5c74-86a0-52e25a1cd507.name: *Précis Historique de la Traite des Noirs et de l'Esclavage Colonial*
1e12d773-b67f-5c74-86a0-52e25a1cd507.description2: Joseph Elzéar Morénas (1776–1830) was born to a wealthy family of merchants. Following an early trip to India, Morénas became specialised in botany and developed a love of languages, which even led him to write a Hindi dictionary. When he was sent to Senegal in 1818 he was horrified by what he saw of the slave trade, and so asked to be repatriated. After a sojourn in Haiti, he began working on research in the agricultural sciences, all the while denouncing the "slave trade". His two petitions, "*Pétition contre la traite des noirs*" (1820 and 1821), which he presented to the Chamber of Deputies, created many problems for him. He therefore began working on a *Précis Historique de la Traite des Noirs et de l'Esclavage Colonial* instead, which was published in 1828. He died in Russia, where the Tsar encouraged the continuation of his agronomical work. This title page points to his relationship with and support for Cyril Bissette, a Martinician accused of having written De la Situation des Gens de Couleur Libres aux Antilles Françaises, who was banished by the royal court along with his so-called accomplices (Fabien and Volny).

1e164505-7b44-5ab0-8ab5-124407905064.name: Model of the brig *Mariţa*
1e164505-7b44-5ab0-8ab5-124407905064.description2: In 1834 Wallachia and Moldavia, which were under Ottoman suzerainty, were granted by the Ottoman Empire the right to sail on the Danube using their national banners. The first Romanian ship to sail under Romanian banner was the brig “Marița”, built in the naval dockyard of the Giurgiu port. Its owner was Wallachian politician Alexandru Vilara, who gave it the name of the wife of Alexandru II Ghica, Wallachia’s ruler between 1834-1842. “Marița” began its first trip in December 1834. Its destination was Istanbul, where it transported 300 kg of wheat. It returned in June 1835 after having been seriously damaged by two storms, one of which on its way back, when the crew had to throw overboard the wine purchased from Istanbul.

1e2be9c1-6927-592d-9052-ed69ed5754c4.name: Ten piasters
1e2be9c1-6927-592d-9052-ed69ed5754c4.description: On obverse: "*amara bi ta'amul al-husayn bin 'ali 1338 'abduhu wa-ibn 'abdihi*" ("It is ordered to deal with by al-Hussein bin' Ali 1334, God servant"). 1e5a98c0-6a45-5ac8-8201-22da00b4e53b.description2: General view of the pyramids of Abusir, in the area of the pyramids of the king Userkaf and king Neferirkare. These pyramids represent vestiges of the Fifth Dynasty, and they date back to 2800 BC (Old Kingdom). The paper photograph is printed from glass plate negatives.

1e650671-cb20-50f3-8f15-8ed06e41849a.holder: Italian Institute for African and Oriental Studies
1e650671-cb20-50f3-8f15-8ed06e41849a.author: Giulia Barrera

1e650671-cb20-50f3-8f15-8ed06e41849a.second_name: An old Greek woman who was the only person remaining in the Libyan town Marsa Susa when the Italian army occupied it
1e650671-cb20-50f3-8f15-8ed06e41849a.description2:
This picture was taken by an Italian military unit during the Italian invasion of Libya.  
Apollonia was the name of an ancient town, dating back to the 7th century BC. By 1911, Apollonia was nothing more than an archaeological site. The modern Arab town was called Marsa Susa. The Italians’ use of the ancient name was intended to remind readers that Libya was once under Roman rule. Italian colonialists claimed that Italy had an historic right to rule over Libya, since the Roman Empire once ruled over that country.
1e650671-cb20-50f3-8f15-8ed06e41849a.holding_institution_org: Istituto italiano per l’Africa e l’Oriente

1e88ab3a-3f62-5a22-b9a2-264a8573788d.name: Two pistols
1e88ab3a-3f62-5a22-b9a2-264a8573788d.type: Military object; metalwork; firearms; arms and armour
1e88ab3a-3f62-5a22-b9a2-264a8573788d.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
1e88ab3a-3f62-5a22-b9a2-264a8573788d.keywords: Military object; Metalwork; Steel; Arms; armour; Pistol
1e88ab3a-3f62-5a22-b9a2-264a8573788d.description2: These Turkish flintlock pistols were used by the Ottoman soldiers in Lebanon in the 19th century to quash resistance movements. As the Lebanese resistance had no weapons of their own, the fighters frequently ambushed Ottoman soldiers and took their weapons. These pistols are an example of such weaponry, which was taken by the resistance and used against the Ottomans. They were commonly known as "knee pistols", as they were fired from horseback by placing the butt of the pistol against the rider's knee. Both have a typical blunderbuss style stock with a beautifully shaped butt stock, a wooden forend and a round barrel. They are made of wood and cast steel.

1ef87e38-e142-56b3-951f-b7d338ff850e.name: *Austrian troops occupy Venice in 1797*
1ef87e38-e142-56b3-951f-b7d338ff850e.description2: Napoleon ended the existence of the 1000-year-old Venetian Republic in May 1797. French troops proceeded to occupy Venice for six months from May 1797 to January 1798, then ceded the city to Austria. Austrian troops occupied Venice starting 18 January 1798 until the Peace of Pressburg in 1805.

1f016872-92d0-54fb-b596-c44b25a26d1a.name: Plate
1f016872-92d0-54fb-b596-c44b25a26d1a.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
1f016872-92d0-54fb-b596-c44b25a26d1a.description2: Kütahya was the second most important ceramic production centre after İznik due to the rich clay deposits in the area. This plate has flat rim, is slightly deep in body and has a circular bottom. It was made of white clay and coated in white on which there are patterns in cobalt blue, yellow, turquoise, purple and red covered with transparent glaze. In the middle of the plate there is an Ottoman coat-of-arms while both sides of the plate are decorated with curtains. Above the coat-of-arms, “Long Live My Sultan” is written in Turkish in Arabic letters forming a crescent and there is a *tuğra* (monogram) of Abdülhamid II (1876-1909) in the middle of the sun covering both the *tuğra* and the crescent.

1f01b620-1564-5cb2-8825-cd2a342b9728.name: *Ambassador Mohammed ibn 'Abd al-Malik, Pasha of Tangier, visits Vienna on February 14, 1783*
1f01b620-1564-5cb2-8825-cd2a342b9728.description2: This picture shows Moroccan Ambassador Mohammed ibn 'Abd al-Malik, Pasha of Tangier, at his first visit to Vienna on 14 Feb 1783. This visit of the Moroccan delegation in Vienna started the more than 200-years-long peaceful relationship between Morocco and Austria.

1f14a324-c1e9-5296-b0e9-2ac16800da16.name: Old wooden slippers
1f14a324-c1e9-5296-b0e9-2ac16800da16.description2: Slippers made out of wood that was usually worn for comfort.

1f2e44d5-854a-519d-868a-777ceb2535e3.name: *Les Folies Turques: quadrille*
1f2e44d5-854a-519d-868a-777ceb2535e3.description2: The 18th century fascination with "turkeries" was followed in the 19th century by a trend for music with more stereotypical, supposedly "oriental" motifs. This operetta about "turkish follies", is an example of this.

1f3e2539-13d7-58c9-871e-2d7832ae9523.name: Child among balls of yarn
1f3e2539-13d7-58c9-871e-2d7832ae9523.description2: In 1930, France imported nearly 350,000 tons of cotton, 2/3 of which came from the United States, with the rest coming from the British Iles and Egypt. The French cotton industry employed around 200,000 people at this time, mainly in the east and the north of the country.

1f4778d6-1457-56dc-8745-6fecef3643f8.name: Hussein Avni Pasha (1819–1876)
1f4778d6-1457-56dc-8745-6fecef3643f8.keywords: Huseyn Avni Pasha; Sultan Abdülaziz; Ottoman army
1f4778d6-1457-56dc-8745-6fecef3643f8.description2: Portrait of Huseyn Avni Pasha, who was murdered in 1876 by Hasan Bey. In 1874 Huseyn Avni Pasha became Grand Vizier. He served in this position until 25 April 1875. From 25 August 1875 until 1 October 1875, he served as War Minister. Starting 11 April 1876, he served again as War Minister and played a major role in toppling Sultan Abdülaziz.

1f47ed93-cd30-5e50-a285-fa35fb1728c8.name: Mada'in Salih Railway Station
1f47ed93-cd30-5e50-a285-fa35fb1728c8.holder: Saudi Commission for Tourism and Antiquities
1f47ed93-cd30-5e50-a285-fa35fb1728c8.location: Northwest of Saudi Arabia in al-'Ula (Alula) region
1f47ed93-cd30-5e50-a285-fa35fb1728c8.history: Historically the Tribe of Lihyan was the first known Tribe settled in the area and founded the Kingdom of Lihyan in the "Oasis of Aula" in  the sixth century until the fourth BC. There is not much historical information about the Lihyanite but mentions that they allied themselves with the Nabataeans later. The largest settlement in the area was in the first century AD when the Nabateans made it as the second capital of  their kingdom after Petra in Jordan. The Nabateans dug their graves in the facades  of the mountains of the region , where there are about 132 tombs cut and carved in the rock. Nabataean state has fallen at the hands of the Romans in the second century AD.
1f47ed93-cd30-5e50-a285-fa35fb1728c8.keywords: Railway; station; Hijaz railway; Arabian Peninsula; history of the Hijaz railway; communication; innovation; route; pilgrimage; hajj; Ottoman; Germany; Abdul Hamid; abd al-hamid
1f47ed93-cd30-5e50-a285-fa35fb1728c8.architects: Mukhtar bey, the general manager of the line
1f47ed93-cd30-5e50-a285-fa35fb1728c8.description2: Mada'in Salih Station, which is located 25 kilometres north-east of al-'Ula City, was one of the main railway stations. The site contains seventeen building in addition to the ancient Islamic castle, and there is an old water pool and five wells folded with stones, as well as sixteen building of the railway station have been built in trimmed stones. The buildings had been converted into a museum tells the history of the Hijaz Railway.

1f9cc409-36e4-51f2-828e-77a94d820a08.name: Istanbul water pipeline map
1f9cc409-36e4-51f2-828e-77a94d820a08.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
1f9cc409-36e4-51f2-828e-77a94d820a08.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; History of Water in Ottoman Empire; Water; map
1f9cc409-36e4-51f2-828e-77a94d820a08.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The Cendere Hamidian Water Pump Station was built by Abdülhamid II in 1902. The station is located at an altitude of 34 metres above sea level. With its function, architectural design and mechanical equipment, the station is a unique reminder of Ottoman architecture. It pumped to Balmumcu and Beşiktaş – with water coming from 20 different pipes in Kağıthane, propelled by steam pump machines.

1fa42ca0-8bff-5098-bc57-bbb59a4fe4bf.name: Monastery of St. George – Rajchica
1fa42ca0-8bff-5098-bc57-bbb59a4fe4bf.author: Darko Nikolovski
1fa42ca0-8bff-5098-bc57-bbb59a4fe4bf.history: The Church was built in 1835. Upper zones of its frescoes were painted in the span of 1840–1852 by icon-painter Mihail and priest Danail. Lower zones were completed by their disciple, the renowned icon-painter Dicho Zograph from v. Tresonche near Debar, one of the most outstanding Macedonian icon painters.
1fa42ca0-8bff-5098-bc57-bbb59a4fe4bf.architects: Local construction masters. Frescoes painted by icon painter Mihail, monk Daniel and their student Dicho Zograph
1fa42ca0-8bff-5098-bc57-bbb59a4fe4bf.description2: The Monastery in v. Rajchica near Debar is one of the most outstanding 19th-century monasteries in the Republic of Macedonia. The Monastery Church is dedicated to St. George Victorious. It is a model of sacral structure distinctive of the 19th century local construction masters from the Reka Area. The church is a combination of inscribed cross and single-nave structure with three domes. Part of the holy remains of St. George the Victorious – that is, his hand – is kept in the monastery. For many years now the monastery has been serving as a nunnery and nuns have been creating and embroidering robes for church dignitaries in Macedonia and elsewhere.

1fade942-a5a0-5acc-a653-81665badee69.name: Tunisia at the 1889 Paris World Fair

1fb1726f-8870-520a-9b34-30b69dacfc97.author: Mina Moraitou

Houtsma and others. It was published by Brill in Leiden and Lyuzac in London. It contains the ex libris of Antonis Benakis.

1fc5fe5c-fbfa-5316-9126-a887d85076f6.name: *Description de l'Arménie la Perse*
1fc5fe5c-fbfa-5316-9126-a887d85076f6.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. Travelling in the 19th century became easier and more reliable due to the advent of steamships and trains. Westerners travelled to the East not only for touristic purposes, but also for scientific research, history, archaeology or for religious reasons. Félix Marie Charles Texier was a French historian, architect and archaeologist. Texier published a number of significant works involving personal travels throughout Asia Minor and the Middle East. These books included descriptions and maps of ancient sites, reports of regional geography and geology and descriptions of artwork and architecture.

1fe23b95-31f5-5b9a-b2ab-2854193671c7.name: *The Outcast*
1fe23b95-31f5-5b9a-b2ab-2854193671c7.author: DGPC
1fe23b95-31f5-5b9a-b2ab-2854193671c7.description2: This sculpture by António Soares dos Reis was made in Italy and it rapidly became an icon of romanticism, as it symbolises a young man who has been forced into exile.  The classic contours of the human body, the position of the model and the remarkable sculpture led to the recognition of the author as one of Portugal’s main exponents of sculpture and this piece a National Treasure.

1fe2bf0f-28b8-574f-bc6b-664e988fdf29.name: Pitcher
1fe2bf0f-28b8-574f-bc6b-664e988fdf29.description2: Çanakkale was a pottery production centre between the end of 17th century and first quarter of the 20th century where pottery with interesting and original forms was produced. Mostly coarse red clay and occasionally beige-coloured paste was used. This jug with a pear-shaped body and long neck has green, brown, dark yellow, under-glazed purplish brown, dark blue and white decorations made by a brush. In front there is a single raised pattern of a flower. On either side there are painted flowers.

1ff4925b-b991-516d-9e19-a6960fbbbed1.name: *Marseille, view of the maritime port*
1ff4925b-b991-516d-9e19-a6960fbbbed1.description2: Marseille port meant that overtook Le Havre in terms of importance in the mid 19th century, as it became the first French port - and one of the largest international ports - to transport both people and goods. As the old harbour was not big enough to accommodate the growing number of ships and their increasingly important cargo new harbours were built, such as that in La Joliette.

2014af0a-f0bc-59a2-9a32-22eb77035668.name: Ferdinand I, Czar of Bulgaria (1861–1948)
2014af0a-f0bc-59a2-9a32-22eb77035668.keywords: Ferdinand I, Czar of Bulgaria; Sachsen-Coburg and Gotha
2014af0a-f0bc-59a2-9a32-22eb77035668.description2: Portrait of Ferdinand I (1861–1948) as Duke of Bulgaria. Ferdinand I was born as the son of the Austrian General August von Sachsen-Coburg and Gotha. In 1887 he became ruler of Bulgaria after the abdication of Alexander I von Battenberg. In 1908 he made himself Tsar of Bulgaria. Because he joined the German and Austrian monarchy in WWI and lost the war, he had to abdicate on 3 October 1918 and to emigrate to Germany and Slovakia. In 1948 Ferdinand I of Bulgaria died in Coburg, Germany.

201e230b-e913-5349-b14d-69a729ecf657.name: Disk
201e230b-e913-5349-b14d-69a729ecf657.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
201e230b-e913-5349-b14d-69a729ecf657.dates: New Kingdom (16th–11th century BC); discovered in 1824
201e230b-e913-5349-b14d-69a729ecf657.dimensions: Diameter 7.2 cm; length of the golden foil 4,6 cm; glass thickness 0,6 cm
201e230b-e913-5349-b14d-69a729ecf657.author: Marina Minozzi
201e230b-e913-5349-b14d-69a729ecf657.keywords: Egyptomania; Gaetano Rosellini; university; collector; photograph; anthropology; palaeoethnology; material culture; Florence; Pisa; Egyptology; Nubia; languages; hieroglyph; William Matthew Flinders Petrie; Jacques de Morgan; David Randall-MacIver
201e230b-e913-5349-b14d-69a729ecf657.description2: The disk in green glass with a golden square foil is considered of remarkable interest because of its label, attributed to Ippolito Rosellini, which proves that the relic was found inside a tomb in Thebes. Rosellini, one of the main figures of the Franco-Tuscan expedition in Egypt, wrote on it "Disco di vetro con entro una lamina d'oro. Trovato in una tomba a Tebe, Egitto, da I. Rosellini 1824 -dono di Elenina Ox Sicard, dicembre 1902". The relic was later acquired by Enrico Hillyer Giglioli. As a result of the excavations by W. Petrie and J. De Morgan, who documented the existence of an era preceding the 1st dynasty, Luigi Pigorini decided to expand the Egyptian archaeological collection in the "Museo Preistorico Etnografico e Kircheriano" which he directed at that time. In 1878 he began to acquire important groups, with the main body of the collection donated by David Randall-MacIver in 1901, after the excavations he carried out on the behalf of the Egypt Exploration Fund in the town of el-Amrah, Upper Egypt. Another major purchase — from the Italian Archaeological Mission in Egypt (excavations of Hammamiye) led by Ernesto Schiaparelli, director of the Egyptian Museum in Turin — followed in 1905. The last main acquisition took place in 1913 when the Egyptian objects from the Enrico Hillyer Giglioli’s collection entered the museum collection.

en: Cappozzo, M., “La collezione egizia del Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico ‘Luigi Pigorini’”, in *Bullettino di Paletnologia Italiana*, Roma, Istituto Poligrafico e Zecca dello Stato, (2005–2007), 96: 131–202, cat. 154.

204250dc-0aee-5c7b-a35b-e5449a289de5.name: Dish
204250dc-0aee-5c7b-a35b-e5449a289de5.description: In the 19th century, new forms and decorative styles began to appear on dishes from Fez, which are remarkable both for the colours used and their design. This dish, decorated with two sailing boats, resembles designs seen on ceramics from Izmir in Turkey.
204250dc-0aee-5c7b-a35b-e5449a289de5.keywords: Applied arts; craftsmanship; Moroccan craftsmanship; ceramic; Iznik; Ottoman influence; Ottoman art

204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.name: A Druse Bride from Lebanon
204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.author: Vito Lattanzi, Marina Minozzi
204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.keywords: Woman; photograph; anthropology; ethnology; geography; travel; exploration; scientific expedition; ethnography; museums; model; genre picture; portrait; representation of the other; costume; material culture; collection; Lebanon; Druze
204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.description2: The bride wears a tantur, a head ornament worn along with a white veil by the women from Antilibano. The photo belonging to Enrico H. Giglioli's collection was collected by the Florentine naturalist on his world travels in 1865 to 1868 as he advanced diplomatic and commercial affairs between the newborn Italian state and the other nations. The images seem to have been created spontaneously to show ethnocentric diversity. The ethnographic photographs in the Giglioli's collection are part of the historical archive of the Pigorini Museum and are important for the histories of anthropological science and photography. The origins of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome can be traced back to the 1875 foundation of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

20742252-5d4f-565f-8b1e-0849b9510ddd.name: Abdul-Mejid I, Sultan of Turkey (1823–1861)
20742252-5d4f-565f-8b1e-0849b9510ddd.keywords: Abdul-Mejid, Sultan of Turkey; Egypt; Syria, Palestine; Hungarian refugees
20742252-5d4f-565f-8b1e-0849b9510ddd.description2: Portrait of Abdul-Mejid I, Sultan of Turkey (1823–1861). When he came to power in 1839, he tried to re-occupy lands lost to Muhammad 'Ali, the ruler of Egypt. In this effort he was supported by Britain and Austria. In 1840 a combined British-Austrian fleet cut off the supply lines of the Egyptian army and forced the Egyptians to sign the 1840 Convention of Alexandria. Abdul-Mejid was able to win back Syria and Palestine. In 1849 he granted the Hungarian refugees exile. In 1861 he died and left his throne to his brother Abdülaziz.

2088a0e4-bb93-514d-9d8c-6b0a1e09ef8a.name: *The Necropolis, Petra, March 9th, 1839*

2088a0e4-bb93-514d-9d8c-6b0a1e09ef8a.description2: The Necropolis' of Petra appears in Volume 3 of 'The Holy Land, Syria, Idumea, Arabia, Egypt and Nubia' from drawings made on the spot by David Roberts, lithographed by Louis Haghe and published in six volumes by F.G. Moon in London between 1842-1845. Situated at the beginning of the steep ravine or siq that leads into the heart of Petra, both the so-called 'obelisk tomb' shown in the centre and the Triclinium situated to its lower right still exist today, even if much eroded since the days Roberts visited Petra in 1839. In the 19th century, Petra was one of Europe's most enduring Orientalist fascinations, but it also played a part in the region's more modern history. In October 1917, T. E. Lawrence, to divert Turkish military resources away from the British advance before the Third Battle of Gaza, led a small force of Syrians and Arabs in successfully defending Petra against a combined force of Turks and Germans. Bedouin women from the Petra area - under the leadership of their Sheikh's wife - were recruited to fight in the defense of the city.

20b75da3-3556-540c-a1f6-b0db4ca7d41f.name: A view of London
20b75da3-3556-540c-a1f6-b0db4ca7d41f.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
20b75da3-3556-540c-a1f6-b0db4ca7d41f.keywords: London; Buildings; Cathedrals; Streets; St Paul's Cathedral; Cityscapes; stereoscopic photography; stereoscope; stereograph
20b75da3-3556-540c-a1f6-b0db4ca7d41f.description2:
A stereograph is a pair of photographic images of the same subject taken from slightly different angles. This gives the illusion of a single three-dimensional image when viewed through a stereoscope designed to hold it. Stereographs were mass produced. Viewing them was a popular amusement carried out in the home from the 1850s until the early 20th century.  
This stereograph is from a series entitled 'Instantaneous Views of London'. The word 'instantaneous' reveals that an important selling-point for such photographs was that they quickly captured a moment in time. In this case the crowd and carriages of a busy London street are frozen in motion.

2107c2f5-2fd6-5b2a-8227-d2730838e6b4.name: École Polytechnique du Bardo
2107c2f5-2fd6-5b2a-8227-d2730838e6b4.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
2107c2f5-2fd6-5b2a-8227-d2730838e6b4.history: Founded in 1837 and opened on the 5 March 1840 by order of the bey, the École Polytechnique du Bardo was the first military academy in Ottoman Tunisia. Conscious of Christian Europe's military superiority and following the example of the Ottoman Tanzimat reforms, Ahmed Pacha Bey set out to "modernise" the state and the army. The school was directed by an Italian Orientalist, the Colonel Luigi Calligaris with the help of a Tunisian scholar, Sheikh Mahmoud Kabadu. The state was forced to shut down the school in 1868 due to lack of funds. It educated the first generation of Tunisian who weren't hostile to the West.
2107c2f5-2fd6-5b2a-8227-d2730838e6b4.description2: Located inside the Palais du Bardo, this school offered a six year course to any 15 to 20 year old student who could pass its rigorous selection process. The best students would then go on to complete their studies at the École Saint-Cyr in France. The English, French and Italian professors here taught sciences as well as literature and French and Italian. The top students had their first real test when they were called to fight in the Crimean war of October 1854, and later in the resistance to the French occupation in 1881. Today, the school is located opposite the Musée du Bardo, and has preserved is grandiose façade decorated with Italian marble and the beylical coat of arms.

21301784-a7a9-5271-b156-37a91e6af337.name: Ma'an Railway Station
21301784-a7a9-5271-b156-37a91e6af337.author: Mohammad Najjar
21301784-a7a9-5271-b156-37a91e6af337.history: In 1900-1908, Sultan Abdul Hamid with the help and support of Germany established a Railway between Damascus and Mecca (1700 km) to facilitate transporting the pilgrims. The track from Medina to Mecca (400 km) was never realized. The cost of the project was estimated at approximately 5 million Ottoman golden liras, which were provided from: private donations, revenues of the Ottoman State from the sale of stamps, and a special tax upon all citizens for the railway. Construction of the narrow-gauge track (105cm) began in 1900 with a wire telegraph line along its side connecting Damascus with Medina across Amman with a total track length of 1303 km. Official inaugurations of the tracks and stations were scheduled to coincide with the accession of the Sultan to the throne in the month of September every year. The construction of the project ended in 1908.
21301784-a7a9-5271-b156-37a91e6af337.keywords: Hijaz; railway; station; pilgrimage; hajj; pilgrimage route; communication; telegraph; Jordan; Damascus; Mecca; Makka; Amman; Zarqa; Qatranah; Ma'an; Amman; Tabuk; Arabian Peninsula; Ottoman; Abd al Hamid; Germany; Meinsner
21301784-a7a9-5271-b156-37a91e6af337.description2: Ma'an station was one of the most important stations along the Hijaz railway. It consists of several buildings parallel to the railway that include a passengers' hall, maintenance workshops, water towers and the residence of the German engineer Meinsner who was in charge for the construction of the Hijaz railway. With its various components including the rails, steam engines, bridges and stations, the project stands as an industrial, architectural and engineering statement that had a huge influence on Jordan. The Amman-Ma'an Section was completed in September 1904. The Ma'an-Tabuk Section was completed in September 1906.

213b0fb4-e0c5-55f3-9d6e-bd61b0fcc5ae.name: Ottoman Clothing Album

213b0fb4-e0c5-55f3-9d6e-bd61b0fcc5ae.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
213b0fb4-e0c5-55f3-9d6e-bd61b0fcc5ae.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

214be064-96bb-55b5-a13e-9888c7b4d009.name: Cup of early-Christian inspiration
214be064-96bb-55b5-a13e-9888c7b4d009.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
214be064-96bb-55b5-a13e-9888c7b4d009.author: Marina Minozzi
214be064-96bb-55b5-a13e-9888c7b4d009.keywords: Applied arts; minor arts; reproduction; model; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; motifs; collection; collector; glasswork; Murano glass; early Christian art; Romanticism; gold leaf; smoked glass
214be064-96bb-55b5-a13e-9888c7b4d009.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century. In the second half of the 19th century the tradition of Murano glass experienced a revival and a museum in Murano was created with an archive to offer models to artisans to copy. Objects included archaeological glasses of Phoenician, Egyptian, Alexandrian, Roman and Byzantine origin. Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. In Venice, one of the most popular glass factories was the Salviati Society, which was awarded with several prizes at National and International Exhibitions. The Venice-Murano Company made the smoked glass cup with gold leaf and biblical scenes (Inv. n.3046) recalling Early Christian tradition dating to the second half of the 19th century. Aquamarine glass and gold leaf medals are applied on the cup.

21713372-5487-5c79-91b5-f6b64a308116.name: Palais Kobbet el-Nhas
21713372-5487-5c79-91b5-f6b64a308116.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
21713372-5487-5c79-91b5-f6b64a308116.history: To the West of Bardo the fresh air and cultivated fields of the Manouba plain attracted royalty and nobility who were moving to their springtime residences. The presence of a revered saint, Lalla Manoubiya, added to the attraction of the area. The Palais Kobbet el-Nhas, built by Mohamed Errachid Bey (Muhammad al-Rashid Bey) c. 1756 and reorganised by Hammouda Pacha Bey in the late 19th century, is located amongst these residences. The palace itself is named after him, a reference to his brass domed pavilion which had originally been built for the beylical harem. The neighbouring Palais de la Rose, which seems to have been connected to it originally, is equally vast and luxurious.
21713372-5487-5c79-91b5-f6b64a308116.keywords: Architecture; art; painting; stucco; mosaic; marble; ceramics
21713372-5487-5c79-91b5-f6b64a308116.description2: This palace is located at the end of a great courtyard, lined with trees and featuring a large elevated façade and gallery, sitting above an annex, accessed via a grand staircase. The full beauty of this palace is evident even from the patio, which leads to a double driba (vestibule), with a vaulted ceiling embellished with Andalusian motifs carved in stucco, and paved with marble and decorated with earthenware tiles, which leads to a great hall. The wall decorations are made from luxurious earthenware and refined marble, and the floor is decorated as a black and white checkerboard. The domed ceilings, like the vaulted ceilings, are decorated with carved stucco with geometric and arabesque patterns. Other rooms are attached to every corner of this great hall, which, like the second reception hall in the right wing of the palace, has a wooden ceiling painted gold in an Italian style.

2186b4e6-4e67-5ef6-a1b9-1f095be746ab.name: Reconstruction of a late AH 13th – early 14th century / AD 19th – early 20th-century trading vessel
2186b4e6-4e67-5ef6-a1b9-1f095be746ab.holder: Sharjah Maritime Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
2186b4e6-4e67-5ef6-a1b9-1f095be746ab.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
2186b4e6-4e67-5ef6-a1b9-1f095be746ab.description2: This reconstruction of a *baghla* was commissioned by His Highness Dr Shaikh Sultan bin Mohammed Al Qasimi in 2004 to represent the most important and largest type of trading craft that plied the waters between the Gulf and India in the late 13th/ 19th century and the early 14th/ 20th century. Built by Emirati and Omani specialists, the vessel incorporates all the traditional elements of a baghla: a length of around 30 meters, two masts for lateen sails, its typically parrot-shaped stem head, its high square stern and its lavishly carved design. All these features were originally influenced by the design of Portuguese ships.

21983581-bf0c-5102-8ca7-8f1af359caf4.name: Muhammad Tawfiq Pasha (1852–1892)
21983581-bf0c-5102-8ca7-8f1af359caf4.keywords: Muhammad Tawfiq Pasha; Egypt; Arabi (Urabi) revolution; Great Britain
21983581-bf0c-5102-8ca7-8f1af359caf4.description2: Portrait of Muhammad Tawfiq Pasha (1852–1892). After the deposition of his father Ismail Pasha, Muhammad Tawfiq took over the government in Egypt. The Arabi revolution diminished his power radically. In 1882 he asked for help from Great Britain. British troops suppressed the Arabi revolution and occupied Egypt. Muhammad Tawfiq became ruler at the grace of the British government.

21b91c4b-40fa-5696-96fc-cfe01762acda.name: A Khorsabad barrel
21b91c4b-40fa-5696-96fc-cfe01762acda.dates: 721–705 BC (reign of Sargon II); discovered in 1851–1854
21b91c4b-40fa-5696-96fc-cfe01762acda.description2: During the archaeological mission led in Khorsabad by French consul Victor Place (1851–1854), fourteen Assyrian barrels were discovered. However, only four were preserved, since most of Place’s findings were lost in a shipwreck that took place in April 1855 on the Shatt el-Arab. As a reward for his archeological activity, the French government offered Place one of the barrels. Between 1855-1863 he was a consul in Moldavia, where he settled and started a family. In 1987 the Romanian state bought the barrel from one of Place’s descendants after the authorities found out that he was trying to sell it abroad. The barrel is made of clay, is nine-sided and bears an inscription recounting the reign of Assyrian king Sargon II, founder of a new capital, Dur-Sharrukin (Khorsabad).

21ba2a39-e5d5-58c6-a42b-e97edf24cfc5.name: Gold medal awarded to l'École Emile-Loubet
21ba2a39-e5d5-58c6-a42b-e97edf24cfc5.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
21ba2a39-e5d5-58c6-a42b-e97edf24cfc5.description2: This certificate for a gold medal was awarded to the vocational college l'École Emile-Loubet in Tunis at the Paris International Trade Fair in 1900 for the training it provided particularly in carpentry, metalwork and book binding. The school was founded in 1898 by 'Ali Bey for teaching the basics of manual occupations. The bey, accompanied by the French President, placed the first stone of its new building in 1900, which then became the Lycée Technique Emile-Loubet.

21cdc970-7b11-5dbd-a00e-75e0673ddd78.description2: "International Exhibition of Marina and Igiene Marinara. Italian colonial exhibition", organised in Genoa in 1914 and curated by the architect Gino Coppede. A copy of the famous Tower of Galata, built by some Genoese colonist in the namesake district of Constantinople in 1348, was constructed for this occasion. The aim of the exhibition was to inform the public about the colonies and the economic and commercial benefits brought by the colonies.

21cf7fa5-ac97-5097-8b52-ba4324bd02bd.name: Edward Dodwell, *View in Greece* (London 1830)
21cf7fa5-ac97-5097-8b52-ba4324bd02bd.description2: Edward Dodwell recorded the trasformation of the ancient Tower of the Winds into a dervish teke and in the early 19th century it wqas particularly popular with the travellers. Scenes from the city of Athens. Over the lintel, which faces the north-east, upon a red ground, is inscribed the Arabic *La Illah, Allah, Mahamed u resoul ullah* declaring there to be no God but God, and Muhammad to be his prophet. The wooden floor of the interior rests upon the lower cornice, many feet above the ancient pavement. The marble walls are washed with a uniform white. The *mihrab*, painted in perpendicular stripes of green and red, indicates by its position the direction of the Kaaba, or oratory of Mecca; each side of this is a wax candle, and the green flag of the prophet has also its place. The Qur'an is deposited within this niche, and an imitation of the two-edged sword of 'Ali is attached to the adjoining wall. Before these is performed the circularly whirling dance of the Dervishes, witnessing which, the spectator will find it as difficult to remain serious, as it would be dangerous to appear otherwise.

21d264d1-3d1b-5ec6-b7d4-e5b54eaaed68.name: *Bindallı entari*
21d264d1-3d1b-5ec6-b7d4-e5b54eaaed68.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
21d264d1-3d1b-5ec6-b7d4-e5b54eaaed68.dimensions: H (front): 128 c, h (back): 146 cm, sleeves: 49 cm
21d264d1-3d1b-5ec6-b7d4-e5b54eaaed68.description2: The attire of Ottoman women included dresses for the outdoors and the indoors. Starting from early 19th century, dresses called *üçetek* (dress with three skirts) and *dörtetek* (dress with four skirts) became fashionable. As relations with Europe increased, women in Istanbul started to use imported European textiles for their new dresses. This *entari* (dress) is made of purple velvet embroidered in the *bindallı* (dress that has embroidered flowers on the branches) style with garlands and flowers in vases in the *dival* (gold or silver embroidery on velvet) technique using silver-gilt thread. It has a short front opening, round neck and fitted sleeves. The skirt is widened by triangular gores and is longer at the back.

21dee5ec-7459-5915-8d20-a2fe4b38d5d8.name: Yıldız Palace State Apartments Kiosk
21dee5ec-7459-5915-8d20-a2fe4b38d5d8.notice: This is an unedited Database entry and may contain errors and inconsistencies in spelling. We are working to raise the funds required to complete the editing; should you wish to contribute please visit our [Support page](https://www.museumwnf.org/atrium_support.php).
21dee5ec-7459-5915-8d20-a2fe4b38d5d8.history:
Yildiz Palace, which is the last architectural example of Turkish Ottoman palace, is located on the Yildiz hill in the district of Besiktas. Sultan Ahmed I was the first to build a pavilion, over this land registered at the time to the Private treasury of the Ottoman Sultan as a hunting place sultans beginning during the reign of Suleiman the Magnificent (1520-1566).  
The main construction in the palace started in the period of Sultan Abdulhamid II (1876-1909) and it was called Saray-i Humayun (Central palace). During this period the palace comprised of buildings for private use of the sultan as well as buildings, allocated for the officials, repair shops and carpentry like repairing shop, carpenter’s shop and the buildings of culture and art such as theatre, museum and library. The Palace begun to serve as a museum under the name of “Directorate of the Museum of Yildiz Palace since 1993.
21dee5ec-7459-5915-8d20-a2fe4b38d5d8.architects: Balyan family – Sarkis Balyan (1835, Istanbul – 1899, Istanbul)
21dee5ec-7459-5915-8d20-a2fe4b38d5d8.description2: This is the most magnificent kiosk of the palace. It was commissioned by Sultan Abdulaziz in 1866 and built by the architects of Balyan family. The exterior siding of the kiosk is decorated with fluted and composite capitals, columns, corbel and sectional architraves. The inner plan of the kiosk is based on the old architectural tradition. It is famous with the Divanhane with pool downstairs and the stairs with the crystal handrails to the second floor. While the upper floor was used by the sultan, other sections were used by senior officials of the palace. Ghazi Osman Pasha, Commander of Plevne War served as Marshal of the Court in this building. Having served as the administration headquarters of the state during the reign of Sultan Abdulhamid II (1876-1909), the kiosk was used for important receptions and feasts both in the Ottoman Empire and after the Declaration of the Republic.

221db0e4-52d5-54d3-a7f0-9a52cbd932ad.name: Italian postcard of colonial propaganda: "Dawn of civilization"

221db0e4-52d5-54d3-a7f0-9a52cbd932ad.second_name: Italian postcard of colonial propaganda at the time of the Italo-Ottoman war of 1911–12 over Libya
221db0e4-52d5-54d3-a7f0-9a52cbd932ad.description2: This postcard explicitly states a key element of colonial propaganda: the notion that the colonisers brought “civilisation” to the newly conquered territories. Italian navy ships in the background are intended to convey the notion of Italy’s military might, but nothing reminds viewers of the violence of the colonial enterprise: the military man in the forefront does not carry weapons, but only the Italian flag.

22722c3a-12c3-54d0-9366-27dfa3fd737f.name: Banknote
22722c3a-12c3-54d0-9366-27dfa3fd737f.keywords: Egyptian currency; money minting; coin; paper money; Abbas Helmy II
22722c3a-12c3-54d0-9366-27dfa3fd737f.description2: 50 piasters from the days of Khedive `Abbas Hilmi II. During this time, a collection of Ottoman coins made of silver and copper circulated, valued at one, five and ten piasters. They were minted in AH 1327 / AD 1909 and bore the name of the Ottoman Sultan Muhammad V. However, the most important monetary event took place in 1898, when Khedive `Abbas Hilmi II granted a franchise to Raphael Suares to establish the National Bank of Egypt. This franchise gave him the right to produce securities that were accepted to pay domanial money, and the right to cash this money as gold upon demand.

2277531a-b3d9-5e52-886d-61cec9e4e5aa.name: Muslim soldiers of an Austro-Hungarian infantry-regiment from Bosnia-Herzegovina worshipping in a mosque
2277531a-b3d9-5e52-886d-61cec9e4e5aa.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
2277531a-b3d9-5e52-886d-61cec9e4e5aa.keywords: Bosnia; Islam; Austrian army; war; warfare
2277531a-b3d9-5e52-886d-61cec9e4e5aa.description2: After the occupation and eventual annexation of the two former Ottoman provinces of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the percentage of Muslims in the Austro-Hungarian Empire reached about 1.2 per cent of the total population by 1910. The quota of Muslim soldiers in the k.u.k. army reached 0.8 per cent.

229065fa-d12d-59dd-89b0-038e40916456.name: Beirut Railway Station
229065fa-d12d-59dd-89b0-038e40916456.description: This railway station, built during the Ottoman period, was the first railway station in Lebanon. It was a public station, intended for both for the transportation of passengers and trading goods.
229065fa-d12d-59dd-89b0-038e40916456.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury
229065fa-d12d-59dd-89b0-038e40916456.history: The Beirut-Damascus railway line, opened in 1895, was built across mountainous terrain to a 1,050 mm gauge. The second line from Riyaq to Aleppo, via Lebanon's eastern Beqaa valley, was also approved around this time. This was built to a standard gauge, even though it was only intended to provide a service between Damascus and Aleppo. The northern city of Tripoli was also connected via railway to Homs.
229065fa-d12d-59dd-89b0-038e40916456.keywords: Commerce; Train station; Railway; Transportation; Trading
229065fa-d12d-59dd-89b0-038e40916456.architects: “Société des chemins de fer Ottomans économique de Beyrouth-damas-Hauran”

22b59916-1001-5666-873e-2d7a62f3d991.name: *Keswa kabbous (wedding outfit)*
22b59916-1001-5666-873e-2d7a62f3d991.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
22b59916-1001-5666-873e-2d7a62f3d991.keywords: Wedding outfit; embroidery with silver thread.
22b59916-1001-5666-873e-2d7a62f3d991.description2: Worn by the bride during the wedding ceremony, the keswa kabous el-Jaraq weighs more than ten kilograms. It consists of a large, billowing pair of trousers secured at the waist by a tekka (similar to a ribbon), with a matching top, short enough to leave the waist uncovered, both made of silk taffeta. Its air of great wealth and elegance comes particularly from the contrast between the floral motifs, embroidered with a flat silver thread, and the sequins, also sewn on with a gold and silver thread. When worn by a seated bride, the trousers resemble a large hoop-skirt, connected to a low-necked bodice, which together give the impression of being a robe de cour (grand habit). The upper section of these trousers, hemmed at the waist but open at the front, consists of almost four metres of fabric, and the legs alone have a circumference of one and a half metres and are a metre long. The end of the legs is hemmed with some robust percale fabric, which contains the hemming and rises up the leg to create an even larger swell around the ankle.

22ba355b-61ed-56c7-97f9-3b2325767140.name: *The Railway Station at Jaffa*
22ba355b-61ed-56c7-97f9-3b2325767140.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
22ba355b-61ed-56c7-97f9-3b2325767140.archival: Jewry afterwards Valentine, Laura, *Palestine Past and Present. Pictorial and descriptive ... Illustrated, etc*, London: F. Warne & Co, 1893, p. 77
22ba355b-61ed-56c7-97f9-3b2325767140.keywords: Pilgrimage; pilgrims; Christian pilgrimage; Jewish pilgrimage; Palestine; Holy Land; Jerusalem; sacred places; travel; travel book;railway; communication; French company; local Jewish community; Ottoman Jews; Joseph Navon; Ottoman Palestine
22ba355b-61ed-56c7-97f9-3b2325767140.description2: *The Railway Station at Jaffa* is a drawing included in the book *Palestine Past and Present* by Laura Jewry Valentine. In the chapters about Jaffa and Jerusalem, the description of the geography, religious history and climate focuses on the route of the Jaffa–Jerusalem railway. It provides an interesting report on this communication route, built by the French and opened on September 1892, connecting Jaffa to Jerusalem and various villages in between.

22dc6a43-58e7-5410-b11f-2c3a946ecbb5.name: St. Cyprien. Post office. School.
22dc6a43-58e7-5410-b11f-2c3a946ecbb5.second_name: Société des Fermes Françaises de Tunisie
22dc6a43-58e7-5410-b11f-2c3a946ecbb5.description2: French agriculture in Tunisia began either through the establishment of large properties by private initiatives, or the introduction of settlers by the public authorities. This photograph shows us an example from the "first phase" - one of the "companies" (of "French farms") had purchased a large plot of land, and employed a number of (largely Arab and Italian) workers to cultivate the land.  Pictured is a school, whose director also worked as the post officer, a vital service for those who wished to communicate with their families back home.

22e62379-2fd3-551c-8a81-3883d3d21495.name: The biweekly paper *Spettatore Egiziano* was the first Italian-language newspaper to be published in Egypt
22e62379-2fd3-551c-8a81-3883d3d21495.author: Massimo Sanacore
22e62379-2fd3-551c-8a81-3883d3d21495.archival: ASLi, Governo civile e militare, b. 451
22e62379-2fd3-551c-8a81-3883d3d21495.third_name: *Spettatore egiziano. Giornale politico, scientifico, letterario e commerciale*
22e62379-2fd3-551c-8a81-3883d3d21495.description2:
The *Spettatore Egiziano* was founded in 1845 by Giacomo Castelnuovo, a Jewish medical doctor from Livorno (Tuscany, Italy) who had to flee his country in 1843 because of his affiliation to the Giovane Italia (the Italian patriotic and republican movement created by Giuseppe Mazzini). The *Spettatore Egiziano* was the first Italian-language newspaper to be published in Egypt. Castelnuovo also founded the *Il Progresso d’Egitto*, a bulletin that kept the Italian community in Egypt updated about the Italian political events like the 1848 revolutions.  
Castelnuovo later moved to Tunis where he became the Bey's physician.

235e2dec-25cb-5d30-8fea-a6de9c3f6d26.name: *The Attack on the Fort of Luft, November 27, 1809*
235e2dec-25cb-5d30-8fea-a6de9c3f6d26.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
235e2dec-25cb-5d30-8fea-a6de9c3f6d26.dimensions: 505 mm x 602 mm (framed); image: 218 mm x 355 mm
235e2dec-25cb-5d30-8fea-a6de9c3f6d26.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
235e2dec-25cb-5d30-8fea-a6de9c3f6d26.artist: R. Temple, HM 65th Regiment, Sixteen views; I. Clark, Sculpt.; William Haines, Publisher
235e2dec-25cb-5d30-8fea-a6de9c3f6d26.description2: This depiction shows the fortress of Luft, one of the Qawasim strongholds on the island of Qishm in the Gulf, being attacked by British forces armed with long muskets. Several large dhows are burning in the foreground, while the smoke from defending gunfire can be seen emanating from the loopholes of the fortress. Local fighters are seen lined up along the top the fortress walls and towers.  After having sacked Ras al Khaimah on the Arabian side of the Gulf, the British proceeded to rout out all remaining Qawasim strongholds on the Persian coast, including those on Qishm island. On the 26th of November 1809, the British reached Luft, and after futile negotiations with the local Qawasim representative, they attacked by sea and land. Despite brave and consistent defence which led to heavy British casualties, the fort was taken, all dhows destroyed and the resident Sheikkh exiled.

2380f8f7-c82d-5b63-945d-edf979f223ee.name: Appraisal by the assessor of the Tribunal of Booty (Tribunale delle prede) of Palermo, of 25 'Turks of the Barbary Coast' captured by Italian corsairs from the Kingdom of Sicily and detained in Palermo
2380f8f7-c82d-5b63-945d-edf979f223ee.author: Renata De Simone
2380f8f7-c82d-5b63-945d-edf979f223ee.archival: ASPa, Consultore del Governo, Tribunale delle prede, vol. 268, carte senza numerazione
2380f8f7-c82d-5b63-945d-edf979f223ee.description2: In this document the assessor of the Booty Tribunal of Palermo explains that the magistrate has declared the booty captured by the captain corsair Domenico Pantò e Trifone Citarrella to be legitimate; they had plundered a Turkish boat and captured 25 Turks from the Barbary Coast. Upon request of the ship-owner, the assessor has been charged to appraise the value of the captives, so that they could be sold at auction. The captives included an entire family of “Barbary Turks”, composed of Salem, “husband” (60 years old, valued at 60 piastres), Cadduccia, “mother” (48 years old, 80 piastres), Agmet, “brother” (24 years old, 80 piastes), Lima, a 21 year old widow with her 2 year old son Ali, together valued at 100 piastres, and a 14 year old black servant called Fatuma, valued at only 20 piastres. Seven of the other captives were sailors, aged from 23 to 60 years old and valued a price ranging from 25 to 50 piastres, and two were passengers, whose commercial value was estimated at between 30 and 40 piastres.

23c0eaa7-284e-5a97-9ac8-8edafc208719.name: A petition to collect signatures in support of an appeal to the Italian parliament to grant women the right to vote, drawn up by Anna Maria Mozzoni
23c0eaa7-284e-5a97-9ac8-8edafc208719.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
23c0eaa7-284e-5a97-9ac8-8edafc208719.author: Rosanna De Longis
23c0eaa7-284e-5a97-9ac8-8edafc208719.description2:
With this appeal, Anna Maria Mozzoni and other women asked members of parliament to leave aside “academic digressions” on women’s nature and on their “mission” and to “consider we \[women\] only in our relation to the State, for what we really are: citizens, taxpayers, and able” who deserved the right to vote.  
Italian women’s campaign to get the right to vote gained momentum at the end of the 19th century and beginning of the 20th but it wasn’t successful until 1946.  
Anna Maria Mozzoni was the most brilliant Italian feminist activist of the second half of the 19th century. She authored books, founded journals and associations, and incessantly campaigned in favour of women’s rights.
