23d98ad7-7f2d-5f3d-a18a-862042cf2b0c.name: The Ottoman Clock Tower
23d98ad7-7f2d-5f3d-a18a-862042cf2b0c.author: Julien El Khoury, Jeff El-Msanne
23d98ad7-7f2d-5f3d-a18a-862042cf2b0c.history: This clock tower was built by Yussef Afimus in 1897 neara the Grand Serail to celebrate the 10th anniversary of the Ottoman sultan 'Abd al-Hamid II's coronation. It was seen as an important tower, indicating Muslim prayer time as well as making up for the absence of a public clock tower in the city, as many private foreign institutions in Beirut had built Western style clock towers in recent years. The construction of the clock tower was approved by the sultan following a letter of supplication from Beirut's governor Rashid Bey. The ceremonial laying of the first stone took place on 9 January 1897 (the anniversary of the sultan) in the presence of high officials, military representatives and members of the municipality of Beirut.
23d98ad7-7f2d-5f3d-a18a-862042cf2b0c.description2: At 25 metres tall, the Hamidiye clock tower was the tallest structure in Beirut at the time of its completion. Similar towers were consequently built in imitation in numerous other cities of the Ottoman Empire, such as Istanbul, Izmir, Izmit, Adana, Jaffa, Nablus, Acre and Tripoli. It was built using local stone: Beirut sandstone, Jounieh limestone, Damascene basalt and Deir al-Qamar red stone. The tower houses a huge bell weighing 300kg on its third floor, and a set of 125 cast iron steps leading up to it. Four miniature orientalist-style balconies adorn this floor. Above these balconies are four large clock faces imported especially from the Ottoman embassy in France.

23e1371d-e17b-5b84-a037-47dc18e8eb2f.name: *Qittan*
23e1371d-e17b-5b84-a037-47dc18e8eb2f.description2: A very rare piece purchased from Sheikh Sa\`ud in 2002. This was his personal *thawb* and he said he found wearing it very relaxing. Called *qittan*, which means 'cord', the piece is embroidered around the neck up until the ends of sleeves, with silk thread. It also contains silk ball buttons.

240766f1-2bff-5c21-abf7-80992ebf2e6a.description2: On the occasion of the International Exhibition of Rome in 1911, the complex of the "Baths of Diocletian” was restored under the direction of the archeologist and topographer Rodolfo Lanciani. The site housed the Archaeological Exhibition dedicated to the Roman culture in the Imperial Era with a particular interest for its positive influence on the ex provinces. Every single nation participated through original reproductions of archaeological materials, often lost. The photo shows material evidence and casts coming from Spain.

24203624-e517-513d-988d-06f0d9b1828a.name: 1 May 1911, a sprig of lily of the valley
24203624-e517-513d-988d-06f0d9b1828a.description2: The roots of 'labour day' go back to the 19th century, when strikers campaigned for an 8-hour working day. The events quickly escalated, and came to a head in Fourmies, France, in 1891. From then on, labour day protesters began wearing a red flower on the first of May in memory of their fallen comrades. This flower was later replaced by a sprig of lily of the valley in Île-de-France, which also commemorates the start of spring.

24505a53-36c5-5b4a-9423-5215da35cb9b.name: *The Café des Platanes*
24505a53-36c5-5b4a-9423-5215da35cb9b.author: Dalila Orfali

24505a53-36c5-5b4a-9423-5215da35cb9b.description2: This famous café is located by a fountain bearing the same name, built by the Dey Hassan. From 1832 it faced the Jardin d'Essai, giving it a view of this beautiful green space in the Hamma neighbourhood. This café and its fountain were immortalised by a number of painters. Various 17th century texts recall its peaceful atmosphere.

248b6ee3-8b98-5fe8-a126-461e9a621403.author: Giulia Barrera

248b6ee3-8b98-5fe8-a126-461e9a621403.description2: The Italian community in Tunisia participated in the 1906 Milan international exhibition. The Committee in charge of organizing exhibition participation included Italian professionals and entrepreneurs who had migrated from Italy to Tunisia or who were children or grandchildren of immigrants, such as Alfredo Coen (owner of the furniture shop “Au Palais Arabe” and of a furniture factory), G. Di Vittorio and L. Rey (owners of constructions companies that built important public and private buildings, Di Vittorio, from Sicily, Rey, the child of an immigrant from Piedmont), Ugo Moreno (a trader, whose the family had migrated from Livorno in 1830) and Doctor Pietro Brignone (who ran a pharmacy in Tunis).

24e0347f-f9f3-5254-ba16-aef618e16ba6.name: Flag
24e0347f-f9f3-5254-ba16-aef618e16ba6.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
24e0347f-f9f3-5254-ba16-aef618e16ba6.author: Huda Kilani
24e0347f-f9f3-5254-ba16-aef618e16ba6.description2: A piece of green Syrian silk fabric, inset on the top of the mast, which used to be carried during religious ceremonies. Trade and crafts were common activities in Jordan between the late 19th century and the earlier 20th century. These activities depended on migration and attracted groups of people who travelled or settled in the Jordanian territory to produce or sell products. Thus, the exchange of goods among different areas was very common, as exemplified by this object and many traditional dresses. Silk textiles were very common products in the Jordanian and Palestinian areas and were purchased from Syria, being an element in local fashion, both in Jordan and in Palestine.

25019945-0006-566a-b1cc-e378a23e92ea.name: Farrokh Khan, Persian ambassador
25019945-0006-566a-b1cc-e378a23e92ea.description2: Diplomatic relations between France and Persia were strained at the beginning of the 19th century, so Persia began to turn more and more to Great Britain. However, following a disagreement with Great Britain over the city of Herat, Persia re-established its diplomatic relationship with France. The ambassador Farrokh Khan was sent to Paris in the midst of the Anglo-Persian war (1856–57), and Napoléon III's diplomatic aid led to the Treaty of Paris (1857) and successfully ended the conflict. Félix Nadar, one of the most famous portrait photographers in Paris, photographed Farrokh Khan for the occasion.

251b2b7e-e8f3-5697-9d6d-a33a6facc5ca.name: *Details and ornaments from the Alhambra by Owen Jones, Architect*
251b2b7e-e8f3-5697-9d6d-a33a6facc5ca.description: The influence of the Islamic art also arrived through different publications as the well-known Owen Jones's books and the pieces displayed in the International Exhibitions, as in the first one in London where Owen Jones displayed the Lion fountain of the Alhambra Palace in a building dedicated to master works of art. This book was well-known for many of the Orientalist artists as an example for decoration and the use of the colour.

257442d0-cc8b-5f59-9bdf-31aeac1cd79c.name: Postcard of Khan Antoun Bey Square
257442d0-cc8b-5f59-9bdf-31aeac1cd79c.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
257442d0-cc8b-5f59-9bdf-31aeac1cd79c.keywords: Postcard; Khan; Souk; Trade; Economy; Beirut
257442d0-cc8b-5f59-9bdf-31aeac1cd79c.description2: Located next to the port, the Khan Antoun Bey Square was the entrance to the city for those arriving by sea. By the 19th century the *khan* itself, pictured here, housed trading offices on the ground and first floors and foreign consulates on the upper floors. The inner courtyard was used to park the consuls' horse-drawn carriages.

25a67385-d901-5896-a204-90f0be3423ed.name: Cartoon
25a67385-d901-5896-a204-90f0be3423ed.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
25a67385-d901-5896-a204-90f0be3423ed.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
25a67385-d901-5896-a204-90f0be3423ed.keywords: French protectorate; resistance; occupation; cartoon; caricature
25a67385-d901-5896-a204-90f0be3423ed.description2: This cartoon, which criticised the French invasion of Tunisia, appeared in the satirical magazine L'Epoca on 1–2 August 1881. The French consul in Tunisia, Théodore Roustan, is depicted as the new ruler of Tunisia, under the tile "His Royal Highness Roustan 1st", and holds the ruling bey Sadok Pacha on a leash.

25cc99b8-ea3d-5a36-aad3-2fdf4e0f6ac5.name: Wedgwood ‘drabware’
25cc99b8-ea3d-5a36-aad3-2fdf4e0f6ac5.description2: Illustrates the influence of Egyptian motifs on Victorian ceramics. Part of the second wave of Egyptianisation, related to the construction of the Suez Canal.

261e731d-c1f3-5549-9d76-8e6eb76876e3.name: Alexander I Obrenovic, King of Serbia (1876–1903)
261e731d-c1f3-5549-9d76-8e6eb76876e3.description2: Portrait of Alexander I Obrenovic, King of Serbia (1876–1903) as a young man. Between the abdication of his father in 1889 and his proclamation as a king in 1893, his mother Natalija Obrenovic ruled as a regent. Being a close ally of Austria, he became Serbian King in 1893. In 1894 Alexander abolished the liberal constitution of Serbia. In 1900 he married Draga Masin, a former lady-in-waiting of his mother. This marriage was very unpopular and weakened the political position of the king. In 1903 he and his wife were murdered by a group of Serbian officers.

2648874b-264b-5142-94b8-f20ea33a01b4.name: Fan
2648874b-264b-5142-94b8-f20ea33a01b4.description: Historical fans were popular accessories in the second half of the 19th century, especially those commemorating important public events such as North Africans wars. These everyday objects as fans would serve as tools to disseminate political or social ideas. The employment of lithography applied to the leaf tells us of the propaganda use of the engraving and its application to the decorative arts. This fan is an example of it, because it shows the Spanish army helping the people from the villages in Spanish territory of North Africa (Morocco).
2648874b-264b-5142-94b8-f20ea33a01b4.author: Mercedes Rodríguez Collado
2648874b-264b-5142-94b8-f20ea33a01b4.materials: Double paper-leaf printed; ribs: mother-of-pearl; fretwork, gilt, carved, lithography, painted

2669ff94-bd70-55d1-a06b-cc0cbefd980d.name: The Great Mosque and University of Zaytuna
2669ff94-bd70-55d1-a06b-cc0cbefd980d.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
2669ff94-bd70-55d1-a06b-cc0cbefd980d.history: Located in the heart of the Tunis medina, the great Zaytuna Mosque is the largest and most revered religious site in Tunis. City life revolved around this mosque, as it was not only an important place of worship, but also a great university, with a reputation matching that of the Qaraouyine University in Fez and the al-Azhar University in Cairo. Many theologians and scholars of literature, arts and sciences were trained here for generations. Although it was the subject of many reforms in the 19th century, the modern Zaytuna University still provides a religious education, and attracts many believers at prayer times.
2669ff94-bd70-55d1-a06b-cc0cbefd980d.description2: An important place of worship, the Zaytuna mosque was subject to a great number of adjustments and expansions since its construction in the 7th century, most notably during the 17th and 18th centuries. The central courtyard is accessible through a suspended portico with horseshoe archways resting on beautiful columns topped with Hafsid capitals, through which the beautiful painted wooden ceilings can be seen. The paved courtyard is dominated by a square minaret, a beautiful sundial and a ribbed calotte which rests on an octagonal base above on a larger, square base. The décor is reminiscent of the Dome of the Rock in al-Quds (Jerusalem) in Palestine.

26bb48d2-0468-5e95-b709-f3f74817bef6.name: Man's trousers (*Chakshiri*)
26bb48d2-0468-5e95-b709-f3f74817bef6.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
26bb48d2-0468-5e95-b709-f3f74817bef6.description2: There used to be around fifty diverse styles of folk costumes worn in different ethnic areas throughout Macedonia in the 19th century and in the early 20th century. Among the most prominent were the costumes of Gorni Polog. Unlike the diverse and numerous women’s garments, men’s outfits were much simpler and rather unified. These men's trousers of white canvas are decorated plainly with black braids.

26d5c466-64f0-57e3-823b-ed86f67a2c66.name: A postcard of Italian colonial propaganda
26d5c466-64f0-57e3-823b-ed86f67a2c66.description: The Roman Empire once ruled over the entire coastal area of North Africa. This postcard explicitly links the Italian colonial conquest of Libya in 1911-12 with ancient Roman rule over the same territory. It suggests that the Italian Kingdom was the legitimate heir of the Roman Empire and had an historic right to rule over Libya. Especially during Fascism, Italian colonial propaganda often referred to the Roman Empire in order to legitimize Italian expansionist policy.

26e9ef4b-0b68-5435-8e38-53a259f9cdaf.name: Portrait of Prosper Enfantin dressed in an imitation of the local style
26e9ef4b-0b68-5435-8e38-53a259f9cdaf.description2: Prosper Enfantin (1796–1864) was one of the most active members of the Saint-Simonian movement (a socio-economic and political movement advocating a fraternal, socialist society based on economic prosperity). After being imprisoned in 1832 for founding a very politically-active community, Enfantin became fascinated by the Middle East, and in 1834 he left for Egypt with a few companions. He was also one of the proponents of the Suez Canal. In this image he is dressed in the local Egyptian style, wearing clothes he made himself.

26ea850d-69fb-528e-98a1-2e8e7c4ad533.name: Glass scent vessel
26ea850d-69fb-528e-98a1-2e8e7c4ad533.description2: Glass produced in Bohemia with a strong Middle Eastern influence. Acquired by Franks.

26fd8fdd-9bc0-5670-be93-f86c07c23383.name: Dresser
26fd8fdd-9bc0-5670-be93-f86c07c23383.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
26fd8fdd-9bc0-5670-be93-f86c07c23383.description2: This wooden dresser contains four large drawers and one thin upper drawer. It is topped with a marble slab and rectangular mirror in a wooden frame, decorated with a wooden crest and carved with floral patterns. The wood is covered in a mosaic of bone or ceramic pieces, organised in a floral design. Each drawer has a keyhole and is opened by two individually painted knobs.

2711a503-9f23-5282-b34a-bc7b254979eb.name: Outline map of Damascus in 1918
2711a503-9f23-5282-b34a-bc7b254979eb.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
2711a503-9f23-5282-b34a-bc7b254979eb.author: Stefan Weber
2711a503-9f23-5282-b34a-bc7b254979eb.second_name: Indicating urban growth to the fin de siecle
2711a503-9f23-5282-b34a-bc7b254979eb.description2: Damascus, now the political and cultural centre of Syria, is one of the world’s oldest continuously inhabited cities. The design of its living spaces and the organization of urban society were always connected to the culture of its inhabitants. Damascus’ geographical space reflects this “spatial turn”: Its public spaces were clearly shaped and influenced by the diverse social, historical and cultural structures and events, which contributed to the vitality of Damascus’ multilayered Urban Design.

27238194-345e-5c00-b880-860d50c950cf.name: The trademark for Chocolat des Pyramides produced by the company Talmone, based in Turin (Italy)
27238194-345e-5c00-b880-860d50c950cf.author: Margherita Martelli
27238194-345e-5c00-b880-860d50c950cf.archival: ACS, Ministero dell’Industria, del Commercio e dell’Artigianato, Ufficio Italiano Brevetti e Marchi, Serie Marchi, Fasc. 284
27238194-345e-5c00-b880-860d50c950cf.third_name: *Chocolat des Pyramides*, cioccolato, Ditta Michele Talmone, Torino
27238194-345e-5c00-b880-860d50c950cf.description2: The Talmone chocolate factory was founded in Turin in 1850. In 1929 merged with Venchi.

272951dc-4e51-55bc-bf53-6fb35a332aa6.name: Joint-stock company for iron, steel and railroad materials “Ferrotaie”. Factory for steel and railroad materials of Vado Ligure [Genoa, Italy]. Women working at milling machines
272951dc-4e51-55bc-bf53-6fb35a332aa6.author: Cristina Mosillo, Giulia Barrera
272951dc-4e51-55bc-bf53-6fb35a332aa6.archival: ACS, Ministero armi e munizioni, Ufficio storiografico della mobilitazione civile e industriale, Archivio fotografico, fasc. 112, foto 1516, neg. 3325B
272951dc-4e51-55bc-bf53-6fb35a332aa6.third_name: Soc. An. Italiana per materiali siderurgici e ferroviari 'Ferrotaie'. Stabilimento per meteriali siderurgici e ferroviari di Vado Ligure (GE). Operaie alla fresatrice
272951dc-4e51-55bc-bf53-6fb35a332aa6.description2:
Women working in a steel and iron factory that produced materials of strategic value. The war had an important impact on women’s work. As historian Perry Willson pointed out, during WWI “women rarely directly substituted for men, instead tending to move into new work roles produced by wartime expansion.”  
In Italy, the number of women who worked in factories producing weapons and ammunitions rose from 23,000 in 1915 to 198,000 in 1918. Those numbers were far less than the women who participated in war production with more traditional “female roles”, such as making uniforms (400,000) or knitting woollen garments for the soldiers (200,000). However, Willson explained, women working in weapons’ factories had a relevance “as symbolic harbinger of change that greatly outweighed their actual numbers.”

en: Willson, Perry R., *Women in Twentieth-century Italy*, New York: Palgrave Macmillan, 2010.

272aabb1-2d59-5faa-9ce5-a28c1305a906.name: Brass head of flagpole
272aabb1-2d59-5faa-9ce5-a28c1305a906.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
272aabb1-2d59-5faa-9ce5-a28c1305a906.author: Huda Kilani
272aabb1-2d59-5faa-9ce5-a28c1305a906.description2: This mast, made of casted brass, bears an Arabic calligraphic decoration with the inscription "Oh God, Oh Muhammad". It is fixed on a pointed piece of copper with a hole at the bottom to install on a long wooden staff. In religious festivities such as pilgrimage, various activities were organized. They would normally include festivals and rallies under flags and standards. The heads of flagstaffs were decorated with metallic items usually with Arabic calligraphy and some cosmic signs such as the crescent and the star.

2739eecb-f1a1-5544-8ead-dcf31ff17148.name: An elderly Paul Draneht (1815–94) with his daughter Despina
2739eecb-f1a1-5544-8ead-dcf31ff17148.author: Massimiliano Cremona, Ignazio Galella
2739eecb-f1a1-5544-8ead-dcf31ff17148.description2: In 1894, Paul Draneht, who had been awarded the title of Pasha, died in Alexandria. His daughter Despina married a Greek businessman, Emmanuel Zervudachi, and the family continued to be part of a Mediterranean cosmopolitan elite.

274e910c-7ec1-5f20-8460-292341da7d08.name: Headdress
274e910c-7ec1-5f20-8460-292341da7d08.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
274e910c-7ec1-5f20-8460-292341da7d08.author: Huda Kilani
274e910c-7ec1-5f20-8460-292341da7d08.keywords: silver chains; coins; decorated; Ottoman coins; Venice coins
274e910c-7ec1-5f20-8460-292341da7d08.description2: Three silver chains formed into a hat with beaded frontispiece decorated with coins. On the back, a long fabric with gold and silver Ottoman and Venice coins. Silver jewellery was the most common, because only rich people could afford gold jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom. The Jordanian economy relied on trades and crafts and new waves of people started to come to Jordan and began to settle for these purposes. This object is an example of how traditional fashion reflected the variegated population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is also an example of local personal attire, fashion, costumes and rites.

2750ade6-0ba3-536b-a712-3d37388d9bf1.name: *Nuit d'Orient*. \[waltz for piano, op. 11\]
2750ade6-0ba3-536b-a712-3d37388d9bf1.artist: Illustrator: Léonce Burret; composer: P. Bermalty
2750ade6-0ba3-536b-a712-3d37388d9bf1.description2: Musical composers' fascination with the "Orient" manifested itself in their music and their titles. The "harem" had intrigued Westerners for a long time.

275443d0-1d7d-5e19-a7ef-50820f9add5d.name: *Convoy of pilgrims*
275443d0-1d7d-5e19-a7ef-50820f9add5d.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
275443d0-1d7d-5e19-a7ef-50820f9add5d.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph pilgrims; pilgrimage; travelling
275443d0-1d7d-5e19-a7ef-50820f9add5d.description2: The Hijaz Railway was a narrow-gauge railway (1,050mm/​3ft, 5 11⁄32 in track gauge) that ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. It got no further than Medina, 400 kilometres (250mi) short of Mecca, due to the construction interruption caused by the outbreak of World War I. The main purpose of the railway was to establish a connection between Constantinople, the capital of the Ottoman Empire and the seat of the Islamic Caliphate, and Hijaz in Arabia, the site of the holiest shrines of Islam and the holy city of Mecca, the destination of the Hajj (annual pilgrimage).

275bf73d-6170-5205-804c-fbb1ff637342.name: Yıldız Tile Imperial Factory
275bf73d-6170-5205-804c-fbb1ff637342.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
275bf73d-6170-5205-804c-fbb1ff637342.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ancient Istanbul; yıldız tile; ceramic; factories
275bf73d-6170-5205-804c-fbb1ff637342.description2: The Yıldız Tile Imperial Factory was founded by Sultan Abdülhamid II (1876-1909) in the early 1890’s in the garden of Yıldız Palace for the purposes of arousing, reshaping and stimulating the Turkish tiling art. The factory, which began manufacturing immediately, was damaged in the earthquake of 1894 and in the same year, it was nearly reconstructed by Italian Architect Raimondo d’Aronco.

278b5403-b655-504e-adcb-106a2c42eaad.name: Ratification document of the Congress of Vienna (29 September 1814 – 9 June 1815)
278b5403-b655-504e-adcb-106a2c42eaad.description2: At the Congress of Vienna (29 September 1814 to 9 June 1815), Austria fully restored its position as one of the great powers in Europe. It renounced the former Austrian territories in the Netherlands and South Germany and regained a number of North Italian possessions. The Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia, together with smaller North Italian territories like Tuscany, Modena, Piacenza, Parma and Guastalla – which came under control of Habsburg Archdukes – confirmed Austrian predominance in Northern and Central Italy.

279d0dc2-0ffe-5cf8-89f7-8199c9c7ec9a.name: *Fantasy in Egyptian Gallery, the British Museum*
279d0dc2-0ffe-5cf8-89f7-8199c9c7ec9a.description2: Fantasy in Egyptian Gallery, the British Museum, by Duncan. A group of sculptures come to life. Closely modelled on the sculptures displayed in the British Museum. Assyrianising figures at rear left. At front right Ry yawns and rubs his eye.

279e1f50-df40-5f44-a5e0-e9a46ddf29b7.name: Bridal coat (*Klashenik*)
279e1f50-df40-5f44-a5e0-e9a46ddf29b7.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
279e1f50-df40-5f44-a5e0-e9a46ddf29b7.keywords: klashenik; broad cloth; textile; embroidery; costume; wedding; marriage
279e1f50-df40-5f44-a5e0-e9a46ddf29b7.materials: Thick twill-weave woollen fabric decorated with braids
279e1f50-df40-5f44-a5e0-e9a46ddf29b7.description2: A *klashenik* is a kind of over-garment in varying lengths and split on the front made of thick woollen broadcloth called *klashna*. This knee-length piece comes from the Veles Region. It is abundantly adorned with embroidery above the lower hem and at the breasts. Embroidery was an inevitable part of decorating the majority of Macedonian folk costumes. The exquisite, meticulously executed embroidery applied on this tunic makes it a real work of art.

27b52e92-40ef-53b5-9de2-ba320998fdf0.name: Lisbon Astronomical Observatory
27b52e92-40ef-53b5-9de2-ba320998fdf0.holder: National Museum of Natural History and Science (MUHNAC) / Museums of the University of Lisbon
27b52e92-40ef-53b5-9de2-ba320998fdf0.author: António Perestrelo de Matos (MUHNAC-UL), Marta C. Lourenço (MUHNAC-UL)
27b52e92-40ef-53b5-9de2-ba320998fdf0.history: The Observatory was constructed with the support and sponsorship of King Pedro V (1837–1861). It began operating in 1867 and its first director was Frederico Oom, followed by Campos Rodrigues (1836–1919), an internationally recognised astronomer and a creator of several scientific instruments. In 1995, the Observatory integrated the University of Lisbon.
27b52e92-40ef-53b5-9de2-ba320998fdf0.keywords: Observatory; Scientific Heritage; Astronomy; National Museum of Natural History and Science; University of Lisbon
27b52e92-40ef-53b5-9de2-ba320998fdf0.architects: Architects: Jean François Gille Colson, José da Costa Sequeira (1800–1872), Valentim José Correia (1822–1900); Engineer: Frederico Augusto Oom (1830–1890)
27b52e92-40ef-53b5-9de2-ba320998fdf0.description2: The Lisbon Astronomical Observatory is the Portuguese national observatory. It has the legal responsibility of national timekeeping. It is located in the Tapada da Ajuda, a green area in the west of Lisbon. It is part of the Museums of the University of Lisbon/National Museum of Natural History and Science. It includes several buildings. It promotes activities regarding the public understanding of astronomy and astrophysics for diverse audiences. The Observatory has important collections: scientific instruments, mostly from the 19th and early 20th century; a Library, which is reference in Portugal, and an important historical archive.

27bffbe0-bf77-51b6-87f3-1667b65ae607.name: *The Ruins of the Temple of the Sun at Baalbec*
27bffbe0-bf77-51b6-87f3-1667b65ae607.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
27bffbe0-bf77-51b6-87f3-1667b65ae607.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
27bffbe0-bf77-51b6-87f3-1667b65ae607.description2: This dramatic view looks across the great court of the temple complex in Baalbek. In the ancient world Baalbek, to the east of Beirut in Lebanon, was a great centre of trade between Europe and Asias, and home to a religion of sun worship. The Scottish artist David Roberts visited in 1839 and over the following years made many images of the still imposing ruins. This painting is Roberts's last of Baalbek, and he considered it as 'a grand finale' to his career as a painter of the Middle East. The complex's imposing architectural and artistic details also inspired European Neoclassical architects and artists such as Robert Adam. Since about 1864 many tourists visited the famed site, including, in 1898, the German emperor Wilhelm II on his way to Jerusalem. Struck by the magnificence of the ruins, he dispatched a German archaeological team, whose subsequent work resulted in a meticulously presented and illustrated publication that further raised interest in Baalbek.

27d99320-2ed8-57cc-b76a-ed939f64f812.name: St George Greek Orthodox Cathedral
27d99320-2ed8-57cc-b76a-ed939f64f812.description: The Cathedral's main plan is rectangular, and approximately 30 metres long by 20 metres wide. The nave itself is 30 metres long by 7.5 metres wide and is subdivided into five bays, which are then subdivided into three aisles. These aisles are divided by eight impressive sandstone piers measuring approximately 8.5 metres in height, with square divisions, chamfered sides and protruding bases. The central aisle is a barrel vault intersected by a vaulted transept. Light which filters through the upper windows shines on the frescoes which cover the vaulted ceiling. The cathedral has three altar spaces, built into three semi-circular alcoves. Finally, the cathedral is most famous for the half-vaulted painted dome above the central apse, in the central aisle.
27d99320-2ed8-57cc-b76a-ed939f64f812.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
27d99320-2ed8-57cc-b76a-ed939f64f812.history: The final modifications to the cathedral's structure were completed in 1910, with its enlargement eastwards and westwards, the addition of a vaulted portico on the south facade and moving the bell tower to the south-east corner. The interior of the Church is decorated with frescoes donated by Ibrahim Yussef Saad.
27d99320-2ed8-57cc-b76a-ed939f64f812.keywords: Greek; Orthodox; Church; Cathedral; Religion; Beirut

27da4fd7-996d-5066-b357-ffc4082c83ad.name: Dr Charles Nicolle
27da4fd7-996d-5066-b357-ffc4082c83ad.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
27da4fd7-996d-5066-b357-ffc4082c83ad.description2: This is a photograph of the Nobel Prize for Medicine won by Dr Charles Nicolle for his work on infectious illnesses during his time at l'Institut Pasteur from 1903 to 1936.

27e660f6-6597-5bf6-8766-18aaf9b3ddc1.name: Petrie Stereo Photobook 1
27e660f6-6597-5bf6-8766-18aaf9b3ddc1.description2: Petrie was a pioneer of archaeological photography, even though at the time the technique of half-toning had not been developed, so that his photographs had to be turned into woodcuts for publication. He was a great believer in the importance of photography, and, at least at this time, took all of his archaeological photographs as stereo pairs, another of his pioneering works.

27f25605-a0d6-5226-be64-b5c88fc6fc1c.name: *Fall of Stalać*
27f25605-a0d6-5226-be64-b5c88fc6fc1c.author: Petar Petrovic
27f25605-a0d6-5226-be64-b5c88fc6fc1c.description2:
Having mastered the cobbling trade and after studying theology, in 1873, the Serb Đorđe Krstić went to further his education at the Munich Art Academy thanks to a scholarship from the Knez that came after he had prepared for admission to an arts and crafts school. By 1920, there were approximately 50 Serbian students enrolled there. Though pieces from his Munich phase measure up to the best works of the time, a later painting by this historical and genre artist is better suited here. After the initial, strong influence of realism, on his return to Belgrade, in 1883, he endeavoured to present an open manner of painting, with strong and coloristic effects.  
Stalać was one of the largest fortified towns in Serbia in the Middle Ages, serving simultaneously as a checkpoint on the approaches to the then capital Kruševac and to strategically important valleys. At the same time as four other forts, Stalać was burned down and laid to waste in 1413, in initial raids by the Ottoman Turks, who subsequently conquered Serbia in 1459.  
This painting was commissioned by King Aleksandar Obrenović for the 1900 Paris Exposition. However, the committee rejected it before the Expo for an excessively extreme depiction of fighting. When the painting was exhibited in the National Museum in Belgrade in 1901, 1,000 visitors flocked to see it every day.

28039875-4e38-5259-a55c-6b799bdfae9b.name: Grand Bazar Arabe. A late-19th-century bazaar built in Tunis by the construction company of G. Di Vittorio, an Italian immigrant in Tunisia
28039875-4e38-5259-a55c-6b799bdfae9b.dates: Photograph: first years of the 20th century; building: late 19th century
28039875-4e38-5259-a55c-6b799bdfae9b.author: Giulia Barrera
28039875-4e38-5259-a55c-6b799bdfae9b.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 189
28039875-4e38-5259-a55c-6b799bdfae9b.third_name: *Grand Bazar Arabe. G. Di Vittorio imprenditore. Tunisi*
28039875-4e38-5259-a55c-6b799bdfae9b.description2:
On the main entrance one can read the shop sign “Grand Bazar Kassar Said”; on the left “Grand Bazar Arab” and on the right, one can read the shop sign “I. Piperno”: Piperno is an unmistakably Italian Jewish name.  
Giuseppe Di Vittorio, who ran the construction company that built this building, migrated from Termini Imerese (a small town near Palermo, Sicily, Italy) in 1882.

281a9738-8bd7-5011-a3f4-2866ccff808e.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury
281a9738-8bd7-5011-a3f4-2866ccff808e.description2: This document records the inauguration of the Ottoman Beirut-Damascus-Hawran railway company, headed by Hasan Effendi Bayham.

2820044b-9046-518a-901e-821f3cb8b715.name: Arabian gold dagger
2820044b-9046-518a-901e-821f3cb8b715.keywords: Weaponry; dagger; Arabian; Arab; floral decoration; weapon; arms; armours; costume; accessories; fashion; dance
2820044b-9046-518a-901e-821f3cb8b715.description2: Arabian (Omani) dagger belonging to Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim. The dagger sheath is made of leather and embroidered with golden thread. The top and base of the sheath is decorated with a traditional flower design whilst the middle of the sheath is decorated with a leaf pattern. The dagger handle is made of rhinoceros ivory and is decorated with ten pearls. The dagger blade is steel called ‘*al-jawhar*’ which is derived from the finest Arabian Damascus plate.

283da928-6b2e-51fe-a9c1-636157c2ae53.name: Dar Jellouli
283da928-6b2e-51fe-a9c1-636157c2ae53.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
283da928-6b2e-51fe-a9c1-636157c2ae53.history: Located in the heart of Sfax medina, the capital of southern Tunisia, Dar Jellouli once belonged to a rich family from the local nobility. Many members of this family had occupied important positions in the Regency's government throughout the modern period. For example, from 1772 to 1782 Baccar Jellouli was the governor of Sfax. His sons Mohamed and Mahmoud were also members of the city's local government. However, the family made much of its fortune through commercial activities, particularly by owning a fleet of privateer ships. This building was the seat of the local government then from 1939 housed the Centre des Arts under the direction of Lucien Golvin. after independence it became the Musée Régional des Arts et Traditions Populaires.
283da928-6b2e-51fe-a9c1-636157c2ae53.description2: With a simple façade and built in a traditional Tunisian style, this house is built around a central square courtyard paved with white marble and with walls covered in blue tiles. The top two storeys are fitted with an ambulatory and wooden railings. The family's wealth is evident from the carved stone framework, ceramics, carved stucco, woodwork, and floors paved with imported marble. The ground floor contains a number of upside-down-T-shaped rooms which attempt to recreate scenes of daily life in 19th century Sfax. The first-floor rooms hold a collection of traditional clothes. Finally, the second floor holds a collection of painting and Arabic calligraphy.

28712296-3b43-5ca3-b4e9-c6cec4c1ce1a.name: Revolver
28712296-3b43-5ca3-b4e9-c6cec4c1ce1a.type: Military object; metalwork; firearms; arms and armour
28712296-3b43-5ca3-b4e9-c6cec4c1ce1a.author: Marie Therese Moujabber

28712296-3b43-5ca3-b4e9-c6cec4c1ce1a.description2: Yusuf Bey Karam's revolver, which he used in the resistance against the Ottomans. It is made of cast steel and fitted with a wooden grip.

2879dbdc-ef5b-53f4-b8f7-d3ae618cfb30.name: Rose sprinkle flask in Persian style
2879dbdc-ef5b-53f4-b8f7-d3ae618cfb30.description: Flask produced in Paris in Oriental style.

28a47b67-f1e7-5f4c-8ee1-b205470d3b94.name: For the working classes. All sorts of good available to buy on credit, paying 1 franc a week.
28a47b67-f1e7-5f4c-8ee1-b205470d3b94.description2: As the working class expanded to huge numbers due to industrial developments and rural exodus to the cities, they also became an important pawn in the nation's economic game. Banks and businesses  introduced systems of paying by credit, claiming to help the less privileged. This poster, for examples, claims that a simple credit system would allow this family to radically change their life, affording them a larger and better lit home, nicer clothes, and a more luxurious dinner on the table.

28ec76df-2d4c-59e5-8b93-2cd4db3c1960.name: Labour certificate No.1(a) [Child’s labour certificate]
28ec76df-2d4c-59e5-8b93-2cd4db3c1960.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
28ec76df-2d4c-59e5-8b93-2cd4db3c1960.description2: Under the Employment of Children Act 1903, a child needed to obtain such a certificate (by passing a certain grade standard in school work) before being able to leave school and commence employment. The certificate is divided into two parallel sections, both stamped with the signature of James Graham, a Local Education Authority officer. The left-hand one gives the holder's name (Annie Waggonheim), address and birthdate, and certifies that she is not less than thirteen years old according to her birth certificate or statutory declaration. The right-hand section certifies that she has made 350 attendances in not more than two schools during each year for five preceding years, and gives 'Darley St C School' (Darley Street Council School) as the school in which the attendances were made.

28f6f7de-3daa-59e6-960d-f0cac66b210d.name: North African caravan, in the west of the Sahara
28f6f7de-3daa-59e6-960d-f0cac66b210d.third_name: A Travers le Monde, Paris: Hachette, 1895–1914
28f6f7de-3daa-59e6-960d-f0cac66b210d.description2: Camille Douls (1864–1889), who was passionate  about Africa, decided in the late 19th century to enter indigenous North African territory, despite it being forbidden for foreigners at the time. He began to learn Arabic and study the Quran for this purpose, and was able to live among the Oulad Delim tribe for five months, although not without risk to his personal safety. He published his observations on his return (1888), which attracted much attention, as no European had lived among these people to date. He was assassinated the following year during a trip to Algeria. The tale of his time in the desert was illustrated by Jules Girardet, an artist specialising in historical scenes who had never seen the subjects of his drawings. This image is therefore interesting, as it sheds light on the nature of the stereotypical Western gaze on nomadic lifestyles.

28f9592c-7e7c-553c-be06-baac37d4447b.name: *The arrival of Suleiman Pasha, envoy of the Porte, in Giurgiu*
28f9592c-7e7c-553c-be06-baac37d4447b.second_name: *The arrival of the Ottoman army in Valahia*
28f9592c-7e7c-553c-be06-baac37d4447b.description2: In June 1848 revolution broke out in Wallachia, aiming to liberate the country from the Ottoman sovereignty. Prince Bibescu was deposed and a provisional government was installed. As a result, the sultan sent an army to Wallachia. The Ottoman army entered on the Romanian territory in July and the Porte’s representative, Suleiman Pasha, began negotiations with the Romanian revolutionary government. This chromolithograph is part of a series of German chromolithographs depicting episodes from the Revolution that took place in Wallachia in 1848. It shows the entrance of Süleyman Pasha, the Porte's envoy, accompanied by a part of his army of 20.000 soldiers, in Giurgiu, a port on the Danube, after having crossed the river. He is received by a Romanian delegation.

29092d3e-f7b7-5e75-a750-72b4e7e7bbd1.name: *Fugitives Of Herzegovina*
29092d3e-f7b7-5e75-a750-72b4e7e7bbd1.author: Petar Petrovic
29092d3e-f7b7-5e75-a750-72b4e7e7bbd1.description2: In response to events in the Serbo-Turkish war of 1875-78, Uroš Predić presents his extremely realistic treatment of a subject glorifying not the heroic struggle for liberation, but the hardships of innocent people forced to go into hiding. The artist was inspired by similar works with historical subjects, like those painted by Jaroslav Čermak (1831-1878), but painted his figures from live models, mostly close relatives who posed for him in a Belgrade studio. Thanks to the world-renowned scientist and benefactor Mihailo Pupin (1854-1935), *Fugitives of Herzegovina* became a part of the collection of the National Museum in Belgrade in 1923.

295e748a-0245-55df-9c43-f50f0272c148.name: Painting on glass
295e748a-0245-55df-9c43-f50f0272c148.holder: Musée des Arts et Traditions Populaires
295e748a-0245-55df-9c43-f50f0272c148.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
295e748a-0245-55df-9c43-f50f0272c148.description2: This image, painted on glass, is a reference to the famous legend of Abla and 'Antar ibn Shaddad a legend which was very much alive in the Tunisian popular imagination of the time. The well-loved Abla is painted here as a queen, with regal clothes and a crown on her head. The horse, a symbol of virility and strength, is a reference to the legendary character of 'Antar.

29723c0f-a1c2-5bb3-aa6b-3b7ef63ed1af.name: Ceramic vase
29723c0f-a1c2-5bb3-aa6b-3b7ef63ed1af.description2: Kütahya was the second most important ceramic production centre after İznik due to the rich clay deposits in the area. Although there was a decline in ceramic production at the beginning of the 19th century, in the last quarter of the same century production was revived and new designs inspired by İznik ceramics were produced. This is a Kütahya-produced vase whose body enlarges toward the top. It has a floral design on a blue base. The inner part of the notched mouth is white.

29756bc5-95e1-5d47-be16-67719e7ac820.name: *The Franco-Tuscan Expedition to Egypt*
29756bc5-95e1-5d47-be16-67719e7ac820.author: Marina Minozzi
29756bc5-95e1-5d47-be16-67719e7ac820.keywords: Campaign in Egypt; Egyptomania; archaeology; Leopoldo II; Charles X; scientific expedition; university; museums; collection; collector; Florence; Pisa; Egyptology; Nubia; languages; hieroglyph; epigraphy; Italian painters; travelling artist; botany
29756bc5-95e1-5d47-be16-67719e7ac820.copyright: Copyright image: Su concessione del Ministero per i Beni Culturali e del Turismo - Museo Egizio di Firenze.
29756bc5-95e1-5d47-be16-67719e7ac820.description2:
In 1827 the artist Giuseppe Angelelli took part in the Franco-Tuscan campaign to Egypt (1828–1829) sponsored by the French Government and the Grand Duke of Tuscany and directed by the archaeologist Ippolito Rosellini. Once back in Florence, the Grand Duke of Tuscany commissioned him to create a painting of those who took part at the campaign in Thebes.  
The two directors are represented in the core of the scene, wearing the Nizam, the official clothing, which has recently been required by the pasha and willingly adopted by most of them. Champollion is seated and Ippolito Rosellini is standing at his right, holding a sheet depicting one of the Kadesh Battle's scenes, that of Pharaoh grabbing an enemy's arm. In the middle, between the two protagonists, is the engineer Gaetano Rosellini, Ippolito's uncle and architect in charge of the two missions. On the left, several members of the Commissions: the elder Raddi, dressed in European garb and holding a lotus flower in his hand; the illustrator Duchesne is shown in the foreground with the colours on one side and a painting of ruins on the other.

en: Guidotti M.C., “Ippolito Rosellini e la Spedizione franco-toscana”, in *Ricerche di Storia dell’arte* 100, 2010, Rome: Carocci, 2010: 43–47.

298f1be0-1a70-55ec-8567-86eda6c195f5.name: Revolver
298f1be0-1a70-55ec-8567-86eda6c195f5.description: This solid-frame, short-barrel pocket revolver was manufactured in Britain. This type of revolver became very popular and had been copied by many gun makers in different countries such as Belgium, Spain, and France among others. The American President James Garfield in 1881 was assassinated by one of these revolvers, probably an American copy of the British Bull Dog. This revolver is fitted with wooden grip plates. The cylinder is smooth and no serial number can be seen on it. The only engravement is what can be read as British Bull Dog at the top of the barrel. The base of the barrel was broken and mended.
298f1be0-1a70-55ec-8567-86eda6c195f5.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities

29d1744d-d29c-54bc-a8d4-afa1ddd2f9e0.name: Algerian Pavilion Garden in the Trocadéro [Paris Exhibition, 1878]
29d1744d-d29c-54bc-a8d4-afa1ddd2f9e0.author: Marina Minozzi
29d1744d-d29c-54bc-a8d4-afa1ddd2f9e0.archival: *L'Esposizione di Parigi del 1878 illustrata*, Sonzogno Editore, 1878, p. 84
29d1744d-d29c-54bc-a8d4-afa1ddd2f9e0.keywords: Exposition universelle de Paris; industrialisation; exhibition building; Moorish city; exhibitions and urban spaces; Moorish style; Islamic architecture; reinterpretation; exoticism; reproduction; model; house; garden; Islamic garden; magazine
29d1744d-d29c-54bc-a8d4-afa1ddd2f9e0.copyright: Copyright image: Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale, Roma.
29d1744d-d29c-54bc-a8d4-afa1ddd2f9e0.description2: International Exhibition in Paris, 1878. The Algerian Pavilion represents one of the greatest examples of French colonisation policy. On the inside, the Algerian Pavilion has a huge garden with a fountain in the middle and represents one of the most beautiful pavilions within the exhibition. The Algerian pavilion was designed by the architect M. Wable, appointed by General Chanzy.

29f9716b-3b17-5ea5-b1e6-06de5e5b0e3e.name: *Funda* (pin)
29f9716b-3b17-5ea5-b1e6-06de5e5b0e3e.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
29f9716b-3b17-5ea5-b1e6-06de5e5b0e3e.keywords: decorative pin; funda; filigree; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; silver; wedding; marriage; fashion; costume
29f9716b-3b17-5ea5-b1e6-06de5e5b0e3e.description2: Over the course of the centuries-long existence of Macedonia in the shadow of the Ottoman Empire there was apparent reflection of Oriental-Islamic influences in its arts and crafts. This also applies to the jewellery of Macedonians and all other ethnic communities. In the east of Macedonia, young women and brides within the Vlach population used to wear exquisite articles of adornment in the area of the temples. This type of jewellery was called *funda*. It was usually in trapezoid or semi-oval shape. *Funda* was made in filigree technique richly adorned with lace and tiny silver coins.

2a226eef-1a17-51ae-9e21-911b78e227e7.name: The Builders
2a226eef-1a17-51ae-9e21-911b78e227e7.author: Marina Minozzi
2a226eef-1a17-51ae-9e21-911b78e227e7.keywords: Sculpture; Italian sculptors; reform; social change; work; post-unitarian Italian society; working class; working class condition; social topics; realism; Verismo; social verismo; artistic exchanges; France
2a226eef-1a17-51ae-9e21-911b78e227e7.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
2a226eef-1a17-51ae-9e21-911b78e227e7.description2: Arturo Dazzi was the son of the owner of a marble quarry and remained attracted to this raw material throughout his life. He attended the Academy of Fine Arts in Carrara and then won two national contests. The group of *The Builders*, as stated by the artist, was made for his final examination during the four years he spent at the Pensionato Nazionale di Scultura between 1904 to 1907. For this reason, the sculpture is very complicated and needed a lot of study and work in order to be completed. Nonetheless it gave great satisfaction to the artist: exhibited in 1907 in Italy and in 1909 in Munich the group was awarded both times with gold medals. The work shows an idealized version of the social “verism”, or truth, a concept common among young Italian sculptors of the time, and shows the influence of the painting of Constantin Meunier, *Enlèvement d’un creuset brisé*, done in 1884.
2a226eef-1a17-51ae-9e21-911b78e227e7.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

en: Damigella A.M., in Elena di Majo and Matteo Lafranconi (eds), *Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Moderna. Le Collezioni. Il XIX secolo*, Milan: Electa, 2006, cat. 16.4.

2a4f3434-97f1-53a2-837d-e4407a1a20de.name: Dagger
2a4f3434-97f1-53a2-837d-e4407a1a20de.type: Military object; metalwork; arms and armour
2a4f3434-97f1-53a2-837d-e4407a1a20de.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
2a4f3434-97f1-53a2-837d-e4407a1a20de.keywords: Military object; Metalwork; Arms; armour; Steel
2a4f3434-97f1-53a2-837d-e4407a1a20de.description2: These small daggers were used by the Ottoman soldiers in Lebanon in the 19th century to quash resistance movements. As the Lebanese resistance had no weapons of their own, the fighters frequently ambushed Ottoman soldiers and took their weapons. This dagger is an example of such weaponry, which was taken by the resistance and used against the Ottomans. The blade is made of steel and has a curved double-edge. The handle is made of wood and painted black, with decorative drawings in gold paint.

2aa49918-c570-5090-b9c9-670c7ca75ff7.name: *The Bazaar at Athens*
2aa49918-c570-5090-b9c9-670c7ca75ff7.author: Tsigakou 1995, 114, fig. 6
2aa49918-c570-5090-b9c9-670c7ca75ff7.description2: The well-known Irish topographer Edward Dodwell toured Greece twice: in 1801 and 1805–6 and he later produced several works on Greece’s scenery, its antiquities and the people’s life. He managed to cover a wide range of Greek subjects and to record faithfully-in both his drawings and his descriptions- various aspects of Greek life and customs. Dodwell’s folio *Views in Greece* (1821) includes an identical image entitled “Bazaar of Athens”, which is obviously based on this watercolour. According to the artist’s description in the text, on the right-hand side is seen a coffee-shop frequented by important people, such as the disdar (e.g. Governor of Athens) depicted in a scarlet gown.

en: Tsigakou, Fani-Maria, *British Images of Greece from the Benaki Museum Collections*, Athens: Benaki Museum, 1995.

2ab573cd-8e69-51f0-8275-3af031e2fa06.name: *The View of the City of Algiers*
2ab573cd-8e69-51f0-8275-3af031e2fa06.author: Dalila Orfali
2ab573cd-8e69-51f0-8275-3af031e2fa06.third_name: *The View of the City of Algiers*

2ae3984e-4d68-5007-ab52-077d0d39f896.name: Alhambra vase
2ae3984e-4d68-5007-ab52-077d0d39f896.dimensions: Height: 107.0 cm, Width: 51.0 cm, Depth: 48.0 cm, Weight: 28.5 kg
2ae3984e-4d68-5007-ab52-077d0d39f896.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
2ae3984e-4d68-5007-ab52-077d0d39f896.keywords: Ceramic; earthenware; vase; geometric patterns; exhibition; revival; lusterware; Nasrids; Spain; workshop; decorative arts; Neo-Mudéjar
2ae3984e-4d68-5007-ab52-077d0d39f896.materials: Earthenware, inlaid with coloured clays and, possibly, painted
2ae3984e-4d68-5007-ab52-077d0d39f896.description2: The Alhambra, the palace and fortress of the Moorish Kings of Granada, Spain, was founded in 1248 and largely completed by 1354. After three hundred years of neglect and destruction, restoration work began in 1828. Its sumptuous architecture excited a great deal of interest, dissemninated most notably by the *Plans, Details and Sections of the Alhambra* published by Owen Jones from 1836. Of the original furnishings of the Palace, some vases survive. The most famous was made before 1400 and is here copied relatively accurately by Deck. This vase was probably shown in the International Exhibition, London, 1862.

2afaee38-c8b6-5f96-881c-e8b6d088c400.name: Amman Railway Station
2afaee38-c8b6-5f96-881c-e8b6d088c400.author: Mohammad Najjar
2afaee38-c8b6-5f96-881c-e8b6d088c400.history: In 1900-1908, Sultan Abdul Hamid with the help and support of Germany established a Railway between Damascus and Mecca (1700 km) to facilitate transporting the pilgrims. The track from Medina to Mecca (400 km) was never realized. The cost of the project was estimated at approximately 5 million Ottoman golden liras, which were provided from: private donations, revenues of the Ottoman State from the sale of stamps, and a special tax upon all citizens for the railway. Construction of the narrow-gauge track (105cm) began in 1900 with a wire telegraph line along its side connecting Damascus with Medina across Amman with a total track length of 1303 km. Official inaugurations of the tracks and stations were scheduled to coincide with the accession of the Sultan to the throne in the month of September every year. The construction of the project ended in 1908.
2afaee38-c8b6-5f96-881c-e8b6d088c400.keywords: Hijaz; railway; station; pilgrimage; hajj; pilgrimage route; communication; telegraph; Jordan; Damascus; Mecca; Makka; Amman; Zarqa; Qatranah; Ma'an; Amman; Tabuk; Arabian Peninsula; Ottoman; Abd al Hamid; Germany; Meinsner
2afaee38-c8b6-5f96-881c-e8b6d088c400.description2: Amman station was one of the main stations on the Hijaz railway. The location of the town of Amman along the Hijaz railroad had become a decisive factor in choosing Amman as the capital city of the Emirate of Transjordan in 1921. The station consists of several buildings including a passengers' waiting hall, maintenance depots and distinctive water towers. The various components of the project including the rails, steam engines, bridges and stations were an industrial, architectural and engineering statement that had a huge influence on Jordan. The Zarqa-Amman Section was completed in September 1903.

2b174c47-ca5a-5be5-853f-ba97cf7eac1e.name: Carthage Cathedral
2b174c47-ca5a-5be5-853f-ba97cf7eac1e.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
2b174c47-ca5a-5be5-853f-ba97cf7eac1e.history: This old Catholic cathedral is located on the Byrsa Hill, near the Carthage archaeological site. It was built by the King of France in honour of his grandfather, King Louis IX, in the very place he had died of the plague. The cathedral is also evidence of the Tunisian beys' tolerance and their help in protecting the Christian religion in the Regency of Tunis in the 19th century. Building works began in 1884, and it was consecrated by the French Protectorate on 15 May 1890. It became the primatial cathedral of Africa once the title of The Primate of Africa was returned to the Cardinal Lavigerie, who was also the Archidiocese of Algiers and Carthage. It was no longer used as a place of worship after Tunisian independence, and has become an important landmark for tourism and culture, having been renamed the Acropolium de Carthage in 1993.
2b174c47-ca5a-5be5-853f-ba97cf7eac1e.keywords: Architecture; Romano-Byzanine style; vaults; stained-glass windows; tapestry; marble
2b174c47-ca5a-5be5-853f-ba97cf7eac1e.description2: The Saint-Louis de Carthage Cathedral was built on the top the Byrsa Hill, the highest point in Punic Carthage, on the site of the Roman Capitol over an area of 1,800 m2. It is built in a North African Byzantine style, supported by 174 marble columns with golden capitals and wooden painted ceilings imported from Europe and carved with arabesques. Inside the cathedral, the choir rises in the shape of two semi-circular arches, covered by a sky-blue dome. It is built with three naves and has an ambulatory on the first floor. Light shines through 284 stained-glass windows decorated with arabesques, with those on the central nave depicting Saint Louis and Saint Augustine, the cathedral's two patron saints.

2b9bd4b7-9bf4-5be0-b693-18e62b5dc6f7.name: Drinking cup
2b9bd4b7-9bf4-5be0-b693-18e62b5dc6f7.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities
2b9bd4b7-9bf4-5be0-b693-18e62b5dc6f7.author: Huda Kilani
2b9bd4b7-9bf4-5be0-b693-18e62b5dc6f7.keywords: Stepped pedestal; silver; geometric decoration; Caucasian immigrants; domestic vessels
2b9bd4b7-9bf4-5be0-b693-18e62b5dc6f7.description2: Small silver cup with a stepped pedestal for drinking hard liquors. The surface is decorated with geometric designs, including dots, lines and triangles. On the upper part of the cup, an engraved inscription in Russian ("your health") runs along the external surface. The year of manufacture (1896) is stamped. Items like this were brought to Jordan in the last quarter of the 19th century by Caucasian immigrants, the Circassians. The immigration of the Circassians started in the middle of nineteenth century and continued until 1900. They migrated to the eastern Arab countries with which they have spiritual and religious links. This object illustrates the variegated population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries and the various local costumes, crafts and rites.

2bc79611-c941-5b21-81f7-7525e5e187ea.name: An example of Italian colonial propaganda describing 'The first railway engine crossing Libya, causing astonishment and panic among the Arabs'
2bc79611-c941-5b21-81f7-7525e5e187ea.author: Giulia Barrera
2bc79611-c941-5b21-81f7-7525e5e187ea.third_name: *'La prima locomotiva attraversa il suolo libico tra lo spavento e lo stupore degli arabi'*
2bc79611-c941-5b21-81f7-7525e5e187ea.second_name: A colonial postcard about the inauguration of the first railway in Libya
2bc79611-c941-5b21-81f7-7525e5e187ea.description2:
The railway in a colonial context was much more than a means of transport: it was a powerful symbol of modernity, of technological superiority of the colonisers over the colonised, and of mastery over the territory. The construction of railways in colonial situations was thus often celebrated by the colonialists’ popular press or in postcards, as in this case.  
In Libya, the Italians started building railroads from the first months of colonial rule. The first lines, inaugurated in 1912, connected Tripoli with Ain Zara (11 kms) and to Zanzur (39 kms). By the end of 1915, the railway lines in Libya amounted to 180 kilometres.

2bcb43f7-b5d0-5c2b-a273-3d6e8643ed05.name: Mosaic of Virgil
2bcb43f7-b5d0-5c2b-a273-3d6e8643ed05.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
2bcb43f7-b5d0-5c2b-a273-3d6e8643ed05.description2: This mosaic shows Virgil listening to Clio and Melpomene. It was discovered in Sousse (ancient Hadrumetum) in 1896 and is one of the gems of the Musée du Bardo. Dressed in a splendid white toga decorated with gold embroidery, this mosaic is one of the most remarkable portraits of the famous Roman poet. He is surrounded by the muses Clio and Melpomene and holds a roll of parchment on his knee, on which the eighth verse of the Aeneid is written. The mosaic is the oldest representations of Virgil known today.

2be85362-6e14-5698-94e1-a895d7c03a8e.name: *Birtles in Jerusalem*
2be85362-6e14-5698-94e1-a895d7c03a8e.description2: Sgt. Birtles, Charles Warren’s chief assistant during the work in Jerusalem, climbing down into the destruction debris of Herod’s Temple in the Tyropoean Valley.

2beb8ede-81f6-5a62-aa22-de18127faa93.name: Photograph of Casablanca Railway Station
2beb8ede-81f6-5a62-aa22-de18127faa93.description: In 1908, the French General Albert d’Amade led the pacification of the Kabyle Berber peoples on the plains of Chaouia and also oversaw the construction of a railway line between Casablanca and Berrechid. By 1914, the railway was mainly used for the civil transportation of people and goods. This shot of Casablanca Station in 1920 depicts a train arriving at the station, where the passengers waiting to board appear to be European settlers and Moroccan notables.

2c003611-f7ea-5e9d-9992-13b824dcddc9.name: Portrait Khalil al-Khury
2c003611-f7ea-5e9d-9992-13b824dcddc9.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
2c003611-f7ea-5e9d-9992-13b824dcddc9.description2: Khalil al-Khuri was born in Choiefat ('Aley) in October 1836. He founded the first non-official newspaper in Arabic, *Hadiqat al-Akhbar* (the garden of news) in 1858. He also wrote a collection of poems, some of which were later translated into French. He died in October, 1907.

2c45ad6b-40d7-5711-b2ec-f75cf2e0ea72.name: Carte du royaume de Tunis
2c45ad6b-40d7-5711-b2ec-f75cf2e0ea72.holder: Musée de la Monnaie : Banque centrale de Tunisie

2c45ad6b-40d7-5711-b2ec-f75cf2e0ea72.archival: Shaw Thomas, “Geographical Description of the Kingdom of Tunis”, in *Philosophical Transactions*, 1729 ; *Travels or Observations Relating To Several Parts of Barbary and the Levant*, Oxford, 1738- 46 fol, 2 vol – London
2c45ad6b-40d7-5711-b2ec-f75cf2e0ea72.description2: This is a copy of a map of the Beylik of Tunis by Sir Thomas Shaw, an English naturalist and traveller. It was one of the first Western maps of the area. Sir Thomas Shaw wrote all the names of all the ancient Roman towns, clearly marked the borders of Africa Romana and Numidia and the ancient sites of Carthage, Sicca Veneria, Suffetula, Hadrumetum, Thysdrus, Tacapae, and more.

2c586151-177a-57bd-9616-76904bd42503.name: *Surre Procession*
2c586151-177a-57bd-9616-76904bd42503.holder: The Painting Collection of the The Grand National Assembly of Turkey, Vice Secretary General, National Palaces, Dolmabahçe Palace
2c586151-177a-57bd-9616-76904bd42503.keywords: Painting; Orientalism; Dolmabahçe Palace; Stefano Ussi
2c586151-177a-57bd-9616-76904bd42503.description2: The Italian Orientalist painter Stefano Ussi's painting *Surre Regiment* depicts the deva caravan carrying gifts from Cairo to Kaaba, the pilgrims and a regiment of the Ottoman army assigned to protect the caravan. *Surre Regiment* is the largest painting of the Painting Collection of the National Palaces. The composition reflects the emotions of Muslims during the pilgrimage to Mecca, whose ethnic structures, growing styles and points of view regarding Islam are different. The frame of the painting dated 1873 is surrounded by Arabic Kufic script, which is a part of the 126th verse in Surah Al-Imran that reads, “There is no help or victory except from Allah, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise”. *Surre Regiment* is presumed to be included in the Palace’s collection by being purchased or given by Mısır Hıdivi as a gift for Sultan Abdülaziz.

2cac8790-8730-5708-8f5a-80058a37752b.name: *Turkish Country Houses on the Bosphorus*
2cac8790-8730-5708-8f5a-80058a37752b.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
2cac8790-8730-5708-8f5a-80058a37752b.provenance: First published in Julia Pardoe, *The Beauties of the Bosphorus*, London 1838, facing page 40
2cac8790-8730-5708-8f5a-80058a37752b.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
2cac8790-8730-5708-8f5a-80058a37752b.artist: Drawn by William Henry Bartlett; engraved by J. C. Bentley
2cac8790-8730-5708-8f5a-80058a37752b.description2: This engraving shows the typical, wooden Ottoman yalis or summer houses built along the shores of the Bosphorus by high-ranking officials and members of the elite since the late 17th century. Designed to reflect both their location, making maximum use of the waterfront, and the taste and status of their owner, the yalis provided a welcome and comfortable escape from the congested city. Their interior, with separate areas for public reception and private family quarters, was furnished, with inbuilt cupboards and diwans, and decorated in the traditional Ottoman style. Only in the 19th century were aspects of European-style interior design and furniture adopted widely. The facades of the yalis were traditionally painted a deep rose colour, until European influence led to the adoption of pastel shades in the 19th century. The image was originally published in Julia Pardoe's 'The Beauties of the Bosphorus', published in London by George Virtue in 1838.

2cf5398f-8d6e-5e13-b679-67442f1bcbc6.name: Menu for the gala dinner offered by the Italian king in honour of the Ambassador from Morocco, who visited Italy in June 1890
2cf5398f-8d6e-5e13-b679-67442f1bcbc6.author: Giulia Barrera
2cf5398f-8d6e-5e13-b679-67442f1bcbc6.archival: ACS, Min. Real Casa, Uff. Prefetto di Palazzo, filza 107, f. 3 "Ambasciata marocchina. Suo arrivo e soggiorno a Roma"
2cf5398f-8d6e-5e13-b679-67442f1bcbc6.description2:
In June 1890, the Sultan of Morocco sent an Ambassador to Italy (Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi), to meet the Italian King and present him with extremely rich gifts.  
The Ambassador – who was escorted by his secretary, an interpreter, and some dignitaries – was received with the highest honours. He met with the Italian Prime Minister and with the King, who offered a gala dinner for him.  
The menu for the gala dinner was in French. A military band played different pieces of music during the dinner.

2d85c81f-8fff-5170-9719-df9f41dbd763.name: Socks (*Chorapi*)
2d85c81f-8fff-5170-9719-df9f41dbd763.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
2d85c81f-8fff-5170-9719-df9f41dbd763.keywords: home-made attire; knitting; silver; gold; embroidery; floral decoration; costume
2d85c81f-8fff-5170-9719-df9f41dbd763.materials: Knitted of wool and silver and gold-wrapped threads. Decoration with embroidery of varied wool
2d85c81f-8fff-5170-9719-df9f41dbd763.description2: In the 18th, 19th and early 20th centuries, all garments for the entire family were made by women themselves. They used to weave all the fabrics, except for the broadcloth, as well as to cut and sew the clothes, decorate them by embroidery and apply varied ornaments for embellishing. Women also used to knit the socks to match the outfit. These men’s socks belong to the set of traditional men’s costume from the Gorni Polog area. They are knitted from black wool and *srma* (silver and gold-wrapped threads). They have been additionally decorated with embroidered floral patterns in different colours.

2df6225e-8ea7-5fef-a311-cc29307168e3.name: *Excavation of Samarra*
2df6225e-8ea7-5fef-a311-cc29307168e3.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
2df6225e-8ea7-5fef-a311-cc29307168e3.author: Stefan Weber
2df6225e-8ea7-5fef-a311-cc29307168e3.second_name: Great Mosque with the famous minaret (Malwiya) of the caliphal city of Samarra, groundbreaking excavation by E. Herzfeld 1911–13
2df6225e-8ea7-5fef-a311-cc29307168e3.description2: Of great importance for the collection of the first Museum of Islamic Art in the western world are the findings made during the excavations in Samarra, which were conducted by Ernst Herzfeld and the museum’s first director, Friedrich Sarre, between 1911 and 1913. The study of the Abbasid’s temporal second capital has contributed to an understanding of the developments and changes in Islamic art at the time.

2e1b7a1f-87a3-5357-a286-a3e13417e1ea.name: *Catalogue Raisonné des monuments exposés dans le Musée National de l'art Arabe*
2e1b7a1f-87a3-5357-a286-a3e13417e1ea.author: Mina Moraitou
2e1b7a1f-87a3-5357-a286-a3e13417e1ea.description2: The *Catalogue Raisonné des monuments exposés dans le Musée National de l'art Arabe* by Max Herz Bey is an illustrated catalogue of the collections at the Museum of Islamic Art in Cairo. It contains an introduction with the history of the different periods from the Umayyads to the Ottomans and chapters following the galleries of the museum and according to material: chapters on stucco and stone, woodwork, metalwork, ceramics, textiles, bookbindings and glass.

2e61e3f7-50c6-567e-8d2c-022e0356b93e.name: Uniform-coat and fez of an officer of the Austro-Hungarian infantry from Bosnia-Herzegovina
2e61e3f7-50c6-567e-8d2c-022e0356b93e.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
2e61e3f7-50c6-567e-8d2c-022e0356b93e.keywords: Bosnia; Austrian army; Ottoman army; war; warfare; military wear
2e61e3f7-50c6-567e-8d2c-022e0356b93e.description2: The terms of the Congress of Berlin (1878) placed the two Ottoman provinces of Bosnia and Herzegovina under the direct administration of Austro-Hungarian Empire. Troops under the command of general (*Feldzeugmeister*) Joseph Philippovich von Philippsberg (1818–1889) occupied both regions, which became – by annexation – integral parts of the empire in 1908. In 1882, the Austro-Hungarian Army began recruiting local troops from the provinces, which provided great military value, especially during World War I.

2e69a533-f8e1-5f1a-92fc-fc2a6fbcefa3.name: Portrait of Shaykh Ahmar Hasan Tabbara
2e69a533-f8e1-5f1a-92fc-fc2a6fbcefa3.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
2e69a533-f8e1-5f1a-92fc-fc2a6fbcefa3.keywords: Writer; Symbol; Revolution; Books; Literature; Prison
2e69a533-f8e1-5f1a-92fc-fc2a6fbcefa3.description2: Shaykh Ahmar Hasan Tabbara was born in Beirut in 1870. He began writing and publishing in newspapers, such as *Thamarat al-Funun* at a young age. He later was an editor for the *al-Ittihad al-Usmani* newspaper. He was emprisoned during the First World War, and then hung alongside other Lebanese prisoners of war on 6 May 1916. He published a number of books in his lifetime, including an important manuscript of *Kalila wa Dimna*.

2e72eeda-f993-5903-ad14-80d226524069.name: Veiled women walking, Algeria
2e72eeda-f993-5903-ad14-80d226524069.description2: Western photographers took great interest in the less known aspects of Arab women's daily lives. This photograph, for example, shows veiled Algerian women going for a stroll, thus contradicting the Western audience's common misconception that Algerian women stayed indoors and did not walk around outside.

2e86f805-0ac2-5af3-82ca-11820cd27c1d.name: Beaufort Castle
2e86f805-0ac2-5af3-82ca-11820cd27c1d.description: The Beaufort Castle was a crusader castle located near the town of Nabatiyeh, in South Lebanon. The castle was named "Bel Fort" or "Beau Fort" by the Crusaders in the 12th century. Its name in Arabic is *Qal'at al-Shaqiif*, meaning Castle on the High Rock. The castle was also used for military purposes in the 20th century, particularly during the civil war, due to its strategic location.
2e86f805-0ac2-5af3-82ca-11820cd27c1d.author: Julien El Khoury, Jeff El-Msanne
2e86f805-0ac2-5af3-82ca-11820cd27c1d.history: In 1139, King Fulk of Jerusalem gained control of this area and begun the construction of Beaufort castle shortly afterwards. Although Saladin recaptured Beaufort in 1190, the castle was returned to crusader hands only 60 years later. In 1268 Sultan Baybars finally gained control of the fortress. However, the upper portion was destroyed by the Ottomans in the 17th century, as they sought to quash Emir Fakhr al-Din II, who had taken the castle as part of his network of fortifications. Following the Galilee Earthquake in 1837, which caused considerable damage to the structure, the castle was abandoned and its ruins were used by local farmers to shelter sheep, and as a quarry.
2e86f805-0ac2-5af3-82ca-11820cd27c1d.keywords: fortress; castle; tourism; ruins; Beaufort; medieval

2efb58fe-14fe-59df-ad70-18b84374d4f5.name: Edmund Count Szechenyi (1839–1922)
2efb58fe-14fe-59df-ad70-18b84374d4f5.description2: Portrait of Count Edmund Szechenyi. He was born in 1839 in Bratislava and studied the work of fire brigades in London. In 1869 he founded in Budapest the first volunteer fire brigade, which was transformed into a professional fire brigade in 1870. From 1871–1874 he commanded the umbrella organisation of all fire brigades in Hungary. In 1875 he was sent by Emperor Franz Joseph to Istanbul to build up a fire brigade in the Ottoman capital. As head of the fire brigade he became the first Christian Pasha in the Ottoman Army and stayed in Istanbul until his death in 1922.

2f3824a9-9c37-59fb-a4fe-8281d4a0ea57.name: \[Red Cross\] *Have you answered the Red Cross?*
2f3824a9-9c37-59fb-a4fe-8281d4a0ea57.keywords: Health; First World War; Red Cross
2f3824a9-9c37-59fb-a4fe-8281d4a0ea57.description2: This English nurse symbolises the actions of the International Committee of the Red Cross, whose humanitarian mission is to protect the life and dignity of the victims of armed conflict and other forms of violence, and to bring them aid. Founded in 1863, the Red Cross won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1917.

2f499780-f936-5142-8597-fc27d9b2d0ce.name: An old exhibition from Tiled Kiosk
2f499780-f936-5142-8597-fc27d9b2d0ce.dates: The Tiled Kiosk: 15th century; The photograph: 19th century
2f499780-f936-5142-8597-fc27d9b2d0ce.description2: The Tiled Kiosk is a pavilion set within the outer walls of Topkapı Palace and dates from 1472. It was built by the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II as a pleasure palace or kiosk. The building was used as the Imperial Museum between 1875 and 1891. In 1953, it was opened to the public as a museum of Turkish and Islamic art, and was later incorporated into the Istanbul Archaeology Museums. The collections of the Tiled Kiosk Museum consist of about 2000 artefacts belonging to the Seljuk and Ottoman eras, dating from the 11th-20th centuries. These artefacts include those that existed when the museum was incorporated into the İstanbul Archaeological Museums due to its closeness and those acquired through excavations, purchases, donations and confiscations.

2fa02ca6-7ad8-55e1-8e26-60c11f068f26.name: Letter from the Dey of Algiers, Muhammad Pasha, to Ferdinando IV of Bourbon, King of Naples, granting a two-month truce from corsairs’ attacks (in Arabic with Italian translation)
2fa02ca6-7ad8-55e1-8e26-60c11f068f26.author: Rossana Spadaccini

2fa02ca6-7ad8-55e1-8e26-60c11f068f26.description2: The Dey of Algiers wrote that he graciously granted to the King of Naples a two-month truce (for April and May of 1787). If his corsairs met ships belonging to the Kingdom of Naples, they would not attack them. The two nations would treat each other “with mutual friendship”.

2fd7dbb0-f684-52f4-93f3-b485ecf82f5e.name: Postcard: *The Strait of Gibraltar in the Future*
2fd7dbb0-f684-52f4-93f3-b485ecf82f5e.description: This curious postcard with a utopian vision of how the Strait of Gibraltar could become in the future was sent to the Marquis of Cerralbo by a friend, Gabriel Vich, but never received a stamp. Although it shows the address of the marquis, maybe it was posted inside an envelope or delivered, finally, on hand. This kind of ephemera was published by the fortnightly publication España en África (Spain in Africa), active in the first decades of the 20th century. The image represented is a beautiful commercial and geopolitical project that would have linked two continents with a 15 km bridge.

3018b07a-449e-5452-bb78-bbcfe4a57bdc.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Rita El Hachem
3018b07a-449e-5452-bb78-bbcfe4a57bdc.description2: This station was used to deliver supplies from Beirut port to the main train station in Beirut, located in Mar Mikhael. The station was an important addition to the region's trade system, linking the sea routes the land routes.

301c225c-a1be-58da-b355-55c3b3a1d1e6.name: *A watchman on a Constantinople street*
301c225c-a1be-58da-b355-55c3b3a1d1e6.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
301c225c-a1be-58da-b355-55c3b3a1d1e6.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
301c225c-a1be-58da-b355-55c3b3a1d1e6.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
301c225c-a1be-58da-b355-55c3b3a1d1e6.description2: This painting shows an old watchman, carrying his lantern around the old streets of Istanbul. By the times of sultan Abd al-Hamid II (1293 H/1876 CE – 1327 H/1909 CE) the nature of urban life in the Ottoman empire began to change markedly. In Istanbul, Izmir, Edirne, Salonica and other major cities, streets were paved and lit with gas lamps, while horse drawn trams increasingly plied the streets. Political reforms and  new technologies introduced in the13th century H/ 19th century CE gradually transformed Istanbul into a modern international city. Innovative technological achievements such as electric lighting became more and more common, slowly replacing traditionally essential services like those provided by the watchmen of the city, guarding the city quarters with their hand-held lanterns during the hours of darkness.

307c3b5c-a525-55c7-89a1-8342e6da903a.name: Dolmabahçe Palace Imperial Gate
307c3b5c-a525-55c7-89a1-8342e6da903a.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; James Robertson
307c3b5c-a525-55c7-89a1-8342e6da903a.description2: James Robertson arrived in Istanbul in 1840 and started work as head etcher in Ottoman Mint. He began taking photos of Istanbul soon after. Dolmabahçe Palace was built by Sultan Abdulmecid (1839-1861), who was the thirty first Ottoman Sultan. The palace, whose construction commenced on 13 June 1843, was brought into use on 7 June 1856, upon completion of its surrounding walls. The palace mainly consists of three parts: the Imperial Mabeyn (State Apartments), Muayede Salon (Ceremonial Hall) and the Imperial Harem. Evident Western influences, observed in the style, details and ornaments, are reflections of the aesthetic values as they changed through the last period of the Imperial. On the other hand, it is a building complex in which traditional Turkish House style was applied on a large scale with respect to spatial organization and the relationships between the rooms and salons.

309c53a9-a0ef-5547-8426-cd89d2b38012.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The construction of Galata Pier began in 1892, and was completed in 1900. Two warehouses were built in 1910, and three more were added in 1928. From 1925 on, the port authority started to give all the necessary logistics support to the ships, including water and coal supply, loading and unloading, maritime pilotage and marine salvage services.

30b613c8-c840-5eba-a2ea-3334a058e6c5.name: *The Temptations of Saint Antony*
30b613c8-c840-5eba-a2ea-3334a058e6c5.author: Marina Minozzi
30b613c8-c840-5eba-a2ea-3334a058e6c5.keywords: Realism; France; La tentation de Saint-Antoine; Orientalism; Orientalist painting; religious topics; exoticism; eroticism; woman; international exhibitions; universal exposition; national exposition; exoticism in fine arts and literature
30b613c8-c840-5eba-a2ea-3334a058e6c5.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
30b613c8-c840-5eba-a2ea-3334a058e6c5.description2:
The painting by Domenico Morelli shown at the Universal Exposition in Paris, it’s among the artist’s most complex artworks. Both realistic and symbolic elements characterise the painting, as well as a strong mystic, but at the same time erotic, tension. Inspired by *La Tentation de Saint-Antoine* by Gustave Flaubert from 1874, the painting shows realism in the imaginary setting influenced by oriental elements. The work was finished in 1878 and sent to the French merchant Goupil to be shown at the Universal Exposition in Paris. It was also presented at the National Exposition in Turin in 1880 and completely misunderstood by contemporaries who blamed Morelli for having resigned to make fashionable art.  
A smaller version of it was painted by the artist while making a lot of preparatory drawings in which Saint Anthony is standing next to the rock wall. In the final version the Saint is seated on the ground trying to resist the temptations embodied by the two half-naked women on the left.
