30b913ab-d3b2-56b2-ac63-f81083c8e870.name: Theresian thaler
30b913ab-d3b2-56b2-ac63-f81083c8e870.keywords: Arabian Pensinsula; Maria Theresia; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics
30b913ab-d3b2-56b2-ac63-f81083c8e870.description2: The Maria Theresian Thaler, a large silver coin originally created by Queen (Empress) Maria Theresia, minted in Austria until 1890. It was used in the Arabic Peninsula as a means of payment. This coin was countersigned at the Arabian mint of Ras Bab el Mandeb in 1890.

30cc5fa9-8b03-5f71-9493-92a9a15324e0.name: Migration preparations from Lemnos island to Turkey
30cc5fa9-8b03-5f71-9493-92a9a15324e0.holder: Population Exchange Museum (The Foundation of Lausanne Treaty Emigrants)
30cc5fa9-8b03-5f71-9493-92a9a15324e0.description2: The 1923 population exchange between Greece and Turkey was based upon religious identity, and involved the Greek Orthodox citizens of Turkey and the Muslim citizens of Greece. The "Convention Concerning the Exchange of Greek and Turkish Populations" was signed at Lausanne, Switzerland, on 30 January 1923, by the governments of Greece and Turkey. During the migration waves during the 1896-97 riots in Crete, 40,000 Cretan Muslims had to migrate to territories under Ottoman rule: Lebanon, Syria and Anatolia. This photograph pertains to migration preparations from Lemnos to Turkey in 1924.

30efc219-29fa-5f32-b34b-24791540a5c9.name: Astrolabe
30efc219-29fa-5f32-b34b-24791540a5c9.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
30efc219-29fa-5f32-b34b-24791540a5c9.description2: This portable astrolabe consists of a suspension device with a 18cm diameter disk, divided up into degrees, and a handle. Two moving parts are used for measurements: the spider on the front, and the alidade (a flat ruler revolving round a point) on the back. The astrolabe remained in use as the primary tool for navigation until the 18th century. However, it was also used as an astronomical tool, to measure the height of stars from the horizon, or the angle separating one star from another.

30f458b3-4363-5cf5-82c6-91c5e3c06c7e.name: *Medjmouaï teçavir* (Collection de costumes)

3145dc39-d491-535e-aaa2-6545cc31f4e7.description2: Misirkov’s book “On Macedonian Matters” lays the foundations of the modern Macedonian language and grammar. Being one of the central figures of the “Slav-Macedonian Scientific Literary Society" in St. Petersburg, he largely contributed to issuing the periodical Macedonian and Russian-language publication, “Makedonski Golos” (“Macedonian Voice").

31671ff1-195a-54da-8c1f-6f9b776bf0e8.name: Statue of Cardinal Lavigerie
31671ff1-195a-54da-8c1f-6f9b776bf0e8.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
31671ff1-195a-54da-8c1f-6f9b776bf0e8.author: Bechir Yazidi
31671ff1-195a-54da-8c1f-6f9b776bf0e8.keywords: French protectorate of Tunisia; missionaries in Tunisia
31671ff1-195a-54da-8c1f-6f9b776bf0e8.description2: On the 23 November 1925, the French resident-general in Tunisia, Lucien Saint, organised a solemn gathering to commemorate 100 years since Cardinal Lavigerie's birth. The municipality of Tunis also received a statue of him brandishing a cross by the sculptor Élie-Jean Vézien, which they chose to put in Place Bab el-Bhar (at the entrance to the medina), a place of great importance to Tunisians. This choice of location angered the Tunisian population and triggered a protest from the students of the Zaytuna University, who considered this act an attack on their religious beliefs (it was placed close to the Zaytuna Mosque) and their traditions. The statue stayed there until Tunisian independence, when it was removed by the Mayor of Tunis.  Lavigerie was the Archbishop of Algiers and Carthage, and the founder of the Pères Blancs in 1868.

316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.name: *Mohamed Sadok Pacha Bey* (painting)
316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.keywords: Oil on canvas; B. de Moynier; Mohamed Sadok Pacha Bey
316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.materials: Canvas, wood, coloured pigments, gold leaf
316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.description2: This 1861 oil on canvas by B. de Moynier shows the Mohamed Sadok Pacha Bey in front of the throne in the great hall of the Palais du Bardo, his right hand on the Tunisian constitution (which he has just proclaimed), his left holding his sword. He is dressed in official uniform, with red trousers with a gold stripe and a short black coat with a gold belt and epaulets, in addition to the Nichan al-Amen medal and a green sash with a double red stripe. On his chest the Nichan al-Dam, the Légion d'Honneur and the Nichan al-Iftikhar (classe majeur) medals can be seen, as well as a Légion d'Honneur and Nichan al-Iftikhar on a sling. This painting is evidence of an active diplomatic relationship between the Palais du Bardo and the European chancelleries.

32533015-dfdb-5437-8c81-e020001b7470.description2:
‘The Suffragette’ was the weekly newspaper of the Woman's Social and Political Union (WSPU), the leading militant organisation campaigning for women’s suffrage in the United Kingdom. This wood block printed advertisement features the patron saint of the Suffragettes, Joan of Arc carrying the banner of the WSPU.  
  
Hilda Dallas was a member of the Suffrage Atelier, which was formed in 1909 to encourage artists to promote 'the enfranchisement of women, by means of pictorial publication'. Its activities also included training non-professional artists in printing techniques. The low cost, low tech method of wood block printing, as used in this poster, was cheap, quick and easy to learn.

32e505cb-9f9d-5883-b87d-e0aff2e6436e.description2: Pera Palace Hotel was built in 1892 for the purpose of hosting the passengers of the Orient Express and was named after its location. Alexander Vallaury, a French-Turkish architect living in the city designed the hotel in a blend of neo-classical, art nouveau and oriental styles. The hotel was the first building in Turkey to be powered by electricity other than the Ottoman Palaces. It was also the only address in the city to provide hot running water for its guests and was home to the first electric elevator in Istanbul.

3339a22b-fc28-5c69-a302-f09a3d0a84b5.author: Dalila Orfali
3339a22b-fc28-5c69-a302-f09a3d0a84b5.description2: This small watercolour was made during the artist's short break in Algeria in 1832, during his visit to Morocco with the Count de Mornay. Delacroix only made a small number of Algerian works, as he spent a very short time in the country. He only stayed in Algiers for three days, where he had the oppurtunity to see the inside of *rais*'s palace. Alazard believes that the watercolour of the museum is only drawing from his brief stay at Oran, and this is corroborated by the art historian Arlette Sérullaz, a specialist of Delacroix. The watercolour is also mentioned in Robaut's book *L’œuvre complet de Delacroix*, and was exhibited at the Louvre in 2003 for the "Chefs d'Œuvre du Cabinet des Estampes" exhibition.

33430dbe-c0fc-5bb4-9845-6bce853a6ea6.name: General Hullin's audience, provided by the Dey of Algeria
33430dbe-c0fc-5bb4-9845-6bce853a6ea6.description2: In August 1802, irritated by the repeated pillaging of his ships by Algerian pirates, Napoléon I sent General Hullin and Consul Dubois-Thainville to the then Dey of Algeria, Mustafa Pasha, with a threatening message. This print is an example of Napoleonic propaganda, as it attempts to highlight the "insolence" of the bey, who stays seated on the sofa, and the "bravery" of the general who, with a sword on his side, makes his speech.

3385951b-c80c-5d8e-8659-f32b8e5ee6a7.keywords: upper garment; broad cloth; costume; textile; accessories; wedding; marriage
3385951b-c80c-5d8e-8659-f32b8e5ee6a7.materials: Klashna – thick woollen fabric adorned with balze, silver and gold-wrapped thread, silver string, sequins, beads and pompons of wool
3385951b-c80c-5d8e-8659-f32b8e5ee6a7.description2: Analysis of the evolution path of traditional costumes in the Republic of Macedonia have shown apparent influences of the Old Slav, Old Balkan, Byzantine and Turkish-Oriental cultures. This piece of traditional overcoat is an exquisite example of the application of *srma* – gold and silver-wrapped thread used widely in the Oriental handicraft of decorating garments. A *gornik* is a sleeveless upper garment made of white broadcloth called *klashna*. It has false sleeves hanging on the back. They are actually strips of white broadcloth richly adorned with pompoms of fluffy red wool, silver thread braids, a silver twisted ribbon, red baize, a silver string, sequins and beads. The lower part of the back is decorated in the same manner. Its rims and seams are also decorated with red and black braids.

33c78378-09b9-5e76-bb0d-85f0948fe81c.name: Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, Marquise of Cerralbo, and Amelia del Valle y Serrano, in Oriental garment
33c78378-09b9-5e76-bb0d-85f0948fe81c.description: The Marquis of Cerralbo and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This albumen portrait of Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, Marquise of Cerralbo, and her daughter Amelia del Valle y Serrano is delicious thanks to the typical Turkish costume, the apparently easy pose and the scenography and the absolute harmony with the idea of aesthetic orientalism.

33daf898-afb6-58bd-95bf-60b7472151c4.name: Illuminated Qur’an manuscript
33daf898-afb6-58bd-95bf-60b7472151c4.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department

33daf898-afb6-58bd-95bf-60b7472151c4.artist: Calligrapher Ali Shukri, known as Nadherzadeh

33daf898-afb6-58bd-95bf-60b7472151c4.description2: 19th-century Qur’an manuscripts produced in Istanbul and the Ottoman Empire continued many Islamic art traditions, but could not entirely escape the increasing taste for Western aesthetics.Ssingle-volume Qur’ans like this one became increasingly popular and were completed in large numbers. This example – which appears to have remained unfinished judging by the empty title cartouches above the chapters, begins – as is customary – with a lavishly decorated double page, showing – on the right - the first chapter ‘Al-Fatiha’ and – on the left - the beginning of the second chapter ‘Al-Baqara’. Both texts are contained within broad geometric borders and framed with colourful illuminations with vegetal detailing. The remainder of the all in all 114 chapters of the Holy Qur’an are written in black naskhi and red detailing, with 15 lines to each page. As was customary, the verse markers are rendered as golden circles and each page is confined within delicate gilt borders. Colourful medallions in some of the margins mark important subdivisions of the text.

340abb76-0aa3-53e7-b9ea-c4ebf5b8737b.description2: The print reproduces the drawing, today at the University Library of Pisa, realised by Giuseppe Angelelli. Angelelli’s painting is used for Table LXXXIII of the Historical Monuments which shows one of the engraved paintings from the southern wall of the temple of Abu Simbel, celebrating King Ramses piercing his enemy with a spear. This is a traditional scene that has been reproduced on numerous Egyptian monuments from early historic periods to show the supremacy of the Pharaoh above all foreign people. The enemies of the Egyptians are characterised by libic hair and dresses. An error was made by the copier in the spear used by Rameses, possibly reproduced within Angelelli’s painting because of the Director of the Commission wanted to correct the hieroglyphical text above.

341be9d6-6bac-5978-aa0e-844e03633f92.name: The port of Brăila
341be9d6-6bac-5978-aa0e-844e03633f92.archival: *Donau-Album. Malerische Reise von Regensburg bis Sulina. Album du Danube. Voyage pittoresque de Ratisbonne a Souline. Danube Album. A picturesque travel from Ratisbon to Suline. A Duna. Festöi utazas Regensburg-tol a Sulina torkolatig*, Vienna, A. Hartleben, 1880
341be9d6-6bac-5978-aa0e-844e03633f92.description2: In 1829, an annex to the peace treaty of Edirne, that was concluded after the Russo-Ottoman war of 1828-1829, concerned the Principalities of Wallachia and Moldavia. One of its provisions was that the Sublime Porte had to give back to Wallachia the three cities situated on the left bank of the Danube, which it had conquered in the 15h-16th centuries. Among these was Brăila, a port on the Danube annexed by the Ottomans at around 1540. After 1829 measures were taken by the local authorities for the modernization of Brăila. The port subsequently developed thanks to the growth of Wallachian commerce as a consequence of the fact that by the treaty of Edirne the Ottoman Empire granted the freedom of commerce to the Romanian Principalities. In 1838 Brăila was given the status of free port (with no or few customs duties).

3461e5ef-930c-5a8d-8393-eeb23e8eaffa.name: The female surgery division of the Italian hospital in Tunis
3461e5ef-930c-5a8d-8393-eeb23e8eaffa.author: Giulia Barrera
3461e5ef-930c-5a8d-8393-eeb23e8eaffa.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906. p. 84
3461e5ef-930c-5a8d-8393-eeb23e8eaffa.description2:
Prior to the establishment of the French protectorate on Tunisia in 1881, Italian doctors operated in Tunisia. The Bey had frequently employed Italian physicians. Some were born in Tunisia, of Jewish families from Livorno, others had arrived in Tunisia as political exiles in the first half of the 19th century. The largest contingent of Italian doctors, however, migrated to Tunisia after 1881.  
In 1890, the Italian community opened a hospital with about 100 beds. Italian physicians worked in the hospital as volunteers and indigent patients were treated for free. The initial funding for creating and running the hospital came from the Italian community; the Italian state contributed to pay the expenses for the construction of a new facility in 1900 and partly subsidized the hospital activities.

34ebe371-2a09-50f9-8e86-921fabe509cc.name: *Portico of the Temple at Edfu, Upper Egypt*
34ebe371-2a09-50f9-8e86-921fabe509cc.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
34ebe371-2a09-50f9-8e86-921fabe509cc.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
34ebe371-2a09-50f9-8e86-921fabe509cc.description2: Considered the best preserved cult temple of ancient Egypt, Edfu temple was swamped with sand in Roberts’s days, and houses had been built on top. The French archaeologist Auguste Mariette eventually excavated it in the 1860s.This view shows the temple's portico, its  sand-filled façade supported by six monumental columns. The columns on either side of the centre have large lotus columns, those flanking them are made to resemble vertically rising date palm fronds. The outermost columns carry capitals derived from composite Theban palm tree designs. Beyond the columns of the facade, two further rows of capitaled columns form the inner area of the portico, or pronaos. Over the entrance of the portico and on the upper shafts of the columns, pharaonic imagery, emblems, cartouches and hieroglyphs are clearly visible.  The artist emphasizes the monumentality of both the portico and the masses of sand that have invaded it by introducing a group of dwarfed visitors resting on one of the sand dunes in the centre – utterly dwarfed by their surroundings.

35118a9c-ae87-5875-b6fd-694c3a29ac01.description2:
In June 1890, the Sultan of Morocco sent an Ambassador to Italy (Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi), to meet the Italian King and present him with gifts.  
The Ambassador was received with the highest honours. He met with the Italian Prime Minister and with the King, who offered him a gala dinner.  
In these pictures one can see (from the top left): four captains who escorted Morocco’s Ambassador, his interpreter Lamfaddal Elkabbagi, the Ambassador on a carriage arriving at the King’s palace, Hamed (one of the Ambassador’s servants), Pà Nadan (another servant), and two children travelling with the Ambassador on the hotel’s terrace.

351cda3e-2855-5288-9f93-722ee2410530.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
351cda3e-2855-5288-9f93-722ee2410530.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ancient Istanbul; pavilion
351cda3e-2855-5288-9f93-722ee2410530.description2: The construction of Beykoz Pavilion began by order of Mehmed Ali Pahsa, Governor of Egypt in 1845 and upon his death was completed in 1854. The two-storeyed, half-timbered building has a symmetrical plan and neo-classical façade and designed as a hall in the middle with rooms surrounded. Photographs of the pavilion taken during the reign of Sultan Abdülhamid II reveal its rich decoration with gilded furniture, upholsteries and curtains of Hereke fabrics, Baccarat vases and large crystal chandeliers.

351e4901-7c17-581f-9b15-8be1d6fc3458.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 164
351e4901-7c17-581f-9b15-8be1d6fc3458.description2: “Au Palais Arabe”, Rue de Rome, 3, Tunis, was once the most important shop in town for furniture and other household items. Eugenio Coen (born in Livorno in 1855, migrated to Tunis in 1885) and his brother Alfredo (born in Livorno in 1868 and migrated to Tunis in 1887) also ran a furniture factory that, in 1906, employed about 100 carpenters, cabinet makers and other workers, 80 per cent of whom were Italian.

351f1d5e-9300-5133-9200-12abc5718e8c.name: *Mosque of Sidi Bu Madyan, Tlemcen, Algeria*
351f1d5e-9300-5133-9200-12abc5718e8c.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
351f1d5e-9300-5133-9200-12abc5718e8c.description2: The mosque adjoins the shrine of Sidi Bu Madyan, a twelfth century holy-man, and was built by the Marinid dynasty in 1339. Fabrizi's view shows clearly the richly carved stucco decoration framing the simple horseshoe arches; through one of these is seen the tiled mihrab (niche indicating the direction of Mecca) and the wooden minbar (pulpit). Fabrizi has captured the moment after the formal prayers when each worshipper makes a personal supplication to Allah, holding his hands out in a gesture to receive His blessing.

3540af77-ea01-5e4b-bd04-3e31d3b139e4.name: Poster for the International Exhibition of Milan, 1906, depicting the opening of the Simplon Tunnel
3540af77-ea01-5e4b-bd04-3e31d3b139e4.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
3540af77-ea01-5e4b-bd04-3e31d3b139e4.author: Marina Minozzi
3540af77-ea01-5e4b-bd04-3e31d3b139e4.keywords: Printing; celebration of science; Positivism; industrialisation; industry; communication; road; railway; tunnel; working class; rights of workers; social topics; post-unitarian Italian society; health; work; labour; poverty; life expectancy
3540af77-ea01-5e4b-bd04-3e31d3b139e4.third_name: Manifesto dell'Esposizione Internazionale di Milano del 1906
3540af77-ea01-5e4b-bd04-3e31d3b139e4.description2: Leopoldo Metlicovitz worked as a lithographer and an illustrator. Among his works are illustrations for the Milanese newspaper *La Sera*, opera librettos and some cover pages of *Corriere della Sera*. He also made posters for an auto exhibition, an insurance company and the opening of the Simplon Tunnel in 1906. The erotic male nude recalls Michelangelo’s figures. The poster was chosen by the Committee of the International Exhibition despite the fact the it was not submitted within the competition. The artist depicts the personification of Progress and Science ideally leading the convoy towards the light beyond the tunnel. The tunnel, almost 20 kilometres long, was started following an 1895 agreement between Italy and Switzerland. The works were finished after long difficulties and the railway was opened on June 1, 1906 and celebrated at the Universal Exposition in Milan.
3540af77-ea01-5e4b-bd04-3e31d3b139e4.holding_institution_org: Biblioteca di Storia Moderna e Contemporanea

en: Mocci, L., “Metlicovitz, Leopoldo”, in *Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani*, Rome: Istituto dell’Enciclopedia Italiana, vol. 74, 2010.

355b8a63-ea50-5b91-9873-7e2c8152cab8.name: *Catholic mission to Brazzaville: Brazzaville mission school - Vive la France!*
355b8a63-ea50-5b91-9873-7e2c8152cab8.description2: Evangelism and colonialism often went hand in hand, working together to Christianise local populations. The missionaries considered French society as the perfect model of Christian society, and the government thought missions would help consolidate colonialism. Schools were one of the places where this relationship is the most evident. This image clearly shows how the French instilled young African children with love for the French flag from a very young age.

35645306-e708-561a-ae81-24e697df6d15.name: *Woman In Oriental Dress*
35645306-e708-561a-ae81-24e697df6d15.author: Petar Petrovic
35645306-e708-561a-ae81-24e697df6d15.description2: In order to evoke and convey the spirit of the Balkans and the Orient as faithfully as possible, Paja Jovanović meticulously recorded each detail of the interior of a typical Balkan or Eastern house. He also collected props that made up a family’s inventory of furniture (e.g. the hexagonal decorative table to the left), and carefully studied the physiognomies and characters of the men and women he encountered in the southern Balkans, in Egypt, Constantinople, the Caucasus and elsewhere. The precision of draughtsmanship and freshness of colour in this painting by Paja Jovanović ranks it among his more successful works from the mid-1880s.

356abb7a-adfb-5423-8a02-b389733f2355.description: Velvet with silver stencilled decorations of arabesques with starts of six points. These decorations recalled the plaster decorations of the Spanish Muslim interiors.

3578fea3-edb8-5ff7-a0a7-aea81c138ad2.description2: Gold brooch based closely on Assyrian reliefs. Illustrates Assyrian influence on 19th century jewellery.

357f3042-331f-5bd6-8477-6430aa4c18a4.name: Ouled el-Hamra Mosque
357f3042-331f-5bd6-8477-6430aa4c18a4.history: Construction began at the end of the 18th century, but the mosque was not completed until the 19th century. It underwent several stages of expansion, especially during the reign of Sultan al-Hasan I, when similar mosques were constructed in Tangier and Asilah.
357f3042-331f-5bd6-8477-6430aa4c18a4.keywords: Religious building; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic architecture in Morocco; Islamic influence; traditional building; traditional city; city; urban space; Islamic city; Islamic urban space; plan; Moroccan city; urban planning; maghribi minaret; zellij; ceramic; applied arts; geometrical decoration; geometrical motifs; public space
357f3042-331f-5bd6-8477-6430aa4c18a4.description2: Occupying a space relative to its size, the mosque covers an area of 1,200m². Its square-shaped minaret is similar to those seen throughout the Muslim West, divided into five sections of sandstone decorated with green *zellige*. The *zellige* decoration is continued on the facade of the mosque, forming a lobed valance or *lambrequin*. Small rectangular openings are apparently recent additions, as are the green tiles on the pitched roof. There is a single fountain for ablutions.

3583d624-13fa-58e9-9d82-9ef1b2d476f5.name: *Beethoven at the Palace*
3583d624-13fa-58e9-9d82-9ef1b2d476f5.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
3583d624-13fa-58e9-9d82-9ef1b2d476f5.description2: Caliph Abdulmecid was interested in art in addition to administration. He opened many art exhibitions. He was chosen as honorary president of the Society of Ottoman Painters, which was founded in 1909, and he gave considerable financial support to the monthly journal published by the society. He took part in the Galatasaray Art Exhibitions with his paintings. For example, one of his paintings was accepted for an exhibition held at Galatasaray during the first years of the First World War. His works reveal him as a colourist and an accomplished portrait painter. Caliph Abdulmecid showed his paintings at the Viyana Exhibition, which was the first exhibition opened by Turkish painters in Europe in 1918.

359a8351-850d-54e6-b825-353190856a52.name: Small vial
359a8351-850d-54e6-b825-353190856a52.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
359a8351-850d-54e6-b825-353190856a52.description2: This small hexagonal vial is decorated with arabesques, floral motifs and Arabic inscriptions, written in cartouches bordered by red copper, reading "work is beneficial, courtesy is a matter of well-being, ignorance is baseness"

35b02f89-4d68-5272-8b1d-532de4511f6a.name: Pottery coffee-cup from Saudi Arabia
35b02f89-4d68-5272-8b1d-532de4511f6a.description2: Cups like these were used predominantly to serve both *qishr* a drink made from the outer shells of coffee beans flavoured with cardamom or cinnamon as well as coffee made from toasted and ground coffee beans. They were frequently glazed in shades of green and yellow. Earthenware cups such as these were gradually replaced by finer porcelain cups during the middle and later parts of the 20th century.

35b961a6-875c-5ccf-a80f-d6f917ccd48e.name: Jozef Zachariasz Bem (1795–1850)
35b961a6-875c-5ccf-a80f-d6f917ccd48e.keywords: Jozef Zachariasz Bem; Aleppo; Syria; Hungary
35b961a6-875c-5ccf-a80f-d6f917ccd48e.description2: Portrait of Jozef Zachariasz Bem as Turkish Pasha. Jozef Bem was born in the Austrian part of Poland. He fought as a Napoleonic officer against the Russians. In 1830 he participated in the Polish uprising against the Russians in Warsaw. In 1848 he was one of the leading Generals fighting with the Hungarian army against the Habsburg troops. After several defeats in 1849, he fled with 6,000 Hungarian-Polish soldiers to the Ottoman Empire. After converting to Islam, he became a Turkish General. In 1850 he suppressed an Arabic pogrom against the Christian population of Aleppo.

363a9b8e-3ef5-567b-a032-97afeab68478.description2: This photograph was taken by an unknown author during the excavations led by Ernesto Schiaparelli in Egypt. Schiaparelli (1856-1928) was Director of the Egyptian Museum of Florence from 1881 to 1894 and in 1894 became Director of the Egyptian Museum of Turin. The photograph shows a section of a trail in the south of Deir el-Bahri. It is easy to recognize the ruins of a residential district, which presumably hosted the workers and the artisans involved in the works for the tombs of the Valley of the Queens. Ernesto Schiaparelli, first as museum director and then as excavation superintendent from 1907 to his death, led several excavation campaigns around 1903-1914 in the Valley of the Queens, a place dedicated to the burial of wives, princes and princesses since the reign of Rameses I.

366a9ff1-e485-57a9-ad1c-a5eb7cf07698.name: Chest of drawers
366a9ff1-e485-57a9-ad1c-a5eb7cf07698.author: Ana Cabrera

366a9ff1-e485-57a9-ad1c-a5eb7cf07698.description2: This chest has a European shape and the decoration is near to Indian or Near-Eastern motifs. It has an Arab inscription, but only the date could be read it. This chest was probably made in India or in Egypt for the European customers who lived there.

36773e08-5d5d-510b-9eaf-d6bc145e39d8.name: Cigarette case
36773e08-5d5d-510b-9eaf-d6bc145e39d8.description: The Orientalism or Neo-Mudéjar style gave new light to old motifs as decoration in ivory or bone, with flowers and interlaces, as in this cigarette case. The decoration is strongly influenced by Arab pieces.

3684ea69-4081-5b3d-99c4-ac49b735a423.name: *L’escalier des lions* (painting)
3684ea69-4081-5b3d-99c4-ac49b735a423.holder: Palais de la Rose – Musée de l’Armée
3684ea69-4081-5b3d-99c4-ac49b735a423.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
3684ea69-4081-5b3d-99c4-ac49b735a423.keywords: Palais du Bardo; capitals; ceramic panels; Andalusian style
3684ea69-4081-5b3d-99c4-ac49b735a423.materials: Canvas, wood, coloured pigments, gold leaf
3684ea69-4081-5b3d-99c4-ac49b735a423.description2: This important painting depicts the official entrance of the Palais du Bardo as it was originally, with the *escalier des lions* and Mohamed Sadok Bey exiting the palace in official uniform, accompanied by Tunisian dignitaries, preceded by protocol officers and surrounded by the beylical guard. It shows the monumental *escalier des lions* with its archways and columns on the façade. We can also see its glorious white marble columns, capitals and ceramic panels decorating the walls and mounted on plaster and stucco (*naqsh hadida*). Through the entrance doors the black and white archways in an Andalusian style can be seen on the first floor.

36a5f8c4-91af-5cb4-9bf8-37f9eb7b40ac.name: *Sadness*
36a5f8c4-91af-5cb4-9bf8-37f9eb7b40ac.description: Amadeo de Sousa-Cardozo (1887–1918) was a famous Portuguese artist from the beginning of the 20th century. His career, which ended at the age of 30, is an example of international dialogue with contemporary artistic trends of his time such as cubism, futurism and expressionism.

36d231d4-e722-5471-936b-e81fdd08dc11.name: Coffee pot
36d231d4-e722-5471-936b-e81fdd08dc11.description2: Coffee formed the basis of all hospitality rituals in the Arabian Peninsula. The coffee beans were freshly roasted, ground and brewed in coffee pots whenever guests were received, and a strict etiquette was followed in the serving of coffee, with offence easily taken if any breach of the expected procedure occurred. Hospitality was a source of tremendous pride and no respectable host would be seen without a variety of coffee pots with which to honour his guests. In the Arabian peninsula, coffee pots were originally made of earthenware, but were replaced by more durable and ostentatious copper coffee pots.

36d58a55-2db8-5fb1-a95f-93e3fa5513d2.name: Ottoman Clothing Album
36d58a55-2db8-5fb1-a95f-93e3fa5513d2.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
36d58a55-2db8-5fb1-a95f-93e3fa5513d2.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
36d58a55-2db8-5fb1-a95f-93e3fa5513d2.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
36d58a55-2db8-5fb1-a95f-93e3fa5513d2.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

36e1b6b4-30ae-5caf-b227-73b35b67c02b.name: Fuad I, King of Egypt (1868–1936)
36e1b6b4-30ae-5caf-b227-73b35b67c02b.keywords: Fuad I, King of Egypt; Hussein Kamil
36e1b6b4-30ae-5caf-b227-73b35b67c02b.description2: Portrait of Fuad I, King of Egypt (1868–1936). In 1917 Fuad I succeeded his brother Hussein Kamil as Sultan of Egypt. In 1922, after Egypt had achieved independence from the Ottoman Empire, he became King of Egypt with the help of the British government.

370bd873-8035-59b2-bc6d-9c176b57e9d5.name: Ibrahim Pasha (1789–1848)
370bd873-8035-59b2-bc6d-9c176b57e9d5.description2: Portrait of Ibrahim Pasha (1789–1848). As the best General under his father Muhammad 'Ali Pasha, he fought successfully against the Wahhabites, the Ottoman Army and the Greeks. In 1831 he conquered Syria and governed it until 1841. In 1848 he deposed his senile father and was declared Vice King of Egypt by Sultan Abdülmecid I.

372e3810-b18e-5d0c-b107-9bd837cefb1e.name: Hijaz Railway Medal
372e3810-b18e-5d0c-b107-9bd837cefb1e.description: Medal of the Hijaz Railway fund. In September 1900, (the 25th anniversary of Sultan Abdul Hamid’s accession to throne) he addressed a call for all the Muslims all over the world to collect donations for establishing a railway between Damascus and the holy places to facilitate transporting the pilgrims. The call was responded to enthusiastically and with great support from all Muslims. Sultan Abdul Hamid II began the donations with 300,000 Ottoman gold lira, then kings and heads of Islamic world donated money or materials for setting the railway. The donations continued till 1907. On this occasion the sultan issued gold, silver and nickel medals to donors – for instance a nickel medal given to whoever donated 5-50 Lira, a silver medal for whoever donated 50-100 Lira and named them bey, and for donations of more than 100 Lira a gold medal and the title of Pasha. After that the donation become compulsory in which the officials disclaim a one month salary. This is a gilt nickel medal issued AH 1318 / AD 1900. On its obverse, within a wreath: tuğra of sultan Abdul Hamid II with "al-Ghazi" and form of locomotive and the date ١٣١۸ (AH 1318) below. On reverse, حميديه حجاز تيمور يولنه خدمت ايدن حميتمندانه مخصوص مدالية در ("Medal reserved to patriots who have served the Hamidiye Hijaz Railway") written in Divan script.

37704ccd-a34d-52a2-84f8-9695829027c7.keywords: Decoration; Silver; Silver chains; Jewels; Precious stones
37704ccd-a34d-52a2-84f8-9695829027c7.description2: These strings of jewels were used on the horses of Ottoman officials and indicated their high status and wealth. The chain consists of a small, red coral, semi-precious gemstones and silver pendants which would bounce against each other to create a tinkling noise and announce the arrival of the rider.

37bd3973-7cb4-5186-ac03-98cda4500caf.name: Ma’an honorary medal
37bd3973-7cb4-5186-ac03-98cda4500caf.description: A medal commemorating the victory of Arab armies over Ottoman forces in 1337/1918 and commemorating the leaders and the martyrs. On April 22nd, 1918 / AH Rajab 5th, 1337, Ma’an was captured by Arab forces after a decisive battle in which the Ottoman forces were defeated. King Hussein b. Ali created a medal bearing the name Ma’an medal, while the Arab revolts documents named it the Ma’an war memorial medal. On 11 August, 1919 when king Faisal became king of Syria, he issued a special law regarding the Ma’an medal, published in the official journal of the Faisal Government of Damascus, 13th November 1919; this law dictates seven articles. The medal formed two silver ears and two silver crossed swords surmounted by brass star. In other words, there is an equilateral triangle over each other and a ring on top. The two ears symbolize welfare and bestowal while the two swords are Arab Islamic Symbols of power and domination. In addition to that, the hexagonal star and Islamic Symbol appeared on Ayyubid and Mamluk Coins. The upper triangle tended upwards, the lower tended downwards, the word Ma’an is inscribed on the upper triangle in simple naskhi script and the date in A.H ١٣٣٧ is below. Historical novels indicate that the medal was made in France. The medal was given to 343 persons from the Arab World who were deemed worthy.

37f2def9-cf7f-5ab5-b473-ee0a55d36f21.description2: This simple implement is an oyster-shucking knife, known as miflaqa (pl. mafaliq).  Such implements are already mentioned in historical sources, including the writings of Al-Idrisi and Ibn Battuta. However, in those days, they were associated with separating and freeing the oysters from the seabed. In more recent times, tools such as this one were definitely used to open the pearl oysters.

3834322c-3b30-5333-9de0-37e6dc5efe5d.name: The statue of Hadrian
3834322c-3b30-5333-9de0-37e6dc5efe5d.dates: The Tiled Kiosk: 15th century; the photograph: 19th century; emperor Hadrian: 76—138 A.D.
3834322c-3b30-5333-9de0-37e6dc5efe5d.description2: Hadrian was the fourteenth Emperor of Rome (10 August 117 to 10 July 138 CE) and is known as the third of the Five Good Emperors (Nerva, Trajan, Hadrian, Antoninus Pius, and Marcus Aurelius) who ruled justly. The statue of the famous Roman Emperor Hadrian is located in the Roman hall of the museum. Hadrian was depicted with a figure under his foot. The statue was found in Crete.

3854487a-c60c-5835-adc0-fa6fe0ed8d59.name: Egyptian Furniture of the Italian Giuseppe Parvis Living in Cairo [Paris Exhibition, 1878]
3854487a-c60c-5835-adc0-fa6fe0ed8d59.author: Marina Minozzi
3854487a-c60c-5835-adc0-fa6fe0ed8d59.archival: *L'Esposizione di Parigi del 1878 illustrata*, Sonzogno Editore, 1878, p. 632.
3854487a-c60c-5835-adc0-fa6fe0ed8d59.keywords: International exhibition; universal exposition; Exposition universelle de Paris; pavillion; social change; applied arts; model; Moorish style; house; middle class; market; trade; Italian craftsmanship; Italians in Egypt; artistic exchange
3854487a-c60c-5835-adc0-fa6fe0ed8d59.copyright: Copyright image: Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale, Roma.
3854487a-c60c-5835-adc0-fa6fe0ed8d59.third_name: *Mobili egiziani del'italiano Giuseppe Parvis dimorante al Cairo*
3854487a-c60c-5835-adc0-fa6fe0ed8d59.description2: Giuseppe Parvis, who emigrated from Italy to Egypt, began extensive production of elegant furniture adapted to Arabian taste and decorated with mother-of-pearl and metal inserts. He won awards for his work at the Universal Exhibitions of Paris in 1867, Vienna and Philadelphia. Giuseppe Parvis is an example of successful businessman who successfully adapted to the Egyptian market. He was able to run laboratories with 50 workers and trained a large number of students in ebony furniture making. Over the span of 20 years he introduced and sold furniture to Arabian people who traditionally did not possess such furniture, using an Arabic style and taste and by using woods found in the East, Egypt and China.

385662fc-85ab-5e90-a9e6-c6b945d3350c.name: Egyptian mummy
385662fc-85ab-5e90-a9e6-c6b945d3350c.dates: 22nd dynasty (c. 950–730 BC); beginning of the 20th century
385662fc-85ab-5e90-a9e6-c6b945d3350c.description2: Romanian politician and doctor Nicolae Kretzulescu, his wife and their daughter spent the winter of 1868-1869 in Egypt at the invitation of the German consul, whose wife was Mrs. Kretzulescu’s aunt. They were very well treated by Isma'il Pasha, khedive of Egypt, who offered them a three weeks’ cruise on the Nile and put at their disposal a translator, all on his expenses. Before they left Egypt, Isma'il Pasha gave Kretzulescu a sarcophagus with an Egyptian mummy, which according to a description made by French Egyptologist Auguste Marriete, belonged to Bes-An, priest of Ammon from Thebes and dated from the 16th century BC. Back in Bucharest, Kretzulescu invited prince Carol of Hohenzollern to see the mummy and then donated it to the National Museum of Antiquities.

3858ddda-6751-5ea3-979b-6f668212f94e.name: Medal – the Congress of Paris (1856)
3858ddda-6751-5ea3-979b-6f668212f94e.description2: Dedicated to the Congress of Paris held after the Crimean War, the medal was designed by G. Loods and W. Kullrich. On the obverse, an angel is handing goddess Minerva an olive branch, the symbol of peace. On the margins are the heads of the rulers who signed the Peace Treaty of Paris: Napoleon III (France), Queen Victoria (Great Britain), Victor II (Sardinia) Alexander II (Russia), Franz Joseph (Austrian Empire), Wilhelm II (Prussia) and Abdul Medjid (Ottoman Empire). On the reverse is inscribed: *Pax Lutetiae Parisiorum D. XXX. MART. A. MDCCCLVI* (The peace concluded in Paris, on 30 March 1856). Regarding Wallachia and Moldavia, the congress decided that the Russian protectorate over them be ended and that they remain under Ottoman suzerainty and the collective guarantee of Great Britain, France, Sardinia, Prussia, Russia.

386fe084-5d31-5abb-9f36-fb457dd43935.name: Edward Jenner Inoculates his Small Son with the Smallpox Vaccine
386fe084-5d31-5abb-9f36-fb457dd43935.author: Marina Minozzi
386fe084-5d31-5abb-9f36-fb457dd43935.keywords: Medicine; health; vaccination; epidemics; disease; life expectancy; social changes; scientific development; social topics; post-unitarian Italian society; Positivism; celebration of science; international exhibitions; universal exposition
386fe084-5d31-5abb-9f36-fb457dd43935.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
386fe084-5d31-5abb-9f36-fb457dd43935.third_name: *Edoardo Jenner inocula il vaccino del vaiolo al figlio*
386fe084-5d31-5abb-9f36-fb457dd43935.description2: Giulio Monteverde was an Italian sculptor who started carving wooden crucifixes before moving on to sculpture during his years at the Academy of Fine Arts in Genoa. In 1865 Monteverde moved to Rome to study at the Academy of St. Luke. The sculpture of Edward Jenner (1749-1823) represents the British physician and naturalist inoculating for the first time, on his own son, the smallpox vaccine that he invented. This work was initially rejected by the Academy of St. Luke, entrusted with selecting works of art for the International Exposition in Vienna, but then exhibited in it thanks to an influential friend. The plaster cast of Jenner won the gold medal in Vienna, and a similar success was had with the marble version presented at the Universal Exhibition in Paris in 1878 when it won the medal of honor. The bronze version shown in the picture represents Jenner administering the smallpox vaccine to his son, blending dynamism and details in the face of the scientist, clothes and objects.
386fe084-5d31-5abb-9f36-fb457dd43935.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

en: Imbellone, A., in Elena di Majo and Mateo Lafranconi (eds), *Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Moderna. Le Collezioni. Il XIX secolo*, Milan: Electa, 2006, cat. 4.28.

387152c3-f2e6-5090-9494-72805f950568.name: AUB Tramway
387152c3-f2e6-5090-9494-72805f950568.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Rita El Hachem
387152c3-f2e6-5090-9494-72805f950568.description2: The Beirut tramway, which covered a total of 12 kilometres in the city's centre, was opened in April 1908, during the Ottoman era. It was used all through the French Mandate era and was finally closed in September 1965.

3879757a-f06b-5c78-885b-5bf3ddf848b8.name: *Convoy of pilgrims*
3879757a-f06b-5c78-885b-5bf3ddf848b8.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
3879757a-f06b-5c78-885b-5bf3ddf848b8.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph pilgrims; pilgrimage; travelling
3879757a-f06b-5c78-885b-5bf3ddf848b8.description2: The Hijaz Railway was a narrow-gauge railway (1,050mm/​3ft, 5 11⁄32 in track gauge) that ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. It got no further than Medina, 400 kilometres (250mi) short of Mecca, due to the construction interruption caused by the outbreak of World War I. The main purpose of the railway was to establish a connection between Constantinople, the capital of the Ottoman Empire and the seat of the Islamic Caliphate, and Hijaz in Arabia, the site of the holiest shrines of Islam and the holy city of Mecca, the destination of the Hajj (annual pilgrimage).

388495f6-3f6d-567c-a227-5d28fc8523c3.name: Palette
388495f6-3f6d-567c-a227-5d28fc8523c3.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
388495f6-3f6d-567c-a227-5d28fc8523c3.author: Marina Minozzi
388495f6-3f6d-567c-a227-5d28fc8523c3.keywords: Egyptomania; Gaetano Rosellini; university; collector; photograph; anthropology; palaeoethnology; material culture; Florence; Pisa; Egyptology; Nubia; languages; hieroglyph; William Matthew Flinders Petrie; Jacques de Morgan; David Randall-MacIver
388495f6-3f6d-567c-a227-5d28fc8523c3.description2: The cosmetic palette in slate is fish-shaped, as are many other objects found in both men and women’s graves in Egypt. It is linked to the practice of painting bodies with colours, probably for magical belief. The palette comes from a tomb excavated by David Randall-MacIver in 1902, who subsequently donated it to the Pigorini Museum in Rome. Along with the palette were found three clay scale models of ships. As a result of the excavations by W. Petrie and J. De Morgan, who documented the existence of an era preceding the 1st dynasty, Luigi Pigorini, director of the "Museo Preistorico Etnografico e Kircheriano" decided to increase the Egyptian archaeological collection. In 1878 he began to acquire important groups, but the main body of the collection was donated by Randall-MacIver in 1901, after the excavations he carried out on the behalf of the Egypt Exploration Fund in the town of el-Amrah, Upper Egypt. Another major purchase — from the Italian Archaeological Mission in Egypt (excavations of Hammamiye) led by Ernesto Schiaparelli, director of the Egyptian Museum in Turin — followed in 1905. The last main acquisition took place in 1913 when the Egyptian objects from Enrico Hillyer Giglioli’s collection entered the museum collection.

388c8605-7211-5829-b5d8-9e4bc739a3af.name: Photograph of the extension of the telephone network in Tangier
388c8605-7211-5829-b5d8-9e4bc739a3af.description: A photograph taken in 1920 showing the installation of a new telegraph pole and wiring in order to extend the telephone network that had been installed in Tangier since 1883.
388c8605-7211-5829-b5d8-9e4bc739a3af.keywords: Telephone; technical innovations; communication; telephone network; photograph; visual document; changes in urban space; modernisation; modern city; city

390fed84-29b4-5b5f-8552-8a2d440391d6.name: *Colonial Education*
390fed84-29b4-5b5f-8552-8a2d440391d6.description2: This article on the "colonial education" the youth received in France, published in a newspaper for the French community in Tunisia, has a didactic objective, encouraging and legitimising French economic colonialism in Tunisia, and thus also the migration of French youth to Tunisia.

392f3d7f-32c6-5e59-aeea-0cf54fb842cc.name: *The Victoria Nile - At Rionga's Island*
392f3d7f-32c6-5e59-aeea-0cf54fb842cc.second_name: Egypt. The Victoria Nile - exploration by canoe among the papyri
392f3d7f-32c6-5e59-aeea-0cf54fb842cc.description2: People had been trying to find the source of the Nile since antiquity. However, interest in this increased significantly in the early 19th century, and lead to various scientific observations. These observations were published and illustrated with engravings, which allowed Europeans to better understand the African continent.

39343989-0847-535d-82c3-ecbf42c6b4d6.name: Valley of the Queens, Tomb of Prince Khaemwaset at the moment of discovery
39343989-0847-535d-82c3-ecbf42c6b4d6.holder: Soprintendenza Archeologia del Piemonte: Authority for the Archaeological Heritage of Piedmont
39343989-0847-535d-82c3-ecbf42c6b4d6.author: Marcella Trapani
39343989-0847-535d-82c3-ecbf42c6b4d6.keywords: Egyptomania; scientific expedition; Vittorio Emanuele III; Florence; university; collection languages; Arabic; Cairo; Thebes; Luxor; Deir el-Medina; Egyptology; Nubia; hieroglyph; papyrus; papyrology; epigraphy; ostrakon; Nefertari; Ramesses II; Kha
39343989-0847-535d-82c3-ecbf42c6b4d6.copyright: Copyright image: Museo Egizio di Torino - Archivi Soprintendenza Archeologia del Piemonte.
39343989-0847-535d-82c3-ecbf42c6b4d6.materials: Silver bromide negative impressed on glass plate
39343989-0847-535d-82c3-ecbf42c6b4d6.third_name: Valle delle Regine, tomba del principe Khaemuaset al momento della scoperta
39343989-0847-535d-82c3-ecbf42c6b4d6.description2: Francesco Ballerini was an archaeologist and a curator of the Egyptian Museum in Turin. He worked at the 1902 Italian Archaeological Mission in Egypt led by Ernesto Schiaparelli. He also took part in four other excavations including the tombs of Khaemuaset (No. 44) and Sethherkhepeshef (No. 43), both sons of the Pharaoh Rameses III (1183–1152 BC). The tombs were found cluttered with wooden sarcophagi and mummies dating back to a period between the 22nd-25th dynasties, as the picture shows. Both tombs had been robbed previously and showed the pink granite sarcophagi already opened and empty. In the background the viewer can see the scene of the triumph of Osiris, God of the Afterworld. The God is flanked by two funeral genii, guardians of the gates to the afterworld.

3940c19d-aee8-57e8-88f6-9ecbdf782174.name: Ancient Egyptian Agricultural museum display hall
3940c19d-aee8-57e8-88f6-9ecbdf782174.author: Ibrahim Abdel Aziz
3940c19d-aee8-57e8-88f6-9ecbdf782174.history:
King Fu\`ad I chose the palace of Fatma Ismail, the daughter of Khedive Ismail, ‎to host the displays of the Agricultural Museum. The ‎palace was chosen due to its location near the Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture in the ‎neighborhood of Dokki in Cairo.  
The museum, which was first called "The Agricultural Museum of King Fu\`ad I", was officially opened for the public on the 16th of January 1938 in a big ceremony that the king himself attended.
3940c19d-aee8-57e8-88f6-9ecbdf782174.keywords: Agricultural museum; Dokki, Agriculture Palace; Khedive Ismail; King Fu`ad I; Princess Fatma; Khedivial palaces; Khedivial Egypt; Ancient Agriculture; Pharaonic Agriculture
3940c19d-aee8-57e8-88f6-9ecbdf782174.description2: The museum of Ancient Egyptian Agriculture is the most interesting section of the Agricultural Museum and it contains the most valuable displays. Tourist groups must receive permission beforehand in order to visit this museum. It represents the first section of the development of agriculture in Egypt ‎and it illustrates the ‎history of Egyptian agriculture from the prehistoric period till the late Pharaonic ‎period. ‎The first floor of the museum of Ancient Egyptian Agriculture hosts all sorts of ‎displays that illustrate how the ancient Egyptians cultivated their lands. The displays ‎include ancient tools and equipment that were used in the days of the Pharaohs and descriptions of ‎how the ancient Egyptians created these tools.

3948e69b-7a69-50c3-8b58-824c4c6e5d46.name: Moods: Those Who Go
3948e69b-7a69-50c3-8b58-824c4c6e5d46.author: Marina Minozzi
3948e69b-7a69-50c3-8b58-824c4c6e5d46.keywords: Migration; Italian migration; Italian painters; painting; sculpture; realism; artistic exchanges; Filippo Tommaso Marinetti; Futurismo; Futurism; unification of Italy; social history; social topics; Italian society; post-unitarian Italian society
3948e69b-7a69-50c3-8b58-824c4c6e5d46.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
3948e69b-7a69-50c3-8b58-824c4c6e5d46.description2: Umberto Bocccioni moved to Rome in 1901 where he was interested in painting, journalism and literature. Through his friendship with Severini, Boccioni attended Balla’s atelier and, at the same time, the school of nude of the Academy of Fine Arts in Rome. In 1907 he moved to Milan and met Previati and Marinetti, who wrote the Manifest of Futurism. In 1910 he signed the Manifest of Futurist Painters, in 1912 he signed the Manifest of Futurist Sculpture. His studies of Munch and Previati influenced the cycle called Moods. He starts doing numerous preparatory studies for the triptych: *Farewell, Those Who Go, Those Who Stay*; in which he set a correspondence between, colours, lines and feelings, moods. The painting is one of the studies for the series *Those Who Go* that belong to the first of two trilogies about Moods created in 1911, before the artist moved to Paris.
3948e69b-7a69-50c3-8b58-824c4c6e5d46.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

39965ec4-de1b-54df-b13b-6f3de0ef242b.name: Morse transmitter
39965ec4-de1b-54df-b13b-6f3de0ef242b.keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication
39965ec4-de1b-54df-b13b-6f3de0ef242b.description2: In 1840, the Ministry of Post made an announcement describing the postal service, declaring it necessary in order to facilitate communication among people. The first regulations about the postal organisation were taken from French Law in 1840. Ottoman Postal Code included 44 specific headlines. In 1855 the first telegraph service and in 1909 the first telephone service were put into common use as a demonstration of modern communication. In order to improve the technology of the telegraph systems, Ottoman authorities imported well-known machines with trademarks such as Siemens & Halske and Western Electric. As a result of this technological improvement, Ottoman officials decided to establish a telegraph factory. Between 1869 and 1915, this factory produced many devices and accessories.

39b49b4c-4d71-5eb2-ae22-21ea92dca300.name: Box with the image of an artillery emplacement of the Austro-Hungarian Army at the Sinai in 1916
39b49b4c-4d71-5eb2-ae22-21ea92dca300.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
39b49b4c-4d71-5eb2-ae22-21ea92dca300.keywords: Palestine; Bethlehem; Suez Channel; Egypt; Austrian army; war; warfare
39b49b4c-4d71-5eb2-ae22-21ea92dca300.description2: This silver box was made in memory of the Sinai Desert campaign embarked upon by soldiers of the Austro-Hungarian Army. At the end of 1915, two Austro-Hungarian artillery units were transported to reach the front at Gallipoli after a demand for support from the Ottoman Empire. In 1916, the 15cm howitzer battery was transferred to Smyrna and the mobile 24cm mortar battery was stationed near Haifa in Palestine to defend Mount Carmel. Other parts of the unit took part in the battle of Gaza and remained in the area till 1918. The last members of these Austro-Hungarian units were finally repatriated to Trieste in 1919.

39b4a764-56c1-5020-87f2-1df398a84d8a.name: Antonis Benaki's list of acquisitions
39b4a764-56c1-5020-87f2-1df398a84d8a.author: Mina Moraitou
39b4a764-56c1-5020-87f2-1df398a84d8a.description2: An album which once belonged to Antonis Benakis with photographs and handwritten notes on his acquisitions made the first decades of the 20th century.

39c4d9ff-e32f-5e06-bea2-e9873ae36a23.name: National Evangelical Church of Beirut
39c4d9ff-e32f-5e06-bea2-e9873ae36a23.description: The National Evangelical Church of Beirut is the first native Arabic Protestant congregation in the Middle East. It acts as the headquarters and administrative centre for the nine evangelical churches which operate under the name of the National Evangelical Union of Lebanon. Today, the church organises social, cultural, and educational activities, and runs two schools in Beirut and one in the Beqaa. It is also involved with the theological education at the Near East School of Theology in Beirut.
39c4d9ff-e32f-5e06-bea2-e9873ae36a23.author: Julien El Khoury, Jeff El-Msanne
39c4d9ff-e32f-5e06-bea2-e9873ae36a23.history: Established in 1848 by Congregational and Presbyterian American missionaries, the National Evangelical Church of Beirut is the oldest and largest of nine congregations situated inside Beirut. The church acted as a centre for the activities and celebrations for both the English and Arabic speaking communities until it was completely destroyed during the Lebanese Civil war. The clock tower was the only aspect of the church to survive the war, and the church itself was rebuilt in 1998. Today, it is fully functioning and located in Beirut's Central District.
39c4d9ff-e32f-5e06-bea2-e9873ae36a23.keywords: church; Evangelical; tourism; site; monument; religion; Protestant

39c5d2fa-be8f-55e6-97ea-9cd4b0e30514.name: *Constantinople et le Bosphore de Thrace*
39c5d2fa-be8f-55e6-97ea-9cd4b0e30514.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. Travelling in the 19th century became easier and more reliable due to the advent of steamships and trains. Westerners travelled to the East not only for touristic purposes, but also for scientific research, history, archaeology or for religious reasons. Western travellers told of their experiences and what they saw in eastern countries in their travel books and they even offer advice about the journey. Istanbul, where East and West meet, has been the subject of many a traveller's book.

3a20e143-6e36-5c47-8630-b7694a01419b.name: Jubbeh
3a20e143-6e36-5c47-8630-b7694a01419b.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
3a20e143-6e36-5c47-8630-b7694a01419b.materials: The original was made of cotton and satin
3a20e143-6e36-5c47-8630-b7694a01419b.second_name: Villager from the Beqaa Valley in traditional dress

3a2530bf-22b3-5651-bacc-f8a748c678a1.name: Headdress
3a2530bf-22b3-5651-bacc-f8a748c678a1.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
3a2530bf-22b3-5651-bacc-f8a748c678a1.author: Huda Kilani
3a2530bf-22b3-5651-bacc-f8a748c678a1.keywords: cotton; embroidered; gold coins; Ottoman coins
3a2530bf-22b3-5651-bacc-f8a748c678a1.materials: Gold, silver, cotton fabric, silk; casting; hand embroidered
3a2530bf-22b3-5651-bacc-f8a748c678a1.description2: A rectangular piece of cotton cloth embroidered with cross-stitching forming a bonnet with a line of 70 gold coins (*ghawasi*) sewn together on the front, with two pieces of cloth on the top sides with silver Ottoman coins and red stuffed velvet pursed from the back side with 7 silver Ottoman coins. The silver coins were used as money and as jewellery given by the groom to the bride, thus being an indication of his financial status. This object reflects the variegated population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It illustrates common elements and traditions in the area in fashion, costumes and social rites. There were no political boundaries at that period between the Jordanian and Palestinians territories. Some cities were like twins because of their close proximity and the exchange of trade goods and business.

3a359947-9b29-545c-9931-7f7be38d3ff5.name: Bracelet
3a359947-9b29-545c-9931-7f7be38d3ff5.description: This bracelet is made from engraved silver was made in 19th century Lebanon.
3a359947-9b29-545c-9931-7f7be38d3ff5.author: Marie Therese Moujabber

3a479e74-ad19-5334-a508-9d331c6ee9bd.name: 'Air force'
3a479e74-ad19-5334-a508-9d331c6ee9bd.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
3a479e74-ad19-5334-a508-9d331c6ee9bd.author: Giulia Barrera
3a479e74-ad19-5334-a508-9d331c6ee9bd.second_name: An Italian cartoon protesting the Italian aerial bombing of Libyan villages
3a479e74-ad19-5334-a508-9d331c6ee9bd.description2: In 1911, in Libya, the newly founded Italian Air Force carried out the very first aerial bombing of civilian targets in world history. Italian anti-colonialists vocally protested such practice, as Scalarini’s cartoon shows.
3a479e74-ad19-5334-a508-9d331c6ee9bd.holding_institution_org: Biblioteca di Storia Moderna e Contemporanea

3a6414c9-05eb-59ee-b5b1-43057ab8b195.name: *Chateaubriand at the ruins of Carthage*
3a6414c9-05eb-59ee-b5b1-43057ab8b195.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
3a6414c9-05eb-59ee-b5b1-43057ab8b195.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
3a6414c9-05eb-59ee-b5b1-43057ab8b195.archival: Chateaubriand, François-René, *Itinéraire de Paris à Jérusalem*, Tours, 1876.
3a6414c9-05eb-59ee-b5b1-43057ab8b195.description2: This engraving of the French poet René de Chateaubriand shows him sitting on a hill facing the sea, surrounded by the ruins of Carthage. Fascinated by Didon's city and its glorious past, the poet visited Carthage in January 1807, and recorded his observations in his book entitled *Itinéraire de Paris à Jérusalem et de Jérusalem à Paris en Allant par la Grèce, en Revenant par l’Egypte*, published in Paris in 1811 by Lenormant, in three volumes.

3a9203b3-ee28-58a5-9738-28760f62fc9b.name: Photograph
3a9203b3-ee28-58a5-9738-28760f62fc9b.dimensions: Height: 27.5 cm album, Width: 80 cm album open
3a9203b3-ee28-58a5-9738-28760f62fc9b.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
3a9203b3-ee28-58a5-9738-28760f62fc9b.description2:
This photograph is taken from a family photograph album. Most of the photographs in it are printed on platinum paper, which was introduced in 1879.  
Throughout most of the 19th century women had few legal rights to property, money, children, or even, after marriage, their own bodies. However, there were great changes in attitudes during the last decade of the century. The traditional role of women was questioned and some women openly defied convention. They educated themselves by reading widely and took up what were seen as 'un-ladylike' activities such as smoking and cycling. The free movement of the bicycle was seen as a symbol of equality and personal freedom.

3ab9503a-ce96-572b-920f-f71d81fadf1c.name: Jacket
3ab9503a-ce96-572b-920f-f71d81fadf1c.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
3ab9503a-ce96-572b-920f-f71d81fadf1c.description2: This small circumcision jacket from old Algiers is made of velvet from Gênes. It is decorated with a palm-leaf pattern and an acorn hanging between each pair of leaves. The sleeves and the edges of the jacket are decorated with a criss-cross pattern.

3abe2459-c22d-5b5d-907a-4be0147c9eec.name: Seated Berber woman (Nailiya)
3abe2459-c22d-5b5d-907a-4be0147c9eec.description:
The image depicts a Nailiya, a woman of the Berber tribe of the Ouled Naïl, in the south of Algeria. She is sitting among rich cushions, wearing a colourful silk dress and the jewels used to perform their traditional dance.  
The Nailiyat were independent women, free to marry men of their choosing. They moved to the cities in the North to earn money as dancers, in order to maintain their families in their community of origin. All this was not fully understood by Europeans. With the emergence of sex tourism these women were forced to introduce sexual content in their originally hieratic performance, and finally they were even considered as prostitutes by the French administration, in turn leading to being repudiated in their villages.  
Early photography contributed to forge this image of the Nailiyat in the European imagination.

3adb9096-0d5a-502e-a3c7-2ce892e11f6a.name: Beirut Evangelical School for Girls and Boys
3adb9096-0d5a-502e-a3c7-2ce892e11f6a.description: Beirut Evangelical School is located in Rabiye, a wealthy area in Metn, Mount Lebanon. The school covers all levels from nursery, to elementary, intermediate and secondary schooling. It consists of two large buildings that house all the school's classes, laboratories, offices and administration, as well as a church and the administrative Synod Building of Syria and Lebanon. The facades are covered in a yellow and blue coating.
3adb9096-0d5a-502e-a3c7-2ce892e11f6a.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
3adb9096-0d5a-502e-a3c7-2ce892e11f6a.history: The Beirut Evangelical School for Girls and Boys is one of the oldest educational institutions in Lebanon, first founded in 1835. It has its roots in the first school for girls founded in west Beirut in 1828 by the early American Presbyterian missionaries to Greater Syria. In 1959, the Presbyterian Church in the USA transferred to the National Evangelical Synod of Syria and Lebanon and who henceforth were responsible for the running of all the educational institutions in the area that had been founded by American Presbyterian missionaries.

3ae243ba-330f-5d5a-a7ac-1134d23470a9.name: The Ottoman Bank
3ae243ba-330f-5d5a-a7ac-1134d23470a9.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
3ae243ba-330f-5d5a-a7ac-1134d23470a9.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph bank; economy
3ae243ba-330f-5d5a-a7ac-1134d23470a9.description2: One of the world's largest photo archives, Abdülhamid II's photo archives – knows as the Yildiz Albums – contain about 37 thousand pictures from that period of the Ottoman Empire. The photo archives contain images of cities, buildings which were built by sultan, schools, students, soldiers, mosques, ports, government departments, shipyards, railways, bridges, bazaars, machines, locomotives and factories. The Ottoman Bank was founded in 1856 in the Galata business section of Istanbul, the capital of the Ottoman Empire, as a joint venture between British interests, the Banque de Paris et des Pays-Bas of France, and the Ottoman government. *Tanzimat* era's principal renovations in the financial field were the reestablishment of the currency and the foundation of the Ottoman Bank.

3b3c9b35-91d8-5460-af41-e16d0268e789.name: Orient Express Poster
3b3c9b35-91d8-5460-af41-e16d0268e789.description2: The Orient Express, owned by the Wagon-Lits Company, connected Paris and Istanbul between 1883 and 1977. French, German, Austrian and Ottoman diplomats and civil servants were on board for its first journey. In the early years, the travellers stayed in different hotels in Istanbul but starting from 1895, passengers stayed exclusively in Pera Palace, which was bought by the Wagon-Lits Company. The Orient Express did not run during World War I, from 1914 to 1918.

3b50b4cf-8492-533e-8f06-4e7806420158.name: Tsar Nikolai and his family visit Queen Victoria
3b50b4cf-8492-533e-8f06-4e7806420158.keywords: Diplomacy; Russia; England; Nicholas II; Victoria
3b50b4cf-8492-533e-8f06-4e7806420158.description2: Alix de Hesse-Darmstadt, who became the last Empress of Russia under the name Alexandra Romanova, was the granddaughter of none other than Queen Victoria of England. Nikolai II and his wife Alexandra stopped off in England on the way to Paris for their official trip in 1896, to introduce their first child (Olga) to her great-grandmother, Queen Victoria.  This photo is more of a family portrait than an official image.

As was typical, this necklace is not derived from an original, but a more free creation based on patrern books.

3c0de00c-d143-5139-b9fd-ae28536aadec.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury
3c0de00c-d143-5139-b9fd-ae28536aadec.description2: This map shows the railway line connecting Beirut and Damascus. The table on the right shows the distance between each city along horse tracks.

3c16e6a6-882d-588d-8f9d-b0309a8c41db.name: *The Empress' boulevard*
3c16e6a6-882d-588d-8f9d-b0309a8c41db.author: Dalila Orfali
3c16e6a6-882d-588d-8f9d-b0309a8c41db.description2: Painted in 1865, this canvas was one of many the artist created depicting "the new boulevard of Algiers". This boulevard, built by the opera house where Saint-Saëns was performing at the time, was the architect Frédéric Chassériau's (the painter's uncle) first significant work. It was inaugurated in 1839 by Napoléon III and the Empress Eugénie, after whom it it was named, and marked the beginning of Algiers' new, European-style urbanisation programme, which affected both the city and its surroundings. Although these changes did bring the city's inhabitants a number of comforts, they also resulted in the irrevocable destruction of a number of very important monuments from the Ottoman era.

3c18dfa3-8e52-5116-bf41-c9550b769ba0.name: Cup with a curved stem
3c18dfa3-8e52-5116-bf41-c9550b769ba0.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
3c18dfa3-8e52-5116-bf41-c9550b769ba0.author: Marina Minozzi
3c18dfa3-8e52-5116-bf41-c9550b769ba0.keywords: Applied arts; minor arts; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; model; reproduction; decoration; motifs; collection; collector; glass; Murano glass; glasswork; zoomorphysm; zoomorphic; floral decoration; floral motifs; vegetal motifs
3c18dfa3-8e52-5116-bf41-c9550b769ba0.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, and was part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. The Crystal cup with curved stem and appliqued aquamarine glass flowers and leaves dates from the second half of the 19th century. Baroque repertory inspired its form and use of floral decoration. A tendency toward abstract form is noticeable.

3c3428ad-e6d9-50dc-93c0-7e7ab1c900d2.name: *An Elephant*; *An indian Ox*; *An Antelope*
3c3428ad-e6d9-50dc-93c0-7e7ab1c900d2.author: Marina Minozzi
3c3428ad-e6d9-50dc-93c0-7e7ab1c900d2.keywords: Orientalism; painting; Orientalist painting; Italian painters; exoticism; artistic exchanges; France; international exhibitions; universal exposition; travel; imaginary trips; travelling artist; natural sciences
3c3428ad-e6d9-50dc-93c0-7e7ab1c900d2.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
3c3428ad-e6d9-50dc-93c0-7e7ab1c900d2.description2: In 1891 Filippo Palizzi donated more than 300 paintings to the National Gallery of Modern Art of Rome in order to describe his entire career through his artworks. All of them are cited in the Chronological List of 1853, which includes 12 studies depicting exotic animals done in The Jardin des Plantes in Paris. The series is considered the preparatory base for the amazing painting *Dopo il Diluvio. Uscita degli animali dall’Arca* (*After the Flood. The Animals Exiting the Ark*), commissioned by King Vittorio Emanuele II for the Museum of Capodimonte and presented in 1867 at the Universal Exposition in Paris. Other animals, like the Indian ox, the antelope and the dromedary were depicted in the Jardin des Plantes in Paris with the same aim.
3c3428ad-e6d9-50dc-93c0-7e7ab1c900d2.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

3cc5829d-ae99-58ec-bc85-707e431d5db4.name: *Edward Jenner*, Marble Group by Giulio Monteverde
3cc5829d-ae99-58ec-bc85-707e431d5db4.author: Marina Minozzi
3cc5829d-ae99-58ec-bc85-707e431d5db4.archival: *L'Esposizione di Parigi del 1878 illustrata*, Sonzogno Editore, 1878, p. 199
3cc5829d-ae99-58ec-bc85-707e431d5db4.keywords: Medicine; health; vaccination; epidemics; disease; life expectancy; social changes; scientific development; social topics; post-unitarian Italian society; Positivism; celebration of science; international exhibitions; universal exposition
3cc5829d-ae99-58ec-bc85-707e431d5db4.copyright: Copyright image: Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale, Roma.
3cc5829d-ae99-58ec-bc85-707e431d5db4.materials: Illustration from a magazine showing the marble group by G. Monteverde
3cc5829d-ae99-58ec-bc85-707e431d5db4.third_name: *Edoardo Jenner*, gruppo in marmo di Giulio Monteverde
3cc5829d-ae99-58ec-bc85-707e431d5db4.description2: Giulio Monteverde was an Italian sculptor who started carving wooden crucifixes and then moved on to sculpture during his years at the Academy of Fine Arts in Genoa. In 1865 Monteverde moved to Rome to study at the Academy of St. Luke. The sculpture of Edward Jenner (1749-1823) represents the British physician and naturalist inoculating for the first time, on his own son, the smallpox vaccine that he invented. This work was initially rejected by the Academy of St. Luke, entrusted with selecting works of art for the International Exposition in Vienna, and then exhibited in it thanks to an influential friend of the artist. The plaster cast of Jenner won the gold medal in Vienna. The engraving celebrates Monteverde's deeds. Chroniclers report that in 1878 the marble version of the group sculpture was awarded a huge prize at the International Exhibition in Paris: a gold medal and a hearty public welcome.

3cce65e9-b5bd-5b53-9b90-2b8d522d809b.name: Cup with serpentine stem
3cce65e9-b5bd-5b53-9b90-2b8d522d809b.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
3cce65e9-b5bd-5b53-9b90-2b8d522d809b.author: Marina Minozzi
3cce65e9-b5bd-5b53-9b90-2b8d522d809b.keywords: Applied arts; minor arts; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; model; reproduction; decoration; motifs; collection; collector; glass; Murano glass; glasswork; zoomorphysm; zoomorphic; glass filaments; Venice; Germany; Neo-Baroque
3cce65e9-b5bd-5b53-9b90-2b8d522d809b.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, as part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. The motif of glass filaments worked with pincers to look like crests, typical of the 17th century objects is used also in the ruby-red glass cup with snake-shaped stem of neo-baroque inspiration and dating from the second half of the 19th century. Its form is inspired by snake goblets common in Venice and Germany in the 17th century.

3cd5a4c9-7c30-53cb-877b-5bf9e71bca5b.name: *One Thousand and One Nights: Arabic fairytales tanslated by Galland, illustrated by the best French artists…*
3cd5a4c9-7c30-53cb-877b-5bf9e71bca5b.second_name: *This edition of the One Thousand and One Nights is a beautiful new volume of eleven hundred and twenty pages* \[…\] *subscriptions available in all bookshops: published in 52 installments.*
3cd5a4c9-7c30-53cb-877b-5bf9e71bca5b.description2: The *One Thousand and One Nights* played an important role in bringing the East and the West closer together. Galland was its first French translator, translating with much liberty the tales that he had been able to understand in the early 18th century. The translated One Thousand and One Nights were extremely successful, and became the subject of a variety of art forms, both allowing Europeans to become better acquainted with the Arab world, but also forming the basis for lasting stereotypes.

3cd68daa-dde5-568b-8623-dcdb17c2cf59.name: One piaster/Type 2
3cd68daa-dde5-568b-8623-dcdb17c2cf59.author: Aida Naghawi
3cd68daa-dde5-568b-8623-dcdb17c2cf59.keywords: Hussein bin Ali; ten piasters; Arab Hashemite Government; Mecca al Mukarrama; coin; currency; coinage; numismatics
3cd68daa-dde5-568b-8623-dcdb17c2cf59.description2: One piaster (type 2), bronze. On obverse, in the middle within a circle of dots, “*al-husayn bin ‘ali*” (“al-Hussein bin ‘Ali”). Marginal legend: “*amara bi-ta‘amul ‘abduhu wa-ibn ‘abdihi / sana 8*” (“It is orders to deal with, God’s Servant and son of God’s Servant, Year 8”). On reverse, in middle within a circle of dots: “*duriba bi-makka al-mukarrama 1334*” (“Minted at Makka al-Mukarrama 1334”). Marginal Legend: “*al-hukuma al-‘arabiyya al-hashimiyya qurush wahid raqam 1 bi-dakhili murabba\`*” (“Arab Hashemite Government, one piaster and number 1 is a square”).

3d0846e1-bd02-5620-aaab-623dc4af1ff9.name: Photo documenting the discovery of the Tutankhamun tomb
3d0846e1-bd02-5620-aaab-623dc4af1ff9.description2: The Tomb of Tutankhamun was discovered in 1922 in the Valley of the Kings by Egyptologist Howard Carter. The discovery of this tomb caused a wide media stir worldwide.

3d0e6f9c-00ca-5d85-9d59-e3d8520d4abc.name: Saint Georges Maronite Cathedral
3d0e6f9c-00ca-5d85-9d59-e3d8520d4abc.description: Designed by the Italian architect Giuseppe Maggiore in the neo-classical style, the Saint George Cathedral bears great resemblance to the Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore in Rome. The Cathedral's nave is covered with a coffer roof with gilding and a double-wood frame decorated with golden leaves on a beige-coloured fond, and the walls are decorated with stucco and marble. The Archbishop of Beirut sits in the heart of the choir.
3d0e6f9c-00ca-5d85-9d59-e3d8520d4abc.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
3d0e6f9c-00ca-5d85-9d59-e3d8520d4abc.history: The Saint George Cathedral is the seat of the Maronite Archdiocese in Beirut. It was built between 1884 and Palm Sunday of 1894, using stone from the Roman columns of the Temple of Deir al-Qala'a in Beit Mery. The cathedral is built on the site of an earlier church, from 1755, which was also dedicated to Saint George.

3d0e79a0-084c-5267-9ebf-6210134cee94.name: National Gallery of Modern Art in Rome
3d0e79a0-084c-5267-9ebf-6210134cee94.author: Marina Minozzi
3d0e79a0-084c-5267-9ebf-6210134cee94.third_name: Galleria Nazionale di Arte Moderna, Roma
3d0e79a0-084c-5267-9ebf-6210134cee94.description2: The Pavilion of Fine Arts, built for the 1911 International Exhibition in Rome and meant to become the permanent location of the National Gallery of Modern Art, was designed by the architect Cesare Bazzani (1873-1939). He also was responsible for the Department of Public Education and the layout of the Tiberine island. The Pavilion covered an area of 5000 square meters and was constructed in only 15 months. The building was designed in a sober classic style that merged perfectly with the environment and city landscape. The massive facade with the huge staircase and twin columns drew inspiration from ancient Roman architecture; the architect added to it more recent elements like Seicento festoons and the Borghese coat of arms with the eagle. The building celebrated the 50th anniversary from the Risorgimento (the unification of Italy) and affirmed the authority of the Italian state among the other countries.

en: Massari, Stefania (ed.), *La Festa delle feste. Roma e l’Esposizione Internazionale del 1911*, exhibition catalogue, Rome: Palombi, 2011: 144–45.
