3d283460-a96d-52c9-8396-14cc20cc6366.name: A young algerian girl
3d283460-a96d-52c9-8396-14cc20cc6366.description2: Between the late 19th century and the 1930s, it became fashionable in the West to take photographs of children, either for publication as postcards or with "anthropological" aims. This photograph highlights the striking contrast between the hardships of poverty and the young girl's smile.

3d2f1713-cb5e-5f8f-9e65-eae62c85f39d.name: A View of Street from Istanbul
3d2f1713-cb5e-5f8f-9e65-eae62c85f39d.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
3d2f1713-cb5e-5f8f-9e65-eae62c85f39d.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ancient Istanbul; Abdullah Freres
3d2f1713-cb5e-5f8f-9e65-eae62c85f39d.description2: The Abdullah Frères were a group of three Ottoman brothers of Armenian descent who were world-renowned photographers. They took pictures of scenic views and notable individuals, including sultans. Most of their photography was of the Ottoman Empire. In 1867, they sold their shop in Beyazid and moved to a more favourable location in Pera.

3d30eac6-fec9-5efa-aa61-82d8011a50af.name: Italian Workers Friendly Society (Tunis)
3d30eac6-fec9-5efa-aa61-82d8011a50af.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 41
3d30eac6-fec9-5efa-aa61-82d8011a50af.third_name: *Società operaia italiana di mutuo soccorso. Tunisi*
3d30eac6-fec9-5efa-aa61-82d8011a50af.description2: The Italian Workers Friendly Society was only one of the many organizations that the Italian migrants set up in Tunisia, ranging from the Chamber of Commerce, to Masonic Lodges, to religious organisations, to cultural associations and political groups.

3d414881-32eb-5cec-9499-511e26749367.name: Photograph of Bab al-Saraya
3d414881-32eb-5cec-9499-511e26749367.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
3d414881-32eb-5cec-9499-511e26749367.description2: Bab al-Saraya was the eastern gate of the city. Whilst other gates were closed at dusk, this was the only gate that was kept open until evening prayer. Thus, it was also commonly known as *bab al-masla*, meaning the worshipper's gate. The official name, Bab al-Saraya, comes from its proximity to the Serail of the Amir Fakhr al-Din by the Sursuq market. It was also located near the Amir Mansur Assaf mosque on the sea front. The gate remained intact until it was destroyed by the French authorities during the mandate era, in 1927. The headquarters of an-Nahar, a famous Lebanese newspaper, now occupy the site.

3d6a39d9-ddd3-5bbb-9a0b-ea068a2f864e.name: *The Great Mosque of Algiers*
3d6a39d9-ddd3-5bbb-9a0b-ea068a2f864e.author: Dalila Orfali
3d6a39d9-ddd3-5bbb-9a0b-ea068a2f864e.keywords: Old Algiers; traditional urban space; colonial city; Orientalism
3d6a39d9-ddd3-5bbb-9a0b-ea068a2f864e.description2: This painting was the first of Sintès' works to be bought by the museum on its opening in 1930. In actual fact it does not depict the mosque known as the "Great Mosque", but rather the "Djemâa ed-Djedid" (Jama'a al-Jadid) built in the 17th century in the style of the Turkish mosques from the city of Bursa. Here, the mosque appears overlooking the city's seafront ramparts, whilst the port neighbourhood's urban development does not appear to have begun.

3d995cca-af40-5f9f-8f23-5a077ea46883.name: Royal Decree to establish the post of *Makhzen*
3d995cca-af40-5f9f-8f23-5a077ea46883.description: The Royal Decree (dated 22 November 1892) of Mulay al-Hasan I asserted his *Makhzen* (royal authority) in order to take official control of the national post and transport services. In most localities, employees of this office were *‘Umana*, government officials, assisted by distributors.
3d995cca-af40-5f9f-8f23-5a077ea46883.keywords: Postal service; post offices; Moroccan postal service; communication; routes; port; rakkas; delivery; local postal service; foreign companies; private firms; postal network

3dfa891b-481b-5a43-b37c-1a41ad7c72c1.name: Resistance to the occupation at Oued Zarga
3dfa891b-481b-5a43-b37c-1a41ad7c72c1.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
3dfa891b-481b-5a43-b37c-1a41ad7c72c1.author: Bechir Yazidi
3dfa891b-481b-5a43-b37c-1a41ad7c72c1.description2: This photograph shows Tunisians attacking the train station at Oued Zarga. The Tunisian resistance caused the French troops many problems as they advanced towards Tunis, where they hoped to force the bey to accept the French protectorate. The attack at the Oued Zarga station, a few hundred kilometres to the west of Tunis, is an example of this. The station itself, which was built by the French, became a symbol through which Tunisians attacked French interests.

3e0c77fe-e569-53cb-a6e6-0d26f3ac626b.name: Coffee pot
3e0c77fe-e569-53cb-a6e6-0d26f3ac626b.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
3e0c77fe-e569-53cb-a6e6-0d26f3ac626b.description2:
This copper pot has been covered in a thin layer of silver and lavishly decorated. Its swelling shape shows the influence of the European Baroque style on the Ottoman decorative arts. Most metal coffee pots were made of cheaper materials such as tinned copper. In richer homes, coffee was served to honoured guests in pots like this one, made of precious metals (or imitations of them) and decorated in the latest taste.  
The Ottoman Baroque style developed from the 1740s as artists and designers began to apply non-figurative European motifs to Ottoman forms. It flourished until the 1820s, when new types of European ornament were introduced.

3e275eb6-4df9-58d4-9e6a-6769cd0b3ad8.description2: Photograph showing workers at the 1904 German archaeological excavations in the area of Abusir.

3e51e99d-8ff0-545e-95fc-52a15be8b042.name: *A Coffee House in Tophane*
3e51e99d-8ff0-545e-95fc-52a15be8b042.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
3e51e99d-8ff0-545e-95fc-52a15be8b042.keywords: Thomas Allom; Jivanian; Orientalism; painting; İstanbul
3e51e99d-8ff0-545e-95fc-52a15be8b042.description2: A Thomas Allom composition which appears in the first volume of Robert Walsh’s book *Constantinople and Scenery of Seven Churches of Asia Minor* is *The Coffee-House*. This is an oil copy of the composition by Civanyan. Written by Robert Walsh, who served as the private priest of British ambassador Lord Strangford after 1820, the book was published in two volumes in London in 1838. It includes engravings and the book, which was later published in French, acted as an important visual resource on Istanbul and its engravings were used as models by numerous artists. In the corresponding text, Robert Walsh provides information on the interior organisation and decoration of the coffeehouse and relates various details ranging from making music and smoking pipes to the plays of the *meddah* (storytellers).

3ea398ff-2713-5bdf-bb44-190566034004.name: Musée Archéologique de Sfax
3ea398ff-2713-5bdf-bb44-190566034004.author: Bechir Yazidi
3ea398ff-2713-5bdf-bb44-190566034004.history: Sfax, a port city in the east of the country, is Tunisia's economic centre and second city. Its town hall was built in the early 20th century, between 1905 and 1906. The builders and architects who oversaw its construction were largely Sicilian Italians and Tunisians. The town hall, built in an Arab architectural style, houses an archaeological museum on its ground floor which displayed mosaics and other Roman artefacts discovered in the ruins of Thyna.
3ea398ff-2713-5bdf-bb44-190566034004.description2: Located in the centre of the new town, Sfax's town hall is topped by a gored dome and overlooked by an elegant minaret with huge clocks mounted on its walls. It was built by the firm J. B. Pace under the supervision of the architect Guy. A section of the building was transformed into an archaeological museum. Today, the museum's collection covers every period of Tunisian history. It is divided between two floors and comes mostly from ancient Taparura, with contributions from the neighbouring archaeological sites at Skhira, Acholla, Tyna and some others. The collection includes many Roman mosaics, as well as ceramics, glasswork, coins and more from the Islamic era.

3eac8587-105c-522d-ac26-54e2094512db.name: Glass hookah base
3eac8587-105c-522d-ac26-54e2094512db.description2: Glass produced in Bohemia with a strong Middle Eastern influence. Acquired by Franks.

3ecd0c7a-1b74-5c15-9202-2b4414a57d9c.name: *Port of Algiers*
3ecd0c7a-1b74-5c15-9202-2b4414a57d9c.author: Dalila Orfali
3ecd0c7a-1b74-5c15-9202-2b4414a57d9c.description2: The artist studied at the École des Beaux-Arts in Algiers in 1905, under Hyppolite Dubois' supervision, and was taught to paint by Léon Cauvy and Georges Rochegrosse. In 1909 he was awarded a scholarship to study in France, and so entered the Atelier Cormon. In 1919 he won the Grand Prix Artistique de l'Algérie for his work "La Famille Attali" and returned to Paris, where he won his second Grand Prix de Rome. He regularly took part in Algerian and Orientalist artists' salons, and in 1934 he received his first commission. In 1936 he completed his first fresco, made of 8 wooden panels, for the Algiers opera house.

3ed77fd5-69e4-56f9-a0e5-48afa1165e32.name: The crown of king Carol I
3ed77fd5-69e4-56f9-a0e5-48afa1165e32.description2: Three years after obtaining its independence from the Ottoman Empire, Romania was declared a kingdom in March 1881. The coronation of prince Carol of Hohenzollern and his wife, Elisabeth, was settled for 10 May. Although the government wanted expensive and richly adorned crowns to be bought for the sovereigns, the king expressed his wish that his crown was made from the steel of a Turkish cannon captured by the Romanian army during the Independence War (the Russo-Ottoman war of 1877-1878), when Romania was Russia’s ally against the Ottoman Empire. Entirely of steel, the crown was made by the craftsmen working at the Army’s Arsenal. Queen Elisabeth’s crown was a smaller golden replica of the steel one and was made by an Austrian jeweler that had set up a workshop in Bucharest.

3f21696b-6178-5310-a618-3b1cbb1ec3d6.name: *Shéhérazade*
3f21696b-6178-5310-a618-3b1cbb1ec3d6.description2: George Auriol, the typographer renamed after his creations, was a multitalented artist, and thus in his work he reflected many different influences of the late 19th century. As an artist and musician, he was interested in the different graphic movements, as is clear from this image: the theme is clearly "Oriental", but the composition of the piece borrows characteristics from Japanese aesthetics and Art Nouveau.

3f284929-6dd8-5a5b-9540-23005e47ac6c.name: Colonial school in Paris, project of M. Maurice Yvon
3f284929-6dd8-5a5b-9540-23005e47ac6c.second_name: *Longitudinal view; Plan of the first floor*
3f284929-6dd8-5a5b-9540-23005e47ac6c.description2: In 1885, the French diplomat Auguste Pavie brought thirteen young Khmers to Paris so that they could see France. This "Cambodian mission" was soon transformed into a colonial school which accepted young students of French, Cambodian or African origins in order to train the future civil servants of the colonies. Over first two, then three, years the students studied a variety of languages, French law, and ethnology. in 1895 the architect Maurice Yvon, son of an Orientalist painter, was appointed as the architect for a specialist school on 2 Rue de l'Observatoire. Insipired by "neo-Moorish" architecture, the resulting structure became a key example of "colonial art".

3f2975b9-cd05-5386-b04d-d6926ecba53e.name: Women in the Revolution of 1919
3f2975b9-cd05-5386-b04d-d6926ecba53e.keywords: 1919 Revolution; Egyptian Revolutions; Egyptian Women; Political Participation
3f2975b9-cd05-5386-b04d-d6926ecba53e.description2: The Egyptian women of the 1919 Revolution – one of the most important Egyptian revolutions in modern times – which started due to objections to the practices of British occupation and the exile of symbols of Egyptian patriotism.

3f3b04ad-02fe-52ca-a1d1-f83f2e45161f.name: Electrical command and control panel for Tejo Power Station I generators
3f3b04ad-02fe-52ca-a1d1-f83f2e45161f.author: Fátima Mendes
3f3b04ad-02fe-52ca-a1d1-f83f2e45161f.keywords: Electricity; Tejo power station, workers, innovation
3f3b04ad-02fe-52ca-a1d1-f83f2e45161f.description2: Using this control panel, the generators at Tejo Power Station I were controlled from the electrical point of view.  The mechanical circuits were controlled locally, which demonstrates well the difficulty in maintaining a uniform electricity supply for consumers at that time. Power fluctuations were fairly common, and these were mainly noticeable in the indoor lighting.

3f4c6fa9-1eb4-5cf8-b351-d019a0e81489.name: Robert Hamilton Lang
3f4c6fa9-1eb4-5cf8-b351-d019a0e81489.description2: Lang was manager of the Imperial Ottoman Bank in Larnaka, 1863–1872, that ran the finances of the Ottoman administration. He conducted excavations at Dali (ancient Idlaion) in the centre of the island in the late 1860s. His report is the first systematic account of an excavation produced on the island. Lang went on to a series of posts with the IOB in Alexandria, Romania and Constantinople, becoming Director General of the bank. He was honoured by Queen Victoria, the king of Rumania, the Khedive and the Sultan.

3f6f9fb2-a5df-53ef-ab7b-89496d344816.name: Sword with scabbard
3f6f9fb2-a5df-53ef-ab7b-89496d344816.description: A sword and scabbard decorated with geometric and floral motifs and crafted in southern Morocco in the 19th century. Sword blades were imported from Europe, especially from Toledo in Spain, or from Damascus in Syria.

3f812372-02bd-5235-89dd-a89ca9e526fd.name: Desk
3f812372-02bd-5235-89dd-a89ca9e526fd.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
3f812372-02bd-5235-89dd-a89ca9e526fd.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
3f812372-02bd-5235-89dd-a89ca9e526fd.description2: This desk, an important object with great symbolic value, was offered by the Tunisian people to the great reforming minister, Khaireddine (Khayr al-Din) Pacha. The wooden desk is painted white, and a floral pattern decorates its drawers.

3f842425-2ace-59ff-ad9e-176b0b58c8f7.name: *Société les Affréteurs Réunis* \[…\] *Weekly, individual direct services from Rouen and Bordeaux-Bayonne to Algeria and Tunisia, and vice versa.*
3f842425-2ace-59ff-ad9e-176b0b58c8f7.description2: In Algeria and Tunisia, the French colonisers developed viticulture, cereal farming, and the extraction of minerals for export to France. The transportation of these goods took place by boat. Various firms emerged specifically for the transportation of this type of product, providing specialised ships and regular shipments between North Africa and the major French Atlantic ports. This map indicates the ports in Tunisia and Algeria and the railway networks connecting them (Oranais network, etc.).

4015cd67-07da-50de-ad09-a73de96638ef.name: Abdul Baha Abbas (1844–1921)
4015cd67-07da-50de-ad09-a73de96638ef.description2: Born in Tehran, Abbas left Iran because of religious persecution. He travelled widely in Egypt, Europe and the United States. In 1913 he settled in Haifa where he founded the religious sect of Baha'i.

401e4018-e1ee-5a6d-87f6-467eb15b5da9.holder: Central Institute for Ethno-Anthropology, National Museum of Arts and Popular Traditions

401e4018-e1ee-5a6d-87f6-467eb15b5da9.archival: Le Esposizioni del 1911, Roma Torino Firenze, Milano 1911, F.lli Treves Editori
401e4018-e1ee-5a6d-87f6-467eb15b5da9.keywords: Esposizione universale di Torino; industrialisation: exhibition building; pavillion; city; urban space; exhibitions and urban spaces; Moorish city; house; imagined Orient; Arabia; Egypt; Tunisia; Turkey; India; Japan; reproduction; model; book
401e4018-e1ee-5a6d-87f6-467eb15b5da9.copyright: Copyright image: Roma, Istituto Centrale per la Demoetnoantropologia, ICDE, Archivio storico.
401e4018-e1ee-5a6d-87f6-467eb15b5da9.third_name: *Le Esposizioni del 1911. Torino. La vita orientale e la grande kermesse*
401e4018-e1ee-5a6d-87f6-467eb15b5da9.description2: In 1911 the city of Turin organized an International Exhibition in the Valentino park, on the banks of the Po River. Beyond the Isabella Bridge another huge park was built to house entertainment and attractions. One of the most popular attractions was the so-called "Kermesse Orientale", in which the public experienced the illusion of making a journey through the different parts of the Eastern world. Five new areas were built, according to photographs taken at the time. The first one represented Arabian, Egyptian, Tunisian and Turkish environments while the fourth area reproduced Japan and India. The park also showcased a harem, a mosque and a Moorish school and the visitors could enjoy belly dancing shows and walks on camelback.

409e4adf-c1cd-577f-9523-9ffc50214d63.name: 'Ethnographic Exhibition' [Paris Exhibition, 1878]
409e4adf-c1cd-577f-9523-9ffc50214d63.author: Marina Minozzi
409e4adf-c1cd-577f-9523-9ffc50214d63.archival: *L'Esposizione di Parigi del 1878 illustrata*, Sonzogno Editore, 1878, p. 525.
409e4adf-c1cd-577f-9523-9ffc50214d63.keywords: International exhibition; Exposition universelle de Paris; international exposition; photograph; anthropology; ethnology; war; ethnography; ethnographic exhibition; book; magazine
409e4adf-c1cd-577f-9523-9ffc50214d63.copyright: Copyright image: Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale, Roma.
409e4adf-c1cd-577f-9523-9ffc50214d63.description2: Colonel Le Clerc organized an ethnographic gallery inside his own museum of artillery for the International Exhibition of Paris in 1878. He arranged 72 examples of warriors coming from almost every part of the world in a three-room exhibit. These characters were modelled from actual examples and resembled Arabic, Australian, African and Indian people with costumes and features. The exhibition paid great attention to facial renderings and the physical appearance of the warriors.

40b694ae-445b-54d8-b559-e424f0a605c7.name: *Alexander Karatheodori Pasha (1833–1906)*
40b694ae-445b-54d8-b559-e424f0a605c7.keywords: Alexander Karatheodori Pasha;Congress of Berlin; Bosnia
40b694ae-445b-54d8-b559-e424f0a605c7.description2: Portrait of Alexander Karatheodori Pasha. He was born in 1833 in the Greek quarter, Phanar, in Constantinople and served as leading diplomat (Premier Plénipotentiaire) of the Ottoman Empire at the 1878 Congress of Berlin. With the consent of the Ottoman government, Austro-Hungarian troops occupied Bosnia-Herzegovina.

40cc028f-a362-5724-b6be-dad14e9c2277.name: *Dagla zabun*
40cc028f-a362-5724-b6be-dad14e9c2277.materials: Cream twill, weave wool fabric, polychrome wool, embroidery threads, brown cotton knit braid, knotted brown silk buttons.
40cc028f-a362-5724-b6be-dad14e9c2277.description2: Men’s ceremonial coat style gown. Full-length A-line coat made from fine cream wool that was embroidered prior to being cut. It is likely that the coat was made from embroidered Kashmiri shawls decorated on corners and edges. Materials are cream twill, weave wool fabric, polychrome wool, embroidery threads, brown cotton knit braid, and 2 knotted brown silk buttons. This type of un-dyed wool is very fine, and we have only one. When this type of coat came back in to popularity, this specific design and color never appeared again. It is very rare. Lined with un-dyed silk in a natural color. There is a slit on the side for a pocket.

40e07960-2c59-5c21-8ff8-0aa9645bf0eb.name: Postcards showing Romanian tourists in Egypt
40e07960-2c59-5c21-8ff8-0aa9645bf0eb.description2: In the 19th century, North Africa was mostly known to Romanians from geography schoolbooks and newspaper articles. However, starting from the middle of the 19th century there are information about wealthy Romanians who visited North African countries, some of them recounting in their memoirs their African experiences. For example, Romanian poet and politician Vasile Alecsandri visited in September-October 1853 the Moroccan ports of Tangier and Tétouan and published his impressions in a Romanian literary periodical. A bit more than half a century later, four Romanian students entered an international competition for travelling by foot 100,000 km. In July 1911 they reached Egypt, where they visited Cairo, the pyramids, the Valley of the Kings, Memphis, Luxor, Karnak, Aswan, the Abu Simbel temples.

40e3019a-dd02-5de8-b6ab-7922650811cb.name: Grand Serail
40e3019a-dd02-5de8-b6ab-7922650811cb.description: The Grand Serail was built in the architectural style known as the "New Order" (Nizam Cedid in Ottoman Turkish), which reflected the new Ottoman military organisation. Indeed, its elevated location and austere facade are reminiscent of the Selimiye Barracks in Istanbul. The structure itself consists of two very tall floors, and a larger, 80m long facade. The eastern side consists of two symmetrical wings with two rows of 16 windows, joined in the middle by a protruding portico.
40e3019a-dd02-5de8-b6ab-7922650811cb.author: Hala Masri
40e3019a-dd02-5de8-b6ab-7922650811cb.history: The Grand Serail, or Government Palace, is used today as the Prime Minister's headquarters. It is located on a hill in downtown Beirut, close to the Lebanese Parliament. The building itself is the most important of the three Ottoman monuments on the Serail hill, and has been consistently in use for a variety of roles since its foundation in 1832.

40ef2328-28fd-59f1-96b3-b75abf4e6c58.name: *Bedouin of the Houran*
40ef2328-28fd-59f1-96b3-b75abf4e6c58.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
40ef2328-28fd-59f1-96b3-b75abf4e6c58.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
40ef2328-28fd-59f1-96b3-b75abf4e6c58.description2: The constant movement of large Bedouin confederations regularly impacted on the history of the Middle East, in particular when it intersected with settled societies and cities. The bedouins of Hauran lived in the Hauran plain in what is now SW Syria/ NW Jordan at the time. The Sheikh of the Hauran bedouins was employed by the Ottoman pasha of Damascus to collect tribute from all tribes in the area and help in its defence. Philip Meeder was a British wood engraver, who died in 1913. The image is taken from ’Picturesque Palestine, Sinai and Egypt’, Charles William Wilson ed., 1881. The accompanying text in the book reads: 'A bedouin of the Haurân. Bedouins occupy the north-west district of the Haurân; the plain is inhabited by peasants, and the Druses for many centuries have colonised the mountain range.

40f40e78-356d-5bdf-a281-3045eb71b83b.name: Hammam-el-Lif, Tunis. Seaside resorts and thermal springs
40f40e78-356d-5bdf-a281-3045eb71b83b.description2: Hammam el-Lif is a seaside town near Tunis. In 1750, Ali II Bey of Tunis had a pavilion built by the thermal springs, which Hussein II Bey then completed in 1826.

412af98f-597f-5bd8-9bce-18aac056c045.name: Jars from the Company of Glass and Mosaic of Venice and Murano [Paris Exhibition, 1878]
412af98f-597f-5bd8-9bce-18aac056c045.author: Marina Minozzi
412af98f-597f-5bd8-9bce-18aac056c045.archival: *L'Esposizione di Parigi del 1878 illustrata*, Sonzogno Editore, 1878, p. 340.
412af98f-597f-5bd8-9bce-18aac056c045.keywords: Applied arts; minor arts; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; model; reproduction; decoration; motifs; collection; collector; glass; Murano glass; glasswork; Venice; Salviati; book; International exhibitions; market; trade
412af98f-597f-5bd8-9bce-18aac056c045.copyright: Copyright image: Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale, Roma.
412af98f-597f-5bd8-9bce-18aac056c045.third_name: *Vasi della Compagnia di Vetri e Mosaici di Venezia e Murano*
412af98f-597f-5bd8-9bce-18aac056c045.description2: “The Chronicle of the Universal Exhibition of Paris” of 1878 celebrates the city of Murano’s commercial success in glass production. A large number of these objects reside in the collection of the Museum of Industrial Arts in Rome (M.A.I.), now part of the acquisitions of the National Museum of Antique Art on display at Palazzo Barberini. M.A.I. was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, as part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. These jars were manufactured by the famous glass company Salviati, founded in 1866 and established in Venice and Murano. In presenting these objects they claimed the rebirth of a long-forgotten antique art and the rebirth of glass industries in Italy. Tomb excavations brought to light a series of vases. New objects based on those excavated were made on the occasion of the International Exhibition in Paris in 1878.

4160c0f6-fb41-5587-96d2-e482623adff8.name: Shoes
4160c0f6-fb41-5587-96d2-e482623adff8.description: Purple velvet flat slippers, with leather soles in their natural colour lined with blue leather. The blade is decorated with floral and geometric motifs in enhancement embroidery of gold metallic thread.

416183bd-8afc-5737-8b32-4fcbb3e2e553.name: Ali ben Ghedhahem's seal
416183bd-8afc-5737-8b32-4fcbb3e2e553.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
416183bd-8afc-5737-8b32-4fcbb3e2e553.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
416183bd-8afc-5737-8b32-4fcbb3e2e553.keywords: Ali Bin Ghedham; Kasserine region; 1864 revolt
416183bd-8afc-5737-8b32-4fcbb3e2e553.description2: This seal, dating to 1864, belonged to 'Ali ben Ghedhahem, an educated man and the son of a qadi from the Kasserine region. He was one of the biggest figures in an insurrection triggered by the issuing of a decree to double taxes in Mejba, April 1864. The revolt started in the west, but quickly spread to the whole regency, with the exception of just a few coastal towns. However, it was soon qashed, and the violent suppression the people were subjected was not forgotten until the mid-20th century. The legendary hero 'Ali ben Ghedhahem was arrested and convicted.

4178a92a-1bcf-538f-a1a9-ee65fc839959.name: Saint Stephen Cathedral (Mar Estephan)
4178a92a-1bcf-538f-a1a9-ee65fc839959.description: The cathedral's construction was supervised by its architect, the Italian Giuseppe Maggiore. It overlooks the fishing port and was mainly built with local Batroun sandstone. The plan consists of a main nave, and two wards facing east and west. It has three altars, and a painting of St. Stephen lies above the central altar.
4178a92a-1bcf-538f-a1a9-ee65fc839959.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
4178a92a-1bcf-538f-a1a9-ee65fc839959.history: Saint Stephen's Cathedral (Mar Estephan) is a Maronite cathedral overlooking Batroun's harbour. It is notable for its size - being one of the biggest cathedrals in Lebanon - and its hybrid architectural style, combining a Byzanto-Roman style with Gothic influences. The cathedral was constructed in 1910 on the same site as an older church.
4178a92a-1bcf-538f-a1a9-ee65fc839959.keywords: Cathedral; St-Stephen; Byzantine; Roman; Gothic; Religion; Giosti; Giuseppe Maggiore; Batroun

41a2680e-8cf9-5ee5-a679-4297b5a1558c.name: Fındıklı
41a2680e-8cf9-5ee5-a679-4297b5a1558c.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; Pascal Sebah
41a2680e-8cf9-5ee5-a679-4297b5a1558c.description2: Pascal Sébah (1823-1886) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. In 1857 he opened his first photography studio, *El Chark Societe Photographic*, in Istanbul and by 1873 was successful enough to open another studio in Cairo. In 1860 he moved to another studio next to the Russian Embassy in order to work with A. Laroche, who worked in Paris. He continued to work with Laroche until 1873.

41adce0c-3867-5629-8e66-064e9b952e0c.name: Refugees' documents for refuge house after the population exchange
41adce0c-3867-5629-8e66-064e9b952e0c.holder: Population Exchange Museum (The Foundation of Lausanne Treaty Emigrants)
41adce0c-3867-5629-8e66-064e9b952e0c.description2: The 1923 population exchange between Greece and Turkey was based upon religious identity, and involved the Greek Orthodox citizens of Turkey and the Muslim citizens of Greece. The "Convention Concerning the Exchange of Greek and Turkish Populations" was signed at Lausanne, Switzerland, on 30 January 1923, by the governments of Greece and Turkey. These are refugees' documents for the Papoukidis family's stay at a refuge house.

41c0d246-c999-5ff4-8002-64210176e2eb.name: An old exhibition from Tiled Kiosk
41c0d246-c999-5ff4-8002-64210176e2eb.dates: The Tiled Kiosk: 15th century; The photograph: 19th century
41c0d246-c999-5ff4-8002-64210176e2eb.description2: The Tiled Kiosk is a pavilion set within the outer walls of Topkapı Palace that dates from 1472. It was built by the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II as a pleasure palace or kiosk. The building was used as the Imperial Museum between 1875 and 1891. In 1953, it was opened to the public as a museum of Turkish and Islamic art, and was later incorporated into the Istanbul Archaeology Museums. The collections of the Tiled Kiosk Museum consist of about 2000 artefacts belonging to the Seljuk and Ottoman eras, dating from the 11th-20th centuries. These artefacts include those that existed when the museum was incorporated into the İstanbul Archaeological Museums due to its proximity as well as those acquired through excavations, purchases, donations and confiscations.

41d110ef-ea08-56b4-9331-39d56114f999.name: Portrait of Archduke Maximilian
41d110ef-ea08-56b4-9331-39d56114f999.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
41d110ef-ea08-56b4-9331-39d56114f999.description2: Portrait of the Archduke Ferdinand Maximilian, who was commander of the Austrian Navy. In 1855 he visited parts of the Ottoman Empire including Smyrna, Palestine and Egypt.

41f94376-0122-5f5e-ba32-dbcad66db68a.name: Watercolour by Claude R. Conder
41f94376-0122-5f5e-ba32-dbcad66db68a.description2: Watercolour by Claude R. Conder, made during the Survey of Western Palestine, showing one of the members of the SWP at work with one of the expedition’s theodolites. The technology they used was the latest cutting edge equipment and techniques available to the Royal Engineers, far in advance on what was being used, for example, by the US Army Corps of Engineers of the day, as was demonstrated when Lieut. Steever, of the Corps of Engineers carried out a similar survey in Transjordan.

42290171-ded6-5da8-9103-76fb7763204e.name: *The Attack of the Enemy’s Cavalry at Shinaass January 2nd, 1810*
42290171-ded6-5da8-9103-76fb7763204e.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
42290171-ded6-5da8-9103-76fb7763204e.dimensions: 505 mm x 602 mm (framed); image: 215 mm x 358 mm
42290171-ded6-5da8-9103-76fb7763204e.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
42290171-ded6-5da8-9103-76fb7763204e.artist: R. Temple, HM 65th Regiment, Sixteen views; I. Clark, Sculpt.; William Haines, Publisher
42290171-ded6-5da8-9103-76fb7763204e.description2: This image, recorded by a British soldier, who participated in the campaign to destroy the Qawasim's economic hegemony in the Lower Gulf, shows a group of Arab fighters, those on horseback carrying lances, those on foot swords, engaged in fierce combat outside the fortress of Shinas, a Qawasim stronghold on the east coast the British turned to after destroying their bases in Ras al Khaimah and on the Persian coast. Seemingly endless rows of British artillery and infantry are approaching from the beach on the right, with the mast of the British frigates clearly visible at sea. For their attack on the east coast postions of the Qawasim, the British enlisted the support of Omani forces, and it is presumably them that are engaging the mounted Qawasim fighters in this image. British eye witnesses report that the Qawasim fought extremely bravely and obstinately, preferring death to surrender. Nevertheless, the overwhelming military machine of the British eventually took Shinas, with at least 400 Qawasim casualities.

423021cf-ae6a-5fd5-a257-4aa4a79ded1d.name: *Pedestal of the Obelisk in the Ancient Byzatine Hippodrome*
423021cf-ae6a-5fd5-a257-4aa4a79ded1d.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
423021cf-ae6a-5fd5-a257-4aa4a79ded1d.keywords: Istanbul photography; Byzantine and Ottoman architecture
423021cf-ae6a-5fd5-a257-4aa4a79ded1d.description2: A frequently employed device in Robertson's Istanbul photographs is the inclusion of the one or more human figures in the foreground – indeed, this is something of a trademark of Robertson’s work. There were two main reasons for the inclusion of these figures. For one thing, the artist used them as a way of creating a more natural scene. The other was to provide one or more reference points so that the photograph’s viewers could get an idea of the dimensions of the scene they were looking at and of the elements contained therein.

427783d7-27c6-57e4-9e7c-ee894a6d6e9d.name: The Hotel Excelsior at the Lido in Venice at the end of construction work
427783d7-27c6-57e4-9e7c-ee894a6d6e9d.holder: Archivio Progetti – Università Iuav di Venezia
427783d7-27c6-57e4-9e7c-ee894a6d6e9d.author: Riccardo Domenichini
427783d7-27c6-57e4-9e7c-ee894a6d6e9d.description2: The photograph shows the Hotel Excelsior on the beach of the Lido sandbar which separates the Venice lagoon from the sea. The building appears to be almost finished but not yet open: since the hotel was inaugurated in 1908, the photograph was probably shot before then. Giovanni Sardi was one of the most gifted architects of the eclectic generation. Here, he uses elements of the Moorish architecture like minarets and domes mixed with decorations in the Art Nouveau style and medieval elements, to emphasize the character of the building as a fabulous place for holidays and amusement.

427b0484-9935-51b8-bf73-9f3ed319e742.name: Laboratorio Chimico of Lisbon Polytechnic School
427b0484-9935-51b8-bf73-9f3ed319e742.holder: National Museum of Natural History and Science (MUHNAC) / Museums of the University of Lisbon
427b0484-9935-51b8-bf73-9f3ed319e742.author: Marta C. Lourenço (MUHNAC-UL)
427b0484-9935-51b8-bf73-9f3ed319e742.history: The Laboratorio Chimico was built in the 1850s, later profoundly restructured during the 1880s and 90s. It was intensely used for teaching and research until 1998, when the Chemistry Department moved to the new campus of the Faculty of Sciences at cidade universitária. The complementary laboratories and rooms were quite modified during the 1960s and 1970s due to the large increase of teachers, students and researchers. The Museum started its recovery and musealization in 1998, which sought restitution of the original design of the Laboratorio’s golden age (1890s) in all areas. Therefore the 60s and 70s partitions and mezzanines were removed. The Laboratorio opened to the public in 2007.
427b0484-9935-51b8-bf73-9f3ed319e742.keywords: Chemistry; History of Chemistry; Laboratory; Integrated Heritage; National Museum of Natural History and Science; University of Lisbon
427b0484-9935-51b8-bf73-9f3ed319e742.architects: Author of the Laboratorio Chimico, gallery and amphitheatre: architect João Pedro Monteiro (original project dating from 1852, continued by Pierre-Joseph Pézerat); A considerable refurbishment was supervised by José Júlio Bettencourt Rodrigues between 1888 and 1890 but the architect is unknown
427b0484-9935-51b8-bf73-9f3ed319e742.description2: The Laboratorio, together with the Amphitheatre and other complementary areas, occupies a surface area of 800 m2 in the west wing of the main building of MUHNAC. Its monumentality, functionality have been praised since its construction. In a first approach it has relevance for its beauty, singularity and for the authentic atmosphere provided to visitors. The Laboratorio Chimico is relevant for the history of chemistry and its teaching, particularly in Portugal, and it’s a historical document in itself, completed by a vast archival and iconographic documentation that complements and enhances the Laboratorio’s importance as a source for the history of science. Finally, the existence of one of the most important chemistry collections of Europe, derived from this site, is worth mentioning.

42a12e5a-4f49-5af5-9a9c-e5db696bbced.name: Portrait of a Lady
42a12e5a-4f49-5af5-9a9c-e5db696bbced.description: The decoration of the cabinet represented in this painting is clearly influenced by Islamic art in the details of the arches and the motifs in Neo-Mudéjar style. This decoration is related to the different publications about the Alhambra or the drawings by Carderera, in which the designers and artists found new inspiration for their works.
42a12e5a-4f49-5af5-9a9c-e5db696bbced.author: Ana Cabrera
42a12e5a-4f49-5af5-9a9c-e5db696bbced.artist: Antonio Maria Esquivel y Suárez de Urbina

42a328aa-1821-5971-b533-2606dafaee02.name: The excavation of Mount Nemrut
42a328aa-1821-5971-b533-2606dafaee02.archival: *Le tumulus de Nemroud-Dagh. Voyage, description, inscriptions avec plans et photographies*, İstanbul, F. Loeffler, 1883.
42a328aa-1821-5971-b533-2606dafaee02.keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters; archaeological excavations
42a328aa-1821-5971-b533-2606dafaee02.description2: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen were exposed to Western ideas through education and travel. The museum was founded by decree in 1891 as the Imperial Museum. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi. Hamdi began construction of the main building in 1881, and it achieved its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. It is one of the prominent structures built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul. Osman Hamdi, during his tenure as museum director, launched the first Turkish scientific excavations. He carried out archaeological excavations at Mount Nemrut, Laguna and Sidon.

42b5c7f1-cc74-5b88-8ab4-25e33352b53f.name: Gilet
42b5c7f1-cc74-5b88-8ab4-25e33352b53f.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
42b5c7f1-cc74-5b88-8ab4-25e33352b53f.description2: This bodice (*frimla*) was worn by young Algerian women. The back is decorated with an interlaced pattern, emerging from a stylised vase. Young Muslim and Jewish girls wore this gilet.

42fe8774-fad6-50ab-b638-8b0201d5f61c.name: Documentary photograph illustrating Morocco's participation in the Universal Exhibition, Paris
42fe8774-fad6-50ab-b638-8b0201d5f61c.description: A caption in *Le panorama* at the 1900 Paris Exhibition reads: “At the foot of the Eiffel Tower in an English landscaped garden, near a small lake in the shade of a clump of poplars, the pavilions of Morocco, dominated by the minaret of Tétouan, form an unexpected decor. The bazaars of Fez and Rabat flow into the bright green notes of their colourful awnings.”
42fe8774-fad6-50ab-b638-8b0201d5f61c.holder: National Library of the Kingdom of Morocco
42fe8774-fad6-50ab-b638-8b0201d5f61c.archival: Published in: *Le panorama, Exposition universelle*, Paris: Librairie d'Art Ludovic Baschet, 1900.
42fe8774-fad6-50ab-b638-8b0201d5f61c.keywords: International Exhibition; universal exposition; Exposition universelle de Paris; pavillion; exhibition building; Moorish city; exhibitions and urban spaces; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; reproduction; model; suq; curiosities; exoticism; magazine

4318dbfb-9a52-562e-8cea-6daf8a6a9d78.name: Rumelia Railway
4318dbfb-9a52-562e-8cea-6daf8a6a9d78.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
4318dbfb-9a52-562e-8cea-6daf8a6a9d78.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Anatolian Railways
4318dbfb-9a52-562e-8cea-6daf8a6a9d78.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

4322212d-bcef-58d6-b7e4-182fd69c53da.name: An Italian family at the end of the 19th century
4322212d-bcef-58d6-b7e4-182fd69c53da.archival: AS Terni, Archivio Gisa Giani, Album “Donne di Terni dentro e fuori la fabbrica"
4322212d-bcef-58d6-b7e4-182fd69c53da.third_name: 'Gradassi-Luzi con la moglie e la figlia Faustina'

433df55d-0327-5977-a447-ca5420a7ce29.name: Laënnec examining a patient at the Necker Hospital in 1816
433df55d-0327-5977-a447-ca5420a7ce29.description2: The 19th century saw a number of important advances in the medical field. René Laënnec (1781–1926) was a French doctor who invented the stethoscope, allowing him to improve medical diagnoses by listening to patients' chests. Doctors were thus able to analyse sounds inside the body, and link them to illnesses such as tuberculosis, which was very common in the 19th century.

43466c72-e5b9-5030-8983-576a5a27f879.name: Alexander I Obrenovic, King of Serbia (1876–1903)
43466c72-e5b9-5030-8983-576a5a27f879.keywords: Edmund Count Szecheny; Budapest; Hungary; Istanbul, Ottoman empire; fire brigade
43466c72-e5b9-5030-8983-576a5a27f879.description2: Portrait of Alexander I Obrenovic, King of Serbia (1876–1903) as a young man. Between the abdication of his father in 1889 and his proclamation as a king in 1893, his mother Natalija Obrenovic ruled as a regent. Being a close ally of Austria, he became Serbian King in 1893. In 1894 Alexander abolished the liberal constitution of Serbia. In 1900 he married Draga Masin, a former lady-in-waiting of his mother. This marriage was very unpopular and weakened the political position of the king. In 1903 he and his wife were murdered by a group of Serbian officers.

43887649-28e4-5e71-ad7d-9a1cc8750dfc.name: *Art exhibition at school, 12–25 June, 1904*
43887649-28e4-5e71-ad7d-9a1cc8750dfc.description2: The introduction of art as a primary school subject was a long and difficult process. Linear drawing was introduced first with a utilitarian objective. From 1879, teaching art became mandatory due to a standardization of teaching practices, and specialised teachers were recruited for this purpose. From the early 20th century onwards art became, supposedly, the art of depicting reality. Various organisations also pushed for the democratisation of art in schools. This poster shows a school student taking interest in famous paintings, such as those by Millet.

43a8c5d9-b3aa-529b-a3f9-5e64b5b32a48.name: The Pearl Carpet
43a8c5d9-b3aa-529b-a3f9-5e64b5b32a48.materials: Pearls, silk, deer hide, beads, gems
43a8c5d9-b3aa-529b-a3f9-5e64b5b32a48.description2: The foundation of silk and fine deer hide is densely embroidered overall with a design worked in strings of natural ‘Basra’ pearls, measuring approximately 1-3 mm, and English coloured glass beads. There are on average 78 pearls and beads per vertical dm. (10 cm), and 68 per horizontal dm., equaling a density of c.4,990 pearls and beads per dm2. The total area of the carpet is c. 45,670 cm2. The 32 smaller rosettes cover an area of c. 400 cm2 with smaller gems, and the total area embroidered with pearls and is beads is approximately 44,500 cm2. Therefore, over 2.2 million pearls and beads have been used to decorate the field. In our estimation, the number of pearls employed in the design is therefor at least 1.2-1.5 million.

43b2594e-92cf-584f-b624-afc4b94a968d.name: Giovanni Miani (1810–1872)
43b2594e-92cf-584f-b624-afc4b94a968d.description2: Portrait of Giovanni Miani (1810–1872). Born in Northern Italy, he was an intellectual who was forced by Austrian authorities to seek exile in the Ottoman Empire. He lived in Athens, Smyrna and Egypt and was one of the European explorers who tried to find the sources of the Nile.

43d0d694-677d-5b4d-8c60-e240f267874f.name: Rome: the Ministry of Finance, in Via XX Settembre
43d0d694-677d-5b4d-8c60-e240f267874f.holder: Central Institute for Cataloguing and Documentation (ICCD)

44156a31-6bfc-5a44-9e81-6e02ec39aee7.name: Jacket
44156a31-6bfc-5a44-9e81-6e02ec39aee7.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
44156a31-6bfc-5a44-9e81-6e02ec39aee7.description2: This short men's jacket is embroidered on the two front panels, with a decoration consisting of curls, all ending in a hook shape and bordered by a floral motif emerging from a stylised vase. The open, elbow-length sleeves are decorated with geometric motifs. The sleeves are secured by small, mother-of-pearl buttons. This formal jacket was worn for important ceremonies.

441fd91e-6a8d-5ba0-b0fb-73ae59155d8a.name: *Voyage Dans Le Levant*
441fd91e-6a8d-5ba0-b0fb-73ae59155d8a.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. Travelling in the 19th century became easier and more reliable due to the advent of steamships and trains. Westerners travelled to the East not only for touristic purposes, but also for scientific research, history, archaeology or for religious reasons. Western travellers told of their experiences and what they saw in eastern countries in their travel books and they even offer advice about the journey. Istanbul, where East and West meet, has been the subject of many a traveller's book.

4430deb8-bf37-5372-9e9f-04d0591d1efa.name: Documentary photograph depicting Morocco's participation at the Exposition Universelle, Paris
4430deb8-bf37-5372-9e9f-04d0591d1efa.description: At the 1900 Paris Exposition, not far from one of the pillars of the Eiffel Tower, the architect Henri-Jules Saladin designed the “Moroccan” pavilion inside the *Palais d’Optiques*. The main body of this exhibition building reproduced the appearance of a mosque, surrounded by an outdoor “bazaar”. The Moroccan exhibition itself was inside the mosque and comprised a collection of Moroccan-made artefacts and raw materials.
4430deb8-bf37-5372-9e9f-04d0591d1efa.holder: National Library of the Kingdom of Morocco
4430deb8-bf37-5372-9e9f-04d0591d1efa.archival: Published in: *Le panorama, Exposition universelle*, Paris, Librairie d'Art Ludovic Baschet, 1900.
4430deb8-bf37-5372-9e9f-04d0591d1efa.keywords: International Exhibition; universal exposition; exhibition building; Moorish city; exhibitions and urban spaces; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; reproduction; model; suq; magazine; Manuel d’art musulman; scientific expedition

443b06f0-b14c-5ef9-9ab2-20b5d7d56003.name: *Clothes for prisoners of war. Charitable organisation attached the French \[Red Cross\]. Donations both in cash and in kind should be delivered to the organisation's headquarters, at 63 Avenue des Champs-Elysées.*
443b06f0-b14c-5ef9-9ab2-20b5d7d56003.keywords: Hygiene; Red Cross; First World War
443b06f0-b14c-5ef9-9ab2-20b5d7d56003.description2: Throughout the First World War, many charitable organisations came to the aid of soldiers and civilian populations in occupied territories. They carried out poster campaigns or published appeals in the press to obtain donations. This poster depicts a military prisoner of war's sadness as he writes to his loved ones. The Red Cross supervised these charitable partnerships in order to ensure the safe arrival of the donations in "enemy" territory.

4454c9bf-8d06-539a-b793-d2ce0b56e6f8.name: Pearl Diver’s Nose Clip
4454c9bf-8d06-539a-b793-d2ce0b56e6f8.type: Horn pearl diver's nose clip on cotton string
4454c9bf-8d06-539a-b793-d2ce0b56e6f8.holder: Sharjah Maritime Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
4454c9bf-8d06-539a-b793-d2ce0b56e6f8.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
4454c9bf-8d06-539a-b793-d2ce0b56e6f8.dimensions: Length of the horn nose clip c. 60 mm
4454c9bf-8d06-539a-b793-d2ce0b56e6f8.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
4454c9bf-8d06-539a-b793-d2ce0b56e6f8.keywords: futam, aftama; khubat; libas al-ghawas; dyyin
4454c9bf-8d06-539a-b793-d2ce0b56e6f8.description2: This simple, but effective nose clip, known as futam (pl. aftama) in the Gulf region, was traditionally made of horn, wood or occasionally tortoise shell. Historical sources reaching back to the 4th century H/ 10th century AD already describe the clips' distinctive 'arrow' or 'scissor' shape, which remained largely unchanged until modern times. Equipped only with his noseclip, finger guards (khubat), occasionally a protective suit against jelly fish (libas al-ghaws) and a basket or bag (dyyin) for the oysters, a pearl diver would descend 50-60 times every day to bring up as many oysters as he could.

4489055a-7c22-5ee2-b83a-00d5a4759ff6.name: Tripoli railway station
4489055a-7c22-5ee2-b83a-00d5a4759ff6.description: This station first opened in 1911, connecting Tripoli to the Syrian city of Homs with a single track. It later became the terminus of the famous Orient Express line, operating in the 1920s, 1930s and 1940s. The station was nationalized in 1920 during the French Mandate following its destruction by the Ottoman forces during World War I.
4489055a-7c22-5ee2-b83a-00d5a4759ff6.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
4489055a-7c22-5ee2-b83a-00d5a4759ff6.keywords: Railway; Transport; Connection; Communication; Innovation; Station; Tripoli; Lebanon

450cc7be-20ef-52cc-862c-1aa33641995b.name: Muslim soldiers of the Austro-Hungarian infantry-regiment N°3 from Bosnia-Herzegovina in a special room for worshipping
450cc7be-20ef-52cc-862c-1aa33641995b.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
450cc7be-20ef-52cc-862c-1aa33641995b.keywords: Bosnia; Islam; Budapest; Austrian army; war; warfare
450cc7be-20ef-52cc-862c-1aa33641995b.description2: This picture shows Bosnian soldiers praying in a room in a barracks in Budapest. The third Bosnian infantry regiment recruited in Tuzla was stationed there. In 1882, the Austro-Hungarian administration of Bosnia-Herzegovina created four Bosnian infantry regiments. Because 50 per cent of the Bosnian population was Muslim, the Austro-Hungarian Army supported the free exercise of the religion amongst its soldiers.

453156d3-f141-581a-96a5-4ef8c83cbae1.name: Dr Charles Nicolle
453156d3-f141-581a-96a5-4ef8c83cbae1.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
453156d3-f141-581a-96a5-4ef8c83cbae1.description2: Pictured here is Dr. Charles Nicolle, a French microbiology doctor born in Rouen on 21 September 1966, in his research laboratory. His name is strongly linked to l'Institut Pasteur, which he directed from 1903–1936, playing the role of administrator, researcher, school headmaster, and advocate for the teaching of hygiene and illness prevention. In 1928 he received the Nobel Prize for Physiology. He died in 1936 and is buried at the Institut Pasteur, where his tombstone is engraved with olive and apple tree branches crossed over, the symbols of Tunisia and Normandy.

4541475a-b5b3-51f1-9463-7a0141b6de58.name: Mohamed Daghabi
4541475a-b5b3-51f1-9463-7a0141b6de58.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
4541475a-b5b3-51f1-9463-7a0141b6de58.author: Bechir Yazidi
4541475a-b5b3-51f1-9463-7a0141b6de58.description2: Born in El Hamma to the Beni Zid tribe (near Gabès), Mohamed Daghbagi (1885–1924) became a deserter in 1915, after the battle of Dhibat between the French troops and the Tunisian resistance. In 1920 he rose to fame through his role in an armed group which took part in various conflicts. He then took refuge in Tripolitaine, and was arrested in 1922 and given back to the French. He was executed in El Hamma on 1 March 1924.

4543ccbf-dceb-5300-941b-8c2f10ba3b29.name: The port of Galaţi
4543ccbf-dceb-5300-941b-8c2f10ba3b29.description2: After the Russian annexation of Bessarabia (the eastern part of Moldavia) in 1812 and until the restoration by Russia of Southern Bessarabia (1856), Galați remained Moldavia’s only port on the Danube. Understanding the city’s importance for Moldavia’s economy and wanting to ensure its development, prince Mihail Sturdza, who was appointed ruler of Moldavia by the Sublime Porte in 1834, issued in 1836 an act stipulating that Galați was to be a free port (with no or few customs duties) starting with March 1837. Also, a new neighborhood was to be built based on modern urban planning prescriptions and Galați received the right to organize annually five national fairs, during which traders from everywhere could sell any type of products.

459c2899-4ce2-5ffd-a17b-a43ffa91c9bc.name: *Milos Obrenovic, prince of Serbia*
459c2899-4ce2-5ffd-a17b-a43ffa91c9bc.author: Petar Petrovic
459c2899-4ce2-5ffd-a17b-a43ffa91c9bc.description2: Milos Obrenović (1783-1860) was Prince of Serbia from 1815 to 1839, and again from 1858 to 1860. He participated in the First Serbian Uprising, led Serbs in the Second Serbian Uprising, and founded the dynasty of Obrenović. Under his rule, Serbia became an autonomous duchy within the Ottoman Empire. He is credited with starting the process of re-establishing Serbian statehood, as well as shaping the domestic and foreign policies of the modern Serbian state. Prince Milos ruled autocratically, permanently refusing to share power. During his rule, he was the richest man in Serbia and among the richest in the Balkans. In the portrait that was painted by Pavel Djurkovitch in Kragujevac, prince Milos is dressed in Oriental costume and has on the top of the head a turban. It is a typically Oriental piece of costume and this was of significance for the attitude and dignity of the Serbian sovereign at the beginning 19th century, who was by all means respecting an Ottoman empire and his Sultan.

45aa6bbe-dbdf-5f6e-b23b-222901c8201e.name: *Cümbüş* (embroidered)
45aa6bbe-dbdf-5f6e-b23b-222901c8201e.description2: This a music instrument developed in the early 20th century and used for folk dances played at engagements, weddings and other traditional celebrations.

45cab7c7-4fad-588f-ae17-e78354e7fd67.name: *Exposition d’Art Musulman*
45cab7c7-4fad-588f-ae17-e78354e7fd67.author: Mina Moraitou
45cab7c7-4fad-588f-ae17-e78354e7fd67.keywords: photo; Egypt; Greeks; Iznik; collecting; exhibition
45cab7c7-4fad-588f-ae17-e78354e7fd67.description2: A photo depicting a showcase with Iznik ceramics belonging to Greek and European collectors such as Benakis, Nomico, Lagonico and Salvago. Many of the works were collected by Greeks in Egypt and were included in the *Exposition d’Art Musulman*, organised by Gaston Migeon and held in Alexandria in 1925 while a number more were shown in the earlier great Islamic exhibition in Munich in 1910.

45ccc1b2-62ae-540c-ba7c-d71565ea58c3.name: Palestine Gendarmerie badge
45ccc1b2-62ae-540c-ba7c-d71565ea58c3.description: The Palestine Gendarmerie, established on 1 July 1921, consisted of Arabs and Jews under British officers. It consisted of cavalry, camelry and infantry units. Enlistment of recruits was regulated so as to maintain a certain proportion amongst the various sects and religious creeds, which comprised Arabs, Jews, Circassians and Druse. In 1922, the strength of the Palestine Gendarmerie was as follows: 234 Arabs, 157 Jews, 72 Circassians and 27 Druses, of whom 250 were mounted on horses and 50 on camels, the remainder consisting of infantry. The badge was usually seen worn on black kalpak hats. It consists of the British imperial crown leaned on the letters PG, the abbreviation of Palestine Gendarmerie written in capital French script. Two crossed flags in the middle of the letters PG, based on a band that displays the full name of the PALESTINE GENDARMERIE and below the date 1921 written on a small band. The flag in the right side is broken.
45ccc1b2-62ae-540c-ba7c-d71565ea58c3.author: Aida Naghawi
45ccc1b2-62ae-540c-ba7c-d71565ea58c3.keywords: Gendarmerie; Arabs; Jews; British officers; cavalry; camelry and infantry; Circassians and Druse

45f8402d-e18b-5199-b2ae-ecde35d016ae.name: The train for VIP guests used during the inauguration of Luxor–Aswan Railway Line
45f8402d-e18b-5199-b2ae-ecde35d016ae.keywords: Egyptian Railways; Aswan Railway Line; Transportation in Egypt
45f8402d-e18b-5199-b2ae-ecde35d016ae.description2:
The inauguration of the Aswan Train Station, with \`Adli Yakan Pasha; Muhammad Najib al-Gharabli Pasha; Husayn Rushdi Pasha; Tharwat Pasha; Fathallah Barakat Pasha; Morkos Hanna Pasha; al-Dagwi Bek, director of Aswan; and Mahmud Shakir Bek, deputy undersecretary of the Ministry of Transportation in attendance. This project took about 10 months, its length is about 218 kilometres and its cost was about 267,000 pounds.  
The Luxor–Aswan line was very important as Aswan city was the centre of trade routes from Nubia and Sudan.

46069753-8d25-527b-8ca3-f62f78f6b3d2.name: Algerian Shoemaker at the Trocadéro [Paris Exhibition, 1878]

46069753-8d25-527b-8ca3-f62f78f6b3d2.archival: *L'Esposizione di Parigi del 1878 illustrata*, Sonzogno Editore, 1878, p. 108
46069753-8d25-527b-8ca3-f62f78f6b3d2.keywords: Exposition universelle de Paris; industrialisation; exhibition building; Moorish city; exhibitions and urban spaces; Moorish style; Islamic architecture; reinterpretation; exoticism; reproduction; model; magazine

46069753-8d25-527b-8ca3-f62f78f6b3d2.description2: At the International Exhibition in Paris, 1878, commercial activities typical of the colony were performed in the park next to Trocadero Pavilion, as part of the reconstruction of a hypothetical typical neighbourhood. The characters shown here are Algerian shoemakers from the Trocadero area working under a tent.

460ebced-3992-593a-a42e-32453e973f11.name: *Mountain people from Mostaganem*
460ebced-3992-593a-a42e-32453e973f11.author: Dalila Orfali
460ebced-3992-593a-a42e-32453e973f11.description2: The subjects of this piece, drawn from life, are men from the west of Algeria. Although we know that Chassériau's main source of inspiration in Algeria was the city of Constantine, he also spent some time in Algiers with his uncle the architect Frédéric Chassériau, who had been employed by Napoléon III to build up the city's seafront. The artist's keen attention to detail is highlighted by his authentic rendition of his subjects' dress and his occasional use of Arabic in his annotations.

460ecb9a-1f86-59fa-b384-df26f5b5b4fa.name: The Chinese quarter at Cormeilles-en-Parisis
460ecb9a-1f86-59fa-b384-df26f5b5b4fa.description2: The first wave of Chinese immigration to France was in 1916, when the Chinese government signed a treaty to send 35,000 Chinese citizens to work in France. This first small group, who had settled mainly in the regions around Paris, was followed by a second wave in the 1930s. Badly paid, and living in makeshift accommodation, these Chinese immigrants were mostly given heavy manual work.

4612c67b-fdc6-5022-bc82-f418c2ebce67.name: Hotel Excelsior
4612c67b-fdc6-5022-bc82-f418c2ebce67.history: Built between 1914 and 1916, the hotel was designed by the French architect Hippolyte-Joseph Delaporte in Neo-Moorish style. It became very popular among the mainly European elite who visited the city and settled there.
4612c67b-fdc6-5022-bc82-f418c2ebce67.keywords: Moorish style; French in Morocco; French in North Africa; French architects in North Africa; protectorate; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic influence; al-Andalus; Andalusian art; Andalusian motifs; Andalusian architecture; Islamic architecture in Morocco; Islamic art of Spain; European influence; European architecture; hotel; travel; tourism; city; urban space; changes in urban spaces; colonial city; colonial building; colonial architecture; city plan; Moroccan city; urban planning; geometrical motifs; column; capital
4612c67b-fdc6-5022-bc82-f418c2ebce67.description2: The four-storey Excelsior Hotel belongs to the style known as Neo-Moorish. The facade contains horseshoe and semi-circular windows protected by flat railings decorated with geometric motifs, some within loggias and flat and bow windows on the first floor. A balcony runs across the top floor – the roof covered in green tiles – supported by columns with capitals decorated with geometric patterns.

4620f58e-dafe-517f-be48-e848bac5e3df.name: Coin
4620f58e-dafe-517f-be48-e848bac5e3df.keywords: Egyptian currency; money minting; coin; paper money; Sultan Hussein Kamel
4620f58e-dafe-517f-be48-e848bac5e3df.description2: Samples of the money used during the reign of Sultan Husayn Kamil. Egyptian money bore the names of Ottoman sultans until World War I, when Egypt ceased to be part of the Ottoman Empire, and was declared a Sultanate under British protection. Money, at the time of Sultan Husayn Kamil, was minted in British mints. Coins circulated at the time of Sultan Husayn Kamil are considered special as they bore his name in the form of “Sultan Husayn Kamil” and the date of his accession to the throne (AH 1333 / AD 1914). Thus, Egyptian money bore no sign of subservience to the Ottoman Empire. During the days of Sultan Husayn Kamil, gold coins were minted as golden 100 piasters; silver two, five, and 20 piasters; and nickel one and five dimes.

462d8120-9ece-5f2c-b1f7-e362d936bd2d.name: L'École de la Rue du Pacha (classrooom exit)
462d8120-9ece-5f2c-b1f7-e362d936bd2d.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
462d8120-9ece-5f2c-b1f7-e362d936bd2d.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
462d8120-9ece-5f2c-b1f7-e362d936bd2d.description2: The school founded by Louise-Renée-Millet, opened 1 May 1900, was the first public school for young Muslim girls. Pictured here are the young girls as they enter school, veiled, accompanied and under the strict gaze of their French teachers. Subsidised by the French Resident-General until it was taken over by a *habous*, the school came under the government's jurisdiction between 1911 and 1912, and was then moved to a new residence on the Rue du Pacha. Despite its humble beginnings, with just five students, the school steadily expanded. Nabeul, Sousse, and Kairouan, on the inside of the country, soon followed suit and opened their own public schools. L'École de la Rue du Pacha held the held the important position as the first school of its kind, as well as the cradle for many important members of the first generation of political militants and feminist activists.

464aad1f-7be1-5c39-ab67-b2b1cb16454a.name: General meeting on women's suffrage
464aad1f-7be1-5c39-ab67-b2b1cb16454a.description2: Throughout the 19th and early 20th centuries, a number of different political movements for votes for women emerged, all using many different tactics. For example in May 1908, following the English model, a group of "suffragettes" held a protest during the Paris municipal elections, in which their actions (upturning ballot boxes, breaking polling station windows) were controversial. The following month, a national congress on women's rights and suffrage was held in Paris, an act which was hugely symbolic in and of itself. Their struggle was a long one, and it was not until 1944 that French women obtained the right to vote, which they exercised for the first time in 1945.

4656ec61-9406-5e34-94e3-612bfbb2e88c.name: *Persian carpet from Haas & Söhne*
4656ec61-9406-5e34-94e3-612bfbb2e88c.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

4656ec61-9406-5e34-94e3-612bfbb2e88c.description2: Persian carpet made by Haas & Söhne in Vienna following the pattern of an original Persian carpet preserved in the Munich National Museum.

465db5c8-a589-5652-8907-593491419960.name: Commemorative cup – the Congress of Paris (1856)
465db5c8-a589-5652-8907-593491419960.description2: According to the peace treaty signed on 30 March 1856 after the Crimean War, Russia had to renounce its protectorate over Wallachia and Moldavia, who apart from the Ottoman suzerainty were put under the guarantee of the Great Powers. The cup, made in France, belonged to Vasile Boerescu, one of Romania’s delegates to the congress. On the six sides of the cup are engraved the coats of arms of the treaty’s signatories (France, Russia, Austria, Great Britain, the Ottoman Empire, Sardinia), above which are the portraits of their delegates, with their names engraved below: A. Walewski and F. Burkene; A.F. Orlov and F.I. Brunnov; H. Buol and I. Gyubner; G. Clarendon and G. Cowley; Ali Pasha and Cemil Bey; C. Cavour and S. Villamarina. On top of the lid there is a small statue of the goddess of Justice.

4680c1d7-2d7f-504c-983e-43f220f6f53b.name: One piaster
4680c1d7-2d7f-504c-983e-43f220f6f53b.description: One piaster ( type 1), bronze. On obverse: "*al-husayn / bin 'ali / 'abduhu / wa-ibn 'abdihi / wafqa Allah*" ("Hussein bin Ali God Servant and son of God Servant Granted by God"). On reverse: "*duriba sana 1334 sana 5 / makka al-mukarrama / 'asima al-hukuma / al-'arabiyya al-hashimiyya / qurush wahid*" ("One piaster minted in 1334 /reign year 5 at Makka al-Mukarrama capital of Hashemite Arab Government").

46d97a8f-bb71-5869-a2ce-ba8b09411232.name: Bond of 100 francs issued by the Caisse Générale de Secours et de Bienfaisance Israélite de Tunis, in order to raise funds for the construction of a new synagogue in Tunis, and bought by Leone Moreno
46d97a8f-bb71-5869-a2ce-ba8b09411232.author: Massimo Sanacore
46d97a8f-bb71-5869-a2ce-ba8b09411232.archival: ASLi, Archivio Moreno di Tunisi, b. 12
46d97a8f-bb71-5869-a2ce-ba8b09411232.description2:
The construction of the Great Synagogue in Tunis had a long and complicated history. In 1883, the Bey granted a plot of land on which to build the temple to the Italian Jewish physician and president of the Alliance Israélite Universelle of Tunis, Giacomo Castelnuovo. However, the synagogue was ultimately built on a different lot, acquired thanks to a private donation. In the first years of the 20th century, different projects were discussed. The synagogue was finally built in the 1930s.  
  
Leone Moreno (Tunis 1852 – Tunis 1950) was a successful Italian entrepreneur. He belonged to a Jewish family that had migrated from Livorno (Tuscany) to Tunis around 1830. He was awarded honours both by the Italian King (Cavaliere dell’Ordine della Corona d’Italia) and by the Bey of Tunis (Nichan Iftikhar).

46e5760e-4ca7-5891-b293-149dd73cdb25.name: *View of Jaffa*
46e5760e-4ca7-5891-b293-149dd73cdb25.description: Travel illustrations in the 19th century, with their images of life, history and topography, had a great influence over Orientalism. This engraving appeared in a publication about the history of Turkey. Jaffa was a very important port in East Mediterranean.
46e5760e-4ca7-5891-b293-149dd73cdb25.author: Carmen Linés Viñuales

47088250-c322-5a2f-8bb2-03e71b5faa1d.name: Materials found in the Kamiros excavations in Rodi
47088250-c322-5a2f-8bb2-03e71b5faa1d.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
47088250-c322-5a2f-8bb2-03e71b5faa1d.author: Marina Minozzi
47088250-c322-5a2f-8bb2-03e71b5faa1d.keywords: Paleoethnology; exploration; ethnography; anthropology; material culture; collection; collector; academy; Rhodes; Cretes; Cyrene; Gortyna; Haghia Triada; Italian archaeologists in Greece; Italian archaeological school; Athens; tomb; Federico Halbherr
47088250-c322-5a2f-8bb2-03e71b5faa1d.third_name: Materiali provenienti dagli scavi di Kamiros a Rodi
47088250-c322-5a2f-8bb2-03e71b5faa1d.description2: Total view of materials chosen by Luigi Pernier, director of Archaeological School of Athens, from the excavation in Kamiros area (Rhodes) in 1912. Pernier sent his student Gian Giacomo Porro to the isle of Rhodes in order to explore this area and find a number of archaeological sites for the Italian Mission to concentrate its future excavations. Pernier decided to send part of the findings to the Prehistoric and Ethnographic Museum in Rome founded by Luigi Pigorini. These materials include mainly grave goods.

en: Mangani, E., “Materiali micenei, geometrici e orientalizzanti di Rodi”, in *Bullettino di Paletnologia Italiana*, Rome: Istituto Poligrafico e Zecca dello Stato (2005–2007), 96, N.S. XIV: 203–310.

471bc9ed-d220-539b-b302-0835391b4214.name: *The Lookouts*
471bc9ed-d220-539b-b302-0835391b4214.author: Dalila Orfali
471bc9ed-d220-539b-b302-0835391b4214.description2:
After his short, initial trip to Algeria in 1846 when he stayed at Blida, the artist returned in 1847 and 1848, staying in Constantine and Biskra. From then on Algeria became his primary source of inspiration, thanks to which he created these Algerian "impressions", as well as a number of paintings and drawings and two pieces of travel writing in 1857 and 1858. The emotions evoked by experience of such a different landscape fill the first account, *Une Année dans le Sahel* (1874), as well as the writer's admiration for the people, their simplicity and their attentiveness, their habits and their customs. He also deplores the Western urbanism which has already begun to destroy the country's authenticity.  
He also visited Egypt for the inauguration of the Suez Canal. He is one of the many artists who brought a degree of humanity back to Orientalist art.

47365132-f164-5764-a7d6-518e266d0b96.name: *Arab Vase*
47365132-f164-5764-a7d6-518e266d0b96.description: Drawing of a vase known as "The Alhambra vase". The ceramic vase is a good example of the development of the Nasrid workshops. This vase came from the church of Nuestra Señora de la Asunción in Hornos (Jaén) and it was acquired by the National Museum of Archaeology in 1875. This type of vase is very rare and few of them have survived.

476f71b7-f16d-54c8-85e4-ed053fa70b87.description2: Penbox from Mosul. Acquired by Augustus Wollaston Franks, a curator at the British Museum who played a key role in the building of the Mediaeval collection.

477c2b68-4a2a-5890-9452-4710f4eee340.name: Jewellery for horses – Type 2
477c2b68-4a2a-5890-9452-4710f4eee340.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
477c2b68-4a2a-5890-9452-4710f4eee340.description2: These strings of jewels were used on the horses of Ottoman officials and indicated their high status and wealth. The chain consists of a variety of differently shaped beads which would bounce against each other to create a tinkling noise and announce the arrival of the rider.

477e3472-eb64-5968-9da0-4243b0453c73.name: *The Great Hall of the Musée Assyrien in the Louvre*
477e3472-eb64-5968-9da0-4243b0453c73.second_name: Taken from the collection *Topographie de Paris*, "1er arrondissement, 1er quartier, Le Louvre"
477e3472-eb64-5968-9da0-4243b0453c73.description2: In May 1847, the world's first " Musée Assyrien" was opened at the Louvre. This was enabled by the arrival of 37 enormous bas-reliefs discovered by Paul-Émile Botta (1802–1870), the French consul in Mosul, at the site of Khorsabad. Botta, a diplomat, doctor, explorer and archaeologist, organised excavations in the hope of rediscovering Nineveh and its Assyrian monuments, and thus brought about the discovery of Khorsabad which in turn aided and accelerated the deciphering of Cuneiform in Mesopotamia. The "Musée Assyrien" pictured here was a great success and  attracted much attention on its opening in Paris in 1847.

478abce7-afc2-532d-82bd-fbecf067ac32.name: *One Thousand and One Nights*: decorative sketch of the palace gardens. Façade of an
478abce7-afc2-532d-82bd-fbecf067ac32.keywords: Orientalism; one thousand and one nights
478abce7-afc2-532d-82bd-fbecf067ac32.description2: The collection *One Thousand and One Nights* was translated into French in the early 18th century. The rise of Orientalism caused it to become extremely popular, appearing as the subject of numerous editions, adaptations, etc. In the 19th century, a tale from the collection was staged in one of Paris' most famous theatres (the Théâtre du Châtelet), and, as this image shows, the theatre was redecorated as an "Oriental palace" for the occasion.

47ae1491-a4bf-5c5f-98f7-d10504afcb6c.name: *Hagia Sophia. General view*
47ae1491-a4bf-5c5f-98f7-d10504afcb6c.description: Photographic print that is part of an album of different Istanbul images taken by the studio of the three Armenian brothers who, in 1880, opened a headquarters in this city. It shows the central nave of the Mosque of Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya Camii), under the main dome, facing the Eastern apse where the altar has been replaced by a *mihrab*. On the left, in the transept, the pavilion for the sultan's personal prayer. A group of men are sitting on the ground, on carpets that cover the entire surface, listening attentively. This kind of album had great success with 19th century European travellers.
47ae1491-a4bf-5c5f-98f7-d10504afcb6c.author: Rebeca C. Recio

47bb854c-9eb2-5d07-b0f1-7d41e63b0500.name: *The Qadous path*
47bb854c-9eb2-5d07-b0f1-7d41e63b0500.author: Dalila Orfali
47bb854c-9eb2-5d07-b0f1-7d41e63b0500.description2: The clever use of light in this painting helps illustrate the beauty of the countryside around Algiers in the 19th century. It highlights the richness of the vegetation in the area surrounding the Algerian notability's country homes.

47de166a-64f2-5809-807d-457eb735b800.name: Stefan Petrovic Knicanin (1809–1855)
47de166a-64f2-5809-807d-457eb735b800.description2: Portrait of Stefan Petrovic Knicanin. The Serbian officer Stefan Petrovic Knicanin supported the Austrian Emperor during the 1848 revolution. In 1849 he returned to Serbia and fostered good relations between Serbia and Austria. He died in 1855 in Belgrade.

47e09866-3a31-5ee5-a109-a01ff8ff7576.name: *Treaty of Peace and Trade between France and the Tunisian Regency*
47e09866-3a31-5ee5-a109-a01ff8ff7576.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
47e09866-3a31-5ee5-a109-a01ff8ff7576.description2: The Treaty of Peace and Trade, signed between France and the Tunisian Regency, was written in both French and Arabic. It protected all French ships from attacks from Tunisian privateers, gave them access to every port in the country, and guaranteed all French nationals full security.

47f1e835-2989-56cc-b52c-52619991c2a5.name: Italian military conscription office in Tunis
47f1e835-2989-56cc-b52c-52619991c2a5.author: Massimo Sanacore
47f1e835-2989-56cc-b52c-52619991c2a5.archival: ASLi, Famiglia Moreno di Tunisi, b. 15
47f1e835-2989-56cc-b52c-52619991c2a5.description2: Under terms of an 1896 agreement with France, Italy ran a military conscription office in Tunis. It was through this office that Italy drafted its migrants in Tunisia for the war on Turkey in 1911-12 and for the First World War. During WWI, many Italians living in Tunisia, because of their knowledge of the French language.  were assigned to the military units posted in France. Many of them died or were crippled for life. After the war, the Italian government opened a War Pensions Bureau in Tunis.

47fcbd3c-bf49-59d2-b9ac-7634939dbb18.name: Islamic pottery from Ephesus
47fcbd3c-bf49-59d2-b9ac-7634939dbb18.description2: Excavated by John Turtle Wood, an architect and surveyor. He was employed by the Ottoman Railway Company from 1858. Between 1863–1874 he excavated on behalf of the British Museum at ancient Ephesus, where he discovered the Temple of Artemis.

481ac567-31d6-55e0-ae01-02dc70f44740.description2: General view of the Step Pyramid of Djoser in the area of Saqqara, taken at the beginning of the excavation, photo taken by Borchardt.

4822489f-e111-5ff5-94a1-552add25ba10.name: *St. George Church*
4822489f-e111-5ff5-94a1-552add25ba10.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
4822489f-e111-5ff5-94a1-552add25ba10.author: Stefan Weber
4822489f-e111-5ff5-94a1-552add25ba10.description2: Built by Monsignor Joseph Debs, the neo-classical cathedral was inspired by the largest Catholic Marian church in Rome, the Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore, and bears great resemblance to it. The construction of this church, dedicated to patron saint St George, was finished in 1894. Heavily hit and looted (including an important Delacroix painting of St Georges) during the Lebanese civil war it was finally restored and re-inaugurated in April 2000.

483e8679-d93d-56cd-b566-f321c598b6de.name: *Dala’il al-Khayrat* (*Guidelines to Blessings*) by Abu Abdallah Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Jazuli)
483e8679-d93d-56cd-b566-f321c598b6de.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation /Sharjah Museums Authority
483e8679-d93d-56cd-b566-f321c598b6de.dimensions: 164 mm x 224 mm (open); 164 mm x 112 mm (closed)
483e8679-d93d-56cd-b566-f321c598b6de.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
483e8679-d93d-56cd-b566-f321c598b6de.description2: The *Dala’il al-Khairat* (The Signs of Benediction) is a compilation of prayers for the Prophet Muhammad and other faith-related information by Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Jazuli (d. ca. 1465). Popular throughout the Muslim world and particularly in Ottoman lands. It also contains descriptions of the Holy Mosque in Makkah and the Prophet’s Mosque in Madina, the two most important Islamic pilgrimage sites. Both are typically depicted in the centre of the manuscript, Here, detailed birds-eye views of both sanctuaries appear, surrounded by gold margins. On the right, at tthe heart of the Makkah mosque, the Ka’bah is dressed with its black kiswa cover, further enhanced by a golden belt (hizam) above and a golden door curtain (sitara or burqu’). On the left, within the mosque complex at Madina, a domed chamber contains the tombs of the Prophet and the first caliphs Abu Bakr and Umar, draped in golden covers – perhaps a reference to the precious, gold and silver-embroidered textiles that were spread over the tombs in Ottoman times.

4859f5a8-7af7-59f7-8271-982ef083627b.description2: Ernest Benecke (1817–1894), a French photographer of Anglo-German origins, was one of the first to be interested in the people rather than the monuments he saw during his travels in the Middle East. His pictures foreground daily life, as we can see from this photograph, which was taken in Egypt and shows a traditional mode of irrigation using the *shadouf*, a weighted appliance which allowed water to be poured from a well over a field.

4884a720-8e5b-52db-b680-609daaf48e72.name: Flag of the Italian Socialist Party’s local branch in a small village near Turin (Cafasse Torinese), bearing the image of a worker breaking a sword (an icon of antimilitarism)
4884a720-8e5b-52db-b680-609daaf48e72.author: Giulia Barrera
4884a720-8e5b-52db-b680-609daaf48e72.archival: ACS, Partito nazionale fascista, Mostra della Rivoluzione fascista
4884a720-8e5b-52db-b680-609daaf48e72.description2:
The Italian Socialist Party opposed Italian participation in World War I. After the government and the King decided to enter the war on the side of French and Britain, the Socialist’s Party line became “né aderire, né sabotare” (neither support, nor sabotage). Anti-war sentiments remained widespread among workers and peasants. In August 1917, without any prior organisation by the Socialist Party or by the trade union, spontaneous bread riots erupted in Turin: women led marchers that demanded bread and the end of the war, and they looted shops and barracks. Such protests were harshly repressed.  
War casualties were very high: 650,000 military deaths, 950,000 wounded, 600.000 prisoners of war or missing.
