48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

48bd5c22-4c67-599d-a92c-16a8ba8b932a.description: Coin struck in 1903 under Mulay Sultan ‘Abd al-‘Aziz al-Hasan I (r. 1894 to 1908) at the mint in Fez. For a century (1800-1900) the ‘Alawid sultans struck coins in the workshops of Fez, but due to the economic crisis at the time, gold was unavailable so most coins were of silver, bronze or other common metals – although the technique remained the same, with the metal poured into moulds. The patterns on the face and on the back vary between the star with eight points (Solomon ring) and the indication of the place of mint.

48f017b2-30fc-5195-8291-3ffaa1a2aeb8.name: Repairing pyramids road, Cairo
48f017b2-30fc-5195-8291-3ffaa1a2aeb8.description2: The Pyramids Road was fully repaired and put into use in 1868, successfully joining Giza to Cairo. Thanks to rising tourism in the area, different modes of transport were introduced along this route: cabs and omnibuses in the 19th century, and a tramway in the 20th century. The road was finally resurfaced following the invention of the motorcar, as we can see in this photograph.

490493f4-f4d8-56c4-8bdc-7207e915de8b.name: Travels in the Read Sea. *The Temple of Medina*
490493f4-f4d8-56c4-8bdc-7207e915de8b.keywords: Travelling; Egypt; Red sea; religious buildings
490493f4-f4d8-56c4-8bdc-7207e915de8b.description2: *L'Illustration* was a weekly French magazine published between 1834 and 1944. The greatest artists and photographers were featured in its pages, which dealt mainly with current affairs, and offered a great variety of information to the French public. Pictured here is a view of the mosque of Medina and the many pilgrims who had travelled there.

4974cb0e-719c-5e1f-975e-0b6646dd1058.name: Notarial seal from Amman
4974cb0e-719c-5e1f-975e-0b6646dd1058.keywords: Seal; city; Jordan; urban model; tribe; settler; Ottoman
4974cb0e-719c-5e1f-975e-0b6646dd1058.description2: Seal made of a round brass disc, inscribed clockwise in *divan* script: “*Amman Nahyan sand Achrafieh mahallasi mukhtar awwal 330*". In the middle there is a round hollow to hold a second seal, bearing the title *mukhtar*, illustrating the fact that, in order to stamp official papers, two seals were needed: one belonging to the quarter, the other belonging to the *mukhtar*. The seal has a pierced handle in the back and a new chain to hold it and to keep it with the *mukhtar*. Amman was a small district (*Nahyan*) in the Ottoman administrative division, following al-Salt province (*qada’*). The *Nahyan* was divided administratively into quarters or tribal units, each one called *mahalla*. Each mahalla had a mayor (*mukhtar*) who was responsible for the verification of births, deaths, marriage affairs, bachelorhood and land affairs. The mukhtar was elected from tribal notables of the quarters. The seal belonged to the first mukhtar of the Achrafieh quarter, “Achrafieh Mahallasi”, in Amman AH 1330 / AD 1911. Achrafieh quarter, as indicated in court records of Amman, existed before the year AH 1338 / AD 1919. It seems that this quarter was the extension of Qabertai quarter which was located below the west south of Amman Citadel, opposite to al-‘Umari mosque. A bridge called the Roman bridge connected the two quarters.

49a80737-c924-5479-8273-7392e3cd1db8.name: Gjorgij Pulevski
49a80737-c924-5479-8273-7392e3cd1db8.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
49a80737-c924-5479-8273-7392e3cd1db8.description2: Gjorgji Pulevski was a prominent figure of the Macedonian Enlightenment. He was born in Galichnik in 1822 and died in Sofia in 1893. In 1873, during his stay in Belgrade, he published the ”Dictionary of Four Languages,” which included Macedonian, Albanian, Greek and Turkish words. His “Dictionary of Three Languages” was issued in 1875. Gjorgji Pulevski was the founder of the Macedonian Literary Society, established in Sofia in 1888. It was one of the independent associations of Macedonian emigrants that made contributions to the awakening of the Macedonian national spirit.

49c47898-4a5f-59d7-a4f2-c9772ec5efeb.name: Colourful Mosque
49c47898-4a5f-59d7-a4f2-c9772ec5efeb.author: Nada Andonovska
49c47898-4a5f-59d7-a4f2-c9772ec5efeb.history: This Colourful Mosque was originally built in 1438 by Isaak Bey. The construction of the mosque was financed by two sisters from Tetovo, Hurshida and Mensure. It was reconstructed in 1833 by Abdurrahman Pasha, who commissioned skilful construction masters from Debar to do the painted decoration. The octagonal *türbe* within the mosque preserves the remains of Hurshida and Mensure.
49c47898-4a5f-59d7-a4f2-c9772ec5efeb.description2: This unique mosque is distinguished by the outstanding architecture and the various painted decoration on the façades. It differs from other mosques by the motifs of landscape applied in the interior decoration, i.e., the depiction of Mecca, as well as the rare example of the illustration of the shrine of Prophet Muhammad. It does not have a distinctive exterior dome as in other mosques, but is covered by a roof in four slopes. Unlike ceramic tile decorations usually applied in traditional Ottoman mosques, the Colourful Mosque has bright paintings with floral patterns.

49ebcfec-7199-5c0b-94f3-8ed498d743df.name: Archaeological excavations
49ebcfec-7199-5c0b-94f3-8ed498d743df.description2: This picture shows workers excavating the archaeological site of Abusir in the year 1901. It documents the discovery of some archaeological pieces and columns. Photo taken by the German archaeological mission.

49fa2453-a0f1-50d3-9c2e-b116b3fe9fdd.name: Frith photograph
49fa2453-a0f1-50d3-9c2e-b116b3fe9fdd.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
49fa2453-a0f1-50d3-9c2e-b116b3fe9fdd.description2: Francis Frith was one of the most successful commercial photographers from the 1850s and 1860s. He also established what was to become the largest photographic printing business in England. This image is part of the V&A's Francis Frith 'Universal Series' archive which consists of over 4000 whole-plate albumen prints predominantly of historical and topographical sites. Images such as these were highly desirable throughout the 1850s and 1860s. Frith's growing business coincided with many technological developments taking place within the field of photography. These developments changed and expanded the audience for photography and Frith's operation was well-prepared to provide for it and, it can be argued, worked to develop it employing a diverse range of publishing channels.

During his travels he brought exotic artworks as Egyptian sarcophagi.

4a68de52-6e31-5b77-857c-17466cc31f3c.name: A photograph of the Wall of al-Buraq (also known as The Western Wall or Wailing Wall)
4a68de52-6e31-5b77-857c-17466cc31f3c.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
4a68de52-6e31-5b77-857c-17466cc31f3c.archival: Johnstone, Catherine Laura, *Christian and Jewish Pilgrims to the Holy Land*, London, 1899
4a68de52-6e31-5b77-857c-17466cc31f3c.keywords: Pilgrimage; pilgrims; Christian pilgrimage; Jewish pilgrimage; Palestine; Holy Land; Jerusalem; sacred places; travel; travel book; Ottoman Palestine; local Jewish community
4a68de52-6e31-5b77-857c-17466cc31f3c.description2: This photograph shows the Wall of a-Buraq/Western Wall as it appeared in 1899. As well as being interested in the Christian holy places in Palestine, many European pilgrims were curious about other meaningful places and the life and habits of the Jewish communities in Palestine. The Wailing Place, as it was called in the caption of the photograph, was seen by many European (Christian) pilgrims not only in relation to historical events but as specifically related to the increasing presence of Jews coming from Europe to Palestine towards the end of the 19th century. Whether describing local Muslims and Jews or the European Jews, many European travellers associated Muslims and Jews with the “exotic” and with “otherness” in their appearance and habits.

4ac252d2-71d1-5064-9680-d48fa70fd153.name: Colonial style building
4ac252d2-71d1-5064-9680-d48fa70fd153.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
4ac252d2-71d1-5064-9680-d48fa70fd153.history: In Tunis, the capital of the Protectorate imposed by France on Tunisia in 1881, the European quarter built itself right next to the old Arab medina. A new kind of home - the investment property - soon appeared, and the term balas (from the Italian palazzo) became widespread. These two or three-storey housing blocks greatly affected the city's urban landscape by introducing many different architectural styles as well as new architects, designers and builders with from different backgrounds. The 19th century was the century of eclecticism in Tunisia (both neo-classical and neo-baroque), whereas the 20th century was most marked by the influence of Art Nouveau.
4ac252d2-71d1-5064-9680-d48fa70fd153.description2:
As the name suggests, Palazzo de Guidi at 9 Rue d'Italie (now Rue Charles-de-Gaulle), was built in 1903–1906 by an Italian architect. The building has traces of different styles and influences (North African, Byzantine), and uses a variety of materials, such as stucco, mosaics, marquetery and ironwork, but as a whole it should be seen as a product of the Art Nouveau movement.  
  
The same trend of using byzantine and "oriental" motifs, but organised in a different way, is clear in the buildings at 18 and 20 Rue des Salines. Built in 1909–1910, these three-storey buildings reflect an attempt to bring together the styles of Neo-Classicism, Art Nouveau and "Arabisance", and the beautiful mosaics on the top floor with golden backgrounds are a perfect example of this.

4acd8717-82fe-538c-b4c9-53b16ce962bb.name: The plan of Haydarpaşa Train Station
4acd8717-82fe-538c-b4c9-53b16ce962bb.description2: The original plan of Haydarpaşa Train Station, viewed from northern frontage. In 1871 Sultan Abdülaziz ordered a rail line to be built from Haydarpaşa to İzmit. Haydarpaşa station opened in 1872, and in 1888 the Anatolian Railway (CFOA) took over the line and the station. Since the station was built next to the Bosporus, freight trains would unload at Haydarpaşa and the freight would be transferred to ships. Haydarpaşa was chosen to be the northern terminus of the Baghdad Railway and the Hijaz Railway in 1904 and with rail traffic increasing, a new and larger building was required. The Anatolian Railway hired two German architects, Otto Ritter and Helmut Conu, to build the new building. They chose a neo-classical structure and construction started in 1906.

4ae45f56-80f0-5f31-82a5-680fa0d249f9.name: Bathroom pot
4ae45f56-80f0-5f31-82a5-680fa0d249f9.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
4ae45f56-80f0-5f31-82a5-680fa0d249f9.description2: The top of this semi-open bathroom pot is decorated with a band of perforated floral motifs beneath a rounded rim. A strip of maghrebi calligraphy covers the rest of the pot's surface, reading: "Wisdom is the crown of the young, which has become a golden blindfold. Honesty is daybreak."

4aea7da2-77b0-548c-ab58-60e5f4c3f6e5.name: Stele of King Nabonidus
4aea7da2-77b0-548c-ab58-60e5f4c3f6e5.type: Arched stele of Mesopotamian type with cuneiform inscription
4aea7da2-77b0-548c-ab58-60e5f4c3f6e5.holder: Saudi Commission for Tourism and Antiquities, Antiquities and Museums Sector, Museum of Archaeology and Ethnography
4aea7da2-77b0-548c-ab58-60e5f4c3f6e5.dimensions: Height: 60 cm, Width: 58.5 cm, Depth/Thickness: 13 cm
4aea7da2-77b0-548c-ab58-60e5f4c3f6e5.provenance: Accumulation of debris east of a former temple building
4aea7da2-77b0-548c-ab58-60e5f4c3f6e5.author: Jamal S. Omar
4aea7da2-77b0-548c-ab58-60e5f4c3f6e5.keywords: Stele; Northwestern Arabia; archaeology; Arabian peninsula; Mesopotamia; Babylonia; cuneiform
4aea7da2-77b0-548c-ab58-60e5f4c3f6e5.description2: Upper part of a stele (once approx. 1.3 m high) with the carved representation of a standing royal figure looking towards right in front of a panel with a cuneiform inscription. Above, there are three symbols of Mesopotamian astral gods (moon disc / crescent for the moon god Sîn, the winged sun for the sun god Shamash, the star for the goddess of love and war, Ishtar). Style of the representation and text are Late Babylonian, and although the name is not preserved, the object can be attributed to the last king of Babylon, Nabû-na’id, who, for ten years, stayed at Tayma, when trying to establish control over Northwest Arabia, most probably because of economic reasons, i.e. his interest in the Arabian long distance trade. The preserved part of the inscription, however, reports on activities in his hometown Babylon.

4afba372-f646-5f65-bf2a-c007b03e354e.name: Secondary school students giving a sports performance during King Fu`ad I's visit to the Fayum Directorate
4afba372-f646-5f65-bf2a-c007b03e354e.description2: A sports show by secondary school students at the Directorate of Fayum, presented before King Fu`ad I. The importance of the picture comes down to its rarity, especially its reference to the field visit conducted by King Fu`ad I.

4b13575d-f82b-573f-aa7d-a0ee196d3874.name: Archaeological excavations
4b13575d-f82b-573f-aa7d-a0ee196d3874.description2: General view of the site of the archaeological excavations in the area of Abusir. The workers' tents and those of the researchers can be observed in front of one of the pyramids of Abusir. The photo dates to 1904.

4b1cc99c-bdcc-51e9-bf03-770c80101277.name: Men's coat (*Mintan*)
4b1cc99c-bdcc-51e9-bf03-770c80101277.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
4b1cc99c-bdcc-51e9-bf03-770c80101277.description2: There used to be around fifty diverse styles of folk costumes worn in different ethnic areas throughout Macedonia in the 19th century and in the early 20th century. Among the most prominent were the costumes of Gorni Polog. Unlike the diverse and numerous women’s garments, men’s outfits were much simpler and rather unified. This upper garment called a *mintan* is of plain cut. It is made of silk in a striped pattern. Its only decorations are pieces of black cloth applied to the sleeves.

4b55c559-2654-5a6f-a502-72a32dfa2c6a.name: Photo of the Aswan Railways inauguration
4b55c559-2654-5a6f-a502-72a32dfa2c6a.keywords: Egyptian Railways; Aswan Railway Line; Transportation in Egypt
4b55c559-2654-5a6f-a502-72a32dfa2c6a.description2: The inauguration of the Aswan Train Station, with `Adli Yakan Pasha; Muhammad Najib al-Gharabli Pasha; Husayn Rushdi Pasha; Tharwat Pasha; Fathallah Barakat Pasha; Morkos Hanna Pasha; al-Dagwi Bek, director of Aswan; and Mahmud Shakir Bek, deputy undersecretary of the Ministry of Transportation in attendance. The Egyptian railway line was the first to be established in Africa and the Middle East, and the second worldwide after the United Kingdom. The establishment of the first railway line in Egypt began on 12 June 1851, and it became operable in 1854. The Egyptian railway construction project supervisor at that time was British engineer Robert Stephenson, son of the famous inventor of locomotives, George Stephenson. The Aswan train station is one of the most important railway lines constructed during the reign of King Fu`ad.

4b603a95-53d0-5a95-be2d-d52aff93ad2c.name: Sprinkler
4b603a95-53d0-5a95-be2d-d52aff93ad2c.author: Mina Moraitou
4b603a95-53d0-5a95-be2d-d52aff93ad2c.description2: A sprinkler made of brownish glass with enamel decoration of sprigs with flowers. The sprinkler is made in a Bohemian workshop and imitates the glass production of the Istanbul workshops – the Beykoz glass. The shape with the screw stopper is identical to the Ottoman prototypes while the decoration is different and more naturalistic. Made in Bohemian workshops. A complex and well organized sales network was spread in the eastern Mediterranean and constituted a binding link between western knowledge and Islamic aesthetics preserving a lucrative market for European works of glass with shapes and decoration of oriental inspiration.

4b63a853-7b5d-5c93-8ec7-7348d5091101.name: Model in plaster
4b63a853-7b5d-5c93-8ec7-7348d5091101.description: Following on the European fascination for the oriental world and for the famous Nasrid Palace of the Alhambra (Granada), a lot of reproductions of its remarkable architecture and decorations were made and spread. José Contreras was commended as restorer and decorator and his son, Rafael (1824–1890), was the leading pioneer of this trend in 1847. His work was continued by the grandson and by a huge number of plaster-cast workshops in Granada, and very likely, in other cities. His plasterworks were very successful in the International Exhibitions and were kept in private collections and museums like South Kensington (London). These delightful polychrome models, accentuated with a black frame, represents different rooms form the Alhambra Palace as the Comares Room, with its double horseshoe.
4b63a853-7b5d-5c93-8ec7-7348d5091101.dimensions: 68 x 41 cm; 72 x 53 and 54 x 49 cm
4b63a853-7b5d-5c93-8ec7-7348d5091101.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes, Cristina Giménez

4b6b4cd7-723b-5fc1-9d39-214740318d2a.name: Panel
4b6b4cd7-723b-5fc1-9d39-214740318d2a.dimensions: Height: 61.4 cm panel, Width: 40.5 cm panel, Depth: 1.9 cm, Height: 20.6 cm each tile, Width: 20.6 cm each tile
4b6b4cd7-723b-5fc1-9d39-214740318d2a.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
4b6b4cd7-723b-5fc1-9d39-214740318d2a.keywords: Ceramic; earthenware; collector; collection; ceramic tile; tile panel; tilework; vegetal decoration; floral decoration; revival; Syrian tiles
4b6b4cd7-723b-5fc1-9d39-214740318d2a.materials: Buff-coloured earthenware, with painting over a white slip
4b6b4cd7-723b-5fc1-9d39-214740318d2a.description2:
William De Morgan designed and produced pictorial tile panels. The smaller versions were sometimes framed for display as pictures, or used in fireplaces. Larger panels, would have been used in architectural settings, grander fireplaces, bathroom walls, and for the decoration of smoking rooms on ocean liners of the P&O company.  
De Morgan had a great interest in Islamic tilework, much of which was thought to be Persian in the 19th century. The Islamic-inspired patterns and the dominant range of colours (turquoise, blue, green, purple), were also often termed 'Persian'. They were in fact more closely related to the tilework of Syria and Turkey. The different regional types of Islamic tile were little understood, despite the acquisition of large quantities of Islamic tiles by European collectors.

4b719ab5-caa8-53d7-a185-809f12af918c.name: Venetian mirror
4b719ab5-caa8-53d7-a185-809f12af918c.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd

4b719ab5-caa8-53d7-a185-809f12af918c.description2: This magnificent wooden mirror, carved and decorated with gold leaf, is deeply moulded (14cm) and engraved with floral patterns. Two different tones of gold leaf, matte and gloss, were used. This Italian style carving was very fashionable with the 19th century nobility.

4ba4221c-c8d6-5be1-9dda-358e2e3b0dd5.name: French plaque for Emperor Napoleon III
4ba4221c-c8d6-5be1-9dda-358e2e3b0dd5.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
4ba4221c-c8d6-5be1-9dda-358e2e3b0dd5.description2: This plaque was erected by Emperor Napoléon III during the French Beaufort d'Hautpoul campaign, a military campaign aimed at ending the conflict that broke out between the Druze and Maronite communities in 1860. The text, written in French, is composed of 14 lines and lists the names of the battalions that took part in the campaign. This plaque replaced the monument that was built here by Pharaoh Ramses II (1279-73 BC).

4ba698dd-340a-5068-ac6e-53bd809620f8.name: *Old Oriental Gilt and Enamelled Glass Vessels extant in Public Museums and Private Collections*
4ba698dd-340a-5068-ac6e-53bd809620f8.author: Mina Moraitou
4ba698dd-340a-5068-ac6e-53bd809620f8.description2: An illustrated publication by Gustav Schmoranz on the history of Mamluk enamelled glass and example from public and private collections. It was published with the sanction and assistance of the imperial Austrian Ministry of Education by the Imperial Handels- Museum of Vienna. It contains the ex libris of Antonis Benakis.

4bacddd8-1bf3-5cf7-ae4b-b8ebd6e26987.name: Archaeological and topographic map of the Carthaginian ruins
4bacddd8-1bf3-5cf7-ae4b-b8ebd6e26987.keywords: Phoenician, punic, roman ruins; archaeological excavations; Tunisia
4bacddd8-1bf3-5cf7-ae4b-b8ebd6e26987.description2: Having been invaded and destroyed many times, the city of Carthage was then subject to various sackings, and its ruins served as a quarry for nearby towns. The site was rediscovered in the 19th century and became fashionable following the publication of Flaubert's novel *Salammbô*. Archaeologists soon felt the need for the different sites to be mapped, and in 1833 a Danish marine, Falbe, put forward a proposal for the *Recherches sur l'Emplacement de Carthage*. Thanks to the maps drawn up by the army's geographical service and military engineers, by the end of the 19th century archaeologists were able to conduct more detailed work, particularly with regards to the division of land.

4bc8852b-4eb9-5ea3-a533-cfbbadd4a2f8.name: *Coronation Of Tsar Dušan*
4bc8852b-4eb9-5ea3-a533-cfbbadd4a2f8.author: Petar Petrovic
4bc8852b-4eb9-5ea3-a533-cfbbadd4a2f8.description2: *The Coronation of Tsar Dušan* was painted on commission from the Kingdom of Serbia for the 1900 Paris Exposition. Jovanović began to prepare for it two years ahead, taking trips and gathering material in Vienna (Habsburg Court Library), Constantinople, Venice, Skopje, Kosovo and Metohija (Gračanica Monastery). Jovanović's consultant in the creation of this piece was the renowned Serbian historian Stojan Novaković. The artist used the *plein air* (outdoor) painting technique fashionable at the time, one of the reasons being the wish of the commissioning party, more specifically King Milan Obrenović, that Jovanović produce a work suitable for crafting a large tapestry. The painting was unveiled at the 1900 Paris Exposition, drawing flattering recognition and praise and winning a gold medal. The artist was somewhat unhappy with the choice of painting technique, and repeated the subject of Tsar Dušan's coronation (or the Proclamation of Dušan's Code, as it was called for a time after World War II) on numerous occasions after the Paris Expo, in various formats, in different ways and for various purposes until late in life. The fact that there are more than ten replicas and variants by the author himself known to date, speaks of how much this work was esteemed and sought after.

4bccb3e9-a964-52ef-937f-7a6d6e11e5cf.name: *Interior of a house in Boussaada*
4bccb3e9-a964-52ef-937f-7a6d6e11e5cf.author: Dalila Orfali
4bccb3e9-a964-52ef-937f-7a6d6e11e5cf.description2: This painting, showing the interior of a traditional house in the Boussaada region, elicits a certain intimacy, recalling the muted atmosphere also evoked by Guillaumet's *Fileuse*. The nervous, moving brushstrokes and his use of melted or soldered lead are clear references to the style of the Dutch masters.

4be86fc9-7fe9-524a-8ea0-665de458829d.name: The Italian woman poet and peace activist of Armenian descent Vittoria Aganoor Pompilj (1855–1910), and a signed copy of her poem 'Peace'
4be86fc9-7fe9-524a-8ea0-665de458829d.type: Photograph and autograph collected in a register
4be86fc9-7fe9-524a-8ea0-665de458829d.author: Maria Grazia Bistoni, Costanza Maria Del Giudice
4be86fc9-7fe9-524a-8ea0-665de458829d.archival: AS PG, Società per la pace e l'arbitrato internazionale di Perugia, 10
4be86fc9-7fe9-524a-8ea0-665de458829d.description2: The descendant of an Armenian family that migrated to Venice at the beginning of the 19th century, Vittoria Aganoor Pompilj authored poems that were translated during her life into English, French and Spanish. She corresponded with many international literary figures and was a member of the International Arbitration and Peace League of Perugia (*Società per la pace e l'arbitrato internazionale di Perugia*), founded in 1892. In 1870, the British trade unionist Randal Cremer (Nobel peace laureate in 1907) founded the International Arbitration League, which –among other things – protested British intervention in Egypt and imperialism.

4bef9a7e-ee5d-50e6-bbc2-ad9258836fd3.name: Carlo de Rossetti (consul of the Grand Duke of Tuscany) gives notice of a new ferry boat service between Alexandria (Egypt) and Constantinople operated by a Tuscan steamship
4bef9a7e-ee5d-50e6-bbc2-ad9258836fd3.author: Cristina Francioli
4bef9a7e-ee5d-50e6-bbc2-ad9258836fd3.archival: AS Li, Governo civile e militare, b. 890
4bef9a7e-ee5d-50e6-bbc2-ad9258836fd3.third_name: *Notificazione concernente l’attivazione di corse regolari fra Alessandria e Costantinopoli, e viceversa, mediante il Battello a Vapore Toscano* Il Generoso, *ed il suo servizio*
4bef9a7e-ee5d-50e6-bbc2-ad9258836fd3.description2: The steamboat Il Generoso had three classes of service: the first-class ticket cost 42.5 Thalers and the second class one 30 Thalers; they both included meals. By contrast, the third-class ticket (12 Thalers) did not entitle one to meals. The trip lasted five days. According to the poster, the steamboat Il Generoso was equipped with “very confortable cabins and living rooms, including a special living room for ladies”.

4bf6a5a2-2ef7-5efd-930f-e900942ddaa6.name: *La Péri: thirteen costume sketches*
4bf6a5a2-2ef7-5efd-930f-e900942ddaa6.description2: *La Péri* is a fantastical ballet in two acts with the scenario written by Theophile Gautier and the music by Burgmüller. This ballet, first performed in 1843, brought the audience to a grand Egyptian palace. Théophile Gautier dreamt of visiting Egypt, where his friend Gerard de Nerval had been living and sending him details to help him make the ballet more realistic.

4c12bb09-5654-50d7-9357-afc588c0f91d.name: Photograph of the dam of Sennar (Upper-Egypt) during its construction in April 1925
4c12bb09-5654-50d7-9357-afc588c0f91d.description2: Since antiquity, those living around the Nile had attempted to take advantage of the floods to better irrigate their lands. Many dams were built in the 20th century, most notably at Aswan (1902). The first Sudanese dam was built in 1925, in Sennar in the Blue Nile state, in order to irrigate the agricultural region of Gezira.

4c22f475-8576-51f3-bde0-fc0eadf0e0ec.name: Italian Company Westinghouse. Factory at Vado Ligure [Genoa, Italy]. The Production of Ogives for Shells
4c22f475-8576-51f3-bde0-fc0eadf0e0ec.author: Cristina Mosillo, Giulia Barrera
4c22f475-8576-51f3-bde0-fc0eadf0e0ec.archival: ACS, Ministero armi e munizioni, Ufficio storiografico della mobilitazione civile e industriale, Archivio fotografico, fasc. 156, foto 2134, neg. 379 B.
4c22f475-8576-51f3-bde0-fc0eadf0e0ec.third_name: Soc. Italiana Westinghouse. Stabilimento di Vado ligure (GE). Lavorazione per ogive per proiettili
4c22f475-8576-51f3-bde0-fc0eadf0e0ec.second_name: Women working in a factory that produced military equipment, during World War I
4c22f475-8576-51f3-bde0-fc0eadf0e0ec.description2:
Women working in an Italian factory that produced military equipment, during WWI. The war had an important impact on women’s work. As historian Perry Willson pointed out, during WWI “women rarely directly substituted for men, instead tending to move into new work roles produced by wartime expansion.”  
In Italy, the number of women who worked in factory producing weapons and ammunitions rose from 23,000 in 1915 to 198,000 in 1918. The numbers were far less than the women who participated in war production with more traditional “female roles”, such as making uniforms (400,000) or knitting woolen garments for the soldiers (200,000). However, Willson explained, women working in weapons’ factories had a relevance “as symbolic harbinger of change that greatly outweighed their actual numbers.”

en: Willson, Perry R., *Women in Twentieth-century Italy*, New York: Palgrave Macmillan, 2010.

4c5ec9e7-571c-57c0-a345-64717d007c10.name: *Nazareth School*
4c5ec9e7-571c-57c0-a345-64717d007c10.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
4c5ec9e7-571c-57c0-a345-64717d007c10.description2: Pictured here is the Nazareth School, founded in 1868 by Mother Pauline de Vaux, Superior General of the Congregation of the Ladies of Nazareth. The decision to found this school was supported by the Bishop Vallegra, in Rome. It was first located in a large house in the European quarter of Beirut, nicknamed "The Blue Castle". However, with the number of students rapidly growing, the school had to relocate. In 1877 the new convent was opened for this purpose on St. George Hill, bought by the *firman* of Constantinople. The building is U-shaped and made of stone, with white cloisters and surrounded by a huge garden.

4c5f8ec8-becc-59f0-937c-3cc5e1969665.name: The digging of the Western Canal of the Aswan Dam
4c5f8ec8-becc-59f0-937c-3cc5e1969665.description2:
Hundreds of Egyptian labourers digging the western canal of the Aswan Dam.  
Located in Upper Egypt, the Aswan Dam was the first water storage project in modern times.

4c67ed2f-ee8b-5b76-827e-611ac07238ea.name: Pearl Trader’s Scales Box
4c67ed2f-ee8b-5b76-827e-611ac07238ea.holder: Sharjah Maritime Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
4c67ed2f-ee8b-5b76-827e-611ac07238ea.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
4c67ed2f-ee8b-5b76-827e-611ac07238ea.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
4c67ed2f-ee8b-5b76-827e-611ac07238ea.description2: This wooden box was designed to contain a sophisticated scales set, which incorporated both a large balance and bowls for weighing quantities of pearls and a smaller version, with several, graded weighing bowls for smaller quantities. The weighing systems for pearls was complex and highly sophisticated to allow for the accurate assessment of mixed batches of pearls of varying sizes and quality. The largest and most valuable pearls were separated and assessed individually. The other pearls would be passed through graded sieves and separated into three batches of specific size.  Apart from the very best items, pearls from these batches were sold by weight.

4c695d43-f03d-5a2c-8f4d-af48b299d76b.name: Map of the Network of Caravans

4c695d43-f03d-5a2c-8f4d-af48b299d76b.description2: This sketch shows the network of caravans in Egypt, North Eastern Africa and Western Arabia.

4c7b394a-e1a0-5aff-b896-8caf9feaef32.dates: Published in the supplement of the *Ocidente*, n. 405, 21 March 1890

4c7b394a-e1a0-5aff-b896-8caf9feaef32.description2: Original sheet music of “The Portugueza”, initially a contest song against the British Ultimatum. It became the national anthem after the Republican Revolution.

4c7e1862-a363-5135-ad52-ffdf9df7a680.name: *The Holy Land, Syria, Idumea, Arabia, Egypt and Nubia, Volume 1, title page*
4c7e1862-a363-5135-ad52-ffdf9df7a680.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
4c7e1862-a363-5135-ad52-ffdf9df7a680.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
4c7e1862-a363-5135-ad52-ffdf9df7a680.description2: This vignette depicts the façade of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem, located on the spot where it is bellieved both the crucifixion of Jesus Christ and his burial took place. David Roberts, the prominent Scottish Orientalist painter(1796-1864) visited at Easter time, when the square in front of the church was crowded with pilgrims and traders selling their wares. Nevertheless, he shows the scene not with contemporary life milling around the church, but enlivened only with his usual repertoire of carefully staged, oriental types. Originally, the church was accessed by a flight of steps from the main street of Jerusalem, but in the 11th century, the entrance was moved its south side, where it remains to this day, including he double-doorway, its right section walled up since 1187. Only the original, carved lintels still recorded by Roberts had to be removed after an earthquake in 1927.
4c7e1862-a363-5135-ad52-ffdf9df7a680.artist_birthplace: David Roberts: Edinburgh, Scotland; Louis Hague: Tournai, Belgium
4c7e1862-a363-5135-ad52-ffdf9df7a680.artist_deathplace: David Roberts: London; Louis Hague: London

4c84389a-5e72-52a7-92f3-aa8604a09e9c.name: Declaration by the Bey of Tunis assuring that in future wars with any European power prisoners will not be enslaved
4c84389a-5e72-52a7-92f3-aa8604a09e9c.author: Edoardo Garis, Giulia Barrera
4c84389a-5e72-52a7-92f3-aa8604a09e9c.archival: ASTo,Materie politiche per rapporto all'estero, Trattati diversi, mazzo 4 seconda addizione, fasc. 7
4c84389a-5e72-52a7-92f3-aa8604a09e9c.description2:
This declaration was an annex to a treaty between the King of Sardinia (who ruled over Piedmont, Genoa and Sardinia) and the Bey (who ruled Tunis), concluded by British Admiral Baron Exmouth, who lead a military expedition against the Berber states in 1816. The Bey declared that in case of future wars with any European power, “none of the prisoners made on either side shall be consigned to slavery, but treated with all humanity as prisoners of war, until regularly exchanged according to European practice”.  
The Exmouth expedition was aimed at stopping Barbary corsairs from raiding European shipping in the Mediterranean. At the time, privateering was considered a legitimate form of warfare by European and North African countries alike. Only in 1856 did France, the United Kingdom and other European powers (except from Spain) declare privateering illegal.

4c9b74cf-404a-5d12-81d7-a9ae783d38bb.name: Plants Museum at the Agricultural museum
4c9b74cf-404a-5d12-81d7-a9ae783d38bb.author: Ibrahim Abdel Aziz
4c9b74cf-404a-5d12-81d7-a9ae783d38bb.history:
King Fu\`ad I chose the palace of Fatma Ismail, the daughter of Khedive Ismail, ‎to host the displays of the Agricultural Museum. The ‎palace was chosen due to its location near the Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture in the ‎neighborhood of Dokki in Cairo.  
The museum, which was first called "The Agricultural Museum of King Fu\`ad I", was officially opened for the public on the 16th of January 1938 in a big ceremony that the king himself attended.
4c9b74cf-404a-5d12-81d7-a9ae783d38bb.keywords: Agricultural museum; Dokki, Agriculture Palace; Khedive Ismail; King Fu`ad I; Princess Fatma; Khedivial palaces; Khedivial Egypt; Ancient Agriculture; Pharaonic Agriculture
4c9b74cf-404a-5d12-81d7-a9ae783d38bb.description2: This building is used as a display museum to show the most important crops, cultivated plants, and food products in Egypt, as well as samples of many agricultural machines that were used in the harvesting, threshing, seed preservation and food manufacturing processes.

4cb14496-4bb6-5ace-9b66-d5e561825dc3.name: Antonio del Valle y Serrano, Marquis of Villa-Huerta
4cb14496-4bb6-5ace-9b66-d5e561825dc3.description: The Marquis of Cerralbo and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This vignetted bust shot albumen portrait shows the elegance and the character of Antonio del Valle y Serrano, marquis of Villa-Huerta and stepson of the marquis of Cerralbo.
4cb14496-4bb6-5ace-9b66-d5e561825dc3.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes
4cb14496-4bb6-5ace-9b66-d5e561825dc3.third_name: Antonio del Valle y Serrano, marqués de Villa-Huerta

4cb2c7b0-e6c5-5421-ba04-8e3b26cad183.name: Purse
4cb2c7b0-e6c5-5421-ba04-8e3b26cad183.description: Miser’s purses, also known as ring or string purses, were very popular feminine accessories during the 19th century and even the first decades of the following century. The Cerralbo Museum has a small collection of these kinds of pieces, souvenirs from Istanbul. This Turkish and colourful beadwork one, with its traditional geometric pattern and the promise of a fashionable outfit, would have surely delighted any lady.
4cb2c7b0-e6c5-5421-ba04-8e3b26cad183.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes

4cd93347-e148-5cb5-8c29-840fe66c94eb.holder: Biblioteca Universitaria Alessandrina (Library of Sapienza University, Rome)

4ceec2b5-7808-56c2-b795-ced282fa861d.name: *24 hour optical telegraphy presented to the minister by a marine officer and used by the coast signalling services* (1802)
4ceec2b5-7808-56c2-b795-ced282fa861d.description2: The telegraph was an important piece of technology for Napoléon I, as it allowed him to send information quickly from both land and sea during the War of the First Coalition. A huge network of telegraph lines was created during his reign.

4d05ada4-2d34-5d8d-a4de-709d122b1851.archival: Berbrugger, *Algérie Historique Pittoresque et Monumentale*, Paris: J. Delahaye, 1843.

4d5b7131-33fe-5c5d-8076-ab9568f98e94.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
4d5b7131-33fe-5c5d-8076-ab9568f98e94.author: Huda Kilani
4d5b7131-33fe-5c5d-8076-ab9568f98e94.keywords: coffee; coffee roasting; coffee beans; domestic furnishing
4d5b7131-33fe-5c5d-8076-ab9568f98e94.description2: Circular iron coffee roaster with long handle decorated with zigzag and triangle motifs. Coffee-drinking in a communal setting is an essential part of traditions in Bedouin communities to celebrate or mourn.

4dcb750e-6c2b-5848-924b-43fb6905059d.name: Memorial Volume – Dedicatory and opening ceremonies of the Chicago World's Colombian Exposition – 1893
4dcb750e-6c2b-5848-924b-43fb6905059d.description2: The World's Columbian Exposition or The Chicago World's Fair was a World's Fair held in Chicago in 1893 to celebrate the 400th anniversary of Christopher Columbus' arrival in the New World in 1492. The fair was an influential social and cultural event to which the Ottoman Empire had been invited. It displayed raw materials and agricultural products at the exposition, as well as handicraft products and plant products belonging to the palace revenue. The 1893 Chicago Exhibition was a big success for the Chamber of Commerce. The Head of the Chamber of Commerce, Azaryan Efendi, was assigned to the head of the commission, which was formed in Istanbul for the Chicago Exhibition.

4e04768a-5d14-5f0c-94df-814f2d4400f7.name: *The Exhibition!! The triumph of industry*
4e04768a-5d14-5f0c-94df-814f2d4400f7.description2: Alfred Rodiba (1848–1926) was the artist of many dystopian works, a very fashionable theme at the time. Although he appreciated the 1889 Exposition Universelle (world fair), the cartoonist inside him also noticed a "universal" worship of industry which made everyone unaware of the pollution these inventions were producing.

4e0af093-1857-5b9b-90ef-f325bd3f29d4.name: Pearling Scales with their casing
4e0af093-1857-5b9b-90ef-f325bd3f29d4.type: Copper alloy and fibre pearling scales with metal and wood casing
4e0af093-1857-5b9b-90ef-f325bd3f29d4.holder: Sharjah Maritime Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
4e0af093-1857-5b9b-90ef-f325bd3f29d4.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
4e0af093-1857-5b9b-90ef-f325bd3f29d4.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
4e0af093-1857-5b9b-90ef-f325bd3f29d4.description2: Pearling scales (mizan, pl. muwazin) like these were an essential tool for any pearl merchant as all aspects of a pearl’s physical appearance – its shape, hue, perfection, size and indeed weight - all determined its value and saleability. The scales typically consisted of small hemispherical copper alloy bowls suspended by simple string from a balance. Polished agate or - more rarely - copper alloy weights were used to determine the pearls' weights accurately. In order to prevent the scales from getting damaged, they were carefully stored in a purpose-made copper alloy container. The scales were generally made in India, with one known centre located in Ahmedabad.

4e0c92b4-02c0-5702-a875-3dcb83eaa576.name: The Miraculous Sea Lady Church
4e0c92b4-02c0-5702-a875-3dcb83eaa576.description: This small Greek Orthodox Church overlooks the Phoenician sea wall. It is built with Batroun sandstone and using single-barrel vaulting from East to West.
4e0c92b4-02c0-5702-a875-3dcb83eaa576.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
4e0c92b4-02c0-5702-a875-3dcb83eaa576.history: Although gold icons made by Isaac of Jerusalem in 1863 were found inside this church, its construction date remains unknown.

4e0e7286-5def-51f5-b4c3-162106c6828c.name: Silverware used on the Orient Express
4e0e7286-5def-51f5-b4c3-162106c6828c.description2: After the Crimean War, Ottoman authorities concluded that a railway connecting Europe with Istanbul was necessary. The construction of a new terminal building began on 11 February 1888. The terminal building is one of the most famous examples of European Orientalism, and has influenced the designs of other architects. The Orient Express was the name of a long-distance passenger train service originally operated by the *Compagnie Internationale des Wagons-Lits*. The route passed through Strasbourg, Karlsruhe, Stuttgart, Ulm, and Munich in Germany, Vienna in Austria, Budapest in Hungary, Bucharest in Romania, Rousse and Varna in Bulgaria and ending in Sirkeci.

4e167204-1a3f-5a86-944d-ab0b42f8681b.name: Parthian Monument: the adoption of the Emperors
4e167204-1a3f-5a86-944d-ab0b42f8681b.description: During his reign, the Emperor Hadrian (figure right) adopted Antoninus Pius (centre left), who in turn adopted the 17-year-old Marcus Aurelius (left) and the eight-year-old Lucius Verus. A head stares from behind Hadrian’s left shoulder, presumably representing the guardian spirit of Aelius Verus, late father of Lucius. A bull is being offered to the gods as a sacrifice.
4e167204-1a3f-5a86-944d-ab0b42f8681b.holder: Kunsthistorisches Museum, Collection of Greek and Roman Antiquities

4e27b872-ecb5-5764-8ab4-12316b90ca21.name: *Marketplace, Morocco*
4e27b872-ecb5-5764-8ab4-12316b90ca21.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
4e27b872-ecb5-5764-8ab4-12316b90ca21.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
4e27b872-ecb5-5764-8ab4-12316b90ca21.description2: This imposing oil painting shows a caravan apparently leaving the gate of a North African city, perhaps Fez, with much commotion going on on either side of the camels and their guides. Although the title of the painting suggest a market scene, in reality little trading activity can be seen apart from an old hooded man sitting next to a large basket with shoes on the right. On the left a group of African men and a little child in a burnous admire the skills of a snake charmer, while his monkey next to him looks on intently. In the background, large numbers of men, apparently both of Arab and Berber origin, and dressed in a variety of traditional dress, walk along or stand together in groups conversing, oblivious to the camels, donkeys and horses moving inbetween them. Ferenc Eisenhut was an Austro-Hungarian painter, known for his monumentally conceived genre scenes of Eastern life and vistas. He was the only internationally acclaimed, Hungarian Orientalist painter.

4e299372-2148-578c-ac70-4b781a5ad8ce.name: *The First Train in Spain: Inaugurated 28 October 1848*
4e299372-2148-578c-ac70-4b781a5ad8ce.description: The railway connecting Barcelona and Mataró was the first one to be inaugurated in Spain. This train connected two important industrial hubs of Catalonia, as an example of the industrial development of this area in the middle of the 19th century.
4e299372-2148-578c-ac70-4b781a5ad8ce.author: Ana Cabrera
4e299372-2148-578c-ac70-4b781a5ad8ce.third_name: *Primer ferrocarril de España, inaugurado en el 28 de Octubre de 1848*

4e4b02a5-e3a8-5005-84bb-56a2cfc8b07a.name: Sword with scabbard
4e4b02a5-e3a8-5005-84bb-56a2cfc8b07a.description: A sword and scabbard decorated with geometric and floral motifs and crafted in southern Morocco in the 19th century. Sword blades were imported from Europe, especially from Toledo in Spain, or from Damascus in Syria.

4ec3aa30-6ba0-5917-9e79-014b48d5cd78.description2: Picture of the Austrian research headquarters in Giza. The German-born Egyptologist Hermann Junker became a professor at the University of Vienna in 1909. In 1911 the Austrian Academy obtained the concession for excavation in Giza. In 1912 Hermann Junker's team started to excavate tombs close to the pyramids of Giza.

4ef4f4cf-3d12-58c3-8cc2-6c635b02100f.name: Plate
4ef4f4cf-3d12-58c3-8cc2-6c635b02100f.description2: Plain inverted rim, shallow body, ring base. Light brown paste, white slip, transparent glaze. Under glaze decoration in cobalt blue, turquoise, dark green, yellow, red and black with black outlines. At the centre of a scalloped sun-shaped medallion formed by intertwined *rumi* and palmette motifs is a star and crescent motif, itself at the centre of a scalloped nine-petal medallion. The remaining surface is covered with a geometric design composed of eight-pointed stars, and the rim is decorated with a wide border of rumi-palmette motifs. The reverse of the plate bears the inscription, *Kütahya Azim Çini Fabrikası Mamulatı* (Product of the Kütahya azim Tie Factory).

4f197f6e-373b-5299-bc3c-8c7b6db1240e.name: Pair of pistols, a diplomatic present of Sidi Mohammed II, Bey (1855–1859) of Tunis, to Emperor Franz Joseph
4f197f6e-373b-5299-bc3c-8c7b6db1240e.holder: Kunsthistorisches Museum, Collection of Arms and Armour
4f197f6e-373b-5299-bc3c-8c7b6db1240e.keywords: Tunis; arms; armours; weapons; diplomatic gifts
4f197f6e-373b-5299-bc3c-8c7b6db1240e.description2: This pair of flintlock pistols was ordered by the Bey of Tunis from the French gunsmith Claude Bizouard, who worked in Marseille. This commission showed the growing French influence in Tunisia after the French conquest of Algeria in 1830. In 1857, the Bey of Tunis presented these weapons to Emperor Franz Joseph I.

4f5a9a60-32ea-5f5b-8f48-76aa1c556539.name: Palette
4f5a9a60-32ea-5f5b-8f48-76aa1c556539.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
4f5a9a60-32ea-5f5b-8f48-76aa1c556539.author: Marina Minozzi
4f5a9a60-32ea-5f5b-8f48-76aa1c556539.keywords: Egyptomania; Gaetano Rosellini; university; collector; photograph; anthropology; palaeoethnology; material culture; Florence; Pisa; Egyptology; Nubia; languages; hieroglyph; William Matthew Flinders Petrie; Jacques de Morgan; David Randall-MacIver; dealer
4f5a9a60-32ea-5f5b-8f48-76aa1c556539.description2: This slate palette, characterized by an unusual shape and an articulated decoration along one of the sides, was used to pulverize cosmetics. The absence of information about the context in which it was found make it difficult to propose a dating. Roberto Paribeni (later named superintendent of the antiquities of Rome and Lazio from 1928 to 1933) bought the palette in 1904 from the antique dealer Ghirghis in Quena on behalf of "Museo Preistorico ed Etnografico" in Rome. In 1878 Luigi Pigorini decided to enlarge the Egyptian archaeological collection in the "Museo Preistorico Etnografico e Kircheriano", which he directed at the time. The main body of the collection was donated by David Randall-MacIver in 1901, from excavations he carried out on the behalf of the Egypt Exploration Fund in the town of el-Amrah, Upper Egypt. In 1905 the Italian Archaeological Mission in Egypt (excavations of Hammamiye) led by Ernesto Schiaparelli, director of the Egyptian Museum in Turin offered more artifacts for purchase. The last main acquisition took place in 1913 when the Egyptian objects from the Enrico Hillyer Giglioli’s collection entered the museum collection.

4f6d8c3a-63e3-50c0-b243-faaa3ddd2001.name: *The Expulsion of the Duke of Athens*
4f6d8c3a-63e3-50c0-b243-faaa3ddd2001.author: Marina Minozzi
4f6d8c3a-63e3-50c0-b243-faaa3ddd2001.keywords: Painting; Italian painters; history painting; celebration of the past; international exhibition; universal exposition; art exhibition; Esposizione nazionale; Florence; post-unitaria Italian society; national identity
4f6d8c3a-63e3-50c0-b243-faaa3ddd2001.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
4f6d8c3a-63e3-50c0-b243-faaa3ddd2001.description2: The painting is a second version by the artist of his masterpiece *La cacciata del Duca di Atene* started by Ussi in 1854 in Rome and finished in Florence, now at the National Gallery of Modern Art in Florence. The artwork was presented at the National Exhibition in Florence in 1861 and sent at the International Exhibition in Paris in 1867 where it was awarded the silver medal. The scene depicted in the painting refers to the book *Istorie Fiorentine* by Nicolò Machiavelli. In particular the painter shows the moment in which Gualtieri di Brienne, Duke of Athens between 1342-43, abdicates from Florence. To his left are the republicans who force him to sign. The second version is slightly different from the original one in characters and manner. The painting shows the city of Florence, represented by the republicans, defending its freedom from a cruel ruler and embodies a strong political, civic and moral relevance, emphasised by the sheer size of the canvas.
4f6d8c3a-63e3-50c0-b243-faaa3ddd2001.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

4fba9c3c-f84d-510f-bba6-f6a6783a23b3.name: Nusretiye Mosque and the Imperial Gun Foundry in Tophane
4fba9c3c-f84d-510f-bba6-f6a6783a23b3.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
4fba9c3c-f84d-510f-bba6-f6a6783a23b3.description2: A frequently employed device in Robertson's Istanbul photographs is the inclusion of the one or more human figures in the foreground – indeed, this is something of a trademark of Robertson’s work. There were two main reasons for the inclusion of these figures. For one thing, the artist used them as a way of creating a more natural scene. The other was to provide one or more reference points so that the photograph’s viewers could get an idea of the dimensions of the scene they were looking at and of the elements contained therein.

4fe44b43-1a7d-5881-a567-e328acd991f0.name: Tunis Cathedral
4fe44b43-1a7d-5881-a567-e328acd991f0.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
4fe44b43-1a7d-5881-a567-e328acd991f0.history: The Cathédrale Saint-Vincent-de-Paul is the active Catholic cathedral of Tunis. It is located on Place de l'Indépendance at the crossroads between the Avenue Habib-Bourguiba (previously Jules-Ferry) and the Avenue de France (previously the French general residence). Built between 1893 and 1897, it is named after the Saint Vincent de Paul, the founder of the Lazaristes and the Filles de la Charité, who was kidnapped as a young priest and sold as a slave in Tunisia in the early 7th century. The Modus Vivendi, signed in 1964 between independent Tunisia and the Vatican, ensured the cathedral became the property of the Roman Catholic Church. Today, the cathedral receives a great number of visitors and tourists, as well as important religious figures such as the Pope John Paul II in 1998.
4fe44b43-1a7d-5881-a567-e328acd991f0.keywords: Architecture; Romano-Byzantine style; vaults; stained-glass windows; tapestry; marble
4fe44b43-1a7d-5881-a567-e328acd991f0.description2: This cathedral was built on land given to the Christian community by the Bey of Tunis, and replaced the Église Sainte-Croix. The first stone was laid by Cardinal Lavigerie on the 7 November 1881, just after the establishment of French Protectorate. It was built in an austere Romano-Byzantine style with neo-classical influences, reflecting the monumental and majestic image of itself France presented to both its protégés and its rival powers. It contains huge statues of Christ, monumental vaults, stained-glass windows, tapestry, and marble columns. The organ inside the cathedral, built in 1921 by an expert from Paris and inaugurated on 28 October 1923, is considered to be the most beautiful organ in the African continent.

4ff37598-ea12-5304-b2b5-a79f541ebf9d.name: Monastery of St. John at Bigor
4ff37598-ea12-5304-b2b5-a79f541ebf9d.dates: Restored in the 18th century, it was expanded and additional wings built in the span of 1812-1825
4ff37598-ea12-5304-b2b5-a79f541ebf9d.author: Nada Andonovska
4ff37598-ea12-5304-b2b5-a79f541ebf9d.history: According to monastery chronicles, the original church was built in 1020 by the first Archbishop of Ohrid, Ivan I. Debranin (1018–1037). It was ruined in the 16th century and restored by the monk Ilarion in 1743. In the span of 1812–1825 during Archimandrite Arsenie (1807–1825) major reconstruction and expansion of the monastery was carried out. From about the same time comes also the exquisite wooden iconostasis. It is considered a masterpiece of Byzantine sculptural art.
4ff37598-ea12-5304-b2b5-a79f541ebf9d.architects: Local construction masters and wood-carving craftsmen: Petre Filipovski Garkata, his brother Marko Filipovski and Makarija Frchkovski
4ff37598-ea12-5304-b2b5-a79f541ebf9d.description2: Situated on the steep slopes of the Bistra Mountain near Debar and rising above the banks of the Radika river, the Monastery of St. John at Bigor is one of the most beautiful edifices in Macedonia. The church within the Monastery is devoted to St. John the Baptist. It preserves the exquisitely carved walnut iconostasis. The iconostasis, which depicts scenes from the Old and the New Testaments, was created by the most outstanding Macedonian masters of wood-carving: Petre Filipovski Garkata and his brothers Marko and Makarij Frchkovski. The monastery complex nowadays comprises the monastery church, the chamber-tomb, defence tower, icon gallery arranged in the dining room and the monastery lodgings.

50134a0e-a943-5f25-a36c-43032ad0dd5e.name: Bob Walter [veiled dancer]
50134a0e-a943-5f25-a36c-43032ad0dd5e.description2: The "serpentine dance", invented by Mary Louise Fuller, was copied by many dancers, and even parodied. Like Fuller, these dancers also used veils and lighting effects, characteristics typical of the Art Nouveau movement.

5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.name: El Sayyid Muhammad Idris al-Mahdi al Senussi (1889–1983), from 1916 Chief of the Senussi Muslim order
5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.holder: Italian Institute for African and Oriental Studies
5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.author: Giulia Barrera
5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.archival: Archivio fotografico, Libia, album 25, “Festeggiamenti per l’arrivo di S.A. l’emiro Senussi a Bengasi (1920)”
5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.description2: El Sayyid (or Sidi) Muhammad Idris al-Mahdi al Senussi (1889-1983), the grandson of the founder of the Senussi Sufi order, became head of the Senussi order in 1916. He took the title of Emir and ruled as King of Libya from 1951 through 1969. In 1920 Italy reached an agreement with him and invited him to Rome, where he met King Victor Emmanuel III. Idris’ relations with the Italian government later deteriorated, and he went into exile in Egypt and encouraged anti-Italian guerrilla from there.
5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.holding_institution_org: Istituto italiano per l’Africa e l’Oriente

en: Del Boca, Angelo, *Gli italiani in Libia*, Milan: Mondadori, 1993.

503f7b59-beb0-5c06-8952-0baa809cc018.name: *The arrival of the refugees*
503f7b59-beb0-5c06-8952-0baa809cc018.author: Maria Dimitriadou
503f7b59-beb0-5c06-8952-0baa809cc018.description2:
A black and white photo from an album depicting the arrival of Greek refugees after the Asia Minor catastrophe. Photographer unknown.  
The “Convention concerning the exchange of Greek and Turkish population" was signed at Lausanne, on 30 January 1923, by the two governments. It involved approximately 2 million people (around 1.5 million Anatolian and 500,000 Muslims in Greece), most of whom were forcibly made refugees.

507be032-d0a6-59ec-914d-6665a856598d.name: Table
507be032-d0a6-59ec-914d-6665a856598d.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
507be032-d0a6-59ec-914d-6665a856598d.author: Bechir Yazidi
507be032-d0a6-59ec-914d-6665a856598d.keywords: Mohamed Sadok Bey; General Bréart; French protectorate in Tunisia
507be032-d0a6-59ec-914d-6665a856598d.description2: This table bore witness to the signing of the so-called "Treaty of Bardo" the 12 May 1881 by Mohamed Sadok Bey and the General Bréart. This circular marble table has a diameter of around 120 cm and an ebony base, carved and embellished with gold leaf.

509dc50d-cdf0-5d63-8c8f-6dcddd22c1f2.name: Bullfight Arena of Campo Pequeno
509dc50d-cdf0-5d63-8c8f-6dcddd22c1f2.author: Cristina Correia
509dc50d-cdf0-5d63-8c8f-6dcddd22c1f2.history:
In 1821 King João VI hands over the organization of non free bullfights to Real Casa Pia de Lisboa, an educational institution founded by his mother in 1780 to support youngsters in risk. To overcome the exiguity of its first arena, in 1889 Casa Pia orders a new one to architect António Dias da Silva who sent the plans from Madrid according to the meanwhile disappeared Neo-Mudejar Bullfight Arena of Madrid by Emilio Rodriguez Ayuso. Built between 1890-1892 it will be inaugurated still unfinished by Royal Prince Afonso of Braganza (1865–1920) on the 18th August 1892.  
From those days onwards keeps being one of the main bullfight arenas in Portugal nowadays renovated and transformed into a multifunctional venue.
509dc50d-cdf0-5d63-8c8f-6dcddd22c1f2.keywords: Architecture; Arab Style; Leisure; Bullfight arena; Lisbon
509dc50d-cdf0-5d63-8c8f-6dcddd22c1f2.third_name: Campo de Touros do Campo Pequeno
509dc50d-cdf0-5d63-8c8f-6dcddd22c1f2.description2: The Bullfight arena, built with monochromatic brick, is an iconic example of the 19th century neo-Arab style in Lisbon, was the neo-Mudejar one in Madrid. With an external perimeter of 80 m, its circular plan includes 4 polygonal towers attached symmetrically and topped by bulbous domes originally polychromatic. The 40.7 m diameter arena was covered with sand, encircled by a wooden fence and separated from the circular rows of seats by a corridor. It seats 8,438 spectators three levels namely in five rows mounted on an iron structure and two rows of 165 lodges and galleries. The access is provided by two 3 m wide covered walks. One of its main features is the use of the brick particularly enhanced on the segments of the several arches rhythmically opened at the external walls.

50c3aa93-d400-5d9f-824f-b394e33b63a6.name: Beylical salon
50c3aa93-d400-5d9f-824f-b394e33b63a6.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
50c3aa93-d400-5d9f-824f-b394e33b63a6.keywords: Palace; Husainid dynasty; carved wood; mashrabiya
50c3aa93-d400-5d9f-824f-b394e33b63a6.description2: This beylical salon is furnished with carved wood from the beylik era, and consists of three large double-seater benches and four smaller benches with full armrests and topped with a pediment. The set is decorated with rectangular panels in the middle and square panels on the sides, all decorated with a mashrabiya. A wood carved table completes the set.

50c481c2-3b97-5936-ae28-31d363a507e2.name: Traditional Lebanese house
50c481c2-3b97-5936-ae28-31d363a507e2.description: Traditional Lebanese houses in the 19th century were generally rather modest. The roofs were supported by wooden beams, and were accessible by an internal stairway made of stone, compared to the wooden stairways of more modest abodes.
50c481c2-3b97-5936-ae28-31d363a507e2.history: The houses were built with wooden windows which were filled with tinted glass. A balcony could usually be found on the first floor, which was covered with a clear window for lighting and ventilation purposes. This architectural style was clearly influenced by European architecture and design, indicating the growing influence of European culture and trends in 19th century Beirut and elsewhere in the region.

50d50f6e-1e18-535b-a66c-a9263d40ac9e.name: *Monastery on Mount Carmel*
50d50f6e-1e18-535b-a66c-a9263d40ac9e.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
50d50f6e-1e18-535b-a66c-a9263d40ac9e.archival: Jewry afterwards Valentine, Laura, *Palestine Past and Present. Pictorial and descriptive ... Illustrated, etc*, London: F. Warne & Co, 1893, p. 241
50d50f6e-1e18-535b-a66c-a9263d40ac9e.keywords: Pilgrimage; pilgrims; Christian pilgrimage; Jewish pilgrimage; Palestine; Holy Land; Jerusalem; sacred places; travel; travel book; Ottoman Palestine; local Jewish community; Biblical places; Biblical archaology
50d50f6e-1e18-535b-a66c-a9263d40ac9e.description2: Another important landmark described in the book *Palestine Past and Present* by Laura Jewry Valentine is Mount Carmel and its monastery. Again, the history of this site is described in terms of its Biblical and Christian past, as the location of the fight between Elijah and the priests of Baal, and the place where the monastery of the Virgin of Mount Carmel was founded in the 12th century. The description highlights other details about specific places on the mount related to episodes from Elijah’s story, the story of the monastery and the description of the monastery of Mar Eliyas built in 1826. Each naturalistic, archaeological and historical detail (such as the discovery of a small synagogue and a Jewish tomb) is presented in such a way that recalls a continuous connection with the Jewish and Christian past.

50ff7499-1e83-52e9-88c7-d80dd581fe29.name: Photograph "Under the Oak Tree"
50ff7499-1e83-52e9-88c7-d80dd581fe29.description: Pictured here is the priest Joseph Delore, speaking to a group of children. Boys are seated at the front, whereas girls, whose hair is covered by a white scarf, are seated at the back.
50ff7499-1e83-52e9-88c7-d80dd581fe29.author: Hala Masri

51101afe-20b5-5b27-9fe9-38dbf49761d6.name: The Imam Uza'i Mosque
51101afe-20b5-5b27-9fe9-38dbf49761d6.author: Hala Masri
51101afe-20b5-5b27-9fe9-38dbf49761d6.history: The name of Imam Uza'i, who died twelve centuries ago, is often associated with the values of tolerance, justice, and brotherhood. Born in Baalbek in the year 681, 'Abd al-Rahman Uza'i was a strong advocate of justice, freedom and mercy over what he considered to be the religious fanaticism and human autocracy of his time. He stood alongside Lebanese Christians in his fervent opposition to the Abbasid regime. He was also a renowned thinker and intellectual. After relocating to Beirut he soon begun to accept visitors in his home where he offered advice and imparted wisdom. To this day, thousands of Lebanese visit his mausoleum in search for blessings and mercy.
51101afe-20b5-5b27-9fe9-38dbf49761d6.description2: The Imam Uza'i Mosque, with its green dome and two minarets, contains the tomb of Imam Uza'i, who died in 774. It became a religious school in the 19th century which is still in use today.

51be354a-b339-5d93-8690-4f26618ea9fb.name: Tramway
51be354a-b339-5d93-8690-4f26618ea9fb.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
51be354a-b339-5d93-8690-4f26618ea9fb.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
51be354a-b339-5d93-8690-4f26618ea9fb.description2: This railway carraige from the French Bône-Guelma company inaugurated, in April 1879, the opening of the first section of a 100 km long line which connected Tunis to Algeria. In 1800 it also acquired the Tuni-Sousse and Tunis-Bizerte lines, and thus gained a monopoly over the construction of railway lines in Tunisia, while the Italians bought the small Tunis-La Goulette-La Marsa (TGM) railway track.

51c01d82-0b4a-5399-8607-c519021252c0.name: Switchboard (*Telefon Santrali*)
51c01d82-0b4a-5399-8607-c519021252c0.keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication
51c01d82-0b4a-5399-8607-c519021252c0.description2: In 1840, the Ministry of Post made an announcement describing the postal service, declaring it necessary in order to facilitate communication among people. The first regulations about the postal organisation were taken from French Law in 1840. Ottoman Postal Code included 44 specific headlines. In 1855 the first telegraph service and in 1909 the first telephone service were put into common use as a demonstration of modern communication. In order to improve the technology of the telegraph systems, Ottoman authorities imported well-known machines with trademarks such as Siemens & Halske and Western Electric. As a result of this technological improvement, Ottoman officials decided to establish a telegraph factory. Between 1869 and 1915 this factory produced many devices and accessories.

51d89765-459f-5a2f-89bb-b09f35a3e9d2.name: Firman issued by Sultan Abdülmecid for the construction of the Constanţa–Cernavodă railway
51d89765-459f-5a2f-89bb-b09f35a3e9d2.description2: The first railway in the European part of the Ottoman Empire was built in Dobruja. Its construction was leased by the Ottoman sultan to the British company "Danube and Black Sea Railway and Kustendge harbour". According to the contract signed on 1 September 1857 the company had to build a railway linking the cities Constanţa and Cernavodă and could exploit it for 99 years, after which it became property of the Ottoman Empire. The railway, inaugurated on 4 October 1860, was 66 km long and was destined for freight transportation. After Dobruja was annexed by Romania in 1878, the state bought the railway from the British company (1882). Later, in order to connect it to the Romanian railway system (since Dobruja is separated from the rest of Romania by the Danube) a railway bridge was built across the Danube.

5213376b-6aff-55de-afcc-32cf7bfb66d1.name: Portrait of Paul Draneht
5213376b-6aff-55de-afcc-32cf7bfb66d1.author: Massimiliano Cremona, Ignazio Galella
5213376b-6aff-55de-afcc-32cf7bfb66d1.second_name: Paul Draneht (1815–1894), the Superintendent of the Cairo Opera who commissioned Aida from Giuseppe Verdi
5213376b-6aff-55de-afcc-32cf7bfb66d1.description2:
Paul Draneht (1815-1894) was born in Nicosia (Cyprus) as Pavlos Pavlidis. He was the child of a Greek Christian Orthodox family who fled Cyprus due to the clashes between Greeks and Turks, and took refuge in Egypt. Muhammad (Mehmet) Ali Pasha (the Khedive of Egypt) sent him to study in France. Trusted by the Khedive (who awarded him the titles of Bey and Pasha), Paul Draneht participated in the negotiations regarding the opening of the Suez Canal.  
He became superintendent of the Egyptian Opera Theatre and commissioned the opera Aida to the Italian composer Giuseppe Verdi. The Aida opened in Cairo on 24 December 1871.

521421e0-80f1-5225-89de-67bdaec30210.name: Narrow street in Pera, Istanbul
521421e0-80f1-5225-89de-67bdaec30210.author: Maria Dimitriadou
521421e0-80f1-5225-89de-67bdaec30210.description2: A black and white photo from a leather bound album. It bepicts a narrow street in Pera, Constantinople, leading to the church of “Panagia tou Stavrodromiou”. Photographer unknown.

52254363-31d0-54f5-bab4-97458eb40b9d.name: Vanadinite
52254363-31d0-54f5-bab4-97458eb40b9d.holder: National Museum of Natural History and Science (MUHNAC) / Museums of the University of Lisbon
52254363-31d0-54f5-bab4-97458eb40b9d.author: Liliana Póvoas (MUHNAC-UL)
52254363-31d0-54f5-bab4-97458eb40b9d.keywords: Vanadinite crystals; Apatite group; hexagonal system; vanadium ore; National Museum of Natural History and Science; University of Lisbon
52254363-31d0-54f5-bab4-97458eb40b9d.description2: Vanadinite crystals on matrix. Vanadinite is a vanadate mineral with the chemical formula Pb5(VO4)3Cl. This mineral species was named Vanadinite (1839) because it contains vanadium. It belongs to the Apatite group of phosphates. Crystals of vanadinite conform to the hexagonal system of symmetry. These Vanadinite crystals are short prismatic, with smooth faces and sharp hedges. Their colour is orange-red and they are nearly opaque. And they present an intense resinous lustre. Vanadinite occurs as a secondary mineral in the oxidized zone of lead-bearing deposits and it is one of the main industrial ores of the element vanadium. This sample has been collected at Mibladen Mine, Midelt, Khénifra Province, Morocco.
52254363-31d0-54f5-bab4-97458eb40b9d.holding_institution_org: Museu Nacional da Historia Natural e da Ciencia (MUHNAC)

522f2144-3034-5e4d-9bc3-6ef8c6f5ecd0.name: Veil
522f2144-3034-5e4d-9bc3-6ef8c6f5ecd0.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
522f2144-3034-5e4d-9bc3-6ef8c6f5ecd0.author: Huda Kilani
522f2144-3034-5e4d-9bc3-6ef8c6f5ecd0.keywords: Linen fabric; natural cotton; embroidered patterns
522f2144-3034-5e4d-9bc3-6ef8c6f5ecd0.materials: Linen, silk; hand weaving, hand embroidered, natural dyes
522f2144-3034-5e4d-9bc3-6ef8c6f5ecd0.description2: Three natural cotton and linen fabrics sewn and decorated with cross-stitch with embroidered folkloric patterns (known as “cypress trees”, “amulets”, “keys”, “saw” and “Shuayb teeth”). They are mainly in red with some green colour; a small linen fringe dangles from two sides. The veil was an essential piece of women’s dress. Girls started preparing their trousseau (clothes, shawls, and other belongings collected for marriage) at the age of ten. Married women had various embroidered costumes worn for special occasions. As the economy of the Jordanian territory in the late 19th century-early 20th century relied on trades and crafts, new waves of traders and artisans started to arrive and to settle. Thus, traditional costumes reflect a variegated population composition, demographic changes, personal attire and local rites.

523087c9-9a15-54a0-b37b-745c43c2cb51.name: An olive oil factory run by an Italian migrant in Monastir (Tunisia)

5250886a-a6a0-5674-9156-a5f133b9cfe8.name: Kerosene lamp
5250886a-a6a0-5674-9156-a5f133b9cfe8.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities
5250886a-a6a0-5674-9156-a5f133b9cfe8.author: Huda Kilani
5250886a-a6a0-5674-9156-a5f133b9cfe8.description2: A cylindrical container filled with gas and injected with air heats a group of emerging pipes from the cylinder, which are surrounded by glass to shield them from air and assist in hashing its light into place. Kerosene lamps were used to light the streets of Amman until the first electricity generator began to operate. The beginning of the 20th century marked the re-urbanisation of Amman after 500 years of abandonment.

5284ca06-d2a1-58f9-b56b-e749fc9d4c22.name: Portrait of Shaykh Ibrahim al-Yaziji
5284ca06-d2a1-58f9-b56b-e749fc9d4c22.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
5284ca06-d2a1-58f9-b56b-e749fc9d4c22.description2: Ibrahim al-Yaziji was born on 2 March 1847 in Beirut. He was educated by his father, Shaykh Nasif, and then in 1872 he became the chief editor of the magazine *al-Najah*. In 1884 he began publishing for *al-Tabib* with Bishara Zalzal and Khalil Sa'adeh. He edited all his father's books, and republished them alongside the *Diwan* of al-Mutanabbi. In 1894 he travelled around Europe, and then settled in Cairo, were he began publishing a new magazine *al-Bayan* and then later *al-Dhiya'*, for eight years. His most famous publication was titled "The Language of Newspapers". He died in Egypt on 28 December 1906.

5296fe8d-c29c-5ac6-9be6-323c7b48cdf1.name: Fleeing the barbarians on the road to Amiens
5296fe8d-c29c-5ac6-9be6-323c7b48cdf1.keywords: Forced migration; exodus; First World War; France
5296fe8d-c29c-5ac6-9be6-323c7b48cdf1.description2: Around 700,000 French citizens fled the country in the face of the German invasion at the beginning of the First World War (Spring 1914–1915). Pictured here are families who have abandoned their homes in a  hurry, taking just a few belongings with them on these carts.

529b4a95-033c-586c-b6c2-ba606e63c4aa.name: Buzuq
529b4a95-033c-586c-b6c2-ba606e63c4aa.holder: Lebanese National Higher Conservatory of Music
529b4a95-033c-586c-b6c2-ba606e63c4aa.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
529b4a95-033c-586c-b6c2-ba606e63c4aa.keywords: Dabke; Music; Lebanese; Oriental; Hybrid; Sound
529b4a95-033c-586c-b6c2-ba606e63c4aa.description2: The word *buzuq* comes from Turkish. *Bashi-buzuq* for example, literally meaning 'burnt head', was one of the nicknames given to the Ottoman troops. The *buzuq* is of hybrid origin and thus is considered neither a traditional Arabic instrument nor a traditional Turkish instrument. Used for *dabke* music, the instrument was originally associated with the traveller communities in Lebanon. It consists of a long, fretted neck with four sets of double strings, and is played with a plectrum.

52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.name: *The Virgin at the Nile*
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.author: Marina Minozzi
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.keywords: Egyptomania; Orientalism; painting; Orientalist paintings; artistic exchange; Egyptology; archaeology; imaginary trips; reinvention; historical events in painting; exoticism; architectural trends in painting; Italian painters; travel
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.description2: Federico Faruffini made his debut as a painter at the 1856 annual exposition of Brera. In his works the artist breaks away from the academic rule of ‘disegno’, or artistic drawing, and focuses on colour. The painting *The Virgin at the Nile* shows a sacrifice. Numerous study sketches survive. They attest that the artist was well educated on customs, traditions and architecture of ancient Egypt. In the painting the artist proposes the integration of two separate themes through different rendering styles: on the brighter upper part he sets the historic characters and in the lower zone the more narrative one, of obvious academic inspiration. The painting was brought to Paris by the artist after he decided to leave Italy because he was having difficulty finding work. After the artist committed suicide, *The Virgin at the Nile* was on display at the retrospective exhibition in Rome in 1883 where Faruffini’s entire portfolio was reconsidered, and the painting was declared his undiscussed masterpiece.
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

52bc1f5c-19f1-5c15-8794-630ecd367289.type: Cultic Object; ornament; talismanic object; jewellery
52bc1f5c-19f1-5c15-8794-630ecd367289.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities

52bc1f5c-19f1-5c15-8794-630ecd367289.keywords: Talisman; crescent; tusks; wild boar; heal of Gazalle
52bc1f5c-19f1-5c15-8794-630ecd367289.description2: This object is a piece of horse jewellery, an amulet worn around the horse's neck to ward off misfortune. Horse jewellery was used among Bedouins and villagers communities. This amulet consists of a silver-cased crescent composed of two joined tusks of wild boar. A ¼ Majidi Ottoman gold coin dangles from the crescent with three crescents and stars at the end. The silver chain is called “heal of gazelle”.

52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.name: Lithographs after the panoramic photograph taken by Robertson and Beato, *Faust: Poligrafisch Illustrirte*, Zeitschrift, 1857, Vienna
52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.keywords: Istanbul panorama; Faust; tower of War Ministry in Beyazıt
52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.description2: James Robertson is the first Istanbul photographer known to have taken 360 degree panoramic photographs of the city. The first panorama, which was taken in May 1854 from the War Ministry tower in Beyazıt, consists of twelve separate photographs. The most successful printed reproductions based on Robertson’s photographs curiously enough were produced in Vienna. Issues of *Faust* published during 1857 report fascinating bits of information as well as pictures that are important to the history of printing and visual arts in the Ottoman Empire. A plate published in *Faust* contained a panoramic view from the Istanbul Beyazıt tower that is made from Robertson’s panorama.

532b4aae-3420-5fef-ba89-4653325f00d7.name: *A young and an old Turk*
532b4aae-3420-5fef-ba89-4653325f00d7.description2: Carol Popp de Szathmari was born in Transylvania, but later settled in Bucharest, Wallachia, where he worked as court painter of princes Alexandru Dimitrie Ghica, Gheorghe Bibescu and Alexandru Ioan Cuza. During the reign of prince Carol of Hohenzollern, he was also court photographer. He is the author of five photographic albums with images of people and places from Bucharest and other regions in Romania, among which there are depictions of people belonging to the ethnic minorities of Romania, such as the Turks. He travelled twice to Istanbul, in 1860 and 1864, as member of prince Alexandru Ioan Cuza’s suite. During the Crimean War (1854-1855) he photographed the Russian and Turkish armies that occupied Wallachia and then went to Crimea, where he took more than 200 photos of the fights.

5381cedb-dcaf-5b98-864b-12a4d739c029.name: State Bank of Morocco
5381cedb-dcaf-5b98-864b-12a4d739c029.history: Establishment of the State Bank of Morocco came about through an Act signed on 7 April 1906 at the Algeciras Conference by delegates from 12 European countries, the United States and Morocco. The bank was incorporated in February 1907 as a public limited company whose registered office was in Tangiers. Its capital was divided between the signatory countries, except the United States.
5381cedb-dcaf-5b98-864b-12a4d739c029.keywords: Economy; trade; banks; banking; financing; money; Europeans in Morocco; Andalusian architecture; Arab architecture; Islamic architecture; city; urban space; changes in urban space; European style banks; European economy; European financing
5381cedb-dcaf-5b98-864b-12a4d739c029.description2: After the State Bank of Tangier was built, the Moroccan state set up a network of banks and subsequently moved the headquarters of the Central Bank to Rabat. The buildings for this banking network were built in a similar Arab-Andalusian style, in most cases in sandstone.
