5384029c-eb52-5179-984d-a80e0e272e8c.name: *Illustrated dictionary of Tunisia: the people and things of Tunisia*
5384029c-eb52-5179-984d-a80e0e272e8c.description2: Italian immigration to Tunisia in the 19th century was, quantitively speaking, extremely significant. This is evident from advertisements such as this one, where the headquarters, names and addresses of a Tunis-based firm are Italian.

5384b8df-a79b-54a7-bdbf-0c4918314519.name: Qanun
5384b8df-a79b-54a7-bdbf-0c4918314519.holder: Lebanese National Higher Conservatory of Music
5384b8df-a79b-54a7-bdbf-0c4918314519.dimensions: H: 4 to 6cm, L: 95 to 100cm, W: 38 to 40cm
5384b8df-a79b-54a7-bdbf-0c4918314519.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
5384b8df-a79b-54a7-bdbf-0c4918314519.description2: The *qanun* is a traditional instrument of the Middle East, whose name in Arabic also means "rule, principle or norm". It has a range of three octaves, and today it is made with nylon or PVC strings are stretched over a single bridge, poised on fish-skins on one end, and attached to tuning pegs on the other. Turkish models have 26 sets of triple strings. It rests on the player's lap and is played by plucking, either with the player's fingernails or with two tortoise-shell plectrums.

5399c399-4ead-5147-a1fb-14b857acaaf5.description2: This medal depicts the Egyptian pavilion of the 1873 World's Fair in Vienna. The opposite side of the medal has a portrait of Emperor Franz Joseph. The medal was created in commemoration of this event.

53ec6f4f-bd40-5ba2-8874-cb460c22b748.holder: Palais de la Rose – Musée de l’Armée

53ec6f4f-bd40-5ba2-8874-cb460c22b748.description2: This flag is divided into three sections, arranged in parallel along a long mast. The topmost flag has a red stripe and a black stripe, the middle is in the same shade of red, with three gold crescents in the centre, and the final flag is also red with a sword resembling that of the Prophet's cousin and fourth caliph, 'Ali.

5401f2b8-18f4-599c-b201-a2d99f1b35ce.name: Dar Zarrouk
5401f2b8-18f4-599c-b201-a2d99f1b35ce.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
5401f2b8-18f4-599c-b201-a2d99f1b35ce.history: This palace was built in the early 19th century on a huge plot of land in La Manouba belonging to 'Ali Zarrouk, the great-grandson of Hammouda Pacha Bey's minister, 'Ali Arbi Zarrouk. The architectural style chosen by 'Ali Zarrouk is evidence for the fashion amongst the urban elites of the time for comfortable, luxurious, houses in a European (and particularly Italian) style. The palace is currently the seat of the La Manouba local government.
5401f2b8-18f4-599c-b201-a2d99f1b35ce.keywords: Architecture; art; painting; stucco; mosaic; marble; ceramics
5401f2b8-18f4-599c-b201-a2d99f1b35ce.description2: This tall white façade with shuttered windows and a curved Italian-style door sits at the heart of a lush garden. Inside, a series of hallways on the ground floor, all leading to different rooms, are built with stunning Italian marble door frames and paving. The flat ceiling is decorated with pendant vaults. On the first floor, an innovative covered patio is beautifully lit by a Venetian crystal chandelier. Four reception rooms surround a central hall. The imported marble and faience pottery contrast with the shining gold gilding on the furnishings and the reflection from the huge windows and mirrors.

54061b49-5654-5a34-bb57-ed20127e9164.name: Gülabdan
54061b49-5654-5a34-bb57-ed20127e9164.description2: It is known that there were workshops producing glass vessels around Beykoz in Istanbul in the 19th century. The first glass workshop was founded by Mevlevi Dervish Mehmed Dede during the reign of Selim III (1789-1807). There were European glass craftsmen working in those workshops as well. Cups, bottles, jugs, etc. made of colourful, colourless and opal glass were among Beykoz' productions. This *gülabdan* (a small flask for sprinkling rose water) is a Beykoz production. Its body is milk white on which floral patterns in dark pink, green and yellow were placed.

5417f6b5-cc8c-53f1-96de-52e25282f580.name: An Egyptian woman giving a public speech during the events of the 1919 Revolution
5417f6b5-cc8c-53f1-96de-52e25282f580.keywords: 1919 Revolution; Egyptian Revolutions; Egyptian Women; Political Participation
5417f6b5-cc8c-53f1-96de-52e25282f580.description2: An Egyptian woman talking to the crowds, encouraging them to fight for their rights. The 1919 Revolution – one of the most important Egyptian revolutions in modern times– started due to objections to the practices of the British occupation and the exile of symbols of Egyptian patriotism.

541b2d25-7056-5660-8154-f73cfaa855f5.name: Qasr al-`Ayni Hospital Administrative Employees
541b2d25-7056-5660-8154-f73cfaa855f5.keywords: Medicine; Doctors; Qasr al-`Ayni Hospital; Egyptian Hospitals; Administrators
541b2d25-7056-5660-8154-f73cfaa855f5.description2: Photograph of the administrative employees at Qasr al-`Ayni Hospital.

541e7afc-c735-5bac-ad3a-928530f9d141.name: Horse adornment used in wedding ceremonies (*Gushnik*)
541e7afc-c735-5bac-ad3a-928530f9d141.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
541e7afc-c735-5bac-ad3a-928530f9d141.keywords: Horse ornament; monistra; horse jewellery; accessories; marriage; wedding
541e7afc-c735-5bac-ad3a-928530f9d141.description2: A *gushnik* is an article used for the adornment of horses. This item shows the tradition of decorating horses on some festive occasions, particularly on weddings. The decoration consists of a string and numerous ornaments made of *monistra* (tiny beads in varied colours) applied on canvas. The pendants are decorated with varied patterns and have fringes at the bottom.

5426a620-cbfc-5b20-bed9-14fa1801de7d.name: *Medjmouaï teçavir* (Collection de costumes)
5426a620-cbfc-5b20-bed9-14fa1801de7d.keywords: costume; diplomacy; fashion; court life; economy; finance; Ottoman; Tercüman; travel; traveller; Orientalism
5426a620-cbfc-5b20-bed9-14fa1801de7d.description2: Popular postcard from Turkey showing the costume worn by various people, according to occupation, activity, etc. At this time Turkish financial officials worked under European management.

54310c6d-87ca-585e-b552-bcb1c5951fe3.name: Dress
54310c6d-87ca-585e-b552-bcb1c5951fe3.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
54310c6d-87ca-585e-b552-bcb1c5951fe3.author: Huda Kilani
54310c6d-87ca-585e-b552-bcb1c5951fe3.materials: Silk, cotton; hand woven Syrian silk fabric (brocade)
54310c6d-87ca-585e-b552-bcb1c5951fe3.description2: This dress of al-Druze (Druse) women is made of a long grey with green and silver brocade, pursed narrow sleeves, wide, open square shaped chest, pursed at the middle and wide at the bottom with ruffles and a cotton liner. This object illustrates the variegated social composition and demographic changes in the Jordanian territory in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The al-Druze tribes migrated from Syria (Hawran) to north east Jordan in the early twentieth century because of their support for the Syrian revolution against the French occupation. The traditional Druse and other Jordanian costumes were influenced by the local trade and economic activities: as illustrated in this case, they were often made of silk textiles, produced in Syria and traded to Jordan and Palestine.

544117f8-c7fb-5075-b36e-315986c47bec.name: Transport plan of Beirut
544117f8-c7fb-5075-b36e-315986c47bec.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury
544117f8-c7fb-5075-b36e-315986c47bec.description2: This map shows a plan of transport terminals in Beirut in 1891.

5441d082-5cb2-51aa-a412-66acc0afe4b5.name: Diadem
5441d082-5cb2-51aa-a412-66acc0afe4b5.description: Joaquin Sorolla travelled with his family to Tetouan in February 1919; there they bought all types of souvenirs of that exotic lands. Thanks to this travel the Sorolla Museum keep a small collection of Berber jewellery. Among the highlights is this headband or diadem, jewellery that represents the typical combination of silver and multiple enamel colours. It would look placed on the front of a woman and is complemented with bracelets, earrings, pins and necklaces, of which the Museum has also other pieces.
5441d082-5cb2-51aa-a412-66acc0afe4b5.author: Covadonga Pitarch

5451b48d-8d64-533c-b7e9-be06d8f670ea.name: Water Carrier’s Portable Water Jug
5451b48d-8d64-533c-b7e9-be06d8f670ea.type: Copper alloy and ceramic water ewer with fibre rope netting
5451b48d-8d64-533c-b7e9-be06d8f670ea.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
5451b48d-8d64-533c-b7e9-be06d8f670ea.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
5451b48d-8d64-533c-b7e9-be06d8f670ea.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
5451b48d-8d64-533c-b7e9-be06d8f670ea.materials: Engraved and punched sheet copper alloy; ceramic base; fibre rope
5451b48d-8d64-533c-b7e9-be06d8f670ea.description2: This large ovoid ewer consists of a metal top and ceramic base. From the hemispherical shoulder rises a tall, waisted cylindrical neck with central collar. The mouth is covered by a bulbous, domical lid. The ewer has a strong, angular handle of roughly square section and a tall, obliquely rising body spout, which is connected to the neck by a curved tube and tapers towards the prominent, slightly waisted mouth section. The entire upper part of the ewer is decorated with incised horizontal bands of plaiting, abstract floral decoration, pseudo-inscriptions and running animals. The spout shows a dense system of punched, arched lines and incised decorative bands near its base. The undecorated ceramic base of the ewer is secured by netting created from fibre ropes. Thicker ropes of the same material, probably used for carrying the ewer, are attached. A ewer identical to this one appears in Ludwig Deutsch’s painting of the Al-Azhar mosque (SH_66).

5476b9e7-1d62-5f52-a389-4e2da362bb9c.name: Skeleton telephone
5476b9e7-1d62-5f52-a389-4e2da362bb9c.description: The phone’s manual states that the Skeleton model was one of the first telephonic devices to be used in Morocco.
5476b9e7-1d62-5f52-a389-4e2da362bb9c.keywords: Telephone; technical innovations; communication; telephone network

5483dab5-d84f-5427-be2a-f5641e4aecc1.name: Monthly revenues deriving from the traffic of boats through the Suez Canal sent by the consul of the Austro-Hungarian Empire in Port Said (Egypt) to the Commodities Exchange of Trieste
5483dab5-d84f-5427-be2a-f5641e4aecc1.author: Chiara Artico
5483dab5-d84f-5427-be2a-f5641e4aecc1.archival: ASTS, Deputazione di Borsa poi Camera di commercio di Trieste, b. 92, fasc. 1222.
5483dab5-d84f-5427-be2a-f5641e4aecc1.third_name: *Compagnie Universelle du Canal Maritime de Suez, Mouvement recettes, Septembre 1876.*
5483dab5-d84f-5427-be2a-f5641e4aecc1.description2: Out of the 109 boats that had passed through the Canal in that month, 78 were from Britain, 8 from France, 7 from the Netherlands and the remaining 16 were from Spain, Germany, Italy, Austria, Denmark and Norway. British ships passed through the Suez Canal on their way to India and to other British colonial possessions.

54877a94-0bd3-5eff-a7df-cba98f2e5ac9.name: Portrait of 'Abd Allah al-Bustani
54877a94-0bd3-5eff-a7df-cba98f2e5ac9.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
54877a94-0bd3-5eff-a7df-cba98f2e5ac9.description2: 'Abd Allah al-Bustani was born in Debbeye (al-Chouf district) in December 1854, and studied at the National School of Butrus al-Bustani until 1873. He first started teaching in the villages of 'Abeyh and Damur, and then moved to Cyprus, where he published a newspaper. He later returned to Lebanon and taught at the Sagesse College for ten years, and then at the Patriarchal College for 14 years. He wrote many plays, of which only one survives today. His most notable work, however, was the dictionary "al-Bustan". He died in February 1930.

54a75fca-9a38-5dc2-9f8e-80faf09f8470.name: *The Artist Girl and Her Studio*
54a75fca-9a38-5dc2-9f8e-80faf09f8470.keywords: Painting; Halil Pasha; orientalist Turkish painters
54a75fca-9a38-5dc2-9f8e-80faf09f8470.description2: The basis of Turkish painting drawing influence from western tradition was laid when *Mühendishane-i Berr-i Hümayun* (the Naval Academy) opened in 1795. Halil Pasha, who had been a student of the painting courses held at the Academy, was foremost among the painters with a military background who founded a western style art tradition in Turkey. He worked with Jean Leon Gerome in his atelier in Paris. He provided a unique distinction to the analysis of impressionist light and colour, and was an example of artists dealing with impressionist technique. Because of his qualified knowledge about anatomy and his interest in depicting the human figure, Halil Pasha had a unique place in Turkish Art History.

54c83199-c653-5912-a4b8-adeaddd7f3e5.name: Sursuq Palace
54c83199-c653-5912-a4b8-adeaddd7f3e5.description: Built in 1860 for Musa Sursuq, in Rue Sursuq, Sursuq Palace is now the residence of his grand-daughter Lady Yvonne Cochrane, who inherited the estate at the age of two. Of all the Sursuq houses, this is the largest and the only one that preserves its original splendour. Its second owner, Lady Cochrane's father Alfred Bey Sursuq, increased the size of the gardens and expanded the house's collection of valuable pictures, carpets and objets d'art.
54c83199-c653-5912-a4b8-adeaddd7f3e5.author: Jeff El-Msanne
54c83199-c653-5912-a4b8-adeaddd7f3e5.history: Other than some nineteenth century plaster-work in the reception rooms which resembles Sicilian palaces of the time, and the employment of some Italian craftsmen, the Sursuq House was built in a strictly traditional Lebanese architectural and aesthetic style. This is indicated first and foremost by the use of a single large block. The Great Hall consists of four sets of traditional Lebanese triple-arches, each supported by fluted marble pillars. The house’s painted furnishings were commissioned and designed privately. It also contains a series of glass cabinets, displaying various valuable collections, including second century glassware and Lebanese jewellery. The garden is one of the largest gardens left in the city, with many landowners having sold their properties to speculative building projects. The kiosk in the garden, which was converted into a Turkish baths when the house was built in 1860, predates the main house and is used as visitor rooms today.

54ee640a-4e1d-59a5-ba23-f9a85bf4e010.name: Gilet
54ee640a-4e1d-59a5-ba23-f9a85bf4e010.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
54ee640a-4e1d-59a5-ba23-f9a85bf4e010.archival: *Algérie, Mémoire de Femmes au Fil des Doigts*, Paris: 2002
54ee640a-4e1d-59a5-ba23-f9a85bf4e010.description2: This velvet bolero, known as a *frimla* has an embroidered front. It was typically worn over a silk shirt. Young Muslim and Jewish girls wore this gilet.

5514d06c-0d42-5cd5-ad41-d94d1fe042aa.name: Photograph of a *Rakkas* (runner) in front of a Post Office
5514d06c-0d42-5cd5-ad41-d94d1fe042aa.description: The photograph is of a Moroccan *Rakkas* (runner or messenger), responsible for taking and bringing back official messages and mail.
5514d06c-0d42-5cd5-ad41-d94d1fe042aa.keywords: Postal office; Spanish protectorate; rakkas; postal system; delivery; magazine

55244670-bd54-51f4-982e-13682dbb1443.name: A map of Tunisia (1:1,600,000) showing Italian agricultural settlements, mines, coral- and sponge-fishing areas and boat lines
55244670-bd54-51f4-982e-13682dbb1443.author: Giulia Barrera
55244670-bd54-51f4-982e-13682dbb1443.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906
55244670-bd54-51f4-982e-13682dbb1443.third_name: Carta della Tunisia protettorato francese, 1906 disegnata dal prof Cesidio Bonanni
55244670-bd54-51f4-982e-13682dbb1443.description2: The green rectangles on the map indicate Italian agricultural settlements; the number of settlers is indicated as well. In 1906 the majority of the Italian peasants had settled around Tunis and the Gulf of Hammamet. By contrast, few Italian peasants had settled in the South and in the interior of the country (the map indicated only 300 Italian peasants near Sfax and 400 near Kef).

554cc278-49e0-58cd-8147-15ce5f2c7002.name: Lady Layard’s jewellery
554cc278-49e0-58cd-8147-15ce5f2c7002.description2: Layard, excavator of Nineveh and other sites, had this necklace made as a wedding present for his wife. It combines ancient cylinder seals in contemporary gold settings. Said to have been much admired during dinner with Queen Victoria in 1873.

55519584-25f8-5377-bd87-8e67cbc0dc2c.name: Matchlock gun
55519584-25f8-5377-bd87-8e67cbc0dc2c.keywords: Weaponry; weapon; arms; armours; military object; metalwork; dance

555612b1-3b0e-5939-af4c-dcd61c208ab2.name: *Reading The Qu'ran*
555612b1-3b0e-5939-af4c-dcd61c208ab2.keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters
555612b1-3b0e-5939-af4c-dcd61c208ab2.description2: Osman Hamdi focused on dilemmas such as East and West, love and hate, life and death. While stylistically reminiscent of western Orientalist painters, his works reflect a more nuanced appreciation of Ottoman society and culture. He also gave importance to details while reflecting the colourful scenes of Turkish culture, traditional architecture, Ottoman fashion and domestic and social life of the women in the Ottoman Empire. And it’s obvious that he is the first painter who used human figures in the western style.

557a3c2b-e69e-533d-a2c9-d263db2c8d12.name: Woman's *entari*
557a3c2b-e69e-533d-a2c9-d263db2c8d12.description2: *Entari*s were worn over thin silk shifts and baggy *shalvar* trousers and were held at the waist by a sash or belt. They could be worn open or buttoned above the waist. Several *entari*s, made of different fabrics, usually with contrasting colours, were often layered on top of one another. They were more often than not made of luxurious silk striped or brocaded fabrics and trimmed with fine braid or *oya* needlework.

55817e68-2681-5c06-a3a1-71fdbd06edc2.name: Photograph of a diplomatic visit to England
55817e68-2681-5c06-a3a1-71fdbd06edc2.description: This photograph depicts the diplomatic delegation that accompanied Sultan of Morocco Mulay al-Hasan I’s Ambassador Hajj Muhammad al-Zebdi on an official visit to Britain at the invitation of Queen Victoria.
55817e68-2681-5c06-a3a1-71fdbd06edc2.keywords: Diplomacy; photograph; visual document; international relations; European powers

559330fc-4f61-535a-9310-1782a48a785a.name: The Tell Clock Tower
559330fc-4f61-535a-9310-1782a48a785a.description: This clock tower is located in Al-Tell square, next to Al-Manshiyya, one of the oldest parks in Tripoli. The tower is 30 metres tall and consists of five separate floors.
559330fc-4f61-535a-9310-1782a48a785a.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
559330fc-4f61-535a-9310-1782a48a785a.history: This clock tower was gifted to the city of Tripoli - like many clock towers of the Ottoman Empire, such as the famous Jaffa clock tower - and erected in 1906, to celebrate the 30th anniversary of Sultan 'Abd al-Hamid II's reign. The clock tower is now working again, following a full renovation in 1992, supported by personal funding from the honorary Turkish consul of Northern Lebanon, Sobhi Akkari.

55d4b6d2-fc7e-5bc6-a971-7a640559de05.name: *A Muslim man praying*
55d4b6d2-fc7e-5bc6-a971-7a640559de05.author: Ámparo López
55d4b6d2-fc7e-5bc6-a971-7a640559de05.description2: One of the drawings by Fortuny, one of the most important European painters of the last quarter of the 19th century. He travelled to Morocco in 1863 and he was taken by the light, colour and characters of the country. He was an important collector of Islamic artworks, some of them depicted in his paintings.

55e346ff-6f0e-5e17-90fe-1d309d2d7056.name: Painted chest
55e346ff-6f0e-5e17-90fe-1d309d2d7056.author: Xenia Politou
55e346ff-6f0e-5e17-90fe-1d309d2d7056.description2: The main façade of the chest is adorned with a composition of flowers, branches and fruits in curvilinear compartments, while the corners depict female figures flanked by columns. The interior of the lid shows a landscape with five male figures: a man with a European garment sitting on the ground observing another figure dressed in European clothes, two figures on horseback with Ottoman costumes and a European traveller. The panels in the style of rocailles that adorn both the main and the side views of the chest, the compositions of fruit and flowers and the soft colours refer to the prevailing influence of the rococo style that is dominant in the frescos of the mansions of Lesvos the late 18th century. Both the structure of the mansions and the decorative repertoire follow Ottoman aesthetic as these were by influenced by European art but blending baroque, rococo and neoclassical styles.

56204438-288e-5b14-9cb8-8b783efa0143.name: Turin: the castle in the Valentino Park
56204438-288e-5b14-9cb8-8b783efa0143.holder: Central Institute for Cataloguing and Documentation (ICCD)
56204438-288e-5b14-9cb8-8b783efa0143.holding_institution_org: Istituto Centrale per il Catalogo e la Documentazione (ICCD)

562cd119-0bf1-544d-a90a-b4094899b356.name: Arabi, Sayed Ahmed Pasha (1841–1911)
562cd119-0bf1-544d-a90a-b4094899b356.description2: Portrait of minister Sayed Ahmed Pasha Arabi (Urabi). In 1882, the war minister took power in Egypt and demanded an end to the financial control imposed by the UK and France. This led to an intervention by the British Navy under Admiral Seymour, who defeated the Egyptian army.

563af385-75b3-5cc2-a71e-50f89ce6f746.name: *Andalucía under Arab rule. Exposition of 1900*
563af385-75b3-5cc2-a71e-50f89ce6f746.keywords: World fairs; Orientalism; japan; north Africa
563af385-75b3-5cc2-a71e-50f89ce6f746.description2: This exhibition on the Arab presence in Andalucía was featured in the 1900 Exposition Universelle (world fair), reflecting a fashion for the rediscovery of Spain's North African past. Recently, for example, buildings in Granada and Córdoba had been rebuilt to host dances and fantasias. The artist of this poster, Eugène Grasset, has combined his two principal sources of inspiration - curiosity towards the Arab world, and japonese-inspired aesthetics.

563b533a-9eb3-5544-b906-bb25cf3be4c9.name: *The Gathering of the Romanians in Blaj (Transilvania), May 1848*

56669d0c-f1dc-5ef6-92fc-a676c2150aa7.name: Wooden shelving unit
56669d0c-f1dc-5ef6-92fc-a676c2150aa7.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
56669d0c-f1dc-5ef6-92fc-a676c2150aa7.description2: This shelf belonged to a traditional house in the town of Ksar Hellal. It would been hung from a wall as decoration, holding vases and perfume sprinklers, as well as weapons. It is characterized by its floral patterns with birds, flowers and leaves painted in stylised colours on a pale green background, all surrounding a multicolour fish.

5686a4e1-e33b-5ad7-8f7a-20b3b101f2ca.name: Petar (Pezia) Petrovich (2nd half of the 19th century – 1900)
5686a4e1-e33b-5ad7-8f7a-20b3b101f2ca.description2: Portrait of Petar (Pezia) Petrovic. He was Chief of the Albanian Mirdita tribes fighting against the Turks in 1876. This insurrection against the Turks provoked the 1878 Congress of Berlin, which led to the occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the Austrian Empire.

56bae231-ad09-5568-8e83-1f1aa7115444.name: Buckles (*Pafti*)
56bae231-ad09-5568-8e83-1f1aa7115444.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
56bae231-ad09-5568-8e83-1f1aa7115444.keywords: Buckles; live gold-plating; wedding; marriage; accessories; costume
56bae231-ad09-5568-8e83-1f1aa7115444.materials: Silver, filigree, granulation. Decoration with semi-precious stones, pearls and live gold plating
56bae231-ad09-5568-8e83-1f1aa7115444.description2: Buckles were distinctive articles of adornment used throughout the centuries by Macedonian women. They were the most frequently worn and most exquisite articles of adornment in Macedonian women’s folk attire. Buckles used to be adorned with stylized geometric and floral patterns, the artistic effect having been emphasized by the application of decorative stones, filigree ornaments, gold-plating, pearls, mother-of-pearl, corals, chains and other embellishments. This outstanding set of buckles in leaf shapes is decorated with pearls and semi-precious stones, by application of the technique of "live" gold-plating.

56ca4b0e-6b96-51e1-9a41-815aad91e661.name: Geomantic instrument
56ca4b0e-6b96-51e1-9a41-815aad91e661.description2: Geomantic instrument. Signed by the craftsman Muhammad b.Khutlukh al-Mawsili. Acquired by Augustus Wollaston Franks, a curator at the British Museum who played a key role in the building of the Mediaeval collection.

56cb7a4a-359b-5730-94fa-2694167837a5.name: Umm Qays
56cb7a4a-359b-5730-94fa-2694167837a5.dates: Greco-Roman until present; visited by Ulrich Seetzen in 1806
56cb7a4a-359b-5730-94fa-2694167837a5.author: Mohammad Najjar
56cb7a4a-359b-5730-94fa-2694167837a5.history: Founded during the 3rd century BCE, Gadara was taken first by the Seleucids of Syria during the 2nd century BCE, then by the Hasmoneans and finally “liberated” in 64 BCE by the Romans. In 30 BCE, it changed hands again to become under Herod the Great, but not for long. After the death of Herod, Gadara became part of the Roman Province of Syria. From the 4th till the 7th century, Gadara was a bishopric seat. After the battle of Yarmuk in 636, Gadara became part of the Islamic state. The most famous monuments of Gadara are its city walls and gates, theatres, octagonal basilicas and Mausoleum.
56cb7a4a-359b-5730-94fa-2694167837a5.keywords: Province of Arabia; Roman Province of Syria; bishopric seat; battle of Yarmuk
56cb7a4a-359b-5730-94fa-2694167837a5.description2: Located at the northern tip of Jordan, much of the Roman old city of Gadara is still covered by the deserted late Ottoman village of Umm Qays. Founded during the 3rd century BCE, Gadara was taken first by the Seleucids of Syria during the 2nd century BCE, then by the Hasmoneans and finally “liberated” in 64 BCE by the Romans. In 30 BCE, it changed hands again to become under Herod the Great, but not for long. After the death of Herod, Gadara became part of the Roman Province of Syria. From the 4th till the 7th century, Gadara was a bishopric seat. After the battle of Yarmuk in 636, Gadara became part of the Islamic state. The most famous monuments of Gadara are its city walls and gates, theatres, octagonal basilicas and Mausoleum.

56f05326-4b1d-5eff-9a58-a822374155ee.name: Portrait Of Binjamin Uziyel
56f05326-4b1d-5eff-9a58-a822374155ee.holder: The Quincentennial Foundation Museum, Archive of Turkish Jews
56f05326-4b1d-5eff-9a58-a822374155ee.keywords: Jewish community in Istanbul in 19th century; trade; sugar; commodities; markets
56f05326-4b1d-5eff-9a58-a822374155ee.description2: In 1911, when the Ottomans had to leave Tripoli, Binjamin Uziyel, who served in the consulate there, did research on a project of setting up sugar factories in Turkey after going to Genoa. He presented it to the Istanbul Chamber of Commerce by preparing a detailed report about setting up sugar factories in Turkey and ways to use the sugar beet.

5714f381-6e11-56d5-9801-fef85803c128.name: Wedding dress
5714f381-6e11-56d5-9801-fef85803c128.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
5714f381-6e11-56d5-9801-fef85803c128.author: Huda Kilani
5714f381-6e11-56d5-9801-fef85803c128.materials: Linen and silk; hand woven and hand embroidered
5714f381-6e11-56d5-9801-fef85803c128.description2: Long black dress, wide at the bottom with narrow sleeves, rounded neck and open chest. Silk linen appliqué, hand embroidery with cross-stitch on the sides, back panel, chest, and sleeves with embroidered folkloric patterns. On the chest: necklace, cypress tree. Side: ivy, amulets, “feathers”. Front: small cypress tree on silk. Back: ivy, cypress tree, pillows, pasha tents. Sleeve: ivy, feather, triangle (amulets). Palestinian women's costumes varied according to each Palestinian city and geographical area. Costumes in the mountain regions were different from those of coastal and desert areas, and had a distinguished embroidery. This costume represents village style. Girls started preparing their trousseau (clothes, shawls and other belongings they collected for their marriage) at the age of ten. Married women's costumes were heavily embroidered. Palestinian weavers used traditional spinning processes using manual spindles to prepare the cotton and linen threads imported from Egypt. Ashkelon city weavers used light vertical hand looms (*Majdalawi* looms) to produce linen fabrics, while silk fabrics were spindled and woven in Syria.

571c2e73-e0f1-5b98-b748-e41a5e7ff2b7.name: Door carved on wood
571c2e73-e0f1-5b98-b748-e41a5e7ff2b7.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
571c2e73-e0f1-5b98-b748-e41a5e7ff2b7.description2: This door from the interior of the museum of the Palais du Bardo is made of carved and studded oak, with two panels on either side. The frames are studded along their horizontal axis, and the panels are richly decorated with flower vase motifs.

5737c1ee-cc7f-51c5-a3a0-7d7bf8615842.name: Iznik bottle
5737c1ee-cc7f-51c5-a3a0-7d7bf8615842.author: Mina Moraitou
5737c1ee-cc7f-51c5-a3a0-7d7bf8615842.keywords: Iznik; Egypt; Greeks; collecting; exhibition; London
5737c1ee-cc7f-51c5-a3a0-7d7bf8615842.description2: An Iznik flask, with a spherical body and a long neck, is decorated with polychrome flowers: roses, hyacinth and carnations and the neck displays vertical panels. Bought by A. Benakis in Cairo in 1920 and according to the etiquettes under the base it was part of the 1885 exhibition at the Burlington Arts Club in London and of the 1925 exhibition in Alexandria. Ottoman c. 1575.

5742022d-5251-5bf2-9309-1b5f081234cd.name: *A Costume from Capri*
5742022d-5251-5bf2-9309-1b5f081234cd.author: DGPC
5742022d-5251-5bf2-9309-1b5f081234cd.description2: Until the 19th century, Portuguese painting focussed on landscape and local habits. The new interest for travelling and for other cultures can be seen in this oil painting by Silva Porto portraying a girl from the Island of Capri and her costume.
5742022d-5251-5bf2-9309-1b5f081234cd.holding_institution_org: Museu Nacional de Soares dos Reis

5747fe8d-4ab0-565c-9e90-6e797f311e64.name: Four guns
5747fe8d-4ab0-565c-9e90-6e797f311e64.type: Military object; metalwork; firearms; arms and armour
5747fe8d-4ab0-565c-9e90-6e797f311e64.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
5747fe8d-4ab0-565c-9e90-6e797f311e64.keywords: Military object; Metalwork; Steel; Arms; armour; Gun
5747fe8d-4ab0-565c-9e90-6e797f311e64.description2: These Turkish flintlock pistols were used by the Ottoman soldiers in Lebanon in the 19th century to quash resistance movements. As the Lebanese resistance had no weapons of their own, the fighters frequently ambushed Ottoman soldiers and took their weapons. These pistols are an example of such weaponry, which was taken by the resistance and used against the Ottomans. They have a wooden butt stock, a slightly broken wooden forend and a round barrel. They are made of wood and cast steel.

574d6f3c-2cbb-5d5b-9f00-e0dd275b71a9.name: *Excavation of the Great Temple of Ramesses II at Abu Simbel*
574d6f3c-2cbb-5d5b-9f00-e0dd275b71a9.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
574d6f3c-2cbb-5d5b-9f00-e0dd275b71a9.description2:
An intrepid and versatile Frenchman, Linant came to Egypt in 1818. In Cairo he adopted the life of an Ottoman Turk, but was known and consulted by European residents and visitors as well as by the Pasha of Egypt, Muhammad Ali. At various times his talents were employed as a geographer, explorer, engineer, cartographer and draughtsman.  
His first adventure was an expedition to Upper Egypt that Henry Salt, British Consul-General in Egypt , took to Abu Simbel in 1818-19. Although there were other artists in the party it is likely that this watercolour is by Linant and that it depicts Salt's attempts to clear away the ever encroaching sand from the facade of the Great Temple. Linant took part in several subsequent expeditions up the Nile, and was one of the first Europeans to reach the Pharaonic sites of Meroe and Musawarat.

574ec553-46f8-5bdf-871c-23a4e10a1779.name: Bellino copy
574ec553-46f8-5bdf-871c-23a4e10a1779.keywords: Cuneiform; drawing; archaeology; exploration; collection; collector; museums; travel; traveller; inscription
574ec553-46f8-5bdf-871c-23a4e10a1779.description2: Hand drawing by Bellino of BM 22502. Bellino’s technique produced wonderfully accurate copies, despite the fact that cuneiform was not yet deciphered.

576f26e0-f45e-5486-860f-0324e1f36b51.name: Bracelet
576f26e0-f45e-5486-860f-0324e1f36b51.description: This silver bracelet is decorated with cobalt blue and enamel and bears an inscription from an Arabic poem. Crafted in Essaouira in the 20th century, it is very likely to have been made for a European woman. Cobalt was a European import.
576f26e0-f45e-5486-860f-0324e1f36b51.keywords: Trade; raw materials; finished products; cobalt-blue; applied arts; enamelling; inscription; decorative inscription; Moroccan craftsmanship for European market; craftsmanship; traditional craftsmanship; Moroccan craftsmen

578a0774-be4c-5eb0-85a3-86bf64c69e71.name: Palais du Bardo
578a0774-be4c-5eb0-85a3-86bf64c69e71.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
578a0774-be4c-5eb0-85a3-86bf64c69e71.keywords: Palais du Bardo; beylical throne; European influences; Italian influences
578a0774-be4c-5eb0-85a3-86bf64c69e71.description2: This postcard shows the throne room of the Palais du Bardo, with its rich furnishings and monumental chandeliers hanging from the ceiling. The bey's throne sits in the centre, surrounded by paintings of the princes of the Husainid dynasty, painted wooden ceilings, mirrors and console tables carved and painted with gold leaf, and with two great rooms on either side. From the 18th century onwards the Husainid beys continuously expanded and decorated the Palais du Bardo. The architecture and furniture all indicate a strong European, particularly Italian, influence.

57952ce7-c1d9-5593-a21a-cd6480d6eec9.name: Illuminated Qur’an manuscript
57952ce7-c1d9-5593-a21a-cd6480d6eec9.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
57952ce7-c1d9-5593-a21a-cd6480d6eec9.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
57952ce7-c1d9-5593-a21a-cd6480d6eec9.materials: European paper, black ink, pigments, gilding, pasteboard, leather
57952ce7-c1d9-5593-a21a-cd6480d6eec9.description2: 19th-century Qur’an manuscripts produced in Istanbul and the Ottoman Empire continued many Islamic art traditions, but could not entirely escape the increasing taste for Western aesthetics. The quality of this Qur’an manuscript suggests that it might have been executed for a member of the Imperial household. The radiant opening double-page shows two delicate cartouches with ‘Al Fatiha’ and the beginning of ‘Al Baqara’ set into a majestic framework of gilt floral arabesque cartouches. The main body of the text is executed in finest black naskh, 15 lines to the page, the sura headings written in white riqa' on a solid golden ground. Beyond the gold margins, delicated medallions mark important subdivisions in the text. The last double page shows the end of sura 113 and sura 114 on the right and the dedication page on the left. Both texts are embedded in rectangular panels accentuated with richly gilt and blue ornamentation. Beyond, the entire page is covered with delicate sprays and leaves painted in solid gold.

579a1e8e-d0d1-5139-bb97-214a66f11b68.name: The Ottoman Navy, Mahmudiye
579a1e8e-d0d1-5139-bb97-214a66f11b68.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
579a1e8e-d0d1-5139-bb97-214a66f11b68.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ottoman navy; Mahmudiye
579a1e8e-d0d1-5139-bb97-214a66f11b68.description2: The 19th century saw further decline in Ottoman naval power, despite occasional recovery. Following the defeat against the combined British-French-Russian fleet at the Battle of Navarino in 1827, Sultan Mahmud II gave priority to developing a strong and modern Ottoman naval force. The first steam ships of the Ottoman Navy were acquired in 1828. The ship of the line Mahmudiye, which had 128 cannons on three decks and carried 1,280 sailors on board, was built for the Ottoman Navy at the Imperial Naval Arsenal (Tersâne-i Âmire) on the Golden Horn in Constantinople.

57af1dd9-6f7e-59ac-a49a-549fb3d6d750.name: Bowl
57af1dd9-6f7e-59ac-a49a-549fb3d6d750.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
57af1dd9-6f7e-59ac-a49a-549fb3d6d750.author: Marina Minozzi
57af1dd9-6f7e-59ac-a49a-549fb3d6d750.keywords: Egyptomania; Gaetano Rosellini; university; collector; photograph; anthropology; palaeoethnology; material culture; Florence; Pisa; Egyptology; Nubia; languages; hieroglyph; William Matthew Flinders Petrie; Jacques de Morgan; David Randall-MacIver; dealer
57af1dd9-6f7e-59ac-a49a-549fb3d6d750.description2: Probably used to keep cosmetics, the artwork is part of the purchases bought by Roberto Paribeni (later Soprintendente alle antichità di Roma e Lazio, 1928–1933) in 1904 from Ghirghis, the antiquities dealer in Quena, on behalf of "Museo Preistorico ed Etnografico" in Rome. In 1878 Luigi Pigorini, director of the "Museo Preistorico Etnografico e Kircheriano", decided to expand the museum’s Egyptian archaeological collection. The main body of the collection was donated by David Randall-MacIver in 1901, after the excavations he carried out on the behalf of the Egypt Exploration Fund in the town of el-Amrah, Upper Egypt. Another major purchase — from the Italian Archaeological Mission in Egypt (excavations of Hammamiye) led by Ernesto Schiaparelli, director of the Egyptian Museum in Turin — followed in 1905. The last main acquisition took place in 1913 when the Egyptian objects from the Enrico Hillyer Giglioli’s collection entered the museum collection.

en: Cappozzo, M., “La collezione egizia del Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico ‘Luigi Pigorini’”, in *Bullettino di Paletnologia Italiana*, Roma, Istituto Poligrafico e Zecca dello Stato, (2005–2007), 96: 131–202, cat. 131.

57d9ec8b-2100-527f-abb2-8188927bef19.name: *The Gate of a Mosque, Istanbul*
57d9ec8b-2100-527f-abb2-8188927bef19.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
57d9ec8b-2100-527f-abb2-8188927bef19.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
57d9ec8b-2100-527f-abb2-8188927bef19.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
57d9ec8b-2100-527f-abb2-8188927bef19.description2: This oil painting shows the entrance gate to an Ottoman mosque or mausoleum complex, set in a lush shaded garden with majestic trees, its tall pointed minaret soaring high above the tiled awnings of the surrounding wall. Two turbaned old men, one seated on the pavement at the gate, the other standing to face him, accentuate the scene on the street outside. The painter of this somewhat melancholy scene, Halil Bey, was trained under Gerome and Courtoix. Under the influence of European artists and encouraged by the tastes of the Ottoman court, the arts underwent a great deal of transformation in the 13th/ 19th century. Painting in western styles gained increasing acceptance, and several local artists now concentrated on depicting their surroundings in a manner and style which they had learned in painting and drawing classes given by European instructors, either in Ottoman cities, or - as in the case of Halil Bey - in the prominent European centres of art.

57e870a3-328c-5454-8a46-128fb0cb4e2a.name: Pair of vases and pedestals
57e870a3-328c-5454-8a46-128fb0cb4e2a.description: The interlacing and the flower decoration of this pair of glass vases can be considered an example of the great influence exerted by the Turkish or Orientalist revival. The glass factories of the Austro-Hungarian Empire played an important role in the spreading of this style.
57e870a3-328c-5454-8a46-128fb0cb4e2a.author: Ana Cabrera
57e870a3-328c-5454-8a46-128fb0cb4e2a.keywords: Turkish style; Applied Arts; Production of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode

57ffa9ee-eaef-5f59-b4a3-2237ac46b63a.name: The ivory trade
57ffa9ee-eaef-5f59-b4a3-2237ac46b63a.second_name: Transporting elephant tusks from Congo. Exhibition of the goods before sale in Anvers.
57ffa9ee-eaef-5f59-b4a3-2237ac46b63a.description2: Although banned in 1989, in the 19th century the ivory trade was flourishing. Many different objects, all marketed to a wealthy buyer, were made from this material: decorations, piano keys, knife handles, combs, fans, umbrella handles, and more.

582735bb-91b8-5a1b-b50e-a4d74176b7d7.name: Knife
582735bb-91b8-5a1b-b50e-a4d74176b7d7.holder: Palais de la Rose – Musée de l’Armée
582735bb-91b8-5a1b-b50e-a4d74176b7d7.author: Bechir Yazidi
582735bb-91b8-5a1b-b50e-a4d74176b7d7.keywords: Tunisian army; Musée de l'Armée; Palais de la Rose
582735bb-91b8-5a1b-b50e-a4d74176b7d7.description2: The surface of this silver-plated bronze knife is covered in beautiful engravings, and the handle is decorated with floral motifs. Various coats of arms are engraved on the blade, along with a stylised ship with an Arabic inscription on the other side. The handle is 65 cm long and the blade is 21 cm long.

5838c354-7008-5b83-99dc-80cbba207468.name: Egyptianising plate
5838c354-7008-5b83-99dc-80cbba207468.description2: Plate with Egyptianising motifs and a copy of a drawing by Dominique Vivant Denon, *Voyage dans la Basse et la Haute Egypte, pendant les campagnes du Général Bonaparte*, 1802. Part of an Egyptian Service. Said to have been one of 3 Sevres plates which were thrown out of the windows of the Tuileries during the Revolution of 1848.

5838d2ce-d94c-553a-ba3e-9f697d70d8a3.name: Photograph of Tell el-Hesi diggers
5838d2ce-d94c-553a-ba3e-9f697d70d8a3.description2: Some members of F.J. Bliss’ workforce at Tell el-Hesi. What is most noteworthy here is that in the period up to 1938 men, women, and children all worked together on excavations.

583ec252-d918-5a71-8d38-4732db2c355a.name: Archaeological Museum of the American University of Beirut
583ec252-d918-5a71-8d38-4732db2c355a.author: Julien El Khoury, Jeff El-Msanne, Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
583ec252-d918-5a71-8d38-4732db2c355a.history: The museum was founded in 1868 after Luigi Palma di Cesnola gifted a collection of Cypriot pottery to the newly formed American University of Beirut. Georges Post was the first curator of this collection and Morris Jesup donated the funds to construct the Post Hall which opened in 1902. The museum kept receiving collection from all around the Middle-East until 1938, after which it closed for the duration of World War II. The museum re-opened in 1948 and expanded by doubling its floor space with a refurbishment under curator D. C. Baramki which became accessible to the public in 1964. Later, in 2006, the building underwent another complete renovation under the present director, Dr. Leila Badre.
583ec252-d918-5a71-8d38-4732db2c355a.keywords: museum; archaeology; exhibition; exploration; research; excavation; Museum; AUB; Archaeological; Beirut; Artefacts; Collection
583ec252-d918-5a71-8d38-4732db2c355a.description2: The Archaeological Museum of the American University of Beirut is the third oldest museum in the Middle East after those in Cairo and Istanbul. The museum collections are organized in chronological order on one side and by themes on the other. The chronological displays are set along the  walls of the gallery, showing the evolution of pottery from the Chalcolitic Age (4000 BC) to the Islamic period (19th century AD). As for the thematic displays, they include the Cesnola collection, the Pre-Historic Section, the Ksar Akil excavation, the Paleolithic and Neolithic Periods, the Terracotta and Metal Figurines, the Bronze and Iron Ages, the Phoenician Civilisations, the Classical, Graeco-Roman and Byzantine and Islamic periods.

585f44a9-1964-5231-b9ed-0ff3c0f07d5c.name: 5 Piastres
585f44a9-1964-5231-b9ed-0ff3c0f07d5c.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury
585f44a9-1964-5231-b9ed-0ff3c0f07d5c.keywords: Commerce; trade; Currency; Coins; coinage; Numismatics
585f44a9-1964-5231-b9ed-0ff3c0f07d5c.description2: This 5 piastres bank note was printed by Bradbury Wilkinson and Co (BWC) without a watermark.

587837e2-ba2c-5d56-b39a-b5dcb62c7f11.name: Model of traditional pearling boat
587837e2-ba2c-5d56-b39a-b5dcb62c7f11.holder: Sharjah Maritime Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
587837e2-ba2c-5d56-b39a-b5dcb62c7f11.dates: Hegira first half of the 14th century / AD 20th century
587837e2-ba2c-5d56-b39a-b5dcb62c7f11.dimensions: Length 2334 mm, width 535 mm, height 395 mm
587837e2-ba2c-5d56-b39a-b5dcb62c7f11.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
587837e2-ba2c-5d56-b39a-b5dcb62c7f11.description2: This type of boat represents the most common type of vessel that was involved in the pearling trade in Sharjah. Throughout the Arabian Gulf, several types of boats such as the Jalboot, Sambooq, Battil and the Sama'a, although in fact multi-purpose, were used for pearling at the peak of the industry in the 19th and early 20th centuries. Depending on the boat and size, the boats had the capacity to carry between 10 and 100 crew. This model is of the 'Saku', a Sama'a-type boat originally belonging to Juma Al Sari, the father of the model donor.

58837723-b1a0-5787-a2b8-812f79e409c5.name: Dr Charles Nicolle, Nobel Laureate for Medicine
58837723-b1a0-5787-a2b8-812f79e409c5.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
58837723-b1a0-5787-a2b8-812f79e409c5.description2: This is a photograph of Dr Charles Nicolle carrying out child vaccination on the indigenous Tunisian population. During his time at l'Institut Pasteur (1903–1936) he worked to prevent or eradicate infectious illnesses

5890a2e4-6da7-5662-bc9c-87c618c5eca2.name: *From the days of the Revolution in Berlin: Philip Scheidemann proclaims the Weimer Republic in front of the Reichstag*

58a491a4-71cc-5b24-a1a9-764a71488439.name: *Works for the opening of the Corinth Canal*
58a491a4-71cc-5b24-a1a9-764a71488439.author: Maria Dimitriadou
58a491a4-71cc-5b24-a1a9-764a71488439.description2:
The Corinth Canal being dug. Photographer unknown.  
The Corinth Canal separates the Peloponnesian peninsula from the Greek. The idea of the canal was revived after Greece gained independence but soon abandoned due to economical reasons. The opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 gave an new impetus and the following year, the Zaimis government passed a law authorising the construction of the canal, which was formally inaugurated on 23 April 1882. Zaimis assigned the project to the Hungarian István Türr who set up the Société Internationale du Canal Maritime de Corinthe but the company failed and the project was finished by the company of Andeas Syngros. The canal was designed by the Hungarian engineer Béla Gerster with the assistance of the French Vincent Dauzants, a chief engineer of the Suez canal.

58b9817a-c39c-5ed0-9922-32e3e0ccbd6a.name: The bronze statue representing 22 countries of member of Universal Postal Union
58b9817a-c39c-5ed0-9922-32e3e0ccbd6a.description2: The Universal Postal Union was created in 1874, initially under the name "General Postal Union", as a result of the Treaty of Bern signed on 9 October 1874. The UPU is a specialized agency of the United Nations that coordinates postal policies among member nations, in addition to the worldwide postal system. Transportation freedom is guaranteed with this treaty.

58b9f9f7-6b17-532d-8f51-0f4b19d4fb8d.name: *Vue d'Alger*
58b9f9f7-6b17-532d-8f51-0f4b19d4fb8d.author: Dalila Orfali
58b9f9f7-6b17-532d-8f51-0f4b19d4fb8d.description2: These two original lithographs depict the city of al-Jaza'ir (Algiers) prior to the English bombardment led by Lord Exmouth on 26 August 1816. The regency was ruled first by the *Beylerbeys* (general governors) from 1518 to 1587, then by the Pashas from 1587 to 1659, the *Aghas* from 1659 to 1671 and the Deys from 1671 to 1830. The reign of the final Dey of Algiers, Hussein, lasted 12 years until the French conquest in 1830.

58d8569e-9dce-5ab4-bed2-63c6b0b22bb0.name: Cabinet on stand
58d8569e-9dce-5ab4-bed2-63c6b0b22bb0.description: The Neo-Mudéjar style gave new light to different workshops and techniques. As a consequence of this revival woodwork technique for furniture, such as the inlay in Granada style, was recreated in different pieces of furniture such as this cabinet. The decoration of stars and interlacing arabesques at the front of the cabinet shows the influence of the Mudéjar art.
58d8569e-9dce-5ab4-bed2-63c6b0b22bb0.author: Ana Cabrera
58d8569e-9dce-5ab4-bed2-63c6b0b22bb0.keywords: Neo-mudejar style; Applied ArtsProduction of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode

58fe74cf-18fc-5029-b7a5-11247965159d.name: *The Torchlight Parade through the Stambol Gate*
58fe74cf-18fc-5029-b7a5-11247965159d.author: Petar Petrovic
58fe74cf-18fc-5029-b7a5-11247965159d.description2: *The Torchlight Parade through the Stambol Gate* presents a historical moment that occurred in Belgrade in December 1858. The citizens who were supporters of the Serbian sovereign dynasty Obrenović, celebrated the return of the dynasty's founder, Prince Milos.

58ffe3b7-a7c4-59ea-a3f7-15adee4841cf.name: Sword that belonged to Carol of Hohenzollern
58ffe3b7-a7c4-59ea-a3f7-15adee4841cf.description2: In April 1866, Carol of Hohenzollern was elected by plebiscite ruler of the United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia. However, according to the Paris Convention of 1858, an act signed by the Ottoman Empire, Russia, Austria, Prussia, France, Great Britain and Sardinia, which established the internal organization of the Principalities, they were supposed to each have their own local prince. So, Carol’s election had to be recognized by the Sublime Porte, the sovereign power, and by the other Great Powers. Following negotiations held at Istanbul, in October sultan Abdul Aziz agreed to give his consent. Carol then travelled to Istanbul, where he was invested as ruler of the Principalities and was given by the sultan five Arabian horses and a sword decorated with 1140 brilliants and 46 diamonds.

59043927-aae8-5c23-9db7-2ff253833d51.name: *The political refugee*
59043927-aae8-5c23-9db7-2ff253833d51.second_name: Illustration for "The Bohemians of Paris", *Le Charivari* 11
59043927-aae8-5c23-9db7-2ff253833d51.description2: The cartoonist Honoré Daumier (1808–1879) was one of the first to be interested in the theme of migration, and drew many cartoon strips which dealt with the difficulties of exile. He did some more comic drawings on this theme, which are harder to understand. In this image, published in a series on the theme of the "Bohemian" (an artistic community attempting to live without restrictions), he highlights the gaze of his contemporaries on the "other" or the "stranger". The image also mocks the suspicious young woman just as much as the asylum seeker.

593969dc-7368-5182-961d-c81a464474fc.name: Bridal headdress (*Kiska*)
593969dc-7368-5182-961d-c81a464474fc.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
593969dc-7368-5182-961d-c81a464474fc.keywords: Decorative pin; kiska; apotropaic intention; amulet; talisman; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; wedding; marriage
593969dc-7368-5182-961d-c81a464474fc.description2: Hairpins and other articles of adornment worn on the head were inevitable elements of Macedonian women's attire in the 19th century and at the beginning of the 20th century. This distinctive decorative pin – *kiska* – was used for supporting the hat or scarf. This type of jewellery also conveyed a symbolic meaning and served an apotropaic purpose in addition to its decorative function. The pear-shaped ornament was made by application of filigree and granulation techniques. It is adorned with pellets and decorative stones in varied colours. Tiny coins are suspended on chains at the bottom of the ornament.

5959e6d7-d24c-578d-ae73-38a0dfc8b00d.name: *Mostaganem*
5959e6d7-d24c-578d-ae73-38a0dfc8b00d.archival: Ravoisié, A., *Exploration scientifique de l'Algérie pendant les annéees 1840-1841-1842*, vol. I, Paris: 1846.

59764ffc-10d9-5e4d-8967-5888b3e97194.name: National Museum of Soares dos Reis
59764ffc-10d9-5e4d-8967-5888b3e97194.history: The Carrancas Palace is a neo-classical palace built by the Moraes e Castro family, which accommodated the English generals during the Napoleonic Invasions, and was later converted into a royal residence. The National Museum of Soares dos Reis, established by King Pedro IV in 1833, was Portugal’s first public museum and was inspired by the cultural and heritage protecting spirit typical of Liberalism.
59764ffc-10d9-5e4d-8967-5888b3e97194.keywords: Neoclassicism; Oporto; Palace; Museum; History of Art
59764ffc-10d9-5e4d-8967-5888b3e97194.description2:
The Carrancas Palace is an imposing neoclassical building with four main areas: the U-shaped noble area, the galleries, the closed central courtyard and the backyard. Despite having been converted into a museum, the palace has preserved most of its original structure.  
The building interior has a refined decoration, shown in the stuccoes embellishing the dining room and the furniture in the music room, both of which were inspired on the creations of Robert Adams.

5984df39-df0b-5179-8186-0d620e962e8c.name: Portrait of Butrus al-Bustani
5984df39-df0b-5179-8186-0d620e962e8c.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
5984df39-df0b-5179-8186-0d620e962e8c.description2: Butrus al-Bustani was born in Debbeye, and studied at Ayn Warka School for ten years. He was appointed professor at this school at the age of 20, before moving to teach in the American College of 'Abeyh. He then moved to Beirut, where he became an interpreter at the US consulate, working with American missionaries and their printing press. He published numerous important books, including his famous Encyclopedia, and founded the National School of Beirut. He died in May 1883.

598e9ec9-1f57-5e63-b1c0-7af5516c4a62.name: Lithograph- Portrait of Pavel Kisselef, Russian governor of Valahia and Moldova between 1829-1834

598fbe2f-0ba0-5a5a-92b7-3f83e20bded7.name: *Mr Drovetti and his entourage measuring a fragment of the Colossus in Upper Egypt*
598fbe2f-0ba0-5a5a-92b7-3f83e20bded7.second_name: Taken from *Voyage dans le Levant en 1817 et 1818*, by M. le Comte de Forbin
598fbe2f-0ba0-5a5a-92b7-3f83e20bded7.description2: Bernardino Drovetti (1776–1852) an Italian who joined the French army, was made a diplomat after having elicited Napoléon I's sympathy by saving his step-brother. Having been sent to Egypt as a consul, he then collected antiquities and thus portrayed himself as a defender of discovered treasures. He is pictured here with his team holding a plumb line in front of a colossus. Jean-Jacques Rifaud is leaning on the sculpture's head and dressed in an imitation of the local style. Dovretti later sold his collections to the Prince of Piedmont, to King Charles X of France and to the King of Prussia.

59c09c6e-e0cc-5963-83cc-fd6b4aea8244.name: Bakırköy Railway Station
59c09c6e-e0cc-5963-83cc-fd6b4aea8244.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
59c09c6e-e0cc-5963-83cc-fd6b4aea8244.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph The Hijaz Railways
59c09c6e-e0cc-5963-83cc-fd6b4aea8244.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

59c2a789-38b6-526c-8c2e-10450f77128f.name: Long Moorish musket
59c2a789-38b6-526c-8c2e-10450f77128f.description: This musket, along with other pieces, was taken by Salvador de Foronda, a member of the Spanish Army, awarded for his actions in battle. He was a relative of the Marquis of Cerralbo and donated to his uncle’s museum these exceptional pieces in 1918. The Moorish musket, a long firearm that could be shot with a single arm while riding the horse, was described by Salvador as “one of the most ancient and authentic", a truly beauty with damascene work, romantically infused with the testimony of the war.
59c2a789-38b6-526c-8c2e-10450f77128f.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes
59c2a789-38b6-526c-8c2e-10450f77128f.materials: Wood, metal, fabric; handmade, damascene work

59da1fe4-84c5-5f28-93ff-51acc78bc1c4.name: *Young Algerian man*
59da1fe4-84c5-5f28-93ff-51acc78bc1c4.description2: Much of what was written about life in Algiers during the 18th and 19th centuries focussed on the elegance of male dress. This lithographic illustrated page is taken from a collection entitled *Costumes Nationaux* which was published simultaneously in both London and Paris. It shows a young Algerian man, wearing a red *chechia* with a blue tassel, a large *sarouel* tied at the waist by a long cotton belt, and a long-sleeved embroidered *ghlila*. He is leaning on a *skemla* with a nargile pipe on top. However, even in this image the model does not have a very Algerian appearance. This was a common occurrence, as European artists would complete their works in their studios after having returned from their travels.

59e106e1-b0a2-5505-af4e-7abfde04a90a.name: Belt
59e106e1-b0a2-5505-af4e-7abfde04a90a.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
59e106e1-b0a2-5505-af4e-7abfde04a90a.author: Huda Kilani
59e106e1-b0a2-5505-af4e-7abfde04a90a.keywords: Leather; belt; embellished; niello; rosette buckles; silver
59e106e1-b0a2-5505-af4e-7abfde04a90a.description2: Leather belt embellished with silver pieces decorated in niello with patterns and symbols at the end. Two silver rosette buckles at the end form a locking mechanism. This is an object produced by Circassian craftsmen. The immigration of the Circassians to the Ottoman Empire started in the middle of 19th century and continued until 1900. The Circassian communities migrated mostly to the eastern Arab countries, with which they had spiritual and religious links. They brought with them their traditional activities, crafts and decorative patterns. All these elements soon mingled with the local Arab society and became part of the social and economic landscape of the Arab countries.

59e91077-81f0-5cb2-9fc1-2e7eb98c95ab.name: Turkish woman
59e91077-81f0-5cb2-9fc1-2e7eb98c95ab.description2: The Zangaki brothers were a pair of photographers working in Egypt who sold "Orientalist" photos to Western tourists. This photograph for example, responds to Western stereotypes by depicting a Turkish woman lying nonchalantly by shisha pipe.

59eb8eb8-862f-5124-b1c8-abb0f2db5588.name: Hydrographic map of Lower Egypt and part of the Suez isthmus, engraved at the Dépôt de la Guerre
59eb8eb8-862f-5124-b1c8-abb0f2db5588.artist: Louis Maurice Adolphe Linant de Bellefonds
59eb8eb8-862f-5124-b1c8-abb0f2db5588.second_name: Drawn according to the work of M. Linant de Bellefonds, reviewed and completed in 1882 for the railways and the Suez canal. 1:250,000
59eb8eb8-862f-5124-b1c8-abb0f2db5588.description2: Louis Maurice Adolphe Linant de Bellefonds (1798–1883), artist and explorer passionate about Egypt, played a key role alongside Ferdinand de Lesseps in drawing and constructing the Suez Canal. He was given the title 'Bey' by the Egyptian viceroy, appointed director of Egyptian public works, and contributed to the irrigation of farmland. The map drawn in 1855 included the barriers; the outline of the Suez Canal and the railways were added in 1882.

5a0832a0-d80b-5889-9b46-4a7e7fdf77f8.name: Pearl Trader’s Gauges
5a0832a0-d80b-5889-9b46-4a7e7fdf77f8.holder: Sharjah Maritime Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
5a0832a0-d80b-5889-9b46-4a7e7fdf77f8.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
5a0832a0-d80b-5889-9b46-4a7e7fdf77f8.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
5a0832a0-d80b-5889-9b46-4a7e7fdf77f8.description2: These seven rectangular and foldable copper alloy gauges were used to ascertain the various sizes and circumferences of pearls, from the most miniscule to the gigantic, which would have fetched the highest price. When not in use, the implement was folded away and stored in a simple copper alloy sheath.

5a3f6e57-a4ba-5aea-abeb-7412fd90e2a9.name: The objects found in the tomb of Tutankhamun
5a3f6e57-a4ba-5aea-abeb-7412fd90e2a9.description2: This photo documented items from the Tutankhamun tomb. The Tomb of Tutankhamun was discovered in 1922 in the Valley of the Kings by Egyptologist Howard Carter. The discovery of this tomb caused a worldwide media stir.

5a482712-4636-5e5b-aa8a-6973d1c66d25.name: *The Approach to Nablus (Shechem)*
5a482712-4636-5e5b-aa8a-6973d1c66d25.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
5a482712-4636-5e5b-aa8a-6973d1c66d25.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
5a482712-4636-5e5b-aa8a-6973d1c66d25.artist: Josiah Wood Whymper (after a pencil drawing by Harry Fenn 1838–1911)
5a482712-4636-5e5b-aa8a-6973d1c66d25.description2: This image shows the approach to Nablus (at the time believed to mark the biblical Shechem, according to the Bible first capital of the Kingdom of Israel and situated in the vicinity of several important Abrahamic sites). The caption further explains that the view is taken through the olive groves on the eastern side of the city, and that 'the gate is shown beneath the minaret'. The artist who created this work, Josiah Wood Whymper, was a British watercolour painter, engraver, and illustrator, who apparently never left Britain, but provided a prolific body of engravings to publishers, in particular the Society for the Promotion of Christian Knowledge. This print originally appeared in Vol. 1, page 243 of Charles William Wilson's  'Pituresque Palestine, Sinai and Egypt', published between 1881 and 1884.

5a77c00d-9eb8-5458-82b1-be2e4374f487.name: The House of Shaykh Said bin Mohammed al-Qasimi
5a77c00d-9eb8-5458-82b1-be2e4374f487.holder: Sharjah Museums Authority / Sharjah Heritage Directorate

5a77c00d-9eb8-5458-82b1-be2e4374f487.third_name: Bayt al-Shaykh Said bin Mohammed al-Qasimi
5a77c00d-9eb8-5458-82b1-be2e4374f487.description2: Bayt al-Shaykh Said bin Mohammed al-Qasimi (today comprehensively restored) was built between 1898 and 1901 for the local Qasimi ruler. A single-storeyed house with windowless surrounding walls, it follows the traditional layout of a local residence arranged around a central courtyard. Its majlis or reception room is unusually large, with a tall central column and beam construction enabling the space to be considerably widened beyond the more commonly applied dimensions. Bait al Shaikh Said bin Mohammed Al Qasimi witnessed the signing of several trucial agreements with the British pertinent to the whole region.

5aae14de-96b5-54d8-bde0-643bb24e8c93.name: Palace of Mulay ʿAbd al-Hafiz
5aae14de-96b5-54d8-bde0-643bb24e8c93.history: Built in the era of Mulay Isma‘il (mid-18th century) by the architect-Pasha ‘Ali al-Rifi, the palace was renovated and adapted by Mulay al-Hasan I’s son, ‘Abd al-Hafiz. However, the latter never lived there because he was exiled to Spain by the French before it was completed, but as a condition of signing the Deed of Protectorate, ‘Abd al-Hafiz insisted that the works be completed. When the restoration was completed in 1912 the palace was ceded to France and sold at auction. In 1926, the palace and the surrounding park were acquired by the Italian government, which turned it into a school, hospital and church. Known also as the Palace of Italian Institutions, it was used as a venue for receptions, exhibitions, and music and theatre performances. Abandoned after independence, the building has recently been restored.
5aae14de-96b5-54d8-bde0-643bb24e8c93.keywords: Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic architecture in Morocco; Islamic influence; Moroccan architects; traditional city; Islamic city; palace; royal palace; garden; Islamic garden; gardens and architecture; plan; urban planning; Moorish style; patio; portico; column; al-Andalus; Andalusian architecture; Andalusian influence; European architecture; European influence; artistic exchanges; column; capital; classicism; Italian influence; Italian marble; protectorate
5aae14de-96b5-54d8-bde0-643bb24e8c93.description2: Renovated and adapted in the late 19th century by Sultan Mulay ‘Abd al-Hafiz, the palace is a masterpiece of Neo-Moorish style architecture, which can be seen in the beauty of its gardens, facade and interiors. Located in the central district of Hasnouna, the estate covers an area of 32,800m2, of which 8,669m2 are occupied by the palace building, which is organised around a large portico-covered courtyard with a central fountain. The Moorish or Arab-Andalusian style of the palace has accents from the European architectural vocabulary, seen for example in the Italianesque marble Neo-Corinthian column capitals decorated with crescent moons.

5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.name: Barbadinhos steam pumping station at the time of its inauguration
5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.holder: Historical Archive, Empresa Portuguesa das Águas Livres (Portuguese Water Company)
5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.dimensions: Rectangular shape; length: 26 cm, width: 18 cm. Mounted on cardboard (30,5 x 24,5 cm)
5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.author: AHEPAL–EPAL’s Historical Archive
5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.keywords: Lisbon; water supply; Innovation; Industrial Archeology
5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.second_name: Central Pumping Station of Barbadinhos, machines storehouse, main or south façade
5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.description2: This picture is part of an album entitled "Canal Alviela / Inauguration / 3 October 1880" that includes 10 photographs by Francesco Rocchini. The picture depicts the main façade of the Barbadinhos steam pumping station at the time of its inauguration. The chimney and the engine room of the water reservoir of Barbadinhos can be seen on the right side of the picture. The steam station was in operation until 1928, when a new electrically powered station was opened. After decommissioning, the machines were not dismantled and are currently preserved. The building of the Barbadinhos steam pumping station houses the Water Museum (opened in 1987) and was classified in 2010 as a building of public interest.

5b0b263b-b41d-5d43-8512-d1b3bf69a2dd.name: An Italian upper-class woman with her children
5b0b263b-b41d-5d43-8512-d1b3bf69a2dd.dates: End of the 19th century – beginning of the 20th century

5b229743-fc47-5975-b220-b56bbbada7be.name: Pair of pistols
5b229743-fc47-5975-b220-b56bbbada7be.type: Military object; metalwork; firearms; arms and armour
5b229743-fc47-5975-b220-b56bbbada7be.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
5b229743-fc47-5975-b220-b56bbbada7be.keywords: Military object; Metalwork; Steel; Arms and armour; Pistol; Coral; Silver
5b229743-fc47-5975-b220-b56bbbada7be.description2: These Turkish flintlock pistols were used by the Ottoman soldiers in Lebanon in the 19th century to quash resistance movements. As the Lebanese resistance had no weapons of their own, the fighters frequently ambushed Ottoman soldiers and took their weapons. These pistols are an example of such weaponry, which was taken by the resistance and used against the Ottomans. They have a wooden bulbous butt plate and engraved silver mounts ornamented with coral. They are made of wood and cast steel and have a small, ornamental, engraved silver piece on the wooden grip.

5b235936-2f14-5bd6-826a-ea220b311aad.name: The old city hall of Bucharest

5b43be53-1e86-5b15-9cc1-477c08fb7fbb.name: Official Bulletin establishing the Post, Telegraph and Telephone Office (PTT.)
5b43be53-1e86-5b15-9cc1-477c08fb7fbb.description: An Official Bulletin, signed by the Sultan of Morocco Mulay Yusuf ibn al-Hasan I, which concerns the creation of the Post, Telegraph and Telephone Office. The establishment of this Office was part of an agreement between Morocco and the French authorities, to promote the telecommunications sector, and put a stop to attempts by Britain and Spain to capitalise from it. The text defined the functions and services of the Office and its organisation. After independence, the Office became the Ministry (*Makhzen*) of Post, Telegraph and Telephone.

5b74420d-61f0-5db6-8b22-107ce274c47e.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
5b74420d-61f0-5db6-8b22-107ce274c47e.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Anatolian Railways
5b74420d-61f0-5db6-8b22-107ce274c47e.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

5bdaed42-778f-5c44-bbc4-20cefe2c165b.name: Retaining wall of the reservoir in Shellal, Egypt
5bdaed42-778f-5c44-bbc4-20cefe2c165b.author: Patrizia Pampana
5bdaed42-778f-5c44-bbc4-20cefe2c165b.second_name: The retaining wall of the first dam on the Nile
5bdaed42-778f-5c44-bbc4-20cefe2c165b.description2: In the year 1900, Count Giulio d’Aspremont, an Italian diplomat, visited the construction site of the first dam across the Nile (today known as the Aswan Low Dam or Old Aswan Dam). He took several photographs of the works and of the monuments on the island of Philae that were slated to be submerged by the water. He published some of them in the *Bulletin of the Italian Geographical Society*, where he wrote that up to 2,000 Italian workers were employed in the works (as stone-cutters, miners and masons), out of a total labour force of about 10,000 or 12,000; an Italian village had sprung up on the Nile banks, with modest little houses, trattorias and shops.

5bdb7155-07a2-5eb8-97fb-cb481391296f.name: A photo of the Dairy Laboratory at Fu`ad Agricultural Museum
5bdb7155-07a2-5eb8-97fb-cb481391296f.dates: 16 January 1938 (Photo taken during the inauguration of the museum)
5bdb7155-07a2-5eb8-97fb-cb481391296f.description2: The Fu`ad Agriculture Museum was considered the first of its kind in the Middle East and the Arab World during the 1930s. It was inaugurated during the time of King Faruq, the son of King Fu`ad, and houses a large number of collections related to agricultural and rural environments, as well as agricultural plants and animals.

5c6bfb8e-5045-5559-8078-f4e37350944b.name: Pillowcase
5c6bfb8e-5045-5559-8078-f4e37350944b.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
5c6bfb8e-5045-5559-8078-f4e37350944b.description2: Textiles and embroidery found a wide array of uses which reflect the imaginations of Turkish women. In these textiles, silk, golden and silver threads were used for embroidery. From the 18th and 19th century on – when Western influence started – almost every colour found use and by using different tones of the same colour, the illusion of light and depth was created. Instead of human and animal figures, floral design, fruits, or calligraphy, ship and architectural patterns became more popular. This piece was made in the Hereke Plant, founded in 1843. There is one big star and crescent in the middle while there are four smaller ones in the corners. The base is covered with plenty of stars and dots.

5c7df1fd-3c74-5952-b9c6-f24375461c19.name: *The Egyptian University – Faculty of Medicine*
5c7df1fd-3c74-5952-b9c6-f24375461c19.keywords: Education; Students; Faculty of Medicine; Egyptian University
5c7df1fd-3c74-5952-b9c6-f24375461c19.description2:
General view of the Egyptian University Faculty of Medicine and Qasr al-\`Ayni Hospital in 1933.  
The 1923 Constitution stipulated that “Primary education is mandatory for all Egyptian boys and girls”. A decree was issued for the establishment of a public university under the name “The Egyptian University” in 1925, comprised of four faculties; literature, science, medicine and law. The Faculty of Medicine, annexed to Qasr al-\`Ayni Hospital, is one of the leading hospitals in the Arab World.

5ce76956-57f6-57ef-9da7-fc2a688258ea.name: Beylerbeyi Palace
5ce76956-57f6-57ef-9da7-fc2a688258ea.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
5ce76956-57f6-57ef-9da7-fc2a688258ea.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ancient Istanbul; palace
5ce76956-57f6-57ef-9da7-fc2a688258ea.description2: Beylerbeyi Palace was commissioned by Sultan Abdülaziz (1830-76) and built between 1861 and 1865 as a summer residence and a place to entertain visiting heads of state. The Palace was designed by Sarkis Balyan in the second Empire. It looks its most attractive from the Bosporus, from which its two bathing pavilions – one for the *harem* (women's only) and the other for the *selamlik* (men's only) – can best be seen. One of the most attractive rooms is the reception hall, which has a pool and fountain. Running water was popular in Ottoman houses for its pleasant sound and cooling effect in the heat.

5cf8b622-bc23-5c90-a393-46a79bb0514b.name: Reliquary of St-George Chiopolites from Aivali
5cf8b622-bc23-5c90-a393-46a79bb0514b.author: Ballian 1992, 84, no. 44
5cf8b622-bc23-5c90-a393-46a79bb0514b.description2: The reliquary contained the head of George Chiopolites, who was martyred in Aïvali / Kydonies in 1807. The container made for the head has intricate rococo decoration with ribbons, bows, roses, blank heraldic shields and St George holding the attributes of a neomartyr under the imposing two-headed eagle of ecclesiastical authority. From the mid-eighteenth century, thanks to special administrative treatment or privileges, the inhabitants of Aïvali transformed what had been a small fishing village into a flourishing commercial centre on the Aeolian coast. The inscription on the reliquary refers to the goldsmith and to the Guild of Soap-Makers, which was one of the biggest trade associations in the town. It also refers to Sophronios, who oversaw the commissioning, and has been identified to the parish priest and a close relative of Theophilos Kaïris, a teacher at the Academy of Kydonies who was later expelled from the Church under the free Greek state for his revolutionary ideas and was to die in prison, the last ideologue of the Enlightenment.

en: Ballian, Anna, *Treasures from the Greek Communities of Asia Minor and Eastern Thrace. Collections from the Benaki Museum*, Athens: Benaki Museum, 1992.

5d117acd-215b-54b0-aefc-38ef0cc38d6b.name: Map of caravan routes
5d117acd-215b-54b0-aefc-38ef0cc38d6b.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
5d117acd-215b-54b0-aefc-38ef0cc38d6b.archival: *The Geography of Africa*, London, Gill & Sons (publisher), 1897, p. 200
5d117acd-215b-54b0-aefc-38ef0cc38d6b.keywords: Route; trade; pilgrimage; pilgrims; Muslim pilgrimage; Islam; Africa; religion; economy; Holy Places; Holy Cities; Hijaz; Makka; al-Madina; Jidda; Arab Peninsula
5d117acd-215b-54b0-aefc-38ef0cc38d6b.description2: This map illustrates the trading caravan routes crossing the Sahara desert from Mediterranean ports (Tripoli, Tafilet, Tunis, Algiers and Oran) to sub-Saharan cities. The trading routes were connected north and south to three pilgrim routes for Mecca. The northern pilgrim route from Tunis and Tripoli included Siwah, Cairo, Suez and Aqaba. From Aqaba, meeting the pilgrim route from Damascus, it continued along the coast of Arabia to Mecca. The central route continued from Siwah through the oases of Dakkel and El-Kharjeh to ports on the Red Sea to Jeddah and Mecca. The southern route followed the valley of the Upper Niger through Timbuctu, Gao, Sokoto, Kano, Lake Chad and Kordofan to the port of Swakin on the Red Sea and continued to Jeddah by ship.

5d280899-351f-5ef7-95bb-ed98a12d141d.name: An open letter from the Tuscan community in Constantinople to the Chargé d’Affairs of Tuscany, protesting the detention of three Italian democrats exiled by Ottoman authorities
5d280899-351f-5ef7-95bb-ed98a12d141d.author: Massimo Sanacore
5d280899-351f-5ef7-95bb-ed98a12d141d.description2: Italian communities abroad actively supported the movement for Italian national unification known as “Risorgimento”. The Italian community in Constantinople raised funding to donate a cannon to the Kingdom of Sardinia, which in 1848 was at war with the Austrian Empire. After the Kingdom of Sardinia’s army was defeated, conflicts between the most moderate wing of the nationalist movement and the republicans (supporters of Giuseppe Mazzini) broke out and the Kingdom of Sardinia’s authorities started to persecute the latter.

5d377e78-b054-59b0-820b-7328307c7e77.description2: A crescent shape made of casted brass fixed on a pointed piece of copper with a hole at the bottom to install a long wooden staff. In religious festivities such as a pilgrimage, various activities were organized. They would normally include festivals and rallies under flags and standards. The heads of flagstaffs were decorated with metallic items usually with Arabic calligraphy and some cosmic signs such as the crescent and the star.

5d84c4b0-6f1a-5b1c-87d0-3d8a61317a0a.name: Flag of the Female Workers Friendly Society (Società di mutuo soccorso femminile) of Cremona, bearing the motto “All for one and one for all”
5d84c4b0-6f1a-5b1c-87d0-3d8a61317a0a.dates: Unknown (probably end of the 19th–beginning of the 20th century)
5d84c4b0-6f1a-5b1c-87d0-3d8a61317a0a.author: Angela Bellardi
5d84c4b0-6f1a-5b1c-87d0-3d8a61317a0a.archival: ASCr, Società di mutuo soccorso femminile di Cremona
5d84c4b0-6f1a-5b1c-87d0-3d8a61317a0a.description2:
During the second half of the 19th century, “friendly societies” flourished in Italy (especially in Central and Northern Italy). They predated trade unionism and were an important element of Italian social life.  
The Female Friendly Society (Società di mutuo soccorso femminile) of Cremona was created in 1863. It mostly comprised factory workers such as spinners and other workers in textile industry, but also included craftswomen like self-employed dressmakers, and even a few teachers.

5dc4fbc5-e8e9-52ae-aa62-690ee8359b41.name: Lake d'Orta. Villa Crespi
5dc4fbc5-e8e9-52ae-aa62-690ee8359b41.author: Ignazio Galella
5dc4fbc5-e8e9-52ae-aa62-690ee8359b41.description2:
Cristoforo Benigno Crespi was a successful businessman active in the cotton industry. In 1879, he bought an estate near the lake d’Orta (Piedmont, Northern Italy), in order to build a vacation house in honour of his wife, Pia Travelli.  
He had fallen in love with the architecture of Baghdad, where he went to buy cotton, and asked architect Angelo Colla to build a villa in the Moorish style. Architect Enrico Combi designed the magnificent park.  
The villa features a 48-meter high minaret and has richly decorated interiors, made with marbles of great value, imported from several different countries. It required 12 year of works to be completed. The estate comprises a greenhouse, a wet dock, stables, a big fountain, an annex, and is surrounded by walls, with valuable wrought iron gates.
