5e05c455-44c3-5bd3-be12-061bbab9de8d.name: Musée de Cherchell. Fragments found in the excavations.
5e05c455-44c3-5bd3-be12-061bbab9de8d.second_name: Taken from *L'Algerie Phtographiée*, vol. 2, Province d'Alger
5e05c455-44c3-5bd3-be12-061bbab9de8d.description2: The French established two museums in Algeria after the conquest: one in Algiers (1838), and another in Cherchell (1840). The latter was overshadowed by the reputation of the former and lacked subsidies. A report from 1855 describes abandoned collections, to which the objects found during an 1856 excavation were soon added. This image, dating from 1856, highlights both the richness of the works presented to the Musée de Cherchell and their inadequate conservation. A new museum, built in 1908, allowed the collections to be stored in better conditions.

5e131b15-3042-5b4a-bc07-e72c9fb0b7fb.name: Figures in Turkish style
5e131b15-3042-5b4a-bc07-e72c9fb0b7fb.description: In these two porcelain figures, it is showed through the clothes, and combined with the Rococo style of the bases. Produced by many European manufactures at the time, this kind of objects could be easily found in rooms as the *fumoir*, usually decorated in an Orientalist style to recreate exoticism.
5e131b15-3042-5b4a-bc07-e72c9fb0b7fb.author: Isabel Ortega Fernández

5e2b03cb-5bee-5604-be76-35ecf0de0e45.name: *Valahian Caravan*
5e2b03cb-5bee-5604-be76-35ecf0de0e45.description2: In Wallachia and Moldavia transportation of merchandise by land was done similarly to the Arab and Ottoman world, but using big carts pulled by horses instead of camel caravans. Both the vehicle and a group of carts travelling together for commercial purposes were called "chervan”, a term derived from the Turkish word "kervan", meaning "caravan". The lithograph, depicting a carriage drawn by 12 horses and followed by a second vehicle, was printed in Vienna and its legend (*Wallachian carriage*) is written below the image in German, Hungarian and French.

5e4318a5-d6ea-59f6-b209-38ea0cff4654.name: Postal map
5e4318a5-d6ea-59f6-b209-38ea0cff4654.keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication
5e4318a5-d6ea-59f6-b209-38ea0cff4654.description2: The network of routes for sending messages and transporting troops and supplies was carried out with a relay system, established in the 16th century in the Ottoman Empire. The messengers, who conveyed dispatches throughout the country, were identified as the Tatars. Private or personal correspondence was not a part of that relay system; it was built to fulfil governmental needs. Because of this reason the *reaya* (public) created an alternative postal method by using caravans, pilgrims, and private couriers called *ulaks*. The *Tanzimat* Decree, which was the declaration of process included reformation, modernization and westernization in 1839, proved that the Ottoman Empire was focused on its policy of changing governing to be more like modern Western European-style administrative practices.

5e51433f-c353-5de6-8d1d-14dc9459c3f2.name: *Moors of Tetouan*
5e51433f-c353-5de6-8d1d-14dc9459c3f2.description:
This painting was made around 1863 when the author travelled to Morocco with Mariano Fortuny. The reason for his travel was to paint the characters and picturesque garments as the way of life of the people from Morocco.  
His experiences can be seen in his paintings and drawings.  
During his travels he bought exotic artworks as Egyptian sarcophagi.  
Harem and markets are considered a genre painting in Orientalism.
5e51433f-c353-5de6-8d1d-14dc9459c3f2.author: Ámparo López

5e9e845e-5f4e-508c-91ed-f52d967dbf97.name: *Family gathering in Alexandria*
5e9e845e-5f4e-508c-91ed-f52d967dbf97.author: Maria Dimitriadou
5e9e845e-5f4e-508c-91ed-f52d967dbf97.description2: Black and white photo in a family album: A family gathering at the garden of Emmanuel Benaki’s mansion in Alexandria. His eldest daughter Alexandra Benaki was engaged to his partner Tom Davis in April 1889. In the center of the picture appear the bride and the groom, the sister of Alexandra Benaki, Penelope Benaki-Delta, as well as their mother, Virginia Benaki. Phototographer unknown.

5ec581f1-3f8e-5a5c-bdc5-c2d1b4b525e3.name: A postcard advertising the Singer sewing machine and at the same time supporting Italian colonial expansion in Libya

5ec581f1-3f8e-5a5c-bdc5-c2d1b4b525e3.description2: This postcard sends the message that the Italian colonisers brought modernity to Libya. Both the sewing machine and the plane in the background epitomise modernity. The soldier is sewing an Italian flag. The postcard’s message is at the same time political and commercial.

5f3b539e-1d3b-5ad6-9c3f-11df8f1f7e2f.name: *Thebes. Hypogea. Pictures drawn after the covering of the mummies*
5f3b539e-1d3b-5ad6-9c3f-11df8f1f7e2f.second_name: Taken from *Description de l'Egypte, ou, Recueil des Observations et des Recherches qui ont été faites en Egypte pendant l'Expédition de l'Armée Française*, vol. 2
5f3b539e-1d3b-5ad6-9c3f-11df8f1f7e2f.description2: During the Egyptian expedition (1798–1801), Napoléon Bonaparte brought with him a group of scholars, engineers and artists, charged with collecting as much scientific information as possible. This was then used in a publication (of exceptional quality and execution) entitled Description de l'Égypte, in which the observations and enquiries made by the military expedition in Egypt were collected. The collection comprises of 10 volumes of illustrations and 9 volumes of texts published betwen 1809 and 1826.

5f76f108-6ffb-5c2b-8fe2-0ec05a6fae48.name: Various hydraulic machines used in Egypt to water the land. The first method is constructed in a linear manner and provides the land with water whenever it is in need. Part of "Dyke A"
5f76f108-6ffb-5c2b-8fe2-0ec05a6fae48.second_name: Illustrations taken from *Voyage d'Egypte et de Nubie*
5f76f108-6ffb-5c2b-8fe2-0ec05a6fae48.description2: The captain of the Danish Royal Marines Fréderic-Louis Norden (1708–1742) was sent to Egypt to draw monuments. His collection, *Voyage d’Égypte et de Nubie*, was published posthumously in 1755, and was added to in 1795 by the inclusion of scientific commentaries by Louis Langlès (1763–1824), founder of the École Spéciale des Langues Orientales and curator of oriental manuscripts at the Bibliothèque Impériale. This new edition, a product of Europen "Egyptomania", introduced some splendid new illustrations. In this particular page, the artist has focused on traditional hydraulic machinery.

5f7be233-5b3b-542f-9b15-c37a25a0932f.name: Plan of Jerusalem
5f7be233-5b3b-542f-9b15-c37a25a0932f.description2: Plan of the area to the South of the Haram al-Sharif, Jerusalem, showing the location of the shafts dug by Lieut. Charles Warren, R.E., and his team to explore the topography of ancient Jerusalem. This work established the history of the development of the Old City of Jerusalem. While engaged in this work, Warren also carried out a major study of the economy of Jerusalem in the period 1867–1870, which was published in the SWP in 1884.

5f944369-bc84-59f2-a3a6-21c5dda0f6fe.name: Wooden clogs
5f944369-bc84-59f2-a3a6-21c5dda0f6fe.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
5f944369-bc84-59f2-a3a6-21c5dda0f6fe.description2: Wooden clogs such as these have a long history in the Middle East, emerging before the Middle Ages and remaining popular for centuries to come. They were made of a variety of woods, including walnut, apricot, willow, poplar, or beech. The wood was cut into wedge shapes then moulded around the foot of the wearer. Excess wood was then shaved off, the heel attached, and the wood painted and polished. Leather girdles in a variety of colours were fixed to the heel with special nails and the wood would often be decorated with mosaics of bone or seashells organised in geometric or floral patterns. Clogs were designed to be comfortable and resistant to water, and thus were usually worn at home, particularly by women. These shoes have a higher heel than usual and would be worn by brides so that they would appear taller than the other girls in the *hammam* (Turkish baths).

601e5d3a-e68f-587a-846c-d0f3657cf4f6.name: *Dar al-Baladiyya, Damascus*
601e5d3a-e68f-587a-846c-d0f3657cf4f6.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
601e5d3a-e68f-587a-846c-d0f3657cf4f6.author: Stefan Weber
601e5d3a-e68f-587a-846c-d0f3657cf4f6.second_name: City Hall at the new urban centre at Merje Square
601e5d3a-e68f-587a-846c-d0f3657cf4f6.description2: Built between 1892 to 1894, the Dar al-Baladiyya was a prestigious edifice in stone. With its neo-classical elements and prominent middle projection, it was designed to display the power of the “new” state. The purpose of building the City Hall was functional, since the administrative workload, which rapidly increased after the reforms of the administrative system had to be accommodated.

602e2e1a-614b-533b-b171-c2a7bb60bc72.name: Bridal apron
602e2e1a-614b-533b-b171-c2a7bb60bc72.dates: End of the19th – beginning of the 20th century
602e2e1a-614b-533b-b171-c2a7bb60bc72.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
602e2e1a-614b-533b-b171-c2a7bb60bc72.keywords: Plain weave; warp; weft; sequins; sash; costume; accessories; textile; shell; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; wedding; marriage
602e2e1a-614b-533b-b171-c2a7bb60bc72.materials: Plain weave of cotton warp and weft consisting of wool and silver and gold wrapped thread. Decoration with sequins – *svetlinke*, *puloi*, and beads
602e2e1a-614b-533b-b171-c2a7bb60bc72.second_name: Apron with sash and bead chain
602e2e1a-614b-533b-b171-c2a7bb60bc72.description2: Belts, sashes and aprons were unavoidable accessories of folk costumes in all areas of Macedonia. This sash was made of white hand-woven cotton cloth, which was decorated at the front with embroidery of pink wool, silver-wrapped thread, silver string, sequins and multi-coloured beads. It has a hook and a loop on the ends for fastening. The apron was made in the technique of plain-weave. The warp of cotton and the weft of red wool and silver and gold-wrapped threads was embellished with sequins – *svetlinke* – and beads. The apron has two strips on the left and right sides woven and decorated in the same manner with shells and coins suspended at the bottom.

604ea0d6-64f6-5863-9076-425493fdad68.name: Lincoln Hotel
604ea0d6-64f6-5863-9076-425493fdad68.description: The Lincoln Hotel, constructed out of load-bearing masonry, has three floors supported by steel beams with brick vaults, plus the ground floor and a small terrace located in the middle. Its Neo-Moorish style is notable for having several features: a red-tiled roof; pointed horseshoe arches on the first and second-floor windows; and corbelled arches, which accentuate the porch that opens up across the lower part of this grand building. The front facade is enriched with columns, which are topped with capitals decorated with floral ornamentation. The Lincoln was the first hotel to be built in the city, in an area devoted to the accommodation and entertainment of European visitors and settlers.
604ea0d6-64f6-5863-9076-425493fdad68.history: The Lincoln Hotel was designed in the Neo-Moorish style by the French architect Hubert Bride. It is an elegant mix of Arab‒Andalusian architecture with some elements introduced from the recently acquired European architectural vocabulary.

607d9250-4214-591c-8b18-c2b7afaacd22.name: Portrait of Prince Bashir Shihab II
607d9250-4214-591c-8b18-c2b7afaacd22.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
607d9250-4214-591c-8b18-c2b7afaacd22.description2: The most important development during the reign of Bashir Shihab II was the shift from a feudal economic system to a cash crop system whereby merchants (often from Beirut) loaned money to peasants. Thus, peasants no longer relied on their feudal lords and the region saw the development of a handicraft economy and an increasingly specialized agricultural sector. Following a Maronite revolt over changes in taxation in 1821, Bashir II was forced to seek refuge with Muhammad 'Ali in Egypt. However, he returned to Lebanon in 1822 and allied himself with Maronite patriarchs and other Lebanese Christians. It has been argued that by doing this, the Emir stoked the tensions between the Maronite community and the historically dominant Druze community of Mount Lebanon.

60b297ce-03b5-5b81-8b64-abe6de2613c4.description2: The National Museum of Popular Arts and Traditions in Rome was founded by Lamberto Loria (1855–1913), an Italian ethnologist passionate about the need to record the agro-pastoral Italian culture that was disappearing to industrialization and the consequent migration from the countryside towards the cities. In 1911, 50th anniversary of Italian unification, or Risorgimento, Loria organized the Italian Ethnographic Exhibition in Rome. Through the help of a group of coworkers, Loria gathered over three-thousand objects from exhibition of 1911, which today form the principal nucleus of the Museum’s collections.

60d42b24-3acf-5ae0-ab4f-e3aae453f313.name: *Still-life with Calligraphic Panel*
60d42b24-3acf-5ae0-ab4f-e3aae453f313.keywords: Painting; Feyhaman Duran; orientalist painters; still life
60d42b24-3acf-5ae0-ab4f-e3aae453f313.description2: Feyhaman Duran was particularly interested in portrait painting and went to Paris in 1910 through the patronage of the Egyptian Prince Abbas Halim Pasha to further his studies in this genre. He greatly profited from the teaching of Paul Richet, professor of anatomy in the School of Fine Arts in Paris. He also attended the Julian Academy where he learned a great deal from Jean-Paul and Albert Laurens. In 1913-14 he worked in the Cormon studio in the School of Fine Arts. Although devoting most of his time to portrait painting, Feyhaman Duran also did paintings of flowers and nudes, but he was definitely most interested in the portrayal of people, and he had very little time for non-figurative painting.

60e43904-297f-56d1-af8b-fa4776b2ccb3.name: Pitcher
60e43904-297f-56d1-af8b-fa4776b2ccb3.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
60e43904-297f-56d1-af8b-fa4776b2ccb3.description2: Çanakkale was a pottery production centre between the end of the 17th century and first quarter of the 20th century where pottery with interesting and original forms was produced. Mostly coarse red clay and sometimes beige-coloured paste was used. There are green, brown, dark yellow and under-glazed purplish brown, yellow, dark blue and white decorations made by a brush. This Çanakkale-produced pitcher is made of red clay; it has green and dark yellow glaze and a bulgy body with long, narrow neck. Its mouth has a stylized bird shape. It has a flat bottom and round handle. On the head, neck and body of the bird, there are raised rosette flower patterns. On the front part of the body, there is a cat and some cypress tree figures. The details were made with the barbotine technique.

6129ee64-d66a-53c2-9b9c-8ac38a87b8b9.name: Moroccan House in Linderhof  Palace Park
6129ee64-d66a-53c2-9b9c-8ac38a87b8b9.type: Pavillion; Park building in Linderhof Palace Park
6129ee64-d66a-53c2-9b9c-8ac38a87b8b9.history:
When the rebuilding of the “Moorish Kiosk” in the Linderhof park undertaken by order of Ludwig II was completed at the beginning of 1878, it evidently reawakened the king’s interest in buildings in the Islamic architectural style.  
The pavilion, acquired at the World Exhibition in Paris in 1878, was remodelled inside at Ludwig II's request and originally built on the Stockalpe near the Austrian border. The "Moroccan House" had already also been shown at the International Exhibition in Vienna in 1873 and had been built for this purpose in Morocco. The wooden building, acquired by a private individual after the king's death, was bought back by the state in 1980 and was reconstructed in the palace park in 1998.
6129ee64-d66a-53c2-9b9c-8ac38a87b8b9.keywords: King Ludwig II; Linderhof Palace; Ettal; Moorish style; Romanticism; gardens
6129ee64-d66a-53c2-9b9c-8ac38a87b8b9.description2: The king had considerable alterations made to both the outside and the inside of the house in keeping with his own lavish tastes. Jean Perron, a sculptor in Paris who had organised the purchase for Ludwig II, also acquired the rich furnishings appropriate for an ornamental setting such as tables, chandeliers, tabourets, mirrors and vessels, none of which have been preserved. Numerous skilled workers and artists were involved in the dismantling, rebuilding and altering of the house.The entire colour scheme was changed with an abundant use of gold, and individual rooms were furnished with costly materials. Coloured glazing “in the Moorish style” and a tessellated floor were introduced to add to the oriental character of the house.

61817120-0f01-5c48-bcf7-a52ed14728f7.description2: French colonisation of Algeria deprived the Algerian schooling system of its traditional funding and brought it into disorder, as very few "indigenous Muslim" students were accepted into the new European schools. 6195ae0a-159f-55a5-b0c8-2cb302571e83.name: Photo of al-Busiri Mosque
6195ae0a-159f-55a5-b0c8-2cb302571e83.keywords: Imam al-Busiri Mosque; Alexandria; Anfushi District
6195ae0a-159f-55a5-b0c8-2cb302571e83.description2: The al-Busiri Mosque was named after the great Imam, famous for writing Sufi poetry about the love of God and in praise of his Prophet Muhammad. The fame of his poem “al-Burda” surpasses that of its writer. The mosque is located in Alexandria, in the Anfushi area in the Gomrok (al-Jumruk) district overlooking the Eastern Harbour, on the *Midan Al-Masajid* (The Square of Mosques). The Square of Mosques is so-named because the area is comprised of a large number of shrines to *Awliya’ Allah* (good people of God), who came to Alexandria during the Ayyubid and Mamluk times. The mosque consists of two separate squares: the mosque courtyard with a water fountain in the middle, surrounded by corridors from all directions; and the second square with the *qibla* wall or *iwan al-qibla*, which leads to the tomb of Imam al-Busiri. Above the tomb is a metal dome and the minaret which takes the shape of an obelisk. The dome and the minaret are in the 19th-century Turkish style.

61c3f6f4-ae5b-5188-a071-b1ffe734cb27.name: Messageries Maritimes's Istanbul-themed posters
61c3f6f4-ae5b-5188-a071-b1ffe734cb27.description2: *Messageries maritimes* was a French merchant shipping company. When it began, it operated on routes to the Middle East. Its ships were used as troop transports during the Crimean War, and were so helpful for the army that the Emperor gave the company the right to operate on the Bordeaux-Brazil route as thanks. This was the first French transatlantic line equipped with steamers. The following year, the *Société générale maritime* (later called *Compagnie générale transatlantique*) received the North Atlantic lines. From 1871 to 1914 the shipping company, now called *Compagnie des messageries maritimes*, saw its Golden Age.

61d517e1-9410-5522-abb9-809bf66d22a5.name: Ewer
61d517e1-9410-5522-abb9-809bf66d22a5.description2: It is known that there were workshops producing glass vessels around Beykoz in Istanbul in the 19th century. The first glass workshop was founded by Mevlevi Dervish Mehmed Dede during the reign of Selim III (1789-1807). There were European glass craftsmen working in those workshops as well. Cups, bottles, jugs etc. made of colourful, colourless and opal glass were among Beykoz' productions. This is an ewer made of dark blue opaline with a water-drop-shaped lid. On its body there are raised flower patterns and *kabaras*.

61dba05c-1c18-5736-85f3-727803bfc389.name: *Housing in the Pierrefitte Chateau and Gardens* \[…\] *Payable in installments* \[…\] *\[Epargne Foncière Immobilière des Quinze - Vingts\]: open to visitors every day.*
61dba05c-1c18-5736-85f3-727803bfc389.description2: Pierrefitte-sur-Seine was still a farming village in the mid 19th century. The construction of the Paris-Lille railway line in 1859 brought in rich Parisians in search of country air. The town was transformed again in the 20th century, thanks to the construction of factories in the Saint-Demis plains and the arrival of people looking for cheaper housing. The first tramway was also built in 1901. This poster advertises housing in an area outside the tramway's reach, which had remained wooded and rural, and was equipped with the most modern technologies available, such as gas and telephone.

61eb1293-6209-599c-bd83-34f180e3bec2.name: *The Port of Constanţa*
61eb1293-6209-599c-bd83-34f180e3bec2.description2: The Black Sea port of Constanța underwent its first modernization while Dobruja, the province where it is situated, was under Ottoman control. In 1857, when the Ottoman government hired a British company to build a railway in Dobruja, the concluded contract also stipulated the reconstruction of the Constanța port. Completed in 1864, it was still a small harbor with a wooden dock, a dam and one cereals depot. After Dobruja was annexed by Romania, a law was issued in 1885 for the “improvement and augmentation” of the port. In 1896 its modernization was leased to a French enterprise but due to some disagreements, three years later the state took over the works, which were led by architect Anghel Saligny. Inaugurated in 1909, the new port had 3 dams, several docks, depots, silos, an oil basin, an electric plant.

61fac5d6-c742-5da5-92f5-ec59e655c9ef.name: Theodor Aman – *Ottoman messengers at the court of Vlad the Impaler* (photo)

61ff0f1e-695e-5970-a8a9-44151ef0e284.name: Traditional peasant attire
61ff0f1e-695e-5970-a8a9-44151ef0e284.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
61ff0f1e-695e-5970-a8a9-44151ef0e284.materials: The costumes were made of cotton and silk
61ff0f1e-695e-5970-a8a9-44151ef0e284.second_name: Villager from the Beqaa Valley in traditional dress
61ff0f1e-695e-5970-a8a9-44151ef0e284.description2: Peasants and ordinary people's clothes did not change much over the centuries. It generally consisted of a shorter, narrower and darker coloured pair of baggy *shirwal* trousers for winter, and another pair in a lighter beige or khaki colour for the summer. This was paired with a cotton shirt or vest, called a *sudriye*, and a short embroidered *abaya*. A *keffiye*, a large scarf made of white cotton, was worn on the head with a *lebbede* or *'agal* on top.

6204d094-907f-5ef3-b378-936a43e07247.name: An Entertainment Scene (The third day of entertainment) from *Surname-i Vehbi*
6204d094-907f-5ef3-b378-936a43e07247.archival: The Library of Sultan Ahmed III
6204d094-907f-5ef3-b378-936a43e07247.description2: These images show events that took place on the Golden Horn on the evening of the third day. In them, we see the sultan seated in a tent on the Arsenal Palace quay surrounded by attendants. Two rafts are floating by. The one at the right, of which we can only see a part but appears to be a platform mounted on a pair of caiques, was donated by Yeğen Mehmed Pasha, Superintendent of the Customs Office. The figures of two rams suspended on gears and pulleys from the roof butt one another. This is following a real raft on which are set two gigantic dummies that face backwards and are dressed in Persian garb. At the front of the raft is a huge wheel of fireworks that one of the pyrotechnicists is causing to revolve. Its supporting frame is surmounted by a fire-spewing bird and rockets hurtle this way and that.

6215ebc8-8b3b-5484-8ac2-a702cc00efad.name: Carol I, King of Romania (1839–1914) / Karl von Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen
6215ebc8-8b3b-5484-8ac2-a702cc00efad.description2: Portrait of Carol I, King of Romania (1839–1914) on horseback/ Karl von Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen. He was elected Prince of Romania on the recommendation of Napoleon III in 1866. In 1881, after achieving formal independence from the Ottoman Empire, Carol declared himself King of Romania.

62681131-068c-54e3-b1f2-e3e7012285ab.name: National Museum of Archaeology
62681131-068c-54e3-b1f2-e3e7012285ab.author: DGPC
62681131-068c-54e3-b1f2-e3e7012285ab.history: The National Museum of Archaeology was founded in 1893 inside the Monastery of Jerónimos, which is one of the most important testimonies to Portugal’s Great Discoveries. With 120 years of existence, the museum became a reference institution of Portuguese Archaeology having regular contacts with museums, universities and research centers across the globe.
62681131-068c-54e3-b1f2-e3e7012285ab.keywords: Archaeology; Museum; Rediscovry the past; National Identiity
62681131-068c-54e3-b1f2-e3e7012285ab.architects: Architects: Master Diogo Boitaca (c.1460–1527), João de Castilho (c.1470–1552), Jerónimo de Ruão (1530–1601)
62681131-068c-54e3-b1f2-e3e7012285ab.description2: The Jerónimos Monastery is one of the most important examples of Manueline architecture. Its church, built in a lengthwise plan to the design of Boitaca, is divided into three naves topped by a flattened vault supported by eight towering octagonal pillars. This system provides a unified and luminous space. The main portal, which also gives access to the cloister, boasts a statuary programme depicting the Nativity. The church’s side portal, by João de Castilho, features sculptural images of the Virgin, the Apostles, Prophets, Doctors of the Church and angels. The museum is located in the monastery’s west wing which held the monks’ dormitories in the past.

62976cc8-0796-59c0-a85a-93425ffb58d1.name: Postcard – P. P Carp, Minister of Industry in 1895

629911e6-06d2-536a-9acd-824991f44ffa.name: Ferdinand, King of Romania (1865–1927) / Ferdinand von Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen
629911e6-06d2-536a-9acd-824991f44ffa.description2: Portrait of Ferdinand I, King of Romania. After the death of King Carol I, Ferdinand (as the nephew of the deceased king) ascended to the throne. In 1916 he joined the *entente* and declared war against Austria and Germany. After World War I, Romania gained Transylvania, Bukowina and the Banat from Austria, and Bessarabia from Russia. Ferdinand died in Romania in 1927.

62a42566-0f5f-5b6d-91af-1bb819d4489f.name: Postcard by A & K Naman (Baghdad) showing the newly constructed entrance to the Iraq Museum, 1930’s

63191935-a807-58a4-b11e-292c88a654f7.name: Dawud Pasha’s living room
63191935-a807-58a4-b11e-292c88a654f7.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
63191935-a807-58a4-b11e-292c88a654f7.description2: This bedroom belonged to the first *mutasarrif* (ruler) of the Mount Lebanon *mutasarrifiyya*, Dawud Pasha, who governed from 1861–68). The room is furnished with four armchairs and one large sofa. The sofa has a high wooden back, covered with a mosaic of white, beige and brown ceramic and bone pieces, organised in floral and geometric patterns. The seat cushions are covered with navy and beige silk decorated with similar patterns. The sofa was reserved for guests, which Dawud Pasha would receive from his large armchair, a sign of power and authority. The room is lit by two glass lanterns painted with white and golden floral patterns, and a round copper table sits in the centre of the room.

6345c672-a66e-5ec9-a903-e3ddfbdcb159.name: *Chiefs of nomadic Arab tribes in Syria visit the Abbot Desmazure, Latin father of the Saint-Sépulcre in the Convent of the Latin Fathers of Jerusalem, built on mount Gihon*
6345c672-a66e-5ec9-a903-e3ddfbdcb159.description2: Syrian tribal leaders visited the Abbot Desmazure in 1827, in the Convent of the Latin Fathers of Jerusalem. He happily volunteered to show Jerusalem to visitors passing through the city, and tried hard to find diplomatic solutions to the religious tensions within the Christian community.

634af5db-b68c-5f95-9cf9-42e43802e5f2.name: A shop in Istanbul
634af5db-b68c-5f95-9cf9-42e43802e5f2.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
634af5db-b68c-5f95-9cf9-42e43802e5f2.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul
634af5db-b68c-5f95-9cf9-42e43802e5f2.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century.

635f5f5e-120a-51d8-b033-3d0504a831cb.name: Rumelihisarı İskelesi
635f5f5e-120a-51d8-b033-3d0504a831cb.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; Abdullah Brothers
635f5f5e-120a-51d8-b033-3d0504a831cb.description2: Abdullah Brothers is the name given to three men with Armenian origin, Viçen (1820-1902), Hovsep Abdullahyan (1830-1908) and Kevork (1839-1918) who started the art of photography in Turkey. For 40 years they photographed the people of Istanbul, landscapes, various political and social events, and prepared albums of historical and cultural values, as well as monuments.

6361ef20-5b25-59b2-bd56-7f7ed9244291.name: Reed pipe
6361ef20-5b25-59b2-bd56-7f7ed9244291.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities
6361ef20-5b25-59b2-bd56-7f7ed9244291.author: Huda Kilani
6361ef20-5b25-59b2-bd56-7f7ed9244291.description2: A pair of blank reeds opened from both sides, of moderate thickness. Each has six holes on the surface attached together with a type of gum. Playing the *mijwiz* requires some ability because it is played by blowing into both reeds at the same time and pushing the air strongly with the cheeks. Shepherds used to play it while taking their flocks of sheep and goats to graze. It is a popular traditional musical instrument in the Middle East.

637e27e9-204e-5721-869e-ad4380dc0140.name: *The great celestial globe. 1900 Exposition Universelle.*
637e27e9-204e-5721-869e-ad4380dc0140.description2: A great celestial globe, measuring 50 metres in diameter and located near the Champ de Mars, was one of the proposed attractions for the 1900 Paris World Fair. A restaurant sat beneath it, and popular science activities inside the globe allowed the visitors to learn about astronomy. Other than the globe's colossal dimensions, the poster also foresees great crowds of people visiting the exhibit.

63946b1b-16ea-516e-a633-bafee1467d3f.name: Ionian capital from the *Ptolemaion*
63946b1b-16ea-516e-a633-bafee1467d3f.description: This fragmented capital, displaying a Greek-scrolled valuta and a wealth of floriform decoration on the cushion, originates from the so-called Ptolemaion, a gateway built in Samothrace for the Egyptian king Ptolemy II Philadelphus.
63946b1b-16ea-516e-a633-bafee1467d3f.holder: Kunsthistorisches Museum, Collection of Greek and Roman Antiquities

63c94290-4824-5fcc-88ab-904bca42d8ca.name: Hussein Kamil, Sultan of Egypt (1853–1917)
63c94290-4824-5fcc-88ab-904bca42d8ca.keywords: Hussein Kamil, Sultan of Egypt; cartoon; caricature
63c94290-4824-5fcc-88ab-904bca42d8ca.description2: Portrait of Hussein Kamil, Sultan of Egypt (1853–1917). On 18 December 1914 the British deposed the Khedive Abbas Hilmi II and declared Egypt to be a British Protectorate. They made the son of Ismail Pasha, Hussein Kamil, the Sultan of Egypt. Hussein Kamil died in 1917 and was succeeded by his brother Ahmed Fuad (King Fuad I).

63e28bd3-5d45-5462-b773-fca1e9fbcffb.name: Photograph illustrating the response to the government's public vaccination campaign
63e28bd3-5d45-5462-b773-fca1e9fbcffb.description: Scientific advances in the medical field, including microbiology, prompted the Moroccan government to take advantage of this progress by integrating public health policy with a vaccination programme to fight against major diseases of the 20th century.

640180dd-059b-54fe-a33c-0700c3dd70f8.name: Photograph of the Beirut–Aleppo railway
640180dd-059b-54fe-a33c-0700c3dd70f8.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
640180dd-059b-54fe-a33c-0700c3dd70f8.keywords: Transport; Railway; Communication; Connection; Innovation; Aleppo; Lebanon
640180dd-059b-54fe-a33c-0700c3dd70f8.description2: The second railway built in Lebanon opened in 1906 and ran from Beirut to Aleppo in present-day Syria. It connected with the first railway line at Riyaq. The connection between Aleppo and Beirut, a well-equipped and sizeable port, decreased trade in Alexandretta, the traditional port for merchandise leaving or entering Syria. Alexandretta was not connected to Aleppo by rail until 1914. Aleppo and Northern Syria became increasingly important as links between Damascus and Beirut were consolidated. This also marked the increasing importance of Beirut as a powerful city in the region and not only as a Mediterranean port.

640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.name: Municipal theatre
640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.history: This building, which was once the Municipal Casino and often affectionately known as the "bonbonnière Resplandy", was built in the early 20th century in the Art Nouveau style by the French Architect Jean-Émile Resplandy and located on Avenue Jules-Ferry (now Avenue Habib-Bourguiba) in the heart of the European quarter. It has been constantly active since its birth, clearing the way for new artistic talent. The biggest names in Tunisian and Arab performing arts stood on its stage, performing ballet, opera, dramatic performances, classical concerts and more. In 2011 it became an important symbol of the Tunisian revolution; protestors, martyrs and rebels from all sides stood on its steps at some point.
640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.keywords: Art Nouveau; theatre; stucco; bas reliefs; Apollo
640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.description2: This theatre, the last remnant of a municipal artistic complex, can hold up to 1,350 seats. An immense white building, it reflects the style of Art Nouveau with evidence for some baroque influences. The bas-relief decorations, showing a scene with Apollo and the two muses, dominate the façade. The interior, from the vestibule to foyer, is notable for its modern structure and the richness of the carved stucco decorations. The bas-reliefs, moulds, cornices and balconies were all made by famous French and Italian artists.

6466b53e-7366-59fb-b2d6-6c90c4bac6cd.name: Italian translation of the decree by the French Civil Affairs Superintendent (intendant civil) of Algeria, Louis-André Pichon, regulating coral fishing along the coasts of Algeria
6466b53e-7366-59fb-b2d6-6c90c4bac6cd.author: Cristina Francioli
6466b53e-7366-59fb-b2d6-6c90c4bac6cd.description2: This decree imposed a heavy tax on foreign ships that fished corals near Algerian shores, while exempting French ships. The decree was translated into Italian in Livorno, an active coral fishing port town that was badly affected by this ruling. Coral fishing was an important economic activity in the Mediterranean. Algeria was the main fishing area for corals, especially after the depletion of Sardinian coral.

647bb6c0-14ae-506b-85c5-060226c34178.name: Poet Nigar Hanım
647bb6c0-14ae-506b-85c5-060226c34178.description2: Nigar Hanım, who was born in Istanbul in 1856, studied in a French school. She also took private Turkish, Arabic and Persian classes. She started to write poems when she was a child. She had a very good command of the French language and French literature. Every Tuesday, she gathered reputable personalities at her place, where they discussed art and literature, listened to music and read poems. She collected her poems in *Efsûs I* (1877), *Efsûs II* (1891), *Nîram* (1896), *Aks-i Seda* (1900) and *Elhan-i Vatan* (1916). She also wrote a work of prose in 1901 entitled *Safahat-i Kalb*. A fine lyricism that expresses her unhappiness in her private life can be observed in her work. Among the Turkish poets, she was the most productive, writing very original pieces in the second half of the 19th century.

64991688-a812-5045-be71-b7c312480a11.name: Mansell photograph
64991688-a812-5045-be71-b7c312480a11.description2: The Black Obelisk became famous in 1850’s because it named two figures known from the Bible, and even depicted one of them. The British Museum experimented with ways to show its collections around the world. One method was to produce photographs of key objects.

64d43d8c-378d-5f7b-8572-8f2de200829a.description2: The mobilisation of the German army in early August 1914 was quickly followed by the mobilisation of the French army. This mobilisation was a long time in the making, the places where French reserves were to join their military units were already planned out, and the recruitment posters put up soon after.

653ec3ae-d9cd-5520-a956-95f7ae1a6d21.name: Thaler of Emperor Franz I
653ec3ae-d9cd-5520-a956-95f7ae1a6d21.keywords: Arabian Pensinsula; Emperor Franz I; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; Hijaz; mint
653ec3ae-d9cd-5520-a956-95f7ae1a6d21.description2: This thaler was a large silver coin minted during the reign of Emperor Franz I (1804-1835). It was countersigned in the Arabic Peninsula at the mint of Hijaz around 1920.

6542d634-c357-5d32-8439-beffa72dfa02.name: *The French Colonies. Book 26. M. de Brazza's Exploration 1875–79. His treaty with Makoko.*
6542d634-c357-5d32-8439-beffa72dfa02.artist: Engraver: L. Geisler; artist; G. Dascher
6542d634-c357-5d32-8439-beffa72dfa02.keywords: Congo; France; colonies; Savorgnan de Brazza
6542d634-c357-5d32-8439-beffa72dfa02.description2: In September 1880, the explorer Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza signed a treaty with Makoko, the Chief of the Bateke (Anziku Kingdom) laying out the new borders of the Congo. The French government ratified this treaty in 1882. Savorgnan de Brazza was henceforth put forward by Jules Ferry's government as the perfect example of non-violent victory, contrasting him with England's Henry Morton Stanley, his rival in this region. Savorgnan de Brazza's image as a "civiliser" became a central theme of colonial propaganda, as we can see from this image.

65ab9cb8-2305-56ee-99fd-eb52c5bbaf5d.name: Valeria Mengarini Rossetti (the wife of an Italian military officer) visiting Menfi (Egypt), escorted by her brother-in-law Roberto Rossetti (an Italian lawyer who migrated to Egypt)
65ab9cb8-2305-56ee-99fd-eb52c5bbaf5d.author: Giulia Barrera
65ab9cb8-2305-56ee-99fd-eb52c5bbaf5d.description2:
During the 19th century, the number of Europeans who could engage in leisure travel steadily increased, and tourism began to flourish. Ancient Egypt became an attractive tourist destination for the European elites. Fascination for Egyptian antiquities and the cultural exoticism were sources of interest.  
Near Egyptian ruins, tourist could also enjoy the exotic experience of riding a camel.

65c00b78-8201-5dbf-834d-9a831343be52.name: The Battle of the Nile fought on 1–2 August 1798 in Aboukir Bay (Egypt), where the British fleet, headed by Admiral Horatio Nelson, defeated the French fleet
65c00b78-8201-5dbf-834d-9a831343be52.author: Rossana Spadaccini
65c00b78-8201-5dbf-834d-9a831343be52.archival: ASNa, Ministero degli affari esteri, Piante, 239

65c00b78-8201-5dbf-834d-9a831343be52.description2: The battle of Nile of 1798 between the French and the British fleets entrenched Britain as the dominant naval power in the Mediterranean.

65c69c9e-9fa5-59d3-9011-708e7d931372.name: Archaeological excavations
65c69c9e-9fa5-59d3-9011-708e7d931372.description2: General view of the pyramids of Abusir, in the area of the pyramids of the king Userkaf and king Neferirkare. These pyramids represent vestiges of the Fifth Dynasty, and they date back to 2800 BC (Old Kingdom). The paper photograph is printed from glass plate negatives.

65d5d950-d069-5d9e-989f-ca9b3eb57b29.name: *Harem*
65d5d950-d069-5d9e-989f-ca9b3eb57b29.description2: Pascal Sébah (1823–1886) was a French photographer working in the Ottoman Empire. This photo of a harem is interesting insofar as it  differs from the mainstream representations of harems in the Western imagination, which were influenced by the painter Gérôme. Indeed, many local customs - both real and imagined - captured the interest of European artists, and their Orientalist art then fuelled both the Western fascination with and revulsion towards the East.

65fd829c-bfae-5827-bf9b-ed418624bfa6.name: Ferdinand I, King of Romania (1865–1927) / Ferdinand von Hohenzollen-Sigmaringen
65fd829c-bfae-5827-bf9b-ed418624bfa6.description2: Street Scene with King Ferdinand of Romania in Vienna. After the death of King Carol I, Ferdinand (as the nephew of the deceased king) ascended to the throne. In 1916 he joined the *entente* and declared war against Austria and Germany. After World War I, Romania gained Transylvania, Bukowina and the Banat from Austria, and Bessarabia from Russia. Ferdinand died in Romania in 1927.

66051236-e6f5-50e1-94a9-729e97d849a2.description: A tea tray, known as a *siniyya*, made in Fez in the 19th century. It’s geometric and floral decoration – a fusion of old and new styles – suggests that it was made before products, especially those of Richard Wright (“RR”) from Manchester, entered the Moroccan market.

66091ad7-e911-585b-ab5f-8072d134485c.name: The House of the Naboodah (Bayt al-Naboodah)
66091ad7-e911-585b-ab5f-8072d134485c.holder: Sharjah Museums Authority / Sharjah Heritage Directorate
66091ad7-e911-585b-ab5f-8072d134485c.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
66091ad7-e911-585b-ab5f-8072d134485c.notice: Please note that this is an unedited database entry and that it may contain grammatical errors and inconsistencies in spelling. We are working to raise the funds required to complete the editing of the database; should you wish to contribute please visit our [Support page](https://www.museumwnf.org/atrium_support.php).
66091ad7-e911-585b-ab5f-8072d134485c.description2: This house at the heart of historic Sharjah belonged to 'Obaid bin 'Isa bin 'Ali Al Shamsi, who was also known as al-Naboodah. He was a well known pearl merchant with good connections to foreign countries such as India, East Africa and France. The house was originally built by 'Obaid's father Essa in 1845, and 'Obaid resided here with his three wives and ten children. Later it passed to his grandchildren, who lived in it till the 1970s. The double-storey house covers an area of 1280 square meters and is built around a large courtyard. Unusually, the kitchen annex with its well and the main reception area (*majlis*) are conceived separately from the main building arrangement. Family rooms and toilets are found on both floors, the first floor rooms preferably used in the summer, as they were cooler and airier than those on the ground floor. Enclosed rooms have high ceilings for the heat to rise and escape. Decoratively carved gypsum screen separate the rooms from washing areas. The house was carefully restored in the 1990s and now gives an excellent impression of the multiculturalism of traditional Sharjah architecture, as it combines local materials such as coral and lime mortar (*jus*) with red silt clay (*sarooj*) from Iran and hard woods from Zanzibar and East Africa.

661636db-2ce1-5462-80af-0f6986d618f3.name: Railway station
661636db-2ce1-5462-80af-0f6986d618f3.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
661636db-2ce1-5462-80af-0f6986d618f3.history: The establishment of the French Protectorate in Tunisia (12 May 1881) quickly led to the introduction of a railway network throughout the country, to support civilian control in the areas where the Europeans had settled. The Grombalia station is an example of one of the new public buildings. This region has always occupied an important strategic position on the communication routes from North to South Tunisia, and its temperate climate and fertile lands made it home to an important wine-producing centre and European settlement, particularly for the Italians and the French.
661636db-2ce1-5462-80af-0f6986d618f3.description2: Designed by the French government during the colonial era as a building for public use, the Grombalia rail station is a rectangular building of around 100 m2 with no architectural features of note. The station is on the ground floor, which contains a shop, ticket office, and waiting room. The first floor was used for the stationmaster's accommodation. Its double-sloped roof is covered in red tiles, and the blue painting around the large windows are juxtaposed with the white façade. The Grombalia station is still in use today.

66eb3d81-e848-51c4-9925-a840ecb8f574.name: *The Egyptian Magician holding a seance with members of the European community in Cairo*
66eb3d81-e848-51c4-9925-a840ecb8f574.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
66eb3d81-e848-51c4-9925-a840ecb8f574.description2: Although this is the roughest of drawings, a composition sketch, or simply on the spot note-taking, it is important because it actually shows an Egyptian Magician, Shaykh Abd al-Qadir al-Maghrabi, in action, possibly in Lewis’s house. A séance was held there on the 8th December 1841, according to Sir Gardner Wilkinson who was present. The Shayk is clearly visible in the centre, and the huddled form in front of him indicates the young lad kneeling and staring at the drop of ink in his palm, answering difficult questions put to him by the onlookers. Although they are in Eastern dress, they are identified on an old label as prominent members of the European community in Cairo, including Henry Abbott, Joseph Bonomi and Colonel Barnett, British Consul-General in Egypt.

670372b2-f67e-5ac4-8b1b-28c10cd4bd8e.name: Section of a rail from Hijaz Railway with commemorative inscription
670372b2-f67e-5ac4-8b1b-28c10cd4bd8e.description: In September 1900, Sultan Abdul Hamid addressed a call for all Muslims all over the world to collect donations to establish a railway between Damascus and the holy places to facilitate transporting the pilgrims. The call was responded to enthusiastically and with the great support of all Muslims. The cost of the project was estimated at approximately five million Ottoman golden lira which were provided from: donations, the revenues of the Ottoman State earned from the sale of the stamps, and a special tax upon all the citizens for the railway. Construction of the narrow-gauge track (105cm) whose axle weight was (10.5 tonnes) began in 1900 with a wire telegraph line along its side connecting Damascus with Medina across Amman with a total track length of 1303km. The construction of the project ended in 1908. All the tracks and the stations were completed as detailed below: Mezerib Dera'a section, September 1901; Dera'a Al-Zarqa section, September 1902; Al-Zarqa Amman section, September 1903; Amman Ma'an section, September 1904; Ma'an Tabuk section, end of 1906; Tabuk Medain Saleh, September 1907; Medain Saleh Medina, September 1908. These rails were brought from the destroyed railroad tracks that were harmed by Arab revolt army attacks in 1917. On one side of the first rail is an Arabic phrase written in divan script: "*min khayrat mawlana Amir al-mu'minin al-sultan al-ghazi 'abdal-hamid khan thani 'azza nasruhu*".

6708efb2-ba21-5a11-8ce4-cff3261576f5.name: *Comic Map of Seat of War with Entirely New Features* (London: Rock Brothers and Payne, 1854)
6708efb2-ba21-5a11-8ce4-cff3261576f5.author: Renata De Simone
6708efb2-ba21-5a11-8ce4-cff3261576f5.archival: ASPa, Ministero per gli Affari di Sicilia, busta 1199, fasc. 212
6708efb2-ba21-5a11-8ce4-cff3261576f5.second_name: A satirical map of Europe during the Crimean war
6708efb2-ba21-5a11-8ce4-cff3261576f5.description2:
In the annex to the map, the authors made explicit their view on the international situation and the political message that they intended to promote. They portrayed Russia as “the Great Bear of Europe”: a tyrannical power, epitome of despotism and oppression, which used the whip against her own subjects. “The claws of the Bear, improperly extended to the Black Sea, are undergoing the process of being clipped by our brave fellows”.  
Turkey, which was participating in the war on the side of Britain, was represented as a turkey. The authors argued that it was no longer the “sick bird of Europe”. With “head erect and again in good feather”, Turkey looked “its defiance to Russia”. England was described as “the old Lion of the World, majestic, strong and patient”.

67353cca-0fe5-559e-ad36-0dee24d15bc8.name: Dar al-Maqri
67353cca-0fe5-559e-ad36-0dee24d15bc8.holder: OFPPT / Office de la formation professionnelle et de la promotion du travail
67353cca-0fe5-559e-ad36-0dee24d15bc8.history: The gardens or *riyadh* are the work of Idris al-Muqri, the brother of the grand vizier Hajj Muhammad, and head of the *muhtasib*, the supervising authority that oversaw the quality of production. Located in the neighbourhood of Oued Sowafine (river), it was built in the early 20th century.
67353cca-0fe5-559e-ad36-0dee24d15bc8.keywords: Palace; house; Moroccan house; traditional house; Islamic house; Islamic city; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic influence; North African house; private space; Moroccan city; Moroccan architects; Islamic architecture in Morocco; garden; Islamic garden; gardens and architecture
67353cca-0fe5-559e-ad36-0dee24d15bc8.description2: Located in an irregular and rugged area, the site consists of several pavilions and interconnected buildings, with many corridors and passages, each of which is organised around a terrace. The rooms are large, distinguished by their carved and painted domes and wall-fountains, which are tiled, and have carved, stone basins. The garden of around 2,000m2 is preceded by a *menza* or terrace, covered with tiles, and decorated with a central fountain. It offers panoramic views of the *Medina*.

6737216e-9ec0-5301-bc44-aa17e6e3cff5.name: Yıldız Ceramic panel
6737216e-9ec0-5301-bc44-aa17e6e3cff5.description2: Sultan Abdülhamid II founded in 1891 the *Yıldız Çini Fabrika-i Hümâyûnu* (Yıldız Royal Tile Factory) in the garden of Yıldız Palace in order to revive Turkish tile art and give it a new direction and momentum. Vases, hanging wall plates and many sorts of daily-use wares were produced in the factory, including writing and dinner table utensils, card plates, lidded bowls, pans, *aşure* (a kind of dessert) trays, sugar bowls, tea and coffee cups. Many native and foreign artists have worked in the tile factory of Yıldız. One of them, Halid Naci received training in tile painting in Sevres, France after his education at the *Sanayi-i Nefise Mektebi* (School of Fine Arts) and he was assigned to be head painter of the tile factories after his return. In the middle of the porcelain plate are a herd of sheep, its shepherd and his dog, all drawn using natural colours.

6752ea88-0922-5aae-a9a3-d9e93a4c8c57.name: Embroidery
6752ea88-0922-5aae-a9a3-d9e93a4c8c57.author: Ámparo López
6752ea88-0922-5aae-a9a3-d9e93a4c8c57.keywords: Nasrid art; islamic influence; orientalism; collectionism
6752ea88-0922-5aae-a9a3-d9e93a4c8c57.description2: This rich embroidery in the Mudéjar style showed the importance of these goods in the Italian and Spanish Renaissance. The influence of the Arab art in the Renaissance has been overlooked many times, but the Mediterranean ceramics and textiles of this period were influenced, in technique and decoration, by this art.

6755e6c3-6bcf-5ff8-9576-394e0f98a7c5.name: Beginning of the Royal Road from the direction of the Fayum Directorate
6755e6c3-6bcf-5ff8-9576-394e0f98a7c5.keywords: King Fu`ad; Fayum Directorate; new roads; The Royal Road
6755e6c3-6bcf-5ff8-9576-394e0f98a7c5.description2: The beginning of the royal road from the Fayum Directorate during King Fu`ad I’s visit to the Directorate on 8 May 1927. Fu`ad I ruled Egypt from 9 October 1917 to 28 April 1936. During his reign, the 1919 revolution began, and the British had to end Egypt's status as a protectorate and declare it an independent country with sovereignty. Independence was declared on 15 March 1922. Also during his reign, the first public ministry was established in January 1924, headed by Sa`d Zaghlul. King Fu`ad had a number of important accomplishments, and for this reason this photo was chosen – to manifest King Fu`ad's concern with roads, especially the royal road towards the Fayum Directorate.

678d0b51-8dc7-59f3-818b-402d1bec24d6.name: *The Barrage or Nile dam*
678d0b51-8dc7-59f3-818b-402d1bec24d6.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
678d0b51-8dc7-59f3-818b-402d1bec24d6.archival: Smith, James - Minister of St. George's-in-the-West Parish, Aberdeen, *A Pilgrimage to Egypt: an account of a visit to Lower Egypt ... With ... Illustrations*, Aberdeen: J. Avery & Co., 1897, p. 261
678d0b51-8dc7-59f3-818b-402d1bec24d6.keywords: Pilgrimage; Christian pilgrimage; travel; travel book; Egypt; Nile; inventions; dams; irrigation; flood; agriculture; economy; French in Egypt
678d0b51-8dc7-59f3-818b-402d1bec24d6.description2: This picture, from the book *A Pilgrimage to Egypt: An Account of a Visit to Lower Egypt*, shows the Delta Barrage dam built by the French engineer Mougelle during the reign of Muhammad 'Ali Pasha to maintain the Nile water at a balanced level all the year. The barrage also served as a fortification against attack on Cairo or Upper Egypt. It consisted of a double bridge, the eastern part spanning the Damietta branch of the Nile, the western the Rosetta, with the head of the Delta between the two. The barrage had to be improved from 1883 by Sir Colin Scott Moncrief to solve structural problems with the foundations and the gates of the dam. The barrage and other dams testify to the importance of these structures to provide the water needed for irrigation in Egypt since antiquity.

67aa0756-7dec-5fdf-a48c-f7c56bbd3c48.name: *Souvenir of Algeria*
67aa0756-7dec-5fdf-a48c-f7c56bbd3c48.author: Dalila Orfali
67aa0756-7dec-5fdf-a48c-f7c56bbd3c48.description2: This painting, made during one of the artist's many trips to Algeria, shows the ancient aqueduct of Cherchell. Algeria, for Fromentin, remained and endless source of inspiration to be constantly reinterpreted, as we can see from this painting's slightly personal touch. This famous work was first exhibited at the Salon in 1859, then again in 1874. It belonged to the old Delagrade collection and was published in *La Gazette des Beaux-Arts* in 1859 along with the following commentary: "This group of brightly dressed horsemen, who stand out like rubies against the green hills of the valley under the acqueduct, is above all the work of a colourist artist who has succeeded in uniting science with audacity.".

67cb161d-180b-5b1b-8420-3bf9a2f55271.name: *The Algiers-Oran line*
67cb161d-180b-5b1b-8420-3bf9a2f55271.author: Dalila Orfali

67cb161d-180b-5b1b-8420-3bf9a2f55271.description2: This illustration, from around 1860 in a local Oran publication in the west of Algeria, *L’Algérie Comique et Pittoresque*, comments on current affairs with a distinctively Mediterranean style and sense of humour. Salomon Assus, the father of the famous painter from the Algerian school Armand Assus, was one of the newspaper's first cartoonists.

67fb9e13-a6ba-5f67-8cea-07a7abdb3da1.name: Moroccan coins
67fb9e13-a6ba-5f67-8cea-07a7abdb3da1.description: Coin struck in 1903 under Mulay Sultan ‘Abd al-‘Aziz al-Hasan I (r. 1894 to 1908) at the mint in Fez. For a century (1800-1900) the ‘Alawid sultans struck coins in the workshops of Fez, but due to the economic crisis at the time, gold was unavailable so most coins were of silver, bronze or other common metals – although the technique remained the same, with the metal poured into moulds. The patterns on the face and on the back vary between the star with eight points (Solomon ring) and the indication of the place of mint.

680c8cb0-7e03-52b8-988d-a7e74dbb89fa.name: *L'Égyptienne*, military operetta in three acts and 11 scenes.
680c8cb0-7e03-52b8-988d-a7e74dbb89fa.description2: Egypt became the subject of choice across the theatrical arts as a symptom of "Egyptomania", a phenomenon which spanned the length of the 19th century. This military operetta, written by de Chivot, Nuitter and Beaumont (with music by Charles Lecocq) is set in Egypt during the arrival of the Napoleonic troops.

6810a977-0fac-5c5e-a9a2-56e6c3bc3a3a.name: Italian and Tunisian miners at work
6810a977-0fac-5c5e-a9a2-56e6c3bc3a3a.author: Giulia Barrera
6810a977-0fac-5c5e-a9a2-56e6c3bc3a3a.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 27
6810a977-0fac-5c5e-a9a2-56e6c3bc3a3a.description2: According to the book where this photo was published, in 1906 the largest number of Italian miners in Tunisia worked in El Kef (2,000) and in Gafsa (1,200). The most important mineral resource in Tunisia were phosphates, but the country also had mines of copper, manganese, iron and lead. One could find Italian miners in all these mines.

685a2ad1-af1f-51a1-a4f2-d4dc7fc2a7f0.name: Wooden Sideboard with Mother of Pearl Inlay
685a2ad1-af1f-51a1-a4f2-d4dc7fc2a7f0.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
685a2ad1-af1f-51a1-a4f2-d4dc7fc2a7f0.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
685a2ad1-af1f-51a1-a4f2-d4dc7fc2a7f0.dimensions: Height 2485 mm, width 1100 mm, depth 415 mm
685a2ad1-af1f-51a1-a4f2-d4dc7fc2a7f0.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
685a2ad1-af1f-51a1-a4f2-d4dc7fc2a7f0.description2: This tall, intricately carved sideboard consists of two parts, the mirror section with intricately carved openwork and mashrabiya ornamentation enhanced with mother-of-pearl inlay, and the narrow table section decorated with similar elements and with its four front legs supporting an elaborate system of lobed arches. the sideboard is further enhanced by religious inscriptions, some of which seem to suggest a Christian context. Sideboards and other European-style furniture were unknown in the Middle East until the second half of the12th/ 18th century. By the 13th/ 19th century, the urban elites in Ottoman cities enthusiastically imported domestic furniture from Italy, France and England or bought locally-made hybrid pieces that combined European and traditional Islamic elements like the item shown here. Many European entrepreneurs like the Italian Furino Brothers, based in Cairo, set up shop in Ottoman cities and specialised in this so-called Arabesque style, especially fashionable for furniture.

6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.name: *View Looking across the Hall of Columns, Karnak*
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.description2: Roberts' viewpoint across the Great Hypostyle Hall, in the Precinct of Amon-Re, at the Temple Complex at Karnak, captures in great detail the physical features of the monument as it appeared in his day. At the same time, he used exaggerated proportions to convey the structure’s imposing scale, which impressed him deeply. In his diary he writes: ’Karnak is even more astonishing than Luxor. Its magnificence is unimaginable. Trying to describe rationally what I have seen would be ridiculous’. In the 19th century,, the Karnak temple complex became one of the most famous ancient Egyptian sites visted by artists and archaeologists. During his travels up and down the Nile, Roberts captured over 300 monuments and ruins in his unprecedentedly detailed and precise works, many of them before excavation or restoration.  In his work, Roberts also drew on the pioneering scholarship of scholars like Champollion. The final depictions subtlely contributed to the Orientalist discourse on Ancient Egypt, which Europe increasingly saw as their right to appropriate.
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.artist_birthplace: David Roberts: Edinburgh, Scotland; Louis Hague: Tournai, Belgium
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.artist_deathplace: David Roberts: London; Louis Hague: London

686e2212-e7f1-527b-a985-4e1c54e9ef94.name: *Arab horseman*
686e2212-e7f1-527b-a985-4e1c54e9ef94.author: Dalila Orfali
686e2212-e7f1-527b-a985-4e1c54e9ef94.second_name: 1846 sketch for the porait of Ali Ben Ahmed, the Bey of Constantine, on horseback. Currently held in the Musée de Versailles.
686e2212-e7f1-527b-a985-4e1c54e9ef94.description2: This piece, drawn in 1846, is a study for the portrait of 'Ali bin Ahmed, the Bey of Constantine, on horseback. The portrait is currently held in the Musée de Versailles. The artist has concentrated on his posture rather than his face, which is sparse on details. The artist came to Constantine in May 1846 and said: "This is the only truly Arab city left in this country". In 1844 he was summoned by the Bey Ahmed, who he met in France, and was commissioned to paint his portrait on horseback surrounded by his beylical guard. The prints cabinet at the Musée National des Beaux-Arts contains the final sketch for this painting, which was exhibited at the Louvre in 2003.

68850fe9-86ff-5692-8ae9-7d758c18ca87.name: *Letta Asım Baloya Giderken* (*Letta Asım was about to go to a ball*)
68850fe9-86ff-5692-8ae9-7d758c18ca87.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts Unıversity Painting and Sculpture Museum
68850fe9-86ff-5692-8ae9-7d758c18ca87.keywords: Women; women painters; Turkish women painters; Ottoman women painters; women condition; social change; dance; opera; theatre; ballet
68850fe9-86ff-5692-8ae9-7d758c18ca87.description2: As a result of modernization efforts and the increase in relations with the West in the 19th century, there were significant changes in Ottoman social life. Instead of the traditional 18th-century entertainment which consisted of miniatures, in Tanzimat Period of the 19th century, theatre, opera, musical performances and ballrooms became popular in Istanbul. In public places, western-style dance and musical instruments began to be seen.

68a95c99-7986-5df2-8af1-8a9cc45a55e6.name: The Damascene Hall
68a95c99-7986-5df2-8af1-8a9cc45a55e6.holder: Wilhelma, Zoological and Botanical Garden Stuttgart
68a95c99-7986-5df2-8af1-8a9cc45a55e6.history:
King Wilhelm I of Württemberg commissioned to Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1837 the design of Moorish style buildings for his Wilhelma garden. The architect planned and built all the buildings with the exception of the Damascene Hall.  
The idea was not to reproduce faithfully the Islamic art but to lend an “oriental” flair to the garden. The mention of an “oriental garden” conjured up visions of elegance, luxury, colourful brilliance, seduction and eroticism.  
The Moorish style recalls the Islamic art of Spain and North Africa between the 12th and 15th centuries which reached its zenith in the Alhambra. It was fashionable in 19th century: Wilhelma is also known as the “Alhambra on the river Neckar” and other buildings – synagogues in Berlin and Vienna for example – were built in the Moorish style.
68a95c99-7986-5df2-8af1-8a9cc45a55e6.description2: In the eastern part of Wilhelma, towards the R. Neckar, is the Damascene Hall. It is the only one of the historical buildings that was not built by the royal architect Karl Ludwig von Zanth, but, after his death, by Professor Wilhelm Bäumer in 1864. It served Wilhelm I as a building for keeping pheasants and chickens. The name comes from that of the inhabitants of the town of Damascus, which used to be a centre of the Moorish style of building. The Damascene Hall was the only one of the historical buildings at Wilhelma to have survived the war undamaged. Despite this it was still very carefully restored in 1992. A small part of the old Moorish splendour of Wilhelma is to be seen here in the sumptuous ceiling painting, the stucco marble of the walls and the wonderful chandelier.

68b4882f-3c89-5cf3-afa6-4aac211b6b47.name: Emperor and King Charles I. (IV.) during an inspection of the Austro-Hungarian infantry-regiment N°2 from Bosnia-Herzegovina
68b4882f-3c89-5cf3-afa6-4aac211b6b47.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
68b4882f-3c89-5cf3-afa6-4aac211b6b47.keywords: Bosnia; Karl I; 1st World War; war; warfare; Austrian army
68b4882f-3c89-5cf3-afa6-4aac211b6b47.description2: This picture shows Emperor Karl I visiting Bosnian troops deployed on the Italian front in the last year of World War I. The Bosnian infantry regiments were the bravest of all Austrian regiments fighting in World War I.

68b5b5d0-76d3-5f73-81cd-d9ccc51a6475.name: Cartoon
68b5b5d0-76d3-5f73-81cd-d9ccc51a6475.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
68b5b5d0-76d3-5f73-81cd-d9ccc51a6475.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
68b5b5d0-76d3-5f73-81cd-d9ccc51a6475.keywords: French protectorate; resistance; occupation; cartoon; caricature
68b5b5d0-76d3-5f73-81cd-d9ccc51a6475.description2: Titled "Une maxime opportuniste", this cartoon by Alfred le Petit condemns the French invasion of Tunisia and points to business and French capital's blame. The poster shows a man bent over under the weight of a sack, full to the brim with silver, whilst a first quadrant on the right shows soldiers going to war, and another on the left shows a man depositing his money. Beneath, the striking line, "(Tunisia's) affairs are the money and blood of others".

68e8b7c1-4b26-5650-8465-4d55145c3d6c.name: *Convoy of pilgrims*
68e8b7c1-4b26-5650-8465-4d55145c3d6c.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
68e8b7c1-4b26-5650-8465-4d55145c3d6c.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph pilgrims; pilgrimage; travelling
68e8b7c1-4b26-5650-8465-4d55145c3d6c.description2: The Hijaz Railway was a narrow-gauge railway (1,050mm/​3ft, 5 11⁄32 in track gauge) that ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. It got no further than Medina, 400 kilometres (250mi) short of Mecca, due to the construction interruption caused by the outbreak of World War I. The main purpose of the railway was to establish a connection between Constantinople, the capital of the Ottoman Empire and the seat of the Islamic Caliphate, and Hijaz in Arabia, the site of the holiest shrines of Islam and the holy city of Mecca, the destination of the Hajj (annual pilgrimage).

68fae760-47a2-58aa-986f-28473ca5d989.name: Revolver
68fae760-47a2-58aa-986f-28473ca5d989.description: Leopold Gasser Austrian navy revolver produced between 1870 and 1919. Serial number 156122 engraved on the frame and on the smooth surface of the cylinder. On the left side of the revolver, the plate at the base barrel has an inscription: "PATENT RAST & GASSER WIEN 171290 GUSS STAHL". On the frame right under the cylinder serial number 156122 and to the left of it an apple pierced with an arrow and L. G. with the word "MARKE" was engraved. The revolver is fitted with chequered wooden grips fixed to the frame by a screw within an oval with ears of steel insert pressed into the wood of the grip plates. On the right side of the revolver an illegible marking was stamped with two Arabic letters ا ح under the marking. The letters are obviously initials of either the maker or the owner. The same initials in Arabic letters were engraved on the cylinder. At the top of the barrel a crown with two letters NI was engraved.
68fae760-47a2-58aa-986f-28473ca5d989.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities
68fae760-47a2-58aa-986f-28473ca5d989.dimensions: Length 37 cm, barrel 24 cm, cartridge 6-chamber cylinder
68fae760-47a2-58aa-986f-28473ca5d989.author: Mohammad Najjar

69063980-1b98-599a-87aa-a06e11b7637c.name: Colonial style building
69063980-1b98-599a-87aa-a06e11b7637c.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
69063980-1b98-599a-87aa-a06e11b7637c.history: In Tunis, the capital of the Protectorate imposed by France on Tunisia in 1881, the European quarter built itself right next to the old Arab medina. A new kind of home - the investment property - soon appeared, and the term balas (from the Italian *palazzo*) became widespread. These two or three-storey housing blocks greatly affected the city's urban landscape by introducing many different architectural styles as well as new architects, designers and builders with from different backgrounds. The 19th century was the century of eclecticism in Tunisia (both neo-classical and neo-baroque), whereas the 20th century was most marked by the influence of Art Nouveau.
69063980-1b98-599a-87aa-a06e11b7637c.description2:
These two residential buildings at 40 and 42 Rue Oum-Kalthoum are two remarkable examples of the Art Nouveau architecture, built between 1906 and 1908. The façades are decorated with a beautiful pattern of cherubs, ribbons, small female heads and garlands, all organised with symmetrically.  
  
The Azerm Building at 53 Avenue de Carthage, built between 1905 and 1906, is a private residence. It is notable for its curved lines, balconies with irregular arches and walled niches. The abundance of rich decorations are evidence of the craftsmen's excellent skill. These buildings are perfect examples of the rich decorations of neo-baroque architecture, the huge curls of Art Nouveau, and the abundance of rococo architecture.

690dbb87-8510-5df7-8b14-e1bf920ecdbc.name: Turkish council seats
690dbb87-8510-5df7-8b14-e1bf920ecdbc.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
690dbb87-8510-5df7-8b14-e1bf920ecdbc.description2: Seats such as these were used to furnish Ottoman councils. They are made of thin mattresses (c. 5cm thick) covered in thick, dark coloured fabric, usually in navy, burgundy or beige.

6918edf0-4e2e-58b2-82d5-437119b828fa.name: Lycée Armand-Fallières
6918edf0-4e2e-58b2-82d5-437119b828fa.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
6918edf0-4e2e-58b2-82d5-437119b828fa.keywords: Colonial school; Franco-Arab school; Armand Fallières
6918edf0-4e2e-58b2-82d5-437119b828fa.description2: The Lycée Armand-Fallières, attended in his time by Jules Ferry and named after the President of the French Republic, was located on the Rue de Russie and had the objective of educating the daughters of European settlers in their secondary education. In the early 20th century, a few Tunisians began to attend the school and thus had access to a modern European education. This photograph shows a secondary school class of young girls.

69333e0f-47a7-51b4-ada7-d43aa30c07fe.name: Flag of the peasants’ league of a small village in Tuscany, central Italy
69333e0f-47a7-51b4-ada7-d43aa30c07fe.author: Giulia Barrera
69333e0f-47a7-51b4-ada7-d43aa30c07fe.archival: ACS, Partito nazionale fascista, Mostra della Rivoluzione fascista
69333e0f-47a7-51b4-ada7-d43aa30c07fe.description2:
Peasants’ leagues (Lega Contadina) were the first form of agricultural workers’ organisations. They flourished in Italy at the end of the nineteenth and beginning of the twentieth century.  
Ravi and Caldana are villages in the municipality of Gavorrano (a mine district in the province of Grosseto, Tuscany).  
In 1911, when the national trade union Confederazione Generale del Lavoro (CGdL) proclaimed a strike against Italy’s colonial war in Libya, the miners of the Gavorrano district participated in the strike.

en: Centro studi Piero Gobetti, *Un' altra Italia nelle bandiere dei lavoratori: simboli e cultura dall'unità d'Italia all'avvento del fascismo*, Turin: Centro studi Piero Gobetti, 1980.

695e33b8-130e-58a9-b5e3-7cf462619cb9.name: The School of the Three Doctors
695e33b8-130e-58a9-b5e3-7cf462619cb9.description: The School of the Three Doctors, pictured here, is located in Downtown Beirut. The inscription above the main entrance bears the school's full name and the date of its foundation (1835).
695e33b8-130e-58a9-b5e3-7cf462619cb9.author: Hala Masri
695e33b8-130e-58a9-b5e3-7cf462619cb9.history: The Three Doctors Association represented the Orthodox educational presence in 19th century Lebanon. The school was also known as the 'Grand School' as it was the biggest school in Beirut. It was temporarily closed from 1840 to 1860, and again during the civil war, from 1975 to 1998.

696bbefe-4763-59bf-ad00-3b86378355df.name: Pin, plaque
696bbefe-4763-59bf-ad00-3b86378355df.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
696bbefe-4763-59bf-ad00-3b86378355df.author: Huda Kilani
696bbefe-4763-59bf-ad00-3b86378355df.description2: A gold pin with three gold ¼ rashadi Ottoman coins welded together; at the end of two chains hang ¼ gold rashadi coins (Sultan Rashadi, 1909), each with a heart shape dangling from it. Ottoman coins were used as decorative objects for jewellery. Gold jewellery was usually bought only by the rich, while most people used silver jewellery. Pieces of gold or silver jewellery were given by the groom to the bride as a dowry, thus the choice of a piece of jewellery indicated the financial status of the groom.

6996faf2-9ef0-57f8-8ffd-b45d86af0d67.name: Third-grade pupils of the Italian state-funded Giovanni Meli primary school in Tunis
6996faf2-9ef0-57f8-8ffd-b45d86af0d67.author: Giulia Barrera
6996faf2-9ef0-57f8-8ffd-b45d86af0d67.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 107
6996faf2-9ef0-57f8-8ffd-b45d86af0d67.description2:
In 1831, siblings Pompeo and Ester Sulema, political refugees from Livorno, opened the first Italian school in Tunis. By the end of the 19th century, there were 21 Italian state schools in Tunisia: 13 in Tunis, three in La Goulette, three in Sousse and two in Sfax. Five of them were pre-schools, eleven were primary schools and five were secondary schools.  
The Italian State could run schools in Tunisia thanks to the treaty signed by Italy and Tunisia in 1868. In 1881, Tunisia became a French protectorate and in 1896 Italy and France signed a treaty over the status of Italians in Tunisia: the Italian state could continue to run schools in Tunisia but could not open new ones. So, classes became very crowded, as shown in this photo.

en: Pendola, M., *Gli italiani di Tunisia: storia di una comunità (XIX-XX secolo)*, Foligno: Editoriale Umbra, 2007.

699fbe74-5142-545f-991c-73824a07527f.name: Author Tevfik Fikret and his book of poetry *Rübab-ı Şikeste*
699fbe74-5142-545f-991c-73824a07527f.description2: Tevfik Fikret, who published his first book of poetry *Rubab-ı Şikeste* (broken instrument), dealt with love, piety, nature and a worldview that was self-enclosed to the environment. His poems influenced other Turkish poets and he is considered a pioneer of contemporary Turkish poetry. His work also has some seeds of the social opposition of the future.

69b1e148-e4f7-554b-abf1-c0b14f2c4827.name: Workers in the mechanical workshop of the Fratelli Orlando shipyard in Livorno (Tuscany, Italy)
69b1e148-e4f7-554b-abf1-c0b14f2c4827.archival: AS Livorno, Cantiere Navale Luigi Orlano, serie Archivio Fotografico

69be0c25-f88f-50e2-b4ee-eb50bcc74ff7.name: Astronomical instrument: Qiblanuma
69be0c25-f88f-50e2-b4ee-eb50bcc74ff7.holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts
69be0c25-f88f-50e2-b4ee-eb50bcc74ff7.keywords: Qiblanuma; Edirnekari technique; lacquer; Turkish Baroque-Rococo; astronomical instrument; pilgrimage
69be0c25-f88f-50e2-b4ee-eb50bcc74ff7.description2: *Qiblanuma*s are portable astronomical instruments that show the direction to the Ka'ba in Mecca, which Muslims face to pray. They remained in use until the late AH 13th / AD 19th century and this example produced in Istanbul was decorated with a lacquering technique known as *Edirnekari*.

69c68c59-f8ea-58f9-8d04-9f7f7e1327d4.name: In the Sicilian Sulphur Mines
69c68c59-f8ea-58f9-8d04-9f7f7e1327d4.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
69c68c59-f8ea-58f9-8d04-9f7f7e1327d4.author: Giulia Barrera
69c68c59-f8ea-58f9-8d04-9f7f7e1327d4.second_name: Children at work in the Sicilian sulphur mines at the end of the 19th century
69c68c59-f8ea-58f9-8d04-9f7f7e1327d4.description2:
Sicilian sulphur mines at the end of the 19th century employed children as young as seven and eight years old to carry the crude ore up from the mines to the surface.  
In Italy, the first piece of law regarding children’s work dates back to 1886. It forbade employing children under the age of nine in factories and mines. It also dictated that children under the age of 12 could not work at night. Such provisions indicated the extremely hard situation of children workers at the time. Particularly appalling were the working conditions of children in the Sicilian sulphur mines. Their plight was highlighted by the Italian writer Giovanni Verga in his short story *Rosso Malpelo*, and by Nobel laureate Luigi Pirandello in his *Ciàula scopre la Luna*.
69c68c59-f8ea-58f9-8d04-9f7f7e1327d4.holding_institution_org: Biblioteca di Storia Moderna e Contemporanea

69f1c95c-2875-58ff-b85b-10d1c2d2ab83.name: Marius Scalesi
69f1c95c-2875-58ff-b85b-10d1c2d2ab83.holder: Institut Culturel Italien (Italian Emabassy in Tunisia)
69f1c95c-2875-58ff-b85b-10d1c2d2ab83.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
69f1c95c-2875-58ff-b85b-10d1c2d2ab83.keywords: Marius Scalesi; literature in French; poetry; migration
69f1c95c-2875-58ff-b85b-10d1c2d2ab83.description2: Pictured here is Marius (Mario) Scalesi, a young poet of Italian origin, born on 6 February 1892 in Tunis to an Italian father and a Maltese mother. He suffered from tuberculosis from birth, and became paralysed following a fall down the stairs in his home in La Goulette, the so-called "Little Sicily" of Tunis. Forced to abandon his studies in order to make a living, he completed his education independently. His articles of literary criticism and poems were published in the journal *La Tunisie Illustrée*. His collection of poems, *Les Poèmes d'un Maudit* sheds light on the hardships of his life. He died in 1922 in an asylum in Palermo. A fascinating figure due to his triple cultural identity - Italian, French and Tunisian - he is considered one of the pioneers of North African poetry in French.
