6a34e64b-e996-5c58-9984-ac149359cb8c.keywords: Commerce; trade; Currency; Coins; coinage; Numismatics
6a34e64b-e996-5c58-9984-ac149359cb8c.description2: This 100 piastres bank note bears no watermark, and is illustrated with horses, symbolising pride, and the famous columns of the Baalbek temple.

6a3c68eb-7bea-5e92-8112-9d9d0c950351.name: The Bach Hamba brothers
6a3c68eb-7bea-5e92-8112-9d9d0c950351.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
6a3c68eb-7bea-5e92-8112-9d9d0c950351.author: Bechir Yazidi
6a3c68eb-7bea-5e92-8112-9d9d0c950351.keywords: Newspaper Le Tunisien; the Young Tunisians movement
6a3c68eb-7bea-5e92-8112-9d9d0c950351.description2: 'Ali (pictured here) and Mohamed were two of the leaders of the protest movement "Harakat al-Shabab al-Tunisi" (the Young Tunisians). Born in Tunis in 1876 and 1881 respectively, these two men of Turkish origin helped found a French-language newspaper, *Le Tunisien*, through which they attacked the politics of the French colonialists and demanded reform. With the help of their comrades, the brothers organised many acts of resistance, such as the Jellaz Affair (1911) and the tramway boycott (1912). The arrest of the majority of the movement's founders, and the suppression of the newspaper *Le Tunisien* marked the end of their activities in Tunisia. However, they continued to make their demands from abroad, working mainly in Geneva and Istanbul, where they finally died in 1818 ('Ali) and 1820 (Mohamed).

6a6e9eb9-6672-5c93-a85f-f911188ec1ce.name: Tankard
6a6e9eb9-6672-5c93-a85f-f911188ec1ce.description: This tankard follows the pattern of Persian jugs of the 15th century. Its rich figurative decoration is reminiscent of the decorative strips used in book painting. The decor gives this tankard a special position in the context of Ottoman silver works, which in most cases present ornamental decoration only.
6a6e9eb9-6672-5c93-a85f-f911188ec1ce.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

6a89da25-5756-58bf-b49f-f4fde99fe13b.name: Istanbul Archaeological Museums
6a89da25-5756-58bf-b49f-f4fde99fe13b.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
6a89da25-5756-58bf-b49f-f4fde99fe13b.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Archaology Museum
6a89da25-5756-58bf-b49f-f4fde99fe13b.description2: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen had been exposed to Westernizing ideas through education and travel. This museum was founded by decree as the Imperial Museum (*İmparatorluk Müzesi*) in 1891. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi Bey. Construction of the main building began in 1881, attaining its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. The site of the museum belonged to the Topkapı Palace outer gardens. It is a prominent structure built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul.

6acad3a4-63f3-5160-bf8e-60081e141ee0.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury

The table on the left contains a numbered list of shops and important landmarks, whereas the table on the right lists the name and location of Beirut's railway and maritime companies.

6b2642e7-7a75-5343-8798-9e4bf21929a4.description2: Portrait of Luca Petrovic. He was a commander of Herzegovinian freedom fighters against the Turks in 1876. This insurrection against the Turks provoked the 1878 Congress of Berlin, which led to the occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the Austrian Empire.

6b87d037-edfd-580b-a728-429fe7822c7b.name: Map of Beirut
6b87d037-edfd-580b-a728-429fe7822c7b.holder: American University of Beirut, Jafet Library, Archives and Special Collections Department

6b87d037-edfd-580b-a728-429fe7822c7b.keywords: Expansion; Map; Districts; Consulates; Routes; City; Beirut
6b87d037-edfd-580b-a728-429fe7822c7b.description2: This map dates to 1876 and was drawn by the acting Danish Consul, Julius Loytved for the Sultan 'Abd al-Hamid II. Loytved was a map-maker, an archaeologist, and the director of various Anglo-Syrian schools. This detailed survey map includes 12 districts of Beirut: 1 - The Old City and the *suq*; 2 - Al-Zaytuna; 3 - Ras Beirut; 4 - Msaytbe; 5 - Mazraat al-Arab; 6 - Ras el-Naba'; 7 - Al-Bashura; 8 - Achrafieh; 9 - St. Dimitri; 10 - Mimas; 11 - Rmeil; 12 - Al-Saifi. The roads to Damascus, Saida and Tripoli are all clearly indicated by emphasis on the edge of the map. The map also indicates 47 other points of interest, including 91 consulates, military posts, government buildings, educational and health institutions, public parks, private gardens, cemeteries, archaeological sites, and sand and rock hills.

6b95b4dd-912b-59ba-93e0-00f63bedc323.name: SWP Geological Map
6b95b4dd-912b-59ba-93e0-00f63bedc323.description2: This was the first ever geological map of Palestine, drawn up in the late 1880’s by Edward Hull. It enabled, for the first time, the accurate assessment of the geological resources of the country, and potentially their exploitation to the benefit of the local economy, as well as revealing the history and structure of the landscape.

The collection comprises of 10 volumes of illustrations and 9 volumes of texts published betwen 1809 and 1826.

6c348586-1356-5ba4-b2b5-0c09d19282dc.name: The Victims of Labour
6c348586-1356-5ba4-b2b5-0c09d19282dc.author: Marina Minozzi
6c348586-1356-5ba4-b2b5-0c09d19282dc.keywords: Sculpture; Italian sculptors; realism; Verismo; social topics; post-unitarian Italian society; rights of workers; working class; life expectancy; poverty; industry; communication; industrial development; road; railway; international; universal exposition
6c348586-1356-5ba4-b2b5-0c09d19282dc.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
6c348586-1356-5ba4-b2b5-0c09d19282dc.description2: Vincenzo Vela studied at the academy of Fine arts of Brera and at the age of 22 he won an Academy of Venice competition. The artwork is an homage to the workers who died during the construction of the Gotthard Tunnel between 1872-82, which had implemented new cost-lowering techniques that also caused numerous incidents and loss of life. Work conditions were very unhealthy: temperatures over 30 degrees, gas exhalations and no air shafts. Even the accommodations were unhealthy and dirty. When the workers went on strike for the inhumane conditions, police shot at protesters, killing four workers. The miners in *The Victims of Labour* are depicted carrying the body of a dying classmate on a stretcher out of the tunnel. A self-portrait of the sculptor is recognisable in the classmate’s face. The harsh modelling of the workers’ bodies, almost deformed, makes the scene even more powerful. The artist affirmed he had no commission for this work which was a passion project. In 1895 it was cast in bronze on request of the Ministry of Education; in 1900 it was sent to the Universal Exhibition in Paris.

6c3d3ee7-fba0-54ef-ae3a-b0810a3caeb2.description2: The bedouin became a symbol of romantic nomadism in the 19th century European imagination. The Zangaki brothers, a pair of Greek photographers working in Egypt, began producing photos of these nomads for Western tourists.

6c58855f-349e-59d4-b95b-645e69fbce46.description2: People had been trying to find the source of the Nile since antiquity. These observations were published and illustrated with engravings, which allowed Europeans to better understand the African continent.

6c5debca-9932-5c4a-89ab-f8f3d13de354.name: Dinar
6c5debca-9932-5c4a-89ab-f8f3d13de354.description: Gold Dinar of Hijaz, King Hussein bin 'Ali, AH 1334. On November, 1916 the notables, ulama of Hijaz and a majority of the sheiks of Bedouins and sedentary tribes, assembled at the great Mosque of Mecca to pay allegiance to al-Hussein and proclaim him “King“ of Arab Countries. On this occasion a coin bearing his name at Mecca, as King of the Arabs was struck. But Britain, France and Italy recognized him only as “King of the Hijaz” on 3 January 1917. On obverse: "*bi-l-bilad al-'arabiyya al-husayn bin 'ali / 'abduhu / hashimi / wa ibn 'abdihi / al-nahidh*" ("Hussein bin Ali / God’s Servant / Hashimi /and son of God’s Servant / leader of Arab renaissance"). On reverse: "*duriba bi-makka al-mukarrama / sana 1334 / dinar / sana 8 / 'asima al-hukuma al-'arabiyya*" ("Dinar minted at Makka al-Mukarrama in 1334 \[AH\] in the reign year 8 capital of Arab Government"). All regular coins of Hijaz bear the accessional date of ١٣٣٤ (AH 1334) of al-Hussein bin 'Ali, plus the regional year, many bronze coins had a light silver wash.
6c5debca-9932-5c4a-89ab-f8f3d13de354.author: Aida Naghawi
6c5debca-9932-5c4a-89ab-f8f3d13de354.keywords: Hussein bin Ali; dinar; Arab Hashemite Government; Mecca al Mukarrama; coin; currency; coinage; numismatics

6c5fc9c1-bb88-513e-a896-4dd682e2510a.name: Pera Palace Hotel
6c5fc9c1-bb88-513e-a896-4dd682e2510a.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
6c5fc9c1-bb88-513e-a896-4dd682e2510a.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ancient Istanbul; hotel; travelling
6c5fc9c1-bb88-513e-a896-4dd682e2510a.description2: Pera Palace Hotel was built in 1892 for the purpose of hosting the passengers of the Orient Express and was named after its location. Alexander Vallaury, a French-Turkish architect living in the city designed the hotel in a blend of neo-classical, art nouveau and oriental styles. The hotel was the first building in Turkey to be powered by electricity other than the Ottoman Palaces. It was also the only address in the city to provide hot running water for its guests and was home to the first electric elevator in Istanbul.

6c6f6415-19dd-5136-9ef7-3e7a144c2f66.name: Memorial Volume – Dedicatory and opening ceremonies of the Chicago World's Colombian Exposition – 1893
6c6f6415-19dd-5136-9ef7-3e7a144c2f66.description2: The World's Columbian Exposition or The Chicago World's Fair was a World's Fair held in Chicago in 1893 to celebrate the 400th anniversary of Christopher Columbus' arrival in the New World in 1492. The fair was an influential social and cultural event to which the Ottoman Empire had been invited. It displayed raw materials and agricultural products at the exposition, as well as handicraft products and plant products belonging to the palace revenue. The 1893 Chicago Exhibition was a big success for the Chamber of Commerce. The Head of the Chamber of Commerce, Azaryan Efendi, was assigned to the head of the commission, which was formed in Istanbul for the Chicago Exhibition.

6c834b03-f120-537f-ad07-f35c0f191253.name: Hanging (*sitara*) for the Mosque of the Prophet, Medina al-Munawwarah
6c834b03-f120-537f-ad07-f35c0f191253.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation /Sharjah Museums Authority
6c834b03-f120-537f-ad07-f35c0f191253.dates: Hegira mid 13th century / AD mid 19th century
6c834b03-f120-537f-ad07-f35c0f191253.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
6c834b03-f120-537f-ad07-f35c0f191253.materials: Silk, cotton, silver and gilt silver metal thread
6c834b03-f120-537f-ad07-f35c0f191253.description2: The interior walls of the Shrine of the Prophet in the Madina were traditionally honoured with elaborate hangings. During the Ottoman period, it was customary for the Sultan to send hangings for the shrine  on the occasion of his ascension to the throne or when wear and tear demanded them to be replaced. The old  hangings were returned to Istanbul.Judging by their inscriptions, it has been suggested that  black-grounded Ottoman textiles like this one may have been commissioned specifically to cover the tomb of the Prophet (pbuh). In addition to qur'anic inscriptions, the calligraphic panels include a large green medallion with a hadith of the Prophet: ‘ (For) whosoever may visit my grave, my intercession will become an obligation’. Below, elaborate arabesque scrolling surrounds the emblem or tughra of the sultan Abd al-Hamid II (1293 H/1876 AD – 1327 H/1909 AD), who commissioned this hanging.

6cc37690-74bf-5956-9550-3a0a66b523c8.name: Photograph of a classroom at a modernised school
6cc37690-74bf-5956-9550-3a0a66b523c8.description: In 1914, the French Protectorate put forward a new policy to modernise the education system in Morocco. Integrating the new policy with the traditional education system, scholars (the *'ulama´*) of al-Qarawiyyin University modernised educational material while still respecting the old system.

6ce39e0b-ba14-5c06-b2e2-792e36cfa958.name: House
6ce39e0b-ba14-5c06-b2e2-792e36cfa958.dates: End of 19th – beginning of the 20th century
6ce39e0b-ba14-5c06-b2e2-792e36cfa958.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Prof. Petar Namichev (consultant)
6ce39e0b-ba14-5c06-b2e2-792e36cfa958.history: The most active period of construction by the *tajfas* from this area was in the 19th century and the beginning of the 20th century. Construction masters along with builders and artisans used to earn their living by building houses not only in Macedonia, but also throughout the Balkans. Activities of the Debar-Reka construction school throughout centuries have given rise to development of diverse crafts: woodcarving, architectural decoration, sculpture and stone-cutting.
6ce39e0b-ba14-5c06-b2e2-792e36cfa958.description2: The dwelling architecture in the Reka Area shows the talent and ingenuity of the anonymous native architects. The male population of this ethnic region was traditionally engaged in the construction trade. Miyak builders were widely known for their skills and distinctive architectural style in the 19th century and at the beginning of 20th century. This house was made of stone by application of bondruk system – a system of horizontal and vertical structural support beams. The usable space of the second storey has been expanded by construction of a room above the entrance area, which is supported by wooden pillars.

6d1c8ebf-40bc-511a-925c-b1e167d60a3d.name: Memo on the profits of the Suez Canal Company
6d1c8ebf-40bc-511a-925c-b1e167d60a3d.keywords: Suez Canal; Profits of the Suez Canal; Future of the Suez Canal
6d1c8ebf-40bc-511a-925c-b1e167d60a3d.description2: An important memo on the profits of the Suez Canal. It shows that the increase in average load during the last 25 years is met with an increase in net profits which are estimated to be less than five Francs per ton, although the navigation fees were much more than that amount during the period stipulated in the document. This is due to the increase in company expenses, and the company’s decision to decrease navigation fees.

6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.name: The Palace of Porto Trade Association Headquarters, the Arabian Room
6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.history: During the siege of Porto (1832-33) by Miguelist Army led by absolutist Prince Miguel (1802-66) against the Liberal troops of his brother Prince Pedro (1798-1834), S. Francisco convent was burnt only surviving the church.  Porto Trade Association’s headquarters was erected over these ruins. Queen Maria II issued the law concession letter of 19th June 1841 to order the establishment of the Stock Exchange and the Trial Court. The solemn placing of the first stone took place on 6 October 1842.
6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.keywords: Oporto; Trade Association; cultural heritage; trade; Queen Maria II; Cabralism
6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.architects: Architects: Joaquim da Costa Lima (1840–1860), Gustavo Adolpho Gonçalves e Sousa (1860–1879), Thomaz Augusto Soller (1879–1883), José de Macedo Araújo Júnior (1883–1890), Joel da Silva Pereira (1894–1899) and José Marques da Silva (1889–1910); Painting and sculptures: Luigi Maninin, António Ramalho, António Carneiro, Veloso Salgado, Marques de Oliveira, Soares dos Reis, Eduardo Malta, Teixeira Lopes and Henrique Medina, among others.
6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.description2: The Arabian Room (1862–1880) is considered as the most emblematic of all the Palace’s rooms, embodying the Neo-Moorish art in Portugal. Inspired by the Palace of Alhambra in Granada combines the Arab ornament grammar and the fertile imagination of the engineer/architect, Gustavo Adolpho Gonçalves e Sousa. The Hall of Nations is decorated with the national shield and the coat of arms of the countries with which Portugal had the closest ties of friendship and trade; consolidating the idea that the greatness of a nation, country or region is not a singular effort, but one of union, strength and the cooperation among people of different nations.

6db232a1-1948-537d-8bad-3c92a264c7c0.name: Stucco panel
6db232a1-1948-537d-8bad-3c92a264c7c0.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
6db232a1-1948-537d-8bad-3c92a264c7c0.keywords: Carved plaster; capitals; palaces; Ottoman style; Italian-esque style
6db232a1-1948-537d-8bad-3c92a264c7c0.description2: "Stucco" is a term used to describe the vast majority of decorations in Islamic Arts. White stucco, made from plaster stones, was used for column capitals, arcs, as well as sloped constructions such as roofs, as it is an incredibly supple, yet strong, adherent, durable and light material. Muslim artisans made countless constructions decorated with stucco. The 18th and 19th centuries, however, saw many constructions in carved golden plaster - both palaces and houses were elaborately decorated in this way. Floral motifs, closer to the Ottoman and Italian styles, soon overtook the geometric designs of previous centuries.

6dbf6cf4-1732-5bea-bb96-c766474a0193.name: *Clock tower, Beirut*
6dbf6cf4-1732-5bea-bb96-c766474a0193.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
6dbf6cf4-1732-5bea-bb96-c766474a0193.author: Stefan Weber
6dbf6cf4-1732-5bea-bb96-c766474a0193.description2: In the Ottoman provinces, clock towers became part of the urban space in the 19th century. These monuments allowed a certain control of time and symbolized "modernity". But they also functioned as imperial monuments. Beirut’s clock tower was for instance built near the Grand Serail to celebrate the anniversary of the Ottoman Sultan Abdülhamid’s [`Abd al-Hamid II]accession to the throne. So clock towers might be the most telling symbol of the presence of a new political order in the wake of the Tanzimat. Designed by Youssef Aftimus, the tower is 25 m tall, which made it the tallest piece of architecture in Beirut at the time of its completion.

6dc1ad58-0a34-56e0-8d64-e8b890165b25.name: Sayyidet al-Saha Church
6dc1ad58-0a34-56e0-8d64-e8b890165b25.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
6dc1ad58-0a34-56e0-8d64-e8b890165b25.history: This Church, inaugurated in 1898, is a made of sandstone from the coastal city of Batroun and built in a plain style, with no vaults.
6dc1ad58-0a34-56e0-8d64-e8b890165b25.description2: The church is situated close to the castle, on its southern side.

6e1d143a-f28c-5e23-bd94-fbe16124f587.name: Crown (*taj*)
6e1d143a-f28c-5e23-bd94-fbe16124f587.description: A crown (*taj*) made in Fez, with geometric and floral decoration, crafted from gold, and set with emeralds and rubies. It illustrates the decorative style that appeared in the early 20th century influenced by French designs, which is notable especially in the three small crowns at the top.
6e1d143a-f28c-5e23-bd94-fbe16124f587.keywords: Applied arts; precious stones; French design; floral decoration; floral motifs; vegetal motifs; vegetal decoration; craftsmanship; traditional craftsmanship; Moroccan craftsmen; European influence; fashion

6e327e6c-97a6-5021-bdda-e534a67a0765.name: Reserve head
6e327e6c-97a6-5021-bdda-e534a67a0765.description: The *Reserve head* is one of the major works of the Viennese collection, found in an early tomb in the burial grounds of Giza. Though stylized, the visage is still full of life, with simultaneously idealized and very regular features. Scholars still disagree about the purpose of this type of object. Traditional explanations proffer their use as surrogate heads for the soul (mummifying having then been only in its earliest stages).
6e327e6c-97a6-5021-bdda-e534a67a0765.dates: 4th Dyn. c. 2600 BC; acquired by Hermann Junker during his excavation in Giza 1912–1929
6e327e6c-97a6-5021-bdda-e534a67a0765.dimensions: Height 27,7 cm, B 17,3 cm, Diameter 24,5 cm

6e335928-9fa2-5b6f-93cb-9088b371f464.name: *Zabun*
6e335928-9fa2-5b6f-93cb-9088b371f464.description2: The *zabun* is similar to a European coat and the Turkish *qaftan* (a European inspired coat). It is speculated that it first arrived in the eastern part of Saudi Arabia through the Hajj, at the time of the Turkish empire, and later became popular in Qatar and Bahrayn. The *zabun* is made out of fine Indian Kashmiri brown wool with intricate embroidery. Decoration: made of light brown wool embroidered with *boteh* design, motif across the coat – paisley, Islamic decorative arts. Imitated because the shape is Kashmiri, shaped like cashew nut, pronounced ‘Gazorah.’ Colours are red, yellow, and edges are lined with metal silk thread – round neck opening. Narrow Nehru collar, or Chinese collar is known in Qatar. Buttons are handmade metal balls down the front. It is worn with the *thawb ishlahat*.

6f001e78-8dfc-56a6-bec2-b6b68344cfd8.name: *Tsar Nikolai II enters Paris, 6 October 1896*
6f001e78-8dfc-56a6-bec2-b6b68344cfd8.keywords: Diplomacy; France; Russia; Nicholas II; Paris
6f001e78-8dfc-56a6-bec2-b6b68344cfd8.description2: Tsar Nikolai II's visit to France in October 1896 was front page news. The French government, hoping to highlight the importance of this day, marked the occasion by giving students the day off, stopping all special train services, and meticulously preparing the path the imperial couple would take once arriving at Cherbourg Port. The true purpose of the trip was to preserve the precious Franco-Russian alliance signed in 1893 with Aleksandr III. Pictured in this image are the Tsar and his wife, accompanied by the President of the Republic Félix Faure, and greeted by a crowd of almost half a million on the Champs-Élysées. The popular imagery contributed to the success and immortalisation of the event.

6f1032fa-b287-57a0-81ee-3a8c6977d38a.name: The Palace of Porto Trade Association Headquarters
6f1032fa-b287-57a0-81ee-3a8c6977d38a.history: During the siege of Porto (1832-33) by Miguelist Army led by absolutist Prince Miguel (1802-66) against the Liberal troops of his brother Prince Pedro (1798-1834), S. Francisco convent was burnt only surviving the church.  Porto Trade Association’s headquarters was erected over these ruins. Queen Maria II issued the law concession letter of 19th June 1841 to order the establishment of the Stock Exchange and the Trial Court. The solemn placing of the first stone took place on 6 October 1842.
6f1032fa-b287-57a0-81ee-3a8c6977d38a.architects: Architects: Joaquim da Costa Lima (1840–1860), Gustavo Adolpho Gonçalves e Sousa (1860–1879), Thomaz Augusto Soller (1879–1883), José de Macedo Araújo Júnior (1883–1890), Joel da Silva Pereira (1894–1899) and José Marques da Silva (1889–1910); Painting and sculptures: Luigi Maninin, António Ramalho, António Carneiro, Veloso Salgado, Marques de Oliveira, Soares dos Reis, Eduardo Malta, Teixeira Lopes and Henrique Medina, among others.
6f1032fa-b287-57a0-81ee-3a8c6977d38a.description2: All the rooms of the Palácio da Bolsa are works of art, with undisputed prominence as a worthy representative of the city of Porto. Along three generations, great names in architecture, painting, sculpture and decorative arts contributed to the creation of a unique heritage at the Palácio da Bolsa, a true jewel of the neo-classical style of the 19th century. In the Palace’s interior, along with the grand architectural design of the Hall of Nations and the famous Arab Room, other noteworthy attractions include: the furniture’s symbolic meaning and its aesthetic originality; the decorative stucco’s’ intricate detail; the masterful detail of the wooden inlaid floors; the coat of arms and heraldic representations; finely sculpted statues and an immense profusion of gigantic oil paintings and frescos by great Portuguese masters.

6f1eea68-18d9-59b6-a602-617d05d6a7ae.name: Sprinkler
6f1eea68-18d9-59b6-a602-617d05d6a7ae.author: Mina Moraitou
6f1eea68-18d9-59b6-a602-617d05d6a7ae.description2: A sprinkler with a low base, spherical body and a narrow tapering neck. The body is decorated with a fish-scale motif anf four stylised leaves. The neck bears a dotted motif and blue motifs. A product of a workshop in France specialising in Islamic shapes and decoration.

6f32665b-a3e9-5152-9c94-67a17540cfed.description2: Picture of the Austrian team's Egyptian cook. In 1911 the Austrian Academy obtained the concession for excavation in Giza. In 1912 Hermann Junker's team started to excavate tombs close to the pyramids of Giza.

6f83b69e-bc0a-5955-8a8f-46818fc39f26.name: *Chechia maker*
6f83b69e-bc0a-5955-8a8f-46818fc39f26.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie

6f83b69e-bc0a-5955-8a8f-46818fc39f26.archival: Tunis au XIXe Siècle: Aquarelles et Textes de Charles Lallemand, Apollonia, 2001.
6f83b69e-bc0a-5955-8a8f-46818fc39f26.description2: This copy of a beautiful watercolour from Charles Lallemand's book *Tunis et ses Environs* shows a Tunisian artisan making a chechia. Before the competition of European industry arose in the 19th century, Tunisian artisans had been the main suppliers of the Middle East.

6f8705b6-8b55-55ab-a02e-52dedab4e4de.name: Long-sleeve women's coat (*Mintan*)
6f8705b6-8b55-55ab-a02e-52dedab4e4de.author: Nada Andonovska
6f8705b6-8b55-55ab-a02e-52dedab4e4de.keywords: Mintan; srma; silk; silver; costume; Yörük community; nomads; Turkish; marriage; wedding
6f8705b6-8b55-55ab-a02e-52dedab4e4de.materials: Decoration with braids and cords of gold wrapped thread
6f8705b6-8b55-55ab-a02e-52dedab4e4de.description2: The enclave of the Turkish Yoruk community in Macedonia living in the mountain villages of Dojran – Valandovo and Radovish – and the Shtip region is a genuine treasure of tangible and intangible heritage that adds to the diversity of traditional culture in Macedonia. This bridal attire preserves some of the traditions in clothing and embellishment of Yoruk women in Macedonia in the 19th century and the early 20th century. A *mintan* is a short upper garment worn over the tunic. This piece is made of red silk. It is decorated with braids and cords of *srma* – gold-wrapped thread applied on the hems and over the front.

6f9a1e3f-fc30-5c29-9157-47822ce579e3.name: Dougga archaeological site
6f9a1e3f-fc30-5c29-9157-47822ce579e3.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
6f9a1e3f-fc30-5c29-9157-47822ce579e3.history: Dougga, which was a North African city under Roman control during the Numidian period, contains almost perfectly preserved remains of an ancient city and its different elements, and presents the best example of how indigenous cities were adapted, for better or for worse, to the Roman urban model. When the first European explorers travelled through the Regency of Tunis, the Dougga (Thugga) site attracted both theirs and the scientific community's attention more than any other ancient city. The site is remarkably preserved, and its ruins were therefore a great source of interest and fascination. This interest peaked when the Englishman Thomas Reade stole a Libyco-Punic inscription.
6f9a1e3f-fc30-5c29-9157-47822ce579e3.keywords: Numidian; Roman; indigenous; temple; sanctuary; Tanit; Ba'al/Saturn
6f9a1e3f-fc30-5c29-9157-47822ce579e3.description2: Located in the Teboursouk region in north-east Tunisia, this archaeological site is notable for its size - 70 hectares - its excellently preserved monuments and its rich past, having witnessed more than 15 centuries of history covering the Punic, Numidian, Roman and Byzantine eras. It contains a great variety of temples and sanctuaries, such as those dedicated to Ba'al/Saturn and to Tanit/Caelestis, a capitoline triad, a public square, a theatre, large public baths, private homes of varying wealth, funerary monuments and more. Many of these monuments were one of a kind, and so in December 1997 Dougga archaeological site was listed as a World Heritage Site by UNESCO.

6f9fb1e8-99e0-571f-8a20-02431dd74f73.name: Yatagan
6f9fb1e8-99e0-571f-8a20-02431dd74f73.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
6f9fb1e8-99e0-571f-8a20-02431dd74f73.keywords: Yatagan; ÖWG; Bosnia; arms; armours; metalwork; military object; war; warfare
6f9fb1e8-99e0-571f-8a20-02431dd74f73.description2: This yatagan boasts the typical traditional ear-shaped hilt, fastidiously decorated with gems, and a blade decorated with simple ornaments. The scabbard is made of sheet metal, the fittings are made of punched brass. The condition is used, with signs of age and regular wear and some gems have been lost. The scabbard is partially showing signs of removed rust and has some minor bruises and spots. This yatagan seems to have been a well-worn part of its owner’s attire.

6faa2e57-f95c-52d9-a61f-402154b53322.name: Organ Made in Tunis by the Italian Firm Cesare Trionfo and Exhibited in Milan
6faa2e57-f95c-52d9-a61f-402154b53322.author: Giulia Barrera
6faa2e57-f95c-52d9-a61f-402154b53322.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 197.
6faa2e57-f95c-52d9-a61f-402154b53322.third_name: *Organo costruito a Tunisi dalla Ditta Cesare Trionfo ed esposto a Milano*
6faa2e57-f95c-52d9-a61f-402154b53322.description2:
Cesare Trionfo was a child when he migrated with his family to Tunisia from Livorno in 1855. He became a trader, and in 1886 he started trading musical instruments. In Tunis, he later also started a shop that made musical instruments such as this organ. Trionfo promoted the construction of the theatre Politeama Roissini, which he co-owned.  
This organ was exhibited in Milan for the 1906 international exhibition. The organ is a traditional Italian musical instrument. This one has decorative elements taken from Arab architecture.

6fb5d317-b1c7-55c6-a5a1-452d17f4b70a.name: *10 cents an issue. Le Télégraphe. Morning Newspaper. Special connections with the whole world.*
6fb5d317-b1c7-55c6-a5a1-452d17f4b70a.description2: Claude Chappe's invention of optical telegraphy was a turning point in the development of telecommunications. Built high up (e.g. on a hill or a roof), the mechanism consisted of a pole with movable arms, visible from a distance, which transmitted a code. Telegraphy became a very popular mode of communication during times of war, and was adopted by the National Convention of the First Republic in 1793. Even Napoléon I, who had shut down the French telegraph lines for fear of political troubles, had them reopened and extended to Europe in order to fight the anti-French Coalition. Telegraphy was an increasingly used mode of communication in the 19th century.

701d0273-bf02-5200-8f32-6dab9287106b.name: Bridal apron jewellery (*Mangura*)
701d0273-bf02-5200-8f32-6dab9287106b.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
701d0273-bf02-5200-8f32-6dab9287106b.keywords: Mangura; filigree; perforation; silver; costume; accessories; wedding; marriage
701d0273-bf02-5200-8f32-6dab9287106b.materials: Silver, silver alloy, tiny beads, hammering, casting, filigree, perforation
701d0273-bf02-5200-8f32-6dab9287106b.description2: The influences of Eastern art in Macedonia were largely expressed in the jewellery of the 19th century through the so-called Levantine Baroque style. This piece preserves evidence of the exceptional diversity of the jewellery. Worn on the apron, it also shows that articles of adornment used to be applied on many different items of clothing. A *mangura* consists of a string of tiny beads adorned with ornaments. The larger central pendant has been made in the filigree technique and embellished with decorative stones. It is flanked by minor ornaments decorated by perforation.

703206c7-1fe3-5807-91ec-e3c954824bfa.name: *Egypt. Plan of the remains of an existing circus, near Alexandria.*
703206c7-1fe3-5807-91ec-e3c954824bfa.second_name: Taken from *Description de l'Egypte: Dessins Préparatoires*
703206c7-1fe3-5807-91ec-e3c954824bfa.description2: During the Egyptian expedition (1798–1801), Napoléon Bonaparte brought with him a group of scholars, engineers and artists, charged with collecting as much scientific information as possible. This was then used in a publication (of exceptional quality and execution) entitled Description de l'Égypte, in which the observations and enquiries made by the military expedition in Egypt were collected. The collection comprises of 10 volumes of illustrations and 9 volumes of texts published between 1809 and 1826.

70423969-df09-5091-ad7b-50e63c993a4d.name: Painting of Vittorio Emanuele II, King of Italy
70423969-df09-5091-ad7b-50e63c993a4d.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
70423969-df09-5091-ad7b-50e63c993a4d.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
70423969-df09-5091-ad7b-50e63c993a4d.keywords: Oil on canvas; Vittorio Emanuele II
70423969-df09-5091-ad7b-50e63c993a4d.materials: Canvas, wood, coloured pigments, gold leaf
70423969-df09-5091-ad7b-50e63c993a4d.description2: This oil on canvas portrait from 1862 depicts the King Vittorio Emanuele II (1861–1878). Fair-skinned with blue eyes and brown hair, the king is dressed in official uniform, with a black jacket and silver buttons and a silver belt. The Ordre du Sang, the Nichan al-Dam and the Annunziata medals are on the left of his chest. A royal red cape is draped over his shoulders, bordered by gold decorations, a white fur collar and lapels embellished with black feathers. A gold crown decorated with red and green strasses sits is on his left, and red curtains with tassels and tiebacks in the same colour form the backdrop. This painting is evidence of an active diplomatic relationship between the Palais du Bardo and the European chancelleries.

70700c8a-84f5-533a-a08c-1e14bd325d9e.description2: A black and white photo from a leather bound album. It bepicts the *Zografion Gymnasion* in Constantinople. Photographer unknown.

707017b0-ac19-5968-8e9b-29b8a4f1aeab.name: Weighing armchair
707017b0-ac19-5968-8e9b-29b8a4f1aeab.description2: Weighing armchairs were used for medical purposes. Early metabolism studies were made by weighing the test subjects before and after eating or any other activities. They were also used to weigh handicapped people and old patients who could not stand up. The chair is made of polished brown walnut wood. There are two rows of metal plates in front of the seating area. There is a decoration made by punched holes on the backside of the armchair. There is a wooden footrest attached with metal bars to the main body of the armchair. On the rear side there is a weighing mechanism.

7080a158-a1b4-545b-bb83-ebdc891f29f8.name: Moroccan coins
7080a158-a1b4-545b-bb83-ebdc891f29f8.description: Coin struck in 1903 under Mulay Sultan ‘Abd al-‘Aziz al-Hasan I (r. 1894 to 1908) at the mint in Fez. For a century (1800-1900) the ‘Alawid sultans struck coins in the workshops of Fez, but due to the economic crisis at the time, gold was unavailable so most coins were of silver, bronze or other common metals – although the technique remained the same, with the metal poured into moulds. The patterns on the face and on the back vary between the star with eight points (Solomon ring) and the indication of the place of mint.
7080a158-a1b4-545b-bb83-ebdc891f29f8.keywords: Coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; gold; silver; bronze; mint; moulding; moulds; six-pointed star; ring; workshop; traditional coinage; European influence

70ae613d-6258-52dc-8ef3-3c83dcfa4fb0.name: *Turkish café, Smyrna, 9 November 1837*
70ae613d-6258-52dc-8ef3-3c83dcfa4fb0.second_name: Taken from *Voyage dans la Russie Méridionale et la Crimée* (Traveling in southern Russia and the Crimea)
70ae613d-6258-52dc-8ef3-3c83dcfa4fb0.description2: Denis-Auguste-Marie Raffet (1804–1860), sketcher and painter, travelled to Southern Russia, Crimea and Turkey with the Prince Demidoff in 1837. He brought back with him a few hundred illustrated pages, which were published in *Voyage en Crimée*. This image, depicting a café in Smyrna (Izmir), the "Little Paris" of the Ottoman Empire, is an excellent example of Orientalist drawing.

70b437a4-41c0-50dd-839c-7f248f97ae34.name: *Theatre of Djemila, ancient Cuicul*
70b437a4-41c0-50dd-839c-7f248f97ae34.author: Hayet Touaibia
70b437a4-41c0-50dd-839c-7f248f97ae34.description2: In August 1840 and again in 1848 Delamare visited the ruins of Cuicul, an ancient Roman colony founded by Nerva and Trajan at the end of the first century. He brought a number of sketches back from these visits, with the most important of these currently kept at the Cabinet du Livre in the old library at the Sorbonne. This drawing, kept at the Musée des Beaux-Arts, accurately reproduces of the ruins of the theatre, built in the second century beyond the city walls.

70b73c8c-526f-5ae3-901a-f7ef4dbf4ea8.name: Arabs listening to a story in their camp
70b73c8c-526f-5ae3-901a-f7ef4dbf4ea8.artist: Engraver: Jean-Pierre Marie Jazet; artist: Horace Vernet
70b73c8c-526f-5ae3-901a-f7ef4dbf4ea8.description2: Horace Vernet (1789–1863), the official painter of both Napoléon III and Louis-Philippe, was tasked with painting the "discovery" and conquest of Algeria. Various images of Algeria were published in the illustrated press in order to acquaint the French with Algeria and feed the narrative of a peaceful conquest. This idyllic painting of a group storytelling was very popular in the Salon des Beaux-Arts in 1834, and was reproduced by the engraver Jean-Pierre Marie Jazet in order to ensure its wider diffusion in the national press.

70c03f94-1563-5fc4-9b32-84ea00fd8d52.name: A Letter from the State Bank of Morocco

70c34b29-b413-5cf3-ba1c-bd2773093060.name: Clothing, sheets and blankets distributed by the Students’ Benevolent Fund to destitute Italian children in Tunis
70c34b29-b413-5cf3-ba1c-bd2773093060.author: Giulia Barrera
70c34b29-b413-5cf3-ba1c-bd2773093060.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 123
70c34b29-b413-5cf3-ba1c-bd2773093060.description2: The Dante Alighieri Society – created in Italy in 1889 and still in existence ‒ is aimed at promoting Italian language and culture abroad; its Tunisian branch was established in 1893. In Tunisia the Dante Alighieri Society devoted its energies to promoting schooling and supporting school attendance. One should consider, in this regard, that the Italian community at the time was composed of workers, miners, and labourers and included several destitute members. The students’ benevolent fund of the Società Dante Alighieri (Patronato scolastico) was created in 1898 and was aimed at supporting school attendance of destitute children by providing free books and clothes.

en: Pendola, M., *Gli italiani di Tunisia: storia di una comunità (XIX-XX secolo)*, Foligno: Editoriale Umbra, 2007.

70d49b3f-e99f-5946-83f7-c0c3b1092a69.name: Osman Hamdi Bey (During the excavation of Mount Nemrut)
70d49b3f-e99f-5946-83f7-c0c3b1092a69.archival: *Le tumulus de Nemroud-Dagh. Voyage, description, inscriptions avec plans et photographies*, İstanbul, F. Loeffler, 1883.
70d49b3f-e99f-5946-83f7-c0c3b1092a69.keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters,; archaeological excavations
70d49b3f-e99f-5946-83f7-c0c3b1092a69.description2: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen were exposed to Western ideas through education and travel. The museum was founded by decree in 1891 as the Imperial Museum. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi. Hamdi began construction of the main building in 1881, and it achieved its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. It is one of the prominent structures built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul. Osman Hamdi, during his tenure as museum director, launched the first Turkish scientific excavations. He carried out archaeological excavations at Mount Nemrut, Laguna and Sidon.

70d8300c-308e-5b69-9c40-e4c3750f6ab8.description: A photograph of a musician in Morocco, he wears local dress and is holding a violin and bow.

70df1938-c4b1-5bed-9f24-8054cc85bf48.description2: Portrait of Karl I, the last Austrian Emperor. The Austrian and the Ottoman Empires disintegrated after World War I. Karl I had to flee from Austria and died in exile on the island of Madeira.

70fdcb57-1eeb-5564-b13a-e80bde43f3ba.name: *Courtyard of Justice at the Alhambra Palace, Granada*
70fdcb57-1eeb-5564-b13a-e80bde43f3ba.description: Sorolla depicted the Alhambra palace often. In this painting he chose the entry to the golden room. The beauty and exoticism of the Alhambra Palace fascinated European painters during the 19th century. Sorolla painted this monument in successive trips in 1909, 1910 and again in 1917. He was interested in architecture and especially in the Arab gardens, the play of light and water in their pools, and not so much in other topics.

712ff58d-128f-55d5-aad2-b4bc62cf22ab.name: *Le Petit Tunisien. Voice for French interests and communities in Tunisia.*
712ff58d-128f-55d5-aad2-b4bc62cf22ab.description2: Italian migration to Tunisia in the 19th century was, quantitively speaking, extremely significant. The French government had to bear in mind, however, that there remained significant population who had hoped Tunisia would become an Italian colony. Some French newspapers, such as *Le Petit Tunisien*, responded to this by emphasising their French-Italian links.

7145d9d7-3f20-55d9-a385-486cd31761ab.name: Women's pants (*Don*)
7145d9d7-3f20-55d9-a385-486cd31761ab.author: Nada Andonovska
7145d9d7-3f20-55d9-a385-486cd31761ab.keywords: costume; embroidery; geometric patterns; geometric motifs; Yörük community; nomads; Turkish; marriage; wedding
7145d9d7-3f20-55d9-a385-486cd31761ab.materials: White canvas decorated with embroidery og varied wool, as well as silver and gold wrapped thread
7145d9d7-3f20-55d9-a385-486cd31761ab.description2: The enclave of the Turkish Yoruk community in Macedonia living in the mountain villages of Dojran – Valandovo and Radovish – and the Shtip region is a genuine treasure of tangible and intangible heritage that adds to the diversity of traditional culture in Macedonia. In general terms, the traditional outfit of Yoruk women in Macedonia is distinguished with exceptional colouring and application of varied elements in all articles of clothing. This bridal attire preserves some of the traditions in clothing and embellishment of Yoruk women in Macedonia in the 19th century and the early 20th century. This piece of trousers shows decoration of embroidery with geometric patterns applied on the lower front part of the trousers.

714736c9-97a7-5e87-b9d2-fc5d38aed09f.name: Thirty belts
714736c9-97a7-5e87-b9d2-fc5d38aed09f.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
714736c9-97a7-5e87-b9d2-fc5d38aed09f.description2: Belts like these were traditionally given to a bride by her parents, and were worn for the marriage ceremony. The belts are made of silver, and each one is carved with its tribe's traditional design. The bride would wear the belt of her own tribe during the ceremony as a sign of belonging. These belts date to the 19th century.

718961a1-beb1-58c3-8832-5f8a278c1682.name: The young ladies of the telephones: a view of a Parisian telephone exchange
718961a1-beb1-58c3-8832-5f8a278c1682.description2: The French telephone network was not automated at the beginning of the 20th century. Young unmarried women were often employed to take paying members' calls, and connect them to their requested number.

71964a69-73f1-55cb-a4b0-08031be5d50e.name: The peace treaty of Bucharest
71964a69-73f1-55cb-a4b0-08031be5d50e.description2: The peace treaty that ended the Russo-Ottoman war of 1806-1812 was signed by the representatives of Russia and the Ottoman Empire in Bucharest, the capital of Wallachia, on the 28 May 1812. Both Wallachia and Moldavia had been occupied by Russia during the war. According to the third article of the peace treaty the Russian army had to liberate Wallachia and the Moldavian territory on the right side of the Prut River. The fourth article stipulated that Russia annexed the territory situated on the left side of the Prut, which became the new border between the Ottoman and the Russian Empires. The new area incorporated into the Russian Empire was given the name Bessarabia, which had in the past designated southern Moldavia.

71bafc31-de50-5515-8301-3411a7a0be01.name: *A market in Bucharest*
71bafc31-de50-5515-8301-3411a7a0be01.description2: Wallachia and Moldavia's contacts with the Ottoman Empire also influenced the aspect of Romanian cities. For example, marketplaces, as known from 19th century paintings and lithographs, were similar to Turkish bazaars and represented, just like in the Ottoman Empire, the commercial centre of a city. The watercolor is part of an album with reproductions after 15 of Amedeo Preziosi’s paintings that depict scenes from Bucharest. Maltese painter Amedeo Preziosi met Carol of Hohenzollern, ruler of Romania, in Istanbul in 1866. Invited by the prince to come visit his country, Preziosi was in Romania between June-July 1868 and May-July 1869. He is the author of more than 250 works inspired by Romanian landscapes, cities and people.

71d1bb15-43f9-5e5d-8a1d-7e157badf90e.name: Daff
71d1bb15-43f9-5e5d-8a1d-7e157badf90e.holder: Lebanese National Higher Conservatory of Music
71d1bb15-43f9-5e5d-8a1d-7e157badf90e.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
71d1bb15-43f9-5e5d-8a1d-7e157badf90e.description2: The *daff*, also known as the *rikk*, is a popular instrument similar to a tambourine. It is made of a round wooden frame, covered on one side with goat or fish skin. Pairs of metal discs are set into the frame to produce a jingling sound when the instrument is struck. It is used to set the rhythm in many traditional Arabic songs, particularly during purely instrumental performances.

71d240aa-d335-59ff-8b64-aa4539d24c3b.name: *The Grand Mosque in Constanţa*
71d240aa-d335-59ff-8b64-aa4539d24c3b.description2: The Grand Mosque of Constanţa, the biggest in Romania, was built between 1910–1913 for the Muslim community of the city, on the initiative of king Carol I. It was erected on the place of a 19th century mosque, whose minbar (pulpit from where the imam delivers sermons) was preserved. The monument, a mixture of Byzantine-Egyptian and Romanian architectural elements, is the work of architect Victor Ştefănescu, who before designing it travelled to Istanbul to get acquainted with Islamic architecture. The mosque was inaugurated on 31 May 1913 in the presence of Romania’s king and queen and of Romanian and Ottoman officials. The envoy of sultan Abdul Hamid II brought a Persian rug for the mosque and awarded the orders of “Medjidie” and “Osmanieh” to Victor Ştefănescu and the city’s may.

721353f1-5e28-56da-9787-f6334515d373.name: Memorial of Sultan Husayn Kamil’s visit to the Islamic Arts Museum
721353f1-5e28-56da-9787-f6334515d373.keywords: Sultan Hussein Kamel; Arabian Archeology Museum; Islamic Arts Museum
721353f1-5e28-56da-9787-f6334515d373.description2: The Islamic Arts Museum in Cairo is the biggest Islamic museum in the world, and it encompasses a wide collection of Islamic arts from India, China, the Arab Peninsula, the Levant, Egypt, North Africa and Andalusia. Sultan Husayn Kamil’s visit to the Museum in 1916 is considered one of the more important visits received by the Museum.

727ea8ec-c6ff-5c30-91b3-9e087af62768.name: *Interior of a Harem*
727ea8ec-c6ff-5c30-91b3-9e087af62768.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
727ea8ec-c6ff-5c30-91b3-9e087af62768.keywords: costume; coffee; tobacco; rococo; Ottoman Baroque; Orientalism; women; Ottoman interior decoration; fashion
727ea8ec-c6ff-5c30-91b3-9e087af62768.description2: Preziosi probably used models to recreate this harem scene which as an infidel Frank he would not normally be allowed to witness. However, there is nothing in this decorous interior which is impossible or unlikely and it may be based on a visit to the house of one of his Turkish friends. The furniture and fittings show western European influence, particularly in the curious rococo wall bracket and the fringed sofa in place of the traditional raised wooden platform covered with carpets. By the middle of the 19th century French style in interior design was fashionable in Turkey, especially a degenerate form of the rococo. A version of this composition, dated 1852, is much less restrained, its details deliberately pandering to the popular western idea of a harem, based on Arabian Nights imagery.

729b315c-3fb9-575e-96d9-d9e48639cd90.name: Revolver
729b315c-3fb9-575e-96d9-d9e48639cd90.description: Revolver of Leopold Gasser (serial number 8106) used for land/terrestrial defence as opposed to the navy. It is also known as “Montenegrin” as it was used not only by the Austrian army but also by the army of Montenegro. The exterior was nickelled, but the nickel finish has mostly worn away leaving only traces on the barrel and the frame. The revolver is fitted with genuine ivory grips. The absence of any indication for Austria and the presence of the crown “R” might indicate to its production in Liege/Belgium.

72aa413c-a02a-5412-a43e-1c63e804854f.name: École Sadiki
72aa413c-a02a-5412-a43e-1c63e804854f.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
72aa413c-a02a-5412-a43e-1c63e804854f.history: Built in 1875 by Sadok Pacha Bey's grand vizier the General Khaireddine (Khayr al-Din), l'École Sadiki was the first Tunisian school to introduce modern teaching and move away from a traditional religious education, a move characterised by the introduction of foregin languages and the mathematical and physical sciences. L'École Sadiki was a breeding ground for Tunisian intellectuals with a love for political protesting and Westernization.
72aa413c-a02a-5412-a43e-1c63e804854f.description2: Although its first home were disused barracks, the École Sadiki moved to its current building on top of the kasbah in Tunis in 1897. It was designed by the French architect Maillet in a typical Arab style, and thus has the grandeur of official French buildings whilst also using shapes from traditional Arab architecture. Built on two floors, its internal layout is similar to Western architecture, but it recalls the Arab medina in its external ornamental features and decor, with arches on marble columns and Turkish capitals, and with cupolas, green-tiled cornices etc.

72dcc4dd-aa26-5a94-9c71-96445ad78087.name: *The Crisis in Egypt – Panoramic View of Cairo 1882*
72dcc4dd-aa26-5a94-9c71-96445ad78087.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
72dcc4dd-aa26-5a94-9c71-96445ad78087.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
72dcc4dd-aa26-5a94-9c71-96445ad78087.description2: This expansive, panoramic engraving focuses of the Citadel of Cairo with the majestic Ottoman-style mosque erected by Muhammad Ali Pasha in memory of his son Tusun at the centre. The view is taken from high up in the Moqattam range, allowing the viewer to appreciate a panorama that takes in the wide expanse of the city of Cairo beyond the fortress, all the way to the river Nile. In composing the image, dated to 1882 CE - the year of the Anglo-Egyptian war, the artist H. W. Brewer most probably drew on contemporary photographs. Little is known about this British illustrator who specialised in depictions of cities viewed from the air.The print was issued as a supplement to The Graphic 1882. The Graphic was a British weekly illustrated newspaper, first published on 4.12.1869 by William Luson Thomas’s company Illustrated Newspapers Limited. By 1882, it had over 1000 employees. The Graphic’s influence on the art word was considerable, its readers including Vincent van Gogh.

72e135bf-f1d2-56f9-a08f-ae59b081701d.name: 'The War on Trial'
72e135bf-f1d2-56f9-a08f-ae59b081701d.author: Giulia Barrera
72e135bf-f1d2-56f9-a08f-ae59b081701d.archival: Giuseppe Scalarini, Il processo alla guerra (Milano: Soc. Anonima Editrice "Avanti!", 1913), pp. 5-6.
72e135bf-f1d2-56f9-a08f-ae59b081701d.second_name: Anticolonial booklet published by the Italian Socialist Party, against Italian colonial expansion in Libya
72e135bf-f1d2-56f9-a08f-ae59b081701d.description2:
This booklet describes an imaginary trial against Giovanni Giolitti, the Italian Prime Minister who directed the colonial conquest of Libya in 1911-12. The judge asks Giolitti:  
– ‘Why did you get into other people’s home?’  
– ‘In order to defend our interests.’  
– ‘Good! And what about the slaughtering of women and children, the massacre of elderly people, and the hanging of men?’  
– ‘You see, your excellence, we needed to uplift Italian prestige.’  
– ‘And what about the thefts, the burnings and the planes that bombed huts?’  
– ‘It was our civilising mission.’ "

730d8f3c-b36e-5edb-a16b-a8c763ab2ca1.name: Order of the Osmanie that belonged to Alexandru Ioan Cuza
730d8f3c-b36e-5edb-a16b-a8c763ab2ca1.description2: Alexandru Ioan Cuza, ruler of the United Principalities of Moldova and Wallachia, received the order of Osmanie in June 1864, when he travelled to Istanbul in order to convince the sultan to agree with the changes he planned to make to the Paris Convention of 1858, which was the Principalities’ constitution. In May the modified act was approved by plebiscite in the Principalities and as a consequence a conference of the Guaranteeing Powers was organized in Istanbul. Cuza spent two weeks in Istanbul and had talks with the sultan and the ambassadors of the Guaranteeing Powers. He managed to achieve his goal since on 28 June, the representatives of the Ottoman Empire, France, Great Britain, Prussia, Russia and Sardinia authorized *The Additional Act to the 1858 Convention*.

7348dd0d-ce53-5539-9f72-098f52664a78.name: *Ali Bey (Domingo Badia y Leblich), Traveller*
7348dd0d-ce53-5539-9f72-098f52664a78.description: Ali Bey, a pseudonym used by Domingo Badia (1767–1818), was a Spanish explorer and spy. He travelled to the Ottoman Empire and North Africa under the identity of a Syrian prince. He published his experiences in different books. His travel descriptions had success in Europe and were translated into several languages. The descriptions reveal his admiration and respect for the Arab world.
7348dd0d-ce53-5539-9f72-098f52664a78.author: Carmen Linés Viñuales
7348dd0d-ce53-5539-9f72-098f52664a78.materials: Paper; ink; stipple engraving; pencil-manner engraving

736574db-9cd1-5e72-95d5-f1860d3596ad.name: *Mashrabiyya*
736574db-9cd1-5e72-95d5-f1860d3596ad.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
736574db-9cd1-5e72-95d5-f1860d3596ad.description2: The *mashrabiyya* is a decorative architectural element characteristic of residences in the Arab world. It was generally used on windows or balconies on the second floor or above. As well as being a natural ventilation device, the *mashrabiyya* served the purpose of shielding the occupant from the vision of passers' by, whilst still allowing natural light to pass through the gaps. This particular piece is square shaped and made of limestone, sculpted in floral patterns.

736a018e-a855-56c6-a0e4-184b1dba4cd5.name: Male head
736a018e-a855-56c6-a0e4-184b1dba4cd5.description: South Arabia (Yemen) has always been famous for its incense. The cultivation and widespread trade of this desirable product turned Yemen into a very important region with a highly autonomous culture. This kind of head, sculpted on tombstones, portrayed the subject partly as abstract idealization and yet in a very naturalistic way.
736a018e-a855-56c6-a0e4-184b1dba4cd5.dates: Beginning of 1st millenium AD South-Arabia; brought to Vienna by Edward Glaser in 1882–1894

736d9205-4e1c-5817-bc04-427dac8d02d2.name: *Constantinople et le Bosphore de Thrace*
736d9205-4e1c-5817-bc04-427dac8d02d2.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. Travelling in the 19th century became easier and more reliable due to the advent of steamships and trains. Westerners travelled to the East not only for touristic purposes, but also for scientific research, history, archaeology or for religious reasons. Western travellers told of their experiences and what they saw in eastern countries in their travel books and they even offer advice about the journey. Istanbul, where East and West meet, has been the subject of many a traveller's book.

737d2ad8-e855-5e34-9a89-714f0aed6dff.second_name: Original page from the Bible, discovered and described by M. Ch. Clermont-Ganneau
737d2ad8-e855-5e34-9a89-714f0aed6dff.description2: Following the work of Champollion, decoding texts and archaeological discoveries became some of the main interests of popular science journals. Graphic items also begin to feature in the late 19th century, adding to the pedagogical side of these articles.

73a8c1a7-47a7-5ac2-8219-524e45f2889c.name: Basin
73a8c1a7-47a7-5ac2-8219-524e45f2889c.holder: Musée de la Céramique Sidi Kacem Jelizi
73a8c1a7-47a7-5ac2-8219-524e45f2889c.description2: This large basin with a flat base and curved, sloping sides is also called a *maajna*. The feet of the basin are circular, and the centre is decorated with a highly stylised floral pattern with palms and winged shapes overlapping. The walls are mainly painted with a *tawq* (collar) motif. This style indicates a symbiosis between Ottoman influences and local traditions. The dominant colours are: yellow, green, brown, and violet. This basin was used to knead dough, roll semolina and as a serving bowl for certain ingredients, and shows traces of both Ottoman and Andalusian influences.

73c04230-63e1-510e-98c5-207e053e23cf.name: Chaplet of an Ottoman dervish
73c04230-63e1-510e-98c5-207e053e23cf.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
73c04230-63e1-510e-98c5-207e053e23cf.keywords: Sufi; Bosnia; Sufi Hadschi Loja; religious object; souvenirs; war; warfare
73c04230-63e1-510e-98c5-207e053e23cf.description2: The Austro-Hungarian troops who joined the Ottoman forces in 1915 performed their service very close to the Allies, but were never put under the administrative control of the Ottoman Empire, as the German soldiers were. Souvenirs of this very exotic mission during World War I were in high demand and were brought back to Austria after the end of the war.

73c32255-eecb-5121-b674-c388b401bbb6.name: Charcoal iron
73c32255-eecb-5121-b674-c388b401bbb6.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
73c32255-eecb-5121-b674-c388b401bbb6.author: Huda Kilani
73c32255-eecb-5121-b674-c388b401bbb6.description2: A heavy iron box with a triangle-shaped lid with a handle and a hollow interior that could hold smouldering charcoal to keep the iron hot. This object of everyday use illustrates how the changes in mundane life affected society at a global level. Objects like this were traded locally within Jordan.

73e736ab-49ec-5eea-8f27-af65046fe133.name: Headdress
73e736ab-49ec-5eea-8f27-af65046fe133.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
73e736ab-49ec-5eea-8f27-af65046fe133.author: Huda Kilani
73e736ab-49ec-5eea-8f27-af65046fe133.keywords: silver; prominent dome; disk; al- Druz women
73e736ab-49ec-5eea-8f27-af65046fe133.description2: A silver circular disk with filigree work and prominent dome above; chains dangling with triple petal and filigree work at the end; placed on the top of a high hat worn by al-Druze (Druse) women. Silver was the most common jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom. This object illustrates the variegated social composition and the demographic changes in the Jordanian territory in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The al-Druze tribes migrated from Syria (Hawran) to north east Jordan in the early twentieth century because of their support for the Syrian revolution against the French occupation.

742e675b-2783-5254-a6e4-abd2e2dc3cd3.name: *Monument commemorating the installation of the Hijaz-Damascus telegraph connection, Beirut*
742e675b-2783-5254-a6e4-abd2e2dc3cd3.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
742e675b-2783-5254-a6e4-abd2e2dc3cd3.author: Stefan Weber
742e675b-2783-5254-a6e4-abd2e2dc3cd3.second_name: Constructed as the focal point of the new Ottoman urban centre at Merje square
742e675b-2783-5254-a6e4-abd2e2dc3cd3.description2: This monument is a well-known benchmark, which remained the symbol of the municipal administration until a few years ago. The bronze column in the middle of the Merje Square was erected in commemoration of the Istanbul-Damascus-Mecca telegraph link. It was the line with the sultan’s Islamist policy, acting as a symbol of the Ottoman claim to leadership over Muslims. The monumental telegraph column is crowned by a model of the Istanbul Hamidiye Mosque, where every week the Sultan ‘Abdülhamid [`Abd al-Hamid II] had his visit to the mosque for Friday prayers celebrated with an imperial march-past- a demonstration of the concentrated political power of the Sultan.

7445c306-1049-5630-9a00-27983ccbe9b6.name: *Khedive Ismail*
7445c306-1049-5630-9a00-27983ccbe9b6.keywords: Ruling Family; Rulers of Egypt; The Alawiyya Dynasty; Turks; The Ruling Elite
7445c306-1049-5630-9a00-27983ccbe9b6.description2: Khedive Ismail, the fifth ruler of the Muhammad 'Ali Dynasty, Khedive of Egypt from 1863 to 1879. Ismail assumed rule over Egypt when work on the Suez Canal was ongoing. He continued the project until the Canal was opened for navigation in 1869. He established Dar al-Kutub (the National Library and Archives of Egypt) on 26 September 1870. The First Egyptian Parliament was inaugurated in 1866, during his reign.

7462293e-bc10-530b-b6dd-2b62e473b830.name: Medal of Sharif Husayn to commemorate the Battle of Ma'an
7462293e-bc10-530b-b6dd-2b62e473b830.author: Huda Kilani
7462293e-bc10-530b-b6dd-2b62e473b830.keywords: Numismatics; Arab Revolt; history of Jordan; world war I; independence; end of the Ottoman empire
7462293e-bc10-530b-b6dd-2b62e473b830.description2: Sharif Husayn ibn 'Ali commissioned this medal in 1920 to commemorate the victory of Arab fighters in the battle of Ma'an against the Ottoman forces. This medal was awarded to a man who lived during a crucial period in the history of modern Jordan.

7474b893-ab5b-5cb0-8dbf-1f03e7b4dcb1.name: Egyptianising pendant
7474b893-ab5b-5cb0-8dbf-1f03e7b4dcb1.description2: The pendant's rich design illustrates the influence of Egyptian motifs on Victorian jewellery. This piece was based on one made for the British Princess Alexandra.

7482dc94-0a66-563c-a048-83788106efb4.name: Portrait of Shaykh Yusuf al-Asir
7482dc94-0a66-563c-a048-83788106efb4.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
7482dc94-0a66-563c-a048-83788106efb4.description2: Shaykh Yusuf al-Asir was born in Saida in 1815. He studied first in Damascus then in Cairo for seven years, and excelled at Arabic language, *hadith* studies, poetry, and logic. After his studies he returned to Lebanon, going first to Saida then to Tripoli, where he stayed for 3 years. He became the Mufti of 'Akkar, and then served as the general prosecutor of Mount Lebanon for seven years. He then moved to Istanbul, where he became a professor at the Teachers College. Upon his return to Beirut he began teaching at the National College, Sagesse College, and the American School. He also published many literary and religious works in his lifetime, and edited a number of newspapers such as *Lisan al-Hal* and *Thamarat al-Funun*. He died on 28 November 1889.

74cb07f0-79d7-57eb-be13-fe55793125ae.name: Milk jar
74cb07f0-79d7-57eb-be13-fe55793125ae.description2: This butter jar with a *dagra* lid has a spherical body and rests on a small pedestal. It is decorated with a polychromatic pattern, organised in rows. Medallion shapes filled with flowers cover the lower half of the body, and the lid is also densely decorated with flowers, and framed by a lattice.

74d83fcd-b7cf-564b-9be7-40732f25938d.name: Illustration, *'A Moroccan Market'* at the Universal Exhibition, Paris
74d83fcd-b7cf-564b-9be7-40732f25938d.description: The illustration depicts a view of the “Moroccan bazaar” at the 1900 Paris Exhibition. To further inform audiences about other cultures, the Palace of Navigation and Commerce exhibited a series of historical views of Morocco’s architecture, cities and bazaars.
74d83fcd-b7cf-564b-9be7-40732f25938d.holder: National Library of the Kingdom of Morocco
74d83fcd-b7cf-564b-9be7-40732f25938d.keywords: International Exhibition; universal exposition; Exposition universelle de Paris; pavillion; exhibition building; Moorish city; exhibitions and urban spaces; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; reproduction; model; suq; curiosities; exoticism; magazine

74dafe7a-b3e7-5be6-b35d-e97ef0242008.name: The cruiser Bascir during a test voyage at sea
74dafe7a-b3e7-5be6-b35d-e97ef0242008.author: Daniela Tazzi
74dafe7a-b3e7-5be6-b35d-e97ef0242008.archival: ASLi, Cantiere Navale Luigi Orlando, cassetta 33, lastra 91
74dafe7a-b3e7-5be6-b35d-e97ef0242008.description2:
In 1890, political pressure from Italian Prime Minister Francesco Crispi secured construction of the cruiser Bascir for the Moroccan Navy for the Fratelli Orlando shipyards located in Livorno (Italy), winning against French competitors.  
The Bascir was the first cruiser built by an Italian shipyard for a foreign navy after Italian unification in 1860. It was delivered to Morocco in 1894. Among its amenities was a hamam (in Western Europe often known as Turkish Bath), expressly requested by the buyer.  
The Fratelli Orlando shipyards also built a yacht for the Khédivé of Egypt.

74e93f42-b022-5056-9d51-bed2d2eb0ca5.name: *Map of Algeria's commercial routes to the "Pays des Noirs"* \[Guinea\]
74e93f42-b022-5056-9d51-bed2d2eb0ca5.description2: Having conquered Algeria, France launched several expeditions in order to open up new trade routes from North Africa to Guinea. Europeans had great difficulty in using the internal trade routes, which were controlled by indigenous African kingdoms, so were instead limited to coastal routes.

74f17e3d-8cbd-5078-a0dc-decb3548d54d.name: *Rihlat al-ʿabdari*
74f17e3d-8cbd-5078-a0dc-decb3548d54d.description: A 15th-century manuscript copied in the early 18th century, consisting of one volume of 156 folios, written in the Moroccan calligraphic style known as *Musnad*.
74f17e3d-8cbd-5078-a0dc-decb3548d54d.keywords: Travel; journey; pilgrimage; Islamic pilgrimage; pilgrimage account; Hajj; Mecca; Medina; Holy Places; Moroccan pilgrim; pilgrim; manuscript; copy; manual copying; calligraphy; musnad

7503191f-13bf-5090-a965-b30a2948d2bd.name: Ibrahim Pasha (1789–1848)
7503191f-13bf-5090-a965-b30a2948d2bd.description2: Portrait of Ibrahim Pasha (1789–1848). As the best General under his father Muhammad 'Ali Pasha, he fought successfully against the Wahhabites, the Ottoman Army and the Greeks. In 1831 he conquered Syria and governed it until 1841. In 1848 he deposed his senile father and was declared Vice King of Egypt by Sultan Abdülmecid I.

750a06a9-2d0d-5ed4-96b6-1e5b28d3634e.name: Plan of the park Bibescu
750a06a9-2d0d-5ed4-96b6-1e5b28d3634e.description2: In 1898, Nicolae Romanescu, the mayor of Craiova (a city in Wallachia), hired French landscape architect Edouard Redont to lay out two parks in Craiova. One of them, called park Bibescu, was completed in 1903. It was built on a terrain bought by the city hall of Craiova in 1853 from Iancu Bibescu, brother of Wallachian prince Gheorghe Bibescu. The park occupied a surface of 100 ha, among which 4 were represented by water. Some of the attractions of the park included: a luxuriant vegetation, two lakes, a waterfall river, several springs, a replica of a medieval castle, a suspended bridge, a zoo. There also existed restaurants and cafes, a library, an exhibition hall, a ceremony hall, a hippodrome, a velodrome and a pier. In 1900 the plan of park Bibescu was awarded a gold medal at the universal exposition of Paris.

7524342a-3c1f-54f5-982b-64c649a18029.name: A pupil praised by his teacher. Picture from a board game known as the Game of the Goose
7524342a-3c1f-54f5-982b-64c649a18029.archival: AS Biella, Archivi del Centro Studi Torrione, Raccolta, mazzo 26 fasc. 2
7524342a-3c1f-54f5-982b-64c649a18029.third_name: 'Il nuovo giuoco della vita umana': 'Prendi il premio e fa ragione. Che allo studio è nuovo sprone'

752e7052-acb6-5576-bba8-5bfde920d54a.name: Jerash
752e7052-acb6-5576-bba8-5bfde920d54a.author: Mohammad Najjar
752e7052-acb6-5576-bba8-5bfde920d54a.history: Jerash has a long occupational history that starts in prehistoric times and goes through various historical periods until the present. During the Greco-Roman period, Jerash was a prominent member of the Decapolis. It was part of the Islamic Empire starting from the 7th century AD. The small village of Jerash was identified by Ceetzen as the Decapolis town of Gerasa by Ulrich Jasper Ceetzen in his journey from Damascus to Jerusalem in 1806.
752e7052-acb6-5576-bba8-5bfde920d54a.keywords: Rediscovery; identification; Decapolis; Greco-Roman period; Seetzen
752e7052-acb6-5576-bba8-5bfde920d54a.description2: Jerash is probably the most famous heritage town in Jordan after Petra. It is one of the best preserved Greco-Roman provincial towns from the Roman/Byzantine period. The western part of the town was completely preserved and protected. It shows a city planned with fortification walls, gates, paved and colonnaded streets, temples, theatres, the hippodrome and many churches with mosaic floors.

757957ce-46d4-5799-8792-5f05be3e1e3f.name: Hanging (*sitara*) for the Mosque of the Prophet, Medina al-Munawwarah
757957ce-46d4-5799-8792-5f05be3e1e3f.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation /Sharjah Museums Authority
757957ce-46d4-5799-8792-5f05be3e1e3f.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
757957ce-46d4-5799-8792-5f05be3e1e3f.materials: Silk, cotton, silver and silver gilt metal thread
757957ce-46d4-5799-8792-5f05be3e1e3f.description2: This green and black silk textile is richly embroidered with silver and gilt metal threads. The centre displays six cartouches with thuluth inscriptions, followed below by a black niche with a central lamp motif. A border with trefoil scrolling surrounds the central panel. The inscriptions used on this textile clearly indicate that this textile was intended for the Prophet’s Mosque in Madina. The four main cartouches contain verse 56 from chapter 33 (Al-Ahzab) of the Holy Qur’an: ‘Allah sends His Salat (merciful blessings) on the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), and also His angels. O you who believe! Send your Salat on him and greet him with the Islamic way of greeting’. The inscriptions in the two cartouches below state that this curtain was ordered by the Ottoman sultan Abd al-Hamid II (1293 H/1876 AD – 1327 H/1909 AD) and renewed by Efendi Abbas Hilmi, the last Khedive Pasha of Ottoman Egypt (1291 H/ 1874 AD – 1350 H/ 1931 AD) in 1321 H/ 1903 AD.

75891604-fdb8-540e-af25-a6509a9103f7.name: *Cairo: houses and gardens in the French quarter.* Flaubert in the foreground.
75891604-fdb8-540e-af25-a6509a9103f7.description2: The writer Gustave Flaubert lived in Egypt for three years from 1849 to 1851 with his friend Maxime Du Camp. He saw and experienced many new things during this time, travelling to Egypt, Beirut, Jerusalem and Damascus. Although Gustave Flaubert did not like being photographed, Maxime du Camp was able to take this snap of him in Cairo.

75ba6380-c797-5b14-a144-d7546e1f3572.name: *Album de la Dobrudgea* by Anatol Magrin
75ba6380-c797-5b14-a144-d7546e1f3572.description2: In 1878 Anatole Magrin was appointed secretary of the French consul to Constanța and then became vice-consul and consul. He married a Romanian woman and eventually settled in Constanța. He was the owner of the first photo studio in the city and later became the official photographer of king Carol I, who decorated him with the Romanian order of the Crown. He is considered to be the first artist to take photographs of Dobruja, a province in the south-east of Romania which was restored to Romania in 1878, after more than three centuries of Ottoman domination. Magrin’s photo album dedicated to Dobruja contains 56 photos of landscapes and people, some of which depict Turkish and Tatar communities (the Tatars and Turks represent one of Dobruja’s main ethnic minorities).

75e14725-44b8-5dc0-b587-1eba09b78832.name: Yıldız Palace Theatre
75e14725-44b8-5dc0-b587-1eba09b78832.notice: This is an unedited Database entry and may contain errors and inconsistencies in spelling. We are working to raise the funds required to complete the editing; should you wish to contribute please visit our [Support page](https://www.museumwnf.org/atrium_support.php).
75e14725-44b8-5dc0-b587-1eba09b78832.history:
Yildiz Palace, which is the last architectural example of Turkish Ottoman palace, is located on the Yildiz hill in the district of Besiktas. Sultan Ahmed I was the first to build a pavilion, over this land registered at the time to the Private treasury of the Ottoman Sultan as a hunting place sultans beginning during the reign of Suleiman the Magnificent (1520-1566).  
The main construction in the palace started in the period of Sultan Abdulhamid II (1876-1909) and it was called Saray-i Humayun (Central palace). During this period the palace comprised of buildings for private use of the sultan as well as buildings, allocated for the officials, repair shops and carpentry like repairing shop, carpenter’s shop and the buildings of culture and art such as theatre, museum and library. The Palace begun to serve as a museum under the name of Directorate of the Museum of Yildiz Palace since 1993.
75e14725-44b8-5dc0-b587-1eba09b78832.description2: This is the only palace theatre that can be seen today. It was built by the Sultan Abdulhamid II for the visit of German Imperial Kaiser Wilhem II, together with the Shale Kiosk in 1899. Three walls of the theatre hall, of a small rectangular plan, are surrounded by the boxes carried by columns. The box that faced the stage belonged to the sultan. The walls were decorated with hand-drawn and the ceiling was endowed with gold star patterns on the blue ground. Oil paintings are hung around the stage. In addition to performer groups consisting of Italian and Turkish artists, foreign theatre groups visiting Istanbul and some local artists were also occasionally allowed to the palace. Among them, there were French artists, Sarah Bernhardt and Coquelain Cadet and Russian singer Feodor Chaliapin, local artists Gullu Agop Efendi and Nashit Efendi. In the theatre the operas such as Barber of Sevil, Norma, Rigoletto, Traviata, Carmen and Aida were put on stage. The original wardrobes representing the period of use are exhibited in a section of the theatre.

75ecd1ca-690e-54ec-ae5c-583c92e90430.name: *Street Scene in Cairo*
75ecd1ca-690e-54ec-ae5c-583c92e90430.description2: *Street Scene in Cairo* from the Austrian painter Alphons Mielich. Mielich specialized in Oriental scenes, which he sold to aristocratic Austrian tourists as mementos of their trips to Egypt.

75ede8fe-76f3-5385-bdc5-f85fce889190.name: Quran
75ede8fe-76f3-5385-bdc5-f85fce889190.holder: Musée des Arts Islamiques de Kairouan
75ede8fe-76f3-5385-bdc5-f85fce889190.description2: These are two pages from a calligraphic Quran written in maghrebi script, dating to the 18th century, and a good example of the symbiosis between Hispano-Islamic and Ottoman influences. Although the script and the colour of the diacritics are typically maghrebi, the decoration and the frontispiece of the fatiha, which is adorned with floral motifs, shows the clear influence of the Ottoman school, which was itself inspired by Iranian art. The vowels are written in red, the *sukun* and the *shadda* in blue, the *hamza* in yellow or gold and the *hamza al-wasl* in green.

760fa584-9cdb-54e9-a484-39638db07064.name: Moorish dagger
760fa584-9cdb-54e9-a484-39638db07064.description: This dagger, along with other pieces, was taken by Salvador de Foronda, a member of the Spanish Army, awarded for his actions in battle. He was a relative of the Marquis of Cerralbo and donated to his uncle’s museum these exceptional pieces in 1918. This piece is enriched with damascene work, and the fabric rope still holds some metallic threads. This dagger was a traditional self-defence tool for North African men.
760fa584-9cdb-54e9-a484-39638db07064.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes

7625cc1a-04cd-541e-97b3-01fa3eac5fdf.name: *Dolmabahçe Palace Portal Under Construction*
7625cc1a-04cd-541e-97b3-01fa3eac5fdf.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
7625cc1a-04cd-541e-97b3-01fa3eac5fdf.keywords: Dolmabahçe Palace; Ottoman architecture; close-up from Dolmahçe Palace portal
7625cc1a-04cd-541e-97b3-01fa3eac5fdf.description2: Lacan heaps particular praise on the artist's panorama taken from Beyazıt Tower as well as on his photograph of the architectural elements of Galata Tower, the Hagia Sophia, the Mosque of Sultan Ahmed I, and Dolmabahçe Sarayı. Robertson’s Istanbul photographs are concerned primarily with the city’s historical monuments. They reveal the city’s magnificent Byzantine and Ottoman structures from different angles and with close-ups taken in an approach that is usually quite aesthetic.

763d6e83-1558-5793-8fef-f63ff6bf1c79.name: Water flask
763d6e83-1558-5793-8fef-f63ff6bf1c79.description2: Flask of zamzam water collected by Sir Richard Francis Burton during his visit in disguise to Mecca. Burton was a diplomat, explorer and author. He published a translation of the *Arabian Nights*.

763ee7df-878c-58a5-84f4-122b7dc9a7e0.name: Helmet
763ee7df-878c-58a5-84f4-122b7dc9a7e0.holder: Palais de la Rose – Musée de l’Armée
763ee7df-878c-58a5-84f4-122b7dc9a7e0.author: Bechir Yazidi
763ee7df-878c-58a5-84f4-122b7dc9a7e0.keywords: Tunisian army; Musée de l'Armée; Palais de la Rose
763ee7df-878c-58a5-84f4-122b7dc9a7e0.description2: This Islamic helmet, known as a "casque de Rostem", has Persian origins. It is 21 cm long from its tip to the joint at the front, the serrated iron mesh is 30 cm long, and the front perimeter is 70 cm long. This helmet is lavishly decorated, coming to two points on either side, and with an Ottoman point at the front and floral motifs all over the surface.

76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.name: Photograph of the Old Railway Station in Skopje
76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.holder: Museum of the City of Skopje
76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.author: Zoja Bogdanovska, historian, Museum of the City of Skopje
76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.keywords: Railroad; railway; railway station; Ottoman Balkans
76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.third_name: Fotografija na starata zeleznichka stanica vo Skopje
76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.description2: The first railroad in Macedonia was the track running from Thessalonica via Skopje to Belgrade. Its construction was financed with foreign investments and began in 1871. The track to Skopje was finished in 1873. The Skopje-Mitrovica railway line was completed in 1878. In 1888, it was connected to Serbian railways at the border crossing Zibevche near Vranje.

768fa90e-d16c-5110-90a0-a312d93927ce.name: Rome: Piazza della Repubblica (previously called Piazza Esedra), with the fountain of the Naiads; in the background, Termini railway station
768fa90e-d16c-5110-90a0-a312d93927ce.holder: Central Institute for Cataloguing and Documentation (ICCD)
