76a1492a-0881-5283-861f-8c45c2c06097.name: L'École de la Rue du Pacha (inside the classroom)
76a1492a-0881-5283-861f-8c45c2c06097.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
76a1492a-0881-5283-861f-8c45c2c06097.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
76a1492a-0881-5283-861f-8c45c2c06097.description2: This photograph shows a classroom of young Muslim girls at l'École Louise-Renée-Millet (renamed l'École de la Rue du Pacha in 1911/1912) in 1908. The presence of a *moueddeb* and a French teacher is notable. The *moueddeb* would have taught the principles of the Quran and elementary Arabic (reading, writing, arithmetic), whereas the French teacher would have covered the French education (literature, history, science and hygiene), as well as needlework (embroidery, sewing, lace). For the younger pupils of the school this classroom was the door to the world and one which allowed them to explore life. Young girls of this time often lived very sheltered lives, shut away in their homes without the opportunity to learn. Their education was usually limited to housework and needlework, either at home or at a Dar el-Maalma, a local atelier run by an old housewife.

76c35457-f8ff-5bff-9a85-a95ba8087f82.name: Advertisement from the International Exhibition in Rome 1911
76c35457-f8ff-5bff-9a85-a95ba8087f82.holder: Central Institute for Ethno-Anthropology, National Museum of Arts and Popular Traditions
76c35457-f8ff-5bff-9a85-a95ba8087f82.author: Marina Minozzi
76c35457-f8ff-5bff-9a85-a95ba8087f82.keywords: Universal exposition; Esposizione universale di Roma; art exhibition; magazine; anthropology;  ethnography; exhibitions and urban spaces; city; social change; internal migration; urban space; rural space; post-unitarian Italian society; popular traditions
76c35457-f8ff-5bff-9a85-a95ba8087f82.copyright: Copyright image: Roma, Istituto Centrale per la Demoetnoantropologia, ICDE, Archivio storico.
76c35457-f8ff-5bff-9a85-a95ba8087f82.description2: During the International Exhibition of Fine Arts in 1911, in a green area near the Tiber river within Rome’s boundaries, exhibitions of regions and ethnography were staged. This show was meant to celebrate ethnography as a new science and, at the same time, to highlight the habits and customs of the different regions of Italy, especially on the occasion of the 50th anniversary celebrations of the unification of the Italian state. A consequence of the exhibition was an enlargement of the city of Rom and massive urban growth. At the same time, upon the Rassegna Illustrata dell’Esposizione commercial pavilions were destined to later become restaurants, shops and pubs. All of them were clearly inspired by the popularity of orientalism.
76c35457-f8ff-5bff-9a85-a95ba8087f82.holding_institution_org: Istituto Centrale per la Demoetnoantropologia, Museo Nazionale delle Arti e Tradizioni Popolari

7799c614-d39a-57bf-8c89-ac0c4d03ec70.name: The Promotional Exhibition of the Alsace and Lorraine Society in the Algerian Section [Paris Exhibition, 1878]
7799c614-d39a-57bf-8c89-ac0c4d03ec70.author: Marina Minozzi
7799c614-d39a-57bf-8c89-ac0c4d03ec70.archival: *L'Esposizione di Parigi del 1878 illustrata*, Sonzogno Editore, 1878, p. 88
7799c614-d39a-57bf-8c89-ac0c4d03ec70.keywords: Exposition universelle de Paris; industrialisation; exhibition building; Moorish city; exhibitions and urban spaces; Moorish style; Islamic architecture; reinterpretation; exoticism; reproduction; model; magazine; French architecture

7799c614-d39a-57bf-8c89-ac0c4d03ec70.third_name: *La mostra della Società promotrice degli Alsaziani e Lorenesi nella Sezione Algerina*
7799c614-d39a-57bf-8c89-ac0c4d03ec70.description2: Paris, International Exhibition, 1878. In one of the streets in the Trocadero Pavilion buildings were constructed based on those built in Algeria after the French-Prussian war (1870–71) by the Society Protecting Alsatian and Lorenese People for refugees coming from France. The interior shows all the territories donated to the Protecting Society and in the lower part the villages of Hanssonvillers and Bacckhalfa.

779c654a-aa90-53f1-a122-5dbb8e302070.name: *Interior of a school, Cairo*
779c654a-aa90-53f1-a122-5dbb8e302070.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
779c654a-aa90-53f1-a122-5dbb8e302070.keywords: education; school; teaching; children; childhood; kuttab
779c654a-aa90-53f1-a122-5dbb8e302070.description2: In this scene depicted by Lewis, the Hoja or teacher is listening to his assistant rhythmically reciting the Quran (while beating time), as some children pay attention and others not. Some commentators have regarded the presence of a young girl as inauthentic, but young girls were able to attend Quran schools, according to the artist Charles de Tournemine, the scholar Edward Lane and the translator Richard Burton. Certainly not all women were illiterate, and some female descendants of the prophet were noted for their ability to read and recite the scriptures.

77bba0ac-27a1-5d3b-a2cc-0a2a96d87a2c.name: Advertisement for the automoble company Lancia & C. Fabbrica Italiana Automobili
77bba0ac-27a1-5d3b-a2cc-0a2a96d87a2c.archival: *Il Secolo Illustrato*, Anno V, n. 1, gennaio 1917

77cb95e6-9ec9-5628-a3f9-c509f77d9e94.name: Astronomical Observatory of Lisbon Polytechnic School
77cb95e6-9ec9-5628-a3f9-c509f77d9e94.holder: National Museum of Natural History and Science (MUHNAC) / Museums of the University of Lisbon
77cb95e6-9ec9-5628-a3f9-c509f77d9e94.author: António Perestrelo de Matos (MUHNAC-UL)
77cb95e6-9ec9-5628-a3f9-c509f77d9e94.history: Teaching of Astronomy existed in the Lisbon Polytechnic School since its creation in 1837. It was aimed at providing training for cartography surveys. Initially, teaching was done at the so-called Marine Tower (1837–1843) and then at the Royal Maritime Observatory (1843–1875). In 1876, a new Observatory was inaugurated in the Garden. However, the first building had low stability and a new one had to be constructed. Astronomy teaching started in 1898. Until the 1930s, the Observatory was autonomous within the School, but later it was put under the jurisdiction of the Department of Mathematics. In 1999 teaching was discontinued and the Observatory was integrated in the Museum.
77cb95e6-9ec9-5628-a3f9-c509f77d9e94.keywords: Observatory; Scientific Heritage; Teaching; Astronomy; National Museum of Natural History and Science; University of Lisbon
77cb95e6-9ec9-5628-a3f9-c509f77d9e94.architects: Vitor Augusto Gomes da Encarnação (19th century) and José Cecílio da Costa (19th century)
77cb95e6-9ec9-5628-a3f9-c509f77d9e94.third_name: Observatório Astronómico da Escola Politécnica de Lisboa
77cb95e6-9ec9-5628-a3f9-c509f77d9e94.description2: The Astronomical Observatory is a teaching observatory. It includes one classroom and three observation domes. It dates from 1898 and it encompasses three buildings. The main building is octagonal in shape, located in the upper part of the Botanical Garden. Inside, it has a classroom and the Meridian Room, all covered in wood panels. Another building, with three-floors, used to host the library, more classrooms and workshops. The Observatory collection includes c. 150 scientific instruments, including several apparatuses built in house by Portuguese astronomer Campos Rodrigues (1836–1919).

77e11861-c38b-50a8-8fb9-b72467f69e2b.name: Algerian Pavilion in the Trocadéro Park [Paris Exhibition, 1878]
77e11861-c38b-50a8-8fb9-b72467f69e2b.author: Marina Minozzi
77e11861-c38b-50a8-8fb9-b72467f69e2b.archival: *L'Esposizione di Parigi del 1878 illustrata*, Sonzogno Editore, 1878, p. 39
77e11861-c38b-50a8-8fb9-b72467f69e2b.keywords: Exposition universelle de Paris; industrialisation; exhibition building; Moorish city; exhibitions and urban spaces; Moorish style; Islamic architecture; reinterpretation; exoticism; reproduction; model; magazine
77e11861-c38b-50a8-8fb9-b72467f69e2b.copyright: Copyright image: Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale, Roma.
77e11861-c38b-50a8-8fb9-b72467f69e2b.description2: At the International Exhibition in Paris, 1878, the Algerian Pavilion was designed by the architect M. Wable, who was appointed by General Chanzy. The building represents one of the greatest proofs of French colonisation policy. The front-door, four metres wide, is a copy from the ‘Ubbad Mosque of Sidi Bumadyan in Tlemcen, and is richly decorated with enamelled majolica and arabesque decorations. The decorations of the minaret echo the tower in ruins from the mosque of Mansoura, 1,200 square metres wide. The pavilion was meant to show the productive potential of the colony to the French capitalists.

77f52d4b-ff6b-552e-acdb-df8edbe68721.name: Ismail, Khedive of Egypt (1830–1895)
77f52d4b-ff6b-552e-acdb-df8edbe68721.keywords: Ismail, Khedive of Egypt; Suez Channel; Emperor Franz Joseph
77f52d4b-ff6b-552e-acdb-df8edbe68721.description2: Portrait of Ismail, Khedive of Egypt (1830–1895), who financed the construction of the Suez Canal. Because of the enormous costs of the building and his reform measures, Egypt's debt rose from three million pounds sterling to 100 million pounds sterling. In 1875 Egypt was bankrupt and Ismail Pasha was forced to sell 176,602 shares to Great Britain for 3,976,582 pounds sterling. Egypt came under financial control of France and Great Britain.

77f5feea-8867-5c80-82a2-d05e34b6fff5.name: Colonial farms
77f5feea-8867-5c80-82a2-d05e34b6fff5.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
77f5feea-8867-5c80-82a2-d05e34b6fff5.history: French colonialism brought significant changes to Tunisians' lifestyles, which consequently affected the country's rural architecture. The colonial settlers built their homes as soon as they arrived, and so Italian and French residential architecture evolved from a small hut to a large house. These old, often large, farmhouses punctuate the landscape with their red roofs and cellars, easily distinguishable against the green of the forest. They remind us that the great Italo-French rivalry was triggered by the competition over the best land, as viticulture was their main economic activity. Single-crop farming was used for these grapevines, which were almost entirely wine varieties.
77f5feea-8867-5c80-82a2-d05e34b6fff5.description2: This farmhouse, belonging to the French winemaker of Béja, can be distinguished by its white walls and industrial red tiles, stamped to show the name of their maker and place of origin. The tiles are overlapping to protect the house from the rainfall and snowfall. Contrary to the traditional farmhouses which were inward facing, this settler farmhouse has large windows on its façade and is built on a empty plot of land. The house is east facing and rectangular-based, with four annexes dedicated to the farm's needs, most importantly pressing the grapes and storing them in the cellars.

77f7d1f5-f298-526e-8bfa-21c5a75d09f2.name: *4 June 1913, Gand, \[pavillion from\] the French Protectorate in Morocco \[Exposition Universelle et Internationale\]*
77f7d1f5-f298-526e-8bfa-21c5a75d09f2.description2: In 1913, Gand (Belgium) hosted the 28th Exposition Universelle (world fair). Like France, Belgium gave pride of place to its colonies. During its universal expositions (world fairs), France tended to exhibit a number of colonial pavilions, whose architecture and "exoticism" fascinated visitors. The "Pavilion from the French Protectorate in Morocco" was built to show off the recent (1912) Moroccan protectorate.

77fc77a2-454c-58fa-aa16-959029610bb1.name: Women's tunic (*Gomlek*)
77fc77a2-454c-58fa-aa16-959029610bb1.author: Nada Andonovska
77fc77a2-454c-58fa-aa16-959029610bb1.keywords: Yörük community; nomads; Turkish; tunic; costume; embroidery; wedding; marriage
77fc77a2-454c-58fa-aa16-959029610bb1.materials: White canvas decorated with embroidery og varied wool, as well as silver and gold wrapped thread
77fc77a2-454c-58fa-aa16-959029610bb1.description2: The enclave of the Turkish Yoruk community in Macedonia living in the mountain villages of Dojran – Valandovo and Radovish – and the Shtip region is a genuine treasure of tangible and intangible heritage that adds to the diversity of traditional culture in Macedonia. In general terms, the traditional outfit of Yoruk women in Macedonia is distinguished with exceptional colouring and application of varied elements in all articles of clothing. This bridal attire preserves some of the traditions in clothing and embellishment of Yoruk women in Macedonia in the 19th century and the early 20th century. The tunic is made of white canvas and modestly decorated by embroidery of two short vertical strips above the lower hem.

7821de49-1833-5656-935a-de7859fecc1b.name: Jacket
7821de49-1833-5656-935a-de7859fecc1b.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
7821de49-1833-5656-935a-de7859fecc1b.description2: Yusuf Bey Karam's jacket, probably worn during the winter months. It is made of dark blue wool, with floral patterns embroidered in black thread and bordered by a black ribbon. The lining is made of a mustard-coloured fabric.

78482946-b8d7-5fca-913f-fd0e2dc38b4a.name: Map (*la Barbarie*)
78482946-b8d7-5fca-913f-fd0e2dc38b4a.description: A 19th-century map of the Moroccan Empire and the states of Algiers, Tunis and Tripoli. Its toponyms are written in French. As the original was monochrome, evidently the *Atlas*’s original owner manually embellished the borders between countries and administrative boundaries.
78482946-b8d7-5fca-913f-fd0e2dc38b4a.holder: National Library of the Kingdom of Morocco
78482946-b8d7-5fca-913f-fd0e2dc38b4a.archival: Published in *Atlas universel de géographie ancienne et moderne à l'usage des pensionnats*

7878caf5-22b7-5137-93bb-b21eeb4df6c5.description: Earrings form triple crescent, central lamellar and mobile; the side streets are filigree, stuffed with coils of wire, each with small mounts. It is decorated with filigree fans.

789458d3-49a6-51d8-9be2-897051433c19.name: Layard Freedom Casket
789458d3-49a6-51d8-9be2-897051433c19.description2: A commemorative piece custom made to honour Austen Henry Layard. Layard was famous for excavating Nineveh. Closely modelled on the sculptures discovered by Layard.

78bd5171-0d47-55a4-9494-234cd6b94735.name: Street lamps produced by the Gaetano Esposito factory (Naples)
78bd5171-0d47-55a4-9494-234cd6b94735.archival: AS Enna, Archivio Storico di Castrogiovanni (Enna) b.30 c.36
78bd5171-0d47-55a4-9494-234cd6b94735.third_name: Nuova fonderia di ferro ed opificio di Gaetano Esposito, Napoli

78eecb65-6040-5c83-8995-b8c35cb4d3a6.name: Nusretiye Mosque and Tophane Square
78eecb65-6040-5c83-8995-b8c35cb4d3a6.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; James Robertson
78eecb65-6040-5c83-8995-b8c35cb4d3a6.description2: James Robertson arrived in Istanbul in 1840 and started work as head etcher in Ottoman Mint. He began taking photos of Istanbul soon after. There was previously a mosque located on the site of the current Mosque, which was known as the Mosque of the Artillery Barracks (Tophane-i Amire Arabacilar Kislasi Camii) built by Selim III (1789-1807). When that mosque was destroyed by the Firuzaga fire, the Nusretiye Mosque, located on Meclis-i Mebusan Street in the Tophane District of Beyoglu, was built on the order of Sultan Mahmud (1784-1839), and was constructed by the Krikor Amira Balyan. The construction lasted from 1823 to 1826 and was broadly restored between the years of 1955 and 1958, and partially again between 1980 and 1992. While its architecture is influenced by Islamic elements, it retains a Baroque style, making it unique to the city.

78ffdbad-67b9-5e33-ad6b-19aeeee48f10.name: Portrait of Metri el-Murr
78ffdbad-67b9-5e33-ad6b-19aeeee48f10.holder: Lebanese National Higher Conservatory of Music
78ffdbad-67b9-5e33-ad6b-19aeeee48f10.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
78ffdbad-67b9-5e33-ad6b-19aeeee48f10.description2: Mitri al-Murr was a famous musician, well known throughout the Arab world. He was a renowned pianist and wrote a number of musical poems that are still known today.

7935012a-92f2-5749-a878-3506ddbb8dc4.name: *The Temple of Venus*
7935012a-92f2-5749-a878-3506ddbb8dc4.author: Marina Minozzi
7935012a-92f2-5749-a878-3506ddbb8dc4.keywords: Italian painters; genre scene; Naples; Rome; Florence; Macchiaioli; Verismo; history painting; celebration of the past; Roman past; archaeology; documentation; post-unitarian Italian society; exhibition; exposition; exoticism
7935012a-92f2-5749-a878-3506ddbb8dc4.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
7935012a-92f2-5749-a878-3506ddbb8dc4.description2: Giuseppe Sciuti initially worked in his hometown as a decorator, then moved to Naples and Florence. In Florence, the artist works with the Macchiaioli painters upon subjects linked to the “Verismo”, or realist, movement, and while in Naples he worked on history paintings. In Rome he decorated public and private buildings with historical and allegorical themes, pagan rituals and scenes from the Greek and Roman tradition, highly valued by the international market. *The Temple of Venus* is an archeological reconstruction of a sacred interior showing an offering to the goddess Venus for the beginning of Spring. The painting is part of the group of works by the artist presented at the Exposition in Milan in 1871, Nice in 1884 and London in 1888.
7935012a-92f2-5749-a878-3506ddbb8dc4.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

794483b6-f573-5ea4-9de3-b7a65c779566.name: Coronation of His Majesty King Charles X, in Rheims,  29 May 1825
794483b6-f573-5ea4-9de3-b7a65c779566.description2: Charles X was Louis XVI's younger brother. During the revolution, Charles (then the Count of Artois) emigrated in search of support from other European royal courts. He disapproved of Louis XVIII's pragmatism, and following his death advocated a return to the Ancien Régime. He had himself crowned in Reims, like his ancestors, although the cost of this grandiose ceremony was the subject of great controversy.

795bacd6-ac66-5eca-9599-838de1b288ee.name: *Natürmort*
795bacd6-ac66-5eca-9599-838de1b288ee.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
795bacd6-ac66-5eca-9599-838de1b288ee.keywords: Painting; Halil Paşa; orientalist Turkish painters; still life
795bacd6-ac66-5eca-9599-838de1b288ee.description2: The foundation of Turkish painting drawing influence from western tradition was laid when the Naval Academy opened in 1795. In the period of Selim II, painting lessons were given at the academy. And course attendees were sent abroad after to develop their painting techniques and skills. These painters, who were known as the soldier-painters, worked in Gerome’s, Cabanel’s and Boulanger’s workshops in Paris. Halil Paşa provided a unique distinction to the analysis of impressionist light and colour. Because of his qualified knowledge about anatomy and his interest in depicting the human figure, Halil Paşa has a unique place in Turkish Art History.

79791fd6-4a63-5950-8b88-e5b802feebd3.name: Research on the location of Carthage (with 15 illustrated pages)
79791fd6-4a63-5950-8b88-e5b802feebd3.description2: Christian Théodore Falbe, captain of a Danish ship and explorer, was the Tunisian consul before becoming  delegate for the Société pour l'Exploration de Carthage. Fable dedicated himself to developing a new map of Tunis, which required the use of newly developed techniques. He had to use his cunning to be able to draw these plans, as he had aroused the suspicion of the Tunisian population, and ended up doing many of them from the roofs of neighbouring consulates. His pioneering work on Carthage should be seen as part of a greater international movement which had recently taken great interest in this destroyed and long-forgotten city.

79c9d2ac-a647-52e8-a549-a07530d6d611.name: Portrait of Rhigas Pheraios, the foremost figure of the Greek Enlightenment, endeavoured to underpin the revolt of the Greeks by bringing about its intellectual and spiritual awakening

79fded3c-fc12-5fa3-bff4-6820a231b3e4.name: Marriage shawl
79fded3c-fc12-5fa3-bff4-6820a231b3e4.holder: Musée des Arts et Traditions Populaires
79fded3c-fc12-5fa3-bff4-6820a231b3e4.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
79fded3c-fc12-5fa3-bff4-6820a231b3e4.description2: This loose marriage shawl is decorated with various symbols of fertility. Two large rectangles of red wool are sewn together, and their joining seam is ornately decorated with gold embroidery. The decorations are spread out across the whole cloth, forming a strip of finely woven motifs in the centre, which is surrounded by various traditional figures and patterns. The human figures are characteristic of the (often enigmatic) decorative arts of the towns of El Jem and Ouerdanine, and feature here in addition to the more common motifs such as the fish, the hand, disks, circles, diamonds, crescents, the dove and the camel.

7a02499c-fb97-5223-b10c-18ecc783aeae.name: *Map to illustrate the Route of David Roberts Esq. R. A. in the Holy Land, Petrea and Syria*
7a02499c-fb97-5223-b10c-18ecc783aeae.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
7a02499c-fb97-5223-b10c-18ecc783aeae.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
7a02499c-fb97-5223-b10c-18ecc783aeae.description2: This map shows the areas visited by the Scottish artist David Roberts (1796-1864) during the 11 months he spent travelling between Egypt, the Sinai, Jordan and Palestine in 1838/39. Roberts subsequently became famous for his meticulous lithographs of Egypt, the 'Holy Land' and other Near Eastern regions, hardly touched as yet by British artists at the time. Maps like this one were provided with each complete set of his lithographs later to help trace the locations Roberts visited and sketched.Roberts' depictions were to become extremely important tools in popularising the ‘Holy Land’ in 19th century British imagination, thus encouraging ever more people to visit, map and survey it. His work also helped to underpin the aspirations and objectives of the Palestinian Exploration Fund, founded in 1865.

7a05190e-1927-5037-ba2d-10e15038ab09.name: Dar al-Makina
7a05190e-1927-5037-ba2d-10e15038ab09.history: Built under the auspices of Sultan al-Hasan I in 1890, this impressive factory building is located in the west of Fez at al-Michour Jedid. One of the most important works of this Sultan in the royal city of Fez, which was constructed for the production of weapons in cooperation with the Italians.
7a05190e-1927-5037-ba2d-10e15038ab09.keywords: Factory; industry; Italian industrialists; Italians in Morocco; Italians in North Africa; migration; work; urban changes; city; urban space; Moroccan city; Islamic city; traditional city; changes in urban space; urban planning; plan; European architecture; European influence; artistic exchanges; war; weapons; arms; protectorate; industrialisation
7a05190e-1927-5037-ba2d-10e15038ab09.description2: Dar al-Makina consists of three distinct areas with several partition walls, but also some extensions and doors for communication with the outside. In fact, the interior of the main building is dominated by a forest of pillars, which together form a square section that connects with the upper level of horseshoe arches and stilted and round arches. Building materials used for the elevation of these elements consist primarily of traditional solid brick, built according to the ancient technique known in Fez, with mortar of lime and sand, and rarely, in some of the load-bearing walls, with stone fragments. The entirety is covered internally with a smooth coating of lime and sand which is whitewashed.

7a167ce5-50e1-5265-b688-b3c912f172b7.name: *View of Valletta from Fort Manoel (Malta)*
7a167ce5-50e1-5265-b688-b3c912f172b7.author: Marina Minozzi
7a167ce5-50e1-5265-b688-b3c912f172b7.keywords: Historical events in painting; realism; landscape painting; travel; travellers; travelling artist; applied arts; Italian travellers; Italian painters; Ottoman empire; Moldavia; Greece; Malta
7a167ce5-50e1-5265-b688-b3c912f172b7.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
7a167ce5-50e1-5265-b688-b3c912f172b7.third_name: *Veduta di La Valletta dal Forte Emanuele (Malta)*
7a167ce5-50e1-5265-b688-b3c912f172b7.description2: Filippo Palizzi came from a numerous family and along with his three brothers, all painters, introduced in Italy a realistic style of painting which breaks away from academic tradition of religious, mythological or history painting. He depicts real landscapes, people and animals. Filippo Palizzi painted *The view of Valletta from Forte Emanuele* during his long travel through Moldavia, Turkey, Greece and Malta. In Naples he was the director of the Academy of Fine Art and also worked at the organisation of the schools of industrial arts.

7a241c8e-d68e-5a99-8f6d-768433eb938e.name: Map of the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia
7a241c8e-d68e-5a99-8f6d-768433eb938e.description2: This map of Lombardy-Venetia from 1827 shows postal routes and information concerning the costs of travelling with the post coaches.

7a66ac7e-e537-5099-bcf6-d574ade2e10c.name: Egyptianising vase
7a66ac7e-e537-5099-bcf6-d574ade2e10c.description2: Glass vase with stylised lotus leaves and buds decoration. Inspired by an Egyptian faience lotus cup in the British Museum.

7a673124-7bea-543e-8cdf-59c06cdc2216.name: Record of the marriage between the Egyptian governmental official Paul Draneht Bey, aged 55, and the Italian Adele Casati, aged 19, celebrated in Oggebbio (Italy) in 1873
7a673124-7bea-543e-8cdf-59c06cdc2216.author: Massimiliano Cremona, Ignazio Galella
7a673124-7bea-543e-8cdf-59c06cdc2216.archival: AS VB, Comune di Oggebbio, Registro Atti di Matrimonio, vol. 523/24, firme degli sposi
7a673124-7bea-543e-8cdf-59c06cdc2216.description2: Apparently, Adelaide Casati and her sister Margarita attended the premiere of the Aida in Cairo (24 December 1871). Their father, Filippo, was participating in the performance as a cello player. In Cairo, the two Casati sisters met their future husbands, respectively, Paul Draneht, and the Greek banker, Joannis Sinadino (who acted as witness in the marriage between Paul Draneht and Adelaide Casati). Both men moved to live in Oggebbio, Italy, when Paul Draneht bought a villa there.

7a6f5cad-f74c-5502-95b2-2068560418a6.name: The Port From The Galata Tower
7a6f5cad-f74c-5502-95b2-2068560418a6.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; Abdullah Brothers
7a6f5cad-f74c-5502-95b2-2068560418a6.description2: Abdullah Brothers is the name given to three men of Armenian origin, Viçen (1820-1902), Hovsep Abdullahyan (1830-1908) and Kevork (1839-1918) who started the art of photography in Turkey. For 40 years they photographed the people of Istanbul, landscapes, various political and social events, and prepared albums of historical and cultural values, as well as monuments.

7a7a871e-70a7-5428-91b9-c5c8fd581ce1.name: Ishtar Gate
7a7a871e-70a7-5428-91b9-c5c8fd581ce1.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
7a7a871e-70a7-5428-91b9-c5c8fd581ce1.author: Stefan Weber
7a7a871e-70a7-5428-91b9-c5c8fd581ce1.second_name: Main gate of the ancient city of Babylon, reconstruction with many original pieces
7a7a871e-70a7-5428-91b9-c5c8fd581ce1.description2: The Museum of the Ancient Near East, dating back to 1899, considers itself as a place where cultures of the region can be studied, but also as the custodian of the rich excavation finds from German field studies. The most eminent examples of the custodial work are the Processional Way and the Ishtar Gate of ancient Babylon, of whom only the foundational walls were exposed during excavations in 1902. Only after thousands of fragments had been put together, the reconstruction could be integrated into the museum.

7a8205d2-2d3a-59d3-b4bb-d33dce902734.name: Handwritten poem by Constantinos Kavafis
7a8205d2-2d3a-59d3-b4bb-d33dce902734.author: Maria Dimitriadou
7a8205d2-2d3a-59d3-b4bb-d33dce902734.keywords: poetry; Greek; Alexandria; Egypt; phanariote; Istanbul; Constantinople; Greek community; literature; journalism; migration; mithology; travel; exile; cosmopolitism; travel and exile in literature; mithology in literature; historical events in literature
7a8205d2-2d3a-59d3-b4bb-d33dce902734.description2: The poem *The City*, here labelled *Again at the same city* (*Pali stin idia poli*) handwritten by Constantinos Kavafis and dated August

7a9b5caa-c0ca-5b9c-a54b-4f65a9d0be8e.name: *Palais de l'Industrie. July to November 1890. International Exhibition of the Industrial Arts and Sciences*
7a9b5caa-c0ca-5b9c-a54b-4f65a9d0be8e.second_name: *Concerts every day, directed by Mayeur of the Opera*
7a9b5caa-c0ca-5b9c-a54b-4f65a9d0be8e.description2: The Palais de l'Industrie et des Beaux-Arts was built in Paris in 1855 with the purpose of hosting the first French Exposition Universelle (world fair). Its great glass and metal structure, the "galerie des machines", was a symbol of industrial progress. This building, unlike others of its kind, was used for the same purpose right up until 1896, when it was destroyed to make space for the Grand Palais and the Petit Palais for the Exposition Universelle of 1900. For 40 years it hosted a variety of exhibits, all aimed at promoting recent technological innovations.

7aaccebe-2608-5891-9e82-c06d9f7a2f1f.name: Traditional house
7aaccebe-2608-5891-9e82-c06d9f7a2f1f.description: Houses in the 19th century were modestly built; the roof was generally supported by wooden beams, and stone stairs were built inside the house to access the upper floors (although many other houses only had wooden stairs).
7aaccebe-2608-5891-9e82-c06d9f7a2f1f.history: The houses were built with wooden windows which were filled with tinted glass. A balcony could usually be found on the first floor, which was covered with a clear window for lighting and ventilation purposes. This architectural style was clearly influenced by European architecture and design, indicating the growing influence of European culture and trends in 19th century Beirut and elsewhere in the region.

7ae3021e-1734-5ae1-8790-803fdcd56e67.author: Marina Minozzi

7ae3021e-1734-5ae1-8790-803fdcd56e67.description2: Paris, International Exhibition, 1878. The facade of the foreign sections of the palace in Campo Marte is an example of the forced and unnatural union of different styles into an example of architectural "pastiche", typical of Universal Exhibitions.

7aeb03eb-d2c3-50a9-9ca0-0776ebf921fd.name: Sarcophagus of the mourning women
7aeb03eb-d2c3-50a9-9ca0-0776ebf921fd.dates: It is thought to be the sarcophagus of the King of Sidon, Straton (374-358 BC)
7aeb03eb-d2c3-50a9-9ca0-0776ebf921fd.keywords: Sarcophagus Sidon; The Hellenistic Period; Istanbul Archaeological Museums
7aeb03eb-d2c3-50a9-9ca0-0776ebf921fd.description2: In the Sarcophagus of the Crying Women, found at the Royal Necropolis in Sidon like the Alexander Sarcophagus, nothing could be found other than the bones of its owner and a bronze belt buckle, since it had been robbed in an earlier time. From the partial traces on the marble that remained until today, it is understood that it had been dyed in blue and red initially. It is the best example of the group called by archaeologists "Sarcophagi with Columns", and it is considered as a final resting place, like the "Mausoleum of Halicarnassus" or the "Nereid Monument", rather than a tomb. Its architectural features were used in the architecture of the old building of the İstanbul Archaeological Museums. It is an example of Greek sculpture displaying Eastern influences. The shaved heads, bare feet, ragged clothes of the figures and their movements and expressions of sadness are features of Semitic societies. It is thought to be the sarcophagus of the King of Sidon, Straton (374-358 BC), who was said to have led a life of pleasure. The sarcophagus has the shape of an Ionian temple.

7b5dfa6d-5872-5368-aeb3-65783684e2ef.name: Pearl Grading Sieves
7b5dfa6d-5872-5368-aeb3-65783684e2ef.holder: Sharjah Maritime Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
7b5dfa6d-5872-5368-aeb3-65783684e2ef.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
7b5dfa6d-5872-5368-aeb3-65783684e2ef.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
7b5dfa6d-5872-5368-aeb3-65783684e2ef.description2: These copper alloy sieves were used to grade pearls into their various sizes. The larger, heavier and more luminous a pearl was, the higher its price.These pearl sieves were known as tus or tasat (sing. Tasa). Carefully graded, they are deep circular vessels, their bases pierced and designed to fit one into the other. According to local sources, sets could consists of between four and 45 units. Traditionally, these pearl sieves were used by the tawwash or sea-going merchant, who carried them in a characteristic cloth bag or dasta, when he visited the pearlers, together with all the other implements of his trade, i.e. portable scales and agate weights, a pearl scoop, and his table for calculating the value of the pearls.

7b607aac-e5db-517f-aaf5-04ce4eb5e62c.name: *Project for a Garden or Park*
7b607aac-e5db-517f-aaf5-04ce4eb5e62c.author: Ana Cabrera

7b607aac-e5db-517f-aaf5-04ce4eb5e62c.keywords: Architecture design; Parks; Urban facilities; Neo-mudejar style
7b607aac-e5db-517f-aaf5-04ce4eb5e62c.description2: This project for a park with fountain, covered, possibly, with tiles decorated in Neo-Mudéjar style. The development of urban design was an important subject from the mid-19th century onwards. The Neo-Mudéjar style was selected by the architects for important buildings such as theatres or bull rings or urban spaces as the International exhibition of Barcelona 1888. One of the characteristics of this style is use of brick and tile decoration in the buildings’ interiors and façades.

7bb89a63-82a6-5695-bd9f-cf857d8d19fb.name: *Northern side of the tomb of the Christian woman. Excavations carried out by detachment of the Zouave regiments, under the direction of Berbrugger* \[curator of the *Musée d'Alger*\].
7bb89a63-82a6-5695-bd9f-cf857d8d19fb.second_name: Taken from *L'Algerie Phtographiée*, vol. 2, Province d'Alger
7bb89a63-82a6-5695-bd9f-cf857d8d19fb.description2: Adrien Berbrugger (1801–1869) was an archaeologist specialising in Algeria, who founded the first Musée d'Algérie in Algiers (1838). He visited the "tomb of the Christian woman" for the first time in 1835. This burial mound, located near Tipaza in the south of the Algerian Sahel, had misidentified as an erroneous French translation had rendered "Roman" as "Christian". Berburgger launched various archaeological campaigns which would demonstrate that it was in fact a royal mausoleum from Mauretania. in 1855, for the first time in the history of archaeological excavations, the work of archaeologists was photographed. This photograph is from a "pictorial report" created by Frère Moulin as he passed through Algiers, and shows Berbrugger (by the door), John Green (the archaeological campaign's photographer) and a dozen Zouaves who had taken part in the excavation.

7bd75a35-d206-5701-b425-b077957ef154.name: Émile Zola. *J'accuse!* … 11-13 January 1898
7bd75a35-d206-5701-b425-b077957ef154.description2: In 1894, the French army officer Alfred Dreyfus was accused of espionage, found guilty, fired and deported. His family, who were fighting to have him pardoned, won over the famous naturalist writer, Émile Zola. In just a few days, Zola wrote an indictment ("J'accuse"), addressed to the President of the French Republic, which was published in *l'Aurore*.

7becfe40-aaa5-590f-a2a3-17c23dfb1f52.name: *Faculty of Medicine First Year Students*
7becfe40-aaa5-590f-a2a3-17c23dfb1f52.keywords: Education; Students; Faculty of Medicine; Egyptian University
7becfe40-aaa5-590f-a2a3-17c23dfb1f52.description2: Photograph of first year Faculty of Medicine students at Egyptian University. The 1923 Constitution stipulated that “Primary education is mandatory for all Egyptian boys and girls”. A decree was issued for the establishment of a public university under the name “The Egyptian University” in 1925, comprised of four faculties; literature, science, medicine and law. The Faculty of Medicine, annexed to Qasr al-`Ayni Hospital, is one of the leading hospitals in the Arab World.

7bed9553-212c-5af6-83dd-ee400becb038.name: *Rysul Khyma from the SW and the situation of the Troops at ½ past 2 pm, November 13th, 1809*
7bed9553-212c-5af6-83dd-ee400becb038.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
7bed9553-212c-5af6-83dd-ee400becb038.dimensions: 505 mm x 602 mm (framed); image: 215 mm x 358 mm
7bed9553-212c-5af6-83dd-ee400becb038.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
7bed9553-212c-5af6-83dd-ee400becb038.artist: R. Temple, HM 65th Regiment, Sixteen views; I. Clark, Sculpt.; William Haines, Publisher
7bed9553-212c-5af6-83dd-ee400becb038.description2: In this image, the artist - a soldier with the British forces attacking and devastating Qawasim strongholds in 1809/10, records the wholescale devastation of Ras al Khaimah on the afternoon of November 13th, 1809. Looking at the town from the southwest, he records in graphic detail the inferno British troups visited on both the town and the Qawasim's majestic dhows. Both are seen being consumed by a firewall of flames, the smoke billowing densely above. A large contingent of inactive British troops is seen standing along the perimeters of the town, unconcerned by the devastation behind them. In the foreground on the left, a group of workers is instructed by British officers to remove  things from a burning builiding, which - interestingly - is marked with a large cross on its side wall. Eye witnesses to this event record that the town was cannonaded since the day before, while troops stormed strategic positions. By 4 pm on the 13th, all the Qawasim's vessels were burning, together with their naval stores and houses, most of which were looted by the British forces.

7c5b0aa9-383a-5b52-bc5a-91c986d3c9eb.name: Toiletries
7c5b0aa9-383a-5b52-bc5a-91c986d3c9eb.holder: Musée des Arts et Traditions Populaires
7c5b0aa9-383a-5b52-bc5a-91c986d3c9eb.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
7c5b0aa9-383a-5b52-bc5a-91c986d3c9eb.description2: In the 19th century the wealthy families of Tunis invented the notion of the knastrou l'aroussa (marriage basket) as a mark of their wealth. Made of engraved or watermarked silver, this basket would contain various toiletries for the bride: a perfume sprinkler (mrach), a khol phial with applicator for the eyes (mokhala), a round or rectangular-framed mirror with engraved floral motifs, and a knife and plate for henna. A pair of clogs (qobqabs) made of wood and covered in silver worn by the bride. As a traditional bath (hammam) was the bride's first event on her wedding day, all her toiletries were set out ready for her, with a series of tools for exfoliation, depilation, application of a clay face mask, and more.

7c628f29-8443-5e2e-8926-884729f02df3.name: Legged violin
7c628f29-8443-5e2e-8926-884729f02df3.description2: The Violin was not a popular instrument in 16th century except among patrons of taverns. In the early 19th century, musicians used both types of violin – the legged violin and the sine or "chest" violin – but the sine violin disappeared afterwards. The legged violin has a cylindrical body with a relatively long handle. The cut body is made of coconut shell and covered with leather.

7c6c4813-f135-5843-8f48-660e13714964.name: The Covered Walkway in the Moorish Garden (Wilhelma Park)
7c6c4813-f135-5843-8f48-660e13714964.holder: Wilhelma, Zoological and Botanical Garden Stuttgart
7c6c4813-f135-5843-8f48-660e13714964.history:
King Wilhelm I of Württemberg commissioned to Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1837 the design of Moorish style buildings for his Wilhelma garden. The architect planned and built all the buildings with the exception of the Damascene Hall.  
The idea was not to reproduce faithfully the Islamic art but to lend an “oriental” flair to the garden. The mention of an “oriental garden” conjured up visions of elegance, luxury, colourful brilliance, seduction and eroticism.  
The Moorish style recalls the Islamic art of Spain and North Africa between the 12th and 15th centuries which reached its zenith in the Alhambra. It was fashionable in 19th century: Wilhelma is also known as the “Alhambra on the river Neckar” and other buildings – synagogues in Berlin and Vienna for example – were built in the Moorish style.
7c6c4813-f135-5843-8f48-660e13714964.description2:
Planned as a bathhouse by Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1846, the Moorish Villa was then, however, built as living quarters with a glasshouse. It was first intended to be a bathhouse because mineral springs had been discovered in the adjacent Rosenstein Park. Rosenstein Palace was already standing in Rosenstein Park, and served the King as a summer residence.  
The Covered Walkaway marks the perimeter of the Moorish Garden at Wilhelma.

7c87bedb-5773-5c25-8dc4-6634c1e81d26.name: Treaty of Bardo
7c87bedb-5773-5c25-8dc4-6634c1e81d26.author: Bechir Yazidi
7c87bedb-5773-5c25-8dc4-6634c1e81d26.keywords: French protectorate of Tunisia; Sadok Pacha Bey
7c87bedb-5773-5c25-8dc4-6634c1e81d26.description2: Also known as the Treaty of Ksar Said, the Treaty of Bardo was signed by the Bey of Tunis and the French government on 12 May 1881. It consisted of two articles which established the French protectorate of Tunisia. The bey was henceforth required to give up all his powers over foreign affairs, defence and administrative reform to the French resident-general.

7c890fcb-159c-520c-b75f-6a2a5003b92c.description2: Back from the Franco-Tuscan expedition (1828-29), Francois Champollion and Ippolito Rosellini worked on publishing drawings and notes collected during the voyage in Egypt. Unfortunately Champollion died in 1831 (he was only 41 years old) and Rosellini had to carry on the huge project on his own, publishing the texts and also the atlas plates in folio. The original materials for the publication are preserved today at the University Library of Pisa.

7c98ed41-590d-5c29-bafe-19140f7e1bc3.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. İzmir Port, due to its geopolitical position, is the gateway to western Turkey. As a result of growth in world trade and increases of raw material needs due to the industrial revolution, İzmir Port was the most important trade route in the 19th century. Construction of new railways in the Ottoman period increased commercial activity.

7cb05e6b-507b-594c-9ddd-3e9a0460ae93.description2: This appliqué is one of a set of six featuring designs that echo the bold geometry of Egypt’s period of Mamluk rule (1250–1517). The format of calligraphy above a central roundel with trefoils is similar to other works of art created during the Mamluk Revival period. This particular textile features the following verse from the Qur’an: “That man can have nothing but what he strives for...” (53:39). Appliqués of this type were often used to embellish tents.

7d30a2cd-fc11-5624-b8c4-b8d92b2e5e38.name: Photograph of Tétouan Railway Station, platform
7d30a2cd-fc11-5624-b8c4-b8d92b2e5e38.description: Completion of the railway line that connected Tétouan with Ceuta relates closely to plans for the construction of the new Port of Ceuta. This photograph depicts Tétouan Railway Station in relation to construction of the port. It was the military engineers Captain Mario Pinto and First Lieutenant Levi Arsenio Jimenez Montera who first offered to draft plans for the new line between the two cities, a distance of nearly 1,435m, and managed to get the project approved by the Ministry of War. While some railway lines in Morocco were abandoned early, this one resisted closure until the dawn of independence. Evidence shows that the route thrived during the Protectorate era as it was one of main Spanish penetration axes to the North at the time.

7d5e25dc-ec5c-5066-946b-cebbacb4f214.description2: This print was dedicated to Napoléon III's coronation. Louis-Napoléon, Napoléon I's great-nephew, came to power legally in the elections of 1848. He became emperor in 1852, after a coup d’état in 1851. This print was produced as propaganda, and depicts the French people as overjoyed at having the great-nephew of Napoléon I as their emperor.

7d67ccb5-cf82-5111-bc4d-df565effb29b.name: *Guernsey and Jersey, Malta and Ceylon* (from *Dickinson's Comprehensive Pictures of the Great Exhibition*)
7d67ccb5-cf82-5111-bc4d-df565effb29b.description:
The Great Exhibition of London, held at the Crystal Palace in 1851, was a notable event for the world for various reasons: It was the very first exhibition of this kind, and it was possible, for the first time, to gather and wonder at products from distant countries at the Crystal Palace, a futuristic building for the time and a symbol of the cosmopolitan nature of the United Kingdom.  
  
*Dickinson’s Comprehensive Pictures of the Great Exhibition of 1851* (published in 1854) is a famous collection of coloured illustrations of the Great Exhibition. The illustration displayed on this page, painted by Joseph Nash, shows the stands with the products of Ceylon and Malta, as well as those of British Channel Islands Guernsey and Jersey, and gives an accurate depiction of what the interior of the Crystal Palace looked like, and a vivid idea of the commercial (and artistic) exchanges this exhibition inaugurated.
7d67ccb5-cf82-5111-bc4d-df565effb29b.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)

7d6b2d8b-aee7-5a0e-bbaf-f3702ae0946a.name: A commercial artery of 19th-century Bucharest
7d6b2d8b-aee7-5a0e-bbaf-f3702ae0946a.description2: Mentioned in documents since the 16th century, this street, one of the oldest in Bucharest, connected the centre of the city with an area situated east of it, where a trade fair took place annually. Because of this, the street was called “The Bridge of the Outside Fair” (in the past the major streets of Bucharest used to be called “bridges” because they used to be covered with wooden boards). In time, as the fair was gradually moved eastwards, the street was extended. On both its sides there used to be many shops, inns, restaurants, craftsmen’s workshops.

7de42026-ed99-5288-a199-da1cae44d5fc.name: Caparison for a horse given by the Sultan of Morocco to the King of Italy, on the occasion of a visit to Italy of a Moroccan Ambassador in 1890
7de42026-ed99-5288-a199-da1cae44d5fc.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography
7de42026-ed99-5288-a199-da1cae44d5fc.author: Vito Lattanzi, Giulia Barrera
7de42026-ed99-5288-a199-da1cae44d5fc.description2:
In 1890, the Sultan of Morocco sent Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi as an Ambassador to Italy. The Ambassador landed in Naples on June 7th and arrived by train in Rome on June 13th. At the railway station, he was received by the Mayor of Rome, the Prefect, and other authorities. A military band was playing and military men in high uniform were paraded in the station to greet the Ambassador.  
Outside the station, three of the King’s gala carriages were waiting for the Ambassador and a military unit was paraded in his honour. Some carabinieri in high uniform escorted the Ambassador to the hotel.  
Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi presented the King with gifts, including some superb horses that the King immensely appreciated. The King presented the Ambassador with a magnificent small gold and diamonds small box and a hunting rifle and gave gold watches to the members of his escort.

7deda599-b0dc-5a5b-a9a1-e34b87edc4f8.name: *The Battle of Abukir 1799*
7deda599-b0dc-5a5b-a9a1-e34b87edc4f8.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
7deda599-b0dc-5a5b-a9a1-e34b87edc4f8.dimensions: Image height 253 mm x length 379 mm, overall size 303 mm x 471 mm
7deda599-b0dc-5a5b-a9a1-e34b87edc4f8.provenance: Published around 1820 by Carle Vernet in his Album *Campagnes des Francais sous le Consulat et L´Empire*
7deda599-b0dc-5a5b-a9a1-e34b87edc4f8.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
7deda599-b0dc-5a5b-a9a1-e34b87edc4f8.artist: J. Couche; J. F. J. Swebach; Francois Dequevauvillers
7deda599-b0dc-5a5b-a9a1-e34b87edc4f8.keywords: Abukir; Abu Qir; Horatio Nelson; Sayyid Mustapha Pasha; Napoleon Bonaparte
7deda599-b0dc-5a5b-a9a1-e34b87edc4f8.description2: During the French occupation of Egypt, in fact three battles centered on the area around Abukir (Abu Qir), a town on the Mediterranean northeast of Alexandria. The first, in 1798, was a naval battle in which the French were defeated devastatingly by the British navy under the command of Rear Admiral Horatio Nelson. The second battle – shown here – marked a decisive confrontation between Ottoman troops under the command of Sayyid Mustapha Pasha, shipped to Egypt by the British navy, and the occupying French forces led by Napoleon Bonaparte. On the 14th of July 1799, the Ottomans stormed Abukir’s harbor and briefly took control of the city, only to be rebuffed and decisively defeated by the French eleven days later. The scene here appears to mark the moment of surrender. Napoleon Bonaparte, seated on a white horse and surrounded by his officers  is supplicated by Ottoman figures, while fighting still goes on and the smoke of battle continues to billow all around. At sea lie the ships of the British navy – unable to intervene.  The last battle fought near Abukir in 1801 between the French and British helped to prepare the ground for France’s final expulsion from Egypt.

7e87a4ee-76a2-59b0-995b-b76a7a6ee825.name: *Woman with mimosa*
7e87a4ee-76a2-59b0-995b-b76a7a6ee825.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
7e87a4ee-76a2-59b0-995b-b76a7a6ee825.keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters
7e87a4ee-76a2-59b0-995b-b76a7a6ee825.description2: Osman Hamdi focused on dilemmas such as East and West, love and hate, life and death. While stylistically reminiscent of western Orientalist painters, his works reflect a more nuanced appreciation of Ottoman society and culture. In the art of his paintings, he depicted unique details so diligently that he made us recognize our environment and Turkish culture. He illustrated carpets, tile panels, calligraphies, decorative arts, shrines, mosques and human figures in his paintings. He also gave importance to details while reflecting the colourful scenes of Turkish culture, traditional architecture, Ottoman fashion and domestic and social life of the women in the Ottoman Empire. And it’s obvious that he is the first painter who used human figures in the western style.

7e932bea-47e5-5386-9498-0e48388f3e95.name: Fountain
7e932bea-47e5-5386-9498-0e48388f3e95.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
7e932bea-47e5-5386-9498-0e48388f3e95.description2: Water fountains such as these were common in Ottoman government buildings in Lebanon, and were turned on whenever there was a meeting to prevent outsiders overhearing or eavesdropping. This marble fountain is octagonal in shape and is decorated with embossed semi-cylinders on each side. The exterior of the structure is decorated with a mosaic of black, white, beige and brown marble organised in geometric designs. A second, circular level of the fountain rests on this first octagonal structure.

7eacd600-e860-593a-aed7-a9329d9d9011.name: Fragment of the Parthenon frieze
7eacd600-e860-593a-aed7-a9329d9d9011.description: The climax of the Greater Panathenaia, the chief festival of Athens, held in honour of Athena, was a procession which ended with the presentation of the newly woven *peplos* (a woman’s garment) to the tutelary goddess of the city. This is the subject of the frieze around the cella of the Parthenon, the temple on the Athenian Acropolis. This fragment depicts the garment being handed over in the presence of the goddess.

7f865df5-a1bf-51f2-943d-4a9bec647c8f.description2: This long dress or *djebba* is made of brocade and has a breast plate on the front. The low-cut sleeves are bordered by a golden ribbon. Jewish women from Constantine wore this long dress, whereas Muslim women wore a slightly shorter one. Although the decoration of the Constantine dress is completely different today, the shape and cut has not changed.

7f8a48e3-b8ea-55d5-9114-484b7cc5c0a2.keywords: Herbarium; vascular plant; aromatic; North Africa; National Museum of Natural History and Science; University of Lisbon
7f8a48e3-b8ea-55d5-9114-484b7cc5c0a2.materials: Pressed and dried plant, glued on paper
7f8a48e3-b8ea-55d5-9114-484b7cc5c0a2.description2: Natural History Museums were an important institution for scientific researching, exchange and circulate ideas and natural knowledge. This object is a Herbarium and the specimen was collected in Algeria, on the Lions Mountain, near Oran, in May 1850 by Giles Munby. The aromatic leaves are grey-green, covered with hairs. The pink flowers are crowded into terminal clusters. It is a drought tolerant species from NW Africa (Algeria and Morocco). It is included in the first Centuria of Plantae Algeriensis Exciccatae, distributed to different herbaria. It is used as a medicinal plant in its area of occurrence.

802c443d-9ccb-5e7b-b692-21b1695a778f.description2: Bags such as these were used by young brides, particularly in the 19th century, in order to transport their belongings to the marital home. As per tradition, the bag is made of black fabric and embroidered with the words *ma sha Allah* in Arabic calligraphy, meaning "as God wills". The words are embroidered in golden silk thread and surrounded by floral patterns.

8138d27f-0df1-5e19-884f-c3f2fabf66df.artist: Photograph: author unknown; building: architect Vedat Tek, architect Muzaffer Bey
8138d27f-0df1-5e19-884f-c3f2fabf66df.keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication
8138d27f-0df1-5e19-884f-c3f2fabf66df.description2: The Istanbul Main Post Office is an office building for postal services located at the *Sirkeci* quarter of the faith district in Istanbul, Turkey. It was designed by architect Vedat Tek in the First Turkish National architectural style and was constructed between 1903 and 1909. (Vedat Tek was a notable Turkish architect, who has been one of the leading figures of the First Turkish National Architectural Movement. He studied at the *École Centrale Paris*, graduating with a degree in civil engineering before he got his further education in architecture at the *Ecole des Beaux Arts* in Paris.) The four-story building houses a post office, the *Sirkeci* Post Office, office space for regional administration and also since 2000 the Istanbul Postal Museum. It is Turkey's largest post office building.

8139411f-fd90-565b-b236-4329f1f00269.name: Italian troops landing in Libya
8139411f-fd90-565b-b236-4329f1f00269.description:
In October 1911 the Italian government sent an expeditionary force of 34,000 men to Libya, with the goal of colonising the country. The conquest proved much more difficult than the Italian government had expected and it soon needed to send reinforcements; at the end of 1911, the Italian army in Libya had reached 103,000 men.  
Many Italians supported the colonial conquest of Libya, believing that the country would provide settlement opportunities for Italian migrants (in the first decade of the 20th century, Italian migrants abroad averaged 600,000 per year). Their hopes went mostly disappointed: in 1927, barely 26,000 Italians had settled in Libya. Only in the 1930s, after crushing Libyan anti-colonial resistance by means of ruthless repression, was the Italian government able to promote Italian settlement in Libya. By 1939, the Italian population in Libya reached almost 120,000.

81a863b7-0e26-5e2a-b1ac-55b331836571.name: The Consuls’ Square [Alexandria, Egypt] after the Fire
81a863b7-0e26-5e2a-b1ac-55b331836571.author: Giulia Barrera
81a863b7-0e26-5e2a-b1ac-55b331836571.second_name: The ruins of the Consuls' Square in Alexandria (Egypt) after the bombing of the city by the British Navy in 1882
81a863b7-0e26-5e2a-b1ac-55b331836571.description2:
The author of this picture, Luigi Fiorillo, was an Italian photographer who migrated to Alexandria (Egypt) around 1870 and opened a successful photography shop. In 1877, he participated as photographer in an expedition to Shewa region (Ethiopia), organised by the Italian Geographical Society, and ten years later in an Italian military expedition for the colonial conquest of Eritrea.  
In 1882, Fiorillo was one of the few Europeans who remained in Alexandria after the anti-foreign rioting and documented the consequences of the British bombardment on Alexandria of July 11th. He collected 50 pictures of the city ruins in an album titled “Souvenir d'Alexandrie: Ruines, 1882”.  
On the back of some photos that he took in the 1880s, Fiorillo defines himself as “le photographe de Son Altesse le Prince Mohammed Toussoun Pasha” (the photographer of his Majesty Prince Mohammed Toussoun Pasha). Luigi Fiorillo died in 1898.

en: Silingardi, Adriano, ”Luigi Fiorillo, l’avventuroso fotografo di Alessandria d’Egitto”, unpublished paper (available on line) for the exhibition of the same name, Genoa, 2014.

81c828fc-8155-513b-b95f-cf8966747f0a.name: *The Romanian pavilion at the world exhibition of 1867*
81c828fc-8155-513b-b95f-cf8966747f0a.archival: *L’exposition universelle de 1867 illustrée. Publication autorisée par la commision impériale*, editeur E. Dentu, redacteur en chef Fr. Ducuing, vol. 2, 1867
81c828fc-8155-513b-b95f-cf8966747f0a.description2: In 1865, the United Principalities of Wallachia and Moldavia were invited by France to participate in the universal exhibition of 1867, that was to take place in Paris. The Romanian government appointed Alexandru Odobescu to negotiate with the Imperial Commission for the Organization of the Exposition the location of the Romanian pavilion. Although the Principalities were under Ottoman sovereignty, the Commission agreed to offer the Principalities their own pavilion next to that of the Ottoman Empire. Odobescu hired French architect Ambroise Baudry, who had been to Romania in 1864 for an archeological mission, to build the Romanian pavilion, which was a combination of architectural elements characteristic of famous Romanian monuments (e.g.: the Stavropoleos Church in Bucharest, the Curtea de Argeș monastery).

823a405a-b8cf-5eeb-af76-1bb8e28081d7.name: First issue of *Al-Ahram*
823a405a-b8cf-5eeb-af76-1bb8e28081d7.notice: This is an unedited Database entry and may contain errors and inconsistencies in spelling. We are doing our best to complete the editing asap. If you are in the position to help - with a donation or as a volunteer copy-editor - please contact us at [editing@museumwnf.net](mailto:editing@museumwnf.net).
823a405a-b8cf-5eeb-af76-1bb8e28081d7.description2:
*Al-Ahram* was founded in Alexandria in 1875 by two Lebanese brothers, Bishara Takla and Salim Takla. It began as a weekly newspaper published every Saturday. Its first issue appeared on 5 August 1876. The paper was relaunched as a daily newspaper in January 1881.  
Its headquarters was in Alexandria until November 1899 when it was moved to Cairo. The newspaper was distributed in Egypt and the Levant. The religious innovators Muhammad Abduh and Jamal al-Din al-Afghani were early writers of the newspaper. Upon the death of Bishara Takla, Dawud Barakat, a Lebanese journalist, was named editor of the daily in 1901.

82418ca9-7d43-5ee2-913a-f1235ecfd9e4.name: House
82418ca9-7d43-5ee2-913a-f1235ecfd9e4.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Prof. Petar Namichev (consultant)
82418ca9-7d43-5ee2-913a-f1235ecfd9e4.history: The most intense development of urban houses in Macedonia occurred in the 19th century, creating a new panorama of towns across the landscape. This applies particularly to the town of Veles, which reached the peak of its rise in the mid-19th century, owing to extensive growth of crafts and trade.
82418ca9-7d43-5ee2-913a-f1235ecfd9e4.description2: In this house the influence of the Levantine architecture was coupled with the individual skills and talents of native architects, which has given rise to a diversity of types and outstanding autochthonous construction solutions. This three-storied house was built by use of the bondruk structural system, which consists of wooden framing and adobe. The façade is coated with mortar and decorated by application of a strip pattern on the band between the second and third storey, as well as above the top storey. It also has painted ornaments applied on the surface under the roof.

825ea881-372b-5499-bcbe-096246ecd917.description2: The items imported from Egypt were cotton, natron (a hydrous native sodium carbonate, used in chemical industry; Egypt had a rich deposit of it in Wadi el-Natrun), coffee, hides, fruit, copper and tamarind roots. The items exported to Egypt included wood and pieces of furniture, fruits and vegetables, butter, bricks and tiles, glass beads, lime, wine, cloth, medicaments, books, and various other products.

82635f79-7381-59a0-8cbe-e72a1b631f83.name: Dish
82635f79-7381-59a0-8cbe-e72a1b631f83.description: The Orientalism or Neo-Mudéjar style gave new light to different workshops, as Fajalauza in Granada. Following this revival, this workshop produced dishes and other object decorated with Alhambra motifs, in this case the gazelles from the very well-known "Gazelle Vase" from the Alhambra Palace, the inscriptions and interlaces.
82635f79-7381-59a0-8cbe-e72a1b631f83.keywords: Neo-mudejar style; Applied Arts; Production of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode

826abea9-d0a5-5b38-9d39-fb3cd81ac626.name: The Şirket-i Hayriyye’s Excursion Steamship
826abea9-d0a5-5b38-9d39-fb3cd81ac626.description2: The Şirket-i Hayriyye was the name of a steam boat joint-stock company which carried passengers and cargo on the Bosporus from 1854 to 1945. The company was established with the approval of the Sultan Abdulmecid. The steam boats belonging to company were sent from European countries, primarily Britain. The first captains of this boats were almost all of Rûm origin. After the establishment of the Republic of Turkey, the company and its goods were purchased by the state.

82a512d3-aced-55a2-b8b4-370dfafb5ffc.name: *Théâtre de l'Opéra. "Aida". The banks of the Nile (act 3). Set by Jean-Louis Chéret*
82a512d3-aced-55a2-b8b4-370dfafb5ffc.artist: Engraver: Auguste Lepère; artists: Henry Scott, Jean-Louis Chéret
82a512d3-aced-55a2-b8b4-370dfafb5ffc.description2: Commissioned by Isma'il Pasha for the inauguration of the Suez Canal, Verdi's opera *Aida* was performed for the first time in Cairo in 1871, with great success. It recreated life at the time of the pharaohs, with the details and the plot developed by the archaeologist Mariette. *Aida* was performed in Paris from 1876, with a grand and successful performance at the Opéra Garnier in 1880.

82ced29b-1974-5648-8a77-a399212ae4e2.name: The horses presented by the Sultan of Morocco to the King of Italy on the occasion of the official visit to Italy by a Moroccan delegation
82ced29b-1974-5648-8a77-a399212ae4e2.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
82ced29b-1974-5648-8a77-a399212ae4e2.author: Giulia Barrera
82ced29b-1974-5648-8a77-a399212ae4e2.archival: *La Tribuna illustrata*, a. I, n. 26, 29 June 1890, p. 403
82ced29b-1974-5648-8a77-a399212ae4e2.third_name: *Nel giardino del Quirinale. I cavalli recati in dono al re dall’ambasciata marocchina (fotografie istantanee del conte Giuseppe Primoli)*
82ced29b-1974-5648-8a77-a399212ae4e2.description2:
In 1890, the Sultan of Morocco sent Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi as an Ambassador to Italy. The Ambassador landed in Naples on June 7th and arrived by train in Rome on June 13th. At the railway station, he was received by the Mayor or Rome, the Prefect, and other authorities. A military band was playing and military men in high uniform were paraded in the station to greet the Ambassador.  
Outside the station, three of the King’s gala carriages were waiting for the ambassador and a military unit was paraded in his honour. Some carabinieri in high uniform escorted the ambassador to the hotel.  
Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi presented the King with gifts, including some superb horses that the King immensely appreciated. The King presented the Ambassador with a magnificent small gold and diamond box, and a hunting rifle and gave gold watches to the members of his escort.
82ced29b-1974-5648-8a77-a399212ae4e2.holding_institution_org: Biblioteca di Storia Moderna e Contemporanea

82f533fb-66d6-5753-8d34-97a1b983f107.name: Scharf lecture
82f533fb-66d6-5753-8d34-97a1b983f107.description2: Lecture by George Scharf at what was to become Queen’s College, London. He made large drawings of important objects for the purpose.

830c2e47-9fe7-5cca-984a-d06b95466a30.name: *Sketches of Aden*
830c2e47-9fe7-5cca-984a-d06b95466a30.description: These drawings show Steamer Point, an early British settlement in Aden, and one early steamer. *Sketches of Aden* is an account by a British officer who settled in Aden in the first half of the 19th century. Published in Madras in 1848, the book offers a synthesis of the history, geography, people and costumes of that important British settlement on the route to India. Although influenced by 19th-century European stereotypes and by the impact of a new environment, the author describes vividly the political events leading to the British conquest of the port in 1839, the ancient legends and the main events in the local history of Aden, its towns, commerce, living conditions and the heterogeneous population living in Aden: the Arab, Somali, Jewish and Indian communities.
830c2e47-9fe7-5cca-984a-d06b95466a30.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
830c2e47-9fe7-5cca-984a-d06b95466a30.archival: *Historical and Statistical Sketches of Aden ... during a two years' residence ... By an officer in the Queen's Army*, Madras, 1848, p. 30
830c2e47-9fe7-5cca-984a-d06b95466a30.keywords: Trade; route; port; Great Britain; India; coffee; Red Sea; Yemen; British settlement on the route to India; communication; telegraph; Suez Canal; Arab Peninsula; steamship; Jewish; Somalian; Indian; migration from India

83126725-c2b3-5d22-9ee2-4e1c45c60872.name: Patriarchal Monument
83126725-c2b3-5d22-9ee2-4e1c45c60872.description: This building has been the main headquarters of the Maronite Patriarchate since 1790.
83126725-c2b3-5d22-9ee2-4e1c45c60872.author: Jeff El-Msanne
83126725-c2b3-5d22-9ee2-4e1c45c60872.history: Patriarch John Hajj, who renovated this monastery, was elected in 1890 following the death of Patriarch Mas'ad. He expanded the structure by adding a second floor.

8341e914-3245-5e20-9233-8addfbd06386.name: Mohamed Bey Mosque
8341e914-3245-5e20-9233-8addfbd06386.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
8341e914-3245-5e20-9233-8addfbd06386.history: Built in the late 18th century, this mosque is also known as the Sidi Mehrez mosque, probably due to its location facing the mausoleum to the saint Sidi Mehrez in the Bab Souika quarter. It is the only multiple-domed mosque in Tunisia. With clear Turkish influences, this mosque is reminiscent of the Hagia Sofia in Istanbul and the Pêcherie in Algiers.
8341e914-3245-5e20-9233-8addfbd06386.description2: The mosque is accessible through three doors, the most important of which opens up onto the *suq*, on one of the medina's most important streets. When seen from the outside, the mosque dominates the city, with its grouped domes and cupolas painted with a white wash. The Anatolian ceramic tiles covering the walls were an innovative addition at the time. The square-based prayer room is bordered on three sides by galleries, which each face onto three V-shaped courtyards. These galleries rest on marble columns with Turkish-style capitals. The richly decorated *mihrab* is covered in Iznik ceramic tiles. This mosque, also known as the Sidi Mahrez Mosque, is notable for being the only mosque in Tunisia with Turkish influences.

83550dcd-d5fe-53bf-ba81-33534dbf86ed.name: Lace skirt
83550dcd-d5fe-53bf-ba81-33534dbf86ed.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
83550dcd-d5fe-53bf-ba81-33534dbf86ed.author: Huda Kilani
83550dcd-d5fe-53bf-ba81-33534dbf86ed.description2: Skirt of light pink lace with black flowers, pursed from the middle, worn over a woman’s dress. This object illustrates the variegated population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, the various local costumes and rites, fashion and personal attire. This skirt was used by al-Druze women in Jordan. The al-Druze tribes migrated from Syria (Hawran) to north east Jordan in the early twentieth century because of their support for the Syrian revolution against the French occupation.

837581e0-006f-52d2-82bf-795b4cf10463.name: Portrait of Abraham Behor And Nisim Camondo
837581e0-006f-52d2-82bf-795b4cf10463.holder: The Quincentennial Foundation Museum, Zulfaris Synagogue Museum
837581e0-006f-52d2-82bf-795b4cf10463.description2: Abraham Salomon's descendants, Abraham-Behor (1829-1889) and Nisim (1830-1889) were partners in banking. As a rival to the Ottoman Bank, The Camondo Family established the Ottoman Empire Company-i Umumiyesi (*Societe Generale de l'Empire Ottoman*) with a capital of two million pounds in 1864. Because of the establishment of the Credit General Ottoman Bank in 1868, the Camondo Brothers decided to move the bank to Paris with the idea that the Bank should have absolutely no external links. Abraham-Behor became president of the institution of the *Alliance Israelite Universelle* in 1864. This institution – which instructed students in French in the name of modernization and westernization – was founded to improve the material and spiritual conditions of the Jews and to ensure the spread of education in İstanbul.

837ec644-be86-5c90-b478-af2509cf304b.name: *The Alhambra Court*
837ec644-be86-5c90-b478-af2509cf304b.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
837ec644-be86-5c90-b478-af2509cf304b.keywords: Exhibition; Courts; Crystal Palace (South London); Photographs
837ec644-be86-5c90-b478-af2509cf304b.description2: One of 43 photographs by Delamotte of the Crystal Palace at Sydenham (opened 1854).

83c3fe83-79b0-588d-a540-cb63c72ac1b4.name: Pearling Scales Case
83c3fe83-79b0-588d-a540-cb63c72ac1b4.holder: Sharjah Maritime Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
83c3fe83-79b0-588d-a540-cb63c72ac1b4.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
83c3fe83-79b0-588d-a540-cb63c72ac1b4.description2: Pearling scales were an essential tool for any pearl merchant. All aspects of a pearl’s physical appearance – its shape, hue, perfection, size and indeed weight all determined its value and saleability. This copper alloy case for pearling scales is of the characteristic type common in the pearling industry throughout the Gulf. It combines a very slightly pointed, circular section designed to receive the two small bowls of the scales, with a narrow elongated section to contain the balance, with the scales's strings carefully wound around it for storage. This example is particularly interesting in that it appears to give the name of the merchant and the date 1280 H/ 1863 AD.

8416e828-5b8b-5b06-93d0-9f518e17c49a.name: The Emigrants
8416e828-5b8b-5b06-93d0-9f518e17c49a.author: Marina Minozzi
8416e828-5b8b-5b06-93d0-9f518e17c49a.keywords: Migration; Italian migration; Italian painters; painting; realism; artistic exchanges; Courbet; Macchiaioli; unification of Italy; social history; social topics; Italian society; post-unitarian Italian society; Livorno
8416e828-5b8b-5b06-93d0-9f518e17c49a.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
8416e828-5b8b-5b06-93d0-9f518e17c49a.description2: Angelo Tommasi is a naturalistic painter, influenced by Courbet’s realism, and he played an active role spreading the technique employed by the Macchiaioli. The monumental painting *The Emigrants* shows a common situation in Italy after the unification process. The dramatic theme of overseas emigration is vividly depicted by the packed crowds at the Port of Livorno, of people who have resigned themselves to their fate and the expectation of embarkation. The painting's extraordinary dimensions contribute to an illustration of the theme of Italian emigration on an almost epic scale.
8416e828-5b8b-5b06-93d0-9f518e17c49a.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

841ba735-7c60-5603-8827-b02f6aedad8e.name: Arab coffee pot
841ba735-7c60-5603-8827-b02f6aedad8e.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
841ba735-7c60-5603-8827-b02f6aedad8e.author: Huda Kilani
841ba735-7c60-5603-8827-b02f6aedad8e.description2: One padded handle with leather, tapered cover; long covered nozzle, stamped reliefs. Coffee-drinking in a communal setting is an essential part of traditions in Bedouin communities to celebrate or mourn. This object of common use reflects the Bedouins’ traditions and everyday life and illustrates the variegated population composition of the Jordanian territory in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

842a5200-0594-5a9c-bea6-e441fe3c4f78.name: Faience pottery tile
842a5200-0594-5a9c-bea6-e441fe3c4f78.author: Houria Cherid
842a5200-0594-5a9c-bea6-e441fe3c4f78.description2: This faience pottery tile is painted with a ship in a circle in its centre, surrounded by flying birds. The rest of the *zelige* tile is decorated with a stylised floral pattern in each of its four corners.

8450e17b-8c6f-5b90-8443-1e6a14d55b9e.name: Orosdi-Back
8450e17b-8c6f-5b90-8443-1e6a14d55b9e.bibliography: Kupferschmidt, Uri, *The Orosdi-Back Saga: European Department Stores and Middle Eastern Consumers*, Istanbul: OBARC, 2007.
8450e17b-8c6f-5b90-8443-1e6a14d55b9e.author: Ahmad al-Bindari
8450e17b-8c6f-5b90-8443-1e6a14d55b9e.history: The Orosdi-Back story starts in Hungary with the liaison of two families when Adolf Orosdi’s sister, Antoinette (?-1879), married Maurice Back. Given that they were Jewish and had supported the Hungarian rebellion against the Austrian Empire, Adolf Orosdi and Maurice Back settled in Galata district in Istanbul, a focal point for Jews and one of the Ottoman Empire’s most vibrant business centres. In 1855, they established their shop under the name of Omar Effendi. The Orosdi-Back enterprise expanded from there, and their branches were given the combined name “Orosdi-Back”. It had outlets in Constantinople, Adana, Izmir, Samsun, Cairo, Alexandria, Port-Said, Zagazig, Tanta, Tunis, Philippopoli (Plovdiv), Bucharest, Aleppo, Beirut, Salonica, Tabriz, Tehran, Casablanca, Meknes, Vienna from 1893 and Basra and Baghdad after WWI.
8450e17b-8c6f-5b90-8443-1e6a14d55b9e.keywords: Orosdi-Back; Omar Effendi; Etablishements Orosdi-Back "Omar Effendi"; department store; architecture; Art Nouveau; Neo Baroque
8450e17b-8c6f-5b90-8443-1e6a14d55b9e.description2: Modern Egypt and cosmopolitan Cairo emerged in the context of diverse foreign communities and their interaction with Egyptians. By the turn of the 20th century, this cultural exchange gave birth to a new kind of commercial activity: big department stores (*grands magasins*), a novelty that developed more or less at the same time as it did in Europe. Foremost amongst these was Orosdi-Back, one of the largest department stores in Egypt, whose rivals included Cicurel, Chémla, Sednaoui and others. Raoul Brandon, a French Jewish architect, designed the Orosdi-Back premises in the corner of two important streets, \`Abd al-Aziz and Rushdi Pasha, in 1906. He designed a building with glamour *à la parisiènne*, evoking the elegant department stores of Paris, in Neo-Baroque style with a glimpse of Art Nouveau flair in its lines.

8469840c-c735-573f-aef2-fdf1fcbc3556.name: Bottle-shaped vase
8469840c-c735-573f-aef2-fdf1fcbc3556.description2: This nipple or bottle-shaped vase, with its central ring-shaped handle and turned-up base, resembles a closed coffin when seen from the side. Vases in this shape are very rare, and this particular one, which is decorated with the image of a great yellow and brown bird, was used for bottle-feeding infants.

846f15c1-f86c-5efe-ab3c-1015370062f6.name: *Al-badr al-safir li-hidayati al-musafir ila fikak al-asara min yad al-ʿaduw al-kafir*
