8483f56d-4097-5e63-a47a-8a53aa99f289.name: *Hilye*
8483f56d-4097-5e63-a47a-8a53aa99f289.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
8483f56d-4097-5e63-a47a-8a53aa99f289.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
8483f56d-4097-5e63-a47a-8a53aa99f289.artist: Ali Al-Shukri; his work is certified by Al-Hajj Hafedh Muhammad Al-Wahbi and Khalil Al-Safi
8483f56d-4097-5e63-a47a-8a53aa99f289.materials: Black ink, pigments, gilding on board; ebru (marbling)
8483f56d-4097-5e63-a47a-8a53aa99f289.second_name: Calligraphic composition describing the noble qualities of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh)
8483f56d-4097-5e63-a47a-8a53aa99f289.description2: Despite the steady advance of western-style artworks, traditional Ottoman arts and crafts did not disappear entirely. This hilye or word portrait of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) has been rendered on tripartite, foldable cardboard, decorated on the outside with elaborate ebru paper marbling. Its composition follows a layout current since the 11th/17th century when it was devised by the famous Ottoman calligrapher Hafiz Osman (1052-1110 H/1642-1698CE). Traditionally, the hilye presents Hadith recounting the noble physical and spiritual attributes of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), often embellished with rich illumination. A large oval cartouche, with the hadith in black naskhi, appears in the centre, surrounded by four roundels naming the four rightly-guided caliphs Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali. Above the cartouche, the Bismillah is written in thuluth style. Below, a verse from the Holy Qur'an (68:4) is followed by the last lines of the hadith, a prayer, the names of the artist and two individuals certifying his work, and the date. All calligraphic elements are set against a stippled gold background enhanced with European-style floral elements.

84d4fca3-e4d2-596e-bea2-0a5eda7a5ccf.name: Traditional dress for a *shaykh* or *shaykha*
84d4fca3-e4d2-596e-bea2-0a5eda7a5ccf.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
84d4fca3-e4d2-596e-bea2-0a5eda7a5ccf.materials: The original were made of silk, velvet, gemstones, cashmere, satin, gold, silver
84d4fca3-e4d2-596e-bea2-0a5eda7a5ccf.second_name: Costume of the shaykha and of the shaykh of Keserwan
84d4fca3-e4d2-596e-bea2-0a5eda7a5ccf.description2: Featured here is the traditional dress for the *shaykh* and *shaykha* of the Keserwan district. The *kubran* is an embroidered jacket (with or without sleeves) made of silk or velvet. The *gumbaz* is a long dress or coat embroidered with gold or silver and sometimes adorned with semi-precious jewels. It consisted of three panels and was split on either side of the body, beginning from the hip area. Other components of this traditional attire were a *mentiene* (blouse), the *shirwal* baggy trousers, a velvet or satin cape with gold or silver embroidery, and a long belt called a *shamle* or *zunnar* made of silk or cashmere depending on the season, and which was wrapped around the waist or hips.

84d5ec45-7bab-5d25-96f2-a48ed1fe7a85.name: *Entrance to Damascus*
84d5ec45-7bab-5d25-96f2-a48ed1fe7a85.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
84d5ec45-7bab-5d25-96f2-a48ed1fe7a85.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
84d5ec45-7bab-5d25-96f2-a48ed1fe7a85.artist: W. H. McFarlane (after a drawing by Harry Fenn 1838 – 1911)
84d5ec45-7bab-5d25-96f2-a48ed1fe7a85.description2: This coloured engraving by W. H. McFarlane shows the entrance to Damascus by the new French-built road through the Merj, or meadow, west of the city. Most probably this is the carriage road that had been established between Beirut and Damascus in 1863, at a time when most other connecting arterties were mere mule paths. French firms also built railways and ports in Syria during the later 19th century. The Ottoman style building in the background on the right is the Tekkiye Mosque Complex, built on the banks of the Barada river at the orders of Suleiman the Magnificent between 1554-1560 and incorporating a mosque, accomodation, a soup kitchen and a hospice.

84e87029-cd5f-539a-b16a-a7fedf6f4c7f.name: The Court Martial at the Palace of Justice
84e87029-cd5f-539a-b16a-a7fedf6f4c7f.author: Giulia Barrera
84e87029-cd5f-539a-b16a-a7fedf6f4c7f.second_name: The military court set up by British authorities in Alexandria (Egypt) in 1882
84e87029-cd5f-539a-b16a-a7fedf6f4c7f.description2:
The author of this picture, Luigi Fiorillo, was an Italian photographer who migrated to Alexandria (Egypt) around 1870 and opened a successful photography shop. In 1877, he participated as photographer in an expedition to Shewa region (Ethiopia), organised by the Italian Geographical Society, and ten years later in an Italian military expedition for the colonial conquest of Eritrea.  
In 1882, Fiorillo was one of the few Europeans who remained in Alexandria after the anti-foreign rioting and documented the consequences of the British bombardment on Alexandria of July 11th. He collected 50 pictures of the city in ruins in an album titled “Souvenir d'Alexandrie: Ruines, 1882”.  
On the back of some photos that he took in the 1880s, Fiorillo defines himself as “le photographe de Son Altesse le Prince Mohammed Toussoun Pasha” (the photographer of his Majesty Prince Mohammed Toussoun Pasha). Luigi Fiorillo died in 1898.

en: Silingardi, Adriano, ”Luigi Fiorillo, l’avventuroso fotografo di Alessandria d’Egitto”, unpublished paper (available on line) for the exhibition of the same name, Genoa, 2014.

84f5327f-428b-5355-b4b7-9d4e62a12ef9.name: *Bashi Bazouk*
84f5327f-428b-5355-b4b7-9d4e62a12ef9.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
84f5327f-428b-5355-b4b7-9d4e62a12ef9.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
84f5327f-428b-5355-b4b7-9d4e62a12ef9.description2: This colourful watercolour, executed by the Istanbul-based, Maltese painter V. A. Preziosi, shows a Bashi Bazouk, a member of the irregular forces of the Ottoman army that came into use in the late 18th century. The bashi bazouk were mercenaries of great ethnic diversity, often from the Balkans, who fought for the Ottomans in hope of plunder, as they were not paid. An attempt by Husrev Pasha in Egypt to disband his Albanian bashi bazouks in favor of his regular forces began the rioting which led to the establishment of Muhammad Ali's rule. The bashi bazouk did not wear regular uniforms. In this case, the flamboyant character depicted here with his formidable moustache wears an astonishing array of clothing: a towering turban with tassles, an embroidered shirt and waistcoat with large open sleeves, a voluminous waistband and trousers. The outfit is finished off by elaborate footwear. A large yatagan dagger is secured in the waistband across the soldier's front, a gun slung across his chest.

84f69ff8-6c1a-5173-a0c7-4b706dba6ef1.name: Arabian Fantasy
84f69ff8-6c1a-5173-a0c7-4b706dba6ef1.author: Marina Minozzi
84f69ff8-6c1a-5173-a0c7-4b706dba6ef1.keywords: Orientalism; reinvention; historical events in paintings; Orientalist topics; exoticism; diplomatic mission; Morocco; Mulay al-Hasan; travel; travelling artist; Italian travellers; Italian painters; Edmondo de Amicis; Marocco; travel book
84f69ff8-6c1a-5173-a0c7-4b706dba6ef1.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
84f69ff8-6c1a-5173-a0c7-4b706dba6ef1.description2: Stefano Ussi lived between Florence and Rome, studied at the Academy of Fine Arts of Florence and then enrolled as a volunteer in the first Italian War of Independence, during which he was taken prisoner by the Austrian troops. He developed a model of historic painting characterized by a quick application of layers (almost a rough draft) and by a sharp chiaroscuro. In 1875 he followed a diplomatic delegation to Morocco, in which the painter Biseo and the writer De Amicis also took part. The Arabian Fantasy documents the "Lab-el-barode", a game with the dust played in honor of the Italian delegation. This episode was masterly described by the writer Edmondo De Amicis.

85842d41-d3a1-5921-ac88-903643f0147a.name: Moorish Kiosk in Linderhof Palace Park
85842d41-d3a1-5921-ac88-903643f0147a.type: Pavillion; Park building in Linderhof Palace Park
85842d41-d3a1-5921-ac88-903643f0147a.history:
Linderhof Palace Park was laid out from 1870 to 1880 from plans by Carl von Effner. Ludwig II decorated the park and its environs with architectural features conjuring up the world of the Orient, such as the Moorish Kiosk and the Moroccan House, or scenes from Wagner's operas, such as the Venus Grotto. Hunding's Hut and the Gurnemanz Hermitage.  
The Moorish Kiosk was built in 1867 as the Prussian contribution to the World Exhibition in Paris. In 1870 the "railway king" Henry Strousberg bought the pavilion. After Strousberg's bankruptcy, Ludwig II bought the building in 1876 for Linderhof Palace Park and had it rebuilt and reappointed to his specifications.
85842d41-d3a1-5921-ac88-903643f0147a.keywords: King Ludwig II; Linderhof Palace; Ettal; Moorish style; Romanticism; gardens
85842d41-d3a1-5921-ac88-903643f0147a.description2: The Moorish Kiosk is located high above the park on two terrace levels. A colourful, exotic arrangement of palms, pomegranate trees and numerous flowering shrubs extends the foreign atmosphere of the Kiosk outside the walls and also distinguishes its surroundings from the rest of the park. – Between 1972 and 1983 the kiosk was completely restored.

8609522c-18c6-5b1c-9149-7c3bb976c5b7.name: Neo-Mamluk, metal-inlaid copper alloy Table
8609522c-18c6-5b1c-9149-7c3bb976c5b7.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
8609522c-18c6-5b1c-9149-7c3bb976c5b7.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
8609522c-18c6-5b1c-9149-7c3bb976c5b7.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
8609522c-18c6-5b1c-9149-7c3bb976c5b7.keywords: Mamluk; blazon; kufi; thuluth; al-Nasir ibn al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun
8609522c-18c6-5b1c-9149-7c3bb976c5b7.materials: Sheet copper alloy with metal inlay
8609522c-18c6-5b1c-9149-7c3bb976c5b7.description2: In 13th/ 19th- century Egypt, the political, cultural and social climate increasingly encouraged a nationalistic reappraisal of indigenous heritage. The era of the Mamluks, who had ruled Egypt and Syria between the later 7th/13th and the early 10th/ 16th centuries, was particularly celebrated as a golden age in national history. As a result, artisans now turned their efforts to reviving the glories of Mamluk artefacts, and particularly their celebrated, silver- and gold-inlaid metalwork. This stand or table is an exquisite example of such revivalist work. It copies a famous Mamluk Qur’an stand in the Museum of Arab Art in Cairo, inscribed with the name of the Mamluk Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun (r. 1294-1340) and made by Muhammad ibn Sunqur al-Baghdadi.

863f2655-60dd-5322-acff-d958595ed2e2.name: *Società d'Esplorazione Commerciale in Africa*
863f2655-60dd-5322-acff-d958595ed2e2.second_name: Taken from *Carta economica della Tripolitana e Cirenaica, colle ultime esplorazioni, 1880-81-82 (ed. 1884)*
863f2655-60dd-5322-acff-d958595ed2e2.description2: This map shows Italian commercial expeditions in Africa, particularly in Tripolitania and Cyrenaica, between the years 1881 and 1882. In the search for a colonial empire Italy particularly targeted Libyan territory, for political and economic reasons, as well as for its proximity and the fact it once belonged to the Roman Empire.

8653fc72-b87d-51ed-9732-e87d6b42578c.name: The Palace of the Poste Italienne (Ruins)
8653fc72-b87d-51ed-9732-e87d6b42578c.author: Giulia Barrera
8653fc72-b87d-51ed-9732-e87d6b42578c.second_name: The ruins of the Italian Post Office in Alexandria (Egypt) after the bombing of the city by the British Navy in 1882
8653fc72-b87d-51ed-9732-e87d6b42578c.description2:
The author of this picture, Luigi Fiorillo, was an Italian photographer who migrated to Alexandria (Egypt) around 1870 and opened a successful photography shop. In 1877, he participated as photographer in an expedition to Shewa region (Ethiopia), organised by the Italian Geographical Society, and ten years later in an Italian military expedition for the colonial conquest of Eritrea.  
In 1882, Fiorillo was one of the few Europeans who remained in Alexandria after the anti-foreign rioting and documented the consequences of the British bombardment on Alexandria of July 11th. He collected 50 pictures of the city ruins in an album titled “Souvenir d'Alexandrie: Ruines, 1882”.  
On the back of some photos that he took in the 1880s Fiorillo defines himself as “le photographe de Son Altesse le Prince Mohammed Toussoun Pasha” (the photographer of his Majesty Prince Mohammed Toussoun Pasha). Luigi Fiorillo died in 1898.

en: Silingardi, Adriano, ”Luigi Fiorillo, l’avventuroso fotografo di Alessandria d’Egitto”, unpublished paper (available on line) for the exhibition of the same name, Genoa, 2014.

868c8876-a63c-5812-a3d6-8c1fbf7d0e19.name: *Panoramic view of the Isthmus of the Suez, tracing the canal between the two seas*
868c8876-a63c-5812-a3d6-8c1fbf7d0e19.artist: Louis Maurice Adolphe Linant de Bellefonds
868c8876-a63c-5812-a3d6-8c1fbf7d0e19.keywords: Suez canal; Egypt; Ferdinand de Lesseps
868c8876-a63c-5812-a3d6-8c1fbf7d0e19.description2: Between 1859 and 1869, the Compagnie Universelle du Canal Maritime de Suez built a canal joining the Red Sea to the Mediterranean, thus opening up a strategic trade route towards the Indian subcontinent. This panoramic image was drawn by Louis Maurice Adolphe Linant de Bellefonds (1798–1883), artist and explorer fascinated with Egypt who played a key role, alongside Ferdinand de Lesseps, in the planning and construction of the Suez Canal.

868e1d9c-d782-5ab4-a356-d8e849b96e6c.name: *Description de L'Egypte: Antiquités Planches*
868e1d9c-d782-5ab4-a356-d8e849b96e6c.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. The *Description de l'Égypte* was a series of publications, appearing first in 1809 and continuing until the final volume in 1829, which offered a comprehensive scientific description of ancient and modern Egypt as well as its natural history. It is the collaborative work of about 160 civilian scholars and scientists, known popularly as the savants, who accompanied Napoleon's expedition to Egypt in 1798 to 1801 as part of the French Revolutionary Wars, as well as about 2000 artists and technicians, including 400 engravers, who would later compile it into a full work.

86959e1d-38a4-5f53-9007-4188fc788f51.name: Post card sent via *Poste-Cherifienne*
86959e1d-38a4-5f53-9007-4188fc788f51.description: A postcard dated 13 February 1920 sent via the postal service that connected the city of Tétouan, which was a city under the Spanish Protectorate, with the town of Kasr el-Kabir, which was on the border between the French and Spanish protectorates. On the postcard are two stamps of five cents and twenty-five cents. The front of the postcard shows a picture of a Moroccan *Rakkas* (runner or messenger).
86959e1d-38a4-5f53-9007-4188fc788f51.keywords: Postal office; Spanish protectorate; rakkas; postal system; delivery

869766dc-71ca-53a7-b67f-e1ed2b58d4ac.name: La Goulette
869766dc-71ca-53a7-b67f-e1ed2b58d4ac.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
869766dc-71ca-53a7-b67f-e1ed2b58d4ac.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
869766dc-71ca-53a7-b67f-e1ed2b58d4ac.description2: The expansion of the city of Tunis necessitated the construction of a large modern port which would be accessible to large-tonnage ships. Thus, in the early years of the French protectorate, the port of Tunis, La Goulette, saw a sharp increase in traffic. As well as a fishing port, the primary function of La Goulette, it also became an industrial centre thanks to the construction of a power plant on the north side of the canal, which served the tramways and the electric railway going to the northern suburbs. Finally, on the eve of the war, La Goulette had also become a residential town, particularly popular in summer for its seaside resorts.

86c2720a-384b-58d3-92a2-3fc1aefd7f1c.name: Small earthenware jar

On vase's belly, a row of medallions filled with flowers are bordered by a lattice strip and a herringbone strip on either side. The neck is decorated with alternating yellow, blue and green vertical lines. This item shows traces of both Ottoman and Andalusian influences.

87367afd-5729-556e-a43a-bec2611cfa83.name: *Napoléon II's journey to Algeria, 7 June 1865*
87367afd-5729-556e-a43a-bec2611cfa83.keywords: Diplomacy; Algeria; France; colonies; Napoléon III
87367afd-5729-556e-a43a-bec2611cfa83.second_name: Taken from *Histoire de l'Algérie et Voyage de Napoléon III en 1865. Photographies entre 1857 et 1867*
87367afd-5729-556e-a43a-bec2611cfa83.description2: Napoléon III visited Algeria twice during his reign (in 1860 and 1865). It was unusual at this time for the French head of state to travel outside the country, so these visits attracted much attention. They also allowed Napoléon to show how important Algeria was to him. He wanted to judge the complex situation which had been described to him in various reports for himself. A lavish welcome was prepared for him wherever he went during both his visits. This image, for example, shows an arc de triomphe which was erected in his honour at the terminus of a small mining train at Bouhamza.

874efcbf-3d66-55db-9523-6302edc55a76.name: Institut Pasteur
874efcbf-3d66-55db-9523-6302edc55a76.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
874efcbf-3d66-55db-9523-6302edc55a76.history: l'Institut Pasteur de Tunis, created in 1893 by the nephew of Louis Pasteur, Adrien Loir, was the third Institut Pasteur in the world after Paris and Hanoi (now Ho-Chi-Minh City), and one of the 32 Institut Pasteur centres scattered around the world. The institute aims to provide a pioneering health service in the field of prevention, prophylaxis and cutting-edge research. Its prestige can also be attributed to the doctor Charles Nicolle, who was the director between 1903 and 1936 and discovered the typhus virus during his time there. l'Institut Pasteur played a decisive role in the fight against certain illnesses, such as rabies. It remains today an important national and international reference centre for many illnesses.
874efcbf-3d66-55db-9523-6302edc55a76.keywords: Charles Nicolle; Institut Pasteur; Nobel prize
874efcbf-3d66-55db-9523-6302edc55a76.description2: Initially a rabies vaccine centre, this building then became a general vaccination centre and finally an analysis laboratory. It is located at the crossroads named Place Pasteur, not far from the old European quarter, and eventually expanded from three, to nine, to eighteen laboratories. One of its biggest missions was concerned with diagnosis and public health, another with the production of vaccines and serums, and a third concentrated on research, development and innovation. The research clinic matched patients to clinical trials and worked in coordination with the various different laboratories and research teams.

875b22bd-4eaf-5621-a282-05cb962a752c.name: Sursuq Palace
875b22bd-4eaf-5621-a282-05cb962a752c.description: Other than some nineteenth century plaster-work in the reception rooms which resembles Sicilian palaces of the time, and the employment of some Italian craftsmen, the Sursuq House was built in a strictly traditional Lebanese architectural and aesthetic style. This is indicated first and foremost by the use of a single large block. The Great Hall consists of four sets of traditional Lebanese triple-arches, each supported by fluted marble pillars. The house’s painted furnishings were commissioned and designed privately. It also contains a series of glass cabinets, displaying various valuable collections, including second century glassware and Lebanese jewellery. The garden is one of the largest gardens left in the city, with many landowners having sold their properties to speculative building projects. The kiosk in the garden, which was converted into a Turkish baths when the house was built in 1860, predates the main house and is used as visitor rooms today.
875b22bd-4eaf-5621-a282-05cb962a752c.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
875b22bd-4eaf-5621-a282-05cb962a752c.history: Built in 1860 for Musa Sursuq, in Rue Sursuq, Sursuq Palace is now the residence of his grand-daughter Lady Yvonne Cochrane, who inherited the estate at the age of two. Of all the Sursuq houses, this is the largest and the only one that preserves its original splendour. Its second owner, Lady Cochrane's father Alfred Bey Sursuq, increased the size of the gardens and expanded the house's collection of valuable pictures, carpets and objets d'art.

879c6b5d-7835-5885-8c9b-1e2618fa25ae.name: Coin
879c6b5d-7835-5885-8c9b-1e2618fa25ae.holder: Musée de la Monnaie : Banque Centrale de Tunisie

879c6b5d-7835-5885-8c9b-1e2618fa25ae.description2: This coin dating from the reign of is inscribed on one side with "20 francs" written in Arabic, the year 1325 from the Hijri calendar, and framed by an olive branch on the right and a palm leaf on the left. The reverse is inscribed with "20 francs" written in French, "Tunisia" and the year 1907, framed by a beaded border which is then decorated with two flower-stem reliefs, a crescent at the bottom and a star at the top.

87af700d-97ab-50c7-9235-e6cd264dbbcc.name: Plaque on the rocks of Nahr al-Kalb documenting the end of WWI
87af700d-97ab-50c7-9235-e6cd264dbbcc.holder: Nahr al-Kalb Authority, Ministry of Tourism
87af700d-97ab-50c7-9235-e6cd264dbbcc.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
87af700d-97ab-50c7-9235-e6cd264dbbcc.keywords: Politics; Army; World War I; Battalion; Memory
87af700d-97ab-50c7-9235-e6cd264dbbcc.description2: This plaque was erected by the French General Gouraud in 1920 to commemorate the entry of French troops in Damascus and their subsequent victory at the battle of Maysalun in July 1920. The text, written in French, is composed of 22 lines and lists the names of the battalions that took part in the battle. The plaque is decorated with bronze embellishments.

87e70362-8746-56dc-8457-3ebaaa0bc58a.name: Ottoman map of the Romanian countries
87e70362-8746-56dc-8457-3ebaaa0bc58a.description2: This is a map of Moldavia and Wallachia dating from after 1812, when following the Russian-Ottoman war of 1806-1812 Russia annexed the Eastern part of Moldavia, thereafter called Bessarabia (which used to be the name by which southern Moldavia was known). The red line marks the new border that the peace treaty of Bucharest (1812) established between the Ottoman Empire and Russia. The light blue line marks the border between Moldavia and Wallachia, the yellow one that between Austria and the Ottoman Empire and the thick blue line represents the border between Bulgaria and Wallachia. The green line marks the frontiers of the Ottoman Empire.

87e89e1f-16b1-5dc6-9a0f-3df85a103fa8.name: Moroccan coins
87e89e1f-16b1-5dc6-9a0f-3df85a103fa8.description: Coin struck in 1903 under Mulay Sultan ‘Abd al-‘Aziz al-Hasan I (r. 1894 to 1908) at the mint in Fez. For a century (1800-1900) the ‘Alawid sultans struck coins in the workshops of Fez, but due to the economic crisis at the time, gold was unavailable so most coins were of silver, bronze or other common metals – although the technique remained the same, with the metal poured into moulds. The patterns on the face and on the back vary between the star with eight points (Solomon ring) and the indication of the place of mint.
87e89e1f-16b1-5dc6-9a0f-3df85a103fa8.holder: Numismatic Museum of the al-Maghreb Bank
87e89e1f-16b1-5dc6-9a0f-3df85a103fa8.keywords: Coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; gold; silver; bronze; mint; moulding; moulds; six-pointed star; ring; workshop; traditional coinage; European influence

87f34acd-b200-5f1a-b478-34b80e307ce2.name: Spanish Franciscan Church of Buenaventura
87f34acd-b200-5f1a-b478-34b80e307ce2.history: Built in 1890, the church closed in 1968 and remained abandoned until fairly recently. When restoration of the Old *Medina* began, the church was selected for renovation and now has exhibition and media spaces, a comprehensive library of over 6,000 titles and a discovery space for children.
87f34acd-b200-5f1a-b478-34b80e307ce2.keywords: Religious building; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic architecture in Morocco; Islamic influence; traditional building; traditional city; city; urban space; Islamic city; Islamic urban space; plan; urban planning; church; Spanish in Morocco; Moroccan city; Christians in Morocco; migration; work
87f34acd-b200-5f1a-b478-34b80e307ce2.description2: Built for the Spanish community based in Casablanca, this church stands in the Old *Medina* on land donated by Sultan Mulay al-Hasan I. The construction of this church testifies to the improving relationship between Morocco and Spain and highlights the importance of the Spanish community in Casablanca, which was very active in the port sector and played a dynamic role in the local and international economy.

8824c22c-0cd4-502b-8da0-b722a3dd6846.name: *Izzedin Yusuf Effendi (1875–1916)*
8824c22c-0cd4-502b-8da0-b722a3dd6846.description2: Portrait of Izzedin Yusuf Effendi (1875–1916). He was the heir to the throne. In 1916 he committed suicide.

884ca90f-561a-57c1-913d-b4aab82da583.name: Pendant necklace
884ca90f-561a-57c1-913d-b4aab82da583.description: This beautiful triangular pendant necklace shows a loop chain decorated with four little floral ornaments and the main pendant decorated small red and green mounted crystals. This also has a shared connection with the traditional Fátima Hand motif.
884ca90f-561a-57c1-913d-b4aab82da583.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes, Cristina Giménez

884d9ccd-97ec-51c8-aec6-d384ad59224c.name: A Tunisian decoration (on the right) and an Italian decoration (on the left) awarded to a member of the Moreno family
884d9ccd-97ec-51c8-aec6-d384ad59224c.author: Massimo Sanacore
884d9ccd-97ec-51c8-aec6-d384ad59224c.archival: ASLi, Famiglia Moreno di Tunisi, b. 17
884d9ccd-97ec-51c8-aec6-d384ad59224c.description2:
Two members of the Moreno family, Raffaello (Tunis 1844-1913) and his brother Leone (Tunis, 1852-1940) were awarded honours both by the Italian King (Cavaliere dell’Ordine della Corona d’Italia) and by the Bey of Tunis (Nichan Iftikhar). The Morenos were Jews from Livorno (Italy), who had migrated to Tunisia in the early 19th century.  
Other Italians migrants in Tunisia were awarded both the title of Cavaliere dell’Ordine della Corona d’Italia by the Italian King and the title of Nichan Iftikhar by the Bey of Tunis, including Giuseppe Di Vittorio (a Sicilian who ran a construction company) and Luigi Rey (born in Tunis to an immigrant family from a village north of Turin, Piedmont, Italy, who also ran a construction company) and the Jewish Doctor Giacomo Castelnuovo.

88655ec5-19eb-505b-a6c2-72dc2d1fac7d.name: The Cotton Museum at the Agricultural museum
88655ec5-19eb-505b-a6c2-72dc2d1fac7d.author: Ibrahim Abdel Aziz
88655ec5-19eb-505b-a6c2-72dc2d1fac7d.history:
King Fu\`ad I chose the palace of Fatma Ismail, the daughter of Khedive Ismail, ‎to host the displays of the Agricultural Museum. The ‎palace was chosen due to its location near the Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture in the ‎neighborhood of Dokki in Cairo. ‎  
The museum, which was first called "The Agricultural Museum of King Fu\`ad I", was officially opened for the public on the 16th of January 1938 in a big ceremony that the king himself attended.
88655ec5-19eb-505b-a6c2-72dc2d1fac7d.description2: This building is used as a display museum to show the types of cotton seeds and strains in Egypt next to the products that come from each type. Egyptian cotton is preferred around the world because of its long fibre, which make it softer and stronger at the same time. For many years, it was so valuable that most of the crop was exported to European countries, and Egyptians themselves could hardly buy items made from its cloth.

887bfe33-59d1-51d9-bdbb-0669dffbc312.name: *Nebamun tomb paintings*
887bfe33-59d1-51d9-bdbb-0669dffbc312.keywords: archaeology; Egyptomania; exploration; collection; collecting; wall painting; museums; travel; traveller; printing

888046f7-3ef2-5941-9017-769431669b16.name: Ring
888046f7-3ef2-5941-9017-769431669b16.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
888046f7-3ef2-5941-9017-769431669b16.author: Huda Kilani
888046f7-3ef2-5941-9017-769431669b16.keywords: Floral decoration; religious objects; waqf; Qur’an; Ottoman Baroque-Rococo
888046f7-3ef2-5941-9017-769431669b16.description2:
Thin silver ring with a squared black stone set in silver. Silver jewellery was the most common, because only rich people could afford gold jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom.  
Jordan's economy in the late 19th and early 20th centuries relied on trades and crafts and new waves of people started to come to Jordan and began to settle for this purpose. This object is an example of how traditional fashion reflected the variegated population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is also an example of local personal attire, fashion, costumes and rites.

88ae5c68-848d-500a-a14d-08612e65ec15.name: *Traitor*
88ae5c68-848d-500a-a14d-08612e65ec15.author: Petar Petrovic
88ae5c68-848d-500a-a14d-08612e65ec15.description2: During his frequent travels across the Balkans in the 1880s, Paja Jovanović acquainted himself with the ethnic makeup of the population, particularly in Lower Zeta (present-day Podgorica and the surrounding area), in the neighbourhood of Bar and in the border-lying area with Albania. It was here that Albanian, Serbian and Montenegrin inhabitants intermingled, so their characters, physiognomies, customs and vivid national costumes were entwined and fused into a whole in the paintings of Paja Jovanović. The image of capturing or trying a traitor, who, according to tribal custom, awaited sentencing, is certainly a noteworthy genre subject among those he selected to depict the life and customs of peoples in the Balkans. Unlike the first version, painted by Jovanović in 1885, this replica of The Traitor from the mid-1920s was painted in a more free-handed manner, in broad brush strokes and without insistence on details.

88e039ef-da59-59a2-bb4a-56259bea2878.name: *French conquest of Tunisia - the battle of Jebel Hadada. 26 avril 1881*
88e039ef-da59-59a2-bb4a-56259bea2878.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
88e039ef-da59-59a2-bb4a-56259bea2878.author: Bechir Yazidi
88e039ef-da59-59a2-bb4a-56259bea2878.description2: Published in a colonial newspaper, this image was intended to highlight the strength of the French army in the face of the Tunisian resistance, which seems unable to hold them back. It depicts one of the episodes which preceded the Treaty of Bardo and took place on the Algerian-Tunisian border near the town of Kef. Zouave troops can be seen at the front of the French troops.

88f4e317-6501-5591-b5b3-41a03b3515d2.name: *Strike fund*
88f4e317-6501-5591-b5b3-41a03b3515d2.description2: "Strike funds" were established during strikes, collecting money which they received from donations and subscription fees. These funds are able to financially support strikers, who no longer received their salaries and therefore had no means of survival. This drawing emphasises the anxiety on the faces of the workers and their families, who relied wholly on this solidarity for their food and lodgings. It also mocks the role of the Minister of the Interior, who was sending in military troops instead of funds. Indeed, many strikes were interrupted by the arrival of military forces between 1899 and 1901.

88f77e6f-b366-5a53-b251-ec7744293c37.description2: View of the people working at the excavations in the area of Abusir during their break. They are supervised by the foreman with the German archaeologists Juncker and Steindorff. The photo dates to 1904.

8951f6af-b5d8-564b-983b-9fd818e52be8.name: Tabla
8951f6af-b5d8-564b-983b-9fd818e52be8.holder: Lebanese National Higher Conservatory of Music
8951f6af-b5d8-564b-983b-9fd818e52be8.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
8951f6af-b5d8-564b-983b-9fd818e52be8.description2: The *tabla*, also known as the *durbakke*, is a small hand drum very common in traditional Arabic music. It is shaped like a vase, and is covered at the top with goat skin. *Tabla*s are often beautifully decorated, with metal, bone inlay, or paint.

896932e2-74ee-5217-8b67-feb647e4f883.name: *4 June 1913, Gand, \[pavilion from\] Tunisia \[Exposition Universelle et Internationale\]*
896932e2-74ee-5217-8b67-feb647e4f883.description2: In 1913, Gand (Belgium) hosted the 28th Exposition Universelle (world fair). Like France, Belgium gave pride of place to its colonies. During its world fairs, France tended to exhibit a number of colonial pavilions, whose architecture and "exoticism" fascinated visitors. The "Tunisian souk" was named thus in order to highlight the economic benefits of colonialism for Europe.

8985fc96-8186-5025-a7f2-72ef2dcdcfcb.name: Decoration of the Egyptian collection of Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna

8985fc96-8186-5025-a7f2-72ef2dcdcfcb.description2: Copy of paintings from the tomb of Chnum-hotep II in Beni Hassan from the Egyptian pavilion of the 1873 World's Fair in Vienna.

89881283-d829-5946-bd7c-505438d8c8c0.name: Costume for Cleopatra in the Ballets Russes production of *Cléopâtre*, 1918
89881283-d829-5946-bd7c-505438d8c8c0.holder: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
89881283-d829-5946-bd7c-505438d8c8c0.author: Kaye Spilker
89881283-d829-5946-bd7c-505438d8c8c0.artist: Sonia Terk Delaunay (born Russia, active France, 1885-1979)
89881283-d829-5946-bd7c-505438d8c8c0.keywords: Clothing; theatre; dance; fashion; abstract decoration; exoticism; textile; painting; coreography; abstract art; avant-garde
89881283-d829-5946-bd7c-505438d8c8c0.materials: Silk, sequins, mirror, beads, wool yarn, metallic thread braid, lamé
89881283-d829-5946-bd7c-505438d8c8c0.description2: The sets and many costumes for the 1909 *Cleopatre* were destroyed in a fire during the company’s 1917 South American tour, so painter Sonia Delaunay was commissioned to fashion new costumes for the principals. The artist’s palette of brilliant color, graphic design, and combination of textures resulted in costumes markedly different from the originals. Cleopatra’s luminous dress, reflecting the abstract forms in Sonia Delaunay’s paintings, as well as aspects of fashionable dress of the period, remains one of her most significant creations for the theatre.

898f2296-ee1f-5e48-a6ee-73f0b9a210a9.name: *Head of the Great Sphinx, Pyramids of Geezeh July 17th, 1839*
898f2296-ee1f-5e48-a6ee-73f0b9a210a9.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
898f2296-ee1f-5e48-a6ee-73f0b9a210a9.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
898f2296-ee1f-5e48-a6ee-73f0b9a210a9.description2: Roberts depicted the Sphinx some twenty years after Giovanni Battista Caviglia had excavated at Giza in 1817 and had cleared masses of sand away from the monument, which up to that point had been buried right up to its neck. Subsequently, he succeeded in clearing the whole front of the Sphinx. At the point of Roberts’ visit, the sphinx was visible from the top of the head to the floor of the temple between its paws. After its initial discovery, the Sphinx soon became one of the foremost fascinations for early European Egyptologists, including Auguste Mariette, the founder and first director of the Egyptian Museum in Cairo, Gaston Maspero, who conducted a survey  of it in 1886, and the British scholar E. A. Wallis Budge.It also proved fascinating for Orientalist artists and artisans all over Europe. In Roberts' artwork, the stone-cut monument is rendered in great detail, carefully recording also the far-reaching damage to the Sphinx’s face, the cause of which had already given rise to much discussion and speculation at the time. The Pyramids in this view are that of Cheops, or the Great Pyramid, seen on the right, and on the left, that of Cephren, also known as the Second Pyramid.
898f2296-ee1f-5e48-a6ee-73f0b9a210a9.artist_birthplace: David Roberts: Edinburgh, Scotland; Louis Hague: Tournai, Belgium
898f2296-ee1f-5e48-a6ee-73f0b9a210a9.artist_deathplace: David Roberts: London; Louis Hague: London

8993cd54-bcab-5bf3-83fb-e37e53bc3db3.name: Jeita Grotto
8993cd54-bcab-5bf3-83fb-e37e53bc3db3.description: Covering a span of over 9 kilometres, the Jeita Grotto forms the biggest Middle Eastern karstic cave complex. It consists of two different, but interconnected, caverns shaped over millions of years by the dissolution and accumulation of layers of limestone. The Jeita upper cave is 2,130 metres long, although only one third (750 metres) is open to visitors. The cave contains a variety of stone formations such as stalagmites, stalactites, natural columns, mushrooms, ponds, curtains and draperies. The lower cave is 60 metres beneath the first, and is almost three times as long. The floor of this cave consists of a long underwater river and lake, nicknamed the "Dark Lake". The lower cave is closed during the winter months due to high water levels.
8993cd54-bcab-5bf3-83fb-e37e53bc3db3.author: Julien El Khoury, Jeff El-Msanne
8993cd54-bcab-5bf3-83fb-e37e53bc3db3.history: Although there is evidence the cave was used in antiquity, the modern discovery of the cave is credited to American missionary Reverend William Thomson, who ventured about 50 meters into the cave until reaching the underground river. He realised he had discovered a cave of great importance after firing a shot and hearing the resulting echoes. J. W. Maxwell and H. G. Huxley of the Beirut Water Company and Dr. Daniel Bliss, then president of the Syrian Protestant College (now the American University of Beirut) ventured a kilometre into the cave in two expeditions in 1873 and 1874. American, English and French explorers carried out further expeditions in 1892 and 1940 which brought them to a depth of 1,750 metres. Lebanese explorers pushed even further into the cave in the following decades.

89a137fb-7ff4-50b4-b635-4fb544d4dd2a.name: *Winters in Algeria*
89a137fb-7ff4-50b4-b635-4fb544d4dd2a.author: Leila Zeghmi
89a137fb-7ff4-50b4-b635-4fb544d4dd2a.description2: Between 1872 and 1873, the famous American Orientalist painter Frederick Arthur Bridgman went on a long trip around North Africa, travelling from Tangier to Algiers, via Tlemcen, Oran, Constantine and Biskra. This trip was the inspiration for his book *Winters in Algeria*, which contains many of his works depicting Algerians' daily lives in the late 19th century.

89aeb1ca-95c8-5b49-a594-4779f19544dd.name: A woman at a sewing machine, making dresses for her daughters

89b9e8c6-f3d0-5b3f-8890-c5a4ed5ba8cf.name: Dreams
89b9e8c6-f3d0-5b3f-8890-c5a4ed5ba8cf.author: Marina Minozzi
89b9e8c6-f3d0-5b3f-8890-c5a4ed5ba8cf.keywords: Realism; Italian painters; social topics; post-unitarian Italian society; woman; women's condition; women's rights; social changes; education; women's education; literacy; illiteracy; fashion; international exhibitions; international exposition
89b9e8c6-f3d0-5b3f-8890-c5a4ed5ba8cf.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
89b9e8c6-f3d0-5b3f-8890-c5a4ed5ba8cf.description2: Vittorio Corcos is well known for his realistic paintings, especially his portraits of women. The woman depicted in the painting *Dreams* is Elena Vecchi, the daughter of a friend of the painter. Elena spent her adolescence at Corcos’ home. Presented in 1897 at the International Exposition Art of Florence, the portrait drew great attention and critical and public acclaim. Given the subject and its allusive title, it’s possible to see the image of a modern, proud and aware young woman that hitherto was represented only in literature: on the contrary, Corcos was able to masterfully represent it in painting. The scene was so admired that it was also reproduced on postcards. Corcos believed that while a portrait of a man has to show his social status, that of a woman always has to be appealing even if she is eighty years old.
89b9e8c6-f3d0-5b3f-8890-c5a4ed5ba8cf.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

89d4c66b-a374-55e7-8284-7f6b427b03c0.description: This painting by António Ramalho (1859–1916) portrays European fascination for eastern cultures. As well as wearing a Japanese costume, the figure in the painting is surrounded by oriental objects in a clear reference to his aesthetic preferences.

89f4e566-e82c-56e3-b94a-d8bd68a1f680.description2: Sheet from *Costumes Turcs*, a lavish set of volumes produced in Turkey for a European audience. They present the appearance of people from different areas, with different jobs etc. *Tercüman*, the interpreter of a diplomatic mission.

8a101d28-6d11-5832-8d73-47c11308f989.name: Letter from Father Joseph Yazbek to the Maronite Patriarch Yuhanna el-Hajj
8a101d28-6d11-5832-8d73-47c11308f989.holder: House of the Maronite Patriarchate of Antioch and all the East
8a101d28-6d11-5832-8d73-47c11308f989.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
8a101d28-6d11-5832-8d73-47c11308f989.description2: A small but growing Maronite community settled in the Chinatown area of Boston in the 1890s. In 1893, the Archbishop of Boston, John Williams, assigned F. Gabriel Korkemaz as the first Maronite priest. He was succeeded by his cousin, F. Stephan Korkemaz, two years later, and shortly afterwards by F. Joseph Yazbek. At the time, the hundred-or-so families that formed Boston's Maronite community worshiped at the St. James' Church on Harrison Avenue. Father Yazbek later bought a four-storey building on Tyler Street, which he remodelled to include a chapel, social hall, and priest's residence. This letter is a copy of a letter sent by Father Yazbek to the Maronite Patriarch Yuhanna el-Hajj, inviting him to the ceremony dedicating the Syro-Maronite chapel to Our Lady of the Cedars of Lebanon.

8a11b8a8-3b2f-5ba0-8118-5ec32059a75d.name: Book cover
8a11b8a8-3b2f-5ba0-8118-5ec32059a75d.holder: Musée des Arts Islamiques de Kairouan
8a11b8a8-3b2f-5ba0-8118-5ec32059a75d.provenance: La zaouia de Sidi Sahbi, Kairouan
8a11b8a8-3b2f-5ba0-8118-5ec32059a75d.description2: This book cover from Rabat is decorated with a red and gold moulded pattern. The central medallion contains various florets, with two teardrops in a similar pattern emanating from it. The rectangular borders are made of a geometric interlaced pattern, whereas the four concave corners are surrounded by a curved border and floral motifs. This cover is evidence of the influence of the Ottoman school on Tunisian book covers.

8a229227-3cb6-53ea-978a-a63f9f557d11.name: Patent for the invention of the fountain pen with a replaceable ink cartridge
8a229227-3cb6-53ea-978a-a63f9f557d11.description2: Pedagogue, engineer and mathematician Petrache Poenaru was the first Romanian inventor to obtain a patent. After 1821 he studied in Germany and then in France. While in Paris, he invented the fountain pen with a replaceable ink cartridge, a pen devised to ensure a constant flow of ink, preventing ink leaks, and to allow the replacement of some of the component parts. On 27 May 1827 the Manufactures Bureau within the French Ministry of Internal Affairs granted him for this invention a patent with a validity of five years. Although his invention did not become known at the time and was not commercially exploited, Poenaru is considered to be the first inventor to receive a patent for a fountain pen.

8a58f4f9-1644-5ff0-8f2d-9e17a9b86098.name: Bills from the Beirut Tramway and Electricity company
8a58f4f9-1644-5ff0-8f2d-9e17a9b86098.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury
8a58f4f9-1644-5ff0-8f2d-9e17a9b86098.description2: Two bills from the Beirut Tramway Company. The first is for the value of 22 Ottoman pounds, and is dated to 1 February 1896. The second is for the value of 11 Ottoman pounds and is dated to 1 November 1990.

8a6b8745-c790-5c63-ae1c-ad2221823d69.name: Fighting the influenza epidemic in England [with medicine for children]
8a6b8745-c790-5c63-ae1c-ad2221823d69.description2: An influenza epidemic swept through Europe after the First World War, killing millions of those who had been weakened by the war. Many failed attempts were made distribute preventative medicines, like in this English school.

8a6cfa46-5a45-55b6-8e98-9c89d191db94.name: Primary students at a village school in central Italy, which followed the teaching methods introduced by Maria Montessori
8a6cfa46-5a45-55b6-8e98-9c89d191db94.author: Giulia Barrera
8a6cfa46-5a45-55b6-8e98-9c89d191db94.archival: Collezione tessile di Tela Umbra, Fondo fotografico
8a6cfa46-5a45-55b6-8e98-9c89d191db94.description2:
When Italy became a nation state in 1861, the illiteracy rate in the country was 78 per cent. In 1901, it was still at 56 per cent. Illiteracy was particularly high in the countryside. In 1877, the “Coppino Law”, made elementary schools mandatory and free of charge.  
Maria Montessori (1870-1952) was a medical doctor who developed innovative teaching methods for primary-school children. Her educational methods were first applied in the first decade of the 20th century. They met with great success and were applied in thousands of schools all over Europe and North America.

8a70de1b-8f52-5be5-84b2-f02ae35a3ab5.name: ‘Abd-al-Hamid (Abdülhamid) II (1842–1918)
8a70de1b-8f52-5be5-84b2-f02ae35a3ab5.keywords: 'Abd-al-Hamid (Abdülhamid) II; Congress of Berlin; Bosnia-Herzegovina; Tunisia
8a70de1b-8f52-5be5-84b2-f02ae35a3ab5.description2: Portrait of 'Abd-al-Hamid (Abdülhamid) II (1842–1918). He was born in 1842 in Istanbul. In 1876 he became Sultan and after the lost war with Russia in 1877, he was forced to agree to the 1878 Congress of Berlin. The signatory powers of the congress allowed Austria to occupy Bosnia-Herzegovina, which belonged to the territory of the Ottoman Empire. In 1888 he had to accept the occupation of Tunisia by France. He tried to modernize the Ottoman Empire with the help of Germany, but in 1908 a revolution of Turkish officers forced him to abdicate. He died in 1918 in Istanbul.

8a730c5e-8120-5c99-a9fa-3fffc09ae06e.name: *Théâtre Impérial du Châtelet. Aladdin and the magnificent lamp; the genies of the lamp (ballet).*
8a730c5e-8120-5c99-a9fa-3fffc09ae06e.artist: Engraver: Auguste Tricon; artist: Auguste Belin
8a730c5e-8120-5c99-a9fa-3fffc09ae06e.archival: ESTAMPES SCENES Aladin ou la lampe merveilleuse (1)
8a730c5e-8120-5c99-a9fa-3fffc09ae06e.description2: The tale of Aladdin became very popular following the rise of Orientalism in the 1820s, and became the subject of multiple adaptations for opera and for theatre. In 1863 Adolphe d'Ennery and Hector Crémieux also transformed it into a "féerie" (fairy play). This féerie, a genre which chose great legends as its subject and spanned many different mediums (ballet, on-stage special effects) was extremely popular in 1860s France.

8aa9aed7-b2ea-50bd-90ad-08ec6d53d8f4.name: Portrait of Émile Prisse d'Avennes dressed in an imitation of the local style
8aa9aed7-b2ea-50bd-90ad-08ec6d53d8f4.description2: The engineer, painter and architect Prisse d'Avennes (1807–1879) lived in Egypt for 20 years, and was to a great extent assimilated into Egyptian society and had adopted many Egyptian customs. Other figures, such as Delacroix in Morocco and Flaubert in Egypt, were also fascinated by the landscapes, knowledge and customs of these countries, which became the inspiration for many of their works, thus initiating the trend of "Orientalist writing".

8ab890a6-368e-5ae9-b93d-cadc7d747a78.name: *Rusul Khyma with the attack of the Honorable Company's cruisers on the evening of 11 November 1809*
8ab890a6-368e-5ae9-b93d-cadc7d747a78.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
8ab890a6-368e-5ae9-b93d-cadc7d747a78.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
8ab890a6-368e-5ae9-b93d-cadc7d747a78.artist: R. Temple, HM 65th Regiment, Sixteen views; I. Clark, Sculpt.; William Haines, Publisher
8ab890a6-368e-5ae9-b93d-cadc7d747a78.description2: This image records one of the many battles between the fleet of the Qawasim rulers of the lower Gulf and the British, who were determined to end their economic and political hegemony in much of the region and gain overall control of the Gulf as a vital corridor between India, the Middle and Near East, and ultimately Britain.This composition shows the Qawasim stronghold of Ras al-Khaimah with the Hajjar mountains in the background, as seen from the sea by the artist, a soldier participating in the British attack on the town. A small number of British ships are positioned along the coast, and billowing smoke in the background on the right evokes an atmosphere of menace and impending major conflict. The British sent a squadron of frigates to Ras al Khaimah to attack and rout out the enemy. Troups disembarked in the afternoon, and despite all attempts by the Qasimi forces - their bravery and skillfullness even acknowledged by the British - by 10 o'clock the town was in ashes, the powerful fleet of the Qawasim, comprising more than 50 very large dhows, destroyed.

8ad123be-79dd-59a7-84a8-ffc0f7c6d8e7.name: *James Robertson and His Brother-in-Law Felice Beato in Turkish Costume*
8ad123be-79dd-59a7-84a8-ffc0f7c6d8e7.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
8ad123be-79dd-59a7-84a8-ffc0f7c6d8e7.keywords: self-portrait; watercolour on photographs; Felice Beato
8ad123be-79dd-59a7-84a8-ffc0f7c6d8e7.description2: A self-portrait of James Robertson and his brother-in-law Felice Beato standing side by side and dressed in Turkish costume is an important work in the history of photography. This picture is in every sense a coloured counterpart of two other portrait photographs by Robertson first brought to light by Bahattin Öztuncay in 1991. The image of Felice Beato in this identical photograph is the only known picture of him in his youth.

8b03882d-24a1-5f9c-9159-8596cb391505.name: *Pulpit on the Platform of the Mosque of Omar*
8b03882d-24a1-5f9c-9159-8596cb391505.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
8b03882d-24a1-5f9c-9159-8596cb391505.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
8b03882d-24a1-5f9c-9159-8596cb391505.keywords: Minbar al-Saif; al-Aqsa Mosque; Dome of the Rock; Haram al-Sharif; Jerusalem; Saladin; Burhan al-Din
8b03882d-24a1-5f9c-9159-8596cb391505.description2: This image, etched after having been originally drawn by Samuel Prout after a sketch made on the spot by F. Catherwood, shows the ‘Minbar al-Saif’ of the Al-Aqsa mosque precinct, on the southern side of the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, right next to the south gateway to its raised platform.  Originally built by Saladin in the 12th century, it was later restored in the 14th century by Burhan al-Din, whose name is also used to refer to the structure.  It forms an important part of the Haram al-Sharif revered by Muslims. The third-most sacred site in Islam, it marks Islam’s first qibla and the spot from which the Prophet undertook his night journey to heaven. The image was first published in 'Landscape Illustrations of the Bible', consisting of Views of the most remarkable places mentioned in the Old and New Testaments. From original sketches taken on the spot and engraved by W. And E. Finden. With descriptiions by the Rev. Rhomas Hartwell Horne, B.D. In 2 Vols, Vol 1, John Murray and Charles Tilt, London 1836.

8b3e69ba-c1ec-5cc8-a491-c79fd70669f0.name: Imaret
8b3e69ba-c1ec-5cc8-a491-c79fd70669f0.holder: IMARET – Institute Mohammed Ali for the Research of the Eastern Tradition (under contract with the Egyptian Waqf Organization)
8b3e69ba-c1ec-5cc8-a491-c79fd70669f0.author: I.M.A.R.E.T.
8b3e69ba-c1ec-5cc8-a491-c79fd70669f0.history: With the passage of time, the charitable and educational purposes of the foundation declined. According to surviving records, the School continued to function as late as 1902, and the Soup Kitchen as late as 1923. After the Lausanne Treaty and the exchange of populations between Greece and Turkey, the complex housed Greek refugees from Asia Minor (1927–1960). In 1954, Imaret was listed as a protected historical monument by the Greek Government. A series of (never realized) agreements between Greece and Egypt to restore the monument followed. In August 2001, a contract was signed between the Egyptian Waqf Organization and the Missirian family, who undertook the demanding task of restoring the two monuments and attributing them to new uses.
8b3e69ba-c1ec-5cc8-a491-c79fd70669f0.keywords: 19th century Ottoman baroque; Waqf; educational and charitable foundation; Mohammed Ali; Egypt; secular education in the Ottoman Empire
8b3e69ba-c1ec-5cc8-a491-c79fd70669f0.description2: *Imaret* was an educational and charitable foundation, donated by Mohammed ‘Ali, founder of modern Egypt, to his hometown. The complex included an elementary school and two higher level colleges dedicated to the instruction of the traditional Islamic curriculum, modern sciences and mathematics. It is one of the earliest examples of western style technical school providing secular education in the Ottoman Empire and reflects Mohammed ‘Ali’s program of modernization. The complex had 61 rooms for up to 300 boarding students, two study halls, a library, a printing press and a soup kitchen to feed students, travellers and the poor, regardless of religion. To meet the religious and hygiene needs of its occupants, the complex also contained a place for prayer, fountains for ablutions and a hammam. Cisterns underneath the structure guaranteed a continuous source of water.

8b529731-afad-5c0e-8816-7664ae89852a.name: Lithographed Qur’an, originally written by Shukr Zadeh (d. AH 1166 / AD 1753)
8b529731-afad-5c0e-8816-7664ae89852a.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
8b529731-afad-5c0e-8816-7664ae89852a.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
8b529731-afad-5c0e-8816-7664ae89852a.artist: Original calligraphed by Shukr Zadeh (d. AH 1166 / AD 1753)
8b529731-afad-5c0e-8816-7664ae89852a.description2: This Qur'an, originally caligraphed by the famous Ottoman calligrapher Shukr Zadeh is the first Qur'an to be printed in an Islamic country by way of lithograpy. It was produced around 1850 AD.While printing had begun in Europe many centuries ago, the Islamic world continued to favour handwritten books, and most certainly as regards copies of the Holy Qur’an. In 1834, the first edition of Gustav Fluegel’s printed Qur’an was published, while in the Ottoman Empire, the printing of Qur’ans began only in the second half of the 19th century, both in Egypt and in Istanbul. Most were lithographed, as they had the look and feel of manuscripts. Most importantly, all the required recitational signs could be rendered accurately.

8b5de31f-f1e0-5ddc-9d8a-dd777ed6d387.name: Mosaic for the inauguration of the Musée du Bardo
8b5de31f-f1e0-5ddc-9d8a-dd777ed6d387.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
8b5de31f-f1e0-5ddc-9d8a-dd777ed6d387.description2: This mosaic was made for the inauguration of the Musée Alaoui, now the Musée du Bardo, on 7 May 1888. At the top right-hand side we can see the Tunisian flag, on the left the the initials of the French General Residence in Tunisia, and in the centre the words  "Le Musée Alaoui"  in red letters. The inauguration was hosted by 'Ali Pacha Bey and the Resident-General M. J. Massicault. The names of the French civil servants who had accompanied the Resident-General and supervised the creation of the museum are written in two colums: M. Georges Perrot and M. Edouard Delpeuch, delegates from the Ministre de l'Instruction Publique des Beaux-Arts, M. Henri Wallon and M. Héron de Villefosse, from l’Académie des Inscriptions et Belles Lettres, and M. R. de la Blanchére, director of the Service des Antiquités et des Arts. Finally, the Arabic text at the bottom of the mosaic celebrates the inauguration of the museum.

8b77b70b-784c-5988-890e-779ea486c18e.name: Letter by the Prefect of Cosenza (Calabria, Italy) to the Ministry of Agriculture, Industry and Trade, referring to the exceedingly long working hours of women and children in the spinning factories
8b77b70b-784c-5988-890e-779ea486c18e.author: Margherita Martino
8b77b70b-784c-5988-890e-779ea486c18e.archival: ASCS, Prefettura, Affari generali, categoria 7, b. 523
8b77b70b-784c-5988-890e-779ea486c18e.description2: In Italy, the first law that introduced some forms of protection for female workers was approved in 1902 (l. 242/1902). It limited the working hours for women to 12 hours a day and introduced a one-month maternity leave after delivery. When this letter was written, there was a discussion in the country on the possible regulation of the working conditions of women and children. The Prefect of Cosenza reported that there were factories in which women and children worked from 4:30 in the morning to 10:30 at night.

8b7e80b3-625e-596c-a8d5-9f93e1bdc94b.type: Military object; firearms; arms and armour; artillery
8b7e80b3-625e-596c-a8d5-9f93e1bdc94b.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
8b7e80b3-625e-596c-a8d5-9f93e1bdc94b.keywords: Military object; Metalwork; Cast steel; Arms; armour; Wood; Carriage; Cannon
8b7e80b3-625e-596c-a8d5-9f93e1bdc94b.description2: This small cannon on wheels was used by the Ottoman soldiers in Lebanon in the 19th century to quash resistance movements. As the Lebanese resistance had no weapons of their own, the fighters frequently ambushed Ottoman soldiers and took their weapons. This cannon is an example of such weaponry, which was taken by the resistance and used against the Ottomans. The cannon is made of cast steel, with the chase, reinforce and cascable forged as one single part. It has two trunnions, used to mount the cannon on its carriage, a wooden body which is hollowed in the middle to make space for the cannon can pivot. It rest on a wooden cylinder and is linked by two wooden wheels.

8b996198-d4aa-5ddf-8793-9747fc36a20c.name: *1594 Burning of the Remains of St Sava*
8b996198-d4aa-5ddf-8793-9747fc36a20c.author: Petar Petrovic
8b996198-d4aa-5ddf-8793-9747fc36a20c.description2:
The Serb Stevan Aleksić was a student of Nikolaos Gyzis at the Munich Academy of Fine Arts. The painting presented here shows him as a representative of academic realism, yet at the same time testifies to a significant gift for a striking play of light effects.  
In 1594, the Ottoman conquerors burned the remains of the Orthodox Christian saint Sava in Belgrade as a punitive deterrent against Serbian rebellion. St. Sava had played a pivotal role in the early 13th century. He was not just an Orthodox archbishop, but also the author of the first Serbian legal code. The foreign rulers thus asserted an important symbol of their power. In order to preserve the memory of the people's saint, a small church was first built on the site. Then, in 1935, the Serbian Orthodox Church prepared the ground for the St. Sava Cathedral, today one of the largest Orthodox churches in the world.  
It is no surprise that Aleksić made this choice of subject in 1912, considering the political backdrop of the time. It was the year when Serbia joined the Balkan League, which launched the First Balkan War against the Ottoman Empire.
8b996198-d4aa-5ddf-8793-9747fc36a20c.artist_deathplace: Modos, Kingdom of Serbians, Croats and Slovenians (nowadays in Serbia)

8ba03860-993b-5dbf-9a66-b44cd6b52d86.name: Simplon-Orient Express Poster
8ba03860-993b-5dbf-9a66-b44cd6b52d86.description2: Roger Broders was a French illustrator and artist best known for his travel posters promoting tourism destinations in France. Broders' illustrations were distinctive for their simple lines and bold, flat areas of colour, combined with noticeable graphical perspective showing the featured mountains and seascapes in the background. Broders' illustrations depicting people show active, elongated figures wearing elegant, contemporary clothes. His posters were simply and boldly lettered identifying the destination, and were supplemented with a brief slogan.

8bca273e-4101-56b4-9c21-1783781d5f11.name: *The future kingdom*
8bca273e-4101-56b4-9c21-1783781d5f11.description2: The Franco-Prussian war (1870–71) led to the production of a great number of cartoons, in an attempt to lift morale and stay strong during the difficult conditions of Paris under siege. This cartoon mocks Bismarck and the Prussian soldiers.

8be256e6-ef08-535a-9646-fcfbd6751a6c.name: Beylerbeyi Palace
8be256e6-ef08-535a-9646-fcfbd6751a6c.keywords: Seaside palace; pavilion; Ottoman architecture; Bosphorus Strait; Sultan Abdülaziz
8be256e6-ef08-535a-9646-fcfbd6751a6c.description2: One of the most magnificent Ottoman coastal palaces, Beylerbeyi Palace is located on the Asian coast of the Bosphorus. It was commissioned by Sultan Abdülaziz and consists of the main palace structure and its auxiliaries. Its façade and interior decorations blend various Western influences with Eastern motifs. This summer residence is remarkable for its rich decoration and its two sea-pavilions on the water are the most striking and typical examples of Orientalism in Istanbul. It was opened to the public as a museum in 1984.

8c2abbac-16e2-5805-a239-068b6318e25d.name: *Hüdavendigar* Newspaper
8c2abbac-16e2-5805-a239-068b6318e25d.description2: After the *Tanzimat* (reforms), newspapers in Arabic, Persian, Bulgarian, Serbian, Albanian, Kurdish, English, French, Italian and German began appearing in the Ottoman Empire. Some of them were bilingual as Turkish-Greek, Turkish-Armenian and Turkish-Arabic. *Hüdavendigar* was a provincial newspaper of Bursa and it was first published on 19 February 1869. The same year, starting with the 80th issue, the back page was printed in Armenian. The paper was published twice (Wednesday and Saturday) and then four times a week. It was 50 x 25cm. Subscription for a year was 100 kuruş, for six months was 50 kuruş and one issue was 20 para (1/2 kuruş). It continued to be published until 1953 under different names.

8c7b0235-6bb9-503d-ac59-f73f7984f36b.materials: Canvas, wood, coloured pigments, gold leaf
8c7b0235-6bb9-503d-ac59-f73f7984f36b.description2: This 1852 oil on canvas by Simil depicts the General Khaireddine (Khayr al-Din) on horseback in official uniform. This brigadier-general uniform from the latter half of the 19th century comprises a full suit, a short coat, a shirt, a checia, a chemla and a pair of shoes. The brigadier-general also wore two crossed capes and a sword, with the Nichan al-Iftikhar (1st class) medal on the right-hand side of the chest, next to the insignas, and the Légion d'Honneur and the Ordre des Saints Maurice et Lazare medals on the left-hand side.

8c914730-20a7-5718-b92c-20ee629a7048.name: Circular letter by the Italian Director General of Police to all the Italian Prefects, regarding 'Italian migration to Tunis and Bona (Algeria)'
8c914730-20a7-5718-b92c-20ee629a7048.author: Anna Maria Iozzia
8c914730-20a7-5718-b92c-20ee629a7048.archival: ASCt, Questura di Catania, el 4, b. 1, c. 76r
8c914730-20a7-5718-b92c-20ee629a7048.description2: The Italian consuls reported large numbers of unemployed Italian migrants in Bona (Algeria), where many Italians ended up begging in the streets, and in Tunis, where many Italians were in dire straits. The Director General of Police instructed the Prefects to inform the Italian population about this situation and warn it against “the shameful and fraudulent enticement by Migration Agents who, out of greed, push our peasants towards the most heartbreaking poverty”. The Prefects were also instructed to “assiduously prevent clandestine migration and repress its promoters”.

8c948912-a36b-5142-9ff7-26c982ac3b28.name: *The opening of the exhibition, by Blass. M. Carnot and his entourage, pass under the Eiffel tower*
8c948912-a36b-5142-9ff7-26c982ac3b28.description2: The Eiffel tower was opened in March 1889 by the President of the Republic, Sadi Carnot, in the presence of several foreign rulers. This inauguration, taking place at a moment of great political tensions, gave rise to many sarcastic comments mocking how the government was using the Exposition Universelle (world fair) for its own gain.

8cbe678a-dcda-57dc-87ce-36a2c9a08898.description2: Paris, International Exhibition, 1878. The text of the magazine describes a big tent built in the garden of the Algerian Pavilion with camel fur, fixed with ropes of the same material and strong bamboo canes. Some Arabian men stayed there, sent by the general Algerian governor, and dressed in the typical light-blue uniform of the "Turkish people", or with a red blanket, typical of the region. The Algerian Pavilion was meant to represent the colony through the reproduction of the Campo Marte and Trocadero buildings and also in the garden.

8ccd3080-01c6-56b9-82eb-95127eef1d1d.bibliography: Walter B. Denny, “Length of Fabric”, in Maryam D. Ekhtiar, Priscilla P. Soucek, Sheila R. Canby, and Navina Najat Haidar, eds., *Masterpieces from the Department of Islamic Art in The Metropolitan Museum of Art* (New York, 2011), pp. 320-1
8ccd3080-01c6-56b9-82eb-95127eef1d1d.keywords: Costume; dress; fashion; Ottoman influence; Turkish influence; design; tulip; floral decoration; vegetal decoration; Ottoman textiles
8ccd3080-01c6-56b9-82eb-95127eef1d1d.description2: The bold pattern of wavy vines, tulips and spear-shaped leaves on this robe designed by Mariano Fortuny, y Madrazo (1871-1949) is based on an imperial Ottoman silk of the 1560s. So appealing was the original Ottoman design that copies were produced in the 17th century and later, not only in textiles but also ceramic tiles. It is unclear whether Fortuny was familiar with the 16th century Ottoman lampas with metal-wrapped thread or with one of the textiles or tiles it inspired. Born in Spain, he was raised in Paris and Venice in a family that collected textiles and other artefacts. In his palazzo in Venice he not only designed fabrics and fashionable clothing but also invented new techniques of theatrical lighting and produced art in a variety of media. Since he lived in Venice with its long tradition of trade with the Ottoman Empire, he would have had extensive exposure to items from the Eastern Mediterranean. Also, from the late 1880s a range of textiles, carpets and other objects stored in the various Ottoman palaces in Istanbul were sold and found their way onto the European market.

8d0345df-1e22-5450-8f37-706dc5be7d91.description2: This photo from Enrico H. Giglioli's collection was taken by the Florentine naturalist during his travels around the world in 1865 and 1868 while advancing diplomatic and commercial relations between the newborn Italian state and the other nations. The images seem to have been created spontaneously to show ethnocentric diversity. The ethnographic photographs in the Giglioli's collection are part of the historical archive of the Pigorini Museum. The origins of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

8d188108-655f-550e-b130-a0eb24f32b9c.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
8d188108-655f-550e-b130-a0eb24f32b9c.author: Huda Kilani
8d188108-655f-550e-b130-a0eb24f32b9c.description2: Three bands of silver (800) chain fitted around the sides and over the crown of the head; 1/4 Ottoman coins (*barah*s) are fixed in the inner section of the band. This kind of jewellery was part of the dowry the groom gave to the bride. Dowries consisted mostly of silver jewellery because only the rich could afford gold jewellery. Thus, the financial status of the groom was highlighted by the jewellery he could give as a dowry and by the use of coins as pieces of jewellery for his wife.

8d7fb33a-5d98-5c0b-a5f1-fab6b28e82f7.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
8d7fb33a-5d98-5c0b-a5f1-fab6b28e82f7.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
8d7fb33a-5d98-5c0b-a5f1-fab6b28e82f7.materials: Canvas, wood, coloured pigments, gold leaf
8d7fb33a-5d98-5c0b-a5f1-fab6b28e82f7.description2: This oil on canvas by Alexandre Debelle shows Mohamed Sadok Bey seeing off the emperor Napoléon III as he leaves Algiers on 20 September 1860. The bey and the emperor are on horseback, surrounded by their garrisons and local inhabitants in traditional dress. This painting is set in an urban dwelling by the sea, and the tricolour French flag is fluttering above the crowds. The bey is dressed in official uniform, with the Nichan al-Ahd round his next, and the Nichan al-Dam, the diamond-crusted Légion d'Honneur and the Nichan al-Iftikhar (with the eagle of the Second Empire) medals are on the left side of his chest. This painting is evidence of an active diplomatic relationship between the Palais du Bardo and the European chancelleries.

8dec350b-560d-5475-8a47-00b9dd25268c.description2: A medal depicting the symbolic figure of Egypt sitting on a sphinx. In the background, the three pyramids of Giza and a sailing ship can be seen. The opposite side of the medal has a portrait of Emperor Franz Joseph. The medal was created in commemoration of the opening of the Suez Canal in 1869.

8e50c089-18d5-5800-bdb6-e0c14282ea69.name: St Justa's lift
8e50c089-18d5-5800-bdb6-e0c14282ea69.author: Cristina Correia
8e50c089-18d5-5800-bdb6-e0c14282ea69.history: Built between 1890–1892 it will be inaugurated still unfinished by Royal Prince Afonso of Braganza (1865–1920) on the 18th August 1892.
8e50c089-18d5-5800-bdb6-e0c14282ea69.keywords: Lisbon; Urban innovation; transportation; Urban iron architecture
8e50c089-18d5-5800-bdb6-e0c14282ea69.architects: Engineer Raul Mesnier du Ponsard (1849–1914 Porto/Inhambane); master builder and Foreman of the building sites: Manuel Cardoso (n.d.)
8e50c089-18d5-5800-bdb6-e0c14282ea69.description2:
This revivalist example of the 1900 iron architecture for transportation foregrounds amidst Lisbon Downtown skyline. The 45 m high lift includes a gangway with Neo-gothic decoration 2 towers with 7 floors, each one with a cabin for 24 passengers. Inside they are covered with wood and mirrors while each floor has its own decoration. The balance between the cabins is provided by a steel cable and was initially water moved.  
Foreseen since 1874 it aimed to overcome the 25 metres gap between Ouro and Carmo Streets thus easing the pedestrian’ traffic between the hills of the Lisbon centre. The inauguration of the gangway by King Carlos I was held in 1901 and the lift itself started to be fully operational in 1902 and electrified in 1907.  
It is classified as a national monument.

8eb7973a-8c9e-5910-83bd-ad5e77872aba.name: *Algerians*
8eb7973a-8c9e-5910-83bd-ad5e77872aba.author: Dalila Orfali
8eb7973a-8c9e-5910-83bd-ad5e77872aba.description2: This study consists of a series of sketches depicting various Algerians. The subjects are mostly women, whose faces, wrapped in a traditional *haik*, are particularly interesting. According to experts only two paintings of this kind exist today. Before being acquired by the museum this study belonged to an important collection from the late 19th century. In 2003 it was published in the Australian scholar Roger Benjamin's collection dedicated to Auguste Renoir's Algerian period, *Renoir and Algeria*.

8ed8ff70-e171-5817-8b08-6644fc9a000d.name: *The Sultan receives the prince Ioan I at his palace in Dolmabahce, Istanbul*
8ed8ff70-e171-5817-8b08-6644fc9a000d.type: Drawing (after a sketch by Carol Popp de Szathmari)
8ed8ff70-e171-5817-8b08-6644fc9a000d.archival: *L'illustration. Journal Universel*, vol. XLIV, nr. 1118, 30 July 1864
8ed8ff70-e171-5817-8b08-6644fc9a000d.description2: In May 1864, prince Alexandru Ioan Cuza dissolved the Parliament and announced his intention of imposing a new constitution (in fact, a modified version of the 1858 Paris Convention, which granted him greater executive powers). Since the Principalities were under Ottoman sovereignty, it was necessary to obtain the sultan’s approval. Therefore, Cuza travelled to Istanbul, where he had several meetings with sultan Abdul Aziz, who eventually recognized the act. Cuza’s visit to Istanbul and its successful outcome were described in an article published on 30 July in the French journal *L'illustration*. The article, written by P. Paget, the journal’s correspondent in Wallachia, was accompanied by a drawing made by Cuza’s court painter, Carol Popp de Szathmar, who depicted one of Cuza’s meetings with the sultan.

8efde259-472d-50ce-9578-75e8ff556e35.name: *Nosocomium* \[Latin: Hospital\]
8efde259-472d-50ce-9578-75e8ff556e35.author: Marina Minozzi
8efde259-472d-50ce-9578-75e8ff556e35.keywords: Italian painters; city; urban space; segregation; medicine; disease; poverty; illness; life expectancy; psychiatry; social changes; scientific development; social topics; post-unitarian Italian society; Positivism; celebration of science; exposition
8efde259-472d-50ce-9578-75e8ff556e35.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
8efde259-472d-50ce-9578-75e8ff556e35.description2: Silvio Rotta was introduced to painting by his father and, in his early years, produced mainly watercolours, genre compositions inspired by Venetian popular customs. In 1887, after an illness, the production of the artist underwent a radical change ad began to show social realism through the depiction of the insane. *Nosocomium* represents a psychiatric hospital where poor and sick were hosted and nursed. The scale of the canvas is accentuated by the diagonal of the benches and the path. The painting won awards at the 1895 Biennale of Venice and is now recognised as one of the most important works by Rotta. The scene’s realism offers a merciless analysis and public complaint about the patients’ living conditions. Caring of poor and sick was an important issue during the 19th century and a law to control hospitals and mental institution was discussed in those years.

8f10719a-7586-5524-9036-a47811acc887.name: *Muhammad 'Ali Pasha*
8f10719a-7586-5524-9036-a47811acc887.keywords: Ruling Family; Rulers of Egypt; The Alawiyya Dynasty; Turks; The Ruling Elite
8f10719a-7586-5524-9036-a47811acc887.description2: Muhammad 'Ali Pasha, founder of Modern Egypt and Wali of Egypt in 1805. He was the head of the Alawiyya Dynasty that ruled Egypt from 1805 to 1952, and founder of modern Egypt. He came to Egypt in 1799 as part of a military unit to fight with the Turks – and the help of the British – to drive the French out of Egypt. However, the Turkish forces were defeated in 1799 in the Battle of Abu Qir.

8f4f45ac-f6ac-5ff3-bfc0-d96fae01d30f.name: Revolver
8f4f45ac-f6ac-5ff3-bfc0-d96fae01d30f.description: This is a solid-frame revolver with 9-chamber cylinder and 8 mm calibre. The ejector and the screw for attaching the cylinder to the frame are missing. This revolver is fitted with two grip silver plates, highly decorated with checking and with a lion under a palm tree on both sides. The screw to attach the plates is installed with the grip plated diamond shape. The base of the barrel is octagonal in shape and the barrel had an inverted lip at its end. On the crown, “R”, a star and “E” are the only visible markings on the right side of the barrel. Right under the screw of the ejector, the number 16 is engraved. Only the last digit “3” of the serial number is visible and most of it is under the museum's inventory number.

8f55adc5-662c-55f8-a485-b18851210a66.name: Anatolian Railways
8f55adc5-662c-55f8-a485-b18851210a66.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
8f55adc5-662c-55f8-a485-b18851210a66.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Anatolian Railways
8f55adc5-662c-55f8-a485-b18851210a66.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

8f60990a-2e19-50e5-b91c-31a7c8a103fd.name: Beirut Port before expansion
8f60990a-2e19-50e5-b91c-31a7c8a103fd.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury, Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
8f60990a-2e19-50e5-b91c-31a7c8a103fd.keywords: Commerce; Expansion; Economy; Trading; Goods; Transportation; Port; Harbor; Communication; Beirut
8f60990a-2e19-50e5-b91c-31a7c8a103fd.description2: This photograph shows the Beirut port before its expansion. The dam was built under the command of Ibrahim Pasha. This old port underwent several important changes in the late 19th century, including the construction of a commercial tribunal and expansion of the port. This expansion involved the enlargement of existing buildings and filling areas of sea with rock brought in along the Nahr al-Kalb railway.

8f8640bd-04ac-5181-ba28-bef663422bf2.name: *Panoramic View of Makkah - Arabia (West Asia). Panoramic View of Makkah during the Celebration of the Pilgrimage of the Muslims to the Kaaba, where the religious treasure is guarded*

8f8640bd-04ac-5181-ba28-bef663422bf2.description2: This coloured print, perhaps from a late 19th-century, Spanish newspaper or magazine, shows a birds-eye view of the city of Makkah with the Holy Mosque and Ka'bah at the centre. The view was recorded from one of the rugged mountains surrounding the city. Hundreds of pilgrims are seen to approach from afar and converge on the city gates. that lead to the sanctuary. The print shows close compositional similarities to an early 19th century drawing by the English officer and artist Charles Hamilton Smith (1776-1859). Smith, although not known to have visited the Arabian peninsula, produced an album of drawings - possibly in turn taken from older engravings - with views from Syria, Persia and Arabia sometime between 1818 and 1846.

8f933cf6-939e-5018-be2c-726c4f9ca78a.name: Little Sicily
8f933cf6-939e-5018-be2c-726c4f9ca78a.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
8f933cf6-939e-5018-be2c-726c4f9ca78a.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
8f933cf6-939e-5018-be2c-726c4f9ca78a.description2: Pictured here is an area, near the port of Tunis, where many immigrants from southern Italy had settled. Between 1865 and 1900, hundreds of small one or two-bedroom houses were built in the lower part of the Avenue Jules Ferry (today Avenue Habib-Bouguiba). The layout of the port allowed for the a rapid increase in the number of residents; a great many (mostly Sicilian) workers settled around the warehouses and workshops. Little Sicily therefore became both the home of the European working classes and the centre of the city's industrial activity. As Gaston Loth described it in 1905, "It's still Sicily, the children live in the streets, speak Arabic but also French, it's a like a swarm of lewd, barely dressed sparrows."
