905cb8f2-54fa-520a-b0bc-209a26809787.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in 19th century. Vassilaki Kargopoulo was of Greek descent. His first studio was opened in 1850 near the Russian Consulate. Between the years of 1859 and 1860, he began to attract the attention of customers from all sections of society. He focused on Ottoman clothing and street vendors in 1860.

908862b3-3d2c-5b16-93ce-f2a0873efd37.name: *Algiers port*
908862b3-3d2c-5b16-93ce-f2a0873efd37.author: Dalila Orfali
908862b3-3d2c-5b16-93ce-f2a0873efd37.description2: Albert Marquet spent 1904 and 1907 in the company of Fauve, and in 1913 he lived in Tangier with Matisse and Camoin. Seven years later in 1920 he visited Algiers for the first time, and went on to spent a few months there every year henceforth. He also lived in Algiers for the duration of the Second World War. Marquet was friendly with most of the artists from the Algerian school, and exhibited his paintings in galleries in the centre of town. Many of his paintings were on the theme of Algiers' harbour. In 1939, his friends from the Salle Bordes organised his first solo exhibition. His style, which was characterised by the luminosity and clarity he saw in North Africa, was an important early influence on the Algerian painter Mohamed Temam.

90898679-94a2-5a74-9442-dce1eaec5acf.name: *Shepherd with his sheep*
90898679-94a2-5a74-9442-dce1eaec5acf.description2: Sheep husbandry has always been a traditional agricultural occupation in the Romanian lands. Shepherds spent summers in mountainous regions, where they found pastures for their flocks, and descended into lower valleys for the winter. Transhumance is still practiced in Romania. During the Ottoman sovereignty, one of Moldavia and Wallachia's economical obligations towards the Porte was to send sheep, but also sheep wool, cheese, meat and tallow in the Ottoman Empire.

90aa72df-4823-5e48-bcc0-2aa150e3f718.name: *The Suez Canal*
90aa72df-4823-5e48-bcc0-2aa150e3f718.author: Marina Minozzi
90aa72df-4823-5e48-bcc0-2aa150e3f718.keywords: Waterway; Austria; Lloyd; Assicurazioni Generali; Bourse; Adriatic; Egypt; Said; Ismail; Pasha; Ferdinand de Lesseps; Suez Canal Company; Compagnie universelle du canal maritime de Suez; vice-president; route; India; International exhibition
90aa72df-4823-5e48-bcc0-2aa150e3f718.description2: Alberto Rieger studied at the Academy of Venice thanks to the patronage of the Baron Pasquale Revoltella, who commissioned him to create the painting showing the Suez Canal, which was presented at the Exposition of Fine Arts in 1864. The artwork is meant to celebrate the most important enterprise in Revoltella’s career; he personally travelled to Suez in 1861-62 to supervise the works for the construction of the channel that he promoted. The painting was executed by studying technical maps of the ground, sketches and photographs. The result is very close to the actual conditions of the city of Cairo, the pyramids and the delta of the Nile. The artist was commissioned also an open view of the city of Trieste by Pasquale Revoltella.

90ac8914-3124-5940-a90b-536222104ba2.name: Pergamon altar
90ac8914-3124-5940-a90b-536222104ba2.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
90ac8914-3124-5940-a90b-536222104ba2.author: Stefan Weber
90ac8914-3124-5940-a90b-536222104ba2.second_name: Main hall of the Pergamon Museum, Berlin, reconstruction of the great altar with many original pieces
90ac8914-3124-5940-a90b-536222104ba2.description2: The Pergamon Museum building owes its name to a spectacular finding in Turkey. The story of this discovery of the past starts in 1864 with the German engineer Carl Humann, who urged the Berlin museums to undertake proper excavations when he saw local lime burners burning ancient remains on the acropolis. The subsequent research unveiled important remains of Hellenistic art. With the museum opening in 1930 and the architectural reconstructions of the Ancient, Hellenistic, Roman and Islamic Middle East the museum developed in one of the most famous institutions of its kind.

90b30aa0-1bcb-5a10-80c9-1a254c7529d3.name: A retrospective: Preparations for the exhibition of 1889 - the Eiffel Tower under construction
90b30aa0-1bcb-5a10-80c9-1a254c7529d3.description2: For the Exposition Universelle (world fair) of 1889, France wanted to both celebrate the centenary of the 1789 revolution and also showcase its skill and inventiveness. The Eiffel Tower, a daring move in the world of cast-iron architecture, became first the symbol of the exhibition then of the city as a whole.

90bb7321-dadf-559d-862c-6d2c919236d2.name: Disembarking captives at La Goulette Port, Tunis.
90bb7321-dadf-559d-862c-6d2c919236d2.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
90bb7321-dadf-559d-862c-6d2c919236d2.description2: This document attests to the disembarkment of cargo and captives, abducted in the Mediterranean, at the La Goulette port, Tunis.

90ca166d-9356-578a-8ad2-de64931fee56.name: The hanging of liberal patriot Ciro Menotti (26 May 1831), who had organised an uprising for national unification in Modena

90e3fb5e-2f89-5468-82a4-55ad1ae995cf.type: Islamic, Indian & Southeast Asian works of art; Metalwork
90e3fb5e-2f89-5468-82a4-55ad1ae995cf.holder: Shangri La, Doris Duke Foundation for Islamic Art
90e3fb5e-2f89-5468-82a4-55ad1ae995cf.dates: Hegira 10th century / AD 16th century or later
90e3fb5e-2f89-5468-82a4-55ad1ae995cf.keywords: panels; Safawid; Mughal; Iran; India; silver; arabesque; inscription; Muhammad Amin al-Kirmani; door; calligraphy; geometrical decoration; geometrical motifs
90e3fb5e-2f89-5468-82a4-55ad1ae995cf.description2: This pair of small metal hinged doors is of rectangular shape and is elaborately ornamented on the interior. At the centre of each door is a field of dense arabesques and stars. The lengthy and exquisite Arabic inscription adorning the perimeter of each of these panels proclaims the sanctity of a shrine and requests permission to enter into it. It is signed by one Muhammad Amin al-Kirmani. On the reverse sides of each door are repeating engraved, peaked crosses with studs inset down the centre.

90f2dfb3-6077-51c6-9668-8f2a4879243c.name: An Italian family at the turn of the 20th century
90f2dfb3-6077-51c6-9668-8f2a4879243c.archival: AS Terni, Archivio Gisa Giani, Album “Donne di Terni dentro e fuori la fabbrica"

90fa424c-bb73-5fd9-ae3d-bc20de07992b.name: Yıldız Palace The World-Displayer Kiosk (Cihannuma Kiosk)
90fa424c-bb73-5fd9-ae3d-bc20de07992b.notice: This is an unedited Database entry and may contain errors and inconsistencies in spelling. We are working to raise the funds required to complete the editing; should you wish to contribute please visit our [Support page](https://www.museumwnf.org/atrium_support.php).
90fa424c-bb73-5fd9-ae3d-bc20de07992b.history:
Yildiz Palace, which is the last architectural example of Turkish Ottoman palace, is located on the Yildiz hill in the district of Besiktas. Sultan Ahmed I was the first to build a pavilion, over this land registered at the time to the Private treasury of the Ottoman Sultan as a hunting place sultans beginning during the reign of Suleiman the Magnificent (1520-1566).  
The main construction in the palace started in the period of Sultan Abdulhamid II (1876-1909) and it was called Saray-i Humayun (Central palace). During this period the palace comprised of buildings for private use of the sultan as well as buildings, allocated for the officials, repair shops and carpentry like repairing shop, carpenter’s shop and the buildings of culture and art such as theatre, museum and library. The Palace begun to serve as a museum under the name of “Directorate of the Museum of Yildiz Palace since 1993.
90fa424c-bb73-5fd9-ae3d-bc20de07992b.description2: The Kiosk, named *Cihannüma* (“World-displayer”) for its wide vision field including Bosphorus, the Golden Horn and Marmara Sea, was built on Hasbahçe as a kiosk for resting and watching. It is one of the most remarkable buildings of the Palace regarding its carpentry work and design elements. Sultan Abdülhamit used the upper story of the Kiosk for watching Istanbul and the Bosphorus with long-sighted binoculars. Because of its panoramic view, it was called as Cihannuma and built as a residence and watching kiosk. This is the most important building of the palace in terms of wooden tectonics and decoration figures. Sultan Abdulhamid II used the upper floor of the kiosk in order to view Istanbul and Bosphorus with effective binoculars.

9107cee6-86c6-50d5-afa3-39c67845bd31.name: Cup stand (*zarf*)
9107cee6-86c6-50d5-afa3-39c67845bd31.description: These delicate silver pieces known as *zarf* are an important part of the coffee ritual in Turkey, as they work as a protection and stand for the hot cups. We can admire those pieces as a part of the scenography in the portrait of the marquise of the Cerralbo and his daughter in Turkish costume made by Abdullah Fréres.
9107cee6-86c6-50d5-afa3-39c67845bd31.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes

9113b91c-e517-59d8-b8a9-ea3d96446cd4.name: Salepçioğlu Mosque
9113b91c-e517-59d8-b8a9-ea3d96446cd4.description2: This mosque, built in the Eclectic style with Orientalist elements, illustrates the degree to which the West influenced Anatolia.

9125eef2-5105-53b7-9631-e449863bd408.description: Changes to Morocco’s public health policy began with the first central pharmacy in 1917; this was followed by the establishment of other public health institutions.

9161faa0-4fe2-54c4-a25b-05a4938ccfd9.name: Memorial Volume – Dedicatory and opening ceremonies of the Chicago World's Colombian Exposition – 1893
9161faa0-4fe2-54c4-a25b-05a4938ccfd9.description2: The World's Columbian Exposition or The Chicago World's Fair was a World's Fair held in Chicago in 1893 to celebrate the 400th anniversary of Christopher Columbus' arrival in the New World in 1492. The fair was an influential social and cultural event to which the Ottoman Empire had been invited. It displayed raw materials and agricultural products at the exposition, as well as handicraft products and plant products belonging to the palace revenue. The 1893 Chicago Exhibition was a big success for the Chamber of Commerce. The Head of the Chamber of Commerce, Azaryan Efendi, was assigned to the head of the commission, which was formed in Istanbul for the Chicago Exhibition.

9162226d-73d0-5c61-8640-f03def3fa40a.name: Pearl Trader’s Pearl Pouch
9162226d-73d0-5c61-8640-f03def3fa40a.holder: Sharjah Maritime Museum / Sharjah Museums Department

9162226d-73d0-5c61-8640-f03def3fa40a.description2: This colourful little bag would have contained a pearl merchant's most priced pearls. Many such bags could be found in a pearl merchant's chest, each one containing a particular grade of pearl, determined by their shape, colour and level of surface perfection.

918c2c1a-37f3-5178-8124-1d569b29d213.name: Dar Ben Abdallah
918c2c1a-37f3-5178-8124-1d569b29d213.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
918c2c1a-37f3-5178-8124-1d569b29d213.history: This princely palace in the Tunis medina was built in the style of 19th century Italian royal courts, and named after its original owners, who were rich silk weavers. During the French Protectorate era it was brought by a French painter, but was then reacquired by the Tunisian state after independence, at which point it became the Musée des Arts et Traditions Populaires of the 19th century Tunisian bourgeoisie.
918c2c1a-37f3-5178-8124-1d569b29d213.description2: The curving hallway, richly decorated with faience pottery, marble and stucco, leads to an open-air courtyard, around which there are several apartments, today housing the museum's collection. The patio is surrounded by porticos with white marble columns. The walls are decorated with Neapolitan faience pottery, above a frieze of carved plaster. At the centre of the patio sits a fountain with three basins made of marble imported from Carrara. On the first floor, a circular gallery with wood railings adds to the palace's opulent style.

91a520f6-9937-54cd-a224-0a3b83e3587f.name: Azurite
91a520f6-9937-54cd-a224-0a3b83e3587f.holder: National Museum of Natural History and Science (MUHNAC) / Museums of the University of Lisbon
91a520f6-9937-54cd-a224-0a3b83e3587f.author: Liliana Póvoas (MUHNAC-UL)
91a520f6-9937-54cd-a224-0a3b83e3587f.keywords: Azurite; carbonate mineral; monoclinic system; copper; pigment; jewellery; National Museum of Natural History and Science; University of Lisbon
91a520f6-9937-54cd-a224-0a3b83e3587f.description2: Two aggregates of azurite prismatic crystals with a radial distribution. Azurite is a copper carbonate mineral, of chemical formula Cu3(CO3)2(OH)2. Its name comes from the antiquity for its deep blue colour after the Arabian azure that came from the Persian lazhward. Azurite crystals conform to the monoclinic system of symmetry. In this sample they are prismatic, opaque and their faces present striations. The lustre is vitreous. Azurite was used as a blue pigment for centuries, providing a wide range of blues. It is also used as jewellery and as an ornamental stone. As a secondary mineral found in the oxidized portions of copper deposits, the presence of Azurite is a good surface indicator of the presence of copper ores. This sample was collected at the Touissit Mine, near Oudja, Morocco.
91a520f6-9937-54cd-a224-0a3b83e3587f.holding_institution_org: Museu Nacional da Historia Natural e da Ciencia (MUHNAC)

91b66b55-0c91-5d46-b3bc-af6121a29639.name: Portrait of Mihai Suţu
91b66b55-0c91-5d46-b3bc-af6121a29639.description2: Mihai Suţu was the last Greek prince of Moldova. The Sublime Porte imposed Greek rulers in Wallachia and Moldavia (called “Phanariotes” because they came from Fanar, the Greek neighborhood of Istanbul) at the beginning of the 18th century and maintained them until 1821. During this period some modernizing reforms, influenced by the ideology of the Occidental Enlightenment, were introduced in the Romanian countries. The drawing was made by French artist Louis Dupré, who visited Greece, Istanbul, the Balkan Peninsula and the Near East in 1819 –1820. In the summer of 1819 he arrived in Bucharest together with Mihail Şuţu, whom he had met in Istanbul. He painted Şuţu laying on a red divan, wearing Oriental clothes.

91c9008b-704b-5717-93d7-868bfaa22521.name: *Asia. Athalide*
91c9008b-704b-5717-93d7-868bfaa22521.description: In this lithography, Asia is represented as a woman dressed in Turkish style. She is Athalide, the lover of Bayaceto, in a 1762 play by Jean Racine. She wears Circassian clothes. Orientalist painting usually represents Circassian women in the seraglios or harems.
91c9008b-704b-5717-93d7-868bfaa22521.author: Carmen Linés Viñuales

920e1526-6e4c-5336-8f89-0cc695c54cff.name: Ker Porter’s box
920e1526-6e4c-5336-8f89-0cc695c54cff.description2: In 1814 Ker Porter, British artist and travelller, visited Rich. Together they explored famous sites in Iraq. He mistook the ruins at Aqar Quf for the Tower of Babel. The box contains fragments of a Babylonian mudbrick and bitumen, matching the Biblical description of the Tower.

9226b1df-56b3-5ffb-a38d-64b0ff5cec56.name: African slaves working the fields
9226b1df-56b3-5ffb-a38d-64b0ff5cec56.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
9226b1df-56b3-5ffb-a38d-64b0ff5cec56.description2: This series of photographs attests to the existence of African slaves working in domestic roles or in agricultural labour.

922ac1b0-e425-5db9-98ed-2ceda9b73f82.name: Zaytuna University
922ac1b0-e425-5db9-98ed-2ceda9b73f82.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
922ac1b0-e425-5db9-98ed-2ceda9b73f82.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
922ac1b0-e425-5db9-98ed-2ceda9b73f82.description2: This photograph shows young students coming out of a class in the Zaytuna University. In fact, the mosque was not only a place of worship, but also a sizeable university. A number of theologians, litterateurs, and art and science scholars from all over the Arab world (with an emphasis on North Africa) founded, across various generations, the Zaytuna university in Tunis. The teaching was constantly being modernized and restructured during the 19th century, and particularly under the reign of Ahmed Pacha Bey and the viziership of the reforming minister Khaireddine (Khayr al-Din).

9241049c-6cdf-5701-af96-c463f9661bf7.name: *Mosque Gate*
9241049c-6cdf-5701-af96-c463f9661bf7.description2: Caliph Abdulmecid was interested in art in addition to administration. He opened many art exhibitions. He was chosen as honorary president of the Society of Ottoman Painters, which was founded in 1909, and he gave considerable financial support to the monthly journal published by the society. He took part in the Galatasaray Art Exhibitions with his paintings. For example, one of his paintings was accepted for an exhibition held at Galatasaray during the first years of the First World War. His works reveal him as a colourist and an accomplished portrait painter. Caliph Abdulmecid showed his paintings at the Viyana Exhibition, which was the first exhibition opened by Turkish painters in Europe in 1918.

92891afc-502b-5609-8db7-99bf7bb50e6c.name: Franz Joseph I, Emperor of Austria (1830–1916)
92891afc-502b-5609-8db7-99bf7bb50e6c.description2: Portrait of Emperor Franz Joseph as an officer of the *Kaiserjäger* (Elite regiment). He ruled Austria for 68 years. During his long reign he had cordial relation to the Sultans of the Ottoman Empire and visited Istanbul and Jerusalem. He died in 1916 during World War I.

928c9e9b-828a-5e50-84b7-70a3d3ef8c88.name: On the Royal Ship Marsala
928c9e9b-828a-5e50-84b7-70a3d3ef8c88.holder: Italian Institute for African and Oriental Studies
928c9e9b-828a-5e50-84b7-70a3d3ef8c88.author: Giulia Barrera
928c9e9b-828a-5e50-84b7-70a3d3ef8c88.archival: Archivio fotografico, Libia, album 25, “Festeggiamenti per l’arrivo di S.A. l’emiro Senussi a Bengasi (1920)”
928c9e9b-828a-5e50-84b7-70a3d3ef8c88.second_name: The official trip to Italy of Amir Sayyid Muhammad Idris al-Mahdi al-Senussi (from Libya)
928c9e9b-828a-5e50-84b7-70a3d3ef8c88.description2: El Sayyid (or Sidi) Muhammad Idris al-Mahdi al Senussi (1889-1983), the grandson of the founder of the Senussi Sufi order, became head of the Senussi order in 1916. He took the title of Emir and ruled as King of Libya from 1951 through 1969. In 1920 Italy reached an agreement with him and invited him to Rome, where he met King Victor Emmanuel III. Idris’ relations with the Italian government later deteriorated, and he went into exile in Egypt and encouraged anti-Italian guerrilla from there.

92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.name: Palais de la Rose
92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.history: The Palais de la Rose was built in the late 18th century, within La Manouba's royal gardens. Although originally used as a recreational palace for the Husainid beys, it soon began to receive many famous guests or persons visiting Tunisia, such as Queen Caroline of Brunswick in 1816. During the reign of Ahmed Pacha Bey (1837–1855) the palace became a residence for foreign teachers at the École Militaire du Bardo, among whom was the famous hero of Italian independence, Giuseppe Garibaldi. From 1881, the beginning of the French protectorate in Tunisia, the palace became the occupying army's headquarters. Following independence, the palace was restored and thus regained its original splendour and the became home to the Musée Militaire National.
92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.keywords: Architecture; art; painting; stucco; mosaic; marble; ceramics
92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.description2: The Palais de la Rose is an example of "Moorish" architecture from Spain and North Africa with Italian influences. Its most notable features are the grand staircase, the great hall surrounded by a marble gallery, and the huge, luxurious courtrooms. It is richly decorated in a variety of styles, with Italian marble in rare colours and an elegant rococo style, as can be seen from the Neapolitan faience pottery, the vaulted ceilings, and the tympanums finely carved from stucco or naqsh hadida in one of the styles popular at the time, such as an eight-point star between two stylised cypress trees. Finally, palace-museum's four great rooms invite its visitors to learn about the history of the Tunisian army from antiquity to the War of Independence.

92c6732e-264e-56fc-b2bd-43a71e310d3b.name: Traditional dress worn by the Emir of the Chouf district
92c6732e-264e-56fc-b2bd-43a71e310d3b.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
92c6732e-264e-56fc-b2bd-43a71e310d3b.materials: The original was made of silk and cashmere
92c6732e-264e-56fc-b2bd-43a71e310d3b.description2: This was the formal dress of the Emir of the Chouf district. It consists of traditional *shirwal* trousers and a silk jacket with embroidered patterns.

92dacff0-b9ed-51f4-8929-313eefaa5ba9.name: Coat of a bedouin collected during the Expedition of the Austrian Ship Pola under the command of Paul von Pott to explore the Red Sea
92dacff0-b9ed-51f4-8929-313eefaa5ba9.keywords: Palmyra; Syria; Palestine; Bedouins; textile; exploration; travel; traveller
92dacff0-b9ed-51f4-8929-313eefaa5ba9.description2: This Bedouin shirt from Palmyra, Syria was collected by an Austrian officer named Karl Alexander Anselm Freiherr von Hügel. He left the army in 1824 and organized a long voyage, which took him from France to the Near East. He first visited Syria and Palestine, then reached Mumbai, India in 1832. From 1832 to 1836 he travelled widely in India, until he returned to Europe.

92edd2fe-ef09-5e83-baba-8f729535104a.name: Dolmabahçe Mosque and Square
92edd2fe-ef09-5e83-baba-8f729535104a.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; Abdullah Brothers
92edd2fe-ef09-5e83-baba-8f729535104a.description2: Dolmabahçe Mosque’s original construction was initiated by Bezm-i Alem Valide Sultan, the mother of Sultan Abdülmecid (1823-61). Upon her death, its construction was continued by her son. It is located in the southern part of the Dolmabahce Palace, situated on the coast. The mosque was opened for prayer services on 23 March 1855. Its architect is Garabet Balyan, a member of the Balyan family, who built various structures for the Ottoman Empire. The Dolmabahçe Mosque is adorned with various items of both Baroque and Ampir styles, which are reflected in the architectural design of that period. Also, an emergent architectural modernity in the mosque is its circular window design. Such a design had rarely been seen in mosques and civil architecture before this time.

92f613dc-01ad-5171-a5dd-b251dab90f70.name: Photograph of Krste Petkov Misirkov with his friends
92f613dc-01ad-5171-a5dd-b251dab90f70.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
92f613dc-01ad-5171-a5dd-b251dab90f70.third_name: Fotografija na Krste Petkov Misirkov so prijatelite
92f613dc-01ad-5171-a5dd-b251dab90f70.description2: Krste Petkov Misirkov (1874–1926) is the author of the book “On Macedonian Matters”, which was published in Sofia in 1903. This work is a starting point in explaining Macedonian distinctiveness, having served as an intellectual and contemplative engine for generations of Macedonians fighting in the battlefield and in literature alike.

933220c7-ac0f-58a4-bd26-9a2aaf27779a.name: Dar Hussein
933220c7-ac0f-58a4-bd26-9a2aaf27779a.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
933220c7-ac0f-58a4-bd26-9a2aaf27779a.history: Built in the 12th century in the heart of the Banu Khorasan's royal city, this palace was occupied by the nobles of various dynasties who had ruled Ifriqiya. It became the seat of Tunis Municipality in 1858, after being restored and redecorated. The palace is named after the General Hussein, who was president of the municipality’s highest council. From 1882 until independence the palace served as the headquarters for the troops of the French occupation. It then became the seat first of Institut National d’Archéologie et Art, and in 1993 of l'Institut National du Patrimoine.
933220c7-ac0f-58a4-bd26-9a2aaf27779a.keywords: Architecture; Andalusian style; Italian style; stucco; carved wood; painting
933220c7-ac0f-58a4-bd26-9a2aaf27779a.description2: Dar Hussein, one of the most beautiful palaces of the Tunis medina, shows traces of all the different eras of Tunisian architecture, from the Khorasani era through the Andalusian, Turkish and colonial eras.  On the ground floor, four large rooms, including a great hall, surround a peristyle. The neo-corinthian capitals topping the columns were made by Italian sculptors. On the first floor there is an elegant second peristyle in a 19th century Italian style, The galleries are divided up into four apartments, decorated with frescoes painted on faience pottery beneath a frieze of carved plaster.

934b04dc-f3d9-52a1-b4a6-850226ba2bd7.name: The Old German Consulate
934b04dc-f3d9-52a1-b4a6-850226ba2bd7.history: Initially built as a residence, the building was then converted into an administrative office for German consular officials in 1902. In 1919, after the Franco-German Treaty, the building became the property of the *Makhzen*, administered by the Pasha Tazi, and was turned into a school.
934b04dc-f3d9-52a1-b4a6-850226ba2bd7.keywords: German in Morocco; German foreign policy; Moorish style; arch; plaster; stucco; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic influence; Islamic architecture in Morocco; geometrical motifs
934b04dc-f3d9-52a1-b4a6-850226ba2bd7.description2: This Neo-Moorish style building consists of three floors with three apertures in the form of arches on the first floor, windows of smaller dimensions on the second floor and a narrower top storey, which has two apertures, and whose facade is decorated with ornamental plasterwork. The simplicity of the facade conceals the splendid design of the building’s interior.

93ae9a92-2eeb-5864-aa3f-f804d80d9877.name: The Moorish Villa (Wilhelma Park)
93ae9a92-2eeb-5864-aa3f-f804d80d9877.holder: Wilhelma, Zoological and Botanical Garden Stuttgart
93ae9a92-2eeb-5864-aa3f-f804d80d9877.history:
King Wilhelm I of Württemberg commissioned to Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1837 the design of Moorish style buildings for his Wilhelma garden. The architect planned and built all the buildings with the exception of the Damascene Hall.  
The idea was not to reproduce faithfully the Islamic art but to lend an “oriental” flair to the garden. The mention of an “oriental garden” conjured up visions of elegance, luxury, colourful brilliance, seduction and eroticism.  
The Moorish style recalls the Islamic art of Spain and North Africa between the 12th and 15th centuries which reached its zenith in the Alhambra. It was fashionable in 19th century: Wilhelma is also known as the “Alhambra on the river Neckar” and other buildings – synagogues in Berlin and Vienna for example – were built in the Moorish style.
93ae9a92-2eeb-5864-aa3f-f804d80d9877.description2:
The "Moorish Villa" at Wilhelma indicates either the whole construction of the botanical section or its central building. The glasshouses are impressive constructions of glass and cast iron adjoined to the central living quarters already during the reign of Wilhelm I of Württemberg.  
The overall construction accommodate five autonomous plant houses, each of them displaying plants according to a super-ordinate theme. From the northern entrance, one first reaches the Cactus Cupola House, then the room with the Tropical Crop Plants. In the centre there follows the Moorish Villa (central part of the construction), with the famous giant titan plant. The next section is the glasshouse with tropical ferns, and in the final room, also with a glass cupola, the tree ferns.  
In the central room of the Moorish Villa construction there is the Department for Nocturnal Animals with nocturnal birds.

93c53f75-811e-5d47-8d12-4f56a360451f.name: Carthage archaeological site
93c53f75-811e-5d47-8d12-4f56a360451f.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
93c53f75-811e-5d47-8d12-4f56a360451f.history: Founded by the Phoenicians around 814 BC, Carthage was the city that brought Africa into mainstream European historical narratives. Hanno's Carthage ruled the seas, and Hannibal's Carthage was master of the land; Carthage certainly saw its golden age before disappearing. Augustus built Carthage as the capital of proconsular Africa, and the Imperial Roman Carthage that succeeded it put great importance on art and literature. Christian Carthage of Saint Augustine's times appeared to be a city fuelled by religion and passion. It was ruled by the Vandals for a century, then the Byzantines and finally the Arabs. However, although the leadership changed many times over the years, Carthage itself did not move. Modern Carthage, therefore, holds the evidence for many different histories. It has been listed as a UNESCO world heritage site since the 26 October 1979.
93c53f75-811e-5d47-8d12-4f56a360451f.keywords: Carthage; Phoenicians; Hannibal; Saint Augustine; Africa
93c53f75-811e-5d47-8d12-4f56a360451f.description2: Explorers and travellers - starting with T. Falbe and E. Beulé in the early 19th century and continuing through to the end of the 20th century - have been fascinated by interrogating and analysing the remains of one of the most important ancient cities: Carthage. It was conquered by Hassan ibn Nu'man in 698, but was then abandoned by the Arab Muslim population in favour of Tunis, and so for twelve decades was used as a quarry for marble and other stone for the construction of monuments in Tunis and other cities. By the early 20th century only some of what is visible today had been uncovered, namely the baths of Antoninus with their great cisterns, the huge cisterns of La Malga, some sections of the aqueduct connecting Carthage to Zaghwan, the lagoons of the two Punic ports, the remains the amphitheatre and the perimeter of the circus.

9438f959-d105-5cd5-890f-56a9cdcc3715.description2: Portrait of Josef Freiherr Philippovich-Philippsberg (1818–1889). In 1836 Philippovich-Philippsberg joined the Austrian Army. In 1878 he became commander of the Austrian invading forces for the occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina. On 17 August 1878, Austrian troops occupied Sarajevo. Philippovich commanded Austrian forces in Bosnia until 1880.

94535829-1f7a-57f3-91f8-a5b331e4d1a1.second_name: *Précis de l'Art Arabe et Matériaux pour servir à la Théorie et à la Technique des Arts de l'Orient Musulman*
94535829-1f7a-57f3-91f8-a5b331e4d1a1.description2: The artist and architect Jules Bourgoin travelled to Egypt many times. Between 1880 and 1884 he took part in a French archaeological campaign to Cairo, directed by Gaston Maspéro, from which he brought back a number of drawings of Egyptian monuments and Arab architecture.

945bf083-a74e-5bce-800b-f411f54c9b67.name: Photograph of diplomatic visit to England
945bf083-a74e-5bce-800b-f411f54c9b67.description: This photograph depicts the Moroccan diplomatic delegation that accompanied Sultan of Morocco Mulay ‘Abd al-‘Aziz’s Ambassador, ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abd al-Sadiq al-Rifi, on an official visit at the invitation of King Edward VII.

9466f4d9-fdf0-535b-998b-5d46de3d70eb.name: A cartoon of Italian colonial propaganda: 'The Roman to the young Libyan People: Come with me: let’s climb together the sacred hill’
9466f4d9-fdf0-535b-998b-5d46de3d70eb.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
9466f4d9-fdf0-535b-998b-5d46de3d70eb.author: Giulia Barrera
9466f4d9-fdf0-535b-998b-5d46de3d70eb.second_name: An open reference to the typical colonialist argument of the 'civilizing mission'
9466f4d9-fdf0-535b-998b-5d46de3d70eb.description2:
Infantilisation of the colonised people was a typical element of colonial discourse. It was a necessary complement of the notions of the “colonising mission” and of the “white man’s burden”. Africans were often described as children who needed to be civilised by the Europeans.  
This cartoon also shows another element typical of Italian colonial propaganda: the idea that Italy was the legitimate heir of Ancient Rome and thus had a historical right to rule over Libya, which was once part of the Roman Empire.  
*Il Ghibli* was an Italian weekly paper printed in Tripoli in 1918-19, addressed to Italian military men stationed in Libya.
9466f4d9-fdf0-535b-998b-5d46de3d70eb.holding_institution_org: Biblioteca di Storia Moderna e Contemporanea

9478a32e-0a07-5107-810d-66b32c256277.name: The Post Office
9478a32e-0a07-5107-810d-66b32c256277.history: Designed by the Uruguayan architect Adrien Laforgue, the building has Neo-Moorish aspects and bears many similarities with the Post Office in Algiers, built a few years earlier, and which Laforgue also designed. This was one of the first administrative buildings to be built on Mohammed V Square (formerly Place de Paris).
9478a32e-0a07-5107-810d-66b32c256277.keywords: Moorish style; French in Morocco; French in North Africa; Uruguayan architects in North Africa; protectorate; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic influence;  Islamic architecture in Morocco; applied arts; ceramic; geometric motifs; arch; column; European architecture; post office; urban planning; technical innovation; postal service; city; urban space; changes in urban spaces; colonial city; colonial building; colonial architecture; colonial economy; city plan; Moroccan city
9478a32e-0a07-5107-810d-66b32c256277.description2: This impressively large administrative building has an entrance formed by two basket arches. These lead to the two entrance doors, both of which are surmounted by an epigraphic band, indicating the services of the institution and highlighted with a rich floral and geometric enamel-green and blue decor. Note that the surroundings of the access doors have recently been painted red-ochre, recalling the colour of houses in Marrakesh. The gallery is supported by columns bearing Ionic capitals. The front is embellished by small semicircular arches in the centre, topped by decorative green *zellige*; the building’s small canopy also has a green-tile frieze.

949e75ce-78cf-577e-95d9-461cc0734d07.name: *On the omnibus (or inside a tramway passing over a bridge)*
949e75ce-78cf-577e-95d9-461cc0734d07.description2: The question of multi-passenger transport emerged first in capital cities. In the 17th century, Blaise Pascal had the idea of creating transport lines in Paris with scheduled itineraries for horse-drawn carriages seating 8 people. This type of transport saw increasing success in the 19th century as did, on the other hand, the use of cabs with specific destinations. In 1855, all Parisian omnibus companies were merged into the "Compagnie Générale des Omnibus" at the request of the Chief Commissioner of the Seine, in a desire to prioritise the movement of tourists visiting the Exposition Universelle (world fair). Steam or fuel-powered tramways were also introduced in the 1870s. This drawing does not accurately reproduce the atmosphere of those overcrowded omnibuses, however, as Mary Cassat chose to foreground a mother who, lost in her thoughts, does not notice the nanny playing affectionately with her daughter.

94bc8ed7-7428-5a36-9919-9335c90547df.name: Migration preparations of Muslim families to Turkey
94bc8ed7-7428-5a36-9919-9335c90547df.holder: Population Exchange Museum (The Foundation of Lausanne Treaty Emigrants)
94bc8ed7-7428-5a36-9919-9335c90547df.description2: The 1923 population exchange between Greece and Turkey was based upon religious identity, and involved the Greek Orthodox citizens of Turkey and the Muslim citizens of Greece. The "Convention Concerning the Exchange of Greek and Turkish Populations" was signed at Lausanne, Switzerland, on 30 January 1923, by the governments of Greece and Turkey. During the migration waves during the 1896-97 riots in Crete, 40,000 Cretan Muslims had to migrate to territories under Ottoman rule: Lebanon, Syria and Anatolia. This photograph pertains to migration preparations from Lemnos to Turkey in 1924.

94c59dc9-5032-599d-bcf3-18eec377e4fa.name: Velvet embroidered kaftan
94c59dc9-5032-599d-bcf3-18eec377e4fa.holder: Musée des Arts et Traditions Populaires
94c59dc9-5032-599d-bcf3-18eec377e4fa.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
94c59dc9-5032-599d-bcf3-18eec377e4fa.materials: Velvet fabric, braided trimmings, silver thread with white and gold
94c59dc9-5032-599d-bcf3-18eec377e4fa.description2: This purple velvet kaftan is decorated with gold and silver braided trimmings and embroidered with silver and golden metal thread. It is fitted with mid-length sleeves embellished with a large "lyonnais" ribbon. The chest is covered by a large breastplate, split into two symmetrical halves, and adorned with large buttons of gold lace. The embroidery on the breastplate features two peacocks facing, on each side, a bowl with floral motifs. The kaftan is lined with a pale blue satinette on the outer rims with a pattern of swallows' wings sewn on. The kaftan, a particularly lavish item in the 19th century, was typically worn for marriage ceremonies, usually with calf-length trousers.

94d92226-8356-5023-81bd-a96c6c114974.name: Design for book cover: *Tres morillas me enamoran*
94d92226-8356-5023-81bd-a96c6c114974.description: The influence of the Spanish Muslim art can be seen in this design that references the illuminated books of Alfonso X, King of Castile (1252–1284). The arches, the dresses and the general decoration recall the illuminated pages of the 13th century illuminated books preserved in the Royal Collection and Library.

94d92226-8356-5023-81bd-a96c6c114974.third_name: Diseño para portada del libro *Tres morillas me enamoran*

9533b9d1-3fe7-5fb5-bdef-8dce66c03f06.name: The Black Obelisk of Assyrian King Shalmaneser III
9533b9d1-3fe7-5fb5-bdef-8dce66c03f06.description2: The Black Obelisk of Assyrian King Shalmaneser III was excavated by a British expedition at Nimrud (Iraq) in 1846. There was great excitement when it was found to contain reference to Biblical king Jehu. Furthermore, it depicted his image, still the oldest image of a king of Israel.

954b0597-1e92-5222-bbca-efdc2174af21.name: *The Egyptian Stock Market*
954b0597-1e92-5222-bbca-efdc2174af21.keywords: The Stock Market; Securities Exchange Market; Old Alexandria
954b0597-1e92-5222-bbca-efdc2174af21.description2: An old photograph of the Egyptian Stock Market in Alexandria, one of the oldest stock markets in the world. It was established in 1899, during the time of Khedive `Abbas II, in the Muhammad `Ali square in Alexandria. The Alexandria Stock Market became a landmark in the city that frequently appears on postcards.

957ca713-c1c0-5491-8542-164f00239bf4.name: *Aladdin, or The Magnificent Lamp: sketch of the set for act 1 or act 2*
957ca713-c1c0-5491-8542-164f00239bf4.description2: The tale of Aladdin and his lamp was very popular in the theatre and the opera following the rise of Orientalism in the 1820s. Its first performance as an opera in 1822 was so successful that gas was used for the first time ever at the Opéra de Paris, to light up the lamp on stage.

9599bee6-4ecd-5e61-803d-f6a17fddee21.name: The Istanbul Main Post Office
9599bee6-4ecd-5e61-803d-f6a17fddee21.notice: This is an unedited Database entry and may contain errors and inconsistencies in spelling. 9599bee6-4ecd-5e61-803d-f6a17fddee21.history: The Istanbul Main Post Office is an office building for postal services located at Sirkeci quarter of Fatih district in Istanbul, Turkey. It was designed by architect Vedat Tek in First Turkish National architectural style and was constructed between 1903 and 1909. The four-story building houses a post office, the Sirkeci Post Office, office space for regional administration and also since 2000 the Istanbul Postal Museum. It is Turkey's largest post office building.

962e3954-6b7a-5ffb-a881-c31a4aa6530a.second_name: Notebook used by a third-grade student in a village school in Central Italy, in 1908–1909
962e3954-6b7a-5ffb-a881-c31a4aa6530a.description2:
In Italy, the first law that introduced compulsory education (the so-called “Coppino law”) dates back to 1877. Only the first three years of elementary school were compulsory. In 1911, the law extended compulsory education up to the age of 12.  
During the 19th century, illiteracy in Italy was very high: in 1867, almost 70 per cent of spouses who could not sign their marriage certificate because were unable to write; in 1901, there were still about 39 per cent of spouses who could not sign their marriage certificate.

9647edd4-27e5-5ed4-a0ce-9b56a5dfc3ea.name: Coffee mortar and pestle
9647edd4-27e5-5ed4-a0ce-9b56a5dfc3ea.description2: Coffee mortar and pestel from Egypt/Morocco.

96a9d112-f072-5e5d-87c6-cce26768e6de.name: Necklace for horses – Type 2
96a9d112-f072-5e5d-87c6-cce26768e6de.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
96a9d112-f072-5e5d-87c6-cce26768e6de.keywords: Decoration; Silver; Silver chains; Jewells; Precious stones; Beads
96a9d112-f072-5e5d-87c6-cce26768e6de.description2: This necklace was used on the horses of Ottoman officials and indicated their high status and wealth. The chain consists of alternating silver spheres and amber cubic beads, with a silver cylindrical pendant in the centre.

96b87e45-a0fc-5ed9-baea-de7b25724cf7.name: *Maktab al-\`Anbar School, Damascus*
96b87e45-a0fc-5ed9-baea-de7b25724cf7.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
96b87e45-a0fc-5ed9-baea-de7b25724cf7.author: Stefan Weber
96b87e45-a0fc-5ed9-baea-de7b25724cf7.second_name: First modern secondary school founded by the state in Damascus. Building was originally a private dwelling
96b87e45-a0fc-5ed9-baea-de7b25724cf7.description2: The growth of Damascus urban culture and the changing role of the state were accompanied by important reforms and social changes. One of them was an increased alphabetisation and an improved public education. Attempts were first made by the state to reform schools in 1869 with the passing of an edict on school reform for the whole Ottoman Empire, officially recognizing private and foreign schools while setting out the basic principles of state education. The law now made a distinction between military schools on the one hand, and schools preparing children for a civil service or administrative career on the other hand. An example for the latter is Maktab al-`Anbar school.

96c8cab7-8009-528f-a877-f2ea68738a97.name: *Jerusalem, al-Haram al-Sharif, Dome of the Rock*
96c8cab7-8009-528f-a877-f2ea68738a97.description2: Joseph-Philibert Girault de Prangey (1804–1892) was a photographer who had, in all probability, worked with Daguerre. Being a wealthy man, he was very well travelled. His photographs, which  remained anonymous for a long time but were among the first photographs to be taken in the Middle East.

96d75b79-58ff-5945-b11e-11a08e7dd7b9.name: *Typical North African interior*
96d75b79-58ff-5945-b11e-11a08e7dd7b9.archival: Berbrugger, *Algérie Historique Pittoresque et Monumentale*, Paris: J. Delahaye, 1843.

96da7333-2414-5c15-9ce1-3664f7119887.name: Mummy board and inner coffin for Nes-pauti-taui
96da7333-2414-5c15-9ce1-3664f7119887.description: An entire set of coffins was made in Thebes for the Amun priest Nes-pauti-taui. The mummy board and both coffin lids bear the same decorative scheme. We see enormous ornamental collars of foliage and flowers. The hands are separately applied and hold the djed-pillar and the Blood of Isis. The faces and wigs are also superimposed.
