96df24b2-d14d-504f-84ae-d796597c98a1.name: Travel case
96df24b2-d14d-504f-84ae-d796597c98a1.author: DGPC
96df24b2-d14d-504f-84ae-d796597c98a1.description2: Travelling became a great cultural and social phenomenon with Romanticism. The “Grand Tour” through the countries of the known world, and particularly around the Mediterranean, became a means of developing cultural and social skills. Travel became refined and even a simple journey to the countryside required such accessories as this travel case for meals.

96e36ed2-2da9-5b5a-b4bb-79b6897cf288.name: Portrait of Ahmad Faris al-Shidyaq
96e36ed2-2da9-5b5a-b4bb-79b6897cf288.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
96e36ed2-2da9-5b5a-b4bb-79b6897cf288.description2: Ahmad Faris al-Shidyaq was born in 1804 in the 'Ashqut (Keserwan) district, and received his primary education in Hadath (Ba'abda), and his secondary education in 'Ayn Warka School. Here, he studied both foreign languages and Arabic literature. He was later converted to Protestantism by American missionaries in the region. He moved to Egypt in 1825, and then to Malta in 1834, where he lived for 14 years. During this period he became the head of the American Printing Press, and started publishing his own books. From Malta, he travelled to London, Paris and Tunis, where he converted to Islam and changed his name to Shaykh Ahmad Faris al-Shidyaq. In 1857, he began publishing his newspaper whilst he continued to edit his books. He died on 20 September 1889, and was buried in Lebanon, in Hazmiyya.

97051bf0-5841-5c21-bc4b-4e7e702b5270.name: Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico 'L. Pigorini' (National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography), Exhibition Room
97051bf0-5841-5c21-bc4b-4e7e702b5270.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
97051bf0-5841-5c21-bc4b-4e7e702b5270.author: Mario Mineo, Marina Minozzi
97051bf0-5841-5c21-bc4b-4e7e702b5270.keywords: Paleoethnology; archaeology; exploration; anthropology; natural history; material culture; academy; Jesuits; Egypt; Egyptology; collection; collector; exoticism; curiosities; wunderkammer; Museum Kircherianum; Baroque; languages; Arabic
97051bf0-5841-5c21-bc4b-4e7e702b5270.materials: Gelatino-bromide negative impressed upon glass plate
97051bf0-5841-5c21-bc4b-4e7e702b5270.third_name: Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico 'L. Pigorini', sala espositiva
97051bf0-5841-5c21-bc4b-4e7e702b5270.description2: The origins, in terms of scientific activity and conservation, of the Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome, can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the “Regio Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico di Roma" (Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography). Initially the museum was located in a wing of the Palazzo del Collegio Romano built in the late 16th century by the Society of Jesus. This rare image represents the old arrangement of one of the rooms of the Roman College, where the collection of antiquities and curiosities gathered by Father Athanasius Kircher was kept after the foundation of the museum. According to the intentions of its founder, Luigi Pigorini, the purpose of this new institution was not only to gather together the remains of Italian prehistoric culture and the "primitive" cultures of other European and non-European peoples in a "central" museum located in the new capital of the Kingdom, but above all to support, promote and participate in research by palethnologists in Italy.

97234026-b759-5b5b-ada5-8fc567b89260.name: Four-poster bed
97234026-b759-5b5b-ada5-8fc567b89260.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
97234026-b759-5b5b-ada5-8fc567b89260.description2: This four-poster bed was made for a Muslim market in a pseudo-baroque style and shows evidence of European influences. The metalworkers who made this kind of furniture worked with both copper and iron, and were organised in their own guild, with their workshops located in the lower kasbah.

9729e384-0aab-59c6-bb73-2a5621d81218.name: Bridal headdress (*Tepelak* – tas)
9729e384-0aab-59c6-bb73-2a5621d81218.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
9729e384-0aab-59c6-bb73-2a5621d81218.keywords: Head-dress; tepelak; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; tughra; marriage; wedding; fashion; costume
9729e384-0aab-59c6-bb73-2a5621d81218.materials: Gilt silver, casting, filigree, adornment with small coins
9729e384-0aab-59c6-bb73-2a5621d81218.description2: Jewellery worn on the head included diverse types of metal articles which served to support the hat or scarf and also had an apotropaic function in addition to their decorative one. Especially noteworthy head-pieces were *tepelaks*. These are headdresses of round form, sometimes slightly concave, abundantly adorned with chains, smaller or larger silver coins and with *trepkas* (tiny ornaments in diverse forms – round, leaf-shaped, rectangular, heart-shaped, etc.). *Tepelaks* used to be worn everywhere in Macedonia, particularly in the Kumanovo, Skopje, Gostivar and Gevgelija regions, as well as within Vlachs. This piece of bridal *tepelak-tas* was made by application of filigree technique. It is abundantly decorated with coins suspended on tiny chains.

97603dc7-78b0-567d-995d-706683438f46.name: Wedding dress
97603dc7-78b0-567d-995d-706683438f46.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
97603dc7-78b0-567d-995d-706683438f46.author: Huda Kilani
97603dc7-78b0-567d-995d-706683438f46.materials: Linen with silk; hand weaving, hand embroidered, natural dyes
97603dc7-78b0-567d-995d-706683438f46.description2: The main fabric of this wedding dress is linen with silk selvedge stripes, with red and yellow taffeta inserts in the sleeves and skirt; the chest panel is couched with gilt cord and yellow, green and purple silk cord, and filled with multi-coloured stain and herringbone stitches. Palestinian weavers used manual spindles to prepare the cotton and linen threads imported from Egypt. Ashkelon weavers used light vertical hand looms (*Majdalawi* looms) to produce linen fabrics, while silk fabrics were spindled, died and woven in Syria. The Jordanian economy in the late 19th and early 20th centuries relied on trade and crafts; new waves of people started to come to Jordan to participate in those industries. This object shows the diverse population composition of Jordan at that time, through personal attire, fashion, local costumes and rites.

97c4a755-5c5e-5725-922a-057501cef5ff.name: Medal – The Great Exhibition Palace, London 1851
97c4a755-5c5e-5725-922a-057501cef5ff.description2: This silver medal was dedicated to the palace that was built for the Universal Exposition of London. On the reverse is depicted the Crystal Palace and a short text reads: "Proposed by H.R.H Prince Albert. Designed by Josh Paxton. Erected by Fox Henderson & Co. Occupies 18 acre", while on the obverse is inscribed: "Length 1848 feet. 408 ft. wide. Roof 66 ft. high. Height of transept 108 ft. 900.000 sq. ft. glazed surface. 3320 cast iron columns. 368 wrougth iron trusses. 8 miles exhibition tables. 202 miles of sash bars. 400 tones of glass. Value ₤ 150.000". In 1851, Romanian products (wines, carpets, animal skins, cloths, dyed silk, candles, printings and lithographs, such as a map of the Danubian Principalities) were exhibited in the Turkish pavilion, as Wallachia and Moldavia were under Ottoman sovereignty.

97c81b60-8583-5d90-b0b2-ac0449741525.name: A watermill in Lagonegro (PZ, Southern Italy)
97c81b60-8583-5d90-b0b2-ac0449741525.archival: AS Potenza, Intendenza di Basilicata, b. 622, fasc. 548
97c81b60-8583-5d90-b0b2-ac0449741525.third_name: Veduta dei mulini dei signori Siervo e Mazzei di Lagonegro

98176d85-368c-5bcb-9ca0-e03314e1aa13.name: Amulet band
98176d85-368c-5bcb-9ca0-e03314e1aa13.keywords: Franks; collection; collector; museums; amulet; talisman; inscription

9825c289-5dc5-5c51-b115-fa920eda0b57.name: The artificial channel built at Shellal, during the construction of the first dam on the Nile
9825c289-5dc5-5c51-b115-fa920eda0b57.author: Patrizia Pampana
9825c289-5dc5-5c51-b115-fa920eda0b57.description2: In the year 1900, Count Giulio d’Aspremont, an Italian diplomat, visited the construction site of the first dam across the Nile (today known as the Aswan Low Dam or Old Aswan Dam). He took several photographs of the works and of the monuments on the island of Philae that were slated to be submerged by the water. He published some of them on the *Bulletin of the Italian Geographical Society*, where he wrote that up to 2,000 Italian workers were employed in the works (as stone-cutters, miners and masons), out of a total labour force of about 10,000 or 12,000; an Italian village had sprung up on the Nile banks, with modest little houses, trattorias and shops.

982f1ac5-a37a-57db-93bb-493e4513bd14.name: *Zarf*
982f1ac5-a37a-57db-93bb-493e4513bd14.description2: *Zarf* made entirely of silver-gilt filigree with granulation. Used to hold a small porcelain coffee-cup. From Syria.

9844c72d-8d2f-50e5-8d5b-86ef15a82164.name: *Egyptian village scene*
9844c72d-8d2f-50e5-8d5b-86ef15a82164.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
9844c72d-8d2f-50e5-8d5b-86ef15a82164.keywords: Economy; Market; sugar cane; Egypt; local product; rural life; eating; paintings
9844c72d-8d2f-50e5-8d5b-86ef15a82164.materials: Water- and bodycolour over pencil, heightened with white, on blue/grey paper
9844c72d-8d2f-50e5-8d5b-86ef15a82164.description2: Egyptian men and women are seen here in a town or village on the Nile. In the shade of an overhanging tree a market stall displays its wares, including paper lanterns and bread. At the stall behind, sugar cane is for sale. In the background is a mosque with a white minaret, though not distinctive enough to establish the scene's locality. Pilleau had visited Egypt in the winter of 1842-43 with Lieutenant Colonel George Everest (after whom Mount Everest was named) and two other companions, on their way home from India. On his return to England he published a set of twelve coloured lithographs, Sketches in Egypt (1845), which, like the better-known publications of Wilkie, Roberts and Owen Jones in the same decade, fuelled popular interest in Egypt and the Holy Land.

98465502-2fc0-537f-8943-a5b60d87d5c5.name: Osman Hamdi Bey (Getting mold of Antiochus relief During the excavation of Mount Nemrut)
98465502-2fc0-537f-8943-a5b60d87d5c5.archival: *Le tumulus de Nemroud-Dagh. Voyage, description, inscriptions avec plans et photographies*, İstanbul, F. Loeffler, 1883.
98465502-2fc0-537f-8943-a5b60d87d5c5.keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters; archaeological excavations
98465502-2fc0-537f-8943-a5b60d87d5c5.description2: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen were exposed to Western ideas through education and travel. The museum was founded by decree in 1891 as the Imperial Museum. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi. Hamdi began construction of the main building in 1881, and it achieved its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. It is one of the prominent structures built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul. Osman Hamdi, during his tenure as museum director, launched the first Turkish scientific excavations. He carried out archaeological excavations at Mount Nemrut, Laguna and Sidon.

9863f692-894f-5cb2-b496-b0ec25aba740.name: Kabyle mother with her child
9863f692-894f-5cb2-b496-b0ec25aba740.description2: Western photographers were particularly interested in both women's daily lives, and family life. This photo from 1920 shows a Kabyle woman carrying her baby with a look of pride on her face.

98c08194-bddc-52e4-a6b8-d9483bc9ad1b.name: Statue of Jules Ferry
98c08194-bddc-52e4-a6b8-d9483bc9ad1b.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
98c08194-bddc-52e4-a6b8-d9483bc9ad1b.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
98c08194-bddc-52e4-a6b8-d9483bc9ad1b.keywords: French protectorate of Tunisia; Jules Ferry; Habib Bourguiba
98c08194-bddc-52e4-a6b8-d9483bc9ad1b.description2: This symbolic statue of the French protectorate in Tunisia was located in the centre of the European quarter, between the cathedral and the official residence of the French government, on the Avenue Jules Ferry, today renamed Avenue Habib-Bourguiba. This bronze statue, reaching around three metres in height, is one of the last surviving elements of a monument which had been dedicated to one of the most important thinkers of French imperialism.

98c3852e-4d88-54fc-b204-73d1b0245994.name: Fan
98c3852e-4d88-54fc-b204-73d1b0245994.description: This fan was used by the Queen Maria Cristina of Spain and showed that the influence of the Orientalism or Neo-Mudéjar style had arrived in lace design. This lace has pointed arches and interlacing decoration very similar to Arab patterns.
98c3852e-4d88-54fc-b204-73d1b0245994.author: Ana Cabrera
98c3852e-4d88-54fc-b204-73d1b0245994.materials: Lace and tortoiseshell; diamonds and pearls

98dd6374-5559-5f34-9752-bbdb0e9ee65a.name: Class photograph in Tartej
98dd6374-5559-5f34-9752-bbdb0e9ee65a.author: Hala Masri
98dd6374-5559-5f34-9752-bbdb0e9ee65a.description2: This photograph was taken in Tartij, a village in the Mount Lebanon district. The sign behind the children reads "*Vive L'Académie Tartej (Liban)*" (Long Live Tartij Academy (Lebanon)). The young boys on the far sides are wearing traditional baggy trousers called *shirwal*. The younger boys underneath the sign are barefoot.

997dbce0-9881-50bc-95f4-a36fa4a0fb35.name: Portrait of Shaykh Nasif al-Yaziji
997dbce0-9881-50bc-95f4-a36fa4a0fb35.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
997dbce0-9881-50bc-95f4-a36fa4a0fb35.keywords: Writer; Scientist; College, Renaissance; Arabic; Lebanese
997dbce0-9881-50bc-95f4-a36fa4a0fb35.description2: Shaykh Nasif al-Yaziji was born in March 1800 in Kfarshima (Ba'abda). He wrote his first poems age ten, and after mastering the sciences became the assistant to Emir Bashir Shihab II for 12 years. In 1840 he moved to Beirut and dedicated himself to writing. He also became a professor at al-Bustani's National School and later at the Syrian Protestant College (now the American University of Beirut). He stayed here until 1869, when he fell ill and retired. He died in February 1871, forty days after the death of his oldest son. He is most famous for his work *Majma' al-Bahrayn*.

99c365eb-e061-5123-97ee-c6128fee870f.name: Arab / Bedouin Gun
99c365eb-e061-5123-97ee-c6128fee870f.holder: Sharjah Al-Hisn Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
99c365eb-e061-5123-97ee-c6128fee870f.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
99c365eb-e061-5123-97ee-c6128fee870f.description2: This matchlock musket, locally made based on a European prototype, is known as 'Abu Futtila'. It is an  example of the type of weapon used from the early 18th century until as late as the early 20th century in the Arabian Peninsula. The type was typically simply stocked, but generally as with this example, fitted with an extremely high quality barrel.  The tang is stamped with a maker's mark. This gun is a good example as it retains what is possibly its original match consisting of twisted fibre cord bound with cotton and two large copper alloy tubular fittings,  probably to hold lighted sections of the match. The gun is muzzle loaded and has a  .50 calibre smoothbore barrel with a single shot firing capacity. The musket shows fine fluting and has a chiseled barrel with geometric designs and silver inlay, as well as a copper alloy mounted forward grip. The copper taper holders under the wick do not appear to be original, but this gun still has its primer pan protector.Weapons were among the most coveted and desirable, if often illicit commodities in the Arab Gulf. European weapons were mainly imported through Muscat and Bushire on the Persian coast of the Gulf, with many than copied locally.

9a0ef88f-4c24-5091-bc8e-2808d0c18501.name: Library museum
9a0ef88f-4c24-5091-bc8e-2808d0c18501.archival: Gavault, P., "Notice sur la Bibliothèque-Musée d'Alger", in *Revue Africaine*, vol. 38 (1894): 41.

9a102fc6-396b-58a9-ba31-7edc20e68a04.name: Report on the behaviour of Rustam Pasha
9a102fc6-396b-58a9-ba31-7edc20e68a04.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
9a102fc6-396b-58a9-ba31-7edc20e68a04.description2: A report on Rustem Pasha, the *mutasarrif* or governor of Mount Lebanon, and his treatment of his subjects. The report describes him as a tyrannical and unjust governor with oppressive policies, curbing the autonomy of tribunals, for example. He also imposed high taxes on the tobacco trade in Mount Lebanon and ignored many of the Sultan's decrees.

9a135c4c-830c-5fdd-a5e6-61129754ecfd.name: Bridal breast jewellery (*Chaprag*)
9a135c4c-830c-5fdd-a5e6-61129754ecfd.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
9a135c4c-830c-5fdd-a5e6-61129754ecfd.keywords: Breast ornament; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; accessories; costume; wedding; marriage
9a135c4c-830c-5fdd-a5e6-61129754ecfd.third_name: Chaprag – Nevestinski ukras za na gadi
9a135c4c-830c-5fdd-a5e6-61129754ecfd.description2: This exquisite article called a *chaprag* shows the exceptional skill and inventiveness of the unknown goldsmith, who makes each piece of jewellery a virtual work of art in itself. The *chaprag* is a breast ornament consisting of a round plate and tiny chains. It is executed in filigree technique and adorned with decorative stones. Besides its decorative function, it was applied for the purpose of fastening the cleavage of the tunic. It was characteristic of the Ohrid-Prespa region, that is, the areas of Ohridsko Pole, Strushko Pole and Debarski Drimkol.

9a2b6628-fecf-51cc-8501-edcd12db0810.name: Portrait of Wadih Sabra
9a2b6628-fecf-51cc-8501-edcd12db0810.holder: Lebanese National Higher Conservatory of Music
9a2b6628-fecf-51cc-8501-edcd12db0810.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
9a2b6628-fecf-51cc-8501-edcd12db0810.description2: Wadih Sabra was the composer of the Ottoman anthem, used today as the Lebanese National anthem. He also established the Institute of Music in Beirut, as decreed by Sultan 'Abd al-Hamid in 1910, and founded the National Conservatory. He was the founder of the first musical-scientific journal of its kind in the Arab region, and wrote the first Arabic language opera.

9a2d1d61-3abf-5d45-a7c7-9550d4cd751a.name: Gold to the country from the [Italian] colony in Tunisia
9a2d1d61-3abf-5d45-a7c7-9550d4cd751a.author: Massimo Sanacore
9a2d1d61-3abf-5d45-a7c7-9550d4cd751a.archival: ASLi, Famiglia Moreno di Tunisi, b. 13
9a2d1d61-3abf-5d45-a7c7-9550d4cd751a.second_name: Receipt for the donation of gold to Italy, in support of its war effort during World War I
9a2d1d61-3abf-5d45-a7c7-9550d4cd751a.description2:
This receipt certified that Leone Moreno (Tunis, 1852-1940) “donated gold to the country” in order to support Italy’s war effort during WWI. Leone was the grandchild of Mosè Moreno, a Jew from Livorno who migrated to Tunis around 1830. In Tunisia, the Morenos became successful in business. Leone’s father and brothers were traders and bankers, while Leone was an agricultural entrepreneur.  
He was a nationalist and was one of the Italians who actively resisted the French policy of assimilating the Italians in Tunisia. He employed only Italian workers on his estate and supported the Società Dante Alighieri, a society aimed at promoting Italian language and culture abroad. Leone Moreno also generously supported the Italian hospital Giuseppe Garibaldi and the Italian orphanage “Principe di Piemonte”.

9a4c0c9b-0185-5c3b-94c2-863439ee8c9a.name: Istanbul Archaeological Museums
9a4c0c9b-0185-5c3b-94c2-863439ee8c9a.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
9a4c0c9b-0185-5c3b-94c2-863439ee8c9a.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Archaology Museum
9a4c0c9b-0185-5c3b-94c2-863439ee8c9a.description2: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen had been exposed to Westernizing ideas through education and travel. This museum was founded by decree as the Imperial Museum (*İmparatorluk Müzesi*) in 1891. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi Bey. Construction of the main building began in 1881, attaining its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. The site of the museum belonged to the Topkapı Palace outer gardens. It is a prominent structure built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul.

9a890b71-5d5a-57ef-b26d-c4592e54b5ac.name: Beirut Tramway station
9a890b71-5d5a-57ef-b26d-c4592e54b5ac.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Rita El Hachem
9a890b71-5d5a-57ef-b26d-c4592e54b5ac.description2: This photograph shows the main tramway station in Beirut, located on Corniche el Nahr Street by the river in the district of Burj Hammud. It was constructed in 1906 under the command of the Ottoman government, and housed the carts and the engineering station.

9aa7bece-df44-557d-99af-6cb4118c4095.name: The yacht Makook III built by the Fratelli Orlando Company (Livorno, Italy) for the Egyptian Khedive Abbas Hilmi
9aa7bece-df44-557d-99af-6cb4118c4095.author: Daniela Tazzi
9aa7bece-df44-557d-99af-6cb4118c4095.archival: ASLi, Cantiere Navale Luigi Orlando, b. 8M2
9aa7bece-df44-557d-99af-6cb4118c4095.description2: In 1910, the Khédivé of Egypt contracted the construction of a yacht to the shipyards Cantieri Gallinari of Livorno, Italy. This company went bankrupt and its business was absorbed by the Fratelli Orlando shipyards, from Livorno as well. After improving the project, the Fratelli Orlando started building the yacht in 1913 and delivered it to the Khédivé Hilmì Abbas in May 1914.  In recognition of the high quality of work on the yacht engineer Giuseppe Orlando was granted the Ottoman decoration of the Order of Osmanieh.

9aa9bf06-9414-5502-8c25-a49ce6269462.name: Belt
9aa9bf06-9414-5502-8c25-a49ce6269462.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
9aa9bf06-9414-5502-8c25-a49ce6269462.author: Huda Kilani
9aa9bf06-9414-5502-8c25-a49ce6269462.description2: A Circassian belt with 15 silver and niello-decorated buckles connected together to form the belt; there is a rosette shape at the end with locking mechanism and three dangling silver tassels. This belt, together with the dagger, was an accessory forming the traditional male Circassian dress. The Circassians used to carry daggers which were an essential part of the national dress. The immigration of the Circassians to the Ottoman Empire started in the middle of 19th century and continued until 1900. The Circassian communities migrated mostly to the eastern Arab countries with which they had spiritual and religious links.

9b0fa536-0fe5-5f95-ba19-41b4f81e9fd4.name: Brass head of flagpole
9b0fa536-0fe5-5f95-ba19-41b4f81e9fd4.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
9b0fa536-0fe5-5f95-ba19-41b4f81e9fd4.author: Huda Kilani
9b0fa536-0fe5-5f95-ba19-41b4f81e9fd4.description2: This mast, made of casted brass, bears an Arabic calligraphic decoration with the inscription "Oh God, Oh Muhammad". It is fixed on a pointed piece of copper with a hole at the bottom to install on a long wooden staff. In religious festivities such as a pilgrimage, various activities were organized. They would normally include festivals and rallies under flags and standards. The heads of flagstaffs were decorated with metallic items usually with Arabic calligraphy and some cosmic signs such as the crescent and the star.

9b133b3d-0949-560f-8199-84ec100bdffc.name: The Porta Pia Breach (20 September 1870)
9b133b3d-0949-560f-8199-84ec100bdffc.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
9b133b3d-0949-560f-8199-84ec100bdffc.third_name: La breccia di Porta Pia (20 settembre 1870)
9b133b3d-0949-560f-8199-84ec100bdffc.holding_institution_org: Biblioteca di Storia Moderna e Contemporanea

9b43f3ea-5b0a-57f2-be8e-3ff0d20fe6f6.name: Beirut Port during its expansion
9b43f3ea-5b0a-57f2-be8e-3ff0d20fe6f6.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury
9b43f3ea-5b0a-57f2-be8e-3ff0d20fe6f6.description2: This photograph shows the Beirut port during its expansion, which involved filling areas of sea with rock were brought along the Nahr al-Kalb railway.

9b44e7da-e4ce-51fe-a09e-946b4f817954.name: *View of Istanbul*
9b44e7da-e4ce-51fe-a09e-946b4f817954.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
9b44e7da-e4ce-51fe-a09e-946b4f817954.description2: Felix Ziem, who incorporated the seasons and the changing light of the sun during the day into Venetian scenes, selected Istanbul – another city intertwined with the sea – as a subject for this particular work. Portraying a quiet village at the shores of the Bosporus and the boats on the sea, the painting is dominated by the golden colour of sunset. Ziem is deemed a particularly successful artist in terms of capturing the reflections of sunlight on the water. Recognizing this feature as Ziem’s forte, Theophile Gautier mentions the effects of the changing light of the sun – as part of the movement in the environment – reflecting on the water as “broken into a thousand fractions”. As in his other works, the figures have been transformed into a few colour stains in the picturesque atmosphere.

9b50a392-dc86-5394-9c83-b97027af7055.name: Ceiling, custom-made for Shangri La's living room
9b50a392-dc86-5394-9c83-b97027af7055.type: Islamic, Indian & Southeast Asian works of art; woodwork; painting; architectural decoration
9b50a392-dc86-5394-9c83-b97027af7055.holder: Shangri La, Doris Duke Foundation for Islamic Art
9b50a392-dc86-5394-9c83-b97027af7055.keywords: ceiling; French Protectorate; Morocco; wood; geometric motifs; floral decoration; painted; gilded; varnished
9b50a392-dc86-5394-9c83-b97027af7055.description2: The living room ceiling at Shangri La was custom-made by Moroccan artisans working under the supervision of the Rabat-based firm S.A.L.A.M. René Martin. It is carved, painted, and gilded throughout. The central field features recessed octagrams in interlocking, knotted niches, predominantly orange and brown in tone. The bottommost border consists of a moulded plaster frieze of floral motifs in an arcade repeated throughout.

9b7af802-1ae8-51cf-9420-82e3e2b1c459.name: Photograph showing Khan Antun Bey Square
9b7af802-1ae8-51cf-9420-82e3e2b1c459.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
9b7af802-1ae8-51cf-9420-82e3e2b1c459.description2: Pictured here is the Khan at Khan Antoun Bey square. The building housed trading offices on the ground and first floors and foreign consulates on the upper floors. There was also an inner courtyard used for parking the consuls' horse-drawn carriages. It was built in 1853 by Antoun Bey Najjar, a merchant who made his fortune in Constantinople. Located by the port, the construction of this building is a reflection of the increasing importance of trade between Beirut and the West following the redevelopment of the port area in 1841. The khan was an important centre for business and trade, and later served many different functions, housing foreign consulates, Ottoman administrative offices, the postal service, merchants' offices and Beirut's first bank.

9b7f13f5-9188-59a0-bf2d-8b4f7c9b66cb.name: Brass head of flagpole
9b7f13f5-9188-59a0-bf2d-8b4f7c9b66cb.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
9b7f13f5-9188-59a0-bf2d-8b4f7c9b66cb.author: Huda Kilani
9b7f13f5-9188-59a0-bf2d-8b4f7c9b66cb.description2: A cultic item with Arabic calligraphy mentioning God and his prophet Muhammad made of casted brass; fixed on a pointed piece of copper with a hole at the bottom to install on a long wooden staff. In religious festivities such as a pilgrimage, various activities were organized that would normally include festivals and rallies under flags and standards. The heads of flagstaffs were decorated with metallic items usually with Arabic calligraphy and some cosmic signs such as the crescent and the star.

9b806efe-99d1-5b6e-913c-0ee466605547.name: Letter from l’Institut d’Afrique in Paris, congratulating Ahmed Bey for having abolished the slave trade
9b806efe-99d1-5b6e-913c-0ee466605547.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
9b806efe-99d1-5b6e-913c-0ee466605547.description2: This letter from August 1841 from l'Institut d'Afrique in Paris, signed by both its president and general secretary, congratulates Ahmed Bey for having abolished the slave trade in his kingdom, and awarding the Tunisian Prince a *diplôme de protecteur*.

9b83a66c-2937-5afb-80f5-4db5f45d441b.name: Slippers
9b83a66c-2937-5afb-80f5-4db5f45d441b.description: The slippers are handcrafted and embroidered by hand, their unique creation emphasizing their value. This type of footwear demonstrates the influence of oriental art in the technical work of 19th century European artisans, and the great fascination with the objects coming from the East that refer to the luxurious craftsmanship of these countries.
9b83a66c-2937-5afb-80f5-4db5f45d441b.author: Mercedes Rodríguez Collado
9b83a66c-2937-5afb-80f5-4db5f45d441b.materials: Silk, metallic thread, leather; velvet, sewn, embroidered, tanning

9ba14117-d905-597a-95be-0025b3200e4e.name: ‘The Younger Memnon’
9ba14117-d905-597a-95be-0025b3200e4e.dates: 19th Dynasty; donated to the British Museum in 1817
9ba14117-d905-597a-95be-0025b3200e4e.keywords: archaeology; Egyptomania; exploration; collection; collecting; museums; travel; traveller; statue
9ba14117-d905-597a-95be-0025b3200e4e.description2: Henry Salt and J.L. Burckhardt donated this colossal bust of Ramesses II to the British Museum in 1817 where it created a sensation and became known as the Younger Memnon. It was removed from the Ramesseum in Thebes by the explorer Giovanni Belzoni, who transported it to Alexandria, from where it was shipped to England.

9ba9df9d-f2a1-5166-9182-6b24185296d6.name: Map (*Africa magna*)
9ba9df9d-f2a1-5166-9182-6b24185296d6.description: An 18th-century map of Africa (*Africa magna*), its toponyms are written in Latin.

9c17568a-e2ca-5524-b5ae-c2d13aa4c2ac.name: The Beirut water factory
9c17568a-e2ca-5524-b5ae-c2d13aa4c2ac.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Rita El Hachem
9c17568a-e2ca-5524-b5ae-c2d13aa4c2ac.description2: Located in the suburb of Dbayeh, this factory provided the daily water supply for all of Beirut. The company was founded in 1873 and the factory was first opened in 1896. The water was taken from the Nahr al-Kalb river and distributed across a large water network.

9c1924a4-a7fb-5b06-b261-325af6945c40.name: Poster of “The Mask of the Red Death: A Fantasy”, by Edgar Allan Poe

9c275ab6-ba7e-5a89-909a-fd6b396dc11b.name: A battle between Algerian ships and ships of the Naples Royal Navy, which chased the Algerian ships and ultimately destroyed them by firing cannon shots on 17 May 1792
9c275ab6-ba7e-5a89-909a-fd6b396dc11b.author: Rossana Spadaccini, Giulia Barrera
9c275ab6-ba7e-5a89-909a-fd6b396dc11b.archival: AS NA, Segreteria di stato di azienda, Piante, 35
9c275ab6-ba7e-5a89-909a-fd6b396dc11b.third_name: *Espressione di una caccia intrapresa a due Sciabecchi Algerini dalla Fragata di Sua Maestà Napoletana denominata Sirena, a dì 17 maggio 1792, nelle acque comprese fra le isole d’Jeres ed il Capo Tagliato, quale termina per distruggerli e sommergerli a colpi di Cannone nella spiaggia denominata Cavallara*
9c275ab6-ba7e-5a89-909a-fd6b396dc11b.description2: In the 18th century the Kingdom of Naples and the Regency of Algiers were among the countries that competed for the control of trading routes in the Mediterranean and that participated in privateering. Only in 1856, by the Declaration of Paris, did Great Britain and most of other major European countries (with the exception of Spain) declare privateering illegal. By the time, Algeria had already become a French colony. The French military occupation of Algeria had in fact started in 1830.

9c2ac3c9-ddf9-5578-9e26-fad8ec3a615c.name: Dhow collection
9c2ac3c9-ddf9-5578-9e26-fad8ec3a615c.keywords: Boat; ship; dhow; pearling; fishing; trade; transportation
9c2ac3c9-ddf9-5578-9e26-fad8ec3a615c.description2: The National Museum of Qatar holds, in its collection, a fleet comprising of 14 dhows. The growing collection includes a variety of traditional dhows, with several models dating to the early 20th century, as well as more recent replicas of traditional vessels. Originating from Oman, Bahrayn, India and Qatar, among other places traditional dhows represented include *jalbut* (small to medium sized), *shuw\`i* (medium sized, once used for fishing and coastal trade), *sanbuq* (largest type in the Arabian Gulf today) and *baglah* (traditional, deep-sea dhows once used for the long – haul transport of goods.)

9c39a32f-844c-5e79-9249-d24aa6612ad5.name: Siamese diplomatic service
9c39a32f-844c-5e79-9249-d24aa6612ad5.description2: in 1861, Mongkut, the King of Siam, sent a diplomatic service to Paris, not in order to create an alliance, but to preserve their independence by sending messages of good will to various European sovereigns. Napoléon III organised a lavish reception at the Palais Fontainebleau, recalling the Siamese reception which Louis XIV received in 1684. This photo reveals the importance of the Siamese delegation (three ambassadors and ten attachés in their military dress) accompanied by the Abbot Larnaudie, interpreter for the Siamese court.

9c6f1f64-15f3-5d35-93ad-16dc50cc2b9f.name: Coat
9c6f1f64-15f3-5d35-93ad-16dc50cc2b9f.description: Coat in green velvet completely decorated in flowers and leaves in gold with the stencil technique. It is lined with a silk and has a green velvet belt.
9c6f1f64-15f3-5d35-93ad-16dc50cc2b9f.holder: Museum of Costume, Ethnographical Heritage Research Centre
9c6f1f64-15f3-5d35-93ad-16dc50cc2b9f.author: Elvira González

9c872904-bce3-5aa4-b6f0-1ecfaddfcbd1.name: Mosque lamp
9c872904-bce3-5aa4-b6f0-1ecfaddfcbd1.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art
9c872904-bce3-5aa4-b6f0-1ecfaddfcbd1.description2: Imitation of a Syrian-Egyptian mosque lamp made by Philippe-Joseph Brocard in Paris, 1867.

9cf0fa7d-8af1-5fb8-bd4a-1b1c8b14129b.name: Newspaper *al-Wataniyya*
9cf0fa7d-8af1-5fb8-bd4a-1b1c8b14129b.holder: House of the Maronite Patriarchate of Antioch and all the East
9cf0fa7d-8af1-5fb8-bd4a-1b1c8b14129b.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
9cf0fa7d-8af1-5fb8-bd4a-1b1c8b14129b.description2: This issue of *al-Wataniyya*, only part of which is shown here, dates to 1 February 1901. *Al-Wataniyya* was a bi-monthly newspaper founded by N. A. Mokarzel and written, edited and printed in Philadelphia, USA. It was distributed internationally.

9cfc95e2-dcd3-56fd-b37e-253ac1e09a34.name: *Immigrants* \[on Ellis Island\]. *Two Italian kids*
9cfc95e2-dcd3-56fd-b37e-253ac1e09a34.description2: At the start of the 20th century millions of Italian families emigrated to America by boat, driven by economic misery and the hope of a better life. Once they arrived, the immigrants were taken to have a number of checks done by the Ellis Island authorities, as they had to satisfy certain standards (hygiene, health) or risk being repatriated. One can understand, therefore, why these two well-dressed Italian children seem anxious.

9d2ab4b5-fef1-530e-806a-e497c463b2a5.name: An old exhibition from Tiled Kiosk
9d2ab4b5-fef1-530e-806a-e497c463b2a5.dates: The Tiled Kiosk: 15th century; The photograph: 19th century
9d2ab4b5-fef1-530e-806a-e497c463b2a5.description2: The Tiled Kiosk is a pavilion set within the outer walls of Topkapı Palace that dates from 1472. It was built by the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II as a pleasure palace or kiosk. The building was used as the Imperial Museum between 1875 and 1891. In 1953, it was opened to the public as a museum of Turkish and Islamic art, and was later incorporated into the Istanbul Archaeology Museums. The collections of the Tiled Kiosk Museum consist of about 2000 artefacts belonging to the Seljuk and Ottoman eras, dating from the 11th-20th centuries. These artefacts include those that existed when the museum was incorporated into the İstanbul Archaeological Museums due to its proximity as well as those acquired through excavations, purchases, donations and confiscations.

9d8c93c7-c25d-5dce-a54d-fe8417fb0adc.name: All Saints' Anglican Church
9d8c93c7-c25d-5dce-a54d-fe8417fb0adc.description: All Saints' Church is an English language church founded in the 1870s. Located in the downtown area near the port, today it is overshadowed by high rise construction.
9d8c93c7-c25d-5dce-a54d-fe8417fb0adc.author: Hady El Hajj, Cynthia Karaki, Jennifer Harb
9d8c93c7-c25d-5dce-a54d-fe8417fb0adc.history: This church was first built for marine workers, located by the sea shore near Beirut Port. It later became the church used by the international English-speaking community. The Arab congregation was established later, mainly by Palestinian refugees who were driven from their homes following the 1948 war. Many of these were Lebanese Christians who had been living in Palestine, and joined the Anglican congregation upon their return. All Saints' Church is one of the 27 Anglican/Episcopal churches in the Diocese of Jerusalem and in the Middle East.

9d99f2a0-088c-5411-b1e4-aab5af09edf0.name: Photograph showing maintenance of the telephone network in Tangier
9d99f2a0-088c-5411-b1e4-aab5af09edf0.description: A photograph taken by a German photographer in 1923 showing maintenance of the telephone network that had been installed in Tangier since 1883.
9d99f2a0-088c-5411-b1e4-aab5af09edf0.keywords: Telephone; technical innovations; communication; telephone network; photograph; visual document; changes in urban space; modernisation; modern city; city

9d9c9b21-26f5-5feb-9433-34771e40c124.name: Nikola Karev
9d9c9b21-26f5-5feb-9433-34771e40c124.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
9d9c9b21-26f5-5feb-9433-34771e40c124.description2: Nikola Karev (1877–1905) was one of the ideological leaders and organizers of the Uprising of Ilinden. The uprising broke out on the night of 2 August 1903. After taking over, Krushevo revolutionaries declared the Krushevo Republic on 3 August. The Headquarters of the uprising took the military control over the town. The other governing bodies were the Revolutionary Council, consisting of sixty of the most prominent citizens representing all nationalities, and the Government, consisting of six members. Vangel Dinu was the Prime Minister and Nikola Karev was the President of the Republic. Owing to the progressive socialist ideas of Nikola Karev and other revolutionaries, the Krushevo Republic was laid on truly democratic foundations and republican principles. Karev announced the Krushevo Manifesto as a truly democratic document addressing all nationalities living in Macedonia, regardless of their religion, envisioning equal rights for everyone.

9dbfd8cd-e3bf-5f5f-bd09-c7f5a2634953.name: The Students’ Benevolent Fund of the Società Dante Alighieri
9dbfd8cd-e3bf-5f5f-bd09-c7f5a2634953.author: Giulia Barrera
9dbfd8cd-e3bf-5f5f-bd09-c7f5a2634953.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 122
9dbfd8cd-e3bf-5f5f-bd09-c7f5a2634953.description2: The Dante Alighieri Society – created in Italy in 1889 and still in existence ‒ is aimed at promoting Italian language and culture abroad; its Tunisian branch was established in 1893. In Tunisia the Dante Alighieri Society devoted its energies into promoting schooling and supporting school attendance. One should consider, in this regard, that the Italian community at the time was composed of workers, miners, and labourers and included several destitute members. The students’ benevolent fund of the Società Dante Alighieri (Patronato scolastico) was created in 1898 and was aimed at supporting school attendance of destitute children, by providing free books and clothes.

en: Pendola, M., *Gli italiani di Tunisia: storia di una comunità (XIX-XX secolo)*, Foligno: Editoriale Umbra, 2007.

9dcd91c6-e5a8-5dd3-b2fb-aa1eefe94502.name: *Plan of the Suez Canal*
9dcd91c6-e5a8-5dd3-b2fb-aa1eefe94502.author: Chiara Artico
9dcd91c6-e5a8-5dd3-b2fb-aa1eefe94502.archival: *Visite au Canal maritime de Suez. Rapport sur l’entraprise de M. Ferdinand de Lesseps adressé à la Chambre de commerce d’Alger par M. Félix Desvignes délégué au Congrès commercial international de Suez*, Alger 1865.
9dcd91c6-e5a8-5dd3-b2fb-aa1eefe94502.description2: This map was printed four years before the opening of the Suez Canal, in a book published in Algiers by the local Chamber of Commerce. It is evidence of the interest that the opening of the Canal aroused in North African countries other than Egypt, because of the business opportunities that it created.

9df78f35-3684-5c0b-9060-d03852ebe154.holder: History and Archeology Museum of Prahova County

9e1f9aa3-ee93-513e-b950-f4b409984db3.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History

9e555530-36a5-59e9-a179-0f1bdff61fd4.name: Seated *Pifferari*
9e555530-36a5-59e9-a179-0f1bdff61fd4.description2: The first significant waves of Italian migration abroad began in the mid-19th century during a period of great economic difficulty, with most migrants travelling to neighbouring European countries. One example of this was the "pifferari" - Italian shepherds from Abruzzo or Calabria who sung traditional songs accompanied by pipes - who started arriving in Paris. The famous French artist Charles Nègre (1820–1880) often focussed his work on street scenes such as this one.

9e674f9b-6875-58c3-9a9a-b05a50df35bb.name: Bellino Cylinder
9e674f9b-6875-58c3-9a9a-b05a50df35bb.keywords: Cuneiform; archaeology; exploration; travel; traveller; collection; collector; museums; clay; inscription
9e674f9b-6875-58c3-9a9a-b05a50df35bb.description2: One of the first objects from Nineveh to reach the West. Studied by Rich’s secretary, Karl Bellino. Bellino was a talented scholar of Middle Eastern languages. His new style of copying set the standard for rigorous study of cuneiform. His life ended tragically short; he died of fever in Mosul in 1820. Many European explorers and excavators lost their lives in the Middle East to disease or one of many other dangers.

9e8a7ea8-8f60-59b4-af77-1fef1a414d6a.name: Construction of the Aswan Dam
9e8a7ea8-8f60-59b4-af77-1fef1a414d6a.description2:
Photograph showing labourers during the construction of the Aswan Dam gates.  
Located in Upper Egypt, the Aswan Dam was the first water storage project in modern times.

9e9366e9-b19e-5ebc-a0ca-190882e7bb74.name: Deir el-Medina, Tomb of Kha at the moment of discovery
9e9366e9-b19e-5ebc-a0ca-190882e7bb74.holder: Soprintendenza Archeologia del Piemonte: Authority for the Archaeological Heritage of Piedmont
9e9366e9-b19e-5ebc-a0ca-190882e7bb74.author: Marcella Trapani
9e9366e9-b19e-5ebc-a0ca-190882e7bb74.keywords: Egyptomania; expedition; excavation; Vittorio Emanuele III; Florence; university; collection; languages; Thebes; Luxor; Giza; Heliopolis; Qaw el-Kebir; Hammamiye; Asyut; Nile; Egyptology; Nubia; hieroglyph; papyrology; epigraphy; ostrakon; Arabic
9e9366e9-b19e-5ebc-a0ca-190882e7bb74.copyright: Copyright image: Museo Egizio di Torino - Archivi Soprintendenza Archeologia del Piemonte.
9e9366e9-b19e-5ebc-a0ca-190882e7bb74.materials: Silver bromide negative impressed on glass plate
9e9366e9-b19e-5ebc-a0ca-190882e7bb74.third_name: Deir el-Medina, sito del rinvenimento della tomba di Kha
9e9366e9-b19e-5ebc-a0ca-190882e7bb74.description2: Photo by an unknown author showing the archaeologists Ernesto Schiaparelli and Francesco Ballerini on the site of the tomb of the architect Kha, together with workers and the supervisor of the Italian Archaeological Mission to Egypt. The tomb of the architect Kha (TT 8) was discovered untouched in 1906 by Ernesto Schiaparelli inside the necropolis of Deir el-Medina. It was located inside the village of the craftsmen who worked at the royal tombs in the Valley of the Kings. The holder had been "Head of the royal necropolis" and "Superintendent to the works of the royal necropolis" in the middle of the 18th dynasty, during the reigns of Amenhotep II (1428–1397 BC), Thutmose IV (1397–1388 BC) and Amenhotep III (1388–1351 BC). The Museum of Egyptian Antiquities preserves all these goods, with the exception of a lamp, which is in the Egyptian Museum of Cairo, while a copy is on display at the Egyptian Museum in Turin.

9e9f6fa6-b6c4-5566-9322-05ca25f72753.name: The Railway Bridge from Anatolia
9e9f6fa6-b6c4-5566-9322-05ca25f72753.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
9e9f6fa6-b6c4-5566-9322-05ca25f72753.dates: Late 19th century – begining of the 20th century
9e9f6fa6-b6c4-5566-9322-05ca25f72753.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Anatolian Railways
9e9f6fa6-b6c4-5566-9322-05ca25f72753.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

9edbfb79-9af7-5f97-a619-da304ecfa112.name: Set of photos illustrating Livestock Room, Donkey Room and Sheeps and Wool Room at Fu`ad Agricultural Museum
9edbfb79-9af7-5f97-a619-da304ecfa112.dates: 16 January 1938 (Photos taken during the inauguration of the museum)
9edbfb79-9af7-5f97-a619-da304ecfa112.description2: The Fu`ad Agriculture Museum was considered the first of its kind in the Middle East and the Arab World during the 1930s. It was inaugurated during the time of King Faruq, the son of King Fu`ad, and houses a large number of collections related to agricultural and rural environments, as well as agricultural plants and animals.

9ee00ba7-2731-5d14-b9bf-0d46da259600.name: Ismail, Khedive of Egypt (1830–1895)
9ee00ba7-2731-5d14-b9bf-0d46da259600.keywords: Ismail, Khedive of Egypt; Suez Channel; Great Britain
9ee00ba7-2731-5d14-b9bf-0d46da259600.description2: Portrait of Ismail, Khedive of Egypt (1830–1895), who financed the construction of the Suez Canal. Because of the enormous costs of the building and his reform measures, Egypt's debt rose from three million pounds sterling to 100 million pounds sterling. In 1875 Egypt was bankrupt and Ismail Pasha was forced to sell 176,602 shares to Great Britain for 3,976,582 pounds sterling. Egypt came under financial control of France and Great Britain.

9ee4a0fa-3ad1-5d46-a700-262cfde9d93d.name: Scarab brooch
9ee4a0fa-3ad1-5d46-a700-262cfde9d93d.description2: Illustrates the influence of Egyptian motifs on Victorian jewellery. Part of the second wave of Egyptianisation, related to the construction of the Suez Canal.

9f4dd257-a6bc-5852-b6b1-45af52c3e4f7.name: Military Medical kit of Carol Davila
9f4dd257-a6bc-5852-b6b1-45af52c3e4f7.description2: In the second half of the 19th century, French doctor Carol Davila played an important role in the development of the Romanian medical system. He came to Bucharest in 1853, sent by the French government at the request of Wallachian prince Barbu Stirbei who needed a specialist to form well trained Romanian doctors. Davila was named medic of the army and later general inspector of the country’s sanitary service and he was the founder of a medicine and pharmacy school. Among other decorations he received for his activity, he was awarded two Ottoman ones (the Orders of Medjidie and of Osmanie), the first for curing Ottoman soldiers who contracted cholera during the Ottoman occupation of Wallachia (1855), and the other for treating wounded Ottoman soldiers during the Russian-Ottoman war of 1877-1878.

9f63568d-d271-5f57-bc5d-a0c73ea5a902.name: Vase
9f63568d-d271-5f57-bc5d-a0c73ea5a902.description: Vase produced in Berlin in Oriental style.

9f63568d-d271-5f57-bc5d-a0c73ea5a902.artist: House of Arts and Crafts of the Hohenzollern family, H. Hirschwald, Berlin

9f6644b9-dc17-533b-8027-80f075461fd1.name: The first car produced by Gottlieb Daimler in 1886

9f97dfd5-8a30-53f7-9503-d00f973c94b8.name: Jacket
9f97dfd5-8a30-53f7-9503-d00f973c94b8.author: Marie Therese Moujabber

9fa1fbea-a4e2-5d50-9509-67fa9073a9d8.description2: Brass token issued by Borel Lavalley et Companie. In the centre is one of the sailing ships whose journey times would be dramatically improved by using the new Suez Canal.

a0ae7c32-123a-5f92-8eb4-161510e42915.name: 'Zahrat Al-Ihsan School
a0ae7c32-123a-5f92-8eb4-161510e42915.description: A view of the modern building of Zahrat al-Ihsan school, one of the most renowned Lebanese charitable institutions founded in the nineteenth century to provide education for young girls in Beirut.
a0ae7c32-123a-5f92-8eb4-161510e42915.author: Hala Masri
a0ae7c32-123a-5f92-8eb4-161510e42915.history: This school was founded by two sisters, Mary Geahchan and Ms Emilie Sursuq. The construction was funded by the donations from the Orthodox Church and first opened on 30 August 1881. Whilst it was originally a school for orphan girls, it later became a private school and became co-educational during the 1975-1990 Lebanese Civil War.

a0d6aa81-6f2f-566c-a687-f570ae278a69.name: Mihrişah Sultan Fountain
a0d6aa81-6f2f-566c-a687-f570ae278a69.description2: Westernisation brought about a change of form and decoration for fountains, which contributed to the urban structure of Istanbul.

a0dc5e60-a3ed-58a3-8317-2db79e5cbc80.name: Mico Liubibratic (1839–1889)
a0dc5e60-a3ed-58a3-8317-2db79e5cbc80.keywords: Mico Liubibratic; Congress of Berlin; Bosnia-Herzegovina
a0dc5e60-a3ed-58a3-8317-2db79e5cbc80.description2: Portrait of Mico Liubibratic. He was a commander of Herzegovinian freedom fighters against the Turks in 1876. This insurrection against the Turks provoked the 1878 Congress of Berlin, which led to the occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the Austrian Empire.

a0e6366a-857a-5838-b99e-0c94fb227f54.name: Dhat Hajj Station
a0e6366a-857a-5838-b99e-0c94fb227f54.holder: Saudi Commission for Tourism and Antiquities
a0e6366a-857a-5838-b99e-0c94fb227f54.history: Dhat Hajj is one of the most famous historical monuments inTabuk region, located at the north of the region at a distance of 85 km close to the Saudi-Jordanian border. This was a village inhabited in previous eras, as experienced by the caravans of pilgrims for rest and water supply. The importance of the village was increased with the arrival of the Hijaz Railway.
a0e6366a-857a-5838-b99e-0c94fb227f54.keywords: Pilgrimage; pilgrimage route; station; hajj; railway; communication; innovation; Arabian Peninsula; Saudi Arabia; Jordan; caravan; Hijaz; al-Madina al-Munawwara; sacred places; Ottoman; Germany; Abdul Hamid; abd al-hamid

a0f99391-e379-547b-847b-d300d897239b.name: Kairouan medina
a0f99391-e379-547b-847b-d300d897239b.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
a0f99391-e379-547b-847b-d300d897239b.history: The Arab Muslims conquerors founded the city of Kairouan in 670 under the orders of Uqba ibn Nafi, as a vital *point d'appui* in their campaign in North Africa. As the first Muslim city in the Maghreb it played a fundamental role in Islamic history, particularly towards the spread of Arab-Islamic civilisation. It remained the region's capital and one of its richest centres of Arab and Islamic culture for five centuries. The value and variety of its archaeological treasures aroused the interest of many European Orientalists in the 19th century. Many did not even hesitate in taking some of the so-called "oriental" aspects of the architecture they saw, and integrating it into their own creations. In fact, the study of Muslim Tunisian heritage saw a significant increase thanks to teh Orientalist architect Henri Saladin in the early 20th century.
a0f99391-e379-547b-847b-d300d897239b.keywords: Orientalism; Oriental architecture; Islamic arts; mosque; mausoleum; world heritage
a0f99391-e379-547b-847b-d300d897239b.description2: Thanks to the value and authenticity of its monuments and the richness and variety of its archaeological treasures, Kairouan can be considered a living museum of Arab and Islamic arts and civilisation. The richness of its monuments' architecture and the variety of its decorations is evidence for the important role Kairouan played in the development of the Islamic arts. Among its most important monuments are the Great Mosque of Uqba ibn Nafi, a masterpiece of universal mosque architecture which was also the foundation of many North African mosques, as well as the Three Doors Mosque with its sculpted façade, the Mausoleum of Sidi Sahbi, and many more. The city was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site on the 7 November 1988.

a104ff6a-9766-59a7-acc1-0e2d2676a230.name: Buckle
a104ff6a-9766-59a7-acc1-0e2d2676a230.description: Silver buckle, chiselled with floral and vegetal motifs, and the application, in golden brass, of an eagle and two hands. This kind of motif as a symbolic protection against the evil eye is reminiscent of the beliefs held before the arrival of the Islamic religion. The eagle is considered to be a symbol of power and the open hand is the most powerful protective existing symbol, but equally it symbolises the five fundamental principles of the Islam. In the North of Africa, the jewels that represented the social status of their carriers have turned into accessible adornment to all the social classes, used with protective character, especially against the evil eye. They are also a symbol of the wealth of a woman when she marries.

a10695d2-fbb1-56b0-aaa5-5b25ce6071ac.name: Sahib el-Tabaa Mosque
a10695d2-fbb1-56b0-aaa5-5b25ce6071ac.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
a10695d2-fbb1-56b0-aaa5-5b25ce6071ac.history: This mosque was the last great work of the Husainid dynasty of Tunisia. It was built by the powerful Youssef Saheb el-Tabaa between 1808 and 1814. Being the richest man in the country during Hammouda Pacha Bey's reign, he used his wealth to set up a variety of activities around his mosque, such as two madrasas and the tomb of its founder, similar to the Turkish Konya. The décor and ornamentation reflect Western influences, with a narrow and elegant minaret.
a10695d2-fbb1-56b0-aaa5-5b25ce6071ac.description2: This mosque's imposing height dominates the Place Halfaouine. The layout of the mosque is organised around its main prayer room, which is composed of nine naves and seven bays. The barrel-vaulted ceiling is covered in stucco, and decorated with vegetative and floral motifs and with geometric elements, such as stripes and stars, reflecting both its Italian and Turkish influences. It is also boasts of having the only five-domed prayer room in the city. The walls are covered in marble panels imported from Carrara (Italy) and ceramic tiles from Qallaline. The thin tall columns are ribbed and topped with composite capitals. The *mihrab*'s polychromatic decoration is mixed with the pseudo-gothic arches and floral motifs. The Sahib el-Tabaaa mosque is noteable for being one of the clearest examples of the Italian influences on religious architecture.

a12c9928-1d6f-5b1e-814c-74692d5b8de6.description2: Portrait of minister Sayed Ahmed Pasha Arabi (Urabi). In 1882, the war minister took power in Egypt and demanded an end to the financial control imposed by the UK and France. This led to an intervention by the British Navy under Admiral Seymour, who defeated the Egyptian army.

a15b7e00-538c-5aa8-a826-c4febf856606.name: In the Desert
a15b7e00-538c-5aa8-a826-c4febf856606.author: Marina Minozzi
a15b7e00-538c-5aa8-a826-c4febf856606.keywords: Orientalism; reinvention; historical events in paintings; exoticism; Verismo; diplomatic mission; Morocco; Mulay al-Hasan; travel; travelling artist; Italian travellers; Italian painters; Edmondo de Amicis; Marocco; travel book
a15b7e00-538c-5aa8-a826-c4febf856606.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
a15b7e00-538c-5aa8-a826-c4febf856606.description2: Cesare Biseo was a decorator and a realistic painter. He was sent to Egypt in 1870 to decorate the Theatre of the Opera in Cairo, where the painter Stefano Ussi also was working. In 1877 Biseo took part in the diplomatic delegation in Morocco with Ussi and de Amicis. Biseo’s painting *In the Desert* shows an exotic Verismo style of painting and is an example of the high status oriental paintings had in those years with the rise of Italian interests in colonialisation. The painting was bought by the Italian state in 1890 and displayed in the National Gallery of Modern Art of Rome in 1907.
a15b7e00-538c-5aa8-a826-c4febf856606.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

a18b6db1-d14e-59e8-adcd-89811928c6c2.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
a18b6db1-d14e-59e8-adcd-89811928c6c2.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; embassy; Ottoman diplomacy
a18b6db1-d14e-59e8-adcd-89811928c6c2.description2: In the 18th century, the Ottoman empire started to open permanent embassies in various capitals of Europe in order to more closely follow developments there and carry out interstate diplomacy more regularly. During the 19th century, the Ottoman Empire entered into intense western influence in almost every field. With the opening of the Ministry of Foreign Affaris, Ottoman diplomacy attained an institutional structure.

a1f0d2c4-ed0e-520e-ae95-52264d8e107d.name: The patients in Darülaceze Hospital
a1f0d2c4-ed0e-520e-ae95-52264d8e107d.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
a1f0d2c4-ed0e-520e-ae95-52264d8e107d.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; hospital; health
a1f0d2c4-ed0e-520e-ae95-52264d8e107d.description2: One of the world's largest photo archives, Abdülhamid II's photo archives – knows as the Yildiz Albums – contain about 37 thousand pictures from that period of the Ottoman Empire. The photo archives contain images of cities, buildings which were built by sultan, schools, students, soldiers, mosques, ports, government departments, shipyards, railways, bridges, bazaars, machines, locomotives and factories. Darülaceze Hospital was established in Okmeydanı, Istanbul İn 1895 on the instructions of Abdülhamid II for the care of elderly, homeless and disabled people in need.

a22ef18b-d87e-5980-a2f7-21310eb82200.name: Revolver
a22ef18b-d87e-5980-a2f7-21310eb82200.description: Revolver of Leopold Gasser, used for land/terrestrial defence as opposed to the navy. It is also known as “Montenegrin” as it was used not only by the Austrian army but also by the army of Montenegro. The exterior was nickelled, but the nickel finish has mostly worn away leaving only traces on the barrel and the frame. The plates of grip are missing. It is similar to item 65.

a234f19a-8239-5974-a86e-03dad4940736.name: St Elias Greek Catholic Cathedral
a234f19a-8239-5974-a86e-03dad4940736.description: The Saint Elias Cathedral, which can be found by the al-Najma Square in Downtown Beirut, is affiliated with the Greek Melkite Catholic Church in Lebanon. The cathedral was considered remarkable at the time of its completion in 1863, due to the architect's combination of Byzantine architecture with beautiful other decoration. It is also known for its neo-classical interior, marble iconostasis, Gothic arcs, and the celestial oculi.
a234f19a-8239-5974-a86e-03dad4940736.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
a234f19a-8239-5974-a86e-03dad4940736.history: This cathedral was completed in 1863 and has been visited by a great many pilgrims. It was restored by the Archdiocese in 1994, following a number of damages the structure bore during the Civil War. The works began in late 2003 and were completed in May 2006.
a234f19a-8239-5974-a86e-03dad4940736.keywords: Catholic; Cathedral; Religion; Tourism; Travelling; Saint; Beirut

a237773b-cce0-5972-a24d-1e563fd1cb62.name: Little jar with crested handle
a237773b-cce0-5972-a24d-1e563fd1cb62.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
a237773b-cce0-5972-a24d-1e563fd1cb62.author: Marina Minozzi
a237773b-cce0-5972-a24d-1e563fd1cb62.keywords: Applied arts; minor arts; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; model; reproduction; decoration; motifs; collection; collector; glass; Murano glass; glasswork; zoomorphysm; zoomorphic; glass filaments
a237773b-cce0-5972-a24d-1e563fd1cb62.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century and as a training school for specialising artisans. The concept was part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. The tendency of Murano's industries in using bizarre shapes, often of zoomorphic inspiration, gave life to manufacts not so much functional as extremely representative of the decorative needs, and it was very successful. The motif of glass filaments worked with pincers to look like crests, typical of the 17th century objects, is used also in the little ruby-red jar with gold leaf from the second half of the 19th century and resembling objects from Cinquecento and Seicento.
a237773b-cce0-5972-a24d-1e563fd1cb62.holding_institution_org: Museo Artistico Industriale presso la Galleria nazionale d’arte antica in Palazzo Barberini

a239b65c-d3b2-56bb-9598-00de8e920231.name: Bank note
a239b65c-d3b2-56bb-9598-00de8e920231.holder: Musée de la Monnaie: Banque centrale de Tunisie
a239b65c-d3b2-56bb-9598-00de8e920231.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
a239b65c-d3b2-56bb-9598-00de8e920231.description2: This 20 franc bill was first issued in 1783. It is blue and black on the front and blue on the back, and was issued by the Banque d’Algérie, which had the exclusive rights to issue notes in the Beylik of Tunis. The front of the note shows Mercury on the left and Hercules on the right. The penalty clause - article 139 - is written at the top in four lines. Beneath it we can see the inscription of the Banque d’Algérie and "20 francs". The number "20" is written in Arabic numerals on each side of the vignette with "Tunisie" written horizontally over it in black. A seated artist decorating vase is depicted on the back of the note on the left, and a harvester is on the right. The penalty clause - article 139 - is written again in six lines in a circle a the bottom. The number "20" is written in Arabic numerals on each side of the vignette.

a2684bac-db79-51f6-9e08-fdd75907b7bc.name: Choueit–'Araya Train Station
a2684bac-db79-51f6-9e08-fdd75907b7bc.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury
a2684bac-db79-51f6-9e08-fdd75907b7bc.history: The train line passing through this station went from Beirut to Damascus (Baramke) via Jamhur, 'Araya, 'Aley, Bhamdun, and 'Ayn Sawfar.
a2684bac-db79-51f6-9e08-fdd75907b7bc.keywords: Commerce; Train station; Railway; Transportation; Trading
a2684bac-db79-51f6-9e08-fdd75907b7bc.description2: This train station was not only built in the French style, but also operated in the same way as French railways, demonstrating the extent of French influence on architecture and infrastructure during this period: both passenger trains and freight trains, transporting goods and raw materials across land, served this line.

a2ba32a3-7747-5b54-b011-e71d3a84e08c.name: Dress
a2ba32a3-7747-5b54-b011-e71d3a84e08c.description: Pink silk twill dress lined with cotton, long-sleeved and high-waisted. The neckline is round in the front and triangle-shaped in the back. The upper bodice area is boned. Both breasts are marked with a U-shaped pleating. The skirt is soberly straight in front but it gains volume towards the back, ending in a short trail. The dress is fastened with invisible hooks at the back and adorned with buttons covered in the same silk fabric. The lower end presents a wide multi-coloured paisley frieze; each drop is composed of minute woven flowers. This elegant dress is a late variation of Empire dresses; the slender high-waisted silhouette is the same, but the fabric is thicker, the neckline has turned more modest and the long sleeves go down to cover part of the hands.

a2f41b51-30af-503a-a290-05cb553751f2.name: Part of a veil
a2f41b51-30af-503a-a290-05cb553751f2.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
a2f41b51-30af-503a-a290-05cb553751f2.author: Huda Kilani
a2f41b51-30af-503a-a290-05cb553751f2.keywords: Gold; Ottoman coins; above the nose; piece of cloth
a2f41b51-30af-503a-a290-05cb553751f2.description2: Five lines of gold ¼ Ottoman lira and other type of coins sewn together on a piece of cloth; such pieces were usually affixed above the nose on the veils, *burqu'*, of women of Beer Sheba. Fashion, local costumes and rites in the territories of Jordan and Palestine show identical elements, as this veil illustrates. It is one of the many examples of jewellery made with Ottoman coins to decorate veils and dresses. Jewellery was an important accessory for married women because pieces of jewellery constituted part of the dowry their husbands gave them for marriage. Jewellery was also a symbol of financial prestige: the more precious it was, the richer the husband’s family. Silver jewellery was the most common because only rich people could afford gold jewellery.

a2f82532-585d-587d-a629-11ce170fec48.name: Medal – Eugeniu Carada, founder of the National Bank of Romania

a318db34-bac0-5d0f-a3b5-606f258a4cf5.name: Ortaköy Mosque
a318db34-bac0-5d0f-a3b5-606f258a4cf5.description2: The original Ortaköy Mosque was built in the 18th century. The current mosque, which was erected in its place, was ordered by the Ottoman Sultan Abdülmecid and built between 1854 and 1856. Its architects were father and son Garabet Amira Balyan and Nigoğayos Balyan (who also designed the nearby Dolmabahçe Palace and the Dolmabahçe Mosque), who designed it in the Neo-Baroque style. It was during the same century that the mosque rose to a higher level of importance on the European side of Istanbul. It is also known as “Great Mecidiye Mosque” and is one of the most beautiful samples of Baroque architecture in Istanbul.

a34c17e6-990c-5cb0-95c0-c85297eb94e1.description: The Mamluks were excellent horsemen and aroused the attention of artists like Carle Vernet and Sebastian of Bourbon, a member of the Spanish Royal family. Artists did not need to have journeyed to the Near East or Arabia to be labelled Orientalists. This is a good example, because the authors did not travel to the Near East.

a3577379-4a3e-5997-913a-756fad78ca88.name: List of 15 'Tunisian Turks' captured by corsair captain Giuseppe Diano from the Kingdom of Sicily and sold in Palermo
a3577379-4a3e-5997-913a-756fad78ca88.author: Renata De Simone
a3577379-4a3e-5997-913a-756fad78ca88.archival: ASPa, Consultore del Governo, Tribunale delle prede, vol. 264, carte senza numerazione
a3577379-4a3e-5997-913a-756fad78ca88.description2: The documents explain that the captain corsair Giuseppe Diano plundered a Tunisian galliot and captured 15 “Tunisian Turks”. The captives’ names and ages (ranging from 15 to 55 years old) are listed. The document further explain that three out of such 15 captives had been sold to private individuals, while the remaining 12 had been bought by the Commissioner of the Committee for the Redemption of Captives (Deputazione della redenzione de’ cattivi); inferring that they were to be exchanged for Italian captives held in Tunisia. The Committee for the Redemption of Captives’ mission, in fact, was to negotiate the liberation of the subjects from the Kingdom of Sicily held as slaves.

a3c1cda7-3cd5-5acd-9fe6-bbcc3a97be64.name: Photograph of Bab Idris street
a3c1cda7-3cd5-5acd-9fe6-bbcc3a97be64.description: Pictured here is Bab Idris street, leading to Bab Idris, the city's western gate and the entrance to the old town. By the time of Ahmad Bey al-Jazzar's reign (1777–1804), the city had four main gates: Bab al-Dirka to the south, Bab al-Santiya to the west, Bab al-Dabbagha to the north, and Bab al-Saraya to the east. Jazzar Pasha built fortifications between these four main gates, which was not a fortified gate. Other city gates included Bab Yaqub, also in the east, Bab Abu Nasr at Burj square, and Bab Idris. These non-military gates are reflections of the city's rapid expansion, particularly due to an increase in trade.
a3c1cda7-3cd5-5acd-9fe6-bbcc3a97be64.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki

a3cb6230-39ef-51b4-80fd-ae00590616b9.name: *Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives*
a3cb6230-39ef-51b4-80fd-ae00590616b9.archival: Johnstone, Catherine Laura, *Christian and Jewish Pilgrims to the Holy Land*, London, 1899

a3cd6343-e399-52fc-beca-9b8315cf4639.name: *Panorama of the Compagnie Transatlantique* (French Line). *The "La Ville de Rome" steamer leaving the port of Algiers via Montenard*
a3cd6343-e399-52fc-beca-9b8315cf4639.artist: Photographer: Neurdein Frères; artist: Frédéric Montenard
a3cd6343-e399-52fc-beca-9b8315cf4639.second_name: Taken from the Exposition Universelle of 1889
a3cd6343-e399-52fc-beca-9b8315cf4639.description2: The emergence of steam boats in the 19th century allowed important maritime trade relationships to develop. In 1855, the Pereire brothers adopted this new method of transport and founded the Compagnie Générale Transatlantique (The French Line). The first line built served New York. In the 1880s the company then established an important line from Marseille to North Africa, which consisted of a 12-steamer strong fleet, the "sister ships" of the "Ville de Rome", which was first put into use in 1881. In March 1889, the "Ville de Rome" was run aground and washed up on the shores of Menorca. The passengers were evacuated in time, but the storm caused the wreck of the ship to break in two.

a417f6af-5483-5922-be43-098a03e3261f.name: *Algiers, site of the Lycée*
a417f6af-5483-5922-be43-098a03e3261f.author: Dalila Orfali
a417f6af-5483-5922-be43-098a03e3261f.description2: This building was home to the first French educational institution in Algiers, as indicated by its name "Lycée". It was built on the site of an ancient columbarium, not far from where the deys' tombs had been prior to their demolition and the construction of Bab el-Oued esplanade. It was constructed under the direction of the architect Frédéric Chassériau, although the archaeologist Adrien Berbrugger organised excavations before the works began. Today, it is called Lycée Émir Abdelkader, and remains one of the most important scholarly institutions in the city.

a434b4ec-9d28-510b-baac-35beab8f46ee.name: A map of the area around the 'Turkish graveyard' in the town of Livorno (Tuscany). The graveyard is represented as a small green rectangle
a434b4ec-9d28-510b-baac-35beab8f46ee.author: Daniela Tazzi
a434b4ec-9d28-510b-baac-35beab8f46ee.description2: In 1762, Muslims living in Livorno were granted a plot of land outside the city walls, near the beach, to build a graveyard (highlighted in green in the map). The graveyard remained in use until the second half of the 19th century. A Muslim graveyard existed in Livorno even before the 18th century. A significant Muslim community lived in the town. Its first members were captives taken to Italy as slaves. Muslim traders settled in town as well. In 1856, the graveyard was enlarged and surrounded by walls. In 1872 it was demolished to build a road and some of the graves were moved to the city graveyard.

a4505a95-37ac-56ac-a759-301f36d101f1.name: Ottoman coin – 10 Kurush 1876
a4505a95-37ac-56ac-a759-301f36d101f1.description2: After Moldavia and Wallachia became vassals of the Ottoman Empire, their rulers lost the right to struck coins. Therefore, commercial exchanges were done using foreign coins, the most widely  circulated being Ottoman coinage. Things changed in the second half of the 19th century when national coins were issued in the United Principalities starting with 1867.

a46e6bab-37d1-5f3c-a753-4f870c27eaf0.name: Babouches [slippers] given to the King of Italy by an Ambassador from Morocco visiting Italy in 1890
a46e6bab-37d1-5f3c-a753-4f870c27eaf0.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography
a46e6bab-37d1-5f3c-a753-4f870c27eaf0.author: Vito Lattanzi, Giulia Barrera
a46e6bab-37d1-5f3c-a753-4f870c27eaf0.description2:
In 1890, the Sultan of Morocco sent Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi as an ambassador to Italy. The Ambassador landed in Naples on June 7th and arrived by train in Rome on June 13th. At the railway station he was received by the Mayor or Rome, the Prefect, and other authorities. A military band was playing and military men in high uniform were paraded in the station to greet the Ambassador.  
Outside the station, three of the King’s gala carriages were waiting for the Ambassador and a military unit was paraded in his honour. Some carabinieri in high uniform escorted the Ambassador to the hotel.  
Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi presented the King with gifts, including some superb horses that the King immensely appreciated. The King presented the Ambassador with a magnificent small gold and diamond box and a hunting rifle and gave gold watches to the members of his escort.

a46e70b6-0a07-57b9-ad2a-d974179b2424.name: Water jug
a46e70b6-0a07-57b9-ad2a-d974179b2424.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
a46e70b6-0a07-57b9-ad2a-d974179b2424.author: Huda Kilani
a46e70b6-0a07-57b9-ad2a-d974179b2424.description2: A copper circular-shaped ewer with a very narrow neck, arched handle and strait long nozzle, used in mosques of Jordan and Palestine to wash before praying. This is another example of how the same objects, traditions, and activities were common in territories that now belong to different Arab states. In the late 19th century and early 20th century, there were still no boundaries between the Arab states and this – together with the lack of geographical barriers – made population movements, nomadism and migration a common factor influencing the everyday life and exchanges in the local society. The local economy, which relied heavily on trade and crafts, depended also on travel and migration in order to sell products or find markets for craft products.

a473894e-afa3-59b7-93f3-cec646d6e272.name: Excavation site in Carthage

a49b0d20-ff69-5123-aea8-1e3778e61417.name: Archaeological excavations
a49b0d20-ff69-5123-aea8-1e3778e61417.description2: Photograph of a pyramid at Abusir. The photo documents the excavation carried out by Juncker, a member of the German archaeological mission. The photo shows the tents for the members of the mission during the excavation of some clay pottery. The photo is printed from glass plate negatives, and it was included in the special archive for the archaeological areas of Saqqara and Abusir.

a4ee987f-15bb-56a1-b262-8f402df53ad9.name: *Inside a Jewish household*
a4ee987f-15bb-56a1-b262-8f402df53ad9.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
a4ee987f-15bb-56a1-b262-8f402df53ad9.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
a4ee987f-15bb-56a1-b262-8f402df53ad9.archival: Tunis au XIXe Siècle: Aquarelles et Textes de Charles Lallemand, Apollonia, 2001.
a4ee987f-15bb-56a1-b262-8f402df53ad9.description2: This copy of a beautiful watercolour by Charles Lallemand shows the inside of a bourgeois Jewish household. This snapshot of daily life reveals a great deal of similarity between Jewish and Muslim traditional dress and interiors.

a508bec6-1ea4-51c9-b5d8-a70ddc2a7baf.name: *Dans le harem: Divertissement Arabe.* For piano.
a508bec6-1ea4-51c9-b5d8-a70ddc2a7baf.description2: Musical composers' fascination with the "Orient" manifested itself in their music and their titles. The sphinx, for example, was a recurring symbol of "Egyptomania".

a50f8085-8ff8-57a1-9ecc-7536a8854029.name: Sword with scabbard
a50f8085-8ff8-57a1-9ecc-7536a8854029.description: A sword and scabbard decorated with geometric and floral motifs and crafted in southern Morocco in the 19th century. Sword blades were imported from Europe, especially from Toledo in Spain, or from Damascus in Syria.

a532878c-9737-5402-a686-e8febd96a222.name: *Klemens Wenzel Lother of Metternich-Winneburg (1773–1859)*
a532878c-9737-5402-a686-e8febd96a222.description2: Klemens Wenzel Lothar of Metternich was the leading diplomat at the Congress of Vienna (1815) who organized the balance of power between the European states. The core of Metternich's policy was supporting Austrian hegemony in Italy and preventing Russian hegemony in Germany. In the German Confederation, there existed an equilibrium between Austria and Prussian influences. Metternich's so-called "balance of power" politics ensured peace in Central Europe for a generation.
