b0aba8f3-6745-5b4a-b3a4-b7ed8dc1dafe.history:
Yildiz Palace, which is the last architectural example of Turkish Ottoman palace, is located on the Yildiz hill in the district of Besiktas. Sultan Ahmed I was the first to build a pavilion, over this land registered at the time to the Private treasury of the Ottoman Sultan as a hunting place sultans beginning during the reign of Suleiman the Magnificent (1520-1566).  
The main construction in the palace started in the period of Sultan Abdulhamid II (1876-1909) and it was called Saray-i Humayun (Central palace). During this period the palace comprised of buildings for private use of the sultan as well as buildings, allocated for the officials, repair shops and carpentry like repairing shop, carpenter’s shop and the buildings of culture and art such as theatre, museum and library. The Palace begun to serve as a museum under the name of “Directorate of the Museum of Yildiz Palace since 1993.
b0aba8f3-6745-5b4a-b3a4-b7ed8dc1dafe.description2: The building, which was opened as a museum on April 8th 1994, consists of a large gallery in 90 meters length. It is understood that the building was used as a museum as indicated by the photos of the reign of Sultan Abdulhamid II (1876-1909) and the valuable objects were exhibited in this residence. Art works, exhibited in the museum belongs to the palace; some of them were taken over while they were in Topkapi Palace. Art works included belongings of Sultan Abdulhamid II, his carpenter tools, gifts given to him and the products of Yildiz Porcelain Factory then.

b0c35ccd-b16d-5ff5-98a0-4001791ebd8b.name: Head of a sphinx of Sesostris III
b0c35ccd-b16d-5ff5-98a0-4001791ebd8b.description: The 12th Dynasty was the most important period of the Middle Kingdom. Its founder, Amenemhat I, vizier to the last Mentu-hotep (11th Dynasty), usurped the throne. His greatest challenge was to reintegrate the two parts of the country, Upper and Lower Egypt, which had split and subsequently grown apart during the First Intermediate Period.
b0c35ccd-b16d-5ff5-98a0-4001791ebd8b.dates: 12th Dyn. Sesostris III, 1878-1843 BC; brought to Vienna in 1893
b0c35ccd-b16d-5ff5-98a0-4001791ebd8b.dimensions: Height 21,9 cm, Width 33,2 cm, Diameter 32,1 cm

b0d5d8cd-688e-53ee-b19d-232a578cf9d0.name: Archaeological excavations
b0d5d8cd-688e-53ee-b19d-232a578cf9d0.description2: Photo showing the site of the archaeological excavations at Abusir, with a general view of the site at the time of the discovery of the foundations of the temple of the Sun (also known as Temple of Sahure). Photo taken by the German archaeological mission.

b0e2a692-ef6a-5333-8e53-cfbbf4c8b01b.name: The first high-rise building in Skopje
b0e2a692-ef6a-5333-8e53-cfbbf4c8b01b.author: Irena Nasteva (niece of Stefan  Nastev)
b0e2a692-ef6a-5333-8e53-cfbbf4c8b01b.history: This was the house of Stefan Nastev, a merchant and owner of the first watermill in Skopje, called Mlin Balkan. During his travels in Vienna, he bought an already worked-out project for construction of a house. His wish was to build a house for his family on the right bank of the Vardar River and he acquired permission from the authorities to do that. The house used to have workshops on the ground floor and an emergency hideout space in the basement, the first one in Skopje. Later the restaurant Pakao was opened in part of the basement. There were wall paintings in the restaurant painted by the renowned painter Nikola Martinoski.
b0e2a692-ef6a-5333-8e53-cfbbf4c8b01b.description2: This house was the first high-rise building constructed in Skopje. Building upon the experience of their predecessors and implementing locally available materials, Macedonian native architects have created their own distinctive style of construction. This structure shows the diversity of the traditional Macedonian urban architecture. It is a five-storey high-rise building of symmetrical type. It has shops on the ground floor. The usable surface of every floor measures 120 square metres. The façade is decorated with garlands and other floral elements, as well as sculptures on the roof.

b0e2dccd-96c5-50e2-b106-1f6ac20db945.name: Portait of a Lebanese boy
b0e2dccd-96c5-50e2-b106-1f6ac20db945.author: Hala Masri
b0e2dccd-96c5-50e2-b106-1f6ac20db945.description2: Pictured here is a small Lebanese boy, standing next to a board which reads "*La France, Louis Khoury*" (France, Louis Khoury).

b0ed31f3-fe54-54b4-a4f4-4797b7b507c3.name: The Stele of Mesha, King of Moab, c. 850 BC. Ruins of Dhiban
b0ed31f3-fe54-54b4-a4f4-4797b7b507c3.archival:
4-G-1036 (2)
L'homme et la terre. Tome 2 / Élisée Reclus
b0ed31f3-fe54-54b4-a4f4-4797b7b507c3.description2: The discovery of the Mesha stele, in August 1868 by the German missionary F. A. Klein in the Jordanian site of Dhiban, incited much excitement from the scientific community, as it helped shed lights on elements of Biblical history.

b0ef4082-e755-5416-9de1-d792e2c9ec9f.name: Tenement
b0ef4082-e755-5416-9de1-d792e2c9ec9f.description: The *wikalat* is a four-storey building with, generally speaking, two apartments per floor. The ground floor is occupied by a shop, and the building is located on a central market street. The central staircase was often built inside a cage. This very rigid separation between the private home and the busy street reflects a new conception between the public and private sphere during this period. If the building included a garden, for example, it was always located at the back of the building. Therefore, the architecture of this building discouraged interaction with the outside world, leaving little access to open air and cutting off the private space from the surrounding environment. This is particularly true of the residences located on the upper floors.
b0ef4082-e755-5416-9de1-d792e2c9ec9f.author: Jeff El-Msanne, David Andos
b0ef4082-e755-5416-9de1-d792e2c9ec9f.history: Two-storey residences emerged in the last decade of the 19th century. Higher, multiple-storey homes were introduced to Beirut after the First World War, following to the arrival of reinforced concrete as an available building material. Although the frame of the building was made of reinforced concrete columns, the walls continued to be built with *ramleh* stone.
b0ef4082-e755-5416-9de1-d792e2c9ec9f.keywords: Tenement; Elevation; Story; House; Architecture; Typology

b0efd48f-c5dd-580f-97dd-0300a02b3fc2.name: *La Tunisie martyre*
b0efd48f-c5dd-580f-97dd-0300a02b3fc2.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
b0efd48f-c5dd-580f-97dd-0300a02b3fc2.author: Bechir Yazidi
b0efd48f-c5dd-580f-97dd-0300a02b3fc2.description2: *La Tunisie Martyre: Ses Revendications* (better known by its abbreviated title, *La Tunisie Martyre*) is a Tunisian book written in French and published in Paris in January 1920, attributed to Abdelaziz Thâalbi (Abdelaziz al-Thalibi). Having arrived in Paris on 10 July 1919, Thâalbi started writing a book by the title *Tounes al-Shahida* (Tunisia the Martyr). Although the published book does not bear his name, Thâalbi admitted to having written it in Arabic, as can be seen from the reports sent from Tunis by the future leaders of the Destour party. As he was not able to write in French, he asked his friend Ahmed Sakka, a lawyer living in Paris, to translate the book into French. A few months after the publication of *La Tunisie Martyre*, an arrest warrant was issued for Abdelaziz Thâalbi. He was arrested on 28 July 1920 in Paris, and transferred, by escort, to Tunis, where he was taken to the military prison and charged with jeopardizing national security.

b111e780-75c2-51e3-bb5c-dda0ea9e3015.name: Execution of the nationalists
b111e780-75c2-51e3-bb5c-dda0ea9e3015.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
b111e780-75c2-51e3-bb5c-dda0ea9e3015.author: Bechir Yazidi
b111e780-75c2-51e3-bb5c-dda0ea9e3015.description2: Pictured here are three Tunisian men sentenced to death and a photograph of a public execution using a guillotine brought over especially from Algeria. These two young men, barely 20 years old, were implicated in the events of the 7 November 1911, known as the Jellaz Affair. The memory of this execution is still alive today in Tunisia.

b1189adf-8651-54d6-9426-8461bdc5c6a6.name: Figurine of a dog
b1189adf-8651-54d6-9426-8461bdc5c6a6.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
b1189adf-8651-54d6-9426-8461bdc5c6a6.description2: Dimitrija Chupovski (1878–1940) was the President of the Slav-Macedonian Scientific Literary Society in St. Petersburg also known as St. Petersburg Colony of Macedonians. Chupovski was also actively engaged in publishing of the periodical Macedonian and Russian-language publication, “Makedonski Golos” (“Macedonian Voice"), first issued in 1912.

b15011a9-1d5f-5210-be56-0a51595a1b75.name: The King's House on the Schachen
b15011a9-1d5f-5210-be56-0a51595a1b75.type: Hunting lodge; summer manor; royal villa in the mountains
b15011a9-1d5f-5210-be56-0a51595a1b75.location: Bavarian Alps near Garmisch-Partenkirchen; altitude 1,866 meters
b15011a9-1d5f-5210-be56-0a51595a1b75.history: The Turkish Room inside the King's House on the Schachen spreads an Oriental fairytale charm with a gold, blue and red colour combination. The design for the room was based on an engraving by the Englishman Thomas Allom, published in an architectural work on Constantinople. The engraving shows a room built by Sultan Selim III (r. 1789–1807) in the Palace of Eyüb. However, the overall impression created by the furniture and colourfulness derives entirely from contemporary influences.
b15011a9-1d5f-5210-be56-0a51595a1b75.keywords: King Ludwig II; Bavaria; mountain refuge; Schachen; Moorish style; Romanticism; gardens
b15011a9-1d5f-5210-be56-0a51595a1b75.description2: The King's House, built from plans by Georg Dollmann in 1869 to 1872 on the Schachen Alp near Garmisch-Partenkirchen, was King Ludwig II's mountain refuge. The wooden post-and-infill structure in the form of a Swiss chalet has five living rooms downstairs with cembra wood panelling and a mixture of stylistic elements. The whole of the upper floor, however, is taken up by the "Turkish Hall". With its coloured glass windows, opulently embroidered textiles, peacock feathers and candelabra it reflects the fascination of the king and his contemporaries with the Orient.

b1761f2e-80b8-586f-b4e2-c3736d979725.name: Photograph of an employee outside the *Poste-Cherifienne* office
b1761f2e-80b8-586f-b4e2-c3736d979725.description: The first national post and transport service in Morocco was founded by Mulay al-Hasan I on 20 Jumada I 1390 (22 November 1892) and was known as the *Poste-Makhzen*. The office was established in order to take control nationally of the postal (mainly parcels and messengers) service in Morocco, but competition from private foreign firms was tough. When in 1892 the Sultan first gave orders for port managers to take control of Morocco’s interests in this regard, this nascent organisation included 13 Moroccan cities, defined as zones connected by transport links, and each defined by specific costs.
b1761f2e-80b8-586f-b4e2-c3736d979725.keywords: Postal service; post offices; Moroccan postal service; communication; routes; port; rakkas; delivery; local postal service; foreign companies; private firms; postal network

b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.name: Steam engine building
b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.holder: Prussian Palaces (Stiftung Preussische Schlösser und Gärten Berlin Brandenburg)
b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.history:
In October 1842 the steam engine in the "Mosque," which could reach 81.4 horsepower, was inaugurated, allowing jets of water from the great fountain in front of Sanssouci Palace to rise to an impressive 38 meters. By possessing what was the most powerful machine in Prussia at the time, built by the young entrepreneur August Borsig, King Frederick William IV hoped to compete with the technical supremacy of England.  
Although today's supply of water to the fountains in Sanssouci Park is provided by means of modern electrical pumps, a visit to the "Mosque" allows the visitor to experience a technical marvel from days past that is still in operation.
b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.keywords: Moorish style; Romanticism; Sanssouci; Potsdam; exoticism; steam engine; steam pumping; Frederick William IV; gardens
b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.description2: The Steam Engine Building, located on a bay of the Havel River called the Neustädter Havelbucht, is at once the most charming as well as the most exotic building in Potsdam. Frederick William IV, the "Romantic on the throne," had it built by Ludwig Persius from 1841-1843, "in the style of the Turkish mosques, with a minaret as a smokestack." The building, which could still be seen at that time from Sanssouci Palace, added a picturesque architectural accent to the Potsdam cultural landscape.

b1ada77d-4a0f-5105-a292-423509ecec6b.name: Haydarpaşa Train Station
b1ada77d-4a0f-5105-a292-423509ecec6b.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
b1ada77d-4a0f-5105-a292-423509ecec6b.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Train Station
b1ada77d-4a0f-5105-a292-423509ecec6b.description2: In 1871 Sultan Abdülaziz ordered a rail line to be built from Haydarpaşa to İzmit. Haydarpaşa station opened in 1872, and in 1888 the Anatolian Railway (CFOA) took over the line and the station. Since the station was built next to the Bosporus, freight trains would unload at Haydarpaşa and the freight would be transferred to ships. Haydarpaşa was chosen to be the northern terminus of the Baghdad Railway and the Hijaz Railway in 1904 and with rail traffic increasing, a new and larger building was required. The Anatolian Railway hired two German architects; Otto Ritter and Helmut Conu to build the new building. They chose a neo-classical structure and construction started in 1906.

b1caaa98-898d-5835-84d6-2569546ecf1d.name: Document attesting to the 'Telegraph Crisis' between Morocco and Great Britain
b1caaa98-898d-5835-84d6-2569546ecf1d.description: A letter from Sultan al-Hasan I to his Minister of Foreign Affairs and representative in Tangier, Muhammad ibn al-‘Arabi al-Torres, ordering the immediate cessation of work on installation of the telegraph system between Gibraltar and Tangier, which the British had undertaken without negotiating with Morocco, thereby causing a diplomatic crisis between the two countries.
b1caaa98-898d-5835-84d6-2569546ecf1d.keywords: Communication; technical innovation; telegraph; telegraph installation; Telegraph Crisis; foreign companies; British in Morocco; diplomacy; Moroccan-British relations

b1dc4de3-1a52-53d0-8dcb-4569af75ef27.holder: Saudi Commission for Tourism and Antiquities

b20d222f-63fe-50b9-acfd-a854de63e772.name: Photograph: *A Mohammedan Funeral, Egypt*
b20d222f-63fe-50b9-acfd-a854de63e772.description: Stereoscopic photography that creates the illusion of depth of field from a two-dimensional image by using a specific viewfinder, or stereoscope. The photograph is formed by two apparently identical images mounted on a rigid board. Stereographic cards turned into a popular entertainment medium from the late 1880s until 1970, reaching its peak of popularity in the first decade of the twentieth century. The ceremonies of funeral, studied for example by the British anthropologist Edward William Lane around the time of the dating of the photography, are very similar for men and women: the wailing is produced by the family and community, and is accompanied by a series of prayers from the Qur´an and ritual cleansing of the body. In this photography, within this "farewell ceremony" we can distinguish the coffin and the funeral procession, mostly male, who plays different songs and prayers; after the coffin, the procession would be closed for the mourners.
b20d222f-63fe-50b9-acfd-a854de63e772.keywords: Photography; funeral; ritual; travel; Egypt; scenes of life

b22085c1-312d-582f-860a-c9fff2302d01.name: Tripoli Evangelical School
b22085c1-312d-582f-860a-c9fff2302d01.description: The school consists of an elementary, an intermediate, and a secondary school, each located in separate buildings. The buildings are all examples of typical traditional Lebanese architecture, with white bordered windows and green shutters on the front facades.
b22085c1-312d-582f-860a-c9fff2302d01.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
b22085c1-312d-582f-860a-c9fff2302d01.history: Founded in 1873 by American Protestant Missionaries, Tripoli Evangelical School is one of the oldest high schools in the country, and one of the first pre-higher education institutions in the Middle East. It is located in the city of Tripoli in northern Lebanon, and is part of the National Evangelical Synod of Syria and Lebanon. The school is still in use today, having survived the violent conflicts that have struck Lebanon since its establishment.

b23d072c-13ac-5c66-9709-b4cefd84d692.name: Inkwell with Oriental decoration
b23d072c-13ac-5c66-9709-b4cefd84d692.description2: The use of this type of inkwell was borrowed in the Romanian lands from the Ottomans. This particular inkwell belonged to Ion Ghica, one of the Romanian politicians who prepared the 1848 Wallachian revolution. As member of Wallachia’s revolutionary committee, he was sent to Istanbul before the start of the revolution to have talks with Ottoman officials and the ambassadors of European states, in an attempt to convince them to support the claims of the Romanian revolutionaries. After the revolution was defeated, he remained in Istanbul. Between 1854-1857 he was governor of Samos. In 1866, after the election of Carol of Hohenzollern as prince of the United Principalities, Ghica went to Istanbul (May-July) to try to obtain the recognition of his reign.

b2525f86-10f4-5e6f-b558-0f92275571e7.name: Sword with scabbard
b2525f86-10f4-5e6f-b558-0f92275571e7.description: A sword and scabbard decorated with geometric and floral motifs and crafted in southern Morocco in the 19th century. Sword blades were imported from Europe, especially from Toledo in Spain, or from Damascus in Syria.
b2525f86-10f4-5e6f-b558-0f92275571e7.keywords: Trade; arms; armours; metalwork; geometric motifs; geometric decoration; floral decoration; vegetal motifs; vegetal decoration; craftsmanship; war; warfare; military objects

b25ced0a-8fbc-5812-85b3-eb1df7ad87a4.name: An Entertainment Scene (The third day of entertainment) from *Surname-i Vehbi*
b25ced0a-8fbc-5812-85b3-eb1df7ad87a4.archival: The Library of Sultan Ahmed III
b25ced0a-8fbc-5812-85b3-eb1df7ad87a4.description2: The image at the left shows an earlier stage of the flotilla. A long raft in the foreground carries a huge structure shaped like a cypress tree from which strings of fireworks are suspended along with two Catherine wheels. Rockets and projectiles hurtle about. On the basis of Vehbi’s account, this is the float prepared by the artillerymen’s corps. A two-story structure set on a pair of caiques carries a troupe of dancers and musicians on the lower floor while pyrotechnicists are busy at work on the upper one.

b29cbfc5-92ab-5924-883e-7d561e5c7761.name: *Temple and fountain of Zaghwan*
b29cbfc5-92ab-5924-883e-7d561e5c7761.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
b29cbfc5-92ab-5924-883e-7d561e5c7761.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
b29cbfc5-92ab-5924-883e-7d561e5c7761.archival: Copied from a drawinig by Sir Grenville Temple, published in his book The Shores and Islands of the Mediterranean in London in 1840, this drawing was taken from Chelli Zouhir, La Tunisie au Rythme des Estampes du XVe au XIXe siecle (Tunis, ed. Tunis Carthage: 1992), p. 65, fig. 25.
b29cbfc5-92ab-5924-883e-7d561e5c7761.description2: This drawing of the temples and fountains of Zaghwan was drawn by Sir Grenville Temple in the mid-19th century. The triumphal arc and the nymphaeum are carved with two important tales from the city's ancient history. This water temple, located at the feet of Mount Zaghwan, contains a 30 metre long semicircle nymphaeum, bordered on the inside by arched galleries fitted with various niches. At its feet lies a pool, flowing with water which is then carried all the way to Carthage.

b2a64729-0616-53e6-bc8d-4d7583ceac8c.name: Plate
b2a64729-0616-53e6-bc8d-4d7583ceac8c.description2: Sultan Abdülhamid II founded in 1891 the *Yıldız Çini Fabrika-i Hümâyûnu* (Yıldız Royal Tile Factory) in the garden of Yıldız Palace in order to revive Turkish tile art and give it a new direction and momentum. Vases, hanging wall plates and many sorts of daily-use wares were produced in the factory, including writing and dinner table utensils, card plates, lidded bowls, pans, *aşure* (a kind of dessert) trays, sugar bowls, tea and coffee cups. This plate features a dark green background on which there is a *tuğra* (monogram) made of gilding and a border around the edge.

b2b60a11-2b17-5d73-a263-caf53997a1bf.name: *The Church of the Holy Sepulchre*
b2b60a11-2b17-5d73-a263-caf53997a1bf.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
b2b60a11-2b17-5d73-a263-caf53997a1bf.archival: Johnstone, Catherine Laura, *Christian and Jewish Pilgrims to the Holy Land*, London, 1899
b2b60a11-2b17-5d73-a263-caf53997a1bf.keywords: Pilgrimage; pilgrims; Christian pilgrimage; Jewish pilgrimage; Palestine; Holy Land; Jerusalem; sacred places; travel; travel book; Ottoman Palestine; local Jewish community
b2b60a11-2b17-5d73-a263-caf53997a1bf.description2: This photograph shows the Church of the Holy Sepulchre as it appeared in 1899. This church, together with other ancient monuments and landmarks, was a typical destination for Christian pilgrims travelling from Europe and Russia. Christian pilgrimage was seen as a starting point to describe "exotic" places and "Eastern" culture. Some Christian pilgrims described in their writings historical and cultural details and curiosities and their impressions of 19th century Palestinian society, the increasing number of pilgrims – especially Russian and Jews – and the institutions such as the Russian consulate, English and German churches and Latin monks that accommodated the Christian pilgrims.

b2d452de-0ae0-577e-b868-f2761e941b26.name: Vase with stand
b2d452de-0ae0-577e-b868-f2761e941b26.description: This vase with stand reproduces the shape of the ceramic vase known as "The Alhambra vase" and the stand recalls the little tables of the Arab cafés. The technique used is damascening and references Arab techniques of metal decoration. It is a good example of the extension of the Neo-Mudéjar style, not only in the decorations, as the interlacing arabesques, or techniques, but also in the shape of the artworks.
b2d452de-0ae0-577e-b868-f2761e941b26.author: Ana Cabrera
b2d452de-0ae0-577e-b868-f2761e941b26.keywords: Neo-mudejar style; Applied Arts; Production of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode

b3139452-a18c-5578-a8f9-65f5a88d9fe0.name: A treaty between the Regency of Tunis and the Grand Duke of Tuscany, concerning the jurisdiction over Tuscan Jews who migrated to Tunisia
b3139452-a18c-5578-a8f9-65f5a88d9fe0.author: Loredana Maccabruni
b3139452-a18c-5578-a8f9-65f5a88d9fe0.archival: ASFi, Trattati Internazionali, CXCII [192]: “Modificazione del Trattato commerciale fatto colla Reggenza di Tunisi nel 1822 relativamente agli Israeliti”
b3139452-a18c-5578-a8f9-65f5a88d9fe0.description2:
Treaty of one article, in Italian and Arabic, signed by the Tuscan Consul Enrico Nyssen and by the Bey Ahmed Bascià, sealed with a wax seal of the Consulate General of Tuscany, and ratified by the Grand Duke of Tuscany Leopold the II on 29 January 1847.  
This treaty modified the 1822 treaty between the two countries which had given to the Jews from Livorno the same status of Tunisian Jews (placing them under the Beys' jurisdiction). According to this new treaty, the Tuscan Jews who had moved to Tunisia (or would move to Tunisia in the future) and registered in the Tuscan Consulate, were placed under Tuscan jurisdiction and protection. Such provision did not apply to the so-called “Grana” Jews who had moved to Tunisia from Livorno (Tuscany) in the late 17th century.

b33144e1-5551-5a5c-a7ba-4cefefd46e94.name: Funeral statue of Lady Khent and her youngest child
b33144e1-5551-5a5c-a7ba-4cefefd46e94.description: The funerary statues of the *mastaba* tombs in the Old Kingdom were kept in sealed rooms called *serdabs*. The statues were believed to be alter egos of the deceased, apt to receive the mortuary rites, which were then completed in the adjacent tomb chapel. Khen (full name, Khentit-ka) was the wife of a high official. The sculpture is a magnificent example of the Old Kingdom canonical sculpture in the round.
b33144e1-5551-5a5c-a7ba-4cefefd46e94.dates: c. 2300 BC; acquired by Hermann Junker during his excavation in Giza 1912–1929

b34a6459-d73e-575a-bf25-d6eeecca51a1.name: *The Opening of the Suez Canal*
b34a6459-d73e-575a-bf25-d6eeecca51a1.author: Marina Minozzi
b34a6459-d73e-575a-bf25-d6eeecca51a1.keywords: Sculptors; route; travel; waterway; Austria; Lloyd; Assicurazioni Generali; Bourse; Adriatic; Egypt; Said; Ismail; Pasha; Ferdinand de Lesseps; Suez Canal Company; Compagnie universelle du canal maritime de Suez; vice-president; Cairo; India
b34a6459-d73e-575a-bf25-d6eeecca51a1.description2: The artist Pietro Magni studied at the Academy of Brera, travelled to Rome in 1849 and battled for the Roman Republic. His first artwork as mentioned in the author’s biography is *The First Steps*, known though the photographs to have been on display at the International Exhibition in London in 1862. In 1863 the businessman Pietro Revoltella commissioned the artist to create a marble group showing the opening of the Suez Canal, now in the Revoltella Museum in Trieste. It shows how important the project was for the commissioner, confident that the new opening toward the East would offer economic advantages to his city. Unfortunately he died two months before seeing the Suez Canal completed. The sculpture shows a classical allegory with Europe uniting the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea, behind them the genius of commerce with winged feet indicating the canal the unifies Europe and Asia.

b36eb729-4fe6-5e15-afd4-f0f28879427d.name: Fort Rottembourg
b36eb729-4fe6-5e15-afd4-f0f28879427d.history: The Krupp Company provided Sultan Mulay ‘Abd al-‘Aziz (1894-1908) with big guns of the latest model. Fort Rottembourg was named after an officer of the Krupp Company.
b36eb729-4fe6-5e15-afd4-f0f28879427d.keywords: Fortress; German in Morocco; Krupp; steel; industrialisation; industrialists; foreign companies; changes in urban space; modernisation; economy; trade; military architecture
b36eb729-4fe6-5e15-afd4-f0f28879427d.description2: Built on a slight hill on the coast, this fortification is surrounded by deeply sloping masonry ditches. At the foot of the slopes – to enhance the effectiveness of them as defensive barriers – two huge wrought-iron domes cover the command posts from which part of the length of two enormous guns are visible.

b3ad190f-fed9-546e-924a-e3b7f2699f23.name: *The Ka'ba in Mecca*
b3ad190f-fed9-546e-924a-e3b7f2699f23.keywords: Mecca; pilgrimage; buildings of worship; plan
b3ad190f-fed9-546e-924a-e3b7f2699f23.description2: Émile Prisse d'Avennes (1807–1879) drew this plan of the Ka'aba in Mecca, a detailed view of the place of pilgrimage which had so fascinated Europeans.

b3ffe5a9-b94e-57b4-815b-88dcdb526256.name: *Tomb of Sultan Selim II*
b3ffe5a9-b94e-57b4-815b-88dcdb526256.description2: Although essentially a realist painter, Şevket Dağ worked with free brush stokes in the style of Corot. He is celebrated for his paintings of the interiors of mosques. He took lessons from Osman Hamdi Bey, and followed his master in painting genre pictures reflecting various aspects of Ottoman life. In addition to mosque interiors he would also paint scenes in market places, still-life compositions and the interiors of houses. Over time, Şevket Dağ's work began to be appreciated abroad following exhibitions in European art centres such as Munich and Paris, and he was awarded a gold medal in the Munich International Exhibition of 1909. He later came under the influence of the impressionists.

b446feeb-3505-58d3-be81-c30f25be28fc.name: Peace Treaty of Campo Formio, 17 October 1797, between the French Republic and the Austrian Empire
b446feeb-3505-58d3-be81-c30f25be28fc.description2: With the Peace of Campo Formio in October 1797, Napoleon confirmed the conditions of the armistice at Leoben, which was signed in April 1797. Austria had to cede Belgium and Lombardy to France and was compensated with the eastern part of the Venetian Republic.

b474efac-e6f6-5108-a2dd-76d0a7cfc596.name: Metal teapot

b4a14dd7-63bc-5f3a-b31a-2ae6a297fc74.name: Qatranah Railway Station
b4a14dd7-63bc-5f3a-b31a-2ae6a297fc74.author: Mohammad Najjar
b4a14dd7-63bc-5f3a-b31a-2ae6a297fc74.history: In 1900-1908, Sultan Abdul Hamid with the help and support of Germany established a Railway between Damascus and Mecca (1700 km) to facilitate transporting the pilgrims. The track from Medina to Mecca (400 km) was never realized. The cost of the project was estimated at approximately 5 million Ottoman golden liras, which were provided from: private donations, revenues of the Ottoman State from the sale of stamps, and a special tax upon all citizens for the railway. Construction of the narrow-gauge track (105cm) began in 1900 with a wire telegraph line along its side connecting Damascus with Medina across Amman with a total track length of 1303 km. Official inaugurations of the tracks and stations were scheduled to coincide with the accession of the Sultan to the throne in the month of September every year. The construction of the project ended in 1908.
b4a14dd7-63bc-5f3a-b31a-2ae6a297fc74.keywords: Hijaz; railway; station; pilgrimage; hajj; pilgrimage route; communication; telegraph; Jordan; Damascus; Mecca; Makka; Amman; Zarqa; Qatranah; Ma'an; Amman; Tabuk; Arabian Peninsula; Ottoman; Abd al Hamid; Germany; Meinsner
b4a14dd7-63bc-5f3a-b31a-2ae6a297fc74.description2: Qatranah is an important station on the Hijaz railway. It consists of a group of building along the railroad. The station had been protected by a renovated small 16th-century fortress located to the west of the railway. The fortress was provided with water wells and pools for both the humans and the animals. The various components of the project including the rails, steam engines, bridges, stations were an industrial, architectural and engineering statement that had a huge influence on Jordan. The tracks and the station was completed in September 1904.

b4dc43ea-b3d1-58c6-bc57-9f2f74291cc6.name: Medal – Semi-centenary of the European Commission of the Danube
b4dc43ea-b3d1-58c6-bc57-9f2f74291cc6.description2:
In 1856, the treaty of Paris, signed on 30 March, internationalized the Danube and established the European Commission of the Danube, an inter-state institution (comprising delegates of Austria, France, Great Britain, Prussia, Sardinia and Russia) that had to ensure and facilitate navigation at the mouths of the river.  
Issued on the 50th anniversary of the Commission, this medal was designed by O. Patey. On the obverse is depicted the god Danubius, holding a trident in his left hand and lying by the Danube, with his elbow on a stone pipe from which water flows into the river. On the edge is inscribed “Commission Européenne du Danube. On the reverse “1856-1906” is engraved inside a wreath of oak and laurel leaves. Above there is the inscription: “Article 16 du Traite de Paris du 30 Mars 1856”.

b4f64de8-89f2-5608-a2d6-f642d0ce7827.name: *Cairo, from the Gate of Citizenib, looking towards the Desert of Suez*
b4f64de8-89f2-5608-a2d6-f642d0ce7827.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
b4f64de8-89f2-5608-a2d6-f642d0ce7827.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
b4f64de8-89f2-5608-a2d6-f642d0ce7827.keywords: Fatimah Khatun; Sultan Khalil; Sayidah Nafisah; Madrasah of Sultan Hassan; Khedive Ismail
b4f64de8-89f2-5608-a2d6-f642d0ce7827.description2: Although entitled 'Cairo from the Gate of Citizenib, looking towards the Desert of Suez', this view actually shows Cairo as seen from Tel Zaynum, situated to the south of the city. The monuments depicted include the tombs of Fatimah Khatun and Sultan Khalil on the left and the mosque of Sayidah Nafisah on the right. In the background, one can discern both the Cairo citadel on the right and the Madrasah of Sultan Hassan on the left. Notwithstanding the incorrect identification of this area of Cairo, the scenes gives a good impression of one of its quarters with its traditional urban architecture and historical monuments before major urban development projects were undertaken under the Khedive Ismail (1863-1879), who was determined to turn Cairo into a modern, international city  on a par with European capitals.

b4f75aa6-644c-5905-aa3f-64df7691791f.name: *Le retour de la guerre de Crimée* (painting)
b4f75aa6-644c-5905-aa3f-64df7691791f.holder: Palais de la Rose – Musée de l’Armée
b4f75aa6-644c-5905-aa3f-64df7691791f.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
b4f75aa6-644c-5905-aa3f-64df7691791f.keywords: Oil on canvas; B. de Moynier; Mohamed Pacha Bey; Crimean war
b4f75aa6-644c-5905-aa3f-64df7691791f.materials: Canvas, wood, coloured pigments, gold leaf
b4f75aa6-644c-5905-aa3f-64df7691791f.description2: This oil on canvas by B. de Boynier shows a Tunisian military parade returning from war in the Crimea, headed by the current bey, Mohamed Pacha, at the gates of the Palais de la Marsa (1856). The Nichan al-Iftikhar can be seen on the bey's chest. Foot soldiers and horsemen, dressed in European style, carry the Tunisian flag. The General Osman is at the head of the horsemen, and the General Rashid, the commanding officer of the Tunisian military expedition to the Crimea, is to the bey's right. Tunisia sent about 14,000 men in support of the Ottomans and their allies during the Crimean war of 1854–1856).

b5036b5d-8c8a-54bc-9e98-cd2351f8ef63.name: *Djouni. The residence of Lady Hester Stanhope*
b5036b5d-8c8a-54bc-9e98-cd2351f8ef63.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
b5036b5d-8c8a-54bc-9e98-cd2351f8ef63.keywords: Joun; Lebanon; women; Romanticism; travel; traveller; drawing
b5036b5d-8c8a-54bc-9e98-cd2351f8ef63.description2: William Henry Bartlett was a prolific topographical artist who travelled extensively in search of new and interesting subjects for his drawings. He visited North Africa and the Middle East seven times and made several other trips in Britain and Europe, as well as North America. Popular demand for travel books was high during the 1830s and 1840s and Bartlett contributed illustrations to several of them including about a dozen written by himself. His aim as he described it was 'to give lively impressions of actual sights'. Bartlett visited the celebrated Lady Hester Stanhope, a British adventurer and traveller, at her residence in Joun in the Lebanon in June or July of 1834 and produced this watercolour during his visit.

b5237ac5-6bde-593f-8bf3-56257cd8a060.author: Marina Minozzi

b5237ac5-6bde-593f-8bf3-56257cd8a060.description2: A half circular hall arranged as an Oriental coffee shop with a Tunisian orchestra of four musicians playing typical instruments. The instruments played are a lute, a type of violin used in the Middle Ages, a little drum decorated like a cymbal and a derbuka, which is a terracotta drum shaped like a particular vase.

b532b295-4380-5ea9-951e-1e3a7150eff2.name: The Central Asian railway. Proposal for a direct line from Europe to India.
b532b295-4380-5ea9-951e-1e3a7150eff2.description2: Charles Cotard was an engineer and graduate of the famous École Polytechnique who dedicated his life to developing new transports. As the engineer-in-chief during the digging of the Suez Canal, he offered Ferdinand de Lesseps a partnership, with the goal of creating a railway line from Europe to India. The biggest obstacle to his plan was the number of hilly or mountainous regions which needed to be crossed. However, Charles Cotard saw many diplomatic and economic opportunities (such as closer relations between England and Russia) in this venture. The map's caption shows the new route's predicted cost and time for passengers compared to the current available routes.

b54a4c02-3027-5de2-965f-2bb5a2395c13.description2: The Albanian community is an important element in the multicultural milieu of ethnicities in the Republic of Macedonia. This outfit preserves some distinctive features of the clothing and adornment worn by Albanian women in Macedonia in the 19th century and early 20th century. The cotton canvas tunic is moderately decorated by embroidery of floral patterns on the sleeves and at the front part of the cleavage. The wool apron is embellished with geometric patterns woven of varied wool threads along the left and right hem, which end with woollen fringes in different colours.

b5762c66-bf5b-5b77-bfe4-6c9e135ce487.name: *Entrance to a Private Mansion, Cairo*
b5762c66-bf5b-5b77-bfe4-6c9e135ce487.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
b5762c66-bf5b-5b77-bfe4-6c9e135ce487.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
b5762c66-bf5b-5b77-bfe4-6c9e135ce487.description2: The Scottish artist David Roberts spent six weeks in Cairo. In his times, Arab architecture was much less known in Europe than that of ancient pharaonic temples, and Roberts' images of ancient and modern Islamic architecture in Cairo were the first window into this ‘exotic’ world for many Europeans. This image shows the monumental, two tiered, marble entrance portal to a Cairo mansio.Although the entire building is not shown, the composition evokes some of its most characteristic aspects: the walls are high and windowless, protecting the inhabitants' privacy. At the same time, a delicately carved, openwork alcove or mashrabiya projects above the entrance portal to allow air and light into the room behind and to provide those within the chance to observe life outside without being seen themselves. With the arrival of major urban development in Cairo from the mid 13th/ 19th century onwards, many traditional buildings were either erased or modified to reflect the new European-style tastes of the urban elite. In the process, the traditional courtyard-style layout of Cairene houses was was often replaced by European-style designs, and traditional architectural elements like mashrabiyas made way for the latest in European technology, including glass pane windows.

b588456d-6066-57a5-856e-b4b1770386d5.name: Plaster cast panel for microbiological education
b588456d-6066-57a5-856e-b4b1770386d5.description2: Maquettes were used in medical education in the Ottoman Empire before a western education system was adopted. The maquettes were commissioned abroad and before working on cadavers, models and moulages were used in classes. Maquettes prepared by Dr. Auzoux in Paris were first taken to Marseilles in boxes, then shipped to İstanbul from there. This example was made of plaster and contains examples of amoeba. There are Roman numerals under each example. On the lower left of the panel one can read "Établissements Auzoux, Rue de Vaugirard, Paris”.

b5c0d18b-e693-55ac-b0f0-5d2195dc1c3e.name: Kaftan
b5c0d18b-e693-55ac-b0f0-5d2195dc1c3e.description: Child's kaftan with *agremán* (tape of braids used as adornment), done in fabric brocade of mauve colour. The brocade is decorated with flower medallions with centres of golden thread. The sleeves are short and straight. The edge of the sleeves and of the whole jacket is edged with dark blue silk tape. The front, sides and shoulders are edged in a golden *agremán*, which ends in a circle. The jacket is lined with white cotton fabric and edged by a red tape. This garment was probably worn by children in the circumcision ceremony ritual. The practice of circumcision in the Islamic world involved a ritual in which the children involved in the ceremony were richly dressed.

b5c715a1-ea35-53d0-8de0-8e0d78cbb7d3.name: *Kurds charging, with Kettle-drummers leading*, from the book *Glimpses of Life and Manners in Persia*
b5c715a1-ea35-53d0-8de0-8e0d78cbb7d3.description:
Mary Leonor Woulfe Sheil, wife of Sir Justin Sheil, a British diplomat at the Qajar court in Persia (Iran), recorded in this book events from her journey to and life in Persia, from 7 August 1849 until June 1853. Persia was a strategic territory. Two years before Lady Shail's journey, a treaty redefined the frontiers between the Ottoman empire and the Qajar territories.  
  
The book describes people seen during the journey, court life, fashion, society, geography and the ancient irrigation system of the *qanat*s. Some of the events described reveal a hidden side of Persia – social unrest, in the shape of ideas considered by the author as a mixture of religious creed, socialism and communism: Lady Sheil witnessed the execution of the religious leader of the “Baabi” group, Sayyid Ali Mohammed, in Tabriz (1850).
b5c715a1-ea35-53d0-8de0-8e0d78cbb7d3.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
b5c715a1-ea35-53d0-8de0-8e0d78cbb7d3.artist: Author of the book: Lady Mary Leonora Woulfe Sheil

b5eeac6a-d016-5d9a-8a53-0fd0bd897372.name: Excavation of l'Avenue de l'Opéra and Boulevard Henri IV
b5eeac6a-d016-5d9a-8a53-0fd0bd897372.description2: When Napoléon III wanted a new opera house to be built (l’Opéra Garnier), he asked Haussmann to excavate the road beneath it, allowing him to go to the opera safely and without risk of being attacked from his residence at the Château des Tuileries. Haussman was forced to dig through an old neighbourhood, built on a hill. This photograph indicates the vastness of the works. The architect Garnier ordered Haussman to ensure no trees blocked the view of the opera house.

b5f42e1e-ecb3-55b6-8189-981be88d8626.name: National loan 1920. *Banque National d'Escompte de Paris… National loan, 1920, 6%... Sign up for a loan and save in the future…*
b5f42e1e-ecb3-55b6-8189-981be88d8626.description2: As the First World War was proving longer and more costly than predicted, the French government took out two loans in 1915 and in 1918 to fund weaponry and other wartime expenses. After the war, more loans were taken out to rebuild the country. Posters with simple messages were used to persuade the population that these loans were beneficial to the country, and would have huge returns. We can see on this poster, for example, a French cockerel standing on a horn, a symbol of abundance, from which money is overflowing.

b6227f02-1142-5b04-b3af-734ad8573ce6.name: Drums
b6227f02-1142-5b04-b3af-734ad8573ce6.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
b6227f02-1142-5b04-b3af-734ad8573ce6.dimensions: Upper diameter 12 cm; lower diameter 10 cm; height 28 cm
b6227f02-1142-5b04-b3af-734ad8573ce6.author: Vito Lattanzi, Marina Minozzi
b6227f02-1142-5b04-b3af-734ad8573ce6.keywords: Darbuka; ceramic; enamelling; cobalt-blue; bleau de Fez; Morocco; museums; collection; collector; anthropology; ethnology; travel; exploration; scientific expedition; geography; representation of the other; material culture; music; musical instrument
b6227f02-1142-5b04-b3af-734ad8573ce6.description2: The two drums are part of the flourishing tradition of enamelled ceramic in Fez, in production since the Middle Ages. Cobalt blue and white decorations identify Fez products dating to the second half of the 19th century. The drums belong to the ethnographic collections of the Pigorini Museum founded between the 19th and the 20th century. The origins of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome, can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

b623eb8c-a4d4-585a-b9d5-23a452054f55.name: *Egypt, San. View of the excavations.*
b623eb8c-a4d4-585a-b9d5-23a452054f55.second_name: Taken from the photo album of Emmanuel de Rougé's mission to Egypt, where he was accompanied by Viscount Aymard de Banville and Jacques de Rougé
b623eb8c-a4d4-585a-b9d5-23a452054f55.description2: Emmanuel de Rougé was a French egyptologist who continued the work of Champollion. He was a member of l'Academie des Sciences, the curator of the "Musée Égyptien" of the Musée du Louvre (1849), professor of Egyptian archaeology at the Collège de France (1864), and authored many works on the history of Egypt. In 1862, he was sent on a mission to Egypt where he travelled along the Nile from the Delta to the cataracts, on a boat which had been loaned to the mission by Isma'il Pasha. This mission was the subject of a report and an illustrated publication with photographs by the Viscount Aymard de Banville. This photograph was taken at San, also known as the ancient site of Tanis, where the archaeologist Mariette was directing an excavation.

b632cf54-9527-5f85-9a5a-5d9445c932a8.description2: This silver coin represents one Indian rupee, minted in 1877. Regal issues of the Indian rupee had begun in 1862, bearing the portrait of Queen Victoria, but Indian Rupees had already been used in the Gulf during the mid 19th century, issued by the British East India Company. The currency began circulating in the region as a result of the pearl trade and the gold exchange between local and Indian merchants. Indian rupees were the main currency used in the Trucial States up until 1966.

b65922f4-01d3-5457-a9bc-98f6df701f87.name: Gospel cover of Dorotheos Proios from Edirne
b65922f4-01d3-5457-a9bc-98f6df701f87.author: Ballian 1992, 86-7, no.46
b65922f4-01d3-5457-a9bc-98f6df701f87.description2: The gospel comes from Adrianople, but a handwritten note on the second page notes that: "…it was crafted and decorated here in Smyrna". From around the mid-eighteenth century Smyrna was the second most important port of the Ottoman Empire, and an important part of its economic life was in the hands of Greeks. The “Frankish quarter” and the preponderance of large-scale, foreign trade gave o cosmopolitan air to Smyrniot society. There is strong western European influence on this impressive silver cover made for Dorotheos Proios. Scrolled cartouches, thronging garlands of roses and conch shells in high relief make it a triumph of Rococo art, at least after the fashion in which it was understood in the Ottoman Empire. Smyrna was an important centre of silver production, but the designs were in general circulation and compositions were put together to fit the circumstances.

en: Ballian, Anna, *Treasures from the Greek Communities of Asia Minor and Eastern Thrace. Collections from the Benaki Museum*, Athens: Benaki Museum, 1992.

b660b1ab-20b9-54c4-8225-fc35360b345d.description2:
5 pounds from the days of Khedive \`Abbas Hilmi II. During this time, a collection of Ottoman coins made of silver and copper circulated, valued at one, five and ten piasters. They were minted in AH 1327 / AD 1909 and bore the name of the Ottoman Sultan Muhammad V.  
However, the most important monetary event took place in 1898, when Khedive \`Abbas Hilmi II granted a franchise to Raphael Suares to establish the National Bank of Egypt. This franchise gave him the right to produce securities that were accepted to pay domanial money, and the right to cash this money as gold upon demand.

b705e8a3-17fc-5217-8640-d86017b77c66.name: Zamzam Water Bottle
b705e8a3-17fc-5217-8640-d86017b77c66.holder: Sharjah Heritage Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
b705e8a3-17fc-5217-8640-d86017b77c66.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
b705e8a3-17fc-5217-8640-d86017b77c66.dimensions: Ca 100 mm diameter; ca 130 mm overall height
b705e8a3-17fc-5217-8640-d86017b77c66.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
b705e8a3-17fc-5217-8640-d86017b77c66.description2: This simple, circular Zamzam bottle has been constructed from copper-alloy sheet and decorated with hammered and incised decoration. A very narrow cylindrical neck gives access to the body of the vessel, and a chain secured to its shoulder allows it to be carried. Every pilgrim to the Holy City of Makkah will make a point of drinking and collecting water from the sacred well of Zamzam, located near the Ka’bah within the precinct of the Holy Mosque at Makkah al Mukarramah. Its never ceasing flow is considered a miracle, and its properties are believed to aid good health and wellbeing. To this day, pilgrims to Makkah make a point of taking as much Zamzam water as they can back with them, not least to distribute it to loved ones and treasured friends in order to allow them to partake in the water's beneficial properties.

b7084bd4-c4a5-5fd8-b3d4-f24093a3a2c3.name: Fiat garage and showroom
b7084bd4-c4a5-5fd8-b3d4-f24093a3a2c3.history: Constructed in 1919, according to a design by Italian architect Aldo Manassi in the Mers Sultan district, the building represents one of the world’s most prolific automotive companies, which began trading in Morocco in 1919.
b7084bd4-c4a5-5fd8-b3d4-f24093a3a2c3.keywords: Art deco; applied arts; classicism; pilaster; floral motifs; decoration; applied arts; geometrical motifs; zellij; ceramic; European influence; Italians in Morocco; Italians in North Africa; Italian architects in Morocco; migration; work; technical innovation; transportation; car; industry; Italian industries; Italian industrialists; FIAT; trade; commerce; city; European architecture; plan; Moroccan city; Casablanca; urban planning; colonial city; urban space; changes in urban spaces
b7084bd4-c4a5-5fd8-b3d4-f24093a3a2c3.description2: The building consists of two floors, the ground-floor designed to accommodate a garage and exhibition hall. Art Deco in style, classical-style pilasters reach up to the first floor and terminate in decorative floral mouldings. The inner detailing surrounds windows that are topped with decorated mouldings with a similar floral theme. Two arched windows, with small balconies, are topped by shallow porches. Two medallions, which bear the name “Fiat” in deep blue, highlight the protruding facade.

b7735908-2a85-5159-97b8-d8499ee4ac07.name: *A Scene from the Turkish Harem*
b7735908-2a85-5159-97b8-d8499ee4ac07.archival: Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection (Orientalist Paintings Collection)
b7735908-2a85-5159-97b8-d8499ee4ac07.description2: Austrian artists, which were part of the retinue of the Embassy delegation led by Hans Ludwig von Kuefstein that Holy Roman Emperor Ferdinand II sent to Murad IV in 1628, depicted audiences of the delegation, the sultan and his family, various Ottoman garments and intriguing facets of daily life. This painting is possibly a part of such a series. The 1654 inscription over the painting reads, “As it is not customary for distinguished Turkish ladies to leave the house or meet strangers, they invite each other to their homes and amuse themselves with dance, comedy and similar forms of entertainment”. In the lower section of the painting, guests are greeted while women dance to the rhythm of the tambourine. In the upper section, two women are seen dancing with scarves on their heads and embroidered kerchiefs in their hands, accompanied by musicians playing traditional instruments, such as rebab, santur, and tambourine. The carpets, garments and instruments are depicted in elaborate detail.

b776a817-c7d7-51b1-8767-4441833fd7a5.name: *The Progress of Steam: A View in White Chapel Road, 1830*
b776a817-c7d7-51b1-8767-4441833fd7a5.second_name: Taken from Salomon's collection, *Transport, Cycles, Automobiles*
b776a817-c7d7-51b1-8767-4441833fd7a5.description2: Steam engines carried a great variety of goods in the 1830s. This English cartoon imagines the chaos the widespread use of collective and individual carbon-fuelled transport systems would bring (pollution, noise, cumbersome, etc.) to one of London's great arteries, Whitechapel Road. These vehicles provided fashionable services such as on-board coffee.

b7ce4f8c-eeaa-5739-a40e-36309170d6fc.keywords: Ceramic; Africa; exhibition; blue-and-white; decorative arts
b7ce4f8c-eeaa-5739-a40e-36309170d6fc.materials: Tin-glazed earthenware, painted in blue and turquoise
b7ce4f8c-eeaa-5739-a40e-36309170d6fc.description2: Fez is an important centre for Moroccan pottery and is particularly associated with a distinctive form of blue and white ceramic ware which became popular in the late 19th century. This bottle was donated to the V&A by George Maw, founder of Maw & Co., a British manufacturer of ceramic tiles. The company won many medals and awards at the international exhibitions which were a feature of the late 19th century. This bottle was displayed at the 1871 Annual International Exhibition held in London.

b7d0545b-be32-5c47-ab91-272824042882.name: Headdress
b7d0545b-be32-5c47-ab91-272824042882.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
b7d0545b-be32-5c47-ab91-272824042882.author: Huda Kilani
b7d0545b-be32-5c47-ab91-272824042882.description2: Line of silver Ottoman coins sewn together on a piece of fabric, part of a headdress. This kind of jewellery was part of the dowry the groom gave to the bride. Dowries consisted mostly of silver jewellery because only the rich could afford gold jewellery. The use of coins as pieces of jewellery in particular was an indirect statement of the financial status of the groom, as brides wore those pieces of jewellery in front of relatives and friends.

b7e5dd09-cf9b-5310-9343-8db43d0c9114.name: *The Emperor of Austria ascending the Great Pyramid*
b7e5dd09-cf9b-5310-9343-8db43d0c9114.description2: William Simpson wrote in his autobiography: "I went out one day and saw the Emperor of Austria lugged to the top of the Great Pyramid by two Arabs as if he had been only an overland passenger". Many visitors were unceremoniously hauled to the top of the monument by local inhabitants, helping unfit and often overweight tourists to clamber up the huge blocks. Emperor Franz Joseph was one of many European dignitaries in Egypt in November 1869 for the opening of the Suez Canal. Simpson was employed by the Illustrated London News as their "Special Artist". Photography would soon replace such drawings.

b814bde1-48f9-5356-8789-4fecae32bde0.keywords: bridal tunic; embroidery; costume; silver; wedding; marriage
b814bde1-48f9-5356-8789-4fecae32bde0.materials: White canvas, embroidery with variegate threads
b814bde1-48f9-5356-8789-4fecae32bde0.description2: This bridal tunic is abundantly decorated with relief embroidery above the lower hem. The embroidery is very impressive owing to the varied relief techniques applied. It has been created by application of black woollen thread with slight borders in other colours, flat silver string and silver-thread braid. The sleeves are also richly adorned with embroidery in predominantly red nuances. The symbolism of embroidered patterns endow this tunic with universal values distinctive to Macedonian home-made women's attire.

b8a6b459-47fa-5a6f-a12b-76e7e938843b.name: *Parmak cura* (little *cura*)
b8a6b459-47fa-5a6f-a12b-76e7e938843b.description2: The *Cura* is an instrument used by Yörüks (nomads). It is the smallest type of *bağlama* and is usually 55-60cm in length. It generally has three, four, five or six strings and is played either with a quill or the fingers. It is suitable for dynamic dance performances.

b8bb387e-75d0-55d8-89ae-9322c204928c.name: Simplon-Orient Express Poster
b8bb387e-75d0-55d8-89ae-9322c204928c.description2: The Orient Express, owned by the Wagon-Lits Company, connected Paris and Istanbul between 1883 and 1977. French, German, Austrian and Ottoman diplomats and civil servants were on board for its first journey. In the early years, the travellers stayed in different hotels in Istanbul but starting from 1895, passengers stayed exclusively in Pera Palace, which was bought by the Wagon-Lits Company. The Orient Express did not run during World War I, from 1914 to 1918.

b8eb5a77-e816-5c46-818d-96a032573547.name: *Landscape from Gebze*
b8eb5a77-e816-5c46-818d-96a032573547.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
b8eb5a77-e816-5c46-818d-96a032573547.keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters
b8eb5a77-e816-5c46-818d-96a032573547.description2: Osman Hamdi focused on dilemmas such as East and West, love and hate, life and death. While stylistically reminiscent of western Orientalist painters, his works reflect a more nuanced appreciation of Ottoman society and culture. In the art of his paintings, he depicted unique details so diligently that he made us recognize our environment and Turkish culture. He illustrated carpets, tile panels, calligraphies, decorative arts, shrines, mosques and human figures in his paintings. He also gave importance to details while reflecting the colourful scenes of Turkish culture, traditional architecture, Ottoman fashion and domestic and social life of the women in the Ottoman Empire. And it’s obvious that he is the first painter who used human figures in the western style.

b8f1e03b-6dae-584b-990b-f69d7ae90efe.description2: Flinders Petrie purchased this figurine in Giza. He was informed by the seller that it had been unearthed at a site in the western Nile Delta. Petrie recognised the Cypriot and Egyptian influences and headed to the region where the figurine was said to have been found. It is here that he found Naukratis.

b8fd5a61-6e87-5479-8b87-53c6a66033f2.name: A drawing showing wooden gratings from various mosques
b8fd5a61-6e87-5479-8b87-53c6a66033f2.author: Marina Minozzi
b8fd5a61-6e87-5479-8b87-53c6a66033f2.archival: A. Melani, *L'ornamento policromo nelle arti e nelle industrie artistiche, medievale e moderne per uso delle scuole e degli artisti…*, Milano 1886, tav. 25
b8fd5a61-6e87-5479-8b87-53c6a66033f2.keywords: Applied arts; museums of applied arts; Islamic art; Islamic influence; book; model; crafstmanship; sketch; drawing; Grammar of ornament; Alfredo Melani; Owen Jones; Prisse d'Avennes; Islamic architecture; schools of applied arts
b8fd5a61-6e87-5479-8b87-53c6a66033f2.copyright: Copyright image: Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale, Roma.
b8fd5a61-6e87-5479-8b87-53c6a66033f2.description2: Alfredo Melani, teacher and then director at the school of applied arts in Milan, was one of the main exponents of oriental decorative motifs in Italy. During the 1880s he published a series of works and texts discussing eastern art, often in the form of handbooks and essays. Subsequently, toward the end of the century Camillo Boito pioneered courses in the history of styles at the Accademia of Brera. Dell’ornamento nell’architettura written by Melani, includes a whole chapter about Muslim decorations, from which the drawing showing wooden grills from mosques is taken.

en: Barucci, C., “L'orientalismo nelle fonti bibliografiche e nella manualistica italiana dell'Ottocento”, in Giusti, M.A. and Godoli, E. (eds), *L’ orientalismo nell’architettura italiana tra Ottocento e Novecento*, atti del convegno internazionale di studi (1997), Siena, 1999, pp. 23–30.

b902f002-452f-5bec-8587-b983db9d1182.name: *Schoolboy*

b9037025-526c-5ec9-ad5b-a435eec55808.name: Travel notebook for meteorological observations
b9037025-526c-5ec9-ad5b-a435eec55808.author: Bruno Gonçalves Neves
b9037025-526c-5ec9-ad5b-a435eec55808.artist: Hermenegildo Carlos de Brito Capelo (4 February 1841, Palmela –  4 May 1917, Lisbon); photo by Rui Salta

b9037025-526c-5ec9-ad5b-a435eec55808.description2: Travel notebook which belonged to Portuguese Navy’s Commander Hermenegildo Capelo, used during the expedition to the interior of the African continent in 1884/1885, from Angola’s coast to the Mozambique’s shore, along with the Portuguese Navy’s Commander Roberto Ivens. The main objective for the Portuguese expeditionary voyages in Africa was to gather all sorts of information: meteorological data, course of rivers, local inhabitants and populations, among others.

b92b2e17-256a-5653-8c8d-8f4555614e91.name: Letter of Sultan Mehmet V to Emperor Karl I
b92b2e17-256a-5653-8c8d-8f4555614e91.keywords: Sultan Mehmet V; Karl I; Emperor Franz Joseph
b92b2e17-256a-5653-8c8d-8f4555614e91.description2: In this letter, Sultan Mehmet V thanks Austrian Emperor Karl I for the conferment of the "Austrian Military Cross" and congratulates him for his succession to the throne. In the same writing, he expresses his condolences for the death of Emperor Franz Joseph.

b94c1c17-a6e6-5cac-b93a-a36603dd4d29.name: *Marseille, unloading the oranges*
b94c1c17-a6e6-5cac-b93a-a36603dd4d29.description2: In the beginning of the 20th century, traditional commerce activities still coexisted alongside newer, modern commercial transport. Pictured in this photograph is an unloading of oranges arriving from Algeria or Spain, France's two main orange suppliers at this time. The oranges are unloaded into two baskets, carried by young girls.

b966135b-aa13-5813-b98e-6dab1d391e68.name: Shelf
b966135b-aa13-5813-b98e-6dab1d391e68.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
b966135b-aa13-5813-b98e-6dab1d391e68.description2: The back on this shelf is decorated with a perforated pattern, whereas the rack is decorated with a floral pattern (daisies) and small hooks. The section directly beneath the shelf is also decorated with a floral motif.

b97bcb71-a957-5608-9199-9926745d01bd.name: Egyptian Pavilion of Chocolate and Cocoa Factories – Michele Talmone – Turin (interior)
b97bcb71-a957-5608-9199-9926745d01bd.holder: The House of Antique Tin Boxes
b97bcb71-a957-5608-9199-9926745d01bd.author: Marina Minozzi
b97bcb71-a957-5608-9199-9926745d01bd.keywords: Esposizione Internazionale di Torino; trade; trademark; commerce; Italian firms; nationalism; raw material; finished product; exoticism; popular culture; imaginary architecture; Italians in Egypt; exhibition building; exhibitions and urban spaces
b97bcb71-a957-5608-9199-9926745d01bd.third_name: Padiglione Egiziano delle Fabbriche di Cioccolato e Cacao – Michele Talmone – Torino (interno)
b97bcb71-a957-5608-9199-9926745d01bd.description2: On the occasion of the International Exhibition in Turin in 1911 the Talmone Company built an Egyptian Pavilion resembling an Egyptian temple. The inside of the Pavilion shows details inspired by Egyptian motifs and related to the company’s name. Items highlight the taste of the age for Egyptian and oriental objects. The stained glass design in the Pavilion was taken from a postcard design. This picture, showing a stunning view of a caravan travelling across the desert and already used for the Exhibition in Turin in 1898, is now employed to promote the logo "Chocolate of the Pyramids".
b97bcb71-a957-5608-9199-9926745d01bd.holding_institution_org: La Casa delle Antiche Scatole di Latta

b98b5c58-b52f-54a7-85fa-fdea8460caf3.name: *Adornment Of The Bride*
b98b5c58-b52f-54a7-85fa-fdea8460caf3.author: Petar Petrovic
b98b5c58-b52f-54a7-85fa-fdea8460caf3.description2: Bright, folkloristically vivid, technically impeccable and with an abundance of ethnographic detail, this is one of Jovanović’s best paintings, both in this period and as a whole. In a broader sense, this work by Paja Jovanović contains all the relevant characteristics of the poetics of academicism and thus – together with Jovanović’s other works from this period – had a crucial impact on the development of realism in Serbian painting in the late 19th century.

b9afa85f-9c6f-5c35-ad19-8ad72d2903a7.name: Moorish City at the Trocadéro, View from the Pavilion of the Insects [Paris Exhibition, 1878]

b9afa85f-9c6f-5c35-ad19-8ad72d2903a7.archival: *L'Esposizione di Parigi del 1878 illustrata*, Sonzogno Editore, 1878, p. 269
b9afa85f-9c6f-5c35-ad19-8ad72d2903a7.keywords: International exhibition; Exposition universelle de Paris; industrialisation; exhibition building; architecture; exhibitions and urban spaces; Moorish style; Islamic architecture; reinterpretation; house; interior design; exoticism; reproduction; model
b9afa85f-9c6f-5c35-ad19-8ad72d2903a7.copyright: Copyright image: Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale, Roma.
b9afa85f-9c6f-5c35-ad19-8ad72d2903a7.third_name: La città moresca al Trocadero, veduta presa dal padiglione degli insetti
b9afa85f-9c6f-5c35-ad19-8ad72d2903a7.description2: Singular mix of "Moorish" Pavilion and "Occidental" architecture from the Universal Exhibition in Paris, 1878. The publication offers images providing a rich documentation about the exhibition and includes frivolous and caustic comments. The magazine presents sharp and close observations about habits and trends common in Paris and in the western world at the time of the International Exhibitions.

b9ec5638-cdfd-59b1-9665-cf8e39b21d9b.name: *A landscape from Eyüp, Istanbul*
b9ec5638-cdfd-59b1-9665-cf8e39b21d9b.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
b9ec5638-cdfd-59b1-9665-cf8e39b21d9b.description2: At the beginning of the 19th century, romantic painters who appreciated eastern mysticism brought newly discovered eastern landscapes with their paintings which contained fiery colours and interesting landscapes. One of those painters coming to Istanbul from Malta and affected by eastern mysticism was Amadeo Preziosi. He usually painted scenes from daily life, such as shops between streets, coffeehouses, baths, peddlers passing the street, a woman filling water from a fountain and figures from different ethnic groups. Like many of his contemporaries, Preziosi had been lured to the exotic city of Istanbul. He also tried to reflect the cultural diversity of the city in his paintings. Especially in his watercolour paintings he loved expressing the blue water of the Bosporus with its caïques, pavilions, palaces, boats, mansions, residences, bazaars and cemeteries.

b9ee7653-5f89-5cc9-b8cc-d6b70b1e48ce.name: Izmir Clock Tower
b9ee7653-5f89-5cc9-b8cc-d6b70b1e48ce.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
b9ee7653-5f89-5cc9-b8cc-d6b70b1e48ce.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ancient İzmir; Tower
b9ee7653-5f89-5cc9-b8cc-d6b70b1e48ce.description2: The clock tower was designed by the Levantine French architect Raymond Charles Père and built in 1901 to commemorate the 25th anniversary of Abdülhamid II's accession to the throne (reigned 1876-1909). The clock itself was a gift from German Emperor Wilhelm II (reigned 1888-1918). It is decorated in an elaborate Ottoman architecture style.

ba1c6502-ece8-50c7-a051-8ccb55d13f84.name: Letter from the Tunisian merchants of Egypt to the Bey of Tunis
ba1c6502-ece8-50c7-a051-8ccb55d13f84.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
ba1c6502-ece8-50c7-a051-8ccb55d13f84.description2: This letter from the Tunisian merchants of Egypt to the Bey of Tunis thanks him for nominating a new representative in Alexandria. The letter is signed by over one hundred merchants in both Cairo and Alexandria

ba3b8c6f-86e6-5a4a-9b9a-6d600f5e1009.name: Archaeological excavations
ba3b8c6f-86e6-5a4a-9b9a-6d600f5e1009.description2: Portrait of three scholars in front of the tent camp during the excavations in the archaeological area of Saqqara, Giza in 1912. The paper photograph was printed from a gelatine print negative.

ba422441-e1c1-5256-9187-632e779470fd.holder: Palais de la Rose – Musée de l’Armée

ba422441-e1c1-5256-9187-632e779470fd.description2: This firearm is a French model from 1822. Its total length measures 353 mm, with the barrel measuring 200 mm and the calibre 17.7 mm. All the embellishments, except the ring, are made of brass. It has a hollow-headed ramrod, and an elongated breech which extends to the pommel.

ba42b954-f590-57ca-907e-01a3ca4dde77.name: *Servant*
ba42b954-f590-57ca-907e-01a3ca4dde77.archival: Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection (Orientalist Paintings Collection)
ba42b954-f590-57ca-907e-01a3ca4dde77.description2: The painting depicts a young girl in front of a wall, the lower part of which has been decorated with ceramic tiles with a floral design. The girl is wearing a white dress with embroidery down its front and a long embroidered belt, while her hair is partially covered with a light veil. On the young girl’s chestnut hair there is a gold crown, with gems at its centre. Around her neck she wears a necklace with large gems, a thin bracelet on her left wrist and an armlet on her right arm. The girl is holding a tray on which there is a decanter and cup of blue-and-white porcelain and fruits.

ba4a9d77-759d-50a9-9165-61cb49c132a4.name: *Caravan in a covered street in Algiers*
ba4a9d77-759d-50a9-9165-61cb49c132a4.archival: Théodore Frère (artist), Courtin (lithography), V. Adam (drawing), A. Godard (printing), in Berbrugger, *Algérie historique, Pittoresque et Monumentale*, Paris: J. Delahaye, 1843.
ba4a9d77-759d-50a9-9165-61cb49c132a4.description2: This lithograph by Théodore Frère shows the "Jennée" alley, beneath the Dey of Algiers' former residence, the "Janina". Both the palace and the alley were destroyed in 1853.

ba590c72-051f-5d9a-898f-073b4347852b.name: *Port, Beirut*
ba590c72-051f-5d9a-898f-073b4347852b.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
ba590c72-051f-5d9a-898f-073b4347852b.author: Stefan Weber
ba590c72-051f-5d9a-898f-073b4347852b.second_name: During the opening of the railway station at the harbour
ba590c72-051f-5d9a-898f-073b4347852b.description2: On 19/6/1887, the Ottoman authority gave the concession of the Port to an Ottoman company under the name of "Compagnie du Port, des Quais et des Entrepôts de Beyrouth". The concession was later fortified when the company gained from the Customs the sole rights to store and carry all the transit goods passing through the Customs. Constructions works namely a maritime dam to expand and develop the Port were accomplished and the opening on the occasion of the accomplishment of these works was celebrated by the end of 1894, basins were developed and spread between Ras Al Shamiah and Ras Al Mudawar. It forms the midpoint of three continents: Europe, Asia and Africa, which makes the Port a passage for ship fleets between East and West. During the mid 70's, the Port of Beirut was an important international trading station with the surrounding Arab countries and up until today it has preserved its commercial nature.

baa9427d-f633-556e-9aa9-f175636f895f.name: Bracelet
baa9427d-f633-556e-9aa9-f175636f895f.holder: Musée des Arts et Traditions Populaires

baa9427d-f633-556e-9aa9-f175636f895f.description2: This silver bracelet, which is lined with gold and encrusted with roses, is made of a longer chain of openwork rosettes and framed by geometric motifs. A jagged gold leaf lines the inside of the bracelet. All the silver motifs are encrusted with roses. The two identical halves of the bracelet are joined by hinge and pin fastening topped by a large pearl.

baa960da-cbd1-54e0-9d5e-f5269a2ff7f6.name: *Al-Maktab al-I‘dadiyya al-‘Askariyya, Damascus*
baa960da-cbd1-54e0-9d5e-f5269a2ff7f6.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
baa960da-cbd1-54e0-9d5e-f5269a2ff7f6.author: Stefan Weber
baa960da-cbd1-54e0-9d5e-f5269a2ff7f6.second_name: Military college founded first in 1830 in the Mamluk mosque of Tankiz
baa960da-cbd1-54e0-9d5e-f5269a2ff7f6.description2: Attempts were first made by the Ottoman state to reform schools in 1869 with the passing of an edict on school reform for the whole Ottoman Empire, officially recognizing private and foreign schools while setting out the basic principles of state education. The law now made a distinction between schools preparing children for a civil service or administrative career on the one hand, and military schools on the other hand. Military primary and secondary schools were established, an example for the latter is the significant Military College al-Maktab al-I‘dadiyya al-`Askariyya.

bab7404e-f6da-51e5-bfe3-7f236f4ef2b2.name: *Wadi el-Tuffah*
bab7404e-f6da-51e5-bfe3-7f236f4ef2b2.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
bab7404e-f6da-51e5-bfe3-7f236f4ef2b2.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
bab7404e-f6da-51e5-bfe3-7f236f4ef2b2.artist: J. Harley (after a drawing by Harry Fenn 1838–1911)
bab7404e-f6da-51e5-bfe3-7f236f4ef2b2.keywords: Mosque of Sheikh Ali Bakka; Hebron
bab7404e-f6da-51e5-bfe3-7f236f4ef2b2.description2: In this image, a Palestinian lady uses a traditional spinning wheel for cotton. 19th-century Palestine became an increasingly viable, agricultural producer of cotton, whose importance on the world market was steadily increasing. Mainly supplying European countries  Palestine's cotton became a key commodity. 6% of its cultivated land was given up for its production. Throughout the 1860s, concerted efforts were made to meet the ever growing demand, but as early as the 1870s, the industry, which was merely based on expanded cultivation rather than industrialisation, declined again.This print originally appeared on page 192 in Charles William Wilson's  'Pituresque Palestine, Sinai and Egypt, published between 1881 and 1884. The caption reads: ''Wady et Tuffah, commonly called the vale of Eshcol. The peasants grouped in the foreground are under the southern branches of Abraham's oak. In the distance the minaret of the great mosque of Sheikh Ali Bakka, Hebron, may be distinguished'.

baca824e-062d-5426-b385-13a5074e8755.name: View of Livorno from the Lighthouse. On the right, one can see the so-called 'Turkish graveyard' highlighted in green
baca824e-062d-5426-b385-13a5074e8755.author: Daniela Tazzi
baca824e-062d-5426-b385-13a5074e8755.third_name: *Panorama della città e contorni di Livorno disegnata dal Fanale*
baca824e-062d-5426-b385-13a5074e8755.description2: In 1762, Muslims living in Livorno were granted a plot of land outside the city walls, near the beach, to build a graveyard (highlighted in green in the lithography). The graveyard remained in use until the second half of the 19th century. A Muslim graveyard existed in Livorno even before the 18th century. A significant Muslim community lived in town. Its first members were captives taken to Italy as slaves. Muslim traders settled in town as well. In 1856, the graveyard was enlarged and surrounded by walls. In 1872 it was demolished to build a road and some of the graves were moved to the city graveyard.
baca824e-062d-5426-b385-13a5074e8755.holding_institution_org: Biblioteca Labronica F. D. Guerrazzi Livorno

bae5f080-ad41-5249-82bc-b0f3de4d1129.name: *Médailles d'honneur d'or et de 1er mérite* \[…\] Biberon-Robert, flexible, patented \[…\] Only the very best doesn't let your child go thirsty
bae5f080-ad41-5249-82bc-b0f3de4d1129.description2: As infant mortality was still commonplace in the 19th century, the need to instil young parents with an understanding of hygiene in order to counter child illness quickly became clear. This poster advertises a new child's feeding bottle, showcasing its high quality and foregrounding an image of a healthy baby.

baf82baf-93a9-5da4-b22c-8e5e634174fe.name: Miniature
baf82baf-93a9-5da4-b22c-8e5e634174fe.description:
This framed octagonal miniature shows a scene in a portico where men and women talk. A large blue curtain, two ribbed columns and a lobulated arch over another hidden column set the composition where a bearded Arab man with a turban, dressed in traditional Turkish costume in blue, red and white, is seated on a carpet, looking at a woman and a man who is introducing her. On the right and left sides, two couples of Circassian odalisques complete the scene and a standing armed man closes it on our right side.  
In the horizon beyond the harem we can see magnificent palaces by the water, probably the sea in Istanbul.
baf82baf-93a9-5da4-b22c-8e5e634174fe.author: Cristina Giménez

baf9e3e8-08a9-59e2-8c21-17ce2e3a24c6.name: *Moorish Parade*
baf9e3e8-08a9-59e2-8c21-17ce2e3a24c6.description:
This painting was made around 1863 when the author travelled to Morocco with Mariano Fortuny. The reason of his travel was to paint the characters and picturesque garments as the way of life of the people from Morocco.  
His experiences can be seen in his paintings and drawings.  
During his travels he bought exotic artworks as Egyptian sarcophagi.  
Harem and markets are considered a genre painting in Orientalism.
baf9e3e8-08a9-59e2-8c21-17ce2e3a24c6.author: Ámparo López

bb542d79-d99d-5291-a57c-0b72137d0e2f.name: Fez of a common soldier of the Austro-Hungarian infantry from Bosnia-Herzegovina
bb542d79-d99d-5291-a57c-0b72137d0e2f.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
bb542d79-d99d-5291-a57c-0b72137d0e2f.keywords: Fez; Morocco; Tunisia; hat gear; Bosnia; Austrian army; war; warfare; military wear; Ottoman army
bb542d79-d99d-5291-a57c-0b72137d0e2f.description2: The fez was more or less the most significant element of the uniform worn by soldiers of Bosnian-Herzegovinian regiments of the Austro-Hungarian Army, who earned a reputation for bravery and loyalty during World War I. While the fez was in use for all common soldiers, only Muslim officers were allowed to wear the fez instead of the normal black officer's cap. The colour of the fez was changed during the war from red to pike grey.

bb75e12c-a4e6-5ac9-952c-ce0d0a5fbea2.name: *Constantinople et le Bosphore de Thrace*
bb75e12c-a4e6-5ac9-952c-ce0d0a5fbea2.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. Travelling in the 19th century became easier and more reliable due to the advent of steamships and trains. Westerners travelled to the East not only for touristic purposes, but also for scientific research, history, archaeology or for religious reasons. Western travellers told of their experiences and what they saw in eastern countries in their travel books and they even offer advice about the journey. Istanbul, where East and West meet, has been the subject of many a traveller's book.

bb7e5c73-80d2-53d1-8bb0-be2895feb51b.author: Patrizia Pampana
bb7e5c73-80d2-53d1-8bb0-be2895feb51b.third_name: *Quartiere europeo e sobborgo di Sugga, parte settentrionale di Tunisi*
bb7e5c73-80d2-53d1-8bb0-be2895feb51b.description2: An early photograph of a view of Tunis, the picture shows in the European neighbourbood. It was taken on a trip to Tunisia organised by the Italian Geographical Society (Società geografica italiana) in 1875.

bb8237ee-e92e-5329-9529-6fd346236dd0.name: *Jaffa from the Camp of Ibrahim Pasha*
bb8237ee-e92e-5329-9529-6fd346236dd0.description: This print shows the Ibrahim Pasha camp at Jaffa during the Egyptian – Ottoman War (1830–1833). Muhammad Ali Pasha demanded control of Greater Syria for the Ottoman Empire. Ali sent his army into Syria under the command of his son Ibrahim Pasha. The Egyptian navy landed at Jaffa.
