bb8237ee-e92e-5329-9529-6fd346236dd0.third_name: *Jafa. Vista del Campamento de Ibrahin Baja*

bb9dad9b-d6d3-5823-9949-97ec2cba42f3.name: Centrally planned collective housing
bb9dad9b-d6d3-5823-9949-97ec2cba42f3.description: This centrally planned house is an example of a style of collective housing, dating back to the 1850s. This type of house is built around a central space to be used collectively by all the building's inhabitants. The separate houses, generally inhabited by families, were also built around this open space.
bb9dad9b-d6d3-5823-9949-97ec2cba42f3.author: Jeff El-Msanne, David Andos
bb9dad9b-d6d3-5823-9949-97ec2cba42f3.history: This style of collective housing emerged alongside other styles (such as the monocellular house or the courtyard house) in the 1850s, a period which is generally considered to be the peak of Ottoman rule in the region. The desire for more economically viable and sociable housing were the main reasons behind its success.

bbeb5c8c-87db-5293-acee-f6b517d2244d.name: Box
bbeb5c8c-87db-5293-acee-f6b517d2244d.description: Box made in Paris in Oriental style.
bbeb5c8c-87db-5293-acee-f6b517d2244d.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

bbeb7fe5-88d9-5182-83a9-e637b3a17a0b.name: Tile panel
bbeb7fe5-88d9-5182-83a9-e637b3a17a0b.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
bbeb7fe5-88d9-5182-83a9-e637b3a17a0b.keywords: Ceramic; earthenware; collection; collector; vegetal decoration; ceramic tile; tilework; tile panel; Iznik; Ottoman ceramic; revival
bbeb7fe5-88d9-5182-83a9-e637b3a17a0b.materials: Slip-covered and hand-painted in various colours and glazed, on earthenware blanks
bbeb7fe5-88d9-5182-83a9-e637b3a17a0b.description2:
The architect of Membland Hall in Devon commissioned this sumptuous design for bathroom tiles from William Morris. Morris had the tiles painted in the studios of William de Morgan (1839-1917). They represent a rare collaboration between these two creative geniuses.  
Edward Charles Baring, 1st Baron Revelstoke, was the builder of Membland Hall. He was a merchant banker. The hall was later demolished.

bc05121b-1942-54f8-ba62-84b29282f089.name: Tile Panel
bc05121b-1942-54f8-ba62-84b29282f089.description2: Kütahya was the second most important ceramic production centre after İznik due to the rich clay deposits in the area. Although there was a decline in ceramic production at the beginning of the 19th century, in the last quarter of that same century production was revived and new designs inspired by İznik ceramics were produced.

bc06907f-aa68-5c8f-a06c-e1664310cd2a.name: Newspaper *al-Hawi*
bc06907f-aa68-5c8f-a06c-e1664310cd2a.holder: House of the Maronite Patriarchate of Antioch and all the East
bc06907f-aa68-5c8f-a06c-e1664310cd2a.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
bc06907f-aa68-5c8f-a06c-e1664310cd2a.description2: This issue of *al-Hawi* dates t 13 April 1914. *Al-Hawi* was a weekly literary, political and comic periodical founded in August 1912 by José M. Shaia and written, edited and printed in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

bc4af44a-740c-54ce-806a-021695934601.name: Yıldız Ceramic vase
bc4af44a-740c-54ce-806a-021695934601.description2: Sultan Abdülhamid II founded in 1891 the *Yıldız Çini Fabrika-i Hümâyûnu* (Yıldız Royal Tile Factory) in the garden of Yıldız Palace in order to revive Turkish tile art and give it a new direction and momentum. Vases, hanging wall plates and many sorts of daily-use wares were produced in the factory, including writing and dinner table utensils, card plates, lidded bowls, pans, *aşure* (a kind of dessert) trays, sugar bowls, tea and coffee cups. The vase has yellow covers and two handles. There is a landscape of a tree and a house near the water on the vase.

bc4ebe5a-094c-56c1-b426-f1d720ea5206.name: Abdülaziz (1830–1876)
bc4ebe5a-094c-56c1-b426-f1d720ea5206.description2: Portrait of Abdülaziz (1830–1876). In 1861 he became Sultan. He was very interested in fostering a good relationship with European powers and to this end visited Paris, London and Vienna in 1867. Because of the uprisings in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Bulgaria, he was forced to abdicate on 30 May 1876.

bc605726-30eb-5689-b5fe-e1831e32d41b.name: Central Market
bc605726-30eb-5689-b5fe-e1831e32d41b.history: Built in 1917 according to a design by French architect Pierre Bousquet, the organisation of shops into galleries is in harmony with the Moroccan market or *suq* tradition. Furthermore, it highlights the economic activity of Casablanca at the time of the French Protectorate.
bc605726-30eb-5689-b5fe-e1831e32d41b.keywords: French in Morocco; French in North Africa; French architects in North Africa; Suq; covered market; covered suq; traditional city; city; Islamic city; Islamic urban space; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic architecture in Morocco; Islamic influence; French in Morocco; protectorate; traditional building; plan; Moroccan city; urban planning; colonial architecture; applied arts; vegetal motifs; zellij; ceramic; geometrical motifs; trade; economy; commerce; work; public space
bc605726-30eb-5689-b5fe-e1831e32d41b.description2: This space is in keeping with traditional Moroccan market structures, wherein different types of shops are grouped in galleries. The main monumental gate, which provides access to the market on Avenue Mohammad V, is surmounted by a horseshoe arch richly decorated with traditional figurative motifs (vegetal tracery) and predominantly green polychrome *zellige* (mosaic tilework). The corners of the structure are softened by two small arched valances or *lambrequins*. At the top of the gate there is a small canopy furnished with green tiles.

bc65e295-73e5-5ae4-84e4-1777b2658828.name: Bracelet
bc65e295-73e5-5ae4-84e4-1777b2658828.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
bc65e295-73e5-5ae4-84e4-1777b2658828.author: Huda Kilani
bc65e295-73e5-5ae4-84e4-1777b2658828.keywords: Bedouin; settler; village; economy; dowry; tradition; marriage; Ottoman Jordan
bc65e295-73e5-5ae4-84e4-1777b2658828.description2:
Hollow domes and welded reliefs with locking mechanism. Silver jewellery was the most common, because only rich people could afford gold jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom.  
The Jordanian economy relied on trades and crafts and new waves of people started to come to Jordan and began to settle for these purposes. This object is an example of how traditional fashion reflected the variegated population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is also an example of local personal attire, fashion, costumes and rites.

bc71fd0a-a9bf-5d5a-881e-ff89569de8a9.name: Small pot
bc71fd0a-a9bf-5d5a-881e-ff89569de8a9.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
bc71fd0a-a9bf-5d5a-881e-ff89569de8a9.description2: This small pot is decorated on its base and its neck by a braided band with a red copper outline. Rectangular cartouches on the body, also outlined in red copper, contain silver Arabic inscriptions reading "hard work brings rewards" and "patience wins the race".

bc794754-d095-53e4-90c2-e4f2b5406077.name: Assyrianising pendant
bc794754-d095-53e4-90c2-e4f2b5406077.description2: Gold pendant made in Rome based on an Assyrian winged bull, now famous throughout Europe. Illustrates Assyrian influence on 19th-century jewellery.

bc8e9132-343b-5b7f-a75d-aa8304520a26.name: Tughra of Sultan Osman III
bc8e9132-343b-5b7f-a75d-aa8304520a26.holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts
bc8e9132-343b-5b7f-a75d-aa8304520a26.keywords: Wood; gilding; watercolour; painting; tuğra; tughra
bc8e9132-343b-5b7f-a75d-aa8304520a26.description2: *Tughras*, official monograms of the sultans, are one the first things to come to mind when Ottoman art or history is mentioned. The size of this *tughra* of Sultan Osman III makes it an interesting example and it has features peculiar to the art of the AH 12th / AD 18th century.

bca9a195-0769-5794-865b-e5e0b784277a.name: Italian police record of Romualdo Peppini (b. Turin 1863, d. Casablanca 1912), an Italian anarchist worker who immigrated to Morocco in 1901
bca9a195-0769-5794-865b-e5e0b784277a.author: Giulia Barrera
bca9a195-0769-5794-865b-e5e0b784277a.archival: Ministero dell’interno, Direzione generale di pubblica sicurezza, Divisione affari generali e riservati, Casellario politico centrale, b. 3725, f. “PAPPINI, Romualdo”
bca9a195-0769-5794-865b-e5e0b784277a.description2: In the 19th century and for the first half of the 20th century political migration streamed from Italy to North Africa. Supporters of Italian unification, and especially the supporters of Republican nationalist ideologue Giuseppe Mazzini, were among the first migrants. After the Italian unification, some anarchists migrated, while under Fascism several antifascists took refuge in North Africa.

bcd52ef5-9e05-5700-9c6f-f573e35eebad.name: *The Admiralty*
bcd52ef5-9e05-5700-9c6f-f573e35eebad.author: Dalila Orfali
bcd52ef5-9e05-5700-9c6f-f573e35eebad.description2: The Admiralty is one of the most important places throughout the history of Algiers. It was first invaded by the Spanish, who built the Peñón there, and was then reclaimed by Aroudj. His brother, Kheireddine (Khayr al-Din), later built the jetty which bears his name. The Admiralty housed the Ottoman arsenal, as well as a beautiful fountain which is now listed as a historic monument. Today, it is the seat of the Musée National de la Marine. On the back of the panel an old label indicates that Sintès was considered the "father of Algerian painting".

bcebbe38-8019-5c28-b4b7-8f04a8b1d7be.name: Ibrahim Pasha (1789–1848)
bcebbe38-8019-5c28-b4b7-8f04a8b1d7be.description2: Portrait of Ibrahim Pasha (1789–1848). As the best General under his father Muhammad 'Ali Pasha, he fought successfully against the Wahhabites, the Ottoman Army and the Greeks. In 1831 he conquered Syria and governed it until 1841. In 1848 he deposed his senile father and was declared Vice King of Egypt by Sultan Abdülmecid I.

bd196d3c-3ad7-5a3c-a7bf-f9e67e2fa612.name: *The Library of Hadrian*
bd196d3c-3ad7-5a3c-a7bf-f9e67e2fa612.author: Tsigkakou 1981, 200-201
bd196d3c-3ad7-5a3c-a7bf-f9e67e2fa612.artist: Théodore Achille Louis, Vicomte du Moncel
bd196d3c-3ad7-5a3c-a7bf-f9e67e2fa612.description2: This representation is entitled *Painted Stoa*, referring to the colonnade (stoa) with monumental columns depicted on the right side of the picture. Nineteenth-century visitors to Athens referred to this monument by various names, such as Painted Stoa of Hadrian or Gymnasium, for its true identity was not discovered until after 1884, when systematic excavations commenced in the area of the Roman Agora (Forum Romanum). Recent archaeological investigation shows that this imposing colonnade is part of the propylon of the Library of Hadrian. Depicted at the edge of the propylon-incorporated in two columns- is a small Byzantine church. This is Hagioi Asomatoi sta Skalia (Incorporeal Saints at the Steps) of the eleventh century, and was demolished before the end of the nineteenth century, falling victim to the antiquarian extremism of ‘purifying archaeological sites’. The works of the artist-travellers who flooded into Greece during the nineteenth century are tangible testimonies not only to the illustrious past, but also to the landscape.

en: Tsigakou, Fani-Maria, *The Rediscovery of Greece: Travellers and Painters of the Romantic Era*, London: Thames & Hudson, 1981.

bd3a3ff1-4b7c-5ae4-a1d2-6d334b286559.name: Set of photos illustrating the Ducks Room, the Birds and Poultry Room, the Poultry and Egg sorting room at Fu`ad Agricultural Museum
bd3a3ff1-4b7c-5ae4-a1d2-6d334b286559.dates: 16 January 1938 (Photos taken during the inauguration of the museum)
bd3a3ff1-4b7c-5ae4-a1d2-6d334b286559.description2: The Fu`ad Agriculture Museum was considered the first of its kind in the Middle East and the Arab World during the 1930s. It was inaugurated during the time of King Faruq, the son of King Fu`ad, and houses a large number of collections related to agricultural and rural environments, as well as agricultural plants and animals.

bd591c95-bb06-5105-b1bd-b95187ad7a88.name: Villa Maria, in Tunis, the mansion of Luigi Rey, the son of a migrant from Piedmont (Italy)
bd591c95-bb06-5105-b1bd-b95187ad7a88.dates: Photograph: first years of the 20th century; building: late 19th century
bd591c95-bb06-5105-b1bd-b95187ad7a88.author: Giulia Barrera
bd591c95-bb06-5105-b1bd-b95187ad7a88.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 44
bd591c95-bb06-5105-b1bd-b95187ad7a88.third_name: *Villa Maria del cav. Luigi Rey, imprenditore*
bd591c95-bb06-5105-b1bd-b95187ad7a88.description2: Luigi Rey was the son of Italian immigrants Giuseppe Rey (1808-1897), of Piedmont and Adelaide Baldacci, of Tuscany. In 1836, Giuseppe Rey was dispatched to Tunis by his employer, a construction company from Genoa, to work in the Bardo Palace (the official residence of the Bey of Tunis). After completing the contract Giuseppe decided to stay in Tunisia, where he continued to work at the service of the Bey. Together with his three children (Luigi, Antonio and Pio), Giuseppe Rey set up a construction company that continued after his death. Predominantly with his brothers but at times on his own, Luigi Rey built a variety of private and public edifices, including the Tunisia Palace Hotel (designed by architect Resplandy).

en: Finzi, Silvia (ed.), *Architectures italiennes de Tunisie/Architetture italiane di Tunisia*, Tunis: Finzi/Ambasciata d'Italia, 2002.

bd5974b2-add3-5352-9473-20bfa7b6d015.name: Beiteddine Palace
bd5974b2-add3-5352-9473-20bfa7b6d015.description: The construction of the palace took ten years. Celebrated Lebanese constructors, such as Rustam and Yusuf Mujahes from Shuwayr were employed, as well as a number of European engineers and architects invited by the Prince Bashir al-Shihabi. Tiles were also imported from celebrated masters in Istanbul, Aleppo and Damascus.
bd5974b2-add3-5352-9473-20bfa7b6d015.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
bd5974b2-add3-5352-9473-20bfa7b6d015.history:
A tile framework imported from Marseille was added to this palace at the beginning of Prince Bashir al-Shihabi's reign resembling the typical Lebanese house, a future national symbol. The palace is interesting, as the ornamentation shows clear influences from the late Ottoman architecture, whereas the façade contains more neoclassical (or late baroque) elements from the late 19th and early 20th centuries. These additions did not alter the basic structure of the building, however. Ways the structure of this palace differed notably from the traditional models include: the location of a central stair inside the main hall, rather than outside, and the transformation of the patio into a public space between the palace and the street.  
Beiteddine palace was built to replace the palace at Deir al-Qamar, which had become too small for the expanding number of soldiers and servants. The prince ordered a luxurious palace to be built on the hill overlooking Deir al-Qamar, on land he had bought upon his marriage to "Sitt al-Shams.”

bd610f90-dbc3-5a38-87c0-75bb5979c752.name: House of Mohammed Ali
bd610f90-dbc3-5a38-87c0-75bb5979c752.holder: IMARET – Institute Mohammed Ali for the Research of the Eastern Tradition (under contract with the Egyptian Waqf Organization)
bd610f90-dbc3-5a38-87c0-75bb5979c752.author: I.M.A.R.E.T.
bd610f90-dbc3-5a38-87c0-75bb5979c752.history: According to local tradition, the building was the house of the local representative of the Ottoman administration or, later, the house of Mohammed Ali, founder of modern Egypt, who was born in Kavala in 1769. An inscription erected outside the house in 1883, almost 35 years after Mohammed Ali’s death, states that the building is among his charitable works, together with Imaret. It seems therefore possible that Mohammed Ali acquired the house, the finest one in town, and made it part of his Waqf, on the occasion of his visit to Kavala on his way back to Egypt from his only visit to Istanbul (August 1846). Currently, the House operates as a Museum and the seat of I.M.A.R.E.T. - Institute Mohammed Ali for the Research of the Eastern Tradition.
bd610f90-dbc3-5a38-87c0-75bb5979c752.keywords: 18th century Ottoman vernacular architecture; male and female quarters (selâmlik and haremlik); Mohammed Ali; Egypt
bd610f90-dbc3-5a38-87c0-75bb5979c752.description2: The House of Mohammed ‘Ali is a typical example of the so-called ‘broad-fronted, two-floor traditional dwelling’ with a row of rooms leading to the main living area on the first floor and a covered courtyard on the ground floor. Today, it is the only remaining example of vernacular architecture from the Ottoman period in the Balkan area, which still preserves the distinction between the male (Selâmlık) and female (Haremlik) quarters.

bd900903-3717-5683-b72b-426c25de43a9.name: Seal
bd900903-3717-5683-b72b-426c25de43a9.description2: This seal with a prayer of someone who has been on the Hajj was collected by the British Museum in 1878.

bd95565d-ce05-5cc5-ad92-00c2e0054f8d.name: Accounting book
bd95565d-ce05-5cc5-ad92-00c2e0054f8d.keywords: architecture; railways; Haydarpaşa Train Station; Anatolian Railway
bd95565d-ce05-5cc5-ad92-00c2e0054f8d.description2: This accounting book belonged to the Anatolian Railway. On it can be seen Abdülhamid II's monogram in gilding, and the words "*Devlet-i Aliye-i Osmaniye’nin Varidat ve Mesarifat-ı Umumiyesinin Muhasebesidir*" (this book belongs to the income and expenses of the state).

bd9ac0b4-17dd-5d2a-86a5-baadbae9f621.name: Jeweller’s tools box
bd9ac0b4-17dd-5d2a-86a5-baadbae9f621.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities
bd9ac0b4-17dd-5d2a-86a5-baadbae9f621.author: Huda Kilani
bd9ac0b4-17dd-5d2a-86a5-baadbae9f621.description2: Jeweller’s wooden box to keep tools such as hand drills, punctures and screws, and soldering iron clumps. This tool box belonged to an Armenian jeweller whose family left their country during the First World War and settled in Jerusalem. The jeweller then moved to Amman and settled there in 1948. The Armenians were well known as skilled craftsmen and jewellers. The owner of this box worked as a jeweller since the 1950's, using his tool box until his death. The tool box demonstrates the relationship between different waves of migration and the variegated demographic composition of the Jordanians.

bdc77deb-d803-5076-89a4-a826a7e730aa.name: The stand of the Italian Community in Tunisia at the International Exhibition held in Turin in 1911
bdc77deb-d803-5076-89a4-a826a7e730aa.author: Massimo Sanacore, Giulia Barrera
bdc77deb-d803-5076-89a4-a826a7e730aa.archival: ASLi, Archivio Moreno di Tunisi, b. 15
bdc77deb-d803-5076-89a4-a826a7e730aa.description2:
The picture shows how, on the occasion of the 1911 international exhibition in Turin the Italian community in Tunisia chose to represent itself by blending elements taken from the Italian and from the Tunisian material culture.  
One can read the sign E. & A. Coen, Tunisi, Susa, Sfax. Eugenio and Alfredo Coen were the owners of a furniture factory and of the imposing furniture shop, “Au Palais Arabe”, in downtown Tunis.

bde2bde2-7481-545c-9b6c-11a32b97be4d.name: Hôpital Habib-Thameur
bde2bde2-7481-545c-9b6c-11a32b97be4d.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
bde2bde2-7481-545c-9b6c-11a32b97be4d.history: This hospital, built in 1891 in the el-Halfaouine quarter by a group of Italian doctors, was initially called l'Hôpital Colonial Italien de Tunis and served the Italian residents of the city, most of which had emigrated from Sicily. It was moved to the building of the current Hôpital Habib-Thameur on the 15 March 1900, and in 1907 was renamed l'Hôpital Giuseppe Garibaldi, after the famous hero of Italian independence. Upon the arrival of English troops on 7 January 1943 it became a French hospital, and was renamed again to l'Hôpital de la Libération on the 6 June of the following year. It was finally given its current name by the Tunisian government following independence, in honour of the great doctor and militant nationalist Habib Thameur.
bde2bde2-7481-545c-9b6c-11a32b97be4d.keywords: Hospital; Charles Nicolle; Giuseppe Garibaldi; Habib Thameur
bde2bde2-7481-545c-9b6c-11a32b97be4d.description2: This hospital, which was constantly being expanded and renovated, started off with 150 beds. The hospital was served by Italian doctors, who were quickly joined by French doctors, and provided general medical services, as well as surgery, internal medicine, ophthalmology and radiology. Like the Hôpital Charles Nicolle, it also became prestigious university hospital following Tunisian independence.

be009de4-94db-5ccd-b043-8e9fe6838bd7.name: *Ma'ara*
be009de4-94db-5ccd-b043-8e9fe6838bd7.description2: Gold necklace with blue stones made of oval beads on a gold chain with coin print discs and heart-shaped leaves attached to them, with a large heart-shaped gold pendant inlaid with a blue stone.

be01848b-7ea6-50bc-b6b0-fc23630b1bfd.name: Casablanca: local inhabitants rebuilding their city
be01848b-7ea6-50bc-b6b0-fc23630b1bfd.description2: Casablanca was host to many French architectural experiments, and became a model for urban planners worldwide. Marshall Hubert Lyautey called on Henri Prost (1874–1859) to direct architectural works in the French Protectorate of Morocco. Thus, Prost established new plans for the cities of Casablanca, Rabat, Fez, Meknes, and Marrakesh. He decided to build a "new French-style city" in Casablanca. This photograph shows the works at the junction between the old medina and the new quarter at the same height as the old clocktower, with a caption stressing the "Arab population's" contribution to the works.

be44b9c0-4045-581b-a6e2-85c0f3bcd137.name: The Austrian ship on which Emperor Franz Joseph participated at the opening ceremony of the Suez Canal in 1869
be44b9c0-4045-581b-a6e2-85c0f3bcd137.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
be44b9c0-4045-581b-a6e2-85c0f3bcd137.description2: Emperor Franz Joseph visited the Suez Canal on board the Austrian ship, *Elisabeth*. He reached the Egyptian port of Ismilia on 14 Nov 1869 and stayed in Egypt until the 26 Nov 1869. During this trip, he also visited Cairo and Alexandria.

be8c9494-f659-53be-b44a-b763609d1e3d.name: Dawud Pasha’s bedroom
be8c9494-f659-53be-b44a-b763609d1e3d.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
be8c9494-f659-53be-b44a-b763609d1e3d.description2: This bedroom belonged to the first *mutasarrif* (ruler) of the Mount Lebanon *mutasarrifiyya*, Dawud Pasha, who governed from 1861–68). The room is furnished with one double bed, one baldachin bed, two curtains, one rug, two embroidery panels, two bedside tables and a coffer. A thin off-white mattress covered in silk and embroidered in gold thread rests on each bed, and both frames are covered with light blue silk draperies. Three small, rectangular off-white silk pillows rest against the baldachin bed's adjustable headboard. Two square pillows rest on the double bed. The blue silk drapery on the bed frames was also used for the identical silk curtains. The curtains served a purely decorative function and could not be closed, as they were sewn to the valances, which are made with off-white silk and gold embroidery. The curtains are held back with golden tiebacks hooked on golden metal knobs. The embroidery panels on the walls are also made with the same off-white silk, and feature a variety of floral designs. The two dark, wooden bedside tables resemble classical columns and the coffer is made with a lighter wood and decorated with floral bas-reliefs.

be90f64f-96f3-5dda-8345-68adf8244431.name: *Commercial port. Marseille*
be90f64f-96f3-5dda-8345-68adf8244431.description2: Frédéric Alexianu (aka F. Hugo d'Alesi) was a painter who quickly became specialised in advertisement posters for different kinds of transports, and in educational maps. This poster, aimed at primary school children, uses the example of Marseille to illustrate a trading port. The artist draws attention to the different commercial activities undertaken here, in addition to the transport of passengers on an ocean liner. The port of Marseille was the most important Mediterranean port in France, as it facilitated a great number of commercial exchanges with the French colonies in North Africa.

bee6cdea-7a07-512a-8073-61c3a5461987.name: *La Sahrienne: Arab dance for piano*
bee6cdea-7a07-512a-8073-61c3a5461987.artist: Composer: P. Codini; illustrator: A. Morel
bee6cdea-7a07-512a-8073-61c3a5461987.description2: The rise of "turkeries" in the 18th century is a good example of the influence of the widespread fascination with the "Orient" on music. In the 19th century, this Orientalism also influenced others art forms, such as painting and photography. Musical motifs started using "oriental" motifs once again in the early 20th century.

bf285df3-f538-57bf-9807-cad97e61acd5.name: *Political and commercial map of Europe, with all maritime communications* \[…\] *indicating* \[…\] *the modifications to the Middle Eastern states, according to the Congress of Berlin.*
bf285df3-f538-57bf-9807-cad97e61acd5.description2: This political and commercial map, drawn after the Congress of Berlin (1878), shows maritime and railway routes, as well as the travel time they require.

bf34096f-295d-5f0d-931b-71a243d32a5b.name: Sofa of Krste Petkov Misirkov
bf34096f-295d-5f0d-931b-71a243d32a5b.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
bf34096f-295d-5f0d-931b-71a243d32a5b.description2: Krste Petkov Misirkov (1874–1926) is among the most prominent personages of the recent Macedonian history. He was highly educated philologist, historian, ethnographer and publicist, having also been engaged in translation. He lived and worked in St. Petersburg, Russia. Besides his most important work "On Macedonian Matters", he had around thirty articles published in different newspapers.

bf3b00b7-e2b1-52d9-ac3a-710b848a0c69.name: Medal – The construction of the Suez Canal
bf3b00b7-e2b1-52d9-ac3a-710b848a0c69.artist:
Eugène André Oudiné (1st January 1810, Paris – 12 April 1887, Paris);  
Alexis Joseph Depaulis (30 August 1792, Paris – 29 September 1867, Paris)
bf3b00b7-e2b1-52d9-ac3a-710b848a0c69.description2: Built between 1859–1869, the Suez Canal represents a direct link between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. It had a positive influence on the commerce of Europe with the southern Arabian Peninsula, as it significantly reduced the duration of transports, given that in the past a longer route, which went around Africa, was used. This bronze medal dedicated to the construction of the canal was issued in 1864. Its obverse, designed by Chaplain, features the laureate head of emperor Napoleon III. On the reverse, designed by Depaulis, is depicted Industria standing between Europe and Africa, who are holding hands. Above the three female figures is inscribed “Jonction des deux mers” (Junction of the two seas) and beyond there are emblems of Egypt (a pyramid, the Sphinx, a palm tree) and of the canal (a ship).

bf7701c8-f1bc-545b-9706-c4d610004f60.name: Authorization of the first Egyptian Ministries
bf7701c8-f1bc-545b-9706-c4d610004f60.notice: This is an unedited Database entry and may contain errors and inconsistencies in spelling. We are doing our best to complete the editing asap. If you are in the position to help - with a donation or as a volunteer copy-editor - please contact us at [editing@museumwnf.net](mailto:editing@museumwnf.net).

bf7b0320-6a5a-5d4b-924a-eaaf6be147cf.name: Sakan house
bf7b0320-6a5a-5d4b-924a-eaaf6be147cf.description: This house is built on a principle of scalability, allowing the house to grow as the family expands, for example, without affecting its internal logic. Many of these houses can still be seen in Médawwar-Rmeil, Beirut, today. They are seen as 'heritage' houses, and are associated with the "triple arched" houses, which use the same fundamental basis. Many have been incorporated into the structure of new modern houses, coating the walls in concrete to create a new building and hiding the old *sakan* inside its very structure. The new, remodelled *sakan* can be identified today by its door, which overlooks/opens onto the main hallway and central shared room. The outdoor spaces in these houses are still built on the traditional model.
bf7b0320-6a5a-5d4b-924a-eaaf6be147cf.author: Jeff El-Msanne, David Andos
bf7b0320-6a5a-5d4b-924a-eaaf6be147cf.history: This type of house was generally a rural habitation until the 1950s. Today, it is part of the urban fabric of many towns, sandwiched between other properties on often narrow streets, or attached to new, modern builds.

bf874599-94fd-5c46-b1fb-9f801d14b0f4.name: *The best known people at the Exhibition, at the pavillions and restaurants*
bf874599-94fd-5c46-b1fb-9f801d14b0f4.archival: *L'Esposizione di Parigi del 1878 illustrata*, Sonzogno Editore, 1878, p. 484.
bf874599-94fd-5c46-b1fb-9f801d14b0f4.third_name: *I tipi più noti dell'Esposizione, nei palazzi e nelle trattorie*
bf874599-94fd-5c46-b1fb-9f801d14b0f4.second_name: A sketch of people at Paris Exhibition in 1878

bf87a0de-3e3f-504b-8bbb-757c5d6c17a8.name: *Faculty of Medicine Sports Teams at the Egyptian University*
bf87a0de-3e3f-504b-8bbb-757c5d6c17a8.keywords: Education; Students; Student Sports; Student Teams; Faculty of Medicine; Egyptian University
bf87a0de-3e3f-504b-8bbb-757c5d6c17a8.description2: The first sports teams at Egyptian University's Faculty of Medicine, where students achieved many regional and international victories. The 1923 Constitution stipulated that “Primary education is mandatory for all Egyptian boys and girls”. A decree was issued for the establishment of a public university under the name “The Egyptian University” in 1925, comprised of four faculties; literature, science, medicine and law. Ever since its establishment, the University has paid great attention to sport and university sport teams.

bf8ccf55-0b9f-51ab-833d-046d658d52ad.name: *Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey* (1784–1839)
bf8ccf55-0b9f-51ab-833d-046d658d52ad.keywords: Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey; Egypt; Janissary; Konya; Ibrahim Pasha; Muhammad Ali; Greece
bf8ccf55-0b9f-51ab-833d-046d658d52ad.description2:
Portrait of Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey (1784–1839). In 1826 Mahmud II initiated the development of a modern army. This led to the uprising of the Janissary, which was quelled by massacring the rebellious troops. Under Mahmud II's reign, in 1821 the Greeks started their fight for freedom which was granted to them in the Peace of Adrianople in 1829.  
After the destruction of the Janissary, the Ottoman Empire under Sultan Mahmud II had only 35,000 badly trained regular soldiers in 1827. Due to the weakness of the Ottoman Empire, Ibrahim Pasha, the son of Muhammad 'Ali (ruler of Egypt), invaded Syria. On 20 February 1832, the Egyptian Army defeated the Ottoman Army at the Battle of Konya. This forced Mahmud II to sign the Peace of Kütahya and to cede Syria and Kilikia to Egypt.

bfd5d0b7-c555-5670-8bef-67d8e0f7c0a2.name: Primary students at a village school in central Italy, which followed the teaching methods introduced by Maria Montessori
bfd5d0b7-c555-5670-8bef-67d8e0f7c0a2.author: Giulia Barrera
bfd5d0b7-c555-5670-8bef-67d8e0f7c0a2.archival: Collezione tessile di Tela Umbra, Fondo fotografico
bfd5d0b7-c555-5670-8bef-67d8e0f7c0a2.description2:
When Italy became a nation state in 1861, the illiteracy rate in the country was 78 per cent. In 1901, it was still at 56 per cent. Illiteracy was particularly high in the countryside. In 1877, the “Coppino Law”, made elementary schools mandatory and free of charge.  
Maria Montessori (1870-1952) was a medical doctor who developed innovative teaching methods for primary-school children. Her educational methods were first applied during the first decade of the 20th century. They met with great success and were applied in thousands of schools all over Europe and North America.

bfe37257-aff0-5289-b8c5-59ecbe78ace2.name: Yıldız Palace Greenhouse Kiosk
bfe37257-aff0-5289-b8c5-59ecbe78ace2.notice: This is an unedited Database entry and may contain errors and inconsistencies in spelling. We are working to raise the funds required to complete the editing; should you wish to contribute please visit our [Support page](https://www.museumwnf.org/atrium_support.php).
bfe37257-aff0-5289-b8c5-59ecbe78ace2.history:
Yildiz Palace, which is the last architectural example of Turkish Ottoman palace, is located on the Yildiz hill in the district of Beşiktaş. Sultan Ahmed I was the first to build a pavilion, over this land registered at the time to the Private treasury of the Ottoman Sultan as a hunting place sultans beginning during the reign of Suleiman the Magnificent (1520-1566).  
The main construction in the palace started in the period of Sultan Abdulhamid II (1876-1909) and it was called Saray-i Humayun (Central palace). During this period the palace comprised of buildings for private use of the sultan as well as buildings, allocated for the officials, repair shops and carpentry like repairing shop, carpenter’s shop and the buildings of culture and art such as theatre, museum and library. The Palace begun to serve as a museum under the name of "Directorate of the Museum of Yildiz Palace" since 1993.
bfe37257-aff0-5289-b8c5-59ecbe78ace2.description2:
The palace has an inner garden which is called “Hasbahce” with a pool inside resembling a natural creek. In different points of this garden there are small independent resort kiosks.  
In the Palace garden winter gardens and greenhouses were constructed for growing plants appropriate for the natural topography. Some greenhouses had unique designs where then-fashionable iron and glass elements were expertly used and it is known some of them had been heated. Especially the Limonluk Köşkü, designed by Raimondo D’Aronco and found just behing the Harem Gate is one of the most distinguished structures in the Palace.

bff5b327-dd8c-55ac-a7f0-49d5bbc62548.name: *Works for the opening of the Corinth Canal*
bff5b327-dd8c-55ac-a7f0-49d5bbc62548.author: Maria Dimitriadou
bff5b327-dd8c-55ac-a7f0-49d5bbc62548.description2:
The Corinth Canal under constuction, circa 1885. Photographer unknown.  
The Corinth Canal separates the Peloponnesian peninsula from the Greek. The idea of the canal was revived after Greece gained independence but soon abandoned due to economical reasons. The opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 gave an new impetus and the following year, the Zaimis government passed a law authorising the construction of the canal, which was formally inaugurated on 23 April 1882. Zaimis assigned the project to the Hungarian István Türr who set up the Société Internationale du Canal Maritime de Corinthe but the company failed and the project was finished by the company of Andeas Syngros. The canal was designed by the Hungarian engineer Béla Gerster with the assistance of the French Vincent Dauzants, a chief engineer of the Suez canal.

c007f06c-d190-5c7f-97a4-f7b8a6259c5a.name: *Palacete* \[small palace\], Avenida da República, Lisbon
c007f06c-d190-5c7f-97a4-f7b8a6259c5a.holder: Photography Archive, Lisbon City Council, CML
c007f06c-d190-5c7f-97a4-f7b8a6259c5a.author: Cristina Correia
c007f06c-d190-5c7f-97a4-f7b8a6259c5a.keywords: Cities; Urban Spaces; Reform; Social Change
c007f06c-d190-5c7f-97a4-f7b8a6259c5a.description2: Avenida Ressano Garcia, a main residential area and development axe opens in the North of Lisbon, one of the “Avenidas Novas” plan. Part of a later phase of the Lisbon Improvements Plan, led by Frederico Ressano Garcia, it also included a sanitation improvement. Its current designation is Avenida da República.

c00a74d5-7adc-54fe-85fc-96f35232755e.name: *Justice Room at the Alhambra, Granada*
c00a74d5-7adc-54fe-85fc-96f35232755e.description: This painting copied, almost literally, an engraving by David Roberts, published on the Tourist in Spain series by Roberts in 1835. Roberts travelled from Cordova to Granada in February 1883 and painted many sketches and drawings that were used afterwards, in engravings and paintings.
c00a74d5-7adc-54fe-85fc-96f35232755e.author: Carolina Miguel Arroyo
c00a74d5-7adc-54fe-85fc-96f35232755e.third_name: *La Sala de la Justicia en la Alhambra de Granada*

c05efb28-37e3-563c-be40-ec598ca0daf7.name: Popular resistance to the occupation
c05efb28-37e3-563c-be40-ec598ca0daf7.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
c05efb28-37e3-563c-be40-ec598ca0daf7.author: Bechir Yazidi
c05efb28-37e3-563c-be40-ec598ca0daf7.description2: Following the signing of the Treaty of Bardo many Tunisian towns declared their opposition to the act and set up a fierce resistance. This was the case in the town of Sfax, which withstood a six-month siege by sealing up, in the dead of night, the holes French bombings had created in the town walls. This image shows the end of the siege as the French forces invaded the town.

c0647b9c-1ac0-53b5-a15b-d5505d2f8137.name: An Italian booklet printed in Tunis in 1898 by Socialist and Anarchist Typography on the trial against the Italian anarchist leader Enrico Malatesta
c0647b9c-1ac0-53b5-a15b-d5505d2f8137.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
c0647b9c-1ac0-53b5-a15b-d5505d2f8137.author: Giulia Barrera
c0647b9c-1ac0-53b5-a15b-d5505d2f8137.archival: *Una pagina di storia del partito socialista-anarchico: resoconto del processo Malatesta e c.ni*, Tunisi: Tipografia socialista-anarchica, 1898
c0647b9c-1ac0-53b5-a15b-d5505d2f8137.description2:
Enrico Malatesta (1853-1932) was one of the most important Italian anarchist leaders and theorists. He spent a good part of his life in exile in different countries (including Argentina, Egypt, France, Lebanon, Siria, England and the United States). In 1882, he went to Egypt to support the revolt of Ahmad Urabi and was arrested by British authorities. In 1897, he was living in Ancona, in Central Italy, when he was arrested and put on trial. After serving seven months in prison, he was placed in internal exile on the island of Lampedusa (south of Sicily) from where, in 1899, he fled to Tunisia, then to Malta, then on to England.  
Italians in Tunisia set up a number of associations, political groups, newspapers, and cultural institutions of different political persuasions.
c0647b9c-1ac0-53b5-a15b-d5505d2f8137.holding_institution_org: Biblioteca di Storia Moderna e Contemporanea

c072d700-9ae2-5214-ad10-69e3cb6824fa.name: Film camera of the Manaki brothers
c072d700-9ae2-5214-ad10-69e3cb6824fa.holder: The Archive of the City of Bitola
c072d700-9ae2-5214-ad10-69e3cb6824fa.author: Aco Kimovski (Archive of the City of Bitola)
c072d700-9ae2-5214-ad10-69e3cb6824fa.second_name: Film camera of Charls Trade Company, serial no. 300
c072d700-9ae2-5214-ad10-69e3cb6824fa.description2: Janaki (1878–1945) and Milton (1880–1964) Manaki were born in Bitola and went on to become pioneers of Macedonian film and the first filmmakers in the Balkans. The Manaki brothers shot their first film merely 10 years after the Lumiere brothers. In 1905, they shot their grandmother Despina spinning wool with women from the neighbourhood. Their first film of ethnographic value was shot soon after. It documents celebration of the feast of St. Cyril and Methodius in front of the Church in Bitola devoted to these saints. In their films, the Manaki brothers strived to document visually events from everyday life and to frame them as real works of art. In 1921, they projected the first film in the open-air arena at the Shirok Sokak Street in Bitola.

c0b1bf14-42de-5081-87b4-b639f51e8816.name: Library museum
c0b1bf14-42de-5081-87b4-b639f51e8816.archival: Gavault, P., "Notice sur la Bibliothèque-Musée d'Alger", in *Revue Africaine*, vol. 38 (1894): 41.

c0d03656-54de-5836-824e-12905a80c7a5.name: Coffee grinder
c0d03656-54de-5836-824e-12905a80c7a5.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Departmant of Antiquities
c0d03656-54de-5836-824e-12905a80c7a5.author: Huda Kilani
c0d03656-54de-5836-824e-12905a80c7a5.keywords: coffee; coffee grinding; coffee beans; domestic furnishing; domestic vessels
c0d03656-54de-5836-824e-12905a80c7a5.description2: Manual coffee grinder carved out of a hard wood, usually oak. The grinder consists of two parts: the mortar and the pestle. The mortar is highly decorated with floral and geometric designs. After roasting the coffee beans, the local Bedouins use these to grind the beans. The sound of grinding functions as an invitation to others to come and chat while enjoying freshly prepared coffee.

c0d68bf3-fc29-5afb-9f0b-b36ef1a39350.name: "Workers' pensions"
c0d68bf3-fc29-5afb-9f0b-b36ef1a39350.keywords: Precarity; workers; pensions; elections; cartoon; caricature
c0d68bf3-fc29-5afb-9f0b-b36ef1a39350.description2: In 1910, a new law on "workers and farmers' pensions" introduced a compulsory insurance scheme. Before this, however, life was very different and many workers lived a very difficult old age, without financial support. The question of workers and farmers' pensions was one of the key electoral questions of the time therefore, as it concerned the majority of the population and those in power feared the social unrest it could trigger. This comical drawing mocks Alexandre Millerand (1859–1943), a socialist politician who forgot all his promises as soon as the elections were over.

c0dbe8f9-c861-5074-9fb8-b7dfcde583ed.name: *Al Azhar University, Cairo*
c0dbe8f9-c861-5074-9fb8-b7dfcde583ed.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
c0dbe8f9-c861-5074-9fb8-b7dfcde583ed.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
c0dbe8f9-c861-5074-9fb8-b7dfcde583ed.description2: Ludwig Deutsch  (1855-1935) was an Austrian-Jewish Orientalist painter. Here he tries to capture the atmosphere within the courtyard of the Al-Azhar mosque, first built in the 10th century and a major religious, intellectual and political hub of activity ever since. One of the oldest and most revered universities in the Islamic world, it was from here that a revolt against French troops was launched in 1798.  The French general Kleber was assassinated by Suleiman al Halabi, an al Azhar student, and later, Al Azhar was a focal point of protest against the Ottoman occupation of Egypt. Despite Deutsch's near-photographic style, his depiction is not entirely accurate and contains several errors: the arcades under the wooden oriel - their arches in reality wider and squatter - were not blocked up in his time, and the colour of the stonework is exaggerated. The praying men in the background are facing in the wrong direction (the direction of prayer or qibla in fact being to their right), Finally, the tall dark figure in the centre of the painting clutches what appears to be a Holy Qur'an between his dirty shoes, an act any Muslim would consider an absolute sacrilege.

c0fa2286-c49d-5054-a7e8-e9736fe3a90e.name: Flag of a workers’ league bearing the sign
c0fa2286-c49d-5054-a7e8-e9736fe3a90e.dates: Unknown (probably immediately after World War I)
c0fa2286-c49d-5054-a7e8-e9736fe3a90e.author: Giulia Barrera
c0fa2286-c49d-5054-a7e8-e9736fe3a90e.archival: ACS, Partito nazionale fascista, Mostra della Rivoluzione fascista
c0fa2286-c49d-5054-a7e8-e9736fe3a90e.description2:
This flag presumably belonged to a league of navvies, or labourers. It shows the tools used by workers employed in road construction, i.e. pickaxe and shovel.  
Starting from the last decades of the XIX century, trade unionism flourished in Italy. In the 1890s, in many towns different unions started to reunite in general unions at a town level, known as Camere del Lavoro (labour unions, modelled on the French Bourse du Travail). In 1906 the Confederazione Generale del Lavoro (CGdL), a national confederation of trade unions, was founded.

en: Centro studi Piero Gobetti, *Un' altra Italia nelle bandiere dei lavoratori: simboli e cultura dall'unità d'Italia all'avvento del fascismo*, Turin: Centro studi Piero Gobetti, 1980.

c1018611-912b-5af9-adeb-c669911527d4.name: Mardhouf al-Qawasim
c1018611-912b-5af9-adeb-c669911527d4.holder: Sharjah Heritage Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
c1018611-912b-5af9-adeb-c669911527d4.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
c1018611-912b-5af9-adeb-c669911527d4.second_name: Coin used by the Qawasim rulers of the lower Gulf region in the AH 13th century / AD 19th century
c1018611-912b-5af9-adeb-c669911527d4.description2: This rare copper alloy coin, known as 'Madhrouf Al Qawasim and weighing around 6.5 grams in weight, was minted in the trading port of Lanja (Linga) on the Persian coast of the Gulf in 1247 H/ 1831 CE.  In the 12th/18th and early 13th/ early 19th century, Lanja belonged to the extensive territories on both sides of the Gulf held by the Al Qawasim, and coins like this were used throughout the regions ruled by the Qawasim family at the time, including their main centres in Sharjah, Ras al Khaimah, Kalba, Khor Fakkan and Diba.

c120b65a-cd13-5c60-a28b-463b99dc6f57.name: Three
c120b65a-cd13-5c60-a28b-463b99dc6f57.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
c120b65a-cd13-5c60-a28b-463b99dc6f57.description2: These water pipes, or *araghil* (sing. *arghile*), is made of translucent glass painted with floral patterns in pale colours. The *araghil* have three main parts: first, you have a bowl for the coals sitting on top of a metal plate. Under this is the body of the *arghile*, which can come in a variety of shapes and sizes, and consists of a gasket and water jar. Connected to the main body is a pipe for smoking. The *arghile* originated in Persia and later became popular in 17th century Turkey, used by the Ottoman elite as a status symbol. The water pipe became hugely popular, and in 1841 even sparked a diplomatic crisis between France and the Ottoman Empire. However, although it remains popular in the modern Middle East, it was largely replaced by cigarettes in the 20th century. The *arghile* woks by vaporizing a flavoured tobacco called *shisha*, which is passed through water and then inhaled. Depending on their placement, the coals can either be used to boil the water and thus create water vapour, or to produce smoke by burning the tobacco. These *araghil* were used by Ottoman officials in 19th century Lebanon.

c1679a4a-eb18-5ec1-bd6f-8c176785d5ff.name: Pendant
c1679a4a-eb18-5ec1-bd6f-8c176785d5ff.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
c1679a4a-eb18-5ec1-bd6f-8c176785d5ff.author: Huda Kilani
c1679a4a-eb18-5ec1-bd6f-8c176785d5ff.keywords: triangle; silver; blue beads; Ottoman coins
c1679a4a-eb18-5ec1-bd6f-8c176785d5ff.description2: A thin silver triangular pendant and welded decoration with blue glass beads. Five chains dangle with Ottoman coins at the end. This kind of jewellery was part of the dowry the groom gave to the bride. Dowries consisted mostly of silver jewellery because only the rich could afford gold jewellery. The use of coins as pieces of jewellery, worn by brides in front of their relatives and friends, was an indirect statement of the financial status of the groom.

c16fad3d-de00-51aa-b32f-c08f9761a3dc.name: *Madame X*
c16fad3d-de00-51aa-b32f-c08f9761a3dc.keywords: Painting; Halil Pasha; orientalist Turkish painters
c16fad3d-de00-51aa-b32f-c08f9761a3dc.description2: The basis of Turkish painting drawing influence from western tradition was laid when *Mühendishane-i Berr-i Hümayun* (the Naval Academy) opened in 1795. Halil Pasha was foremost among the painters with a military background who founded a western-style art tradition in Turkey. He worked with Jean Leon Gerome in his atelier in Paris. He provided a unique distinction to the analysis of impressionist light and colour, and was an example of artists dealing with impressionist technique. Because of his qualified knowledge about anatomy and his interest in depicting the human figure, Halil Pasha had a unique place in Turkish Art History.

c183f4c0-12ee-5c65-bc23-c8e71cccb311.name: Qusayr Amra
c183f4c0-12ee-5c65-bc23-c8e71cccb311.dates: AD 8th century; visited by Alois Musil in 1896
c183f4c0-12ee-5c65-bc23-c8e71cccb311.author: Mohammad Najjar
c183f4c0-12ee-5c65-bc23-c8e71cccb311.history: The best-known of the desert castles and a World Heritage Site. This monument was most probably built sometime between 723 and 743, by al-Walid Ibn Yazid, the future Umayyad caliph Walid II. The abandoned structure was re-discovered by Alois Musil in 1898, with the frescoes made famous in drawings by an Austrian artist named Mielich for Musil's book.
c183f4c0-12ee-5c65-bc23-c8e71cccb311.keywords: World Heritage Site; Alois Musil; rediscovery; archaeological investigation
c183f4c0-12ee-5c65-bc23-c8e71cccb311.description2: Qusayr Amra is one of few Jordanian sites that have been listed as a World Heritage site. It represents the formative stage of Islamic art and architecture. It consists of vaulted reception hall and a bath house the walls of which were richly decorated. Its famous figurative wall paintings are proof that figurative art was not prohibited outside religious contexts at least during the first two centuries of Islam.

c1c21018-70eb-5e4f-93fb-c53b4de7b9a0.name: Glass vessel (*cista*) with *fenicio* ('Phoenician') decoration
c1c21018-70eb-5e4f-93fb-c53b4de7b9a0.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
c1c21018-70eb-5e4f-93fb-c53b4de7b9a0.author: Marina Minozzi
c1c21018-70eb-5e4f-93fb-c53b4de7b9a0.keywords: Applied arts; minor arts; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; motifs; collection; collector; glasswork; Murano glass; Phoenician art; Spanish glassworks; model; reproduction; decoration; Façon de Venise
c1c21018-70eb-5e4f-93fb-c53b4de7b9a0.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, as part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. The massive emigrations of Murano's glass workers to Spain during the 1600s spurred the building of many kilns that fused formal training with the strong local glass tradition. The *cista* is part of a series of objects made in Murano in the second half of the 19th century, mainly by the Murano Venetian Glass Society, and inspired to Spanish models called "Façon de Venise", showing a Phoenician decoration. The *cista*, or vessel, has a lid with a pinnacle in aquamarine glass.

c1d26025-2ca5-57a6-a96a-62abae4ddcf7.name: Port of Casablanca
c1d26025-2ca5-57a6-a96a-62abae4ddcf7.history: When the Port of Casablanca began trading in 1572 it was very small and known as the Port of Anfa. At this time, the port was used to export goods such as wheat and wool to the southern Mediterranean. When two centuries later, in 1785, Sultan Sidi Muhammad ibn ‘Abdallah decided to intensify trade between Morocco and countries beyond the southern Mediterranean, the port grew. A century later, in 1873, Sultan Mulay al-Hassan I launched a major project to improve the port's infrastructure and increase its capacity, and it was at this time that the commercial potential of the port was really exploited. Construction lasted several decades. In 1904, under Sultan Mulay ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, a contract was signed with the French company *Compagnie Marocaine* for the construction and development of a small port exclusively for barges that were used for loading and unloading the ships. The reorganisation in 1907 increased the harbour to 20ha. In 1921 this was increased to 140ha. In 1913 a Moroccan company and a German company, Schneider et Cie, began to co-manage the port.
c1d26025-2ca5-57a6-a96a-62abae4ddcf7.keywords: Technical innovation; communication; port; trade; commerce; economy; strategical port; strategical hub; modernisation; industrialisation; Moroccan ports; traditional port; work; urban space; changes in urban space; industrialisation and changes in urban spaces; Islamic city; Moroccan city; urban planning; plan; foreign company; French in Morocco; French in North Africa; German in Morocco; migration; southern Mediterranean; northern Mediterranean; trading route
c1d26025-2ca5-57a6-a96a-62abae4ddcf7.description2: In 1913 the port had a number of terminals under several different managements according to its wares. Terminal I, with a capacity of 7000,000 TEU, was managed by Marsa Morocco while Terminal II, with a capacity of 1,000 TEU, was managed by Somaport. There was a terminal for phosphates with a capacity of 19 million tons, operated by OCP; another for citrus with an 18.6ha capacity; and another for ore and hydrocarbons with a 14.5ha capacity. There was also a *Terminal Roulier* for vehicles, of 9.6ha capacity. After its enlargement in 1921, the port became a major international port with many warehouses, administrative offices and a large lighthouse. It had two gigantic locks, which meant that the harbour covered an area of 140 ha.

c1e7dbd9-cbc7-5538-9374-b4737a990584.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)

c1e7dbd9-cbc7-5538-9374-b4737a990584.keywords: Mount Moriah; Garizim; Messiah; Bible; Jewish; Hebrew; maiuscule; manuscript; Exile to Babilonia; pilgrimage; Palestine; Holy Land; sacred places; travel; book; Ottoman Palestine
c1e7dbd9-cbc7-5538-9374-b4737a990584.description2: This 19th-century photograph, included in an illustrated travel book, shows the Samaritan Pentateuch. The Samaritans are a religious community (today numbering only a few hundred people) born in Palestine from Judaism; nowadays, they live mostly on Mount Garizim (Nablus) and near Tel Aviv. They consider themselves to be the descendants of the ancient Israelites who did not leave Palestine for Babylon. Mount Garizim holds great religious value and is a place of pilgrimage for the Samaritans. The Samaritan Pentateuch is an important religious (and linguistic) symbol for this community. The British Library holds an important manuscript of the Samaritan Pentateuch, copied in Damascus in 1339.

c25b97af-3b31-51d4-8c86-07d5d3f06ecd.description2: The structure of an Egyptian home was considered particularly interesting and was rebuilt inside the Trocadero Park. The idea and the execution of the house were supported by the famous French Egyptologist Mariette-Bey, who was responsible for numerous excavations along the Valley of Nile and was the founder of the Cairo Museum. This work differs from the one presented by Mariette at the Exhibition in 1867 and was meant to represent a common living building. One room was dedicated to the opening of the Suez Canal and numerous photos and albums provided documentary evidence of Egyptian fashion, oases and travel memories.

c2b2223d-a18d-567f-a3db-ca8e7fcc63f5.name: Decorative ivory plaque
c2b2223d-a18d-567f-a3db-ca8e7fcc63f5.author: Mina Moraitou
c2b2223d-a18d-567f-a3db-ca8e7fcc63f5.description2: This fragmentary plaque, datable to the late Umayyad period is a superb example of high quality craftsmenship. It is carved in high relief allowing the decoration to stand in depth. Its main decoration consists of a vine scroll with five-lobed leaves and bunches of grapes. The vine stalks curl symmetrically creating three large circles. The central circle contains four smaller ones, two with a five-lobed leave and two with a bird, which turns its head backwards so as to pluck the fruit. The upper and lower circles form a spiral with five-lobed leaves and bunches of grapes. Outside the main scroll there are smaller three-lobed leaves and at the edge a hare and another bird. The object was bought by Antoni Benaki in 1919 from the Cairo dealer Maurice Nahman who provided objects for most of the important collectiors at the beginning of the 20th century.

c2b70678-bfae-5de0-a210-547e266d7099.holder: Population Exchange Museum (The Foundation of Lausanne Treaty Emigrants)

This photograph belongs to the Luka Likidis family, who migrated from Bodrum to Crete in 1916.

c2d7dded-69f6-5450-9ae1-d5680237968b.name: *Caiques and Sailboats at the Bosporus*
c2d7dded-69f6-5450-9ae1-d5680237968b.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
c2d7dded-69f6-5450-9ae1-d5680237968b.description2: Felix Ziem was able to produce works in many styles such as portraits, still life, genre scenes and historical depictions, though he is primarily renowned as a landscape artist. He was an active member of the Barbizon school, which primarily focused on the depiction of nature. In the painting, Istanbul is represented through a few mosque silhouettes in the background. Nonetheless, as in his Venetian scenes, the painting emphasizes the picturesque union of the city, the sea and human figures, which have been reduced to mere colour stains. Ziem, who produced his own paints from natural pigments, influenced other artists with the use of colour in his paintings. He is known to have used “lapis lazuli” for the dominant blue colour in this painting.

c2ef4889-9f51-575f-8794-b1fe85502111.name: An Entertainment Scene (Evening entertainment in the Golden Horn) from *Surname-i Vehbi*
c2ef4889-9f51-575f-8794-b1fe85502111.archival: The Library of Sultan Ahmed III
c2ef4889-9f51-575f-8794-b1fe85502111.description2: In this miniature we see an evening of rafts and fireworks on the Golden Horn. The grand vizier is seated on the Aynalıkavak quayside in the right frame and the sultan on the palace balcony. On the first of the two rafts in this procession, dancers and musicians perform in a garden of blazing cypress tree and Solomon’s seal fireworks. On the second is a revolving fortress stuffed with fireworks that have been set off while the military band at the stern of the raft plays.

c3322b4d-5cf0-5412-aee3-1fd52f0cba22.description2: In the 19th century and the beginning of the 20th century, metal jewellery and other articles of adornment in Macedonia were made by goldsmiths. They were distinguished with exceptional diversity reflecting the skill and creativity of artisans. This versatility applies particularly to headdresses. The bridal hat is made of broadcloth – *klashna* – which is decorated with small silver coins reminiscent of fish scales. This particular headdress is part of a jewellery set that goes with a piece worn on the breasts, which was called *mingjuska so vot*.

c3469ef6-684c-5443-94aa-94ce360bb640.name: House
c3469ef6-684c-5443-94aa-94ce360bb640.dates: End of 19th – beginning of the 20th century
c3469ef6-684c-5443-94aa-94ce360bb640.author: Prof. Petar Namichev (PhD)
c3469ef6-684c-5443-94aa-94ce360bb640.history: *Tajfas* were very well organized and had extremely professional approach to their work. These construction masters developed a secret construction language which they used for communication among themselves. There were even variants of the secret construction language, depending on the local dialects and the origin of the members of the *tajfa*. The best known artists of the woodcarving craft in Macedonia came from the Reka Area, including Makarija Frchkovski, Petre Filipovski Garkata and his brother Marko Filipovski – as well as many others.
c3469ef6-684c-5443-94aa-94ce360bb640.description2: The construction trade has an exceptionally long tradition in the Reka Area. The artisan school in the Debar-Reka area, with its centre in Galichnik, was mentioned in sources from as early as the 10th century. People from this area – the Miyaks – have given birth to numerous generations of construction masters throughout the centuries. Construction *tajfas* from the Reka Area were widely known and used to build houses, churches, mosques and other structures throughout the Balkans, even in Asia Minor. This three-storey house was built completely of stone. It is the type of tower house of asymmetrical lay out distinctive to the Reka Area. Construction of tower houses developed in this area for the purpose of defence and protection from intruders in the turbulent times of the 18th and 19th centuries.

c369fdd9-b766-5049-9f4f-a257d2df3d50.name: Rome Exhibition 1911 (Piazza d'Armi) – Sicilian Pavilion
c369fdd9-b766-5049-9f4f-a257d2df3d50.holder: Central Institute for Ethno-Anthropology, National Museum of Arts and Popular Traditions

c369fdd9-b766-5049-9f4f-a257d2df3d50.description2: Within the International Exhibition of Rome in 1911 and related to the celebrations for the 50th anniversary of the Unification of Italy, a "Forum of Regions" was arranged in the Piazza d’Armi. The architect Ernesto Basile (1857–1932), author of the project for the Sicilian Pavilion, took inspiration from the Arab-Norman architecture in Sicily, in particular from Zisa Palace, the church of Saint John of the Hermits and the Cathedral of Monreale. On the outside, the building looked like a cube with plain walls decorated with blind pointed arches and battlements on top. Doors and windows show pointed arch as well. At the sides of the facades two small towers topped by a small small dome give to the palace a striking oriental look. On the inside, there was an open space with columns topped by capitals, walls decorated with mosaics and majolicas, and fountains.

c3b4eb2f-61ad-53f7-a9e3-79fafd0deca5.description2: Italy and the Ottoman Empire signed a peace treaty that officially ended the Italo-Turkish war on October 18th, 1912, passing control of the former Ottoman provinces of Tripolitania, Fezzan, and Cyrenaica to Italy. The Ottoman army left Libya, but hostilities between Italian troops and the Arabs that did not acknowledge Italian authority continued. By July 1914, Italy was able to occupy almost all the territory of Tripolitania, the coast of Cyrenaica and part of the territory of Fezzan. In 1915 a great Arab insurrection broke out and forced Italy to abandon much of the territory it had previously occupied.

c4179abe-6375-58e2-9109-f22b4b9e5ebd.name: Photograph: *Arabic School, Learning the Koran, Egypt*
c4179abe-6375-58e2-9109-f22b4b9e5ebd.description:
Stereoscopic photography that creates the illusion of depth of field from two apparently identical images mounted on a rigid board by using a specific viewfinder, or stereoscope.  
The arrival of Islam to Africa caused the birth of schools where the Qu'ran was taught in Arabic. Probably Islamic education was the first education system introduced in African populations. Islam establishes education as a key priority for children.  
Universities, *madrasas* (organised institutions with different levels for studying Islamic religion), and Qur'anic schools (first education that children receive) are used by Islam as educational institutions and have played an important role in spreading Islamic religious, social, moral and cultural values between African populations.  
In the *madrasas* and Qur'anic schools, the Qur'an is learned and memorised by reading and writing at a wooden table. The memorization of the Qur'an is done by copying the teacher a text written on paper, and later recited aloud until memorised. Students were not allowed to pass to another passage until the current passage had been memorized.

c4322598-8028-5f79-ae2e-c4ce254ee9ee.name: Military Infirmary
c4322598-8028-5f79-ae2e-c4ce254ee9ee.description: This hospital (or *hastahane* in Ottoman Turkish), commissioned by Sultan 'Abd al-'Aziz (Abdülaziz) (1861-76) in 1865, was often referred to as the military infirmary. The building included two wings, and the northern wing housed a drugstore (*ajzah*). The courthouse which later inhabited the building was moved to a different location when it became the Lebanese University's Institute of Fine Arts.
c4322598-8028-5f79-ae2e-c4ce254ee9ee.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
c4322598-8028-5f79-ae2e-c4ce254ee9ee.history: In 1865, this military hospital was commissioned by the Ottoman sultan 'Abd al-'Aziz (Abdülaziz).The hospital was later converted to a courthouse by the French, who took control of the city in 1918 following the collapse of the Ottoman Empire. Today, the building houses the Lebanese University's Institute of Fine Arts.

c4e1a5f3-c276-5476-bae6-589764a31420.name: House
c4e1a5f3-c276-5476-bae6-589764a31420.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Prof. Marula Nikoloska, Ph.D. (consultant)
c4e1a5f3-c276-5476-bae6-589764a31420.history: Krushevo houses had to be adjusted to the naturally steep terrain on which they sit. The dwelling architecture of this town thus shows notable vertical development, which has given rise to creative architectural solutions for the purpose of maximum use of space.
c4e1a5f3-c276-5476-bae6-589764a31420.description2: The architecture of Krushevo was influenced by houses in Moscopole, as well as by the mountain dwellings in Epirus and Thessaly. Native architects, Vlachs originating from Moscopole and Miyaks from the Reka Area, created their distinctive and highly autonomous dwelling architecture which combined the traditional mode of building with architectural solutions arising from the steep terrain. This house is a three-storied structure of symmetrical type. The ground floor is made of stone and mortar. Upper stories were built of wooden framing and adobe, covered with plaster. The dynamic rhythm of the front façade has been achieved by the repetitive layout of windows and balconies above the front door at the second and third storey. The decoration is enhanced by the intricate wooden and iron balcony balusters on the second and third storey.

c4f3ee34-3e55-5cf6-ab02-eee9f50cdc11.name: *Danilo I, Prince of Montenegro (1871–1939)*
c4f3ee34-3e55-5cf6-ab02-eee9f50cdc11.keywords: Danilo I, Prince of Montenegro; Jugoslavia; Vienna; Austria
c4f3ee34-3e55-5cf6-ab02-eee9f50cdc11.description2: Danilo I, Prince of Montenegro (1871–1939) as a child. Danilo was the eldest son of King Nicola I of Montenegro. He was married to Princess Jutta von Mecklenburg-Strelitz and had to leave Montenegro after it was integrated in the kingdom of Yugoslavia after WWI. He died in 1937 in Vienna, Austria – in exile.

c5af0628-6524-5b0d-a3ae-ef6099a54a96.name: *Encampment of the Awlad Said Mount Sinai 1839*
c5af0628-6524-5b0d-a3ae-ef6099a54a96.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
c5af0628-6524-5b0d-a3ae-ef6099a54a96.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
c5af0628-6524-5b0d-a3ae-ef6099a54a96.description2: The Awlad Said are a large clan of the Sawalha tribe, traditionally based on Southern Sinai. It was escorts from this tribe that accompanied Roberts during his traversing of the Sinai. This depiction gives a detailed impression of their traditional encampments and tent construction. Situated in a valley sheltered by high, rugged mountain ranges, the encampment consists of severalrows of low, rectangular tent structures with flat roofs. Separating walls and screens within are created by striped, woven textile units. Inhabitants of the camp are seen seated in small groups, engaged in conversation or standing in groups, lances in hand. The men are dressed in headscarfs, gowns and cloaks of varying colour, while the few female figures that appear are cloaked in black abayas, all-enveloping black cloaks. From a ravine in the far background, a long caravan of men and camels approaches the camp.

c60364d0-48c1-5f1e-9f18-2ee410152391.name: Drawing
c60364d0-48c1-5f1e-9f18-2ee410152391.keywords: Victor Rousseau; Factory; Vista Alegre; Aveiro estuary; master of painting
c60364d0-48c1-5f1e-9f18-2ee410152391.description2: In 1826, Victor Rousseau, French artist living in political exile in London, was hired by Augusto Ferreira Pinto Basto, son of the Vista Alegre Factory’s founder. Regarding the artistic aspect, his hiring allowed for the introduction of new models and decorations, into the eclectic and romantic spirit of those times, and was essential in providing Vista Alegre’s portfolio with a new aesthetic and formal wealth and exuberance. Along with his pedagogical and artistic contribution in the Factory, Victor Rousseau also left as a legacy an interesting drawing album. The drawing, with scenes from the Factory representing the Aveiro Estuary and river Bôco, calls our attention to the specificities needed for the implementation of an industry in the 19th century. The proximity of the estuary represented not only abundance of water, but also offered easy routes for transporting raw materials and other commodities.

en: Valente, Vasco, *Porcelana Artística Portuguesa*, Porto: Imprensa Moderna Limitada, 1949.

c64f3835-f9f7-5723-9b30-b413f5f0111c.name: *Homarus hakelensis* Fraas 1878 and clupeomorph fishes
c64f3835-f9f7-5723-9b30-b413f5f0111c.holder: National Museum of Natural History and Science (MUHNAC) / Museums of the University of Lisbon
c64f3835-f9f7-5723-9b30-b413f5f0111c.author: Liliana Póvoas (MUHNAC-UL), Pedro Dantas (MUHNAC-UL)
c64f3835-f9f7-5723-9b30-b413f5f0111c.keywords: Homarus hakelensis; clupeomorphs; Upper Cretaceous; lithographic limestone; National Museum of Natural History and Science; University of Lisbon
c64f3835-f9f7-5723-9b30-b413f5f0111c.description2: *Homarus* is as genus of marine crustacean decapode (lobster). Its first pair of legs is transformed into big claws showing dimorphism (one specialised into a crushing claw and the other into a cutting claw). In the fossil register we can find about eight species of Homarus. But nowadays only two exist: *Homarus gammarus* (European lobster) and *Homarus americanus* (American lobster). *Homarus hakelensis* is a fossil species described from specimens found at the Upper Cretaceous (Cenomanian) site of Hakel, Lebanon. In this plate we can also find some specimens of clupeomorph fishes. In this group of teleosts, that date back to the Early Cretaceous (c. 140 million years) belongs, today, the herring, the sardine and the anchovy, for example. They are generally small silvery marine fishes.
c64f3835-f9f7-5723-9b30-b413f5f0111c.holding_institution_org: Museu Nacional da Historia Natural e da Ciencia (MUHNAC)

c671443a-8a37-5c35-975f-840074e8db8a.name: *Woman Playing a String Instrument*
c671443a-8a37-5c35-975f-840074e8db8a.archival: Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection (Orientalist Paintings Collection)
c671443a-8a37-5c35-975f-840074e8db8a.keywords: Music; harem; court music; musician; female musician; traditional entertainments
c671443a-8a37-5c35-975f-840074e8db8a.description2: In this painting there is an Ottoman woman in her daily attire with her hair covered by an embroidered and printed kerchief. She plays a string instrument. Music was one of the most popular kinds of amusement in Turkish harems. The lute in particular, and similar string instruments, have always occupied an important place in the lives of women. This picture was used on the cover of a special issue of *Le Figaro Illustré* dedicated to Zonara and published in 1908, and also appeared in *Der'i Se'adet*, a book written by Adolphe Thalasso and illustrated by Zonaro.

c74178c2-ab9f-5408-9cbb-cf1f4eff394d.description2: A press release in the Al-Ahram newspaper regarding the Raml Tramway and related views of the Prime Minister at that time. The tramway of Alexandria was the first method of mass transportation in Egypt and in Africa, and the most common. The tramway began operating in 1860, and is thus considered the oldest tramway in Africa – and among the oldest in the world.

c7656766-ff0b-53a9-a4ef-3d548544e45d.name: *The Royal Stock Exchange*
c7656766-ff0b-53a9-a4ef-3d548544e45d.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
c7656766-ff0b-53a9-a4ef-3d548544e45d.archival: Fearnside, William Gray and Harrel, Thomas, *Holmes's Great Metropolis: or, Views and history of London in the nineteenth century ... Edited by W. G. Fearnside ... and T. Harrel. Illustrated with ... Engravings*, London: Thomas Holmes, 1851, p. 19
c7656766-ff0b-53a9-a4ef-3d548544e45d.keywords: Trade; finance; bank; European finance; London
c7656766-ff0b-53a9-a4ef-3d548544e45d.description2: This illustration of the new Royal Stock Exchange was included in a book called *The Great Metropolis*, published in London by Thomas Holmes in 1851. The book was conceived as an illustrated collection of all the notable monuments in London, providing historical information about the city and about each monument. Although it looks like a tourist guide, it offers more than this kind of guide because it describes not just monuments, but also other landmarks that testify to the social and commercial development of the city. Among the landmarks illustrated and described, as well as the new Royal Stock Exchange, is the Crystal Palace, the site of the Universal Exhibition (the Great Exhibition) of 1851.

c7c7015e-6302-5b17-8d29-534365062bab.name: View of Torre de los siete Picos, the Alhambra Palace
c7c7015e-6302-5b17-8d29-534365062bab.description: In his travels to Granada Joaquin Sorolla was fascinated by the monument of the Alhambra, the palace of Naridd kingdom of Granada. It is, along with the Mosque of Cordoba, the most important monument of Muslim Spain. Sorolla's paintings are far away from the Orientalism topics, and instead it recreates in the beauty of its nooks and gardens, capturing a more personal and intimate perspective of the monument. In this view from afar, highlights the beauty of the building and its surroundings.

c7de3940-ac44-5e99-93fd-416c7b6e83ea.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
c7de3940-ac44-5e99-93fd-416c7b6e83ea.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ancient Istanbul; palace; pavilion
c7de3940-ac44-5e99-93fd-416c7b6e83ea.description2: The Ihlamur Pavilion is located at the intersection of Nüzhetiye Street between Ihlamur and Tesvikiye and has an area of about 25,000 square meters. The Ihlamur Pavilion consists of two kiosks: the Maiyet and Merasim Kiosk. The Merasim Kiosk was reserved for the sultan’s personal use. The Maiyet Kiosk, the simpler of the two, was used by the sultan’s entourage and family members, and it currently serves as a beautiful cafeteria. The kiosk is decorated with crystal chandeliers, European-style furniture, Hereke carpets, and decorated vases.

c7f58b8f-d101-5a99-a3cc-dcb898bbfeeb.name: An Algerian woman grinds her meal in an old wooden mill
c7f58b8f-d101-5a99-a3cc-dcb898bbfeeb.description2: Many Western photographers took great interest in women's daily lives, or in daily rural tasks. In this photograph from 1920 an Algerian woman is pictured as she grinds wheat with a wooden pestle and mortar.

c82a2a26-f746-5771-93c4-6bcceedcab50.name: *Mount Gilboa from Sulem, a woman spinning cotton*
c82a2a26-f746-5771-93c4-6bcceedcab50.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
c82a2a26-f746-5771-93c4-6bcceedcab50.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
c82a2a26-f746-5771-93c4-6bcceedcab50.artist: Philip Meerer (after a pencil drawing by John Douglas Woodward 1846–1924)
c82a2a26-f746-5771-93c4-6bcceedcab50.description2: 19th-century Palestine was an increasingly viable, agricultural producer of cotton, whose importance on the world market was steadily increasing. Mainly supplying European countries, cotton became a key commodity. 6% of the cultivated land of Palestine was given up. Throughout the 1860s, concerted efforts were made to meet demand, but as early as the 1870s, the industry, which was merely based on expanded cultivation rather than industrialisation, declined again. This print originally appeared in Vol.1, page 269 of Charles William Wilson's 'Pituresque Palestine, Sinai and Egypt, published between 1881 and 1884. The caption reads: 'Mount Gilboa from Sulem (Shunem). The northern extremity of the range of Jebel Fuku'a (Gilboa) is shown; the highest point is crowned by the sanctuary of Neby Mezar. In the foreground a woman is spinning cotton.

c869c0fc-13da-5c97-9a34-aeb4470de17e.name: *Top of the garden at Marengo, ancient Marabout*
