c869c0fc-13da-5c97-9a34-aeb4470de17e.description2: This part of Algiers has a particularly rich history. The painting depicts the famous mausoleum of Sidi Abderrahmane Ettaâlibi ('Abd al-Rahman al-Thalibi) who was a member of one of the most ancient families of Algiers. He was buried here in the 7th century and was made the Patron Saint of Algiers due to his reputation as a wise and knowledgeable man.

c88e4cac-7c3a-5acf-8cad-3a3c6bf1777f.name: Photograph: *Music School, Syria*
c88e4cac-7c3a-5acf-8cad-3a3c6bf1777f.description:
Stereoscopic photography that creates the illusion of depth of field from two apparently identical images mounted on a rigid board by using a specific viewfinder, or stereoscope.  
The images taken by the Keystone View Company show very different scenes related to lifestyles and traditions of different continents. In this case, there is a man playing a stringed instrument with a bow, possibly a type of rebec, surrounded by a group of children and two adults, who watch and listen carefully. In Syria, as in many other parts of the world, music has had and still has an important role as a means of transmitting knowledge and to celebrate individual and collective events, and is closely linked to rites, institutions, cultural and ideological activities of different humans. This image illustrates not only the practice of this activity, music, but also the transfer of knowledge from one generation to another; music serves as a vehicle of expression and relationship between members of a society.
c88e4cac-7c3a-5acf-8cad-3a3c6bf1777f.keywords: Photography; music; Syria; scenes of life

c8dcb99a-4981-58af-a357-22664ca7f472.name: Trade agreement between the Sublime Porte and the Grand Duke of Tuscany. Annexed to the treaty, a booklet with the duties that the merchants from the Grand Duke of Tuscany had to pay in Turkey
c8dcb99a-4981-58af-a357-22664ca7f472.author: Loredana Maccabruni
c8dcb99a-4981-58af-a357-22664ca7f472.third_name: 'Trattato di Commercio concluso tra la Sublime Porta e la Corte di Toscana' (Costantinopoli, 7 giugno 1841) and *Tariffa dei diritti da pagarsi dai negozianti granducali alle dogane in Turchia per le merci che asportano o v’importano stata fissata in Costantinopoli il dì 25 luglio 1841 fra i Commissari nominati a tale effetto dall’incaricato d’affari di Toscana e dalla Porta ottomana*, Firenze, 1842
c8dcb99a-4981-58af-a357-22664ca7f472.description2: With this treaty, the Grand Duke of Tuscany Leopold II and the Ottoman Sultan Abdul Megid Han intended to encourage economic exchanges between the countries. Tuscan citizens and ships were accorded the same privileges that those from other countries had received. The treaty also provided for some tax reduction in favour of Tuscan merchants.

c95dc265-e63b-5039-8f8f-a2652ee2dcba.name: Tripolitania (Libya). Italian soldiers in front of a Roman mosaic
c95dc265-e63b-5039-8f8f-a2652ee2dcba.holder: Central Institute for Cataloguing and Documentation (ICCD)
c95dc265-e63b-5039-8f8f-a2652ee2dcba.author: Giulia Barrera
c95dc265-e63b-5039-8f8f-a2652ee2dcba.description2:
Italian soldiers in front of a Roman mosaic in Tripolitania, Libya. At their feet, almost at the centre of the photo, a plaque explains that: “These wonderful remains of Ancient Rome art and civilization” have been brought back to the admiration of posterity by the Italian soldiers of the Bersaglieri 33rd Battalion in 1911 and they “confirm… Italy’s right to rule over Tripolitania”.  
The plaque explicitly claims that Italy colonial ambitions over Libya were legitimate because Ancient Rome had once ruled over that territory. This line of argument was often used by Italian colonialists in order to legitimize Italian colonial ambitions over Libya.
c95dc265-e63b-5039-8f8f-a2652ee2dcba.holding_institution_org: Istituto Centrale per il Catalogo e la Documentazione (ICCD)

c96923cb-dba0-5c95-81e1-1742fdb0a515.name: *View of Istanbul*
c96923cb-dba0-5c95-81e1-1742fdb0a515.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
c96923cb-dba0-5c95-81e1-1742fdb0a515.description2: This particular Istanbul painting by Felix Ziem reveals the picturesque aspect of life at sea against the backdrop of the city’s silhouette. The composition of the sailboats and marines in the foreground is balanced by the cityscape with a monumental mosque structure in the background. The artist’s use of vibrant colours and his efforts to capture the shimmering effects of the constant change of light with a fast, dynamic brush stroke technique dominate the painting. This style has led Ziem to be compared with impressionist painters, and even to be regarded as an artist who foreshadowed the emergence of impressionism with his work. The use of brilliant sunlight, which is considered as the major contribution of orientalist painting to European art is evident in the city's cap in the background.

c99f4a2d-2d4c-538b-b57e-e1ba93984854.name: *Votes for Women*
c99f4a2d-2d4c-538b-b57e-e1ba93984854.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
c99f4a2d-2d4c-538b-b57e-e1ba93984854.artist: Artist: Alfred Pearse; publisher: The Women's Press; printer: Spottiswoode, Dixon & Hunting Ltd
c99f4a2d-2d4c-538b-b57e-e1ba93984854.keywords: Women; equality; George; poster; suffragette; print; politics; propaganda; printing
c99f4a2d-2d4c-538b-b57e-e1ba93984854.materials: Paper, lithographic ink; colour lithograph on paper, planographic printing
c99f4a2d-2d4c-538b-b57e-e1ba93984854.description2:
This Suffragette poster was created in response to the Liberal Prime Minister Herbert Asquith's suppression of the 1910 Conciliation Bill, which proposed extending the vote in Britain and Ireland to around one million wealthy, property-owning women. It shows King George V painting the text 'We Bow to the Will of the People' onto a poster, whilst a man paints on the King's back, and a Suffragette paints onto the man’s. The cartoon aimed to show how Asquith had gone against the will of Parliament, the elected representatives of the people. The Suffragettes urged male voters to register their protest by voting against Liberal candidates in the next election.  
  
This poster was published by the Woman's Press, who oversaw the publishing and propaganda for the Suffragettes. It was designed by Alfred Pearse, under the pseudonym ‘A. Patriot', Pearse was a dedicated Suffragette supporter and designed many of their posters.

c9c74f64-866f-5104-9cb6-e6c2fc0927e4.name: *O Grupo do Leão*
c9c74f64-866f-5104-9cb6-e6c2fc0927e4.holder: National Museum of Contemporary Art – Chiado Museum
c9c74f64-866f-5104-9cb6-e6c2fc0927e4.author: DGPC
c9c74f64-866f-5104-9cb6-e6c2fc0927e4.second_name: The group of artists in the Leão de Ouro beer house
c9c74f64-866f-5104-9cb6-e6c2fc0927e4.description2: This is a Portuguese new generation of artists who played a major role in naturalist and realist painting in Portugal. Meant to decorate the beer house, this painting became famous and marked the beginning of a period of great artistic activity. This painting by Columbano Bordalo Pinheiro (1857–1929), the greatest painter of his time, depicts a group of artists who got together at the “Leão de Ouro” beer house in Lisbon.
c9c74f64-866f-5104-9cb6-e6c2fc0927e4.holding_institution_org: Museu Nacional de Arte Contemporânea – Museu do Chiado

ca166ea6-6764-5d07-b12e-8c86a410ba79.name: Medal of Emperor Franz Joseph I
ca166ea6-6764-5d07-b12e-8c86a410ba79.description2: This medal shows the symbolic figure of faith. The angel on the right side presents the crown of Austria to her. The opposite side of the medal has a portrait of Emperor Franz Joseph. The medal was created in commemoration of Franz Joseph's visit to Jerusalem in November 1869.

ca3349d1-e207-5344-a1a6-a09eff99322b.name: Bashura school for girls 'Al-Makassed'
ca3349d1-e207-5344-a1a6-a09eff99322b.author: Hala Masri
ca3349d1-e207-5344-a1a6-a09eff99322b.history: This was the first school the 'Al-Makassed' association founded. It was built with the principle of admitting all girls.
ca3349d1-e207-5344-a1a6-a09eff99322b.description2: This two-storey building, with its patio and well-defined arcades, shows clear influences from Spanish architecture.

ca4bf20e-94a9-50b1-bca9-38b4f7855c35.name: *Salt Watercolours*
ca4bf20e-94a9-50b1-bca9-38b4f7855c35.keywords: archaeology; exploration; Egyptomania; travel; traveller; collection; collector; museums; historical document
ca4bf20e-94a9-50b1-bca9-38b4f7855c35.description2: A watercolour scene showing the king before various gods from the tomb of Seti I in the Valley of the Kings, Thebes, drawn by Henry Salt shortly after the discovery of the tomb by the explorer Giovanni Belzoni in 1817. The freshness of the colours amazed the early travellers.

ca59fd60-c057-5dbf-a2fa-484dcab24b97.name: Ring
ca59fd60-c057-5dbf-a2fa-484dcab24b97.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
ca59fd60-c057-5dbf-a2fa-484dcab24b97.author: Huda Kilani
ca59fd60-c057-5dbf-a2fa-484dcab24b97.description2: Thin silver ring with oval-shaped agate stone set in silver with inherent decoration on the soundings. Silver jewellery was the most common, because only rich people could afford gold jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom. The Jordanian economy relied on trades and crafts and new waves of people started to come to Jordan and began to settle for this purpose. This object is an example of how traditional fashion reflected the variegated population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is also an example of local personal attire, fashion, costumes and rites.

ca6bd475-805d-5b06-a1e3-16bb93242b3b.name: *The interior of the Queen's carriage: meeting between Louis-Philippe and Queen Victoria*
ca6bd475-805d-5b06-a1e3-16bb93242b3b.artist: Lithographer: Jules David; artist: Édouard Pingret
ca6bd475-805d-5b06-a1e3-16bb93242b3b.description2: Keen on keeping up good relations with the United Kingdom, King Louis-Philippe of France accepted Queen Victoria's invitation in 1844. Accompanied by Guizot and his youngest son, the Duke of Montpensier, he was received lavishly by the English royal family. In 1842, Queen Victoria became the first sovereign to take the train between London and Windsor. Since then, British rail companies had begun setting up carriages especially reserved for the Royal Family. One of the key experiences offered to Louis-Philippe was the opportunity to travel by train in one of these spectacular carriages.

ca7cde0f-42ef-5233-9987-adf5389bf28f.name: *Ma'ara*
ca7cde0f-42ef-5233-9987-adf5389bf28f.description2: Gold necklace with blue stones made of oval beads on a gold chain with coin print discs and heart-shaped leaves attached to them, with a large heart-shaped gold pendant inlaid with a blue stone and pearls.

ca84a358-0e08-5345-bc08-43570cf84e04.name: *Women grinding corn in Sinai*
ca84a358-0e08-5345-bc08-43570cf84e04.dimensions: Height: 8.5 cm Size of card, Width: 17.4 cm
ca84a358-0e08-5345-bc08-43570cf84e04.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
ca84a358-0e08-5345-bc08-43570cf84e04.artist: War Office Topographical Department (publisher); Royal Engineers (photographers)
ca84a358-0e08-5345-bc08-43570cf84e04.archival: 'Woman grinding corn in Sinai', no. 3 in a series of Ordnance Survey of Sinai photographs by Royal Engineers for the War Office Topographical Department. Egypt, 1869
ca84a358-0e08-5345-bc08-43570cf84e04.keywords: Women; stereograph; stereoscope; agriculture; peasants; work; Egypt; Sinai; grain; grinder; topography; photographs
ca84a358-0e08-5345-bc08-43570cf84e04.description2: Many of the most popular subjects of stereographs were of topographical views or of scenes unfamiliar to the western audience for whom they were generally produced. This group of Islamic women from Egypt's Sinai Peninsula is shown grinding corn. Their faces are hidden by veils. The veil turns away the gaze while at the same time attracting it. The secrecy of the veil prompted fascination for what was often seen as the mysterious and exotic world of the East or the 'Orient' to 19th-century western viewers. In contrast, the men in the background confront the camera.

ca9bb919-8384-510d-b5f3-6ce0848cba75.name: *The conquest of Acre by Austrian troops, November 4th, 1840*
ca9bb919-8384-510d-b5f3-6ce0848cba75.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
ca9bb919-8384-510d-b5f3-6ce0848cba75.keywords: St. Jean d'Acre; Archduke Friedrich; Admiral Stopford; Austrian army; Ottoman army; war; warfare
ca9bb919-8384-510d-b5f3-6ce0848cba75.description2: After the blockade of the Nile delta by the Royal Navy and the Austrian War Navy, and the conquest of Sidon, British and Austrian forces then attacked the city of Acre. Similar to Sidon, the port and the city of Acre were first bombarded for one day (November 3rd). The following day, a small landing party of Austrian, British and Ottoman troops – led personally by the Austrian fleet commander Archduke Friedrich of Austria (1821–1846) – finally took the citadel.

cab1d1b6-5bd0-5d68-aaf4-36e8d7c863e4.name: *View of Smyrna*
cab1d1b6-5bd0-5d68-aaf4-36e8d7c863e4.author: Papastratos 1990, vol. 2, 578-79, figs. 617-18; Delivorrias, Fotopoulos 1997, 508-9, figs. 900-901
cab1d1b6-5bd0-5d68-aaf4-36e8d7c863e4.description2: Both this print and the *View of Constantinople* are based on earlier Western ones, which have been assimilated into the distinctive Athonite topographical style. They are exceptions to the corpus of Athonite prints, since they are of secular subjects. The printmaker was, indeed, active outside Athos, where he executed nonreligious commissions. The subjects relate to the tradition of topographical murals depicting important commercial and cultural centers of the day that decorated the mansions of wealthy merchants by the mid-eighteenth century. Kaldis aimed to supply a wider public with inexpensive works of a decorative nature. The activity of merchants from Lesbos at Smyrna, Constantinople, and the Black Sea on the one hand justified the choice of subject and, on the other, provided the appropriate network in which the multiple printed works could circulate. In order to attract the largest possible clientele, the view is coloured.

en: Delivorrias, Angelos, and Fotopoulos, Dionisis, *Greece at the Benaki Museum*, Athens: Benaki Museum, 1997.
Papastratos, Dory, *Paper Icons: Greek Orthodox Religious Engravings, 1665–1899*, vol. 2, Athens: Papastratos, 1990.

caccb7ea-2e4d-5085-b38b-eaad85d82020.name: Bracelet
caccb7ea-2e4d-5085-b38b-eaad85d82020.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
caccb7ea-2e4d-5085-b38b-eaad85d82020.author: Huda Kilani
caccb7ea-2e4d-5085-b38b-eaad85d82020.keywords: Bedouin; settler; village; economy; dowry; tradition; marriage; Ottoman Jordan
caccb7ea-2e4d-5085-b38b-eaad85d82020.description2: Silver jewellery was the most common, because only rich people could afford gold jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom. The Jordanian economy relied on trades and crafts and new waves of people started to come to Jordan and began to settle for this purpose. This object is an example of how traditional fashion reflected the variegated population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is also an example of local personal attire, fashion, costumes and rites.

cafcd6e4-6930-5d23-8538-b552e0f9216e.name: Hôtel Majestic
cafcd6e4-6930-5d23-8538-b552e0f9216e.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
cafcd6e4-6930-5d23-8538-b552e0f9216e.history: This was the first luxury or grand hotel in Tunis. Built in 1912 and designed by the architect Paul Baron in an Art Nouveau style, in the early 20th century the Hôtel Majestic was the best hotel around. It was requisitioned by the German army between November 1942 and May 1943 and became the seat first of the Kommanduntur, then, after liberation, of the American army headquarters. After Tunisian independence and until the mid sixties President Habib Bourguiba used the hotel to receive many foreign heads of states and official guests. Many famous foreign artists, such as Brasser, Barbara, Aznavour, Luis Marino and Bécaud, who had come to Tunisia to give concerts or recitals, also stayed in the Hôtel Majestic.
cafcd6e4-6930-5d23-8538-b552e0f9216e.description2: Located on Avenue de Paris, the Hôtel Majestic offered, from a decorative and structural point of view, something totally new. With its sunny façade and terrace, this four-storey building was the first of its kind in the city. The furniture, woodwork, lighting and the rooms, which opened out onto one another in a modern fashion, were what gave the hotel its charm.

cb48c75d-bd2a-5fb9-9430-da529ee7f01a.name: Bedstead
cb48c75d-bd2a-5fb9-9430-da529ee7f01a.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
cb48c75d-bd2a-5fb9-9430-da529ee7f01a.description2: This closed bedstead is made of a wooden panel, carved and painted with in an arc. This kind of furniture was a part of the architecture of traditional homes. The bed is made of a wooden plank attached to the wall and sitting in an alcove, sealed by the bedstead. This bedstead is decorated with small flowers and foliage, painted in green on a paler background.

cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.name: Tourbet el Bey
cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.history: The Tourbet El Bey monument is Tunisia's largest and most famous royal mausoleum from Ottoman or Husainid times, notable for its architecture and exterior, as well as for its size and number of cupolas and tombs. It was built by 'Ali Pacha Bey II, the fourth bey of the Hussainid dynasty, around 1770. A *kouttab*, a *sabil*, and a large *madrasa* were also founded in association with this mausoleum. This necropolis for the Beys of Tunis holds the tombs of the Husainids and their families, as well as those of a few important members of the nobility or loyal servants and ministers.
cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.keywords: Architecture; Andalusian style; Italian style; stucco; necropolis
cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.description2:
This funerary complex, composed of eight spacious rooms, is set around two courtyards, one surrounded by porticos and another open-air. The rooms and patios contain the tombs of 165 different beys who had governed Tunis from 1759 to 1942. The room for the ruling beys is notable for by its Arab-style cupolas, similar to those in the Sidi Mahrez Mosque.  
A second room is covered by a barrel vault - unique to Tunisia - decorated with wonderfully carved stuccos. The walls, on the other hand, are decorated in an Italian style with slabs of coloured stone or marble marquetery. The rooms are all decorated with faience ceramics, which are evidence of this necropolis' European and Arab influences as they were both imported from Europe and locally produced. This monument-cum-museum houses one of the most important collections of funerary inscriptions.

cb52291b-7b0d-5472-b972-2e4f32848e2f.name: Recreating Assyria
cb52291b-7b0d-5472-b972-2e4f32848e2f.description2: Early stereoview of the Assyrian Court at the Crystal Palace. Based on recent discoveries by Layard, who wrote the guidebook.

cb597bd9-06a6-5ba9-b5db-5eea1c140fcc.name: The disembarking of the first railway car in Libya
cb597bd9-06a6-5ba9-b5db-5eea1c140fcc.holder: Italian Institute for African and Oriental Studies
cb597bd9-06a6-5ba9-b5db-5eea1c140fcc.author: Giulia Barrera
cb597bd9-06a6-5ba9-b5db-5eea1c140fcc.archival: Archivio fotografico, Libia, foto sciolte, n. 749, negativo 5697
cb597bd9-06a6-5ba9-b5db-5eea1c140fcc.description2: The railway in a colonial context was much more than a means of transport: it was a powerful symbol of modernity, of technological superiority of the colonisers over the colonised, and of mastery over the territory. In Libya, the Italians started building railroads from the first months of colonial rule. The first lines, inaugurated in 1912, connected Tripoli with Ain Zara (11 kms) and to Zanzur (39 kms). By the end of 1915, the railway lines in Libya amounted to 180 kilometres.
cb597bd9-06a6-5ba9-b5db-5eea1c140fcc.holding_institution_org: Istituto italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente

cb836758-5e12-5a3f-adea-db7c9212b700.name: *Bisotun, geometric drawing of a bas-relief*
cb836758-5e12-5a3f-adea-db7c9212b700.artist: Engraver: A. Guillaumet; artist: Pascal-Xavier Coste; author: Eugène Flandin
cb836758-5e12-5a3f-adea-db7c9212b700.second_name: Taken from Eugène Flandin and Pascal Coste's *Voyage en Perse*, which took place from 1840 to 1841.
cb836758-5e12-5a3f-adea-db7c9212b700.description2: In 1840, the painter Eugène Flandin (1809–1876) and the architect and painter Pascal Coste (1787–1879) were sent on mission to Persia by l'Institut de France in order to write up an inventory of the country's past and contemporary riches, and to renew the political and economic ties between France and Persia. The mission was directed by Édouard de Sercey, who soon returned to France. However, despite the trying conditions, Flandin and Coste were able to stay for two more years and collected an impressive archive documenting the sites they explored. This is a print of one of the bas-reliefs in Mount Behistun (Iran), which  Darius had carved during the 6th century BC.

cb9aac80-a43a-5209-9eef-9e074e191e18.name: Massacre of the Citadel
cb9aac80-a43a-5209-9eef-9e074e191e18.notice: This is an unedited Database entry and may contain errors and inconsistencies in spelling. We are doing our best to complete the editing asap. If you are in the position to help - with a donation or as a volunteer copy-editor - please contact us at [editing@museumwnf.net](mailto:editing@museumwnf.net).

cba9697e-4726-5cc0-9a64-80be790a931d.name: Fragment of an interior Kiswa Cover for the Ka'ba in Makkah
cba9697e-4726-5cc0-9a64-80be790a931d.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Authority
cba9697e-4726-5cc0-9a64-80be790a931d.dates: Hegira late 12th – early 13th century / AD late 18th – early 19th century
cba9697e-4726-5cc0-9a64-80be790a931d.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
cba9697e-4726-5cc0-9a64-80be790a931d.materials: Lampas woven, red and beige silk
cba9697e-4726-5cc0-9a64-80be790a931d.description2: For four hundred years, the Ottomans sent money and gifts to Makkah and Medina with the Surre procession. The gifts included covers for the Ka’ba, made in Cairo and Istanbul, which were replaced every year. Old covers were returned to the palace in Istanbul, distributed to the faithful or sometimes reused.Textiles like this one were made in Istanbul and Bursa from the 10th century H/ 16th century to the early 14th century H/ 20th century. Woven in red and beige silk, they were intended for draping either the inner walls of the Ka’bah in Makkah or those of the Tomb of the Prophet in Madina. Their zig-zag design echoes that of the main kiswa but the religious inscriptions vary according to the textiles’ intended use. Here, the combination of texts with their emphasis on the Prophet suggests that this fragment was part of a hanging intended for the Prophet’s tomb chamber, which also houses the cenotaphs of his first two successors, the caliphs Abu Bakr and Umar ibn al Khattab.

cbb40c71-7aeb-5535-9a2b-a6c47c378b7d.name: Postcard - The Viaduct between Oraviţa and Anina

cbc34421-cbf1-565d-b4bd-d91bdc792930.name: Rosette shaped part of the *minbar* of the Mosque of Ibn Tulun
cbc34421-cbf1-565d-b4bd-d91bdc792930.description:
The mosque of Ibn Tulun was built in Cairo in the 9th century AD, and was restored and renovated during the reign of the Mamluk Sultan Hosam al-Din Lajin in 1296. One of the most important items of the equipment of a mosque is the *minbar* – originally a raised seat – used as a pulpit, but having also a symbolic meaning as the "Throne of Muhammad". The *minbar* was decorated with stone or wood inlays.  
  
The *minbar* of the mosque of Ibn Tulun was one of the most precious. Its wooden decoration was exhibited at the World Trade Exhibition of 1867 in Paris as one of Egypt’s most significant craft works. After that, important pieces of the *minbar* reached numerous European collections.
cbc34421-cbf1-565d-b4bd-d91bdc792930.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art
cbc34421-cbf1-565d-b4bd-d91bdc792930.dates: 1296; exhibited at Paris World Trade Exhibition in 1867

cbdc629e-10f9-51ce-82d1-89858dea84f0.name: Munchar - arrival of the post
cbdc629e-10f9-51ce-82d1-89858dea84f0.second_name: Société des Fermes Françaises de Tunisie
cbdc629e-10f9-51ce-82d1-89858dea84f0.description2: French agriculture in Tunisia began either through the establishment of large properties by private initiatives, or the introduction of settlers by the public authorities. This is a photograph from the "first phase" - one of the "companies" (of "French farms") had purchased a large plot of land, and employed a number of (largely Arab and Italian) workers to cultivate it. Pictured is a local driver bringing the mail van to the immigrant communities in Munchar (in the Béja region.) This picture was taken to reassure prospective immigrants that they would be able to easily communicate with their families back home.

cbf85605-4ba0-5a95-83bb-a01c29a67fc3.name: The Rosetta Stone
cbf85605-4ba0-5a95-83bb-a01c29a67fc3.keywords: archaeology; Egyptomania; exploration; collection; collecting; inscription; museums; travel; traveller; historical document
cbf85605-4ba0-5a95-83bb-a01c29a67fc3.description2: A letter from General Lord Hely Hutchinson, Commander of the British army in Alexandria, Egypt, to the traveller and scientist Edward Daniel Clarke. Clarke is to ensure the security of the Rosetta Stone which he, W.R. Hamilton and Colonel Turner are acquiring from the French army under the terms of the Capitulation of Alexandria. The letter also asks Clarke to copy the inscription from the Stone. It is dated September 13, 1801.

cbffe8c2-7457-5662-8cc7-208d2edc343c.name: The English Consulate (Ruins)
cbffe8c2-7457-5662-8cc7-208d2edc343c.author: Giulia Barrera
cbffe8c2-7457-5662-8cc7-208d2edc343c.second_name: The ruins of the English Consulate in Alexandria (Egypt) after the bombing of the city by the British Navy in 1882
cbffe8c2-7457-5662-8cc7-208d2edc343c.description2:
The author of this picture, Luigi Fiorillo, was an Italian photographer who migrated to Alexandria (Egypt) around 1870 and opened a successful photography shop. In 1877, he participated as photographer in an expedition to Shewa region (Ethiopia), organised by the Italian Geographical Society, and ten years later in an Italian military expedition for the colonial conquest of Eritrea.  
In 1882, Fiorillo was one of the few Europeans who remained in Alexandria after the anti-foreign rioting and documented the consequences of the British bombardment on Alexandria of July 11th. He collected 50 pictures of the city ruins in an album titled “Souvenir d'Alexandrie: Ruines, 1882”.  
On the back of some photos that he took in the 1880s, Fiorillo defines himself as “le photographe de Son Altesse le Prince Mohammed Toussoun Pasha” (the photographer of his Majesty Prince Mohammed Toussoun Pasha). Luigi Fiorillo died in 1898.

en: Silingardi, Adriano, ”Luigi Fiorillo, l’avventuroso fotografo di Alessandria d’Egitto”, unpublished paper (available on line) for the exhibition of the same name, Genoa, 2014.

cc27cb2b-74b2-53c7-99e4-842dcfe24334.name: The post office
cc27cb2b-74b2-53c7-99e4-842dcfe24334.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
cc27cb2b-74b2-53c7-99e4-842dcfe24334.history: Following the establishment of the French Protectorate in Tunisia, the French administration set up the post and telegraphy service in the Regency of Tunis. The post and telegraph office was created on 1 July 1888. The first Tunisian stamp was issued the following day. Finally, the Hôtel des Postes de Tunis was opened on the 11 July 1882. The first telegraph lines connecting Tunis and Marseille were soon built, and the first international communication was effectuated in November 1915 between Tunisia and Algeria.
cc27cb2b-74b2-53c7-99e4-842dcfe24334.description2: The Hôtel des PTT was designed by the architect Henri Saladin, and built on the Rue d'Italie (now called Rue Charles-de-Gaulle) in a network of straight roads lined with apartment blocks. This imposing building is designed in a Greco-Roman style. The windowless arches and huge wall clock on the main façade hint to the enormous dimensions of this municipal building's great hall. It was listed as a historic monument in 1992.

cc3b74af-a7c4-51db-b788-69489a7072e4.author: Marina Minozzi
cc3b74af-a7c4-51db-b788-69489a7072e4.keywords: Italian sculptors; realism; Positivism; Verismo; social topics; post-unitarian Italian society; health; work; rights of workers; peasant; agriculture; working class; social changes; reforms; life expectancy; poverty; literacy; illiteracy; labour
cc3b74af-a7c4-51db-b788-69489a7072e4.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
cc3b74af-a7c4-51db-b788-69489a7072e4.description2: In 1880 Achille D’Orsi submitted two artworks, including *Proximus Tuus*, to the National Exhibition of Fine Arts in Brera. The sculpture of *Proximus Tuus* made D’Orsi famous as a member of the Italian “Verismo” school of painting. The misery and harshness of fieldwork is represented for the first time in sculpture to denounce the consequences of the brutalisation of the human beings. This clear social denunciation created the emergence of a huge debate over this issue. The body and the facial expression of the peasant exhausted by labour became a symbol of the working class. The sculpture makes a plea for sympathy and pity for the worker right from the work’s title, expressed in Latin. The subject of the painting has been reproduced and copied several times in order to produce greater awareness over these problems.

cc3eb98f-be74-5f38-85da-465d5c36d52e.keywords: Ottoman coins; silk cloth; Atlas; cotton
cc3eb98f-be74-5f38-85da-465d5c36d52e.description2: A rectangular piece of Syrian silk cloth (*atlas*) with a small piece of coloured cotton cloth on the front on two sides. There is a line of Ottoman coins sewn together with three tassels dangling at the end with different stones. Silver was the most common jewellery, given by the groom to the bride as dowry. The use of Ottoman coins as pieces of jewellery – shown by women to friends and relatives – was an indirect reference to the financial status of their husbands. Silk was imported from Syria. Its trade in the Syro-Palestinian area was common because of the lack of geographical and political boundaries; some cities were like twins because of their close proximity and exchange of trade goods and business.

cc673275-b5d7-50ff-bc5e-1a4f9c06e998.description2: Stefano Ussi lived between Florence and Rome and studied at the Academy of Fine Arts of Florence before enrolling as a volunteer in the first Italian War of Independence, during which he was taken prisoner by the Austrian troops. In 1875 Italian King Vittorio Emanuele II sent an embassy to Morocco which included the writer Edmondo De Amicis and the painters Ussi and Cesare Biseo. The innovative international relations policy of the young Sultan Mulay al-Hassan fostered relations with the Italian King. During his trip, Ussi sketched drafts on Arab every-day life scenes which later inspired his larger paintings.

ccd55fea-ff71-54b1-802d-9b86aa9adc8d.name: Records of the tests and of the delivery of the yacht Makook III built by the Fratelli Orlando Company (Livorno, Italy) for the Egyptian Khedive Abbas Hilmi
ccd55fea-ff71-54b1-802d-9b86aa9adc8d.author: Daniela Tazzi
ccd55fea-ff71-54b1-802d-9b86aa9adc8d.archival: ASLi, Cantiere Navale Luigi Orlando, b. 8M2
ccd55fea-ff71-54b1-802d-9b86aa9adc8d.description2: In 1910, the Khédivé of Egypt contracted the construction of a yacht to the shipyards Cantieri Gallinari of Livorno, Italy. This company went bankrupt and its business was absorbed by the Fratelli Orlando shipyards, also from Livorno. After improving the project, the Fratelli Orlando started building the yacht in 1913 and delivered it to the Khédivé Hilmì Abbas in May 1914. In recognition of the high quality of work on the yacht engineer Giuseppe Orlando was granted the Ottoman decoration of the Order of Osmanieh.

cce9ed43-6802-51d5-8553-802e6dafb35e.name: *Siever's patent pedestrian carriage for Ladies and Gentlemen*
cce9ed43-6802-51d5-8553-802e6dafb35e.description2: Many different two-wheeled cycles, such as dandy horses and velocipedes, were invented in the early 19th century. Their underlying principle was the parallel use of feet and wheels to propel the vehicle forward. They quickly become very fashionable amongst the European upper classes, who saw them as a source of entertainment, as we can see from this English print. However, it was not until the 20th century, after many alterations (pedals, etc.) that the "bicycle" became a widespread mode of transport.

cd05b644-c357-52ab-89b2-eb3a5e54560e.name: Parian ware colossus
cd05b644-c357-52ab-89b2-eb3a5e54560e.description2: Figurines based on the Assyrian sculptures were popular collecting pieces. Owners displayed their interest current events. Buyers included the rich and famous, as well as museums. These Parian ware figurines were also exhibited. Winged bull.

cd191826-9521-5bf9-9d19-dd2913e5662a.name: Egyptian vases
cd191826-9521-5bf9-9d19-dd2913e5662a.dates: 3800–3500 BC; bought by Mihail C. Sutu in 1870
cd191826-9521-5bf9-9d19-dd2913e5662a.description2: In 1870 historian, numismatist and academician Mihail C. Șutu travelled to Egypt accompanied by his wife. They took a cruise on the Nile, visited Cairo, where he studied antique Egyptian units of measure for weight (one of his of domains of interest). A passionate collector, he purchased a series of Egyptian coins and antiquities, among which some vessels that are considered to be part of a funerary inventory and have been dated in the first phase of the Naqada culture (c. 3900–3300 BC).

Both buildings were completed in 1573 and richly decorated with tile panels. The palace and the mosque were restored after an earthquake in 1890, and the tile panels were sold all over the world. At least nine identical tympanums are now in American and European museums.

cdc33d9b-33cd-5f2e-9225-8b2a4c860230.archival: Jewry afterwards Valentine, Laura, *Palestine Past and Present. Pictorial and descriptive ... Illustrated, etc*, London: F. Warne & Co, 1893, p. 142
cdc33d9b-33cd-5f2e-9225-8b2a4c860230.keywords: Pilgrimage; pilgrims; Christian pilgrimage; Jewish pilgrimage; Palestine; Holy Land; Jerusalem; sacred places; travel; travel book; Ottoman Palestine; local Jewish community; Biblical places
cdc33d9b-33cd-5f2e-9225-8b2a4c860230.description2: The Tomb of Rachel is another sacred religious site described in *Palestine Past and Present* by Laura Jewry Valentine. The place was equally sacred for Jews, Christians and Muslims, but apart from a short reference to the prayers performed by the Muslim and Jews at this site, the description is devoted to finding the correspondence between the existing site and the Biblical story of Rachel. The site is therefore seen as one of the places revealing the main scope and aim of the book: the discovery of the Christian tradition related to the Holy Land.

ce15a428-c117-5ec8-bdb2-e57a6da94a62.name: Villa Crespi
ce15a428-c117-5ec8-bdb2-e57a6da94a62.holder: Since the 1980s, Villa Crespi has been transformed in a 4-star hotel owned by the 'Villa Crespi-Ca.pri srl'
ce15a428-c117-5ec8-bdb2-e57a6da94a62.author: Ignazio Galella
ce15a428-c117-5ec8-bdb2-e57a6da94a62.history:
Cristoforo Benigno Crespi was a successful businessman active in the cotton industry. In 1879, he bought an estate near Lake d’Orta (Piedmont, Northern Italy), to build a vacation house in honour of his wife, Pia Travelli.  
Crespi had fallen in love with the architecture of Baghdad, where he went to buy cotton, and asked architect Angelo Colla to build for him a villa in Moorish style. Architect Enrico Combi designed the magnificent park.  
After it was inaugurated, the villa became a centre of high-society life: it hosted members of the Italian royal family and even the King of Spain. The Crespi organised theatre performances in the park and invited nobles, industrialists and bankers. At the end of the 1980s, Villa Crespi was transformed into a four-star hotel.
ce15a428-c117-5ec8-bdb2-e57a6da94a62.description2: An astonishing three-storey villa in Moorish style, near Lake d’Orta in Piedmont, Northern Italy. It features a 48-meter high minaret and has richly decorated interiors made with lavish marbles imported from several countries. Construction lasted 12 years. The estate includes a greenhouse, a wet dock, stables, a big fountain, an annex, and is surrounded by walls with valuable wrought iron gates.

ce2320b1-90a7-587e-a23e-2b91e7aba0bb.holder: Kunsthistorisches Museum, Collection of Greek and Roman Antiquities
ce2320b1-90a7-587e-a23e-2b91e7aba0bb.description2: Late antique relief of a woman and a man from Palmyra. This relief was given to the Imperial collection by k.k. Legationsrat Dr James Samson, an Austrian diplomat in the Ottoman Empire.

ce2e2bbf-52d8-50a7-83d7-5ee68152c911.name: \[The clown\] *"Chocolat" entertaining children at the hospital*
ce2e2bbf-52d8-50a7-83d7-5ee68152c911.description2: Rafael Padilla (1868–1917) was born to an African family and sent to Cuba as a slave, where he was bought by a farmer from Bilbao. Once in Paris, he performed as a duo with Footit for twenty years. They drew their success from the contrast between the bad-tempered white clown and his punch-bag in the form of a black clown named "Chocolat", which left parisians, still unaccustomed to difference, in hysterics.

ce785e40-77c2-5e37-a375-478e1a61faa0.description: This engraving is an example of an illustration travel book in the 19th century. These books offered readers a view of exotic and distant lands through richly detailed illustrations. Thomas Allom (1804–1873), the painter of this engraving, was a topographical illustrator who travelled to East Mediterranean, North Africa and China. Allom was also architect, hence the description of the architectural details in “The interior of a Moorish palace in Alger”.

ce8c6cf9-eba8-53fb-82b0-2eb939b70f74.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
ce8c6cf9-eba8-53fb-82b0-2eb939b70f74.keywords: Julius von Blaas; Livno; Dalmatia; Sarajevo; Bosnia; Austrian army; Ottoman Balkans; war; warfare
ce8c6cf9-eba8-53fb-82b0-2eb939b70f74.description2: Julius von Blaas received many commissions from the court and mostly painted portraits of the imperial family. He also painted naturalistic battle scenes depicting victories of the Austrian Army both past and present, like this scene of the occupation campaign of 1878. Here, the Dalmatian Imperial Infantry is attacking in line formation at Livno. The soldiers in the vanguard are already falling. Contrary to the prognoses of the foreign minister, Count Gyula Andrássy (1823–1890), the occupation campaign in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1878 was not just a short “Sunday walk with a concert band”; instead the Austro-Hungarian troops had to face hard military resistance and rugged defence.

cf6fd523-ce44-5925-8fcb-a5eba1bea0a5.name: General Giuseppe Garibaldi, hero of the Italian national unification, arriving in Tunis in 1834
cf6fd523-ce44-5925-8fcb-a5eba1bea0a5.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
cf6fd523-ce44-5925-8fcb-a5eba1bea0a5.author: Giulia Barrera
cf6fd523-ce44-5925-8fcb-a5eba1bea0a5.archival: *Storia illustrata della vita di G. Garibaldi* per Antonio Balbiani
cf6fd523-ce44-5925-8fcb-a5eba1bea0a5.description2:
In 1833, Giuseppe Garibaldi (1807-1882) joined Mazzini’s organization, Giovane Italia, a republican group that supported the unification of Italy, and in 1834 he participated in an attempted insurrection. He was sentenced to death by the Kingdom of Sardinia and fled abroad. He spent time in Tunis in the first half of 1835.  
Later, Garibaldi went to South America (1835-1848) where he fought for the independence of different countries. When he came back to Italy he fought to defend the Roman Republic (1849), and in 1860 led a successful expedition of one thousand volunteers in Southern Italy to defeat the Kingdom of Two Sicilies and unify it with Central and Northern Italy.  
During the Italian Risorgimento, several other liberals and supporters of Italian unification were forced to go into exile. Several went to North Africa.
cf6fd523-ce44-5925-8fcb-a5eba1bea0a5.holding_institution_org: Biblioteca di Storia Moderna e Contemporanea

cf731a2d-eeba-5936-b7db-3a4740cb21ee.name: Print
cf731a2d-eeba-5936-b7db-3a4740cb21ee.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
cf731a2d-eeba-5936-b7db-3a4740cb21ee.keywords: Prints; Entertainment & Leisure; Eating; The Great Exhibition; Menus; Illumination
cf731a2d-eeba-5936-b7db-3a4740cb21ee.description2:
The English architect Owen Jones designed this menu card for a farewell banquet coinciding with the Paris International Exhibition – or Exposition Universelle – of 1867. International exhibitions played an important role in introducing imported styles of ornament. The design of this card echoes illuminated Persian manuscripts, which Jones included in his book Grammar of Ornament.  
Apart from working as an architect, Jones also designed interiors, wallpapers and textiles. He created the interior for the Crystal Palace in Hyde Park, which housed the Great Exhibition of 1851.

cfc8881a-67a2-5e47-b165-244089d5800d.name: Colonial farms
cfc8881a-67a2-5e47-b165-244089d5800d.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
cfc8881a-67a2-5e47-b165-244089d5800d.history: French colonialism brought significant changes to Tunisians' lifestyles, which consequently affected the country's rural architecture. The colonial settlers built their homes as soon as they arrived, and so Italian and French residential architecture evolved from a small hut to a large house. These old, often large, farmhouses punctuate the landscape with their red roofs and cellars, easily distinguishable against the green of the forest. They remind us that the great Italo-French rivalry was triggered by the competition over the best land, as viticulture was their main economic activity. Single-crop farming was used for these grapevines, which were almost entirely wine varieties.
cfc8881a-67a2-5e47-b165-244089d5800d.description2: This farmhouse, belonging to the French winemaker of Grombalia, can be distinguished by its white walls and industrial red tiles, stamped to show the name of their maker and place of origin. The tiles are overlapping to protect the house from the rainfall and snowfall. Contrary to the traditional farmhouses which were inward facing, this settler farmhouse has large windows on its façade and is built on a empty plot of land. The house is east facing and rectangular-based, with four annexes dedicated to the farm's needs, most importantly pressing the grapes and storing them in the cellars.

cff9d211-aedd-5f72-abe6-63319cd03d80.description2: Krste Misirkov (1874–1926) was a grandiose and profoundly nationally designated personage of the 19th century. He lived in St. Petersburg and was an esteemed and highly engaged member of the Slav-Macedonian Scientific Literary Society. He contributed to the standardization of the modern Macedonian language, having given responses to some important issues of the history, culture and language of Macedonians.

d0201dc5-b133-5197-929c-a269917b72e1.author: Mina Moraitou
d0201dc5-b133-5197-929c-a269917b72e1.description2: A publication in three volumes *L'art arabe d'après les monuments du Kaire depuis le VIIè siècle jusqu'à la fin du XVIIIè* is a monumental work by archaeologist and architect Prisse d'Avennes. It was published in parts by V.A. Morel et Cie. from 1869 to 1877. In 200 plates he reproduced illustration on the art and architecture of Islamic Cairo.

d04ab320-9a12-53d1-93fd-cefc444af612.name: Italian postcard of colonial propaganda: 'The Turco-Italian War. The Italian governor taking possession of Tripoli'
d04ab320-9a12-53d1-93fd-cefc444af612.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
d04ab320-9a12-53d1-93fd-cefc444af612.author: Maria Pia Critelli, Giulia Barrera
d04ab320-9a12-53d1-93fd-cefc444af612.description2:
In this postcard we see the first Italian public ceremony during the colonial conquest of Libya.  
As Terence Ranger pointed out in his essay “The invention of tradition in colonial Africa” in E. Hobsbawn and T Ranger, *The Invention of Tradition* (Cambridge University Press 1983), public ceremonies were a tool that was much used by colonial powers. Their goal was to grant a public image of legitimacy to colonial domination. In other words, colonial pomp and circumstance were intended to convey to colonial subject a notion of might and “prestige” of the colonisers.
d04ab320-9a12-53d1-93fd-cefc444af612.holding_institution_org: Biblioteca di Storia Moderna e Contemporanea

en: Hobsbawn, Eric, and Ranger, Terence, *The Invention of Tradition*, Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1983.

d0602307-9a81-587d-b9b3-2b8e93c844eb.name: Al-Madina al-Munawwara Station
d0602307-9a81-587d-b9b3-2b8e93c844eb.holder: Saudi Commission for Tourism and Antiquities
d0602307-9a81-587d-b9b3-2b8e93c844eb.history:
The Hijaz railway was very important for the Islamic world where pilgrims could reach al-Hijaz safe and in short time comparing to what was before. The station was known in al-Madina as *istasyon*, a Turkish word meaning station.  
The station is located west of the Prophet 's Mohammed (PBU) Mosque and approximately 1 km a way, in the region now known Aanbariyah beside Anbariyah Mosque and Alanbariyah Gate, which was removed for the purpose of expanding the streets in the area.  
The first train arrived to al-Madina in 23rd of August 1908 and the official ceremony for the opening of the Station was held a week later.
d0602307-9a81-587d-b9b3-2b8e93c844eb.keywords: Hijaz; railway station; pilgrimage; hajj; pilgrimage route; caravan; sacred places; communication; innovation; architecture; Arabian Peninsula; Ottoman; Germany; Abdul Hamid; abd al-hamid

d0602307-9a81-587d-b9b3-2b8e93c844eb.description2: The station is rectangular in shape with a length of about 700 meters and a width of about 150 meters, and is surrounded by a fence built of black basalt stone, and comprises a set of 11 buildings including the main one. All the station buildings and remaining trains and carriages were restored by the Saudi commission for Tourism and Antiquities and converted into an Islamic museum for the city of al-Madina.

d07a016a-4cbb-5e3f-8479-fd71b40996a8.name: Exposition in Algiers - façade of the Pavillon des Beaux-Arts, in the Place du Gouvernement
d07a016a-4cbb-5e3f-8479-fd71b40996a8.description2: In 1800, the first "Algerian" exposition was held in Algiers, in a building built especially for this purpose at the Place du Gouvernement (now Place des Martyrs). However, this was in reality an opportunity for France to advertise the "benefits" of colonialism - pacified and economically improved, Algeria was apparently now able to take interest in the arts. The review magazine therefore decided to prioritise paintings with an Algerian theme, irrespective of whether they had been created there or abroad.

d07dfd62-b703-5f69-ae57-1fcc78858569.name: Armchair
d07dfd62-b703-5f69-ae57-1fcc78858569.dimensions: Height: 113 cm, Width: 68 cm, Depth: 68.7 cm approx
d07dfd62-b703-5f69-ae57-1fcc78858569.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
d07dfd62-b703-5f69-ae57-1fcc78858569.keywords: Furniture; Exhibition; Art Nouveau; Islamic Art; North Africa; Japan
d07dfd62-b703-5f69-ae57-1fcc78858569.materials: Walnut, turned and partly ebonised, with painted vellum and stamped brass, silk cords
d07dfd62-b703-5f69-ae57-1fcc78858569.description2:
This chair was made in the workshop of the Italian designer Carlo Bugatti (1856-1940). Bugatti’s furniture attempted to break away from historical conventions, reflecting the Art Nouveau appreciation in nature and the aesthetics of Japan, the architecture of North Africa and the motifs of Islamic art. His use of materials such as painted vellum and stamped brass was also adventurous.  
Bugatti’s designs became very sculptural, using bold geometric forms and large areas of sparsely painted vellum. This chair is similar to one exhibited by Bugatti at the International Exhibition of Modern Decorative Art in Turin in 1902.

d0827146-e2b8-5b30-8059-2505a64042be.name: *The arrival of the refugees*
d0827146-e2b8-5b30-8059-2505a64042be.author: Maria Dimitriadou
d0827146-e2b8-5b30-8059-2505a64042be.description2:
The arrival of Greek refugees in Thrace 1922. Photographer unknown.  
The “Convention concerning the exchange of Greek and Turkish population" was signed at Lausanne, on 30 January 1923, by the two governments. It involved approximately 2 million people (around 1.5 million Anatolian and 500,000 Muslims in Greece), most of whom were forcibly made refugees.

d08f212c-1246-5ca4-a5cb-8f7562d35936.name: Farmers and sharecroppers at Munchar with their families
d08f212c-1246-5ca4-a5cb-8f7562d35936.second_name: Société des Fermes Françaises de Tunisie
d08f212c-1246-5ca4-a5cb-8f7562d35936.description2: French agriculture in Tunisia began either through the establishment of large properties by private initiatives, or the introduction of settlers by the public authorities. This photograph shows an example from the "first phase" - one of the "companies" (of "French farms") had purchased a large plot of land, and employed a number of (largely Arab and Italian) workers to cultivate the land. The number of people in this photograph - many of whom are pitifully dressed - shows us that those employed were often large families, searching for work in an attempt to escape the poverty of their home countries.

d1281641-f7a2-5961-be72-73fcc5949104.name: Telegraph transmitter
d1281641-f7a2-5961-be72-73fcc5949104.keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication
d1281641-f7a2-5961-be72-73fcc5949104.description2: The primary reasons for the Ottoman Empire adopting the telegram earlier and more easily than railroads were the telegram's convenience and lack of cost. American scientist Lawrence Smith – using tools sent by Samuel Morse – made a successful trial in front of the Sultan Abdulmecid, who was interested in technological innovations and science, and began modernization of the empire. Due to the outbreak of the Crimean War, the first underwater telegraph line was established between Crimea and Istanbul. This telegraph transmitter (1912, Siemens & Halske) was used in Istanbul in World War I.

d182a16f-df1f-5ece-848d-95d8514da95e.description2: The glazed tile or azulejo is a particularly expressive component of Portuguese art that is constantly being renovated. Between the end of the 19th century and beginning of the 20th century, it is strongly influenced by art nouveau, as is shown by this tile by Rafael Bordalo Pinheiro, made in one of Portugal’s main ceramic centres, the town of Caldas da Rainha.

d199debb-1836-5a98-80c3-90ef128b824b.description2: This mosque lamp may have been made in 19th century Hebron, a century-old Palestinian centre for glass manufacture that managed to survive despite the increasing influx of cheap, mass-produced goods from Europe. While its shape continues a style already popular in Mamluk times, its etched and gilt decoration relates closely to other neo-Mamluk artefacts produced for European tourists at the time.

d1dd52e7-9117-58ed-9803-87a620891cda.name: Moorish gunpowder flask
d1dd52e7-9117-58ed-9803-87a620891cda.description: This gunpowder container, along with other pieces, was taken by Salvador de Foronda, a member of the Spanish Army, awarded for his actions in battle. He was a relative of the Marquis of Cerralbo and donated to his uncle’s museum these exceptional pieces in 1918. These kinds of pieces typically display rich decoration that in this case is hand made in local workshops. As with the other two pieces, both the Moorish dagger and musket, the flask has a fabric rope for the rider to carry it more easily.

d2048b88-33d5-5ed1-89ae-15f1e67d41fc.author: Huda Kilani
d2048b88-33d5-5ed1-89ae-15f1e67d41fc.keywords: Numismatics; Arab Revolt; history of Jordan; world war I
d2048b88-33d5-5ed1-89ae-15f1e67d41fc.description2: Sharif Husayn ibn 'Ali commissioned this medal in 1921 to commemorate Arab independence from Ottoman rule in 1916. This medal was awarded to a man who lived during a crucial period in the history of modern Jordan.

d2105247-15f5-56b4-9a41-1c51ab776885.name: Lamp
d2105247-15f5-56b4-9a41-1c51ab776885.author: Ballian 1992, 80, no. 41
d2105247-15f5-56b4-9a41-1c51ab776885.keywords: neoclassical; Greeks; vegetal decoration; coin; currency; numismatics; tughra; tuğra; monogram; Ottoman monograms; Ottoman imperial symbols; metalwork
d2105247-15f5-56b4-9a41-1c51ab776885.description2: The lamp has a rounded, pierced body covered in foliate scroll with acorns and ribbons that form interlocking circles. The tall, convex neck is decorated with large acanthus leaves with wind-blown tips. From the base hangs a tassel made up of chains attached to Ottoman coins. The three suspension chains are attached to cast caryatids in softly pleated drapery holding plinths on their heads. The influence of Neoclassicism is obvious in the shaping of the neck, which is reminiscent of a vase, and in the use of caryatids instead of the angels which usually decorate lamps. The acanthus, though another Neoclassical motif, is used here with the naturalism and movement characteristic of Venetian lamps of the previous century (cat. no. 71). The lip is stamped with a semi- obliterated *tugra*.

en: Ballian, Anna, *Treasures from the Greek Communities of Asia Minor and Eastern Thrace. Collections from the Benaki Museum*, Athens: Benaki Museum, 1992.

d2153895-57ef-583f-b177-30f75fa578f2.keywords: Painting; Italian painters; archaeology; documentation; research; history painting; celebration of the past; Roman past; post-unitarian Italian society; realism; rediscovery of the past

d2153895-57ef-583f-b177-30f75fa578f2.description2: Filippo Palizzi came from a large family and, along with his three brothers, all painters, introduced in Italy a realistic style of painting which breaks away from academic tradition of religious, mythological or history painting. He depicted real landscapes, people and animals. In 1864 the painter went to Pompei and Paestum where he made a series of studies of archeological ruins discovered in that period from excavation campaigns promoted by the new Italian State.

d27f7bc1-9e5e-581e-a7d7-9666172ce6a8.name: *The Cock Fight*
d27f7bc1-9e5e-581e-a7d7-9666172ce6a8.author: Petar Petrovic
d27f7bc1-9e5e-581e-a7d7-9666172ce6a8.description2: Among the best known of his Orientalist paintings from the Balkans are those of domestic life, such as *The Cock Fight*. In this painting Jovanović builds a credible, believable scene. The spectators are fully engaged, each one reacts in his or her own particular way, consistent with their age and appearance. The singularity of Jovanović’s approach is even more evident when contrasted to Western European Orientalist paintings such as Jean Léon Gérôme’s famous *The Cock Fight* of 1847 or Ferentz Eisenhut’s depiction of a cock fight in 1894. Awarded the first prize at the Wien Künstlerhaus exhibition 1898, and having a great success at the Paris Salon in 1906, it was widely reproduced in subsequent years and was surely known to Jovanović. It is evident that studies of the figures directly from nature inform this painting. Jovanović was not only providing a new and authentic category of genre paintings but speaking specifically to a culture that was his own. In the process, he was giving significance to an area and ethnic groups heretofore ignored.

d320c5a3-16a0-5b02-8130-8a58ce2b34cb.name: Patriarchal College
d320c5a3-16a0-5b02-8130-8a58ce2b34cb.author: Hala Masri
d320c5a3-16a0-5b02-8130-8a58ce2b34cb.history:
Each confession in Lebanon worked on spreading its beliefs and principals. Therefore, religiously based educational institutions were built. In this case the catholic Greek Church inaugurated the Patriarchal College in 1865, and still exists nowadays.  
Many religious education institutions were built in Lebanon, a multi-confessional country, with the aim of spreading the beliefs and principles of the respective confession. This Patriarchal College was inaugurated by the Catholic Greek church in 1865 and is still in use today.
d320c5a3-16a0-5b02-8130-8a58ce2b34cb.description2:
During his reign Gregory founded both the Patriarchal College in Beirut in 1865 and the Patriarchal College in Damascus in 1875 and re-opened the Melkite seminary of 'Ayn Traz in 1866. A western kind of architecture with balconies and balustrades.  
Gregory II Youssef founded the Patriarchal College in Beirut in 1865 as well as the Patriarchal College in Damascus in 1875 and re-opened the Melkit seminary of 'Ayn Trez in 1866. The college was built in a Western style, as seen by the use of balconies and balustrades.

d3253a8b-e29d-5956-a599-90638d365b17.name: The Flood Tablet
d3253a8b-e29d-5956-a599-90638d365b17.keywords: archaeology; exploration; travel; traveller; collection; museums; cuneiform; inscription; clay; Gilgamesh; science
d3253a8b-e29d-5956-a599-90638d365b17.description2: Inspired by Layard’s discoveries, George Smith began to study cuneiform. His dedication was rewarded with the amazing discovery of a version of the Biblical Flood Story. The British Prime Minister came to his lecture. The news amazed the world. The Daily Telegraph financed an expedition to Nineveh to find the missing piece. Having found it, Smith died of fever on his way home.

d33416a4-0a7d-53e7-981b-69aa3e40b575.name: *The Grand Bazaar Istanbul*
d33416a4-0a7d-53e7-981b-69aa3e40b575.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
d33416a4-0a7d-53e7-981b-69aa3e40b575.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
d33416a4-0a7d-53e7-981b-69aa3e40b575.description2: This painting provides a fascinating insight into the activities within the Grand Bazaar of Istanbul during the 19th century CE. First built in the 15th century, its importance had declined somewhat in the 19th century, as non-Muslim merchants increasingly established independent shops in the European quarters of Istanbul rather than staying in the ‘outdated’ bazaar. Nevertheless, in 1890, there were still well over 4000 shops in the Bazaar. This image provides much detail about the appearance of traditional merchants and shops. Men, including some soldiers in European-style uniforms, and women in colourful local dress can be seen milling about the bazaar, their costume revealing important details about their ethnicity, profession and social status.

d3410e10-8985-5cc3-ac90-027e59aa77c9.name: Order of the Medjidie that belonged to Alexandru Ioan Cuza
d3410e10-8985-5cc3-ac90-027e59aa77c9.description2: In January 1859, Alexandru Ioan Cuza was elected prince of Moldavia and Wallachia despite the fact that in 1858 the suzerain power (the Ottoman Empire) and the Guaranteeing Powers (Russia, Austria, Prussia, France, Great Britain, Sardinia) had decided that the Principalities could unite, but were to have separate parliaments, governments and rulers. The double election was recognized by the Ottoman Empire in September 1859. The following year, Cuza travelled to Istanbul to introduce himself to the sultan. He crossed the Black Sea on an Ottoman ship sent for him. He had three meetings with the sultan, who decorated him with the order of the Medjidie and offered him a sword adorned with diamonds. One evening he was the sultan’s guest to a play performed in his private theatre at the Dolmabahçe palace.

d3abd1eb-d054-57dc-92dc-e1b2ea8806d5.description2: Rugs and carpets are an essential artwork category within the Islamic culture. In the late 19th century, Oriental carpets became collectible and valued art objects. The Museum of Islamic Art’s collection of carpets is one of the most important in the world. It was started in 1904 with the gift of 21 carpets from Wilhelm von Bode. The important carpet no 1 burned partially 1945 and was restored partially with fragments later. This specific artwork was created in the North West of Iran before the middle of the 16th century and shows an animated scene featuring animals and trees.

d3db70b3-c132-5835-9372-de3aadb98307.name: Bridal outfit (*entari*, long jacket and shoes)
d3db70b3-c132-5835-9372-de3aadb98307.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
d3db70b3-c132-5835-9372-de3aadb98307.dimensions: Dress h(front): 140, h (back): 158, sleeves: 55 cm; fleece h: 124, sleeves: 52 cm.
d3db70b3-c132-5835-9372-de3aadb98307.description2: This *entari* (dress) is made of turquoise satin embroidered in various stitches using silver-gilt thread. The bridal outfit is completed by a matching *hırka* (long jacket) made of the same fabric and lined with red fox fur, and matching heeled shoes with uppers of the same fabric and soles made of leather. The tailored bodice of the *entari* is lengthened by flaps of fabric that fall over the skirt, giving the *entari* the appearance of a two-piece skirt and blouse. The front of the bodice is decorated with frills. The skirt flares out from the waist downwards. The scalloped hem is trimmed with a tiny pleated frill. The jacket has a round neck and fitted sleeves, and opens down the front. The shoes are embroidered in silver and decorated at the toe with a blue-tasselled flower.

d3ddaba2-605a-593a-84dc-d55cd6a60174.name: Pearl Diver’s Finger Protectors
d3ddaba2-605a-593a-84dc-d55cd6a60174.type: 15 leather finger protectors with cotton bag
d3ddaba2-605a-593a-84dc-d55cd6a60174.holder: Sharjah Maritime Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
d3ddaba2-605a-593a-84dc-d55cd6a60174.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
d3ddaba2-605a-593a-84dc-d55cd6a60174.dimensions: The finger protectors length around 40 mm, width c. 20 mm; the bag c. 250 x 200 mm
d3ddaba2-605a-593a-84dc-d55cd6a60174.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
d3ddaba2-605a-593a-84dc-d55cd6a60174.description2: These finger guards are known as khabt (pl. khabta). They were an essential part of a pearl-diver's equipment, as they protected his finger tips from the sharp oyster shells and other unexpected dangerous objects the pearl-diver might brush his fingers against while searching the murky seabed. Much of his work had to rely on touch, as visibility was minimal and few dangers could be anticipated by sight alone. When not used, the finger guards were kept in a container filled with water to keep them supple.

d3f8650a-4599-5d0e-a22f-cd44a5f3ea38.name: The Pietroasa Treasure
d3f8650a-4599-5d0e-a22f-cd44a5f3ea38.dates: 4th century AD; discovered in 1837; exhibited in 1867
d3f8650a-4599-5d0e-a22f-cd44a5f3ea38.description2: One of the most valuable gold treasures of Romania is the Pietroasa hoard, which consists of five golden vessels and seven golden pieces of jewelry with a total weight of 19 kg. Dating from the centuries 4-5 AD, the hoard is attributed to the Goths. It was discovered accidentally in April 1837 by two peasants who sold it to an Albanian contractor named Verussi. Knowing that all treasures found in the Romanian soil had to be handed in to the authorities, Verussi tried to hide the hoard and even smashed some of the items to make them smaller. Even though he was eventually caught by the police, from the initial 22 items of the hoard only 12 were recuperated. The Pietroasa treasure was first internationally exhibited in 1867 at the universal exposition in Paris, where it enjoyed a great success.

d467849e-57d5-56af-821f-861425864b86.name: Pair of tables
d467849e-57d5-56af-821f-861425864b86.description: Little tables like these ones had an important place in typical oriental rooms for the tea and coffee, and in *fumoirs* (smoking rooms), masculine intimate spaces that proliferated all around Europe, like the Arab Room in the Cerralbo Museum. These tables decorated with geometrical patterns could have been produced in the East Mediterranean, but more likely is an Indian production for the Arab market. The second one, a two-level table, could have been produced in a south Spain or Morocco workshop.

d46c6076-f552-5c09-aeaa-96eb625e9090.name: Lady of Harissa
d46c6076-f552-5c09-aeaa-96eb625e9090.description: Harissa is a mountain village in Lebanon. Located 650 metres above sea level, it is home to an important pilgrimage site, the Our Lady of Lebanon statue, which attracts both pilgrims and tourists who want to enjoy the view of Jounieh bay. The statue, which is made of 15 tons of bronze painted white, shows the Virgin Mary with her arms out-stretched. The village itself is 20km north of Beirut, and accessible from the coastal city of Jounieh either by road or by cable car.
d46c6076-f552-5c09-aeaa-96eb625e9090.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
d46c6076-f552-5c09-aeaa-96eb625e9090.history: The Our Lady of Lebanon statue was built at the end of the 19th century and inaugurated in 1908. A small chapel occupies the base of the chapel, and a huge Maronite cathedral built of concrete and glass in a modern style stands beside the statue. Being a pilgrimage site, the statue has received many important visitors, such as Pope John Paul II in May 1997 and Pope Benedict XVI in September 2012.
d46c6076-f552-5c09-aeaa-96eb625e9090.keywords: Harissa; Virgin Mary; Pilgrims; Jounieh; Sanctuary; Statue

d4c7f9c0-dc66-5391-8685-09943014060f.name: Gjorche Petrov
d4c7f9c0-dc66-5391-8685-09943014060f.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
d4c7f9c0-dc66-5391-8685-09943014060f.description2: Gjorche Petrov (1865–1921) was a prominent member of the Internal Macedonian Revolutionary Organization (VMRO). He was born in Prilep on 2 March 1865. He obtained his elementary education in his native town and attended gymnasium in present day Bulgaria. He worked as a teacher in several Macedonian towns. He worked out, together with Gotze Delchev, the Statute of VMRO. The aim of the organization clearly expressed in Article 1 of the Statute was attaining full political autonomy of Macedonia and the Adrianopole Region. The structure of the organization was also defined as consisting of village, regional and district committees and lead by the Central Committee. Becoming one of the leaders of the Internal Macedonian Revolutionary Organization he shared Gotze Delchev’s conviction that the uprising was not supposed to begin before all regions in Macedonia were fully prepared for it in terms of training of the troops and providing arms.

d4f7349c-29d1-5924-babf-a4c0256713a9.name: Pair of pistols
d4f7349c-29d1-5924-babf-a4c0256713a9.type: Military object; metalwork; firearms; arms and armour
d4f7349c-29d1-5924-babf-a4c0256713a9.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
d4f7349c-29d1-5924-babf-a4c0256713a9.keywords: Military object; Metalwork; Steel; Arms and armour; Pistol; Silver
d4f7349c-29d1-5924-babf-a4c0256713a9.description2: These Turkish pistols were used by the Ottoman soldiers in Lebanon in the 19th century to quash resistance movements. As the Lebanese resistance had no weapons of their own, the fighters frequently ambushed Ottoman soldiers and took their weapons. These pistols are an example of such weaponry, which was taken by the resistance and used against the Ottomans. They are silver decorated miquelet-lock pistols with bulbous butt plates. They are made of wood and cast steel.

d4f761e5-39cf-5040-a028-277cc5dd0f2b.name: Jewellery for horses – Type 2
d4f761e5-39cf-5040-a028-277cc5dd0f2b.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
d4f761e5-39cf-5040-a028-277cc5dd0f2b.keywords: Decoration; Silver; Silver chains; Jewels; Precious stones
d4f761e5-39cf-5040-a028-277cc5dd0f2b.description2: This pendant was used on the horses of Ottoman officials and indicated their high status and wealth. It is made of a single, lozenge-shaped silver plaque decorated with turquoise, burgundy and blue gemstones. Short, thin silver chains with leaf-shaped pendants dangle from this plaque and produce a tinkling noise when moving, announcing the arrival of the rider.

d5128529-40d7-5f5d-b7ae-d2f02acced08.name: Mihail Dan - *Mihail Kogălniceanu*, prime minister in 1864 and a close collaborator of Cuza's

d5146f7c-a989-5ed0-8084-92511311bc67.name: An insurance policy by the company Compagnia Affricana (based in Trieste), for the merchandise transported by the Tuscan brigantine *Otello*, from Alexandria (Egypt) to Livorno (Italy)
d5146f7c-a989-5ed0-8084-92511311bc67.author: Cristina Francioli
d5146f7c-a989-5ed0-8084-92511311bc67.archival: ASLi, Governo civile e militare, busta n. 890
d5146f7c-a989-5ed0-8084-92511311bc67.description2: This insurance policy testifies to the intricate economic relations across the Mediterranean. The insurance company “Compagnia Affricana”, whose headquarter was in Trieste (at the time, under the Austrian Empire), specialised in transports to and from North Africa. The brigantine *Otello* was transporting incense and oxen horns.

d51c4926-dec8-5d72-9ed4-34a107dddbd4.name: *Shipping at Constantinople*
d51c4926-dec8-5d72-9ed4-34a107dddbd4.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
d51c4926-dec8-5d72-9ed4-34a107dddbd4.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
d51c4926-dec8-5d72-9ed4-34a107dddbd4.description2: Istanbul’s geographic position between Europe and Asia and on the only sea route that connects the Black Sea with the Mediterranean gave Istanbul great strategic importance. The control of the Bosphorus, which connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Marmara, was repeatedly at stake in the 19th and early 20th centuries. This 1910 watercolour gives a wonderful impression of the bustling shipping and trading activities on the waters surrounding the city of Constantinople at the time. The view is taken from the Galata side of the city, looking across the Golden Horn towards its historic heart, dominated by imperial Suleymaniye mosque on the right and Bayezid tower in the centre. The Galata bridge, in its third incarnation as completed by the British firm G. Wells in 1875, can be seen connecting the two shores. Sailing boats like those seen here brought in wheat, spices and wood. The emergence of the steamship later in the century lead to enormous increase in the speed and volume of commodities shipped to Constantinople.

d549811b-c5d8-5fa3-9488-5db916492dba.name: *The Dinner held at Delphi in Honour of the Painter by the Elder of the Village at Chryso*
d549811b-c5d8-5fa3-9488-5db916492dba.author: Tsigakou 1995, 116, fig. 7
d549811b-c5d8-5fa3-9488-5db916492dba.description2: This drawing is almost identical to the plate entitled “Dinner at Crisso in the house of the Bishop of Salona”, which is included in Dodwell’s folio *Views in Greece*, (1821). The accompanying text testifies to the artist’s antiquarianism and his attempt to identify classical customs in 19th century life. *“The Bishop of Salona gave us a favourable opportunity of observing some customs which merit commendation as instances in which classical usages have survived. Before sitting down to dinner and after we rose from table we performed the ancient ceremony of washing the hands. Atin bason is taken round to all the company, the servant holding it on his left arm, while with his right hand he pours water from a pewter vessel on the hands of the washer, having a towel thrown over his shoulder to dry them with. This ceremony is mentioned by Hesiod, by Homer, and other authors…”.*

en: Tsigakou, Fani-Maria, *British Images of Greece from the Benaki Museum Collections*, Athens: Benaki Museum, 1995.

d571791c-a497-50be-b648-cbb508ceae8f.name: Manifestation celebrating King Fu`ad I
d571791c-a497-50be-b648-cbb508ceae8f.keywords: King Fu`ad; Fayum Directorate; new roads; The Royal Road
d571791c-a497-50be-b648-cbb508ceae8f.description2: Fayum Directorate Arabs at the reception of King Fu`ad I. Fu`ad I ruled Egypt from 9 October 1917 to 28 April 1936. During his reign, the 1919 revolution began, and the British had to end Egypt's status as a protectorate and declare it an independent country with sovereignty. Independence was declared on 15 March 1922. Also during his reign, the first public ministry was established in January 1924, headed by Sa`d Zaghlul. King Fu`ad had a number of important accomplishments, and for this reason this photo was chosen – to manifest King Fu`ad's concern with roads, especially the royal road towards the Fayum Directorate.

d5ef573d-2a05-5d47-a3e9-ad45caf58169.name: Flag of the St Petersburg Colony of Macedonians
d5ef573d-2a05-5d47-a3e9-ad45caf58169.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
d5ef573d-2a05-5d47-a3e9-ad45caf58169.description2: This flag was the symbol of the St. Petersburg Colony of Macedonians, a group of Macedonian intellectuals who lived and worked in St. Petersburg and shared the same ideas and interests – working for the liberation and recognition of Macedonia. The red colour of the flag symbolizes the blood shed in the centuries-long Macedonian struggle for autonomy. The white rectangle in the upper left corner bears a depiction of a unicorn, also in red colour.

d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.name: Barbadinhos Steam pumping station
d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.holder: EPAL- Portuguese Society for Water Supply
d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.author: Bárbara Bruno
d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.history: Classified as CIP – Setting of Public Interest through Decree. º 1176/2010, DR, 2nd Series, no. 248 of 14/12/2010, the Station of Barbadinhos was designed to raise water from the Alviela river to the reservoir of Veronica and to the Cistern of Monte. Opened on 3 October 1880, the station considerably increased the volume of water supplied to the city of Lisbon. Its main equipment, consisting of four steam engines built in the workshops of E. W. Windsor of Rouen, ran until 1928.
d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.keywords: Lisbon water supply; Steam Machinery; Water Museum; Barbadinhos; industrial archaeology building
d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.architects: Windsor House & Fils and Workshops of CAL – Companhia das Águas de Lisboa (Water Company of Lisbon)
d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.description2: This Lisbon Water Museum is the urban memory symbol of innovation and improvements in public health issues. The Barbadinhos Steam Pumping Station opened on 3 October 1880. It was built to raise the water coming from the Alviela Canal to the Veronica and Cisterna do Monte reservoirs. It was used to increase the volume of the water supplied to the city of Lisbon. The main equipment consists of four steam machines that worked uninterruptedly until 1928. They were built in the workshops of “Constructeurs - Mecaniciens” E. W. Windsor & Fils, of Rouen, France, an English owned company. The machines, whose steam was produced by five boilers, are all of the same kind: vertical pistons with two cylinders each and steam liner – Woolf system – of variable expansion and condensation.

d62a8aad-7189-5f2c-a39f-c9a6febe7aa4.name: *Ancient Istanbul Houses*
d62a8aad-7189-5f2c-a39f-c9a6febe7aa4.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
d62a8aad-7189-5f2c-a39f-c9a6febe7aa4.keywords: Painting; Hoca Ali Rıza; orientalist Turkish painters
d62a8aad-7189-5f2c-a39f-c9a6febe7aa4.description2: Hoca Ali Rıza is known as the first painter who used landscapes in Turkish painting. A study of the artist’s works also readily reveals architectural structures which have changed since his time. Such structures included mosques, fountains, dervish monasteries and lodges, tombs, *sebils* (public fountains installed by charities), ruins, cemeteries, bridges, stately homes new and old, towers, old houses and other subjects which architecturally and historically speaking might have been considered ordinary in his day, but which he pursued with a passion. Riza is completely realistic in his works and he specialized in depicting landscapes using light and shadow.

d6481ac4-6c4b-57b0-a7f3-e97d7469d47b.name: Central Hotel
d6481ac4-6c4b-57b0-a7f3-e97d7469d47b.history: The style of the building refers to contemporary architecture seen in European Mediterranean cities at the time.
d6481ac4-6c4b-57b0-a7f3-e97d7469d47b.keywords: French in Morocco; French in North Africa; protectorate; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic influence; European influence; European architecture; hotel; travel; tourism; city; urban space; changes in urban spaces; colonial city; colonial building; urban planning; colonial architecture; colonial economy; city plan; Moroccan city
d6481ac4-6c4b-57b0-a7f3-e97d7469d47b.description2: A white Mediterranean-style building with three floors plus the ground floor, the facade has an open feel due to the blue-painted, geometrically ornamented wrought iron balconies, which echo designs seen in lacework and headbands. Located on Place Ahmad el Bidaoui (formerly Place Admiral Philibert), on the port side of the *Medina*, near the customs premises, the hotel played an important historical role in accommodating both tourists and officials.

d66e9193-b359-50c2-9fea-50514b0595be.name: Reflecting circle
d66e9193-b359-50c2-9fea-50514b0595be.author: Bruno Gonçalves Neves
d66e9193-b359-50c2-9fea-50514b0595be.artist: E. Lourieux (company); photo by Rui Salta
d66e9193-b359-50c2-9fea-50514b0595be.description2: Reflecting circle wich belong to Portuguese Navy’s Commander Hermenegildo Capelo. It works on the principle of double reflection, like the octant and sextant, with the advantage of its limbus corresponding to a full circle, making possible the measure of angles of any amplitude. This instrument was used in the “Portuguese Scientific Expedition to the Southern Africa’s Hinterland”, in 1877.

d6720426-2881-5b4a-8e11-89649a430aa6.name: *Loie Fuller: the serpentine dance*
d6720426-2881-5b4a-8e11-89649a430aa6.description2: Mary Louise Fuller was an American dancer who lived in Europe for many years. As an artist, she was inspired by her travels and by new inventions - the dance of the veils (the "serpentine" dance) mixes Arab influences with light tricks using electricity. Loie Fuller was an important influence in the Art Nouveau and Symbolist movements, and helped train other great artists such as Isadora Duncan. The "serpentine dance" was imitated by many artists, and inspired the first cinematographers, such as the Lumière brothers, who dedicated a short film to it.
