d68fb94f-f627-54b5-a330-7d4a6b4992ab.name: Portrait of Shakir Shukayr
d68fb94f-f627-54b5-a330-7d4a6b4992ab.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
d68fb94f-f627-54b5-a330-7d4a6b4992ab.description2: Shakir Shukayr was born in 1850 in Choueifat. He received his primary education here, before moving to the Orthodox School in Suq al-Gharb. He was tutored in Arabic by Shaykh Nasif al-Yaziji, and became a professor first at the Three Doctors School and then at the National School. In 1868 he became a member of the Syriac Scientific Association. Author of numerous books, he died in October 1896.

d698b39b-7d12-5410-a70f-c142ce18b236.name: *Servet-i Fünun* Journal
d698b39b-7d12-5410-a70f-c142ce18b236.description2: This is a magazine published by the authors from the *Servet-ı Fünun* (*Edebiyat-ı Cedide*) movement. It was first published as a scientific magazine by Ahmet İhsan Tokgöz, a pupil of Recaizade Mahmud Ekrem, in 1891. Recaizade Mahmud Ekrem agreed with his pupil to turn this magazine into one of literature, so he arranged that Tevfik Fikret, another student of his from Galatasaray High school, would become head of the literature department. This movement came to an end when the magazine was closed after if published an article entitled “Literature and Justice,” translated by Hüseyin Cahit Yalçın, which was taken as hostile to the governance of Abdülhamid II. Members of the *Edebiyat-ı Cedide* movement remained adherent to Diwan literature due to the political situation of the period as well as political suppression. They were not as open to novelties as the first generation of Tanzimat Era and they adopted art for sake of art.

d6cffdd2-cbd5-5bf7-bd67-0a2b5084a2cc.third_name: *Sussidi governativi. Il pagamento del soccorso giornaliero alle famiglie dei richiamati*
d6cffdd2-cbd5-5bf7-bd67-0a2b5084a2cc.description2: According to a booklet published in 1917 by the Tunisian branch of the Dante Alighieri Society and quoted by historian Adriano Salmieri (see his contribution to the volume *Mestieri e professioni degli italiani di Tunisia* – *Métiers et professions des Italiens de Tunisie, a cura di S. Finzi, Tunisi: Finzi*, 2003), by the end of April 1917 11,146 Italians in Tunisia had been drafted for the war, and 700 had died. According to the same source, in 1917 in Tunisia the Italian government was paying daily allowances to almost 5,000 destitute families of drafted soldiers.

en: Finzi, Silvia (ed.), *Mestieri e professioni degli italiani di Tunisia/Métiers et professions des Italiens de Tunisie*, Tunis: Ambasciata d'Italia, Istituto di cultura, 2003.

d6d5f11a-71c5-5934-871d-7aa7c6836d79.name: Henry Salt’s 1817 excavations at the Pyramids and Sphinx
d6d5f11a-71c5-5934-871d-7aa7c6836d79.keywords: archaeology; exploration; Egyptomania; travel; traveller; collection; collector; museums
d6d5f11a-71c5-5934-871d-7aa7c6836d79.description2: On his arrival in Egypt, Salt sponsored and recorded the excavations of Captain Giovanni Battista Caviglia at the Giza pyramids and Sphinx. Caviglia discovered new chambers in the Great Pyramid and a lost chapel beneath the head of the Sphinx.

d6ede956-3098-5ac6-8afc-b9788d8dd31f.name: The first postmaster's office in Tunis, 1892
d6ede956-3098-5ac6-8afc-b9788d8dd31f.holder: Musée des Postes, Télégraphes et Télécommunications
d6ede956-3098-5ac6-8afc-b9788d8dd31f.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
d6ede956-3098-5ac6-8afc-b9788d8dd31f.keywords: Painted wood; floral decoration; Turkish influences; European influences
d6ede956-3098-5ac6-8afc-b9788d8dd31f.description2: The objects assembled in this room all date to the late 19th century and belong to a set of urban Tunisian furnishings. These articles were all part of Tunis' first municipal postmaster's office. They consist of four chairs and a bench in painted wood, centred around a two-layered desk, painted in a floral motif on a pale blue background. Behind, a shelving unit, painted in the same style. This furnishing set shows evidence of traditional Tunisian, Turkish and various European influences.

d70e9882-8463-5f48-be2a-a1278275395f.author: Mina Moraitou

Each chapter is dedicated to one aspect of the arts: architecture, stone and plaster, mosaic, woodwork, ivory, metalwork, glass, heraldry, ceramics, textiles and illuminated manuscripts.

d72b69f9-a4da-50e3-9f8d-3294ff84d9e9.name: The 1861 constitution
d72b69f9-a4da-50e3-9f8d-3294ff84d9e9.author: Bechir Yazidi
d72b69f9-a4da-50e3-9f8d-3294ff84d9e9.description2: Despite the promulgation of the fundamental pact, the new reforms did not, in practice, take effect. The French and English consuls therefore continued to remind the Tunisian sovereign of the importance of judiciary reform in particular and offered to create a senate to assist him in this. Mohamed Bey's successor, Sadok Bey, promised to complete his predecessor's work and create a deliberative assembly. On 1 July 1860, the completion of the new reforms was announced. On 17 September 1860 in Algiers, the bey solemnly handed Napoléon III a copy of the richly bound text. Proclaimed in January 1861, the constitution was put to effect the following 23 April.

d7624db0-56ea-5f6c-a4ec-671242a3d4eb.name: Illuminated Qur’an manuscript
d7624db0-56ea-5f6c-a4ec-671242a3d4eb.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
d7624db0-56ea-5f6c-a4ec-671242a3d4eb.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
d7624db0-56ea-5f6c-a4ec-671242a3d4eb.artist: Calligrapher Hashim al-Kashafi, one of the students of Abd al-Qader al-Rasmi
d7624db0-56ea-5f6c-a4ec-671242a3d4eb.materials: European paper, black ink, pigments, gilding, pasteboard, leather
d7624db0-56ea-5f6c-a4ec-671242a3d4eb.description2: This 19th-century Qur'an manuscript opens with an elaborately decorated and gilt double page giving the first chapter 'Al-Fatiha' on the right and the beginning of chapter 2 'Al-Baqara' on the right. The text, disposed in 15 lines on each page and framed by gold margins, is executed in black naskhi script, with red detailing. The chapter headings are executed in white riqa' script against a solid golden cartouche with blue floral detailing. The verse dividers are rendered as small gold discs. major subdivisions in the text are marked by small red inscriptions or elaborate, colourful medallions in the margins. The last double-page has elaborately coloured and gilt cartouches, the right giving the name of the calligrapher Hashim al-Kashafi, one of the students of Abd al Qader al-Rasmi, in the year 1286 H/ 1865 CE.

d7670c25-7540-57e5-9687-097d572b293a.name: *Moor with oranges*
d7670c25-7540-57e5-9687-097d572b293a.description: Sorolla painted this Moor with oranges in Italy (where he lived on a scholarship), at the end of 1885 or beginning of 1886, long before he travelled to Tiwan, Morocco, in 1919. This is a typical example of Oriental painting made for sale, as Orientalist painting was very fashionable at the time. Sorolla painted mostly Moors and concubines, which conformed to Western ideals of life in the East and not necessarily with reality. Like the main character of this painting, a Moor smoking, wearing the exotic hijab and barefoot, holding an orange in his hand.
d7670c25-7540-57e5-9687-097d572b293a.author: Covadonga Pitarch

d7b44516-bffd-5b76-8377-02433184be03.name: The Cairo Electric Railways and Heliopolis Oasis Company
d7b44516-bffd-5b76-8377-02433184be03.holder: Heliopolis Company for Housing and Development
d7b44516-bffd-5b76-8377-02433184be03.author: Ahmad al-Bindari
d7b44516-bffd-5b76-8377-02433184be03.history:
The HOC (Heliopolis Oases Company) was founded by decree on the 14th of February 1906. Its inception, however, came first in the 20th of May 1905 when the land was purchased and the railway concession was attained by both founders of Heliopolis: the Belgian Baron Edward Empain and Boghos Nubar Pasha.  
The company’s Neo-Mamluk premises were built in 1908, following the designs of Belgian architect Ernest Jaspar (1876–1940). Currently, the building houses the company that used to handle services in the suburbs of Heliopolis like water, gas, electricity, tramways, etc.
d7b44516-bffd-5b76-8377-02433184be03.keywords: The Cairo Electric Railways and Heliopolis Oases Company; Heliopolis Oasis Company (H.O.C.); Heliopolis Company for Housing and Development; Moorish Architecture; Neo-Mamluk Architecture; Islamic Architecture
d7b44516-bffd-5b76-8377-02433184be03.second_name: Heliopolis Oasis Company (H.O.C.); Heliopolis Company for Housing and Development (current name)
d7b44516-bffd-5b76-8377-02433184be03.description2: The first administrative premises of the Heliopolis Oases Company (HOC). The architecture of Heliopolis represents quite a unique and outstanding experiment with form architecture. The neighbourhood's buildings – mostly designed by French and Italian architects – followed the European styles of the time, employing the principal of Eclecticism. Features of Arab, Andalusian, Art Nouveau and Art Deco styles are characteristic of the district.

d7bf5b87-41a9-54ad-80be-78334ba1edff.name: 3 May 1919, demolishing the fortifications at Porte de Clignancourt
d7bf5b87-41a9-54ad-80be-78334ba1edff.description2: Between 1841 and 1844, Adolphe Thiers had a 33km long city wall built to protect Paris. These "fortif'" (fortifications), which were proved to be useless during the war in 1870, soon became inhabited by the poor. It was an area made up of shacks, and soon became a lawless zone. The demolition of the "fortif" began in Clignancourt in 1919, in order to make way for new urbanisation projects and disperse the inhabitants. In this photograph, we can see the neighbourhood children contributing to the works.

d7bf9369-064f-5991-9f23-3b988f805ff6.name: The Emir Abdelkader, Bey of Mascara in 1807
d7bf9369-064f-5991-9f23-3b988f805ff6.author: Dalila Orfali
d7bf9369-064f-5991-9f23-3b988f805ff6.description2: The Treaty of Tafna was finally signed on 30 May 1837 between General Bugeaud and Emir Abdelkader, a fierce supporter of the armed fight against the French expeditionary corps and of the political and territorial unity of Algeria. This followed a ferocious resistance campaign in the mid-west of the country, marked most notably by the victory at Mazagran. The victories at Mazagran and Sidi-Brahim near Ghazouet in 1745, which resulted in the death of many officers from the French expeditionary, have rarely been depicted by European lithographers, who preferred to focus on Algerian defeats.

d7bfd409-e2ad-54bc-aea9-cbf7cee1a22d.name: Bridal jewellery worn on the breasts (*Mingjuska so vot* and necklace)
d7bfd409-e2ad-54bc-aea9-cbf7cee1a22d.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
d7bfd409-e2ad-54bc-aea9-cbf7cee1a22d.keywords: Broad cloth; klashna; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; textile; costume; wedding; marriage
d7bfd409-e2ad-54bc-aea9-cbf7cee1a22d.materials: Klashna - thick woollen fabric, silver coins, silver alloy, decorative stones, tiny beads - *monistra*
d7bfd409-e2ad-54bc-aea9-cbf7cee1a22d.third_name: Mingjushka so 'vot' – nevestinski ukras za gradi
d7bfd409-e2ad-54bc-aea9-cbf7cee1a22d.description2: This piece of jewellery provides evidence on the versatility of articles of adornment worn by women in Macedonia in the 19th century. *Mingjushka so vot* belongs to the group of jewellery decorating the chests, although there is no clear distinction from pieces worn around the neck. This exquisite breast jewellery consists of a rectangular piece of broadcloth – *klashna* – covered with small silver coins reminiscent of fish scales and adorned with decorative stones. It is bordered by a chain, which is additionally adorned with coins. It used to be worn suspended on a chain. Abundant ornamentation with coins was applied on diverse pieces of jewellery and articles of adornment within all ethnic communities in Macedonia.

d7c8788d-6f4d-5251-abb7-406fabefb7b2.name: *Napoleon returning from the Island of Elba*
d7c8788d-6f4d-5251-abb7-406fabefb7b2.description2: Following his abdication in April 1814 due to his defeat at the hands of the coalition between Austria, Prussia and Russia, Napoléon was exiled to Elba, a French territory at the time. He then unexpectedly disembarked at Antibes (France) on 1 March 1815, accompanied by a small army, and went on to take control of Grenoble, Lyon, and finally Paris. King Louis XVIII fled, and Napoléon temporarily regained the throne (the "Hundred Days"), until his defeat at Waterloo marked his final abdication. This image contributed to the myth of Napoléon, illustrating the emperor's determination during his journey from Elba to Paris, also known as the "Vol de l'Aigle" (flight of the eagle).

d8173314-6d92-53ea-81e3-578a39f31c80.name: *Greek Ladies of Smyrna*
d8173314-6d92-53ea-81e3-578a39f31c80.author: Tsigakou 114
d8173314-6d92-53ea-81e3-578a39f31c80.description2: *Greek Ladies of Smyrna* (*Dames Grecques de Smyrne*) is a plate by Jacques Grasset de Saint-Sauveur (1757–1810) from the *Voyages pittoresques dans les quatre parties du monde*, which was published in parts. The plate contains three figures, within rules, with the name of the engraver Mixelle jeune and the heading ‘Europe. L’An 1801’.

d81a90e8-c3be-5aa0-8a9a-b3efa68184af.name: Portrait Album – Ottoman State Officers
d81a90e8-c3be-5aa0-8a9a-b3efa68184af.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
d81a90e8-c3be-5aa0-8a9a-b3efa68184af.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
d81a90e8-c3be-5aa0-8a9a-b3efa68184af.keywords: Yıldız Album; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Vassilaki (Basile) Kargopoulo
d81a90e8-c3be-5aa0-8a9a-b3efa68184af.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in 19th century. Vassilaki Kargopoulo was of Greek descent. His first studio was opened in 1850 near the Russian Consulate. Between the years of 1859 and 1860, he began to attract the attention of customers from all sections of society. He focused on Ottoman clothing and street vendors in 1860.

d86bffa6-0320-50d5-b0a4-c47134d7d642.name: Water pumping equipment in Kağıthane, Istanbul
d86bffa6-0320-50d5-b0a4-c47134d7d642.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
d86bffa6-0320-50d5-b0a4-c47134d7d642.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; History of Water in Ottoman Empire; Water Pump Station
d86bffa6-0320-50d5-b0a4-c47134d7d642.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. Cendere Hamidian Water Pump Station was built by Abdülhamid II in 1902 at an altitude of 34 metres above sea level. With its function, architectural design and mechanical equipment, the station is a unique monument to the history of the architecture industry in the Ottoman Empire. It pumped to Balmumcu and Beşiktaş – in the direction of Tophane, moving water coming from 20 different pipes in Kağıthane using steam pump machines.

d8832d40-d884-5998-a0e8-a3f9f85b3dea.name: The Robert Muawad Private Museum
d8832d40-d884-5998-a0e8-a3f9f85b3dea.author: Julien El Khoury, Jeff El-Msanne, Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
d8832d40-d884-5998-a0e8-a3f9f85b3dea.history: The Robert Muawad Private Museum was a private residence in Beirut's Zokak el-Blat neighbourhood that the Lebanese businessman Robert Muawad turned into a museum. It is located in Beirut's central district, and contains a mix of local, Western and orientalist artefacts. The palace itself was built in 1911 near the Grand Serail, and is decorated with wooden panels dating to the 14th to 19th centuries. Muawad acquired this historical state-of-the-art residence to host his precious collection of fine arts and antique pieces.
d8832d40-d884-5998-a0e8-a3f9f85b3dea.keywords: museum; antiques; art; collection; cultures; traditions; heritage; Palace; Museum; Robert Muawad; Beirut
d8832d40-d884-5998-a0e8-a3f9f85b3dea.description2: The collection, housed in the luxurious Pharaun Palace, contains a vast and rare collection of antiques, books and manuscripts, objets d'art, Byzantine mosaics, Roman marble sculptures, ancient weaponry and treasures such as clocks, carpets, metal work, Chinese and Islamic pottery as well as jewellery and precious stones. The magnificent interior includes original wood panelling dating from the 14th to 19th centuries, and reflects the grand exterior and the palace's setting in expansive and beautiful gardens. The palace was built in the neo-gothic style in 1911 and reflects the Pharaun's infatuation with so-called "Islamic art", especially following his numerous travels to Syria.

d8d34fe2-1034-53c0-ae9e-ca9794a01c63.name: Railway Bridge from Anatolia
d8d34fe2-1034-53c0-ae9e-ca9794a01c63.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
d8d34fe2-1034-53c0-ae9e-ca9794a01c63.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Anatolian Railways
d8d34fe2-1034-53c0-ae9e-ca9794a01c63.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

d8f09c37-b8cb-56c1-917a-f069f4830ef2.name: *The Governess*
d8f09c37-b8cb-56c1-917a-f069f4830ef2.dimensions: Height: 71.1 cm estimate, Width: 91.5 cm estimate
d8f09c37-b8cb-56c1-917a-f069f4830ef2.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
d8f09c37-b8cb-56c1-917a-f069f4830ef2.keywords: Governess; painting; women; children; childhood; teaching; musical instruments; education; work
d8f09c37-b8cb-56c1-917a-f069f4830ef2.description2: The position of governess was one of the few professions open to middle-class women of modest means, but it was often a lonely and difficult life because the social status of a governess was ambiguous. She was not a servant in the usual sense but nor was she on equal terms with the family who employed her. Here, the young woman holds a letter which has obviously stirred memories of home. It may be news of a death in her family - letters or cards with black borders were used to announce deaths. Redgrave had a personal interest in representing the life of a governess: his sister Jane was a governess and died young.

d91bd95e-d043-5ebb-9f83-4ff6245ed95a.name: House of the Robev family
d91bd95e-d043-5ebb-9f83-4ff6245ed95a.author: Nada Andonovska
d91bd95e-d043-5ebb-9f83-4ff6245ed95a.history: The construction of the first house of the Robev family was finished on the 15 April 1827 as witnessed by the inscription in Greek on the marbled flagstone. It was rebuilt in 1863–1864. Construction foreman Todor Petkov built the house from scratch. Konstantin Robev lived in the left part of the house and his brother Atanas Robev in the right one. The two families lived in the newly built house until 1900 when they moved to Bitola and used the house as a summer residence. At present this building houses the exhibition galleries of the Institute for Protection of Culture Monuments and Museum of Ohrid.
d91bd95e-d043-5ebb-9f83-4ff6245ed95a.description2: The house of the Robev family is one of the highlights of traditional urban architecture in Macedonia. It represents the best of the distinctive style of Ohrid architecture, as well as exquisite layout and interior decor. The house was listed as protected architectural heritage after the First World War. It is a three-storied house having been divided vertically into two parts (left and right), thus belonging to the type of brothers' house traditionally built in Macedonia in the 19th and 20th centuries. The distinctive features of this structure are protruding decks expanding the usable surface on the second and third stories. The most outstanding elements decorating the interior of the house are niches in the walls, as well as wood-carved ornaments applied in the rooms and on the ceilings.

d9278f88-7c6f-5ba2-a99d-94b0d6496626.name: Portrait Album – Ottoman State Officers

d9278f88-7c6f-5ba2-a99d-94b0d6496626.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
d9278f88-7c6f-5ba2-a99d-94b0d6496626.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Fotoğraf; Eski Istanbul; Nikolas Andriomenos
d9278f88-7c6f-5ba2-a99d-94b0d6496626.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Born in Costantinople in 1851, Nicolas Andriomenos was an Ottoman Greek who learned photography in the 1870s from Cosmi Abdullah. At that time, Cosmi operated a studio of his own in Beyazıt, but turned the business over to Andriomenos in late 1879, after which its new proprietor soon made it into one of the city's most prestigious portrait studios.

d92eefc6-b8cb-57be-9e74-3bd00aa19302.name: *Théâtre de l'Opéra. "Aida". Avenue of the sphinxes at the gates of Thebes (act 2 scene 2)*
d92eefc6-b8cb-57be-9e74-3bd00aa19302.artist: Engraver: F. Moller; artists: Henry Scott, Jean-Baptiste Lavastre
d92eefc6-b8cb-57be-9e74-3bd00aa19302.description2: Commissioned by Isma'il Pasha for the inauguration of the Suez Canal, Verdi's opera *Aida* was performed for the first time in Cairo in 1871, with great success. It recreated life at the time of the pharaohs, with the details and the plot developed by the archaeologist Mariette. *Aida* was performed in Paris from 1876, with a grand and successful performance at the Opéra Garnier in 1880.

d9708463-f720-5673-ac88-cf01adf12b47.name: *Portrait of a Greek Wearing a Fustanela*
d9708463-f720-5673-ac88-cf01adf12b47.author: Tsigakou 1984, 195
d9708463-f720-5673-ac88-cf01adf12b47.description2: It may depict a notable of Aighion, Andreas Londos (1786–1846) who entertained Lord Byron on his first visit to Greece. The picture is similar in style, setting and pose to that entitled ‘Un Grec de Janina’ in Dupré’s *Voyage à Athènes et Constantinople*, 1825. Louis Dupré (1798–1837) was one of the most talented painters who travelled to Greece. He arrived in 1819. The French artist who was an ardent philhellene published in 1825 a set of coloured lithographs of views and studies of costumes from Greece, entitled *Voyage a Athènes et Constantinople*.

d993a25c-fe0f-55cb-b4fb-77d8dd825454.holder: Soprintendenza Archeologia del Piemonte: Authority for the Archaeological Heritage of Piedmont
d993a25c-fe0f-55cb-b4fb-77d8dd825454.dimensions: Print: 24 x 24 cm; engraving: 14,6 x 22,4 cm

d993a25c-fe0f-55cb-b4fb-77d8dd825454.archival: A. Peyrot, *Turin in the ages. Views and plants, ceremonies in the incision from '500 to '800*, Turin 1965, volume II, Photo 542/16, p.778
d993a25c-fe0f-55cb-b4fb-77d8dd825454.keywords: Egyptomania; Thebes; Karnak; Memphis; papyrology; epigraphy; Alexandria; Cairo; Ferdinand de Lesseps; Napoleon Bonaparte; Vienna; Berlin; collector; Egyptology; Nubia; languages; diplomacy; Muhammad Ali; Charles X; Louvre; Cailliaud; Henry Salt; botany
d993a25c-fe0f-55cb-b4fb-77d8dd825454.copyright: Copyright image: Museo Egizio di Torino - Archivi Soprintendenza Archeologia del Piemonte.
d993a25c-fe0f-55cb-b4fb-77d8dd825454.description2: The drawing shows the arrangement of Drovetti's collection inside the right wing of the building of the Academy of Sciences in 1852. The wall decoration mimics a wall of green stone tiles. The organisation of this room remained roughly unchanged until 2006. The institution of the Egyptian Museum in Turin marked an essential stage in the rediscovery of Egypt and followed the interpretation of hieroglyphics by Champollion. In 1824 King Carlo Felice of Savoy bought the collection of Egyptian antiquities gathered together by Bernardino Drovetti, general consul of France in Egypt from 1803 to 1830, in order to give to the Piedmontese capital an archaeological museum able to compete with all the other museums around Europe. The Drovetti’s collection was donated to the University Museum together with other Egyptian monuments already part of Savoy's collection. This collection already included more than five thousand pieces including statues (one of them is the famous statue of Rameses II), steles, offering tables, wood and bronze objects, mummies, furniture, jewellery, other materials and a significant number of papyri. A catalogue of the collection was made by Champollion around the 1820s.

d9b9133d-3db3-50b8-9527-532bd887cb5c.name: *The Holy Land, Syria, Idumea, Arabia, Egypt and Nubia*, Volume 3, title page: *Temple of El Khasne*
d9b9133d-3db3-50b8-9527-532bd887cb5c.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
d9b9133d-3db3-50b8-9527-532bd887cb5c.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
d9b9133d-3db3-50b8-9527-532bd887cb5c.description2: This image represents the vignette on the title page of Volume 3 to 'The Holy Land, Syria, Idumea, Arabia, Egypt and Nubia' from drawings made on the spot by David Roberts, lithographed by Louis Haghe and published in six volumes by F.G. Moon in London between 1842-1845. It is entitled 'Temple of El Khasne, Petra' and shows the spectacular treasury of Petra as seen by travellers approaching the ancient city through the famous, steep and narrow ravine. Petra had remained forgotten until rediscovered by the Swiss explorer Johann Ludwig Burckhardt in 1812. Subsequently, it became one of the romantic fascinations of European Orientalist artists and writers.Roberts visited Petra in early March 1839, and he wrote that it was 'probably one of the greatest challenges on earth to a painter'.

d9c388f4-ae74-56f2-b3d4-341eda234a0f.name: Panel with a large bouquet
d9c388f4-ae74-56f2-b3d4-341eda234a0f.description2: This polychromatic panel is decorated with an image of a bowl filled with pears, apples and other fruits, topped by a small vase with flowers such as carnations, tulips, sunflowers and daisies coming out of it, which are interlaced with a rinceau pattern of palmettes, half-palmettes and vine leaves. The main colours are blue, green and brown. The decorative style, colour palette and manufacture all indicate a typical Tunisian ceramic, containing a mix of Andalusian and Ottoman influences.

d9cffa1d-0e9d-59ee-a8f9-0f2a12a3c7dd.name: Dish serving for dried fruits or nuts
d9cffa1d-0e9d-59ee-a8f9-0f2a12a3c7dd.description2: Sultan Abdülhamid II founded in 1891 the *Yıldız Çini Fabrika-i Hümâyûnu* (Yıldız Royal Tile Factory) in the garden of Yıldız Palace in order to revive Turkish tile art and give it a new direction and momentum. Vases, hanging wall plates and many sorts of daily-use wares were produced in the factory, including writing and dinner table utensils, card plates, lidded bowls, pans, *aşure* (a kind of dessert) trays, sugar bowls, tea and coffee cups. Many native and foreign artists have worked in the tile factory of Yıldız. One of them, Halid Naci received training in tile painting in Sevres, France after his education at the *Sanayi-i Nefise Mektebi* (School of Fine Arts) and he was assigned to be head painter of the tile factories after his return.

d9f215eb-4992-5ee7-b7b8-cde7536471d9.name: *Guisot* (sic): *Sir, do we have to agree to the reforms? Philippe: No! No! No my friend, not even the slightest reform* \[etc.\]
d9f215eb-4992-5ee7-b7b8-cde7536471d9.description2: Pictured in this cartoon are the King Louis-Philippe and the Head of Government François Guizot. The latter, who in 1848 did not foresee the importance of reform, advised the King to maintain a conservative approach. Since 1847, the opposition to the regime had been getting around the ban on political gatherings by organising banquets. The suppression of one of these banquets triggered the 1848 revolution.

da0ac07d-2149-50b6-a034-3d3ec0987ead.name: *Al-Maryamiyya (St. Mary’s Church), Damascus*
da0ac07d-2149-50b6-a034-3d3ec0987ead.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

da0ac07d-2149-50b6-a034-3d3ec0987ead.description2: This church was a late 4th century foundation, which was, after its destruction in 1860, rebuilt in red brick with the financial support from Russia. Today the Maryamiyya Church, one of the oldest Greek-Orthodox churches in Damascus, is still very  popular and regularly used by the Christian community there.

He was married to Princess Jutta von Mecklenburg-Strelitz and had to leave Montenegro after it was integrated in the kingdom of Yugoslavia after WWI. He died in 1937 in Vienna, Austria – in exile.

db057e21-fbd4-560f-92fe-dac033689842.name: Dar al-Batha (Batha Museum)
db057e21-fbd4-560f-92fe-dac033689842.history: Although the foundations for the Palace of Dar el-Batha were laid during the reign of Mulay al-Hasan I, it was completed during the reign of Mulay ‘Abd al-‘Aziz in 1897. The palace was used for private meetings, receptions and sometimes as a summer residence. The Museum of Arts and Traditions of Fez and its region took over the palace in 1915 and, although the building was altered at this time, the outline of its plan has remained intact.
db057e21-fbd4-560f-92fe-dac033689842.keywords: Palace; royal palace; public space; private space; garden; Islamic garden; gardens and architecture; Islamic city; Moroccan city; traditional city; urban space; urban planning; plan; house; traditional house; North African house; Moroccan architects; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic influence

db057e21-fbd4-560f-92fe-dac033689842.description2: Dar al-Batha is the site of a large palace with two wings (east and west) and separate dwellings located at either side of a rectangular Andalusian-type garden (*riyadh*), which also surrounds the entire main palace. Within the palace are some large rectangular rooms that lead on to porches, at the corners of which are doors opening to outbuildings and annexes (*Douira*, sheds or *khzine*, etc.), and leading to the basement (now the Palace Museum) from which one can access the nearby Batha Square. Two side galleries (north and south) connect the two wings with the main house.

db149753-6678-5bb1-939e-d9e0339d08a2.name: Yıldız Palace Small State Kiosk
db149753-6678-5bb1-939e-d9e0339d08a2.notice: This is an unedited Database entry and may contain errors and inconsistencies in spelling. We are working to raise the funds required to complete the editing; should you wish to contribute please visit our [Support page](https://www.museumwnf.org/atrium_support.php).
db149753-6678-5bb1-939e-d9e0339d08a2.history:
Yildiz Palace, which is the last architectural example of Turkish Ottoman palace, is located on the Yildiz hill in the district of Besiktas. Sultan Ahmed I was the first to build a pavilion, over this land registered at the time to the Private treasury of the Ottoman Sultan as a hunting place sultans beginning during the reign of Suleiman the Magnificent (1520-1566).  
The main construction in the palace started in the period of Sultan Abdulhamid II (1876-1909) and it was called Saray-i Humayun (Central palace). During this period the palace comprised of buildings for private use of the sultan as well as buildings, allocated for the officials, repair shops and carpentry like repairing shop, carpenter’s shop and the buildings of culture and art such as theatre, museum and library. The Palace begun to serve as a museum under the name of “Directorate of the Museum of Yildiz Palace since 1993.
db149753-6678-5bb1-939e-d9e0339d08a2.description2: Small State Kiosk was built in 1901 as the studying and resting kiosks upon the order of Sultan Abdulhamid II. The Sultan was holding official meetings here and it was used for the same purpose by the subsequent sultans. The two storied building has also a garret known as Winter Garden. The kiosk is famous for its ceiling decorations, the handrails decorated with flower branches in the form of elegant Art Nouveau and leaded windows bearing Bonet s signature. Sultan Abdulhamid II was informed about his dethronement in this kiosk. After his residence in Dolmabance Palace, Sultan Vahidettin settled in Yildiz Palace and made his interviews in this kiosk in the armistice period. Mustafa Kemal Ataturk also met Sultan Vahidettin for the last time on May 15th, 1919, in one of the room of this kiosk , before heading to Samsun with the title of 3rd Army Inspector.

db8efe20-85f0-56b3-9f4f-d965040ce729.name: A treaty of peace and trade between the Grand Duke of Tuscany and the Regency of Tripoli, written in French, Italian and Arabic
db8efe20-85f0-56b3-9f4f-d965040ce729.author: Loredana Maccabruni
db8efe20-85f0-56b3-9f4f-d965040ce729.third_name: *Trattato di Pace e Commercio confermativo degli antecedenti tra S.A.I.R. il Granduca di Toscana e Joussef Pascià Caramanlì, Capo e Sovrano della Reggenza di Tripoli*
db8efe20-85f0-56b3-9f4f-d965040ce729.description2:
In order to avoid misunderstandings that could negatively affect the peace and goodwill between the Grand Duke of Tuscany and the Regence of Tripoli, the two countries signed this treaty, with the French chargé d'affaires acting as mediator.  
The treaty confirmed other treaties along the same lines previously signed by the Grand Duke of Tuscany and the Regence of Tripoli. Moreover, the treaty committed the Grand Duke of Tuscany to grant the Regent a lump sum payment (6,000 piastre), providing that the Regent not expect further payments or presents from Tuscan consuls.

db907e57-774c-5cda-a1a5-d1356aa44b85.name: A plan showing the seats assigned to guests at the gala dinner offered by the Italian King in honour of the Ambassador from Morocco, who visited Italy in June 1890
db907e57-774c-5cda-a1a5-d1356aa44b85.author: Giulia Barrera
db907e57-774c-5cda-a1a5-d1356aa44b85.archival: ACS, Min. Real Casa, Uff. Prefetto di Palazzo, filza 107, f. 3 "Ambasciata marocchina. Suo arrivo e soggiorno a Roma"
db907e57-774c-5cda-a1a5-d1356aa44b85.description2:
In June 1890, the Sultan of Morocco sent an Ambassador to Italy (Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi), to meet the Italian King and present him with extremely rich gifts.  
The Ambassador was received with the highest honours. He met with the Italian Prime Minister and with the King, who offered a gala dinner for him.  
This chart shows that at the gala dinner the Italian King was sitting in front of the Queen. At her right was sitting the Crown Prince and at her left was Ambassador Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi. The Italian Prime Minister and other members of the government participated in the dinner, together with the members of the Ambassador’s escort.

dbeedf3f-9b7e-5868-aa07-16d65ca3dfc9.name: Cairo in Milan. Exhibition 1906
dbeedf3f-9b7e-5868-aa07-16d65ca3dfc9.holder: Central Institute for Cataloguing and Documentation (ICCD)

dbeedf3f-9b7e-5868-aa07-16d65ca3dfc9.keywords: International exhibition; Esposizione universale di Milano; industrialisation; celebration of progress; pavillion; exhibition building; city; urban space; architecture; exhibitions and urban spaces; Moorish city; Moorish style; house; interior design

dbeedf3f-9b7e-5868-aa07-16d65ca3dfc9.description2: This series of postcards shows the reconstruction of a representative area of the city of Cairo in Milan for the Universal Exhibition of 1906. The Exposition was organised on the occasion of the opening of the Simplon Tunnel in 1906 and covered a space of over a million of square meters. One-third of the area was filled with pavilions designed by famous Italian architects. The exhibition cost was over twelve million lire. The event drew the attention of over five million spectators and the participation of 35 thousand exhibitors.

dbf4dc13-3f6b-5da9-bf05-cfabe7876ad3.name: Headdress
dbf4dc13-3f6b-5da9-bf05-cfabe7876ad3.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
dbf4dc13-3f6b-5da9-bf05-cfabe7876ad3.author: Huda Kilani
dbf4dc13-3f6b-5da9-bf05-cfabe7876ad3.description2: A silver circular disk with inherent decorations in the carving, and prominent dome above; chains dangling with oval shapes at the end. With two different length. This ornament was placed on the top of a high hat worn by al-Druze (Druse) women. Silver was the most common jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom. This object illustrates the variegated social composition and the demographic changes in the Jordanian territory in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The al-Druze tribes migrated from Syria (Hawran) to north east Jordan in the early twentieth century because of their support for the Syrian revolution against the French occupation.

dc296dc9-ccb7-508b-bd42-c197d02e0db4.name: Çakırağa Mansion
dc296dc9-ccb7-508b-bd42-c197d02e0db4.keywords: Birgi; Ödemiş; house; mansion; sofa (hayat); decoration; wall painting; woodwork; ceiling decoration; vegetal decoration; geometric decoration; landscape; architectural compositions; still life; trompe l’oeil
dc296dc9-ccb7-508b-bd42-c197d02e0db4.description2: This private mansion is one of the most authentic surviving examples of an Anatolian Turkish house with its layout and painted and woodwork decoration. This monumental mansion is three-storeyed and has a courtyard-garden. The ground floor, which is paved with stone plaques, is given over to service rooms. The living quarters on the upper two floors have an outer *sofa*. Among the wall paintings on the exterior and interior walls of the structure are noteworthy panoramas of Istanbul and Izmir. The wooden ceilings and cupboards have remarkable decoration. The structure has been open to public as a museum since 1995.

The book provides a historical and archaeological description of the place, reporting the story of its discovery and identification with the site that is referred to in Jewish and Christian tradition.

dc607c77-31f1-570e-8446-1bb4e69fad90.name: Courtyard house
dc607c77-31f1-570e-8446-1bb4e69fad90.description: The central courtyard would include a water fountain, occasionally a small square garden, and would be separated from the street by high surrounding walls. This particular courtyard is accessed by a relatively low arched door. The main building (*al dakhil dar*, meaning indoor building) is north facing, whereas the smaller outdoor buildings (*al-barrani*) such as the kitchen, pantry and toilet, are generally located on the east side. The living quarters included a central living room and two square side rooms. The central living room is an enclosed shared space, keeping the inhabitants dry on rainy days and cool on hot summer days.
dc607c77-31f1-570e-8446-1bb4e69fad90.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury
dc607c77-31f1-570e-8446-1bb4e69fad90.history:
Older courtyard houses built with clay walls resting on wooden beams began to be replaced by concrete slabs with supporting walls made of *ramleh*, as we can see from this example. In other areas, such as Ashrafiyyeh, the old style was replaced with alternating sandstone and limestone-marl walls, a style known as *ablaq*.  
The *dar* is built on a principle of scalability: rooms were added as the number of inhabitants expanded and thus the building was able grow without any changes to its internal logic. This kind of house became popular in the 1850s, and generally belonged to the city's aristocracy. It was specifically designed to be able to host the same family in the same building across many generations.

dc620fad-84b0-5474-b1ee-8a583440c84a.name: Textile fragment from Archbishop Ximenez de Rada's burial garments
dc620fad-84b0-5474-b1ee-8a583440c84a.description: The textile fragment was part of the alb which was buried the Archbishop Rodrigo Ximénez de Rada in 1247 at the Monastery of Santa María de Huerta (Soria, Spain). The tomb was opened at the beginning of the decade of 1880 at the request of the Master of Sigüenza. The fragment was found in the coffin and the master give it to the Marquis of Cerralbo, who was present. After this event, because of the importance of the Archbishop garments and the marquis’ interest in the history of the Monastery, the marquis paid all the expenses of two new openings of the grave. The first one in 1886 for the Spanish Royal Academy of the History researches, and the second one in 1907 for his own studio, when he completed the description of the garments and took photographs to his publication in 1908.
dc620fad-84b0-5474-b1ee-8a583440c84a.dates: 13th century, before 1247; discovered at the beginning of the decade of 1880
dc620fad-84b0-5474-b1ee-8a583440c84a.author: Rebeca C. Recio

dc9bec02-eb7b-5be5-b697-9d2faab3da93.name: *La Mhalla* (painting)
dc9bec02-eb7b-5be5-b697-9d2faab3da93.holder: Palais de la Rose – Musée de l’Armée
dc9bec02-eb7b-5be5-b697-9d2faab3da93.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
dc9bec02-eb7b-5be5-b697-9d2faab3da93.description2: This oil on canvas by Bertrand de Moynier depicts the disembarkment of the *mhalla*, the field army, in the mid-19th century for the collection of taxes. The *mhalla*, a military term, was made up of soldiers, *mamluks*, civil servants, merchants and artisans, which were split into three categories: infantry, cavalry and artillery. This army was supported by informal troops and horsemen from local tribes. The beylical tent has been erected in the centre of the mhalla, next to the service tents for the bey's personnel and the tents for the administrative and fiscal representatives. The future 'Ali Bey III (1882–1902) can be seen in the centre of the painting, in front of the red and green flags.

dd685f6f-e2d6-5e02-846e-ac9afcd7f6a4.keywords: Decoration; Silver; Silver chains; Jewels; Precious stones; Necklace
dd685f6f-e2d6-5e02-846e-ac9afcd7f6a4.description2: This necklace was used on the horses of Ottoman officials and indicated their high status and wealth. The chain consists of fifteen silver squares with sawtooth framing, connected to a smaller rectangular silver piece and three dangling silver bells. The silver squares are decorated with red coral semi-precious gemstones arranged in a circular shape. The bells would make a tinkling noise and announce the arrival of the rider.

ddc859b5-2660-59d5-a43e-bea3692d92db.name: Italian stonecutters in Tunisia
ddc859b5-2660-59d5-a43e-bea3692d92db.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 25
ddc859b5-2660-59d5-a43e-bea3692d92db.description2: At the turn of the twentieth century, the Italian community in Tunisia included large numbers of masons, stonecutters, diggers and other manual workers. In this period, most of Italian migrants preferred to seek their fortunes in the Americas and in other European countries. Those who migrated to North Africa were only a small percentage, nonetheless they amounted to dozens of thousands.

ddd75581-2e37-5baa-8483-63c54f368af5.name: Dress
ddd75581-2e37-5baa-8483-63c54f368af5.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
ddd75581-2e37-5baa-8483-63c54f368af5.author: Huda Kilani
ddd75581-2e37-5baa-8483-63c54f368af5.description2: Long black silk dress (*malas*), narrow at the waist, wide at the bottom, embroidered with cross-stitch dark blue and red on the chest and on the front side, worn by women of the al-Druze tribes, with a shirt underneath. This object illustrates the variegated composition and the demographic changes of the Jordan population in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It also shows how the different populations brought with them their fashion, costumes and rites which contributed to the multifaceted social and cultural heritage of Jordan. The al-Druze tribes migrated from Syria (Hawran) to northeast Jordan in the early twentieth century because of their support for the Syrian revolution against the French occupation.

dde582f0-5bed-53bd-adaa-91e404fab4de.name: Orfella. The kaimacan Mohàmmed-el-Jesir [Qaimaqan Muhammad al-Jazir] and Notables Observe Studies on Subterranean Water of Wadi Beni Ulid Requested from the Italian Mission

dde582f0-5bed-53bd-adaa-91e404fab4de.third_name: *Orfella. Il kaimacan Mohàmmed-el-Jesir ed i notabili assistono agli studi chiesti alla missione sulle acque sotterranee dell’uadi Beni-Ulid*
dde582f0-5bed-53bd-adaa-91e404fab4de.second_name: Local authorities observing the work of the Italian mission headed by Ignazio Sanfilippo
dde582f0-5bed-53bd-adaa-91e404fab4de.description2: In 1911, right before the beginning of Italy’s colonial war in Libya, an expert in sulphur mining, Ignazio Sanfilippo, headed a mission to Libya to look for mineral resources (in particular, for sulphur mines). The mission was sponsored by the Libyan branch of the Banca di Roma (one of the most important Italian banks, which supported Italian colonial expansion in Libya), and it was encouraged by the Italian government. In 1910, Sanfilippo had already headed another Italian mission to Libya. He had been secretly charged by the Minister of Foreign Affairs to look for sulphur mines and the Banca di Roma had helped organising the mission.

ddeb963b-beac-5725-a081-6afda69f1c6f.name: Moroccan coins
ddeb963b-beac-5725-a081-6afda69f1c6f.description: For a century (1800-1900), the ‘Alawid sultans struck coins in the workshops of Fez, but due to the economic crisis at the time, gold was unavailable so most coins were of silver, bronze or other common metals – although the technique remained the same, with the metal poured into moulds. The patterns on the face and on the back vary between the star with eight points (Solomon ring) and the indication of the place of mint.

de6e2f8b-9a8b-550e-bef8-94cf2f8b25ed.provenance: Egypt, Valley of the Kings, tomb of Pharaoh Sethy Ist (XIX Dynasty)
de6e2f8b-9a8b-550e-bef8-94cf2f8b25ed.author: Marina Minozzi
de6e2f8b-9a8b-550e-bef8-94cf2f8b25ed.keywords: Campaign in Egypt; Egyptomania; archaeology; Leopoldo II; Charles X; scientific expedition; university; museums; collection; collector; Florence; Pisa; Egyptology; Nubia; Thebes; languages; hieroglyph; epigraphy; Orientalist; travelling artist; botany

de6e2f8b-9a8b-550e-bef8-94cf2f8b25ed.description2: The fragment comes from the parietal relief from the tomb of Sethy I (1289-1279 A.C.), discovered in 1817 and located in the Valley of the Kings. The relief is part of one of the most important group of the Franco-Tuscan expedition (1828–1829) and has been brought to Florence by Ippolito Roselllini. The relief shows the goddess Maat, recognised by the feather on her head.

en: Guidotti M.C., “Ippolito Rosellini e la Spedizione franco-toscana”, in *Ricerche di Storia dell’arte* 100, 2010, Rome: Carocci, 2010: 43–47.

de834889-8d91-5a45-91c0-917eb5e7de6f.name: Ceramic panel with eight azulejos [tiles] (from the Odescalchi collection)
de834889-8d91-5a45-91c0-917eb5e7de6f.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
de834889-8d91-5a45-91c0-917eb5e7de6f.author: Marina Minozzi
de834889-8d91-5a45-91c0-917eb5e7de6f.keywords: Applied arts; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; model; reproduction; motifs; collector; Spain; Moorish; Islamic art; Islamic influence; Neo-Mudéjar style; production of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode; Manises
de834889-8d91-5a45-91c0-917eb5e7de6f.third_name: Pannello ceramico con otto azulejos (dalla collezione Odescalchi)
de834889-8d91-5a45-91c0-917eb5e7de6f.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, as part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". The collections of the M.A.I. included large samples of pottery, wooden objects, fabric, bronzes and ivories dating to Roman, Renaissance and Baroque times. The best part of this collection is on display at the National Gallery of Palazzo Barberini in Rome, while other pieces are housed in Castel Sant'Angelo and Palazzo Venezia. Within the series of the Hispanic-Moorish ceramics are some pottery with azulejos, bought by Prince Baldassarre Ladislao Odescalchi in 1880. The panel with eight azulejos dates from 15th and 16th centuries. It shows both geometric and floral decorations.

deb4b3a7-5e57-5235-b533-346c36e88be2.name: *Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey* (1784–1839)
deb4b3a7-5e57-5235-b533-346c36e88be2.keywords: Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey; Egypt; Janissary; Konya; Ibrahim Pasha; Muhammad Ali; Greece
deb4b3a7-5e57-5235-b533-346c36e88be2.description2:
Portrait of Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey (1784–1839). In 1826 Mahmud II initiated the development of a modern army. This led to the uprising of the Janissary, which was quelled by massacring the rebellious troops. Under Mahmud II's reign, in 1821 the Greeks started their fight for freedom which was granted to them in the Peace of Adrianople in 1829.  
After the destruction of the Janissary, the Ottoman Empire under Sultan Mahmud II had only 35,000 badly trained regular soldiers in 1827. Due to the weakness of the Ottoman Empire, Ibrahim Pasha, the son of Muhammad 'Ali (ruler of Egypt), invaded Syria. On 20 February 1832, the Egyptian Army defeated the Ottoman Army at the Battle of Konya. This forced Mahmud II to sign the Peace of Kütahya and to cede Syria and Kilikia to Egypt.

deea46be-8061-564e-a1de-c2f20389f8a7.name: *Ayasofya (Hagia Sophia)*
deea46be-8061-564e-a1de-c2f20389f8a7.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
deea46be-8061-564e-a1de-c2f20389f8a7.keywords: Painting; Hüseyin Zekai Paşa; orientalist Turkish painters
deea46be-8061-564e-a1de-c2f20389f8a7.description2: The majority of Turkish painters in the 19th century were Ottoman officers who had studied abroad. Hüseyin Zekai Paşa was one of those painters who paints in the western style. In his first works, he followed the painting tradition of 19th century by including thin paint dough and light colours. He made changes in his painting techniques through the Galatasaray Exhibition and turned into an impressionist, his work dominated by thicker brush strokes. In his paintings he combined impressionist colour techniques and a totality of composition with dexterity. Şeker Ahmet Paşa, Osman Hamdi Bey and Hüseyin Zekai Paşa opened the way for other Turkish artists – and in particular impressionists – in Turkey.

df2df39f-10d6-5018-8f8a-0c38e886c096.name: *View of Cairo*
df2df39f-10d6-5018-8f8a-0c38e886c096.author: Dalila Orfali
df2df39f-10d6-5018-8f8a-0c38e886c096.description2: Émile Bernard is known first and foremost for his friendship with the artist Paul Gaugin within the movement often known as the Pont-Aven school. He is known only secondly as an artist of the symbolist movement, along with Odilon Redon. This painting reveals a little-known aspect of the painter's career, namely that he spent some time in Cairo where he mostly painted cafés and theatres. This Egyptian work by Émile Bernard is therefore rare enough to be considered one of the collection's most important works.

dfc4cc0b-d5f3-5aa9-a482-5dd72c63bdf8.name: Map of the Red Sea
dfc4cc0b-d5f3-5aa9-a482-5dd72c63bdf8.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
dfc4cc0b-d5f3-5aa9-a482-5dd72c63bdf8.archival: *The Red Sea Pilot ... With directions for the navigation of the Suez Canal. Second edition. \[Compiled by J. C. Richards\]*, *Sailing Directions. Red Sea*, London: Hydrographic Office, 1883, third edition
dfc4cc0b-d5f3-5aa9-a482-5dd72c63bdf8.keywords: Trade; route; port; Great Britain; India; coffee; Red Sea; Yemen; Mocha; British settlement on the route to India; communication; telegraph; telegraph between ports; Suez Canal; pilgrimage; Makka; Arab Peninsula; Holy places
dfc4cc0b-d5f3-5aa9-a482-5dd72c63bdf8.description2:
*The Red Sea Pilot* included sailing indications and directions for navigation from the Suez Canal to the strait of Bab el-Mandeb, including Aqaba, Jeddah and the coast of Hijaz as far as Aden.  
  
Trading activity (especially in grain) between the two coasts of the Red Sea and the maritime traffic after the opening of the Suez Canal were fundamental economic activities, hence the importance of reliable knowledge of navigation routes, sailing directions, climate, winds and currents. In addition to the local ships used to carry pilgrims to Mecca and for trading activity, European ships crossed the Red Sea. The book also provides information about the main ports and their facilities. For example, it states that the telegraph had been installed from Suez to Swakin and from Swakin to Jeddah, and that there was telegraph communication between Aden, Suez, Bombay and the Cape of Good Hope.

dfd2eeea-301b-506a-85f9-f9ad927ce8f2.name: Dress
dfd2eeea-301b-506a-85f9-f9ad927ce8f2.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
dfd2eeea-301b-506a-85f9-f9ad927ce8f2.author: Huda Kilani
dfd2eeea-301b-506a-85f9-f9ad927ce8f2.keywords: Dress; machine embroidery; patterns; custmes and rites; Ottoman coins
dfd2eeea-301b-506a-85f9-f9ad927ce8f2.materials: Chinese cotton, silver coins; machine weaving, machine embroidery
dfd2eeea-301b-506a-85f9-f9ad927ce8f2.description2: Women's costumes of the central regions of Jordan are characterized by length, dark colours, light vertical strips of embroidery and very long sleeves. This black and blue dress has a very loose fitting, open chest and long flared sleeves pulled over a head band. The length of the dress was adjusted to the height of the woman by a sash. Wide at the bottom, it is decorated horizontally with blue cotton stripes and vertically with embroidery lines and Ottoman coins. The traditional costumes reflect the variegated population composition and demographic changes of the late 19th century-early 20th century Jordanian territory, when new waves of people arrived and settled for the purpose of trades and crafts. Craft was not limited to the everyday life and the profits from crafts were a source of income.

dfd5b69e-9c27-52e5-93bf-9d6d1a4fd259.name: Tekke panel
dfd5b69e-9c27-52e5-93bf-9d6d1a4fd259.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
dfd5b69e-9c27-52e5-93bf-9d6d1a4fd259.materials: Rokoko ornament on paper, art of illumination on bordure
dfd5b69e-9c27-52e5-93bf-9d6d1a4fd259.description2: A *tekke* (dervish lodge) plate with *celi sülüs* calligraphy in the shape of a bird made with black ink. It reads *"Yâ Bâz el-eşheb Kuddise sırruhu Şey'en lȋ'l-lâh"* (religious text, untranslatable). On the upper right corner there is a date and signature together with a bouquet of rose, tulip and rosebuds. The plate is framed in rose colour.

dfe6ce78-8f49-57a2-8d22-f6a5967fc725.name: *Constantinople et le Bosphore de Thrace*
dfe6ce78-8f49-57a2-8d22-f6a5967fc725.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. Travelling in the 19th century became easier and more reliable due to the advent of steamships and trains. Westerners travelled to the East not only for touristic purposes, but also for scientific research, history, archaeology or for religious reasons. Western travellers told of their experiences and what they saw in eastern countries in their travel books and they even offer advice about the journey. Istanbul, where East and West meet, has been the subject of many a traveller's book.

dfe6e123-1970-5707-8279-08002d40fd1f.name: Ottoman Clothing Album
dfe6e123-1970-5707-8279-08002d40fd1f.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
dfe6e123-1970-5707-8279-08002d40fd1f.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
dfe6e123-1970-5707-8279-08002d40fd1f.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
dfe6e123-1970-5707-8279-08002d40fd1f.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

dff63501-6388-5281-9baf-bb1a3d253e7f.author: Huda Kilani
dff63501-6388-5281-9baf-bb1a3d253e7f.keywords: goats gut; animals skin; horse hair
dff63501-6388-5281-9baf-bb1a3d253e7f.materials: Wood, animals skin; handmade and hand painted
dff63501-6388-5281-9baf-bb1a3d253e7f.description2: Four pieces of wood formed into a rectangular shape; the top and bottom are covered with animal skin and joined with goat’s intestines. The rababa is played with a bow consisting of an arched stick with horse hair. The rababa is a musical instrument widely used in the Bedouin tradition. Music played in communal setting is an essential part of the traditions in Bedouin communities for leisure at communal gatherings.

e04ca700-4cef-584a-b2aa-bf9feabea8a0.name: Université Saint-Joseph (USJ)
e04ca700-4cef-584a-b2aa-bf9feabea8a0.description: Jesuits were very active in Lebanon in the 19th century. They founded a small school in Beirut in 1839, and then a larger school in Ghazir (Keserwan) in 1855, which would be moved to Beirut in 1875 and become the Saint Joseph University. It was granted the title of "university" by the local authorities, which allowed it to issue academic degrees, mainly doctoral degrees in philosophy and theology. Various faculties were founded soon after, such as the Institute of Medicine in 1883, which would become the Faculty of Medicine in 1888, and the Faculty of Medicine and Pharmacy a year later. A Maternity clinic opened in 1896, followed by the Oriental College in 1902 and the School for French Law in 1913, which became the Faculty of Law in 1946. The French School in Engineering was also founded in 1913, and became the Higher Institute for Engineering in 1948.
e04ca700-4cef-584a-b2aa-bf9feabea8a0.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
e04ca700-4cef-584a-b2aa-bf9feabea8a0.history: The Université Saint-Joseph (USJ) in Beirut evolved from a seminary founded by Jesuits in Ghazir in 1843. The Collège in Ghazir, intended to train the local Maronite clergy, relocated to Beirut in 1875 where it took the name of Saint Joseph University.

e055e6ed-ffba-5b33-a42a-7f9060dc3802.name: Paul Draneht, his wife Adele Casati and their daughter Despina
e055e6ed-ffba-5b33-a42a-7f9060dc3802.author: Massimiliano Cremona, Ignazio Galella
e055e6ed-ffba-5b33-a42a-7f9060dc3802.description2:
Paul Draneht (1815-1894) was born in Nicosia (Cyprus) as Pavlos Pavlidis. He was the child of a Greek Christian Orthodox family who fled Cyprus to escape the clashes between Greeks and Turks and then took refuge in Egypt.  
The Khedive of Egypt sent him to study in France. He later had a brilliant career in service to the Khedive participating in the negotiations on the opening of the Suez Canal. He became superintendent of the Egyptian Opera Theatre and commissioned the opera Aida to the Italian composer Giuseppe Verdi.  
Paul Draneht married Adelaide Casati, the daughter of a cello player who performed at the Aida premiere. Their daughter Despina Draneht married a Greek businessman, Emmanuel Zervudachi.

e06ef895-2b01-5e26-b048-45ebf4f4ecc7.name: Palace of Monserrate
e06ef895-2b01-5e26-b048-45ebf4f4ecc7.holder: Sintra Parks Monte da Lua, Conservation Company
e06ef895-2b01-5e26-b048-45ebf4f4ecc7.author: Carlos Marques, Cristina Correia
e06ef895-2b01-5e26-b048-45ebf4f4ecc7.history: The Monserrate estate, known as the Quinta da Boa Vista,  goes back to the 16th century, belonging to the Royal All Saints Hospital as a source of revenue. The name Monserrate comes from the 1540 chapel dedicated to Our Lady of Montserrat. Formerly owned  by Beckford’s, then by the Melo e Castro family, in 1841, at the end of his grand tour, Francis Cook stops in Lisbon and marries the daughter of an English merchant. He discovers Sintra during his honeymoon and fascinated by Monserrate, manages to purchase it and starts its rehabilitation. The ensemble belonged to the Cook family until 1929. In 1947, it is sold to antiques dealer Saul Sárraga who sells in auction the contents of the palace and tries to divide the estate leading to the acquisition by the Portuguese State, in 1949.
e06ef895-2b01-5e26-b048-45ebf4f4ecc7.keywords: Sintra; Romanticism; William Beckford; Neo-Moorish; Eclecticism
e06ef895-2b01-5e26-b048-45ebf4f4ecc7.architects: Architect: James Thomas Knowles; Landscape architect: William Colebrooke Stockdale; Master gardener: Francis James Burt
e06ef895-2b01-5e26-b048-45ebf4f4ecc7.description2:
The Palace of Monserrate is a key example of Portuguese romanticism, due to its eclecticism blending Venetian Gothic influences with those of India and the Moors. The building is a landmark in the landscape, with its distinctive profile punctuated by three towers, perfectly framed with the surrounding gardens.  
The former building’s volumetry, two cylindrical turrets, horizontal galleries and a square-based central turret, the windows with Gothic arches are combined to the 19th century influences of Venetian palaces and a decorative composition of vegetative motifs. The stuccoes of the Corridor of the palace of Monserrate are inspired by the ones of Alhambra Palace in Granada whereby the several columns is thought to recall those of the Hypostyle Hall of the Cordova Mosque.

e18d88ea-cdd3-514a-a77b-17670ead2f02.name: *Jews’ Place of Wailing, Jerusalem*
e18d88ea-cdd3-514a-a77b-17670ead2f02.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
e18d88ea-cdd3-514a-a77b-17670ead2f02.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
e18d88ea-cdd3-514a-a77b-17670ead2f02.artist: Drawn by William Henry Bartlett; engraved by Ebenezar Challis
e18d88ea-cdd3-514a-a77b-17670ead2f02.description2: The wailing wall is situated at the foot of the western side of the Temple Mount/ Haram al-Sharif in Jerusalem, sacred to Jews, Christians and Muslims. It has been a site for Jewish prayer and pilgrimage for centuries. From the mid-19th century onwards, several unsuccessful attempts to purchase rights to the wall and its immediate area were made by Jews. With the rise of the Zionist movement in the early 20th century, the wall became a source of friction between the Jewish community and the Muslim religious leadership, who were worried that the wall was being used to further Jewish nationalistic claims to the Temple Mount/Haram al-Sharif and Jerusalem.This print first appeared (facing p. 140) in 'Walks about the City and Environs of Jerusalem. And: Forty Days in the Desert on the Track of the Israelites, a publication created in two volumnes by the writer and artist W. H. Bartlett and the engraver Ebenezar Challis. The work, based on Bartlett's visit to Jerusalem in the summer of 1842, was first published in London around 1850 by Arthur Hal, Virtue and Co.

e19b330e-2bba-52d4-86d4-2f8b8d208303.name: Dr Joseph Hariz, doctoral thesis in medicine
e19b330e-2bba-52d4-86d4-2f8b8d208303.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
e19b330e-2bba-52d4-86d4-2f8b8d208303.description2: Pictured here is the cover of a doctoral thesis in medicine written by Joseph Hariz, a Jewish Tunisian doctor at l’Université de Marseille, in 1922. In the early 20th century, the Beylik of Tunis contained 170 qualified doctors, 81 of which were French, 83 were foreigners, and 6 Tunisian, with 2 Muslims and 4 Jews.

e1b84d6c-9cc4-503f-aaf7-19adce734645.name: Petra
e1b84d6c-9cc4-503f-aaf7-19adce734645.type: World Heritage Site; archaeological site; Nabatean city
e1b84d6c-9cc4-503f-aaf7-19adce734645.author: Mohammad Najjar
e1b84d6c-9cc4-503f-aaf7-19adce734645.history: Petra's history goes back to prehistoric times, but its most famous monuments are from the Hellenistic and Nabataean periods. After the annexation of the Nabataean state by the Romans in 106 AD, Petra became part of the Roman Province of Arabia. The city continued to be important during the Late Antiquity and Islamic periods. Two fortresses were built in the vicinity of Petra during the Crusader period.
e1b84d6c-9cc4-503f-aaf7-19adce734645.keywords: Heritage; Nabataean; Roman; Late Antiquity; monuments; the Siq; Burckhardt
e1b84d6c-9cc4-503f-aaf7-19adce734645.description2: Petra is the crown jewel of Jordanian heritage. It has been a World Heritage Site since 1986. The most prominent monuments of Petra are the Siq, the Treasury, the Winged Lions Temple, the Great Temple, Qasr al-Bint Temple, the monastery, the theatre, the church with mosaic floors and many other monuments.

e1be7517-b6b1-576b-8acd-653f24c29ba9.name: *Hijaz Railway Station, Damascus*
e1be7517-b6b1-576b-8acd-653f24c29ba9.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
e1be7517-b6b1-576b-8acd-653f24c29ba9.author: Stefan Weber
e1be7517-b6b1-576b-8acd-653f24c29ba9.second_name: Main Station of the Hijaz railway leading from Damascus to Medina
e1be7517-b6b1-576b-8acd-653f24c29ba9.description2: The Hijaz station was originally built in 1903 to provide faster transportation for Pilgrims to Medina. So the today closed-down railway station used to be an essential transport and communication link. Furthermore it was built to integrate aloof provinces better into the Ottoman state and hence establish a closer political and economic connection. The new building completed in 1917 also embodies a desire for innovation in terms of design: its architecture is a mix between traditional local Ottoman elements and monumentalizing features of historicism.

e1cd5653-5f77-5751-ab03-dac1cdcd3c94.archival: Tipografia di Bernardo Virzì, *Saggio d caratteri, fregi, ornamenti ed altro* (Palermo 1871), ASPA, Miscellanea II 13

e1f071ed-6026-5f1b-bac8-49caf60ecd7a.name: Migration preparations from Lemnos island to Turkey
e1f071ed-6026-5f1b-bac8-49caf60ecd7a.holder: Population Exchange Museum (The Foundation of Lausanne Treaty Emigrants)
e1f071ed-6026-5f1b-bac8-49caf60ecd7a.description2: The 1923 population exchange between Greece and Turkey was based upon religious identity, and involved the Greek Orthodox citizens of Turkey and the Muslim citizens of Greece. The "Convention Concerning the Exchange of Greek and Turkish Populations" was signed at Lausanne, Switzerland, on 30 January 1923, by the governments of Greece and Turkey. During the migration waves during the 1896-97 riots in Crete, 40,000 Cretan Muslims had to migrate to territories under Ottoman rule: Lebanon, Syria and Anatolia. This photograph pertains to migration preparations from Lemnos to Turkey in 1924.

e24c667e-3e74-52ad-9357-51224ea2c3d0.name: A letter from the Hashemite court
e24c667e-3e74-52ad-9357-51224ea2c3d0.description: A letter from the Hashemite court signed by al-Hussein bin 'Ali, the king of Arab countries and Sharif of Mecca. The letter was sent to the princes Faisal and al-Aziz al-Jarba, from Umm al-Qura (Mecca) in Rajab, 18th, AH 1336 / AD 1917 asking them to take care of Jacobean Armenian confession and to help them and to protect them as they protect themselves, their fortune and their sons. It says also to facilitate what they need either in their stay or travel, because they are free non-Muslims enjoying Muslim protection. Those are people who prophet Muhammad makes his will to take care of, and the one who doesn’t do so will be his (Muhammad's) adversary till Judgment Day. King Hussein says: this is one of the most important orders we ask you to do. He ends his letter by praying to God to grant the Emirs to do what he asks them.

e25a6015-7ec0-5c37-9571-2555b21065b7.description2: The book “On Macedonian Matters” by Krste Petkov Misirkov (1874–1926) provides the only comprehensive national program dealing with important national and political issues at the turn of the 20th century. The work of this great visionary and analyst was published for the purpose of drawing the attention of the European League of Nations to Macedonia, whose existence as separate nation was not recognized.

e2b48175-dfa4-5317-9f12-0d280735f099.name: Drawing of the railway bridge between the mainland and Venice
e2b48175-dfa4-5317-9f12-0d280735f099.description2: This panoramic view shows the railway link between Venice and the mainland. In 1837 a company was founded to organize the building of the railway in the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia. Construction started in 1840 and the railway reached the Venetian station of Santa Lucia in 1846.

e2ed7029-baf0-5a6c-b94c-553bba5ed68d.name: Medal commemorating the opening of the Suez Canal
e2ed7029-baf0-5a6c-b94c-553bba5ed68d.description2: This silver medal designed by O. Roty was struck in 1869, to mark the opening of the Suez Canal, which was built to connect the Mediterranean directly to the Red Sea. On the obverse of the medal is depicted a seated female figure holding the light of Progress in front of the standing figure of Industry. Beyond there is a sketched route of the Suez Canal. In the centre and on the margin of the reverse there are two inscriptions: “Le 17 novembre 1869 le canale maritime a été ouvert à la grande navigation” (On the 17th November 1869 the maritime canal was opened for heavy navigation) and “Compagnie Universelle du Canal Maritime de Suez” (Universal Company of the Suez Maritime Canal). On the coin’s rim is inscribed “L’epargne française prepare la paix du monde” (The French thrift prepares the world peace).

e3029e51-8121-5e09-b08a-bd958da4cd09.name: 'The first railway engine in Tripoli'
e3029e51-8121-5e09-b08a-bd958da4cd09.author: Giulia Barrera
e3029e51-8121-5e09-b08a-bd958da4cd09.description2:
The railway in a colonial context was much more than a means of transport: it was a powerful symbol of modernity, of technological superiority of the colonisers over the colonised, and of mastery over the territory. The construction of railways in colonial situations was often celebrated by the colonialists’ popular press or in postcards, as in this case.  
In Libya, the Italians started building railroads from the first months of colonial rule. The first lines, inaugurated in 1912, connected Tripoli with Ain Zara (11 kms) and to Zanzur (39 kms). By the end of 1915, the railway lines in Libya amounted to 180 kilometres.

e38d66f4-10f9-566e-84d8-1278b05a6847.name: *The Three Ages of Woman*
e38d66f4-10f9-566e-84d8-1278b05a6847.author: Marina Minozzi
e38d66f4-10f9-566e-84d8-1278b05a6847.keywords: International exhibition; universal exposition; art exhibition; Esposizione universale di Roma; Jugendstil;realism; symbol; woman; body; water; gold; glass; metal; mosaic; geometrical motifs; Byzantine; Ravenna; Austrian painters
e38d66f4-10f9-566e-84d8-1278b05a6847.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
e38d66f4-10f9-566e-84d8-1278b05a6847.description2: *The Three Ages of Woman* is one of the few works by Gustav Klimt, the main artist of the Vienna Secession movement, in Italy. The painting was exhibited in 1911 at the International Exhibition of Fine Arts in Rome inside the Austrian Pavilion built by the architect Josef Hoffman (1870-1956). An entire room was dedicated to Klimt (*The Three Ages of Woman*, *The Kiss*, *The Sisters* and several portraits). On this occasion the painting of *The Three Ages of Woman* won a prize and was subsequently bought by the Italian State along with other 51 paintings and seven sculptures in order to be displayed inside the newborn National Gallery of Modern Art in Rome. The canvas, painted in the artist’s maturity, shows an old woman in profile with her body carrying the signs caused by the passing of time. The young woman and mother next to her and frontally depicted, holds her sleeping daughter. The central theme of the canvas is the three steps of woman’s life marked by childhood, maturity and old age. The outstanding “verism”, or “truth” of the figures is in sharp contrast to the decorative background that, with its gold and geometric decorations, is reminiscent of the Byzantine mosaics the artist saw during his voyages to Ravenna in 1903. The use of metals, glaze, coloured glass, and gold show the vogue of orientalism that spread among the artists who wanted to free themselves from western art conventions.
e38d66f4-10f9-566e-84d8-1278b05a6847.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

e396b7b2-cb07-51d7-86f1-b131b11dbfe2.name: Portrait of a lady of the court playing the tambourine
e396b7b2-cb07-51d7-86f1-b131b11dbfe2.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
e396b7b2-cb07-51d7-86f1-b131b11dbfe2.keywords: Pierre Desire Guillemet; Orientalism; painting; İstanbul
e396b7b2-cb07-51d7-86f1-b131b11dbfe2.description2: This painting is one of the four half-length portraits painted by Pierre Désiré Guillemet in 1874-1875 depicting a young woman of the Ottoman Court. Her dress has been emphasized by means of a neutral background. She is wearing a *dört etek* (four-skirted) robe, made of *savai* fabric. Part of her undershirt with embroidered borders is visible from her large sleeves and around the edges of the robe. Her robe has a floral pattern with lively colours and her belt has a clasp with a two large stones in a silver setting. Her chestnut-coloured hair flows down to her shoulder. She wears two strands of pearls around her neck and a gold earing with pearls and gems. On her head she wears a cap of blue fabric decorated with small white flowers, plumes and toile.

e3b28f28-4ce6-5e60-9902-8e13ef295f77.name: Photograph of Tétouan Railway Station
e3b28f28-4ce6-5e60-9902-8e13ef295f77.description: The image does not give one a sense of the real scale of Tétouan Railway Station, one of the first to be built in Morocco in 1918, covering an area of about 1,200m2 and comprises three buildings: one castle-shaped and two large hangars. The station is a model of colonial architecture, bearing the signature of Julio Rodriguez Roda, an engineer working for the Spanish Society of Colonisation, which was responsible for many structures in northern Morocco. Receiving its first travellers at the end of World War I, the line stretched from Tétouan to Ceuta, calling at Martil, Ben Karrich and Zinat.
e3b28f28-4ce6-5e60-9902-8e13ef295f77.keywords: Communication; technical innovation; economy; trade; route; trading routes; industrial railways; foreign companies; Spanish in Morocco; French in Morocco; port; port of Ceuta; strategic port; strategic hubs; trading hubs; Moroccan ports

e3bca328-205b-530c-8cb6-99cd21d8c8dd.name: *Two Musician Girls*
e3bca328-205b-530c-8cb6-99cd21d8c8dd.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
e3bca328-205b-530c-8cb6-99cd21d8c8dd.keywords: Osman Hamdi Bey; Orientalism; painting; İstanbul
e3bca328-205b-530c-8cb6-99cd21d8c8dd.description2: As opposed to the Western Orientalists who emphasize sexuality in their female figures, in Osman Hamdi’s paintings the female figures are often conscious of the period of Westernization in the Ottoman Empire, as well as their individual identities and talents, and are thus open to learning and self-development. In a number of Osman Hamdi’s works, the Ottoman woman is portrayed playing an instrument or reading and she always appears fully clothed. In this painting, which incorporates architectural elements of the Bursa Green Mosque, apart from musical instruments like the *tambur* (lute) and the tambourine, Ottoman decorative elements such as rugs, woodwork, stone carving, and tiles complement the artist’s unique approach to the female identity.

e3bfc26f-8bee-5688-a4c2-f5a33020ddd2.name: Maria Theresa Dollar
e3bfc26f-8bee-5688-a4c2-f5a33020ddd2.holder: Sharjah Heritage Museum/ Sharjah Museums Department
e3bfc26f-8bee-5688-a4c2-f5a33020ddd2.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
e3bfc26f-8bee-5688-a4c2-f5a33020ddd2.description2: This large silver coin is known as the Maria Theresia Dollar. It shows a portrait of the Austrian Empress Maria Theresia on the obverse and the Imperial double-headed eagle of the Habsburgs on the reverse. Originally minted in 1741, the Austrian Maria Theresia dollar became extremely important for Levant trade and was eventually  declared official trade coinage in 1857, one year before it ceased as currency in Austria itself. In the Arab peninsula, and especially in the lower Gulf and Oman, it remained the favoured currency until 1920, highly regarded for its high silver content. Those involved in the pearling trade, including captains of the pearling ships plying the Gulf, preferred to receive their money in Maria Theresia Dollars.

e3d1028e-c33d-53a4-a895-0276547994a0.name: *Construction of the Bordeaux bridge in 1821*
e3d1028e-c33d-53a4-a895-0276547994a0.second_name: Taken from the collection *Topographie de la France*, "Département de la Gironde"
e3d1028e-c33d-53a4-a895-0276547994a0.description2: The construction of bridges had always been a complicated matter, and particularly so in Bordeaux, where the river was especially temperamental. Until the 19th century people crossed it by ferry. However, in 1810 Napoléon I ordered a bridge to be built in Bordeaux, which was completed in 1822. The expertise this required (particularly the building of tunnels to reduce the size of the structure) attracted the attention of many contemporary engineers and architects.

e3f48d7b-3bf0-5b73-ae59-24ec80351340.name: Tantur (woman's headdress)
e3f48d7b-3bf0-5b73-ae59-24ec80351340.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”

e3f48d7b-3bf0-5b73-ae59-24ec80351340.keywords: Woman; photograph; anthropology; ethnology; geography; travel; ethnography; museums; model; genre picture; portrait; representation of the other; costume; material culture; collection; Lebanon; floral decoration; animal decoration; zoomorphism; zoomorphic
e3f48d7b-3bf0-5b73-ae59-24ec80351340.materials: Silver laminate decorated with embossed work
e3f48d7b-3bf0-5b73-ae59-24ec80351340.description2: The Tantur is an example of cultural tradition developed inside the contaminations typical of the Mediterranean world. It is decorated with symbolic images of leaves, flowers and animals and it is engraved with the year of Egira, 1172. Its cylindrical shape is reminiscent of an *asherah*, one of the emblems of the Phoenician goddess of fertility Astarte (the Siriac Atargotis), often represented with cylindrical headgear. The origins in terms of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome, can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.
