e4c6d454-9f18-5654-bdf6-7ba2ce34e089.name: *Map of the desert between the Nile and the Red Sea, including Mount Zabara \[…\] and the remains of the ancient trade route between Egypt and India*
e4c6d454-9f18-5654-bdf6-7ba2ce34e089.artist: Author: Frédéric Cailliaud; cartographer: Edme-François Jomard; engraver: Alexandre Blondeau
e4c6d454-9f18-5654-bdf6-7ba2ce34e089.second_name: Drawn according to M. Caillaud's itinerary, by M. Jomard, and engraved by M. Blondeau.
e4c6d454-9f18-5654-bdf6-7ba2ce34e089.description2: The explorer and naturalist Frédéric Cailliaud made significant contributions to the birth of Egyptology thanks to the hieroglyphic tracings he made during his two trips to Egypt (1815–1818; 1819–1822). Muhammad 'Ali Pasha had tasked him with exploring the banks of the Nile and Nubia, where he discovered the monuments and emerald mines of Mount Zabara, and took several tracings from them, which he brought back to France with him. His observations were compiled and published by E.F. Jomard as a sequel to *l'Expedition d'Egypte*.

e4e13104-3af0-5b6e-9e16-b30a037f184b.name: *Wilaya* (district), Casablanca
e4e13104-3af0-5b6e-9e16-b30a037f184b.history: The first plan was drawn in 1914, but construction according to the designs of French architect Marius Boyer was not completed until 1936. Formerly a prestigious hotel and one of grandest buildings on Place Mohammed V, it is still well preserved.
e4e13104-3af0-5b6e-9e16-b30a037f184b.keywords: Moorish style; art deco; Art Nouveau; Vienna; French in Morocco; French in North Africa; French architects in North Africa; protectorate; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic influence; Islamic city; European influence; European architecture; hotel; travel; tourism; city; urban space; changes in urban spaces; colonial city; colonial building; colonial architecture; urban planning
e4e13104-3af0-5b6e-9e16-b30a037f184b.description2: This now-administrative building, formerly a hotel, is of notable design and colossal dimensions. The entrance has three large doorways with extensive copper surrounds, two large blank windows, and four small windows. It is highlighted by a gallery supported by large hexagonal stone pillars. The window openings – of different sizes and in different styles – pointed horseshoe and curved arches, have sandstone surrounds. The first-floor gallery has rich, predominantly green *zellige* decoration. The building is topped by a square clock tower with a timepiece on all four sides.

e50ae40d-d2e5-50ff-9f8d-f861d8f298d4.name: *Woman from Constantine*
e50ae40d-d2e5-50ff-9f8d-f861d8f298d4.author: Dalila Orfali
e50ae40d-d2e5-50ff-9f8d-f861d8f298d4.description2: This painting belonged first to the collection at St. Martin's Church, Cologne, then to the Duchess of Reggio. It can be found in the catalogue written by the art historian Léonce Bénédite on Chassériau (see vol. 2, p. 495; cf. André Dezarrois, *Théodore Chassériau, sa Vie et son Œuvre*). The artist used women from the Jewish community in Constantine as models for woman's face and dress, following Dehodencq's example from his time in Morocco. This explains her resemblance to Rachel's portrait, which is also kept in the museum.

e532dd30-df15-5462-88cf-6f2eaa8cf7bd.name: Portrait of David Roberts, Esq., R. A.
e532dd30-df15-5462-88cf-6f2eaa8cf7bd.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
e532dd30-df15-5462-88cf-6f2eaa8cf7bd.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
e532dd30-df15-5462-88cf-6f2eaa8cf7bd.description2: This engraving shows a portrait of David Roberts (1796 – 1864), first completed in the 1840s by Charles Baugniet. Roberts is shown seated on an ancient plinth or capital, holding a drawing board and a pencil. A classical temple structure appears in the background on the left. David Roberts was a Scottish painter especially known for a prolific series of detailed lithograph prints of Egypt and the Near East produced during the 1840s from sketches he made during extensive tours of the region (1838–1839). These, and his large oil paintings of similar subjects, made him a prominent and highly influential Orientalist painter. Charles-Louis Baugniet (1814 - 1886), was a Belgian artist famous for the lithographing of portraits of prominent European figures.

e53bb5a4-b7fc-5802-a8fd-9ee4197aa491.name: Illuminated Qur’an manuscript
e53bb5a4-b7fc-5802-a8fd-9ee4197aa491.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
e53bb5a4-b7fc-5802-a8fd-9ee4197aa491.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
e53bb5a4-b7fc-5802-a8fd-9ee4197aa491.artist: Calligrapher: Hussayn al-Hilmi, a student of Muhammad Amin know as Izzi
e53bb5a4-b7fc-5802-a8fd-9ee4197aa491.materials: European paper, black ink, pigments, gilding, pasteboard, leather
e53bb5a4-b7fc-5802-a8fd-9ee4197aa491.description2: 19th-century Qur’an manuscripts produced in Istanbul and the Ottoman Empire continued many Islamic art traditions, but could not entirely escape the increasing taste for Western aesthetics.The exquisite execution of this manuscript suggests a wealthy patron. The opening double page is set within an elaborate framework of floral and geometric arabesque cartouches, executed in gold, blue and other colours. The design recalls those of early Ottoman manuscripts, which - in turn - took their artistic inspiration from Iranian Qur’an production. The remainder of this Qur’an is executed in black naskhi on 390 gilt-edged folios, with 15 lines to each page. As a rule, Ottoman calligraphers preferred an odd number of lines to each page, be it 11, 13 or 15. The script is enhanced with red detailing, and the verse dividers are gilt. The chapter headings are executed in white riqa' on a golden ground enhanced by delicate floral ornament. Large coloured medallions in the page margins mark important sub-divisions of the text. The signature of the calligrapher – set into an elaborate gold rosette – appears on the last page.

e58ba153-b1b5-50fd-aa8e-53f869209b9a.name: Mosque of Amir Mundhir al-Tanukhi
e58ba153-b1b5-50fd-aa8e-53f869209b9a.author: Jeff El-Msanne
e58ba153-b1b5-50fd-aa8e-53f869209b9a.history: The Mosque of Amir Mudhir al-Tanukhi was built in 1620 and is located in today's downtown Beirut. Although it was built during the Ottoman period, the architecture bears more resemblance to the traditional Lebanese style than an Ottoman or even earlier Mamluk style. The courtyard was covered during the restorations following the civil war, in order to shield worshippers from the heat of the sun.
e58ba153-b1b5-50fd-aa8e-53f869209b9a.description2: The mosque's octagonal minaret decorated with *muqarnas* is the only aspect of the structure which resembles a Mamluk architectural style. It also has a courtyard, surrounded by a tall portico with pointed arches resting on eight grey granite columns, taken from pre-existing Roman structures.

e5b5e193-f08b-5657-b562-1f2add9c333b.name: *Egyptian Landscape*

e5c4e1fa-cda0-5a71-9b74-c7a6f465f4ad.name: Portrait of Hammouda Pacha Bey
e5c4e1fa-cda0-5a71-9b74-c7a6f465f4ad.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie

Hammouda Pacha Bey, nicknamed the builder of modern Tunisia, was a qualified and military man and was known as a firm but fair ruler.

e5dcb5be-a7f2-5f24-b1e8-fae35ee4b7b5.name: *Foundations of Haram al-Sharif*
e5dcb5be-a7f2-5f24-b1e8-fae35ee4b7b5.description2: Foundations of the South-Eastern corner of the Haram es-Sharif, as revealed for the first time by Charles Warren. This tunnel was some 85 feet below ground. Warren’s team were experienced mining engineers, and were assisted, as shown in several of this sequence of watercolours by William ‘Crimea’ Simpson, sent to record the expedition for the Illustrated London News, by extremely courageous local Jerusalem residents.

e5df4bff-604d-5c36-92f9-4dd289a5ab3d.name: Two plates from the book *Reproducción del Panorama de la Guerra Civil en el norte ejecutado por los artistas Pla y Pellicer* \[Reproduction of the Panorama of the Civil War in the North, executed by the artists Pla and Pellicer\]

e5e027ae-6390-53b1-82f7-668b99a7615c.name: Slave market
e5e027ae-6390-53b1-82f7-668b99a7615c.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
e5e027ae-6390-53b1-82f7-668b99a7615c.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
e5e027ae-6390-53b1-82f7-668b99a7615c.description2: This souk, Souk el-Birka, was built by Youssef Dey in the early 17th century in the Tunis medina, and was used for the purpose of selling slaves. It was served, until the 16th century, by seasonal carriages from sub-Saharan Africa. By 1850, the number of slaves and their descendants in Tunisia was estimated to be around 80,000. The majority did agricultural work in the oases in the south, but many were also working in domestic roles in bourgeois households and the bey's residence. In 1841 Ahmed Bey banned the sale of slaves and demolished the stores reserved for this purpose, and in 1842 he abolished slavery.

e5e89b24-3038-55eb-a80c-b9bb6fb8a999.name: A rare photo of the inauguration of the Luxor–Aswan Railway Line
e5e89b24-3038-55eb-a80c-b9bb6fb8a999.keywords: Land Roads; Adly Yakan Pasha; Railway Lines; Luxor; Aswan
e5e89b24-3038-55eb-a80c-b9bb6fb8a999.description2: The Honour Guard lining up to receive the guests of the inauguration of the Luxor–Aswan railway line at the Shalal Station in 1926. One of the rare photos of the inauguration of the Luxor–Aswan railway line, with `Adli Yakan Pasha; Muhammad Najib al-Gharabli Pasha; Husayn Rushdi Pasha; Tharwat Pasha; Fathallah Barakat Pasha; Morkos Hanna Pasha; al-Dagwi Bek, director of Aswan; and Mahmud Shakir Bek, deputy undersecretary of the Ministry of Transportation in attendance, in 1926.

e696126e-a8d7-5829-87b8-1372eb83e64c.name: A book on the activities of the Italian community in Tunisia, published by the Italian Chamber of Commerce of Tunisia for the 1906 International Exhibition in Milan
e696126e-a8d7-5829-87b8-1372eb83e64c.author: Giulia Barrera
e696126e-a8d7-5829-87b8-1372eb83e64c.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906.
e696126e-a8d7-5829-87b8-1372eb83e64c.description2:
In 1906, in celebration of the Simplon Tunnel opening between Italy and Switzerland, the Italian government organised an international exhibition in Milan. On that occasion, Italian communities in Egypt and Tunisia published books that described their lives and activities.  
In Tunisia, Italians entrepreneurs and professionals set up a committee charged with organising the participation to the exhibition of the Italian community in Tunisia.

e69b13bf-d0c7-5ed7-8570-ac7defc7d2a4.name: An image from the book *Eastern Hospitals and English Nurses*
e69b13bf-d0c7-5ed7-8570-ac7defc7d2a4.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
e69b13bf-d0c7-5ed7-8570-ac7defc7d2a4.archival: Taylor, Fanny Margaret, *Eastern Hospitals and English Nurses; the narrative of twelve months' experience in the Hospitals of Koulali and Scutari. By a Lady Volunteer. \[Miss Fanny M. Taylor\]*, London, 1857, p. 6
e69b13bf-d0c7-5ed7-8570-ac7defc7d2a4.keywords: Women; work; Crimean war; politics; hygiene; hospitals; travel; traveller; science; medicine; surgery; nurse
e69b13bf-d0c7-5ed7-8570-ac7defc7d2a4.description2: Frances Margaret Taylor converted to the Roman Catholic faith from Anglicanism and founded the order of the Poor Servants of the Mother of God. In *Eastern Hospitals and English Nurses* (1856) she describes her experience as a nurse, prior to her conversion, in the hospitals of Scutari and Koulali, during the Crimean War, with Florence Nightingale. In addition to her personal experience, the book gives an account of medical and sanitary conditions, voluntary service and nursing, one of the few volunteering and job opportunities available to British women in the 19th century. The Crimean War carried nurses outside the boundaries of their country. The book highlights how their support was crucial in the organisation of medical activity and living conditions in the British military hospitals in Turkey and Crimea.

e6b08b1b-d850-518a-9f8a-7c3f457e761d.name: Palais du Baron d’Erlanger
e6b08b1b-d850-518a-9f8a-7c3f457e761d.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
e6b08b1b-d850-518a-9f8a-7c3f457e761d.history: The history of this monument cannot be separated from its creator's personality. The rich Orientalist painter and Arabic musicologist Baron d'Erlanger moved to Sidi Bou Said in 1911, where he built is palace. He dedicated his life to the preservation of Tunisia's architectural, artistic and musical heritage, and on his death in 1932 was buried in Sidi Bou Said. Notable examples of his work are his vital efforts towards the preservation of Sidi Bou Said, and his remarkable seven-volume work on Arabic music.
e6b08b1b-d850-518a-9f8a-7c3f457e761d.keywords: Architecture; Andalusian style; Italian style; stucco; carved wood; painting
e6b08b1b-d850-518a-9f8a-7c3f457e761d.description2: This palace is built on a hill overlooking the sea, and covers approximately 3,300 m2, occupying just a small portion of the 5-hectare grounds. Built between 1912 and 1922, the palace is notable for its interesting architecture, inspired by Tunisian traditions with elements of Andalusian, Venetian and Arab ornamentation. Behind its huge sea-facing façade, it is organised into three distinct sections. The two main square patios, on two separate floors, are connected by galleries, and all surround a covered central space. The décor consists of wall decorations, ceramic panels, carved stucco panels, stucco carved ceilings, golden or painted carved wooden ceilings, and more.

Making pasta was hard work. In Tunisia, the industrialization of pasta production started only in the 20th century.

The site housed the Archaeological Exhibition dedicated to the Roman culture in the Imperial Era with a particular interest for its positive influence on the ex provinces. Every single nation participated through original reproductions of archaeological materials, often lost. The photo shows material evidence and casts coming from Greece.

e6cf18df-e25d-5b11-980d-12274cacd23c.name: Syrian Kingdom dinar
e6cf18df-e25d-5b11-980d-12274cacd23c.description: In March 8, 1920 the general Syrian congress met in Damascus and declared Syria and Palestine independent, with Faisal as king of the Arab Kingdom of Syria and Palestine. On that occasion a gold dinar was struck. In obverse field is “Faisal al-Awwal” written in Divan Jali script, surrounded by a wreath, on top seven pointed stars and the date 1338 (AH) below, all are within a circle of dots. On the reverse, a seven-pointed star and a shield surmounted by a crown and leaning on a wreath, with the date 1920 below. The marginal legend has the word "dinar" on the right, "*al-mamlaka*" on the top and "*al-suriya*" on the left, all are within a circle of dots. It is considered a rare coin.
e6cf18df-e25d-5b11-980d-12274cacd23c.author: Aida Naghawi

e6f49abd-8e7a-5131-a593-cada7ee6ab5e.description2: International Exhibition in Paris, 1878. Tunisia is represented by the creation of different bazaars. The reporter's descriptions of Cattan's Bazaar report mainly religious objects such as wooden rosary beads, mother-pearl crosses and the biblical plant, the Rose of Jericho. The Ben Athia Bazaar displayed cultural objects from Tunisia: luxury arms, rich materials, embroidery, perfumes of roses, bronze and enamelled jewellery. The Eskenazi bazaar displayed various antique objects.

e6f7eabb-fc4e-5c98-b6ca-f2544ae496d9.name: Model in plaster
e6f7eabb-fc4e-5c98-b6ca-f2544ae496d9.description: Following on the European fascination for the oriental world and for the famous Nasrid Palaces of the Alhambra (Granada, Spain), a lot of reproductions of its remarkable architectures and decorations were made and spread. José Contreras was commended as restorer and decorator and his son, Rafael (1824–1890), was the leading pioneer of this trend in 1847. His work was continued by the grandson and by a huge number of plaster-cast workshops in Granada, and very likely, in other cities. His plasterworks were very successful in the International Exhibitions and were kept in private collections and museums like South Kensington (London). This polychrome plaster cast res a window in the Mexnar Palace of Granada (Spain).
e6f7eabb-fc4e-5c98-b6ca-f2544ae496d9.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes, Cristina Giménez

e714183d-faa1-5c38-bf56-e05a8f41f61e.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie

e714183d-faa1-5c38-bf56-e05a8f41f61e.keywords: Porte de France; Tunis medina; European quarter
e714183d-faa1-5c38-bf56-e05a8f41f61e.description2: This copy of a beautiful watercolour from Charles Lallemand's book *Tunis et ses Environs* shows the Porte de la Mer, or the Porte de France, around which both European settlers and Tunisian residents are gathered. Its location was strategic, as it led to both the Tunis medina and the European quarter.

e71cbefd-c4b2-5e4b-a2b6-9dd7a89e735f.name: Portrait of Doctor Rashid al-Dahdah
e71cbefd-c4b2-5e4b-a2b6-9dd7a89e735f.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
e71cbefd-c4b2-5e4b-a2b6-9dd7a89e735f.description2: Rashid al-Dahdah was born in 'Armun in 1813. He studied first at 'Ayn Warka School, and then at Bzummar monastery. He worked first as a secretary, before moving to Saida in 1843 where he studied Islamic law. He later moved to France (Marseille and Paris), where he founded a newspaper in both French and Arabic. Author of numerous books, he died in May 1889 in France.

e71e341d-eb52-561e-8abf-141b52235da5.name: St. Andrew's Church
e71e341d-eb52-561e-8abf-141b52235da5.history: The land for the church was donated by Sultan Mulay ‘Abd ‘Aziz in 1880 to serve the British Christian community in Tangier. Soon it was found that the building was not sufficient for the growing number of worshippers, so a new one was built in 1894, which became the church of St. Andrew. It was consecrated in 1905.
e71e341d-eb52-561e-8abf-141b52235da5.keywords: Religious building; tolerance; plaster; painted wood; marble; geometric decoration; vegetal decoration; epigraphic decoration; British in Morocco; Morocaan architects; craftsmen; craftsmanship; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic influence; Islamic architecture in Morocco; public space
e71e341d-eb52-561e-8abf-141b52235da5.description2: Built on a plot of land donated by Sultan Mulay ‘Abd ‘Aziz, both church and grounds served British Christian residents. In the grounds alongside the church, there is a cemetery that contains the graves of some well-known English personalities such as *The Times* correspondent Walter Harris. In both style and decoration, the building’s Arab-Islamic inspiration is testimony to the Moroccan workers and craftsmen that constructed it. The belfry, built in the style of Moroccan mosque minarets, is square, its base decorated with mosaic and high-relief stucco geometric decoration. Doors and windows are a mixture of round-horseshoe and pointed-horseshoe arches. The canopy over the main entrance is of wood, decorated with brackets. Inside, twin marble columns separate the nave; the choir is accessed through a horseshoe arch that is surrounded with floral decoration, again in high-relief stucco. The arch-surround is framed by text from the gospel in *kufic* script. The ceiling is of painted woodwork and the roof is covered with green tiles. Located behind the altar, the niche is decorated with plaster latticework that holds the motto of Nasrid Granada “There is no conqueror but God”.

e72a56fc-762a-58a7-9573-a53ca4ec40e7.name: Qur'an stand (*kursi*)
e72a56fc-762a-58a7-9573-a53ca4ec40e7.type: Islamic, Indian & Southeast Asian works of art; Metalwork

e72a56fc-762a-58a7-9573-a53ca4ec40e7.keywords: Qur'an stand; kursi; Mamluk Revival; Egypt; copper alloy; brass; silver; copper inlay; Qur'an; inscription; geometric motifs; furniture
e72a56fc-762a-58a7-9573-a53ca4ec40e7.materials: Copper alloy (brass); inlaid with silver and copper inlay
e72a56fc-762a-58a7-9573-a53ca4ec40e7.description2: This tall, hexagonal brass side table has a flat top, six-sided body, and six baluster-shaped feet. The table is inlaid with inscriptional panels offset by engraved or pierced vegetal patterns. The sides are composed of several panels inset within a frame. This stand may originally have been used to support the Qur’an as it was read. For protection, the Qur’an could be stored inside the stand by opening the small doors and placing the text within.

e733f2a6-8940-5e1d-ba96-bb338e5c87f6.name: Hooded cloak (*burnus*)
e733f2a6-8940-5e1d-ba96-bb338e5c87f6.description: Cloak in green velvet with stencilled decoration of pomegranates and leaves in brown. This velvet is based on the Venetian ones of the 15th and 16th centuries. The cloak has a wide fullness at the bottom and a big hood, formed by four points. The cloak is lined in a green silk, printed in silver vegetal motifs.

e76382a2-64c9-5d5c-8c41-049ddd06c52d.description2: These two issues of *al-Hoda* date to 12 October 1901 and 27 November 1901. *Al-Hoda* was a semi-weekly critical periodical founded by N. A. Mokarzel and written, edited and printed in Philadelphia, USA.

e76f2cd3-86ac-51b9-b076-e4ec90a04fbc.name: *Illustrations of the One Thousand and One Nights, vol. 1*
e76f2cd3-86ac-51b9-b076-e4ec90a04fbc.description2: The *One Thousand and One Nights* played an important role in bringing the East and the West closer together. Galland was its first French translator, translating with much liberty what he had been able to understand in the early 18th century. The translated *One Thousand and One Nights* were extremely successful, and became the subject of a variety of art forms, both allowing Europeans to become better acquainted with the Arab world, but also forming the basis for lasting stereotypes.

e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.name: *Interior of the Great Temple at Baalbec*
e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.artist: Drawn by William Henry Bartlett; engraved by Ebenezar Challis
e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.description2: This view into the interior of the Temple of Bacchus at Baalbek, Lebanon originally formed appeared in 'Syria, The Holy Land, Asia Minor, &c', illustrated views printed in 3 series over 2 volumes (37 plates, 37 plates, and 48 plates for each series respectively) including maps and title pages. The publication resulted from the 1836-1838 collaboration between the painter William Henry Bartlett, the engraver Ebenezer Challis and the Publishers Fisher, Son and Co. The architectural and artistic details they recorded subsequently inspired European Neoclassical architects and artists such as Robert Adam, who based one of the ceilings at Osterley House on the ceiling of the Temple of Bacchus and the portico of St George's, Bloomsbury on its portico. Since the 1860s, many tourists visited the site, including, in 1898, the German emperor Wilhelm II. Struck by the magnificence of the ruins, he dispatched a German archaeological team, whose subsequent work resulted in a meticulous, illustrated publication that further popularised the site.

e80567bb-4a41-5dd5-a8c2-8530ecf7b427.name: Abdelaziz Thâalbi (Abdelaziz al-Thalibi)
e80567bb-4a41-5dd5-a8c2-8530ecf7b427.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
e80567bb-4a41-5dd5-a8c2-8530ecf7b427.author: Bechir Yazidi
e80567bb-4a41-5dd5-a8c2-8530ecf7b427.keywords: The Young Tunisians movement; "La Tunisie Martyre"
e80567bb-4a41-5dd5-a8c2-8530ecf7b427.description2: Born in Tunis in 1876, Abdelaziz Thâalbi (Abdelaziz al-Thalibi) was a Tunisian politician. In 1920, he became the founder of the political party Destour, and participated in all the first fights of the nationalist movement. This activism caused him to be sent into exile in 1912, not for the first time, with six other nationalist politicians. In 1920 he wrote and published the manifesto La Tunisie Martyre with Ahmed Sakka, for which he was arrested on 31 July and taken to Tunis. However, feeling threatened there, he fled and left Tunisia once again in 1923. Destourian militants in Tunisia kept calling for his return, which finally happened in July 1937, 14 years after being forced into exile. However, upon his return he entered into conflict with Neo-Destour politicians, led by Bourguiba. He died on 1 October 1944, and his funeral was an opportunity for the Neo-Destour movement, as well as all the fringes of the nationalist movement to gather, and pay tribute to one of the founding fathers of Tunisian nationalism

e80c1234-42a0-5c12-9754-82402e1fca45.name: Umbonate plate
e80c1234-42a0-5c12-9754-82402e1fca45.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
e80c1234-42a0-5c12-9754-82402e1fca45.author: Marina Minozzi
e80c1234-42a0-5c12-9754-82402e1fca45.keywords: Applied arts; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; model; reproduction; motifs; collector; Spain; Moorish; Islamic art; Islamic influence; Neo-Mudéjar style; production of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode; Aragon
e80c1234-42a0-5c12-9754-82402e1fca45.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, as part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". The collections included large samples of pottery, wooden objects, fabric, bronzes and ivories dating to Roman, Renaissance and Baroque times. The best part of this collection is on display at the National Gallery of Palazzo Barberini in Rome, while other pieces are housed in Castel Sant'Angelo and Palazzo Venezia. The series of the Hispanic-Moorish ceramics, bought by Prince Baldassarre Ladislao Odescalchi in 1880, were among the models often reproduced by the training school inside the M.A.I. The umbonate plate (inv.n. 2828) is an aragonese manufacture dating from the first half of 16th century. It shows concentric strips with blue and red tones.
e80c1234-42a0-5c12-9754-82402e1fca45.holding_institution_org: Museo Artistico Industriale presso la Galleria nazionale d’arte antica in Palazzo Barberini

e80dfa93-78f5-57ec-a258-0a31de9fef63.name: *The daughter of the English ambassador riding in a palanquin*
e80dfa93-78f5-57ec-a258-0a31de9fef63.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
e80dfa93-78f5-57ec-a258-0a31de9fef63.keywords: Fausto Zonaro; Guillemet; Orientalism; painting; İstanbul
e80dfa93-78f5-57ec-a258-0a31de9fef63.description2: Until he was appointed as the court painter in 1896, Zonaro was predominantly commissioned by European embassies in Istanbul. In his memoirs, the artist reveals that British Ambassador Sir Philip William Currie (1894-96), who was one of Zonaro’s clients, commissioned a painting depicting his stepdaughter on the palanquin on her way to the church to marry a diplomat. Sir Currie also requested the view of the Golden Horn – as seen from the garden of the embassy – to be included in the background of the painting. The palanquin carriers, two embassy officials smartly dressed in their uniforms and the young woman sitting on the palanquin in her bridal veil, posed for the artist for several days.

e87a28c8-480d-590e-ba3c-b84ef6e8d476.name: Abdul-Mejid I, Sultan of Turkey (1823–1861)
e87a28c8-480d-590e-ba3c-b84ef6e8d476.keywords: Abdul-Mejid, Sultan of Turkey; Egypt; Syria, Palestine; Hungarian refugees
e87a28c8-480d-590e-ba3c-b84ef6e8d476.description2: Portrait of Abdul-Mejid I, Sultan of Turkey (1823–1861), riding a horse. When he came to power in 1839, he tried to re-occupy lands lost to Muhammad 'Ali Pasha, the ruler of Egypt. In this effort he was supported by Britain and Austria. In 1840 a combined British-Austrian fleet cut off the supply lines of the Egyptian army and forced the Egyptians to sign the 1840 Convention of Alexandria. Abdul-Mejid was able to win back Syria and Palestine. In 1849 he granted the Hungarian refugees exile. In 1861 he died and left his throne to his brother Abdülaziz.

e8867b07-6d42-5182-8664-51768b182008.name: Abd al-Kader at Amboise
e8867b07-6d42-5182-8664-51768b182008.description2: Emir 'Abd al-Kader was the symbol of Algerian resistance to the French occupation from 1832 to 1847. After his resignation in 1847, he was taken to the Château de Pau, followed by hundreds of people, where he was detained until he was moved to the Château d'Amboise. His behaviour during his time in captivity attracted the admiration of the French, who saw him as a romantic hero: he studied, meditated, and was always ready to receive visitors. The various portraits and photographs of him that were produced portrayed him as a pious man rather than the warrior he had been. In 1852, the Prince Louis-Napoléon Bonaparte went to Amboise to officially announce the end of his captivity.

e89aa553-0859-53ef-ad91-bdaddb8ac231.name: *Hüdavendigar* Paper in Armenian
e89aa553-0859-53ef-ad91-bdaddb8ac231.description2: After the *Tanzimat* (reforms), newspapers in Arabic, Persian, Bulgarian, Serbian, Albanian, Kurdish, English, French, Italian and German began appearing in the Ottoman Empire. Some of them were bilingual as Turkish-Greek, Turkish-Armenian and Turkish-Arabic. *Hüdavendigar* was a provincial newspaper of Bursa and it was first published on 19 February 1869. The same year, starting with the 80th issue, the back page was printed in Armenian. The paper was published twice (Wednesday and Saturday) and then four times a week. It was 50 x 25 cm. Subscription for a year was 100 kuruş, for six months was 50 kuruş and one issue was 20 para (1/2 kuruş). It continued to be published until 1953 under different names.

e8b27287-7930-5858-8acb-830809b29cd2.name: Saint George Church (Mar Gerges)
e8b27287-7930-5858-8acb-830809b29cd2.description: Located south-west of the 'Judge's well', this Greek Orthodox church was built by Batroun's chief mason, Tanios Deebo, with Batroun sandstone. The main gate, on the southern side, however, was built in limestone from Tum. The church consists of two vaults: one is a cupola, the tallest cupola in Lebanon, and the other is in the form of a cross and overlooks the altar. This church is notable for the two women's niches located under the dome on the north and south sides.
e8b27287-7930-5858-8acb-830809b29cd2.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
e8b27287-7930-5858-8acb-830809b29cd2.history: This Greek Orthodox church was built in a Byzantine style, with a remarkable dome that was completed in August 1867.
e8b27287-7930-5858-8acb-830809b29cd2.keywords: Church; Religion; Batroun; Sandstone; Cupola; Cross; Dome

e8e2873a-17d1-558a-a507-0fd33c1cc8ae.name: Palette
e8e2873a-17d1-558a-a507-0fd33c1cc8ae.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
e8e2873a-17d1-558a-a507-0fd33c1cc8ae.author: Marina Minozzi
e8e2873a-17d1-558a-a507-0fd33c1cc8ae.keywords: Egyptomania; Gaetano Rosellini; university; collector; photograph; anthropology; palaeoethnology; material culture; Florence; Pisa; Egyptology; Nubia; languages; hieroglyph; William Matthew Flinders Petrie; Jacques de Morgan; David Randall-MacIver
e8e2873a-17d1-558a-a507-0fd33c1cc8ae.description2: The cosmetic palette is fish-shaped and reproduces the form of a fish from the Nile River, *Tilapia nilotica*. The palette was found in a woman's tomb along with a turtle-shaped cosmetic palette, ivory findings, a comb, a huge ring and ceramics. As a result of the excavations by W. Petrie and J. De Morgan, who documented the existence of an era preceding the 1st dynasty, Luigi Pigorini, director of the "Museo Preistorico Etnografico e Kircheriano”, decided to expand the Egyptian archaeological collection. In 1878 he began to acquire important groups, but the main body of the collection was donated by David Randall-MacIver in 1901, after the excavations he carried out on the behalf of the Egypt Exploration Fund in the town of el-Amrah, Upper Egypt. Another major purchase — from the Italian Archaeological Mission in Egypt (excavations of Hammamiye) led by Ernesto Schiaparelli, director of the Egyptian Museum in Turin — followed in 1905. The last main acquisition took place in 1913 when the Egyptian objects from Enrico Hillyer Giglioli’s collection entered the museum collection.

en: Cappozzo, M., “La collezione egizia del Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico ‘Luigi Pigorini’”, in *Bullettino di Paletnologia Italiana*, Roma, Istituto Poligrafico e Zecca dello Stato, (2005–2007), 96: 131–202, cat. 69.

e8fa6bb3-c6a3-5e41-9e45-50c1fbee8ea8.name: *Excavation in Giza*
e8fa6bb3-c6a3-5e41-9e45-50c1fbee8ea8.description: Hermann Junker with Egyptian workers excavating a statue from the mastaba of Schepsesptah in 1913. The German-born Egyptologist Hermann Junker became a professor at the University of Vienna in 1909. In 1911 the Austrian Academy obtained the concession for excavation in Giza. In 1912 Hermann Junker's team started to excavate tombs close to the pyramids of Giza.

e8fc4581-ee8f-583c-a11e-54b1e44bda1a.name: Arabic eye liner, *kohl* and perfume container
e8fc4581-ee8f-583c-a11e-54b1e44bda1a.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
e8fc4581-ee8f-583c-a11e-54b1e44bda1a.author: Huda Kilani
e8fc4581-ee8f-583c-a11e-54b1e44bda1a.description2: Padded bag to hold three small brass bottles of Arab eye-liner, perfumes and essential oils. It was used as a wall decoration. Decorated with silk tassels, glass beads, Egyptian and Ottoman coins. The Jordanian economy relied on trades and crafts and new waves of people started to settle in the Jordanian territory for these purposes. This object is an example of how traditional fashion reflected the variegated population composition of the area in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is also an example of local personal attire, fashion, costumes and rites.

e92c5fac-cccf-5730-b2e6-c7774c2761e7.name: The paved road between Beirut and Damascus
e92c5fac-cccf-5730-b2e6-c7774c2761e7.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Rita El Hachem
e92c5fac-cccf-5730-b2e6-c7774c2761e7.description2: This paved road was constructed between over a period of six years, between 1857 and 1863. It measured six metres in width and facilitated the circulation of horse-drawn carriages owned by the "diligence" transportation company.

e93e2356-ce89-5c16-b735-40f476c4b07d.name: Gustave Eiffel. The Eiffel Tower in 1889.
e93e2356-ce89-5c16-b735-40f476c4b07d.description2: Today, the Eiffel Tower is one of the great symbols of Paris and of France. This metal structure, a huge technological achievement in and of itself, was constructed by Gustave Eiffel (1823–1923) for the Exposition Universelle (world fair) of 1889, which celebrated the centenary of the French revolution. Many of his contemporaries, such as Guy de Maupassant, considered the structure hideous and called for its demolition. This drawing recalls the tower's function as a symbol of the vitality of French industry, highlighting its exceptional size and its proximity to the great Palais de l'Industrie, which housed the Dôme Central, the first building to use electricity on a large-scale.

e9467b9f-6942-5d4d-ad65-2a08497b1ca5.name: The Majlis of Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Midfa'
e9467b9f-6942-5d4d-ad65-2a08497b1ca5.holder: Sharjah Museums Authority / Sharjah Heritage Directorate
e9467b9f-6942-5d4d-ad65-2a08497b1ca5.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
e9467b9f-6942-5d4d-ad65-2a08497b1ca5.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
e9467b9f-6942-5d4d-ad65-2a08497b1ca5.notice: Please note that this is an unedited database entry and that it may contain grammatical errors and inconsistencies in spelling. We are working to raise the funds required to complete the editing of the database; should you wish to contribute please visit our [Support page](https://www.museumwnf.org/atrium_support.php).
e9467b9f-6942-5d4d-ad65-2a08497b1ca5.description2: The Majlis of Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Midfa' is one of the very few remaining buildings in Sharjah dating back to the turn of the 14th/ 20th century. A traditional, now carefully restored, courtyard house, its unique feature is its circular *barjeel* or wind tower, the only one in the United Arab Emirates. Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Midfa', was a prominent cultural and intellectual personality in Sharjah. A keen observer and commentator on local and pan-Arab affairs, al-Midfa' transformed his majlis into a hub of intellectual activity and culture. The first ever newspaper in the UAE, entitled ‘Oman’, was published by him in 1927.

e94849dd-ffd1-5aaf-9003-7370d13bf18e.name: Traditional Lebanese house
e94849dd-ffd1-5aaf-9003-7370d13bf18e.description: Houses in the nineteenth century were generally rather modest: roofs were supported by wooden beams, and whilst a handful of houses had stone stairs indoors as well as outdoors, most had only wooden stairs indoors.
e94849dd-ffd1-5aaf-9003-7370d13bf18e.author: Jeff El-Msanne
e94849dd-ffd1-5aaf-9003-7370d13bf18e.history: Mount Lebanon was well known, during the 19th century, for its houses with high ceilings and red roof tiles. The windows were generally made of wood and tinted glass, with the first floor opening out onto a balcony with tall windows for lighting and ventilation. This architectural style has clear signs of European influence.

e952d626-e57d-5b8e-b2e2-24763b1c7b83.name: Receipt for a subscription among the Italians in Tunisia to buy Italy a plane
e952d626-e57d-5b8e-b2e2-24763b1c7b83.author: Massimo Sanacore
e952d626-e57d-5b8e-b2e2-24763b1c7b83.archival: ASLi, Famiglia Moreno di Tunisi, b. 6
e952d626-e57d-5b8e-b2e2-24763b1c7b83.description2:
We do not know whether the Italians living in Tunisia who collected money to buy Italy a plane were aware that Italy would use planes to bomb civilians in Libya. To be sure, they supported Italian expansionist policy.  
This receipt bears the signature of the treasurer of the committee that was collecting funding to buy Italy a plane, Giuseppe Di Vittorio, the owner of a successful construction company. The donor, Ugo Moreno, was another “big man” of the Italian community in Tunisia: a lawyer, he established a bank (Banca Italiana di Credito), in 1901 started an oil company (Societé du Pétrole) and in 1919 became town councillor in Tunis.

en: Sanacore, Massimo, "Storia della famiglia di Moisè Moreno", *Nuovi studi livornesi*, 18 (2011): 347–53.

e97ad326-57ea-571c-be97-f63b11fcafbc.name: Chorographical plan of the attack waged by Lord Exmouth against Algiers on 27 August 1816
e97ad326-57ea-571c-be97-f63b11fcafbc.author: Edoardo Garis, Giulia Barrera
e97ad326-57ea-571c-be97-f63b11fcafbc.archival: ASTo, Carte Topografiche e disegni, Carte Topografiche Segrete, Algeri 3 E I Rosso (1816)
e97ad326-57ea-571c-be97-f63b11fcafbc.third_name: *Plan / de l'attaque donnée à Alger / par S.E. Lord Exmouth / le 27. Août 1816. / et levé sur le lieu même par un Ingénieur / de la Flotte Anglaise / publié à Turin en décembre 1816. / Avec permission et privilege du Roi*
e97ad326-57ea-571c-be97-f63b11fcafbc.description2: In the spring 1816, a large Anglo-Dutch fleet headed by Admiral Lord Exmouth forced the three Ottoman regencies of the so-called “Barbary Coast” (the coastline of Algiers, Tunis and Tripoli; “Barbary” comes from “Berber”, the name given to the original people and culture of North-West Africa) to release Christian captives and to sign agreements over the abolition of corsairing, or privateering, and the enslavement of captives. In August, the Anglo-Dutch fleet returned to Algiers and made additional demands to the Turkish regent, who refused to comply. Lord Exmouth then ordered a heavy bombardment that destroyed the Algerian navy and part of the city of Algiers.

en: Clancy-Smith, Julia, *Mediterraneans: North Africa and Europe in an Age of Migration, c. 1800–1900*, Oakland, CA: University of California Press, 2011.

e9860dcd-6e70-574d-9bd8-9f806ad37335.name: Buckle for enlisted rank of the Austro-Hungarian gendarmerie in Bosnia-Herzegovina
e9860dcd-6e70-574d-9bd8-9f806ad37335.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
e9860dcd-6e70-574d-9bd8-9f806ad37335.keywords: Bosnia; Gendarmerie; Austrian army; Ottoman Balkans; military object; war; warfare; military wear; Coat of arms; blazon
e9860dcd-6e70-574d-9bd8-9f806ad37335.description2: This characteristic metal buckle with the coat of arms of Bosnia and Herzegovina was used by all enlisted ranks of the Austro-Hungarian gendarmerie in Bosnia-Herzegovina, which maintained domestic order in these two provinces. The main deployments of the gendarmerie were in the regions of Sarajevo, Travnik, Banja Luka, Bihac, Tuzla, Mostar, Trebinje and Gorazde.

e99ec60f-9439-5be8-b2c8-63118d0cc859.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury

e9d20fa0-c214-51e8-a022-980c7d31384c.name: Tekke panel
e9d20fa0-c214-51e8-a022-980c7d31384c.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
e9d20fa0-c214-51e8-a022-980c7d31384c.description2: *Hüsn-i Hat* is a type of calligraphy. Turks probably started to get interested in calligraphy after their arrival to Anatolia. The brightest period was during the Ottoman era. Calligraphy developed well beyond its functional role; it almost played a similar role to the paintings in Western art in terms of the level of its aesthetics. The script *"Ya Hazreti Şeyh Sultan Yusuf Sümbül Sinan Kaddes Allahu sırrahu"* (religious text, untranslatable) is written on a black background with *Zerendud* (gilded) calligraphy and designed as the *sikke* (tall felt hat) of the Sünbüli order. It stands over a small table in Rococo style and there are hyacinth flowers on either corner of the upper part. The sides of the plate are surrounded by two borders that are Rococo in design.

e9dc3805-7eb0-5025-b948-d69dd0ddfe00.name: *The Citadel of Cairo, the Residence of the Pasha*
e9dc3805-7eb0-5025-b948-d69dd0ddfe00.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
e9dc3805-7eb0-5025-b948-d69dd0ddfe00.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
e9dc3805-7eb0-5025-b948-d69dd0ddfe00.description2: The citadel of Cairo, here captured by the Scottish artist David Roberts in the 1830s, was undergoing major changes under Muhammad Ali Pasha (1769-1849). Having overcome the Mamluks of Egypt in 1805, Muhammad Ali erased all traces of their rule, including remaining palace and administrative structures. He rebuilt most of the walls, erected four new palaces - his own royal residence in the northern enclosure, a courthouse, an expansive terrace and state-of-the-art accomodation for his army. At the heart of the citadel complex, Mohammad Pasha ordered a memorial mosque for his son Tusun in the Ottoman style. Building work on the mosque lasted from 1828 to 1848. Roberts incorporates the new structures existing in his time, like the palace on the right, cresting the hill - the ongoing building works on the mosque are concealed by the Mamluk structure in the foreground on the right.
e9dc3805-7eb0-5025-b948-d69dd0ddfe00.artist_birthplace: David Roberts: Edinburgh, Scotland; Louis Hague: Tournai, Belgium
e9dc3805-7eb0-5025-b948-d69dd0ddfe00.artist_deathplace: David Roberts: London; Louis Hague: London

e9e0d077-22ec-5da6-8968-784248276025.name: Palais Kasr el-Said
e9e0d077-22ec-5da6-8968-784248276025.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
e9e0d077-22ec-5da6-8968-784248276025.history: Located near the Bardo palaces, this palace had belonged to a noble of the Husainid court until 1867. It was then subject to a series of adjustments and expansions under the reign of Sadok Pacha Bey, who took up residence there once the works were completed. It was in this palace that, on 12 May 1881, Sadok Pacha Bey added his signature to the treaty which would impose a French Protectorate on his country, headed by General Bréart. The building was restored and taken over by l'Institut National du Patrimonie in 1988, and now houses the first landmarks of the Musée d'Histoire de la Tunisie Moderne et Contemporaine, whilst also preserving its Husainid foundations. It also holds many historically valuable paintings, thrones and coaches which had belonged to the bey.
e9e0d077-22ec-5da6-8968-784248276025.keywords: Architecture; art; painting; stucco; mosaic; marble; ceramics
e9e0d077-22ec-5da6-8968-784248276025.description2: This palace is an excellent example of a typical beylical palace, with an architecture, décor and furnishings that show distinct signs of European, and particularly Italian, influences. The large, tall building is surrounded by trees and orchards. The grand staircase, the marble columns, the marble, ceramic and faience mosaics on the walls, the Italian-style window frames and the Andalusian-style carved stucco all contribute to the decorations' opulent and varied quality, which characterised the 18th and 19th centuries.

ea0dd19a-059c-55b1-ad56-fcbfe2341d01.name: *Souvenirs d’Egypte; Femme Fellah du Caire*
ea0dd19a-059c-55b1-ad56-fcbfe2341d01.dimensions: Height: 57.3 cm Size of covers, Width: 38.9 cm
ea0dd19a-059c-55b1-ad56-fcbfe2341d01.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
ea0dd19a-059c-55b1-ad56-fcbfe2341d01.keywords: Egypt; peasants; agriculture; portrait; print; women; work; souvenirs; travel
ea0dd19a-059c-55b1-ad56-fcbfe2341d01.description2: Lithograph, tinted with one tint stone, with additional colouring by hand, depicting a female agricultural worker (or fellah). ea1f55bf-b075-5e73-a04a-db3e93d8bff2.name: Revolver
ea1f55bf-b075-5e73-a04a-db3e93d8bff2.description:
According to the engraving on the barrel, this revolver was manufactured by J. Nikittis Erben in Constantinople. Erben was a revolver-maker and retailer who sold Colt firearms. Another engraving also reads ""POUCARTOUCHE NAGANT"". The serial number was engraved on the left side of the revolver right under the cylinder. Only the last two digits (76) can be seen. The revolver is fitted with wooden grips and fixed to the frame by a screw. This  
revolver is similar to the Swiss revolver of 1882, but not identical. It might be a variation of that revolver.
ea1f55bf-b075-5e73-a04a-db3e93d8bff2.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities

ea3a91f8-4029-5f91-8e55-44b4089bf748.name: *Bayt al-Barudi steamship murals, Damascus*
ea3a91f8-4029-5f91-8e55-44b4089bf748.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
ea3a91f8-4029-5f91-8e55-44b4089bf748.author: Stefan Weber
ea3a91f8-4029-5f91-8e55-44b4089bf748.second_name: Mural in the main reception hall of the Barudi House at the quarter of Qanawat
ea3a91f8-4029-5f91-8e55-44b4089bf748.description2: The steamships are of one of the most important technical innovations in the nineteenth-century, because they introduced new modern possibilities of transport and trade and hence contributed to the economic transformation of the Ottoman Empire. Because of this new transportation, cities on the Euphrates or Tigris experienced drastic changes and flourished even more. This impact lead to numerous depictions of steamships in artwork, such as this mural from Bayt al-Qabbani (Damascus, built at the turn of the 19th/20th century) shows. As symbols of the new time they represent global exchange of goods, ideas and people.

ea5004e5-f4e7-5291-8059-9bc54d1ba863.name: Archaeological excavations
ea5004e5-f4e7-5291-8059-9bc54d1ba863.description2: General view of workers behind some scholars who supervise their work. The photograph was taken next to the pyramid of Niuserre at Saqqara in 1904. The photo is printed from glass plate negatives.

ea530416-e3b0-5749-9237-eed6b02b7d4b.name: Ancient Egyptian Agricultural museum main entrance pathway and garden
ea530416-e3b0-5749-9237-eed6b02b7d4b.author: Ibrahim Abdel Aziz
ea530416-e3b0-5749-9237-eed6b02b7d4b.history:
King Fu\`ad I chose the palace of Fatma Ismail, the daughter of Khedive Ismail, ‎to host the displays of the Agricultural Museum. The ‎palace was chosen due to its location near the Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture in the ‎neighborhood of Dokki in Cairo.  
The museum, which was first called "The Agricultural Museum of King Fu\`ad I", was officially opened for the public on the 16th of January 1938 in a big ceremony that the king himself attended.
ea530416-e3b0-5749-9237-eed6b02b7d4b.keywords: Agricultural museum; Dokki, Agriculture Palace; Khedive Ismail; King Fu`ad I; Princess Fatma; Khedivial palaces; Khedivial Egypt; Ancient Agriculture; Pharaonic Agriculture
ea530416-e3b0-5749-9237-eed6b02b7d4b.description2: The museum of Ancient Egyptian Agriculture is the most interesting section of the Agricultural Museum and it contains the most valuable displays. Tourist groups must receive permission beforehand in order to visit this museum. It represents the first section of the development of agriculture in Egypt ‎and it illustrates the ‎history of Egyptian agriculture from the prehistoric period till the late Pharaonic ‎period. ‎The first floor of the museum of Ancient Egyptian Agriculture hosts all sorts of ‎displays that illustrate how the ancient Egyptians cultivated their lands. The displays ‎include ancient tools and equipment that were used in the days of the Pharaohs and descriptions of ‎how the ancient Egyptians created these tools.

ea56c676-8f35-5489-88dc-00a76f28ef9d.name: *Turkish ladies buying jewellery*
ea56c676-8f35-5489-88dc-00a76f28ef9d.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
ea56c676-8f35-5489-88dc-00a76f28ef9d.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
ea56c676-8f35-5489-88dc-00a76f28ef9d.description2: This watercolour, completed in 1873, shows three elegantly dressed society ladies, their faces concealed by a light veil, visiting the shop of a jeweller, his wares displayed in a small multi-tiered glass case placed on the low platform in front. While one of the ladies is seated on a carpet at the entrance to the shop to examine a pearl necklace that the old, bespectacled proprietor has offered her, her two companions wait outside and shield her to some extent from curious eyes. Vittorio Amadeo, 5th Count Preziosi (1816-1882) was an artist of Maltese origin, who left for the Middle East in the early 1840s. He settled in Istanbul as a diplomatic translator and artist, specialising in touristic scenes, vistas and types

ea68ca74-8e7f-519d-98cf-82fb84aa3d58.name: Medal to commemorate the inauguration of Ma'an station
ea68ca74-8e7f-519d-98cf-82fb84aa3d58.keywords: Numismatics; Hijaz; Hijaz Railway; Ottoman empire; 'Abd al-Hamid; railway; pilgrimage; Hijaz; sharif; Makka al-Mukarrama; Mecca; al-Madina al-Munawwara; Medina; Ottoman imperial symbols; monogram; Ottoman monograms

On the obverse is the *tuğra* of Sultan ‘Abd al-Hamid II with the inscription “al-Ghazi” and the image of a locomotive. On the reverse is the date (AH) 1322.

ea69f41d-1b91-5ee4-8097-8aba9db33c0f.name: *Le consul Joseph Raffo* (painting)
ea69f41d-1b91-5ee4-8097-8aba9db33c0f.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
ea69f41d-1b91-5ee4-8097-8aba9db33c0f.author: Bechir Yazidi
ea69f41d-1b91-5ee4-8097-8aba9db33c0f.materials: Canvas, wood, coloured pigments, gold leaf
ea69f41d-1b91-5ee4-8097-8aba9db33c0f.description2: Giuseppe Maria Joseph Raffo, the subject of this painting, was born in Tunis in 1795 and is depicted here in full uniform with the air of an important Turkish dignitary. He entered service as a secretary to Bey Hassine, and later served as Tunisia's Minister for Foreign Affairs under his rule as well as that of his successors, despite being a Sardinian subject all the while. He made a fortune by taking over a tuna farm in the Cap Bon region in the form of private concession. This painting is evidence of an active diplomatic relationship between the Palais du Bardo and the European chancelleries.

ead4767a-7d82-5048-a0d2-07b5b5b4d68a.name: Table of of Krste Petkov Misirkov
ead4767a-7d82-5048-a0d2-07b5b5b4d68a.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
ead4767a-7d82-5048-a0d2-07b5b5b4d68a.description2: Krste Petkov Misirkov (1874–1926) was actively engaged in politics, fighting for the recognition of Macedonians as a people with distinct tradition and language. He is one of the few who made great contribution to raising international awareness of Macedonian people at the close of the 19th century and in the early 20th century.

eae0553a-c677-57b1-9a70-eda8e6211616.name: The Belvedere (Wilhelma Park)
eae0553a-c677-57b1-9a70-eda8e6211616.holder: Wilhelma, Zoological and Botanical Garden Stuttgart
eae0553a-c677-57b1-9a70-eda8e6211616.history:
King Wilhelm I of Württemberg commissioned to Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1837 the design of Moorish style buildings for his Wilhelma garden. The architect planned and built all the buildings with the exception of the Damascene Hall.  
The idea was not to reproduce faithfully the Islamic art but to lend an “oriental” flair to the garden. The mention of an “oriental garden” conjured up visions of elegance, luxury, colourful brilliance, seduction and eroticism.  
The Moorish style recalls the Islamic art of Spain and North Africa between the 12th and 15th centuries which reached its zenith in the Alhambra. It was fashionable in 19th century: Wilhelma is also known as the “Alhambra on the river Neckar” and other buildings – synagogues in Berlin and Vienna for example – were built in the Moorish style.
eae0553a-c677-57b1-9a70-eda8e6211616.description2: The Belvedere is situated on the Rosenstein slope and, as the name signifies (it is Italian for "lovely view"), it is one of the loveliest viewing spots at Wilhelma. From 1851 onwards it served King Wilhelm I of Württemberg as a place to enjoy the view across to the Burial Chapel on Rotenberg Hill and over the Swabian countryside. The Belvedere forms the upper limit of the Sub Tropics Terraces and also of the entire historical Wilhelma, The pavilion itself is closed to the public, but the view can still be enjoyed.

eaed42bd-51b3-5083-8735-9c1467c68055.name: An example of Italian colonial propaganda: 'Italy takes up the sword of ancient Rome. To the Italian sailors who are fighting in Tripolitania'
eaed42bd-51b3-5083-8735-9c1467c68055.holder: Central Institute for Cataloguing and Documentation (ICCD)
eaed42bd-51b3-5083-8735-9c1467c68055.author: Giulia Barrera
eaed42bd-51b3-5083-8735-9c1467c68055.third_name: *'L'Italia brandisce la spada dell'antica Roma - Ai marinai italiani combattenti in Tripolitania'*
eaed42bd-51b3-5083-8735-9c1467c68055.second_name: A colonial postcard for the Italian soldiers fighting in Libya in 1911–12
eaed42bd-51b3-5083-8735-9c1467c68055.description2:
Italian sailors fighting in Libya are portrayed as the heirs of Roman soldiers. On the ground, one can see the personal military equipment of an ancient Roman soldier. The modern sailor holds in his right hand the Roman soldier’s sword and in his left hand an Italian flag.  
Italian colonial rhetoric looked at the Roman Empire as a justification for Italy’s colonial conquests of Libya. The current territory of Libya was for centuries part of the Roman empire.
eaed42bd-51b3-5083-8735-9c1467c68055.holding_institution_org: Istituto Centrale per il Catalogo e la Documentazione (ICCD)

eaf5a4c2-fc34-59cc-85e1-5bfdbe4b17c3.second_name: Watercolour sketch for the great painting of the 1863 Salon, for Napoléon III's collection; Sketch for the painting at the Louvre
eaf5a4c2-fc34-59cc-85e1-5bfdbe4b17c3.description2: Fromentin's inspiration for this painting came from the journey he made in 1853 from Médéa to Laghouat, crossing the great expanses of the halfa grass and wormwood deserts. On his way, he came across a spring where grey vultures were drinking.

eb38e940-7f0e-59a0-8e60-897613089325.description2: Within the International Exhibition in Paris, 1878, commercial activities typical of the colony were performed in the park next to Trocadero Pavilion. Working activities were part of the project of the reconstruction of a hypothetical neighbourhood. The picturesque recreation of the Algerian surroundings includes a drinkseller offering lemonade kept fresh inside "*alcarazas*” made by red earth.

eb5033cb-f5e6-537a-88bb-7d6bf116bf69.name: Laledan
eb5033cb-f5e6-537a-88bb-7d6bf116bf69.description2: It is known that there were workshops producing glass vessels around Beykoz in Istanbul in the 19th century. The first glass workshop was founded by Mevlevi Dervish Mehmed Dede during the reign of Selim III (1789-1807). There were European glass craftsmen working in those workshops as well. Cups, bottles, jugs etc. made of colourful, colourless and opal glass were among Beykoz' productions. This is a *laledan* made of dark blue opaline. On the body there are white vervain motives with green leaves. There are three circles with stars and crescents.

eb5b5b6f-3b83-5284-8eb0-50673debe16c.name: Medical box of Dr. İbrahim Göze
eb5b5b6f-3b83-5284-8eb0-50673debe16c.description2: Dr. İbrahim Ethem Göze started studying medicine first in Civilian Medical School and graduated from Darülfünun Medical Faculty in 1914. He specialized in dermatology in Gureba Hospital in Istanbul. This medical box belonged to Dr. İbrahim Ethem Göze is rectangular in shape, brown and covered with leather. It also has a handle for carrying. It is in two pieces with four chambers inside. One of the chambers has a cover. In the front there are salvarsan (Arsphenamine) medicine boxes used to cure syphilis, in the chamber at the back there are brown bottles on which sulphur, ammonia, alcohol and tincture of iodine is written. In the covered chamber there are ampules, bandage, a metal syringe with its needle and one tongue holder. On the box one can read the figure of 152.

eb84b6d8-fe2b-592c-9960-26f03ef21c4d.name: House
eb84b6d8-fe2b-592c-9960-26f03ef21c4d.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Prof. Marula Nikoloska, Ph.D. (consultant)
eb84b6d8-fe2b-592c-9960-26f03ef21c4d.history: This traditional house in Macedonia shows the influence of Levantine architecture, which was largely enhanced by the skills and knowledge of local masters bringing about outstanding architectural achievements. The town of Krushevo emerged in a relatively short period of about half a century in the late 1700s and early 1800s. Vlachs from Moscopole and minor places around it migrated to this area, bringing with them their construction and dwelling culture and tradition. Miyaks from the Reka area also moved here enriching the architecture with their great construction and architectural decoration skills.
eb84b6d8-fe2b-592c-9960-26f03ef21c4d.description2: The distinctive layout and interior organization of Krushevo houses arose from the need for adjustment to the steep terrain and severe climate. This house is a two-storied structure with a basement. As in most houses in Krushevo, levelling of structures has been done by construction of a basement embedded in the steep terrain. The basement was built of stone and the upper stories of adobe are coated with plaster. The usable space of the second storey has been expanded by protruded decks. The abundant decorative treatment of the front façade includes symmetrically laid windows flanking the balcony door on the second storey. The impression is enhanced by the peaked roof-edge and semi-round decorations above the balcony door and central windows.

eb85ace1-331f-51ea-a2d6-78f331e3d54f.name: Pena Palace
eb85ace1-331f-51ea-a2d6-78f331e3d54f.holder: Sintra Parks Monte da Lua, Conservation Company
eb85ace1-331f-51ea-a2d6-78f331e3d54f.author: Maria Regina Anacleto (Palácio da Pena)
eb85ace1-331f-51ea-a2d6-78f331e3d54f.history:
The initial small convent of friars Hieronymites rebuilt by King Manuel I (1481-1495), was rather damaged with 1755 earthquake. It was purchased in ruins with the surrounding forest by King Ferdinand II (1838) husband of Queen Maria II (1819-1853), to be adapted as a royal summer residence.  
The convent fascinated the king, namely the hill and the aesthetic enhancement of the ruins as a result of his Germanic origin and of the romanticism in vogue. Firstly the convent’s accommodations around the old cloister were adapted for residential use and the convent’s church became a private chapel. In 1843, a new wing was added with larger rooms and reception hall, such as the Great Hall. German amateur architect Baron von Eschwege carried out the work under the king’s close supervision.
eb85ace1-331f-51ea-a2d6-78f331e3d54f.keywords: Romantic Period; Sintra; Pena; Palace; Architecture; Neo-Moorish; Neo-Manueline; Eclecticism
eb85ace1-331f-51ea-a2d6-78f331e3d54f.architects: Architects: Baron of Eschwege (1840–1847), Demetrio Cinnatti, Wenceslau Cifka (1846–1847); Carpenter: Gregório Casimiro; Ceramist: Company Pickman (1846–1847); Designers: Fernando de Saxe-Coburgo (1846–1847), Nicolau Pires (1840), Visconde de Meneses (attr., 1841–1843); Sculptor: Nicolau de Chanterene (attr., 1532); Menuisier: Barbosa e Costa (1846–1847); stoneman: João Henriques (1840–1847), João Luís (16 th cent.); Stained glass artist: Kerner.
eb85ace1-331f-51ea-a2d6-78f331e3d54f.description2: Fernando II conceived a romantic revivalist and eclectic palace, blending Gothic, Manuelin and Arab styles into what became the epitome of the Portuguese Romanticism. The main features are the outside walls crowned by a Neo-Moorish arcade, the Queen’s terrace with arcades in the Arabian style; the entrance gate with a drawbridge, functioning as an “antecamber” that prepares the visitor to understand the portico, the “Triton Arch”, an allegory of the creation of the world, sited in the façade of the new palace. The arch leads to the arcaded courtyard with an Arab inspired ceiling in its passageway. For the façade overlooking the courtyard the king designed a window inspired on the one of the Convento de Cristo (Tomar)  that is now seen as the beginning of the neo-Manueline style.

eba85bbe-07ea-54e1-b12e-dd3f891151d0.author: Dalila Orfali
eba85bbe-07ea-54e1-b12e-dd3f891151d0.description2: Women in Orientalist art were frequently idealised: the theme of the naked, languishing concubine dominated European art throughout the 19th century. Alfred Chataud's work, however, seems to approach the theme with less artificiality, and indeed this watercolour shows a great degree of authenticity in depicting a scene from Algerian women's daily lives in the late 19th century. The painting even seems to resemble Gustave Courbet's *Demoiselles au bords de la Seine*.

ebc1fbff-c25e-5ca5-86ba-1be3dbc34cbf.description2: Two of the most important inventions of the 19th century, the rotary and four-colour printing (quadrachrome), are attributed to Augusto Ippolito Marinoni. The new machines changed the printing of journals, achieving up to 18,000 to 20,000 copies per hour. Marinoni had extraordinary success in Paris, where his factory produced 4000 samples of machines which also sold in London, Berlin and Vienna. In Italy at the time, only the journal *Il Secolo* had a "Marinoni".

ec198745-bf85-5cf3-a025-264676b49e2d.name: *Histoire de la Princesse Boudour (Conte des mille et une nuits)*, Translation by J.C. Mardrus of *The Story of the Princess Boudour: Tales of a Thousand and One Nights*
ec198745-bf85-5cf3-a025-264676b49e2d.description: François-Louis Schmied (1873–1941) and Jean Dunand (1877–1942) worked together on *Histoire de la Princess Boudour*, the French translation of one of the tales from *The Arabian Nights* by J.-C- Mardrus. The painter, illustrator, engraver, bookbinder and publisher François-Louis Schmied was primarily responsible for producing the graphic design and handling of the text, the illustrations and their wood interpretations. Dunand produced a lacquered metal plaque that transmitted the eroticism and voluptuousness revealed throughout the text. Using warm colours, Princess Boudour is portrayed on a red ground sprinkled with gold, and appears as a very elongated, tubular figure holding a flower with both hands. It’s a limited edition, just twenty copies, it’s a extremely rare Art Deco book.

ec43977b-e543-5455-bbeb-c0f1565cf50d.name: Photograph of the Krushevo Revolutionary Squad
ec43977b-e543-5455-bbeb-c0f1565cf50d.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
ec43977b-e543-5455-bbeb-c0f1565cf50d.description2: The Krushevo Revolutionary Squad played an active role in the Uprising of Ilinden, which broke out on 2 August 1903. The main battles of the uprising were waged in the Bitola Revolutionary Region, more precisely, in the town of Krushevo. Pitu Guli (1865–1903) was leader of the squad. He was a Vlach from Krushevo who was fully devoted to the idea of an autonomous Macedonia from an early age. It is noteworthy that not all revolutionaries taking part in the uprising were Macedonians. Vlachs from the Krushevo region were also actively involved in the battles. The Krushevo Squad played a crucial role in taking over of the town. Together with troops from other parts of Macedonia, they managed to liberate the town and declare the Krushevo Republic. Pitu Guli lost his life defending the Krushevo Republic on 12 August 1903.

ec7fd0d9-9cc8-500f-9c45-55773ae4604c.name: *The Tortoise Trainer*
ec7fd0d9-9cc8-500f-9c45-55773ae4604c.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
ec7fd0d9-9cc8-500f-9c45-55773ae4604c.keywords: Osman Hamdi Bey; Orientalism; painting; İstanbul
ec7fd0d9-9cc8-500f-9c45-55773ae4604c.description2: Rather than depicting the “other” as a number of foreign painters did, Osman Hamdi portrayed his own culture and propounded his own cultural perceptions. The architectural decor suggests that the scene takes place in one of the upper-story chambers of the Bursa Green Mosque. Dressed as a dervish and slightly bent over, a man is examining in a contemplative fashion the tortoises roaming the floor. He sports an *araqiyya*, a flattish skull cap commonly worn by dervishes with a *destar*, or sash wrapped around it. He wears a belted, long red robe the borders of which are embroidered; his feet are clad in *çedik*, or slippers for indoor wear, made of yellow *sahtiyan*, Moroccan (goatskin) leather. He holds a ney in one of the hands he has clasped behind; a *nakkare* or a small kettledrum hangs down from his back.

ec85bb2a-f3be-5bb8-8daf-5b03128455ed.name: One Arab man and two Arab children in front of Kabyle house, Paris Exposition, 1889

eca99cf6-1929-5d7d-bf2a-e8ec044b0d68.name: A Jewish family
eca99cf6-1929-5d7d-bf2a-e8ec044b0d68.description2: The Jewish community, which had gone through various waves of migration since the beginning of the Islamic period, had, by the 19th century, become an important part of Tunisian society.

ecbd97bc-85ed-53b3-ab05-ca13100e4055.name: Reconstruction of Ancyra Temple at the Rome International Exhibition, 1911
ecbd97bc-85ed-53b3-ab05-ca13100e4055.holder: Central Institute for Cataloguing and Documentation (ICCD)
ecbd97bc-85ed-53b3-ab05-ca13100e4055.author: Marina Minozzi
ecbd97bc-85ed-53b3-ab05-ca13100e4055.keywords: Esposizione Internazionale di Roma; post-unitarian Italian society; anniversary; celebration of Ancient Rome; nationalism; map; topography; reproduction; model; exhibitions and urban spaces; archaeological findings in urban context
ecbd97bc-85ed-53b3-ab05-ca13100e4055.copyright: Copyright image: Roma, Istituto Centrale per il Catalogo e la Documentazione, ICCD.
ecbd97bc-85ed-53b3-ab05-ca13100e4055.description2: Over the centuries the Baths of Diocletian, sacked by the barbarians of Alaric, were abandoned and restored several times. In 1563, Pope Paul IV commissioned Michelangelo to transform it into a church “Santa Maria degli Angeli”. In 1749 the architect Vanvitelli rebuilt it again. For the International Exhibition of Rome in 1911, the complex of the "Baths of Diocletian” was restored again under the direction of Rodolfo Lanciani for the International Exhibition of Rome in 1911, to host the Archaeological Exhibition dedicated to Roman culture in the Imperial Era with a particular interest for its positive influence on the "ex provinces". The most incredible reconstruction on display was the Temple of Ancyra (ancient capital of Galatia, in the centre of Minor Asia) dedicated to Augustus and the goddess Roma, based on casts taken by the archaeologist Azeglio Berretti. Included in the display are the famous engraved inscription on bronze tablets, the so-called "Res Gestae” that represents the testament of emperor Augustus.
ecbd97bc-85ed-53b3-ab05-ca13100e4055.holding_institution_org: Istituto Centrale per il Catalogo e la Documentazione (ICCD)

ecc37fb3-5606-5413-bfb4-48ac62d9c763.name: Turkey. Inside view of the Scutari Hospital during the Crimean war.
ecc37fb3-5606-5413-bfb4-48ac62d9c763.second_name: *One of the Wards of the Hospital at Scutari*
ecc37fb3-5606-5413-bfb4-48ac62d9c763.description2: Florence Nightingale (1820–1910), a British nurse famous for her commitment to and improvement of the health service, was sent to on a humanitarian mission to Scutari in the middle of the Crimean war. With a team of about 30 nurses, she cleaned the hospital and reorganised the wards in order to prevent the outbreak of epidemics. In this image she is pictured in the sick ward, taking various measures to improve its hygiene.

ecda8323-4cc5-5e96-a034-122e8ca1bb6c.name: Textile from the Prince Felipe of Castile burial
ecda8323-4cc5-5e96-a034-122e8ca1bb6c.description: This fragment came from the set of garments wore by the Castilian Prince Phillip in his burial at Villalcázar de Sirga (Palencia). The fragment is a very good example of the richness of the textile from al-Andalus. The textile has an inscription in Arabic that could be translated as “Glory to our Lord the Sultan”. This an early example of the interest in collecting important textiles, even before the important research made by Gómez-Moreno in the Royal Convent of the Huelgas (Burgos).
ecda8323-4cc5-5e96-a034-122e8ca1bb6c.author: Ámparo López
ecda8323-4cc5-5e96-a034-122e8ca1bb6c.keywords: Nasrid art; islamic influence; orientalism; collectionism
ecda8323-4cc5-5e96-a034-122e8ca1bb6c.third_name: Fragmento de tejido de la tumba del Infante D. Felipe

ece4e33c-7204-5b42-8e58-18b1ae8b4d17.name: *Ruins of Troy: general excavation plan by Mr Schliemann*
ece4e33c-7204-5b42-8e58-18b1ae8b4d17.keywords: Greek antiquities; archaeological excavations; Schliemann; Turkey; plans
ece4e33c-7204-5b42-8e58-18b1ae8b4d17.description2: Heinrich Schliemann (1822–1890) was a German businessman who discovered his passion for archaeology whilst travelling. In 1870 he decided to direct an archaeological campaign in Turkey where he discovered the ruins of Troy. Various scandals (stolen objects, scientific errors) quickly destroyed his reputation, and today he is credited only with having created sites which led to important advances in the field. However, this plan of Troy is evidence for Schliemann's efforts to direct the excavations in a rigorous scientific manner.

ed280684-f7be-5238-afc4-1fd992c55380.name: An old exhibition from Tiled Kiosk
ed280684-f7be-5238-afc4-1fd992c55380.description2: The Tiled Kiosk is a pavilion set within the outer walls of Topkapı Palace and dates from 1472. It was built by the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II as a pleasure palace or kiosk. The building was used as the Imperial Museum between 1875 and 1891. In 1953, it was opened to the public as a museum of Turkish and Islamic art, and was later incorporated into the Istanbul Archaeology Museums. The collections of the Tiled Kiosk Museum consist of about 2000 artefacts belonging to the Seljuk and Ottoman eras, dating from the 11th-20th centuries. These artefacts include those that existed when the museum was incorporated into the İstanbul Archaeological Museums due to its closeness and those acquired through excavations, purchases, donations and confiscations.

ed4ef36e-eda4-545f-87d2-ba68beef2c54.name: Photograph of archaeological excavations at Volubilis
ed4ef36e-eda4-545f-87d2-ba68beef2c54.description: Initial excavations revealed that this site was of great archaeological and historical significance, uncovering the Triumphal Arch, the Basilica and the Capitol.
ed4ef36e-eda4-545f-87d2-ba68beef2c54.holder: Conservation of the Archaeological Site of Volubilis
ed4ef36e-eda4-545f-87d2-ba68beef2c54.keywords: Archaeology; excavation; scientific expedition; exploration; Morocco; Roman city

edab323b-dc63-5faf-a178-579bc04253cd.name: Pitcher
edab323b-dc63-5faf-a178-579bc04253cd.description2: Kütahya was the second most important ceramic production centre after İznik due to the rich clay deposits in the area. Although there was a decline in ceramic production at the beginning of the 19th century, in the last quarter of that same century production was revived and new designs inspired by İznik ceramics were produced.

edae7a23-07b5-5d83-9c59-298568ea0cc0.name: The Moroccan Embassy in Rome
edae7a23-07b5-5d83-9c59-298568ea0cc0.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History

edae7a23-07b5-5d83-9c59-298568ea0cc0.archival: *La Tribuna illustrata*, a. I, n. 25, 22 June 1890, p. 380.
edae7a23-07b5-5d83-9c59-298568ea0cc0.second_name: The Sultan of Morocco’s Ambassador, Haji el Maati Ben-el-Kebir Ben el Madani el Mazamizi during his visit to Italy in 1890
edae7a23-07b5-5d83-9c59-298568ea0cc0.description2:
In June 1890, the Sultan of Morocco sent an Ambassador to Italy (Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi), to meet the Italian King and present him with extremely rich gifts.  
The Ambassador was received with the highest honours. He met with the Italian Prime Minister and with the King, who offered him a gala dinner.  
In this picture one can see Morocco’s Ambassador, his interpreter, two Moroccan dignitaries who travelled with him, an Italian diplomat and another Italian high official.
edae7a23-07b5-5d83-9c59-298568ea0cc0.holding_institution_org: Biblioteca di Storia Moderna e Contemporanea

edd18c27-fe22-5339-967d-92f28407d76f.name: House
edd18c27-fe22-5339-967d-92f28407d76f.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Prof. Petar Namichev (consultant)
edd18c27-fe22-5339-967d-92f28407d76f.history: As most of the architectural heritage in Macedonia, dwelling architecture of the Maleshevo Region developed a mode of construction combining locally available building materials: stone, wood and earth. In the Berovo area in particular, the proximity of forests led to wide use of wood, not only as material for composing the structural elements but also for building walls.
edd18c27-fe22-5339-967d-92f28407d76f.description2: This house, built with a wooden framework, stone and earth, represents the specific traditional style of Macedonian dwelling architecture that developed under both Western and Oriental influences. It is a two-storey house constructed in the traditional style of the Maleshevo Region in the east of Macedonia. The ground floor consists of massive stone walls. The upper storey was built of horizontally laid laths and coated with mortar. The usable surface of the upper storey has been expanded by protrusions on the two sides of the house, supported by wooden poles and laths.

ede0b2ce-0710-54bf-ab1e-1d03d63a1f3d.name: *View of the Arab Courtyard: National Museum of Archeaology, Madrid*
ede0b2ce-0710-54bf-ab1e-1d03d63a1f3d.description: View of the "Arab courtyard" in the National Museum of Archaeology before 1920. This room displayed different pieces including the Alfajería arch and a copy of the fountain of the Lions of the Alhambra palace. This room was one of the first museum gallery focused in the Arab or Islamic pieces in Europe.

ede894ef-e932-5091-a746-d1686d47ff68.name: Photos of the entrance to the Birds Room, photos of the Birds Room and of the Egyptian Gazelle at Fu`ad Agricultural Museum
ede894ef-e932-5091-a746-d1686d47ff68.dates: 16 January 1938 (Photos taken during the inauguration of the museum)
ede894ef-e932-5091-a746-d1686d47ff68.description2: The Fu`ad Agriculture Museum was considered the first of its kind in the Middle East and the Arab World during the 1930s. It was inaugurated during the time of King Faruq, the son of King Fu`ad, and houses a large number of collections related to agricultural and rural environments, as well as agricultural plants and animals.

edea7f90-3f66-5675-adbf-cd4fe3995f84.description: A painting depicting the presentation of ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abd al-Sadiq al-Rifi, Ambassador to Mulay Sultan ‘Abd al-‘Aziz of Morocco, at the accession of King Edward VII in 1901 that also demonstrates the good relations between Morocco and Great Britain at this time.
edea7f90-3f66-5675-adbf-cd4fe3995f84.keywords: Diplomacy; travel; diplomatic visits; ambassador; Moroccan-British relations; international relations; agreement; France; Great Britain

ee0cbe27-f7a7-56db-b5c5-18038a38b0c8.name: Omar Pasha (1806–1871)
ee0cbe27-f7a7-56db-b5c5-18038a38b0c8.keywords: Omar Pasha; Croatia; Bosnia; Ottoman empire; Herzegovina
ee0cbe27-f7a7-56db-b5c5-18038a38b0c8.description2: Portrait of Omar Pasha. He was born in Croatia in 1806 near the Turkish-Hungarian border. In 1828 he deserted from the Austrian army and joined the Ottoman administration in Bosnia. After a long career in the Ottoman army, he became the military governor of Bucharest and commanded the Ottoman forces at the siege of Sevastopol in Crimea. In 1862 he suppressed an uprising in Herzogovina and led a victorious campaign against Montenegro. In 1868 he became War Minister and died in 1871 in Istanbul.

ee1f0807-ca9d-507c-adf4-27f446a10f42.name: Statue of Athlete – Ephesos
ee1f0807-ca9d-507c-adf4-27f446a10f42.description: After competitions in the *palestra* (sports arena), it was customary for the athletes to clean the sand from their oiled bodies with a strigil, or scraping iron. The Ephesian athlete seen here has already finished this task and – with his hair still soaking in sweat – is cleaning the strigil itself. This statue cannot be attributed to any Greek artist with certainty, yet Roman reproductions in marble and depictions on pottery reliefs and engraved stones speak to a high degree of familiarity with the original.
ee1f0807-ca9d-507c-adf4-27f446a10f42.holder: Kunsthistorisches Museum, Collection of Greek and Roman Antiquities
ee1f0807-ca9d-507c-adf4-27f446a10f42.dates: 2nd century AD (copy after a Greek original from the last quarter of the 4th century BC); found in 1895
