eeee249c-f43e-5b78-852f-c10c356bd5fc.name: Monumental Ensemble of Bussaco
eeee249c-f43e-5b78-852f-c10c356bd5fc.type: Civil architecture changing the ancient religious architecture
eeee249c-f43e-5b78-852f-c10c356bd5fc.author: Alexandre d'Almeida, Marta Simões
eeee249c-f43e-5b78-852f-c10c356bd5fc.history: 1620 - the Barefoot Carmelite created a “Bos Sacrum” in a walled forest of 105 acres, on the Bussaco Mountain, north of Coimbra, supposed to represent “Mount Carmel” and the “Earthly Paradise”. Following the dissolution of the monasteries in 1834 the forest was abandoned. 1850 - plans followed to turn the ancient convent into a royal residence for Queen Maria Pia, with  luxurious landscape intervention by Roda & Figli (Torino) taking place.  Political circumstances interrupted the project that was later commisioned by her grandson King Charles with the construction of the iconic Neo-Manueline castle, from 1888 to 1907, under project of Luigi Manini, as an homage to the Portuguese Age Discovery and the Battle of Bussaco. 1917 it was transformed into the deluxe Bussaco Palace Hotel.
eeee249c-f43e-5b78-852f-c10c356bd5fc.keywords: Tourism; Leisure; Trekking; Botanic; Royal Palace; Nature; Natural landscape; Wellington; Romanticism; Jerónimos Monastery; Belém Tower; Burgenromantik; Carmelites; Battle of Bussaco
eeee249c-f43e-5b78-852f-c10c356bd5fc.architects: Luigi Manini (scenographer and architect); architects: Nicola Bigaglia, Manuel Joaquim Norte Júnior, José Alexandre Soares, José Paulo dos Santos; tilework: Jorge Colaço; painters: António Ramalho, Veloso Salgado, Carlos Reis, João Vaz e Ernesto Condeixa; sculptors: António Augusto Gonçalves, Costa Mota, Simões de Almeida Sobrinho, João Machado; stonemasons: Bernardo António Figueiredo, João das Neves Machado, Manuel Francisco, António de Sousa Lemos, Manoel Cardoso, José Barata, José Fonseca, António Joaquim, Alberto Caetano, José Ferreira e Anacleto Garcia
eeee249c-f43e-5b78-852f-c10c356bd5fc.description2:
The Bussaco Park and the monastery were created by the Discalced Carmelites (1620–1834). From 1888 to 1930s a new ensemble is erected, with multiple buildings, either close to the former convent, or replacing the convent’s library, kitchen and dining room.  
By mid-19th century the forest is revitalized associated to emergent rituals of tourism, journeys and leisure. The design of Buçaco Palace was commissioned by King Charles to Luigi Manini, scenographer and architect. Later on, Nicola Bigaglia, José Alexandre Soares and Norte Júnior also cooperated, namely in the Casa dos Embrechados, Casa dos Arcos, Casa dos Cedros and Casa dos Brasões. The final result reflects a fragmentary romanticist attitude, deeply marked by revivalism and multiple references to the Portuguese Discoveries.

eefb1961-57d7-5239-9988-b5ce36ab258e.name: Triple-arched house
eefb1961-57d7-5239-9988-b5ce36ab258e.description: The layout of this house is composed of various rooms, symmetrically arranged around three sides of a large, north-facing central room called a *dar*. Three large arched windows, in a neo-gothic style, open onto a narrow balcony. The three sides of rooms do not communicate with each other, and thus the *dar* is both a communal living space and the physical centre of the home.
eefb1961-57d7-5239-9988-b5ce36ab258e.author: Jeff El-Msanne, David Andos
eefb1961-57d7-5239-9988-b5ce36ab258e.history: This kind of house started appearing around Beirut in the 1860s. It is often read as being representative of "Ottoman modernity" during the Tanzimat period, and its design and construction was outlined in/limited by the law. Indeed, this new architectural style was based on a new conception of the domestic space: domestic activities have been absorbed into the living space, and outdoor spaces are less prevalent. Balconies, backyards, courtyards and gardens, for example, no longer play an important role in the design of these homes.

ef29d044-78f8-52d1-a065-bb93ee480704.description2: One curiosity, presented at the Universal Exhibition of Paris in 1878, is a modern "bed wardrobe" designed by the Milanese industrialist Luigi Elli. Appreciated more in France than in Italy, and initially excluded from Italian orders, it was reintroduced when the France decided to display it within other French works.

ef67fa8c-4ff1-55bf-83f3-ae6118113aaa.name: *Sorolla in Tetouan*
ef67fa8c-4ff1-55bf-83f3-ae6118113aaa.description:
This picture was taken in Tetouan during a trip of the painter Joaquín Sorolla and his friends to Morocco in 1919. Sorolla's family and friends were portrayed with local people, a highlight of which is the Moor Selam and other characters and exotic animals, such as the monkey. Especially interesting is her daughter Helena who appeared in a Moorish costume.  
This travel appeared in the newspapers El Confidencial and ABC which also published this photograph.  
This family trip brought back memories and objects. The painter's daughter, Helena, had their little Moorish corner on the stairs of the house which is now the Sorolla Museum. A table, a chest, tambourines, fabrics, jewellery were bought back as souvenirs.
ef67fa8c-4ff1-55bf-83f3-ae6118113aaa.author: Covadonga Pitarch

ef89ce14-252d-5bb0-8014-da9c14164139.name: *Egypt. Construction of the Suez canal: the construction workers*
ef89ce14-252d-5bb0-8014-da9c14164139.keywords: Suez canal; Egypt; Ferdinand de Lesseps
ef89ce14-252d-5bb0-8014-da9c14164139.second_name: Taken from *Canal Maritime de Suez: Photographies D'apres Nature par Justin Kozlowski*
ef89ce14-252d-5bb0-8014-da9c14164139.description2: Photographers such as Justin Kozlowski photographed the excavation works throughout the construction of the Suez Canal. In contrast to the usual photos of Egypt which were taken for tourists, photographs such as this were taken for documentary purposes: it allowed the Suez Canal Company to see the progress and cost of the works.

efb40382-898f-59c5-99c9-337e5b9fd997.name: Europeans leaving Alexandria (Egypt) during the antiforeign rioting in June 1882
efb40382-898f-59c5-99c9-337e5b9fd997.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
efb40382-898f-59c5-99c9-337e5b9fd997.author: Giulia Barrera
efb40382-898f-59c5-99c9-337e5b9fd997.third_name: *La partenza degli europei da Alessandria d’Egitto (da uno schizzo preso dal vero)*
efb40382-898f-59c5-99c9-337e5b9fd997.description2:
Ahmed Urabi, an army colonel of peasant origins, led a protest movement in 1881 against European domination of Egypt’s affairs and in favour of placing constitutional limits on the Khedive’s power. In 1882 Urabi was appointed minister of war and started working for the creation of a national assembly.  
In May 1882, Britain and France, concerned about access to the Suez Canal and intending to protect their financial interests in Egypt, sent a fleet to Alexandria, hoping to weaken Urabi’s nationalist movement. The presence of the fleet only worsened tensions. In June, anti-foreign rioting erupted in Alexandria and left several hundreds dead, including about 50 foreigners.  
18,665 Italians were living in Egypt at the time, mostly in Alexandria and Cairo.
efb40382-898f-59c5-99c9-337e5b9fd997.holding_institution_org: Biblioteca di Storia Moderna e Contemporanea

efe60dc6-7155-5eb3-a180-d0bfbd548106.name: Revenue stamp
efe60dc6-7155-5eb3-a180-d0bfbd548106.description2: A revenue stamp issued in 1888 during the reign of Khedive Muhammad Tawfiq with the value of one dime. Written at the top is “Egypt Post” in Arabic with its French translation below it. To the left is the value of the dime in French, and in the centre is an image of one of the Giza pyramids and the Sphinx. The first postal stamp was issued in England in 1840. It bore the portrait of Queen Victoria, as suggested by Sir Roland Hill. This stamp was issued twice, in red and in blue. The United States of America was the second country in the world to use stamps, and the first Egyptian stamp was issued in 1866 by order of Khedive Ismail.

f0020c49-694c-556a-855c-e631e86ab20b.name: Survey of Western Palestine
f0020c49-694c-556a-855c-e631e86ab20b.description2: Field sheet showing a week’s work mapping the environs of Gaza for the Survey of Western Palestine, dated 29th April, 1875. The SWP was the first detailed and fully accurate map ever made of Palestine, at 1 inch to the mile, for the Palestine Exploration Fund. The Survey Party was commanded by Lieut. Claude R. Conder, R.E., and his assistant, Lieut. H.H. Kitchener.

f0157113-5673-5605-86fe-951af8c08ff8.name: Map of Aden
f0157113-5673-5605-86fe-951af8c08ff8.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
f0157113-5673-5605-86fe-951af8c08ff8.archival: *The Gulf of Aden Pilot ... Compiled from memoires of Officers of the Indian Navy, by ... C. Y. Ward*, *Sailing Directions. Aden*, London, Hydrographic Office, 1882, second edition, with additions
f0157113-5673-5605-86fe-951af8c08ff8.keywords: Trade; route; port; Great Britain; India; coffee; Red Sea; Yemen; Mocha; British settlement on the route to India; communication; telegraph; telegraph between ports; Suez Canal; Arab Peninsula
f0157113-5673-5605-86fe-951af8c08ff8.description2:
*The Gulf of Aden Pilot* included sailing indications and directions for navigation of the Suez Canal, the Gulf of Suez, the central route for steamships on the Red Sea, main ports on the Red Sea and directions for navigation through the Gulf of Aden, for a safe navigation.  
After the opening of the Suez Canal, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden were becoming increasingly important as maritime routes for communication and trade to the East. Reliable knowledge of routes, harbours, accomodation, supply stations, telegraph lines between the ports, winds, currents of the whole area was therefore of fundamental importance. The book also provides some information about communication and trade. For example, it states that Aden was declared a free port in 1850 and in the following years replaced Mokha as the main port for coffee trade.

f02e2658-e5a5-5c73-8f21-a84aea27d4e2.name: Osman Hamdi Bey (During the excavation of Lagina, together with French archaeologists Cammonard and Cartier)
f02e2658-e5a5-5c73-8f21-a84aea27d4e2.keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters; archaeological excavations
f02e2658-e5a5-5c73-8f21-a84aea27d4e2.description2: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen were exposed to Western ideas through education and travel. The museum was founded by decree in 1891 as the Imperial Museum. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi. Hamdi began construction of the main building in 1881, and it achieved its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. It is one of the prominent structures built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul. Osman Hamdi, during his tenure as museum director, launched the first Turkish scientific excavations. He carried out archaeological excavations at Mount Nemrut, Laguna and Sidon.

f03672a7-5a8f-5216-8d53-07817c3aa415.name: *The Prayer in the Desert*
f03672a7-5a8f-5216-8d53-07817c3aa415.author: Marina Minozzi
f03672a7-5a8f-5216-8d53-07817c3aa415.keywords: Orientalism; imaginary trips; reinvention; Egyptomania; Egyptology; architectural trends in painting; exoticism; diplomatic mission; Mulay al-Hasan; travel; travelling artist; Italian travellers; Italian painters; Edmondo de Amicis; Marocco; travel book
f03672a7-5a8f-5216-8d53-07817c3aa415.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
f03672a7-5a8f-5216-8d53-07817c3aa415.description2: Stefano Ussi lived between Florence and Rome and studied at the Academy of Fine Arts of Florence before enrolling as a volunteer in the first Italian War of Independence, during which he was taken prisoner by the Austrian troops. He developed a model of history painting characterised by a quick application of layers (almost a rough draft) and by a sharp chiaroscuro. In 1875, along with the painter Cesare Biseo, and Edmondo De Amicis, he accompanied an Italian diplomatic delegation to Morocco. At the opening of the Suez Canal the artist went to Egypt and created his first version of *The Prayer in the Desert* which is exhibited at the Accademia di Belle Arti in Florence. From that moment on, Ussi made both history and oriental-themed paintings.

f0667100-6159-569b-9a0e-84fec1b968f0.name: Headdress
f0667100-6159-569b-9a0e-84fec1b968f0.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
f0667100-6159-569b-9a0e-84fec1b968f0.author: Huda Kilani
f0667100-6159-569b-9a0e-84fec1b968f0.keywords: Ottoman; Russian coins; pendent; red and green silk
f0667100-6159-569b-9a0e-84fec1b968f0.materials: Silver, fabric, glass beads, coins; casting, welding, weaving
f0667100-6159-569b-9a0e-84fec1b968f0.description2: Three bands of silver chain fitted around the sides and over the crown of the head and attached to a surrounding fabric patterned in minute beadwork and sewn with various Ottoman and Russian coins. From this head-piece hangs a long piece of cotton sewn with coins of the Ottoman Empire with a rectangular pendant and multiple red and green silk tassels on the back. Headdresses like this one were worn by married women, as silver was the most common jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride. The Ottoman and Russian coins reflect the social and economic situation of Jordan between the end of the 19th century and the early 20th century, when it was part of the Ottoman empire and it was influenced by population movements, demographic changes and trade with distant countries.

f0e5d0e1-0d9f-5dac-9166-a688b53727f8.name: Zaghwan aqueduct
f0e5d0e1-0d9f-5dac-9166-a688b53727f8.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
f0e5d0e1-0d9f-5dac-9166-a688b53727f8.history: Water problems were one of the Tunisian governments' constant preoccupations. It was the custom for wealthy people to build public fountains called *sabils*. Rulers, however, were preoccupied with the organisation of large scale water conveyance. In 1859, just before the establishment of the French protectorate and on the advice of the French consul Léon Roches, Mohamed Bey tasked the engineer Pierre Colin with the restoration of the old Roman aqueduct running from Zaghwan to Carthage, and its Hafsid era diversion towards Tunis, which had been out of use and abandoned for a long time. The works were completed in 1862, during Mohamed Sadok Bey's reign.
f0e5d0e1-0d9f-5dac-9166-a688b53727f8.description2: The hydraulic works are described in the general administration's 1883–1889 Public Works report as follows: "89 km of brick canal between Zaghwan and Goulette were refurbished, 41 km of metal piping has replaced the huge aqueducts at Djouggar, Oued Miliane, Djedeida and the Aryanah plains". Water supplies for Tunis and the beylical residences were thus assured. The piping was put into operation for the first time on 19 May 1862. You can still see the impressive row of columns and arches today.

f12fed73-12b9-5991-a430-4273cea32560.name: Revolver
f12fed73-12b9-5991-a430-4273cea32560.description: A Liege/ Belgium manufactured revolver. Some of these revolvers were produced in Liege by the Leon Nagant factory for the Russian army between 1895 and 1898 (The Belgian Contract Revolvers), but some other revolvers of this type were produced in Russia itself (Tula) after that. The revolver is fitted with chequered grip plates that are fixed to the frame with a screw installed in a round steel insert. On the left side of the revolver the word Liege was engraved preceded by two illegible words. Only the last letter S can be clearly seen. Right under the word Liege two words were completely erased. On the barrel from the right side of the revolver a crowned oval with the letter R in the middle was engraved. Under the oval a star with what might be a letter g is engraved. The same letter is repeated on the frame at the base of the barrel.

f16ca057-a0e1-511d-9754-d9f37c51ca07.description2: Pascal Sébah (1823-1886) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. In 1857 he opened his first photography studio, *El Chark Societe Photographic*, in Istanbul and by 1873 was successful enough to open another studio in Cairo. In 1860 he moved to another studio next to the Russian Embassy in order to work with A. Laroche, who worked in Paris. He continued to work with Laroche until 1873.

f175d1d2-4ea7-502d-8b4f-2dbcdf510fc9.name: *Tunis 2*
f175d1d2-4ea7-502d-8b4f-2dbcdf510fc9.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
f175d1d2-4ea7-502d-8b4f-2dbcdf510fc9.keywords: Black History; Great Exhibition; The Great Exhibition; Prints
f175d1d2-4ea7-502d-8b4f-2dbcdf510fc9.description2:
Designed by Joseph Nash, this is one of the set of views published with accompanying text as Dickinson's Comprehensive Pictures of the Great Exhibition. The prints used the newly available technique of colour lithography to record scenes from the popular 1851 Exhibition. This particular scene shows the Tunisian exhibit, Tunisia being one of few African countries represented at the Exhibition. Exhibits were selected by the bey, Mushir Basha, and included a Bedouin tent. The wealth of material displayed and the charisma of the exhibitors, Hamda Elmkadden and his assistant Saido Belais, ensured that the exhibit proved ‘one of the most remarkable features’ of the Exhibition.  
Following the Exhibition, a government grant was awarded to a committee headed by Henry Cole to purchase items from the Exhibition to form the basis of a Museum of Manufactures (later the V&A).

f1948597-53b1-578c-8bd5-dbd5ac4ee6c3.name: *The Great Khan of Damascus*
f1948597-53b1-578c-8bd5-dbd5ac4ee6c3.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
f1948597-53b1-578c-8bd5-dbd5ac4ee6c3.provenance: England; published in Etching depicting *'The Great Khan At Damascus'*, first published in John Carne, *'Syria, The Holy Land, Asia Minor, &c'*, 1836–1838
f1948597-53b1-578c-8bd5-dbd5ac4ee6c3.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
f1948597-53b1-578c-8bd5-dbd5ac4ee6c3.artist: Painted by William Henry Bartlett; engraved by William H, Kelsall
f1948597-53b1-578c-8bd5-dbd5ac4ee6c3.description2: Damascus had long been a major commercial hub in the Middle East, with trading caravans converging on its numerous souqs from all over the Islamic world. Commercial complexes had already flourished in the 18th century and were an integral part of Ottoman modernisation projects in the 19th century. This image gives a wonderful impression of the activities within a traditional Near Eastern khan or market complex in the 19th century. Under high vaulted domes, man and beast are engaged in various activities. Pack animals bring wares or are being unloaded, traders discuss their wares, rest or ponder their accounts. A fountain in the centre provides respite and coolness. On the second floor, figures are visible at the balconies, overlooking the activities below. The print was originally published in Volume I, p. 49, of 'Syria, The Holy Land, Asia Minor &c', printed in 3 series over 2 volumes, drawn by William Henry Bartlett and William Purser, engraved by W. Kelsall, with descriptive text by John Carne. Published by Fisher and Son, with series I and II bound together.

f22befb9-5e91-59ad-a5d6-b1b4804da1d6.artist: Composer: Angelo Dal Vesco; Illustrator: L. Denis
f22befb9-5e91-59ad-a5d6-b1b4804da1d6.description2: French "Egyptomania", which began with the campaign in Egypt and lasted the whole 19th century, saw a period of particular intensity during the construction of the Suez Canal. The illustrator of this score, responding to the music's supposedly Egyptian inspiration, focused his illustrations on stereotypical Egyptian images (pyramids, sphinx, palm trees), but notably failed to include images of Egyptian people or daily life.

f23c34bf-814d-5e9e-8baf-ebe84ce157b4.name: *Folies Rambuteau. New quartet from the Auvergne.*
f23c34bf-814d-5e9e-8baf-ebe84ce157b4.description2: The 19th century saw mass rural to urban migration, particularly to Paris, for largely economic reasons. These migrants often settled with people from their region, who offered them work in specific fields. Thus, those from the Savoy region became specialised in chimney-sweeping, those from the Auvergne were water-carriers or coal-merchants, those from Brittany were domestic workers, and so on. Regional solidarity therefore ensured the survival of regional culture. In this image, for example, a quartet from the Auvergne are advertising their performance in a *café-concert* in traditional dress. Music from the Auvergne was the origin of the Parisian *bal-musette* (a dance accompanied by accordion music).

f23c9866-5c58-5675-bd30-f9e664734c96.name: *View on the Jordan*
f23c9866-5c58-5675-bd30-f9e664734c96.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
f23c9866-5c58-5675-bd30-f9e664734c96.archival: Jewry afterwards Valentine, Laura, *Palestine Past and Present. Pictorial and descriptive ... Illustrated, etc*, London: F. Warne & Co, 1893, p. 65
f23c9866-5c58-5675-bd30-f9e664734c96.keywords: Pilgrimage; pilgrims; Christian pilgrimage; Jewish pilgrimage; Palestine; Holy Land; Jerusalem; sacred places; travel; travel book; Ottoman Palestine; local Jewish community; Biblical places
f23c9866-5c58-5675-bd30-f9e664734c96.description2: In the 19th-century United Kingdom, cultural, political and religious interest in the Middle East grew alongside scientific and economic exploration of the area. The creation of the Palestine Exploration Fund and the development of Biblical studies testify to this approach. In addition, the public came into contact with a land that was becoming a myth and a symbol: the Holy Land. Hence the publication of travel or pilgrimage reports, or of books collecting information to be disclosed among the readers, trying to trace some correspondence between existing sites and the those appearing in the Scriptures. These publications offered a sort of virtual journey through the Holy Land and were very often enriched with evocative photographs and illustrations, such as this view on the Jordan river, with all its symbolic meaning.

f262f19f-c5f9-5c05-bd10-8873d3e30db2.name: *Interview with Mehemet Ali in his Palace at Alexandria 1839*
f262f19f-c5f9-5c05-bd10-8873d3e30db2.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
f262f19f-c5f9-5c05-bd10-8873d3e30db2.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
f262f19f-c5f9-5c05-bd10-8873d3e30db2.keywords: Muhammad Ali Pasha; diwan; Thomas Waghorn; Patrick Campbell; Bogosh Bey
f262f19f-c5f9-5c05-bd10-8873d3e30db2.description2: This scene shows Muhammad Ali Pasha, comfortably seated on a diwan with sword and waterpipe by his side, receiving a British Delegation at his palace in Alexandria on May 12th, 1839 - an event at which the artist David Roberts himself was present after receiving an invitation from the British Consul General in Alexandria, Colonel Patrick Campbell, to accompany him to the meeting at the city's Arsenal. On entering the audience room, Roberts noticed the magnificent view of the harbour from the window, and he eternalises this impression at the centre of his composition, accentuating at the same time the separation of the Egyptian ruler and his entourage on the left and the six-strong, British delegation on the right. Campbell is seated closest to the ruler, followed by Thomas Waghorn and David Roberts, eagerly leaning forward to listen and observe. Other identifiable individuals include Bogosh Bey, the Armenian chief minister, standing left of the seated Pasha, Dr Tattam, a Coptic scholar commissioned by the British Museum and Mr Pell. Campbell  was soon to be recalled due to his attempts to influence British politics towards Mehmet Ali, whom he greatly admired.

f2d5cedb-276c-5bcc-adf8-742a01444f80.description2: This photo from Enrico H. Giglioli's collection was collected by the Florentine naturalist while travelling the world between 1865 through 1868 as he advanced diplomatic and commercial affairs between the newborn Italian state and the other nations. The images seem to have been created spontaneously to show ethnocentric diversity. The ethnographic photographs in the Giglioli's collection are part of the historical archive of the Pigorini Museum. The origins of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

f2e1525e-6b39-51de-8e19-c3cca74a4562.name: *A Turkish Coffee-House, Constantinople*
f2e1525e-6b39-51de-8e19-c3cca74a4562.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
f2e1525e-6b39-51de-8e19-c3cca74a4562.description2: Preziosi was of noble Maltese birth, but against the wishes of his family rejected their chosen profession of the law to become an artist. From 1842, until his death forty years later, he lived and worked in Istanbul, renowned for his vibrant and evocative images of all the different races and cultures of that most cosmopolitan of cities. He became for a time well-known in Western Europe because many travellers, (including in 1869 the Prince of Wales) took his pictures home as souvenirs of their visit. Demand for his work prompted the publication in Paris in 1858 of a series of lithographs, Stamboul Recollections of Eastern Life.This is a fine example of Preziosi’s keen observation of contemporary Ottoman life, rapidly sketched yet full of accurately depicted detail.

f2f8e110-2548-568d-9481-67689f396cdc.name: Al-Zubarah
f2f8e110-2548-568d-9481-67689f396cdc.dates: 5th millennium BC; 18th century settlement; abandoned probably at the beginning of the 20th century
f2f8e110-2548-568d-9481-67689f396cdc.history:
Earliest human occupation near the site of al-Zubarah may date back as early as the Late Neolithic period (5th millennium BC). The ceramic assemblage recovered from al-Zubarah site itself is pointing to a possible Abbasid (8th – 9th century AD) occupation, prior to a Late Islamic village existing during the final period of the reign of Safavids in the upper Gulf region (18th century).  
According to the current knowledge, the major development of the town took place after the arrival of the Utub-tribe in northern Qatar. Al-Zubarah flowered during the 2nd half of the 18th century AD and played an important political role until it was totally destroyed after a major attack of Omani led forces in 1811.  
In a second phase of occupation after this event the city was considerably smaller. It never obtained the same importance than the 18th century settlement and by the beginning of the 20th century, the village was probably left abandoned.
f2f8e110-2548-568d-9481-67689f396cdc.description2:
The ruins of Al Zubarah are a traditionally well-known tourist destination in Qatar.  
Recognized as an archaeological site as early as in the 1950es by a Danish led team of archaeologists, the first systematic archaeological excavations were conducted in 1983. Under the direction of the National Museum of Qatar, the Qatari team uncovered several structures in the northern part of the ruins. Later on, the attention was turned to what was identified as the suq area and the inner quarters.

f30a52d1-4558-58b4-bdf7-91782044f03c.name: Brooch
f30a52d1-4558-58b4-bdf7-91782044f03c.author: Ámparo López
f30a52d1-4558-58b4-bdf7-91782044f03c.keywords: Nasrid art; islamic influence; orientalism; collectionism
f30a52d1-4558-58b4-bdf7-91782044f03c.description2: This brooch is part of the contemporary pieces from North Africa collected by Lázara Galdiano. It is important to point out that most of the Spanish collectors and museums not only acquired early Arab pieces of the Middle Ages, but also pieces from the North African or Near Eastern workshops of the mid-19th century or early 20th century, as part of the interest in these countries.

f30ed628-c2e1-59e3-9002-64e3343526ab.name: Karpino Monastery
f30ed628-c2e1-59e3-9002-64e3343526ab.author: Nada Andonovska
f30ed628-c2e1-59e3-9002-64e3343526ab.history: According to the legends, the monastery was originally built in the 14th century, having been set on fire and reconstructed many times. The present-day edifice of the Karpino Monastery dates from 1892, when it was restored to preserve some portions of the structure and frescoes dating from the 16th and 17th centuries. Throughout the Middle Ages, the monastery was a sanctuary for many Macedonian monks who acquired their education to become priests and serve God and the Church. Extensive literary activities were developed there by monks who used to prescribe various liturgical books, manuscripts and other patristic literature. In the late 19th century, monks from the Karpino Monastery formed a public school for teaching children from neighbouring villages.
f30ed628-c2e1-59e3-9002-64e3343526ab.description2: The Karpino Monastery was the cultural and literary centre of the Kumanovo region throughout the Middle Ages. The Church within the Karpino Monastery is dedicated to the Presentation of the Virgin in the Temple. It was built of crafted stone in the form of a single-nave basilica with an apse forming a triconch. Parts of the 16th and 17th-century edifice and wall paintings have been preserved during its reconstruction in 1892, including the frescoes depicting the Virgin and Child, as well as the effigies of St. Theodore Tyron and St. Theodore Stratylates. The exquisite early 17th-century wooden iconostasis has been preserved in the Monastery Church including seven valuable original icons which were painted by Nikola Zoograf and his students.

f310be0c-2e4a-5a7a-ab0c-baaa41091e32.name: *Dokhla* (wedding dress)
f310be0c-2e4a-5a7a-ab0c-baaa41091e32.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
f310be0c-2e4a-5a7a-ab0c-baaa41091e32.keywords: Embroidery from Nabeul; sequins and gold thread
f310be0c-2e4a-5a7a-ab0c-baaa41091e32.materials: Embroidered fabric with gold-plated silver thread
f310be0c-2e4a-5a7a-ab0c-baaa41091e32.description2: This tunic is entirely embroidered with gold-plated silver thread. This is the most important element of the marriage ceremony (jelwa) in Nabeul (Tunisia). The rectangular tunic's splendour comes from its incredibly rich embroidery, which is made of various different silk ribbons, all embellished with tal. In fact, the embroidery entirely covers the fabric itself. The breast and belt areas are embroidered with sequins and gold thread. The tunic is calf-length, and a luxurious pair of silk trousers can be seen beneath, covered in gold embroidery to match the sleeves. In addition to this, one of the bride's many items of jewellery is a great chain of golden rings, a rihana, which she wears with a large necklace made of a scented material. Lastly, the bride's head is covered by an embroidered veil made of muslin and silk.

f31fd223-2144-5b45-8b4a-8cf3c4d36bc5.name: *London-Paris-Constantinople* \[…\] *Orient Express. Paris-Munich-Vienna-Budapest-Belgrade & Constantinople: fast and direct service, without your car and without your passport* \[…\] *Winter 1888–89 ...*
f31fd223-2144-5b45-8b4a-8cf3c4d36bc5.description2: Founded in 1872, the Compagnie Internationale des Wagons-lits was originally a Belgian company. Its founder (Georges Nagelmackers) had the idea of creating a luxury train line, without the need for changes at each border, in order to allow wealthier tourists a more comfortable journey. The opening of the famous Orient Express between Paris and Constantinople in 1883 was an extremely successful example of this.

f36b7d3e-8e7a-5356-9555-d10076d72a09.name: Muhammad Tawfiq Pasha (1852–1892)
f36b7d3e-8e7a-5356-9555-d10076d72a09.keywords: Muhammad Tawfiq Pasha; Egypt; Arabi (Urabi) revolution; Great Britain
f36b7d3e-8e7a-5356-9555-d10076d72a09.description2: Portrait of Muhammad Tawfiq Pasha (1852–1892). After the deposition of his father Ismail Pasha, Muhammad Tawfiq took over the government in Egypt. The Arabi revolution diminished his power radically. In 1882 he asked for help from Great Britain. British troops suppressed the Arabi revolution and occupied Egypt. Muhammad Tawfiq became ruler at the grace of the British government.

f3942bb8-28a9-5994-bff0-f962391fad28.name: Sanayeh Garden
f3942bb8-28a9-5994-bff0-f962391fad28.description: This green lung of the city is very popular among the neighbourhood residents. The garden features a large Ottoman fountain and covers a total surface area of 22,000 square metres.
f3942bb8-28a9-5994-bff0-f962391fad28.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
f3942bb8-28a9-5994-bff0-f962391fad28.history: The garden is one of the oldest public open-air spaces in the capital. Khalil Pasha (1864–1923), commander of the Turkish Sixth Army during World War I, had the park built in 1907. The park has had many names since its construction in the early 20th century, It was first called the Hamidi Public Garden, but was renamed the René Muawad Garden in honour of President René Muawad, who was assassinated nearby on November 22, 1989. However, it has been referred to as Sanayeh Park by the public for decades.
f3942bb8-28a9-5994-bff0-f962391fad28.keywords: Beirut; Sanayeh; Garden; Public; Space; René Muawad

f3955418-aaed-57fc-96f9-18195a4d076b.name: *Atik Valide Mosque*
f3955418-aaed-57fc-96f9-18195a4d076b.keywords: Painting; Hüseyin Zekai Pasha; orientalist Turkish painters
f3955418-aaed-57fc-96f9-18195a4d076b.description2: The majority of Turkish painters in the 19th century were Ottoman officers who had studied abroad. Hüseyin Zekai Pasha was one of those painters. Following his education at the Kuleli Military High School, he continued his studies at the Military Academy (*Mektebi Harbiye*), where he had a chance to learn technical drawing and perspective. His first period was realistic and his pictorial representation includes scenes or events from everyday life. In his first works, Hüseyin Zekai Pasha followed the painting tradition of 19th century, including thin paint dough and light colours. He made changes in his techniques through the Galatasaray Exhibition and eventually he turned into an impressionist whose work was dominated by thicker brush strokes.

f398bf92-d6b1-56a3-bb47-793d5811643e.name: Models of traditional agricultural environment in Egypt and Sudan and the life in the Egyptian oases at Fu`ad Agricultural Museum
f398bf92-d6b1-56a3-bb47-793d5811643e.dates: 16 January 1938 (Photos taken during the inauguration of the museum)
f398bf92-d6b1-56a3-bb47-793d5811643e.description2: The Fu`ad Agriculture Museum was considered the first of its kind in the Middle East and the Arab World during the 1930s. It was inaugurated during the time of King Faruq, the son of King Fu`ad, and houses a large number of collections related to agricultural and rural environments, as well as agricultural plants and animals.

f441f874-4d85-5d61-a241-aca16296bfa2.name: Programme card for the Exposition Universelle of 1900. Phono-Cinéma-Théâtre.
f441f874-4d85-5d61-a241-aca16296bfa2.keywords: World fairs; Paris; cinema; Frères Lumière
f441f874-4d85-5d61-a241-aca16296bfa2.description2: World fairs were an opportunity to discover new inventions, and to make them known worldwide. The "cinematograph" was present, in various forms, at the 1900 Exposition Universelle in Paris. The invention of the "Phono-Cinéma-Théâtre" brought sound and image together for the first time, and Henri Lioret and Clément-Maurice Gratioulet used a phonograph to combine the voices and images of famous actors such as Sarah Bernhardt.

f455e6ad-2c78-5838-b5a1-f48b1f307561.name: Hammouda Pacha Mosque
f455e6ad-2c78-5838-b5a1-f48b1f307561.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
f455e6ad-2c78-5838-b5a1-f48b1f307561.history: This mosque was built on top of the kasbah by the Muradid sovereign, Hammouda Pacha Bey, in the 17th century, and was modelled on the Turkish mosque built by Youssef Dey near the Sidi Ahmed Ben Arous *zawiya* on the intersection between Rue Sidi Ben Arous and the kasbah. The mosque is also located near the Great Zaytuna Mosque, which gave these new Hanafi masters some legitimacy.
f455e6ad-2c78-5838-b5a1-f48b1f307561.description2: The Hammouda Pacha Mosque is an example of a new type of architecture, with a square floor and a pyramid roof with green tiles. The décor is rich and varied, featuring many panels in carved stucco and marquetery, with alternating motifs on a black and white marble base, and elements of baroque decorations can be seen on the façade of the *tourba*. Other innovative elements include a V-shaped courtyard, an octagonal minaret and a mausoleum (tourbet). This mausoleum marked the opening of the first funerary mosque in Tunis, which creates a link between the place of worship and the founder's tomb.

f4606868-6540-5152-bd07-486c73a7f541.name: Jug
f4606868-6540-5152-bd07-486c73a7f541.description2: Çanakkale was a pottery production centre between the end of 17th century and first quarter of the 20th century where pottery with interesting and original forms was produced. Mostly coarse red clay and occasionally beige-coloured paste was used. This vase has pear-like shape with a long neck. On its neck there are three horn-like projecting forms. On the sides and in the front there are embossed decorations.

f4c22e70-95b9-576e-af85-4267539e8ace.name: Précis Historique de la Traite des Noirs et de l'Esclavage Colonial
f4c22e70-95b9-576e-af85-4267539e8ace.description2: This illustration, taken from the Précis Historique de la Traite des Noirs et de l'Esclavage Colonial  had didactic objectives. It attempted to show the inhuman treatment slaves were subjected to (yoke, chains, whipping) by traders. In this image, a mother is begging King Charles X of France to spare her son this dark fate and abolish slavery. However, even though the National Convention did abolish slavery in 1794, Napoléon Bonaparte then reintroduced it to most of the territories under French control.

f4d69a3e-9925-5ec2-a00c-7db5ff29d9d2.name: Register listing 'all of the subjects of the Grand Duke of Tuscany [Italy] residing in Tunisia'
f4d69a3e-9925-5ec2-a00c-7db5ff29d9d2.author: Massimo Sanacore
f4d69a3e-9925-5ec2-a00c-7db5ff29d9d2.archival: ASLi, Governo civile e militare, b. 433
f4d69a3e-9925-5ec2-a00c-7db5ff29d9d2.third_name: *Stato nominativo di tutti i Sudditi di Sua Altezza Reale il Gran Duca di Toscana residenti in Tunisi*
f4d69a3e-9925-5ec2-a00c-7db5ff29d9d2.description2:
The names appearing in this list are mostly Jewish, including that of Giacomo Castelnuovo (Livorno, Italy, 1819 – La Goulette, Tunisia, 1886), a medical doctor who had to flee Italy because of his liberal ideas and his support for Italy’s national unification. Initially he went to Egypt, where he founded two Italian newspapers, *Lo Spettatore Egiziano* and *Il Progresso d’Egitto*.  
The author of many medical publications, in Tunis Castelnuovo became the Bey’s personal physician. He served as president of the Tunisian branch of the Alliance Israélite Universelle, and promoted the construction of a synagogue, on a plot of land granted by the Bey.  
A Freemason, he fought in Italy in the wars for Italy’s unification. He was awarded honours by both the Italian King (who ennobled him) and by the Bey of Tunis.

f4ee2a86-2553-5a0f-a698-a195e71a3ffd.description2: This drawing shows an important moment in modern Tunisian history: the signing of the treaty of the French Protectorate over the Tunisian regency, at the Palais Kassar Saïd, in Bardo, on 12 May 1881. The main players are featured in this drawing, namely Sadok Bey who ruled Tunisia from 1859 to 1882, with his hand resting on the table, and to his right the general Jules Aimé Bréart, the leader of the invading French troops.

f596dba8-2ee8-5042-9e06-4a090887dd12.name: Armchair of Krste Petkov Misirkov
f596dba8-2ee8-5042-9e06-4a090887dd12.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
f596dba8-2ee8-5042-9e06-4a090887dd12.description2: Krste Petkov Misirkov (1874–1926) was an imposing figure that contributed to the standardization of the modern Macedonian language. He lived and worked in St. Petersburg, Russia. Misirkov’s book “On Macedonian Matters” is a starting point in explaining Macedonian distinctiveness, having served as an intellectual and contemplative engine for generations of Macedonians fighting in the battlefield and in literature alike.

There are two holes on the base indicates how it was fixed on a post. The standard used to be hold by a guard in front of the palace gate, it belongs to king Hussein I 1853–1931.

f5b47725-414d-52d8-902a-bee467f7d304.name: *Works for the opening of the Corinth Canal*
f5b47725-414d-52d8-902a-bee467f7d304.author: Maria Dimitriadou
f5b47725-414d-52d8-902a-bee467f7d304.description2:
The Corinth Canal being dug, circa 1885. Photographer unknown.  
The Corinth Canal separates the Peloponnesian peninsula from the Greek. The idea of the canal was revived after Greece gained independence but soon abandoned due to economical reasons. The opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 gave an new impetus and the following year, the Zaimis government passed a law authorising the construction of the canal, which was formally inaugurated on 23 April 1882. Zaimis assigned the project to the Hungarian István Türr who set up the Société Internationale du Canal Maritime de Corinthe but the company failed and the project was finished by the company of Andeas Syngros. The canal was designed by the Hungarian engineer Béla Gerster with the assistance of the French Vincent Dauzants, a chief engineer of the Suez canal.

f5eca8aa-876e-503f-b619-df15835f81aa.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
f5eca8aa-876e-503f-b619-df15835f81aa.description2: This silver necklace from Grande Kabylie was traditionally worn on a woman's bosom to hold the *ddill*, a finely woven cloth worn by women of the region. It is made of of two ornate brooches with a coral in the centre, connected by a gold chain necklace to which the jeweller has added various French coins (francs) that were no longer in use. A number of jewellers used coins to decorate their jewellery. They usually used coins which had suddenly gone out of use.

f659e676-c7e7-5974-ace5-795fdd1ed49b.name: *Bayt Lisbuna, Damascus*
f659e676-c7e7-5974-ace5-795fdd1ed49b.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
f659e676-c7e7-5974-ace5-795fdd1ed49b.author: Stefan Weber
f659e676-c7e7-5974-ace5-795fdd1ed49b.second_name: Inhabitants in the courtyard demonstrating the new style of decoration and clothing
f659e676-c7e7-5974-ace5-795fdd1ed49b.description2: The Bayt Lisbuna saw two major construction phases. The existing structures date from the 19th century (around 1810) and were remodelled after 1865 and 1872. This house of a Jewish family like many other houses of Muslim or Christian families underwent major changes in style and plan at the end of the 19th and beginning of the 20th centuries. Several thousand private homes were adopted to the new modern style, with a radical change in techniques and forms of decoration. While still being a Damascene courtyard house these monuments of private taste became witness of a comprehensive urban change in the light of an entangled modernity.

f672a566-07c0-5def-83e1-f7239ef4cf19.name: Cup with *merletto* ('lace') decoration
f672a566-07c0-5def-83e1-f7239ef4cf19.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
f672a566-07c0-5def-83e1-f7239ef4cf19.author: Marina Minozzi
f672a566-07c0-5def-83e1-f7239ef4cf19.keywords: Applied arts; minor arts; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; model; reproduction; decoration; motifs; collection; collector; glass; Murano glass; glasswork; zoomorphysm; zoomorphic; lace; Venice; Victorian; Quattrocento
f672a566-07c0-5def-83e1-f7239ef4cf19.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, as part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. The tendency of Murano's industries in using bizarre shapes, often of zoomorphic inspiration, gave life to manufacts not so much functional as decorative. It was very successful. The cylindrical cup in green glass with white glaze and “lace” decoration is the result of a combination of common design details in the second half of the 19th century: while it shows a Victorian decoration, the structure of the object recalls a late 14th century model.
f672a566-07c0-5def-83e1-f7239ef4cf19.holding_institution_org: Museo Artistico Industriale presso la Galleria nazionale d’arte antica in Palazzo Barberini

f6a4d871-3bbf-5f91-943b-4fb7cd618871.name: Saddle (*serj*)
f6a4d871-3bbf-5f91-943b-4fb7cd618871.description: A saddle (*serj*) crafted in Rabat in the 19th century, but making use of British imports such as velvet (*nta‘a*), leather and gold thread.
f6a4d871-3bbf-5f91-943b-4fb7cd618871.keywords: Craftsmanship; traditional craftsmanship; Moroccan craftsmen; leather; leatherwork; trade; raw material; finished products; British in Morocco; horsemanship

f6a973df-a6b0-51b8-8bb0-fd4026b06319.name: Photograph of Ion Ghica (sitting)
f6a973df-a6b0-51b8-8bb0-fd4026b06319.description2: In 1848, Ion Ghica was the envoy of the Wallachian revolutionaries to Istanbul, where he remained after the suppression of the revolution. He created connections among the Ottoman officials, being appreciated by Reshid-Pasha (Grand Vizier from 1854), and became a supporter of the Romanian Principalities’ union under Ottoman sovereignty. A former journalist, he devised the project (not realized) for an economic and literary periodical, published in all the languages spoken in the Empire. In 1854 he was appointed governor of the island of Samos, where he took measures against piracy and founded several schools (a middle school, an agricultural school, a marine school and a girls’ institute). His activity earned him the title of “prince”(bey) of Samos, which he received from sultan Abdülmecid in February 1856.

f6ba7168-fb9b-59f4-96f4-181869aa5b52.name: *The Battle on Dealu Spirii*
f6ba7168-fb9b-59f4-96f4-181869aa5b52.description2: In June 1848 revolution broke out in Wallachia. In terms of relations with the Ottoman Empire, Wallachia’s suzerain, revolutionaries claimed the administrative and legislative independence of the country. In the autumn, as negotiations with the revolutionaries proved unsuccessful, the Sublime Porte decided to intervene militarily. On the 13th of September, Bucharest was attacked. The battle that took place on Dealu Spirii between the Ottoman army and the Romanian soldiers helped by a company of firefighters was won by the former. Afterwards, the Ottoman sovereignty over the Romanian countries was re-imposed. The lithograph is entitled *The fight of the Romanian soldiers with the numerous column of the Ottoman army* and below the drawing a short text describes the battle.

f6ce25ef-e196-51ea-878e-f582be55dc3a.name: Petrie and typology
f6ce25ef-e196-51ea-878e-f582be55dc3a.description2: In 1890 Petrie carried out a six-week season of excavations at Tell el-Hesy (as he transliterated it), which he identified, wrongly, as the ancient city of Lachish.  This was the first proper archaeological excavation ever carried out in Palestine, and in the course of this single season Petrie established the principle of dating strata by the pottery which they contained, thus establishing the outlines of the archaeological sequence, which continues to be refined to this day. This section drawing was made by Frederick Jones Bliss, who continued Petrie’s excavations from 1892–1894.

f6d57164-e259-50a0-ab24-9a96f4a486a0.name: Postcard – Hospital in Bucharest, built between 1835-1838

f6f098bc-4e9c-5171-b766-ca9c47aabe50.name: New maps
f6f098bc-4e9c-5171-b766-ca9c47aabe50.description2: Sgt. George Armstrong, R.E., who was a key member of the Survey Party, later made a 3D ‘Raised Contour Map’ of Palestine from the 2D maps originally produced. This was shown all over the western world, and won him a medal at the St. Louis World’s Fair in 1903. It was the first such map ever constructed of Palestine, and served to introduce scholars and the public to the nature of the landscape in a way that no previous maps had done.

f7033496-607e-547b-91fa-2429e3eba90a.name: Portrait of Nawfal Ni'mat Allah Nawfal
f7033496-607e-547b-91fa-2429e3eba90a.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
f7033496-607e-547b-91fa-2429e3eba90a.description2: Nawfal Ni'mat Allah Nawfal was born in Tripoli in 1812. He studied first in Tripoli then in Egypt, after moving there with his father. In 1828 he returned to Lebanon and was hired as an accountant in the wilayat of Tripoli. He remained in this post for seven years, before moving briefly to Beirut and then back to Tripoli. Upon his death, he donated his vast library to the Syrian Protestant College (now the American University of Beirut). He wrote several books on literature, and had many articles published in popular contemporary newspapers, such as *Lisasn al-Hal*. He died in 1887.

f7200f78-5313-51de-bc47-0097fe1cd9c2.name: Image of one of the newly excavated cuneiform tablets from Nineveh, by pioneer photographer Roger Fenton, c. 1852

f7cee5d1-1e01-5071-9419-091425349403.name: Dictionary of Three Languages
f7cee5d1-1e01-5071-9419-091425349403.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
f7cee5d1-1e01-5071-9419-091425349403.description2: The *Dictionary of Three Languages* by Gjorgji Pullevski (1822–1893) shows the political context and coexistence of Macedonians, Albanians and Turks in the territory of Macedonia. It also provides evidence of the awakening of the national spirit of Macedonian people. The dictionary has 190 pages in paperback. It gives words in Macedonian, Albanian and Turkish in three columns. Despite its orthographic errors, the dictionary provides a valuable source for studying of the evolution of the Macedonian language.

f7fde934-bd37-5990-9d4a-995069413fad.name: Textile
f7fde934-bd37-5990-9d4a-995069413fad.description: Textile with stencilled decoration with Arab calligraphy. The textile surface has different shades.

f88cd52e-27ec-5aee-beba-ea252bcda254.name: *Gunsmiths at the Palace of the Alhambra*
f88cd52e-27ec-5aee-beba-ea252bcda254.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
f88cd52e-27ec-5aee-beba-ea252bcda254.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
f88cd52e-27ec-5aee-beba-ea252bcda254.description2: This painting, entitled 'Gunsmiths at the Palace of the Alhambra, Granada' is a romantic, Orientalist phantasy designed to pander to the taste of 19th-century Europeans fascinated by the palace complex in particular since the publication of Washington Irving's 'Tales of the Alhambra' after his stay in Granada in 1828, and that of the British artist and designer Owen Jones, entitled 'Plans, Elevantions, Sections and Details of the Alhambra',  published in twelve parts between 1836 and 1845. Owen's work in particular, with its numerous precise architectural drawings and detailed speculations regarding the Alhambra's original colour schemes, was to exert a revolutionary influence on the European artists of his time, and there is little doubt that the Italian artist Filippo Baratti, too, consulted Owen's work in elaborating his painting's colour scheme, depicting especially the stuccoed walls in hues familiar from Owen's reconstructions.

f89cf7b6-1d81-540b-9de6-dc2fc4a7ec9d.name: Portrait of Queen Maria II

f8c2bcec-57eb-5f11-8bfe-5d3461e46436.name: Lute
f8c2bcec-57eb-5f11-8bfe-5d3461e46436.description:
Plucked instrument with four double orders. The headstock is inlaid with silver motifs. It has eight round pins decorated with flowers which end in bone buttons. The nut is also made of bone. The fingerboard is adorned with marquetry and inlay work and has been partially restored; it has no frets.  
The lid is decorated with a quite flamboyant pierced rosette. The bridge is made of bone and wood with stars decoration. The wavy tailpiece is made of wood. The neck is decorated with marquetry in two colours forming a zigzag. The soundboard is concave and consists of eleven staves.

f8cd2cbd-0428-53e7-a7ce-f3ee1f3011f9.name: Shelving unit
f8cd2cbd-0428-53e7-a7ce-f3ee1f3011f9.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
f8cd2cbd-0428-53e7-a7ce-f3ee1f3011f9.description2: This unit is made of two shelves, one in an arch shape and the second topped by small hooks and a perforated decoration. The name of its maker, "Becghtache" is written on its underside, flanked by two six-point stars.

f8e91c25-98ab-5b7c-8cb2-16ce5beb2795.name: 25 Syrian Piastres
f8e91c25-98ab-5b7c-8cb2-16ce5beb2795.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury
f8e91c25-98ab-5b7c-8cb2-16ce5beb2795.keywords: Commerce; trade; Currency; Coins; coinage; Numismatics
f8e91c25-98ab-5b7c-8cb2-16ce5beb2795.description2: This 25 piastres bank note was printed by Bradbury Wilkinson and Co (BWC) without a watermark.

f913a36e-6a1b-5710-a0b7-52e815a3703a.name: Arab Room
f913a36e-6a1b-5710-a0b7-52e815a3703a.description: The Arab Room shows the collections of the Marquis coming not only from Arabia but also from China, Japan, the Philippines, Turkey, Morocco and New Zealand. He collected and displayed these works, similar to other European palaces of the 19th Century, because his taste ran to oriental, exotic, foreign or ancestral cultures. This room was also known as *fumoir*, associated with smoking, essentially thought for masculine use. The ceiling is decorated with interlacing designs and six-pointed star in the middle, from which hangs a superb Arab lamp. There are kilims on the walls and carpets on the floor and furniture. Among all, we can also find arms and armouries, musical instruments and six scale-model reproducing walls and windows from some rooms of the Alhambra palace.
f913a36e-6a1b-5710-a0b7-52e815a3703a.author: Cristina Giménez

f918b78f-57d9-5c0d-a75f-075ce7156c35.name: Dagger
f918b78f-57d9-5c0d-a75f-075ce7156c35.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
f918b78f-57d9-5c0d-a75f-075ce7156c35.author: Huda Kilani
f918b78f-57d9-5c0d-a75f-075ce7156c35.materials: Silver, iron; casting, incised and niello
f918b78f-57d9-5c0d-a75f-075ce7156c35.description2: Silver knife with silver handle and niello decoration on the front; metal on the backside and four Turkish coins along the edge of the sheath; a name (‘Jomaah Ali’) is inscribed on the blade of the dagger. This object is functional and can be used in everyday activities, but at the same time it is a prestigious object that every Bedouin man must have. The most common types of daggers in Jordan are the Yemeni dagger, the Hijazi and other local types.

f92e54e2-12d0-5aaf-9ae2-ccb42b9f2df7.name: The monuments in the Hippodrome surrounded by protective fences
f92e54e2-12d0-5aaf-9ae2-ccb42b9f2df7.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
f92e54e2-12d0-5aaf-9ae2-ccb42b9f2df7.description2: Robertson’s Istanbul photographs are concerned primarily with the city’s historical monuments. They reveal the city’s magnificent Byzantine and Ottoman structures from different angles and with close-ups taken in an approach that is usually quite aesthetic. A frequently employed device in Robertson's photographs is the inclusion of the one or more human figures in the foreground – indeed, this is something of a trademark of Robertson’s work. In this photo, the monuments in the Hippodrome are surrounded by protective fences.

f936f85a-a23f-55c1-ba78-3750eb672753.name: Portrait of Hajj Husayn Bayham
f936f85a-a23f-55c1-ba78-3750eb672753.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
f936f85a-a23f-55c1-ba78-3750eb672753.description2: Born in Beirut in 1833, Hajj Husayn Bayham studied under great masters such as Shaykh 'Abd Allah Khalid and Shaykh Muhammad al-Hut. He mainly worked in public posts, including the council of the wilayet of Saida, the tribunal of commerce and the municipal council. He also wrote poetry in his spare time and had a vast collection of works in his private library. In 1878 he was elected to represent Beirut in the Ottoman parliament. He died in 1881.

f939b530-8866-5fba-afa5-e436e2211419.name: Rich drawing
f939b530-8866-5fba-afa5-e436e2211419.description2: Portrait of a standing male Yezidi from Sinjar. Claudius Rich made observations and drawings not only of sites but also of people. Early travellers often studied the customs and costumes of local peoples, as well as drawing landscapes or mapping territories. There was no such thing as a professional archaeologist yet.

f93ac236-5e79-538f-9787-749f853c9165.name: *Turin: The Antonelliana Mole*
f93ac236-5e79-538f-9787-749f853c9165.holder: Central Institute for Cataloguing and Documentation (ICCD)

f94fb43c-ce0a-57b2-b9cb-171b27871fa2.name: *Arabs of the Desert*
f94fb43c-ce0a-57b2-b9cb-171b27871fa2.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
f94fb43c-ce0a-57b2-b9cb-171b27871fa2.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
f94fb43c-ce0a-57b2-b9cb-171b27871fa2.description2: The constant movement of large Bedouin confederations regularly impacted on the history of the Middle East, in particular when it affected settled societies and cities.This print provides much interesting detail about the dress of the Bedouin at the time David Roberts visited the Near East in 1838/9. The individual in the foreground wears a white turban and short gown with belt, a dark red jacket and a voluminous, all-enveloping blue cloak. His legs remain uncovered, and he wears simple leather sandals on his feet. A formidable dagger or khanjar in its sheath is secured in his belt, and he carries a long slender gun through a sling. The bullets for the gun appear to be secured in an ammunition belt strapped diagonally across his chest. In the background, four male figures wearing striped headscarfs and cloaks as well as short white gowns and holdings lances appear on the right. On the left, a bedouin leads his camels away. The inscription states: *Arabs of the tribe of Benisaid, Feb. 17th 1839*.
f94fb43c-ce0a-57b2-b9cb-171b27871fa2.artist_birthplace: David Roberts: Edinburgh, Scotland; Louis Hague: Tournai, Belgium
f94fb43c-ce0a-57b2-b9cb-171b27871fa2.artist_deathplace: David Roberts: London; Louis Hague: London

f95568b2-4453-57ae-8628-5bcd17d70b23.name: Tray with Oriental landscape
f95568b2-4453-57ae-8628-5bcd17d70b23.description: Following the Turkish style, this tray is depicted with an Orientalist landscape that might be related to the Greek War of Independence. The man on the left is dressed in the Greek skirt called *fustanella*, worn to fight against the Ottoman Empire. The different clothes of the man on the right who is turning his back may be identified with those of a Turkish warrior or janissary.
f95568b2-4453-57ae-8628-5bcd17d70b23.author: Isabel Ortega Fernández
f95568b2-4453-57ae-8628-5bcd17d70b23.materials: Moulded; enamelled, painted and gilded earthenware

f9783bd6-7a5b-5ca2-8a70-781a2af32872.name: Cross chain
f9783bd6-7a5b-5ca2-8a70-781a2af32872.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
f9783bd6-7a5b-5ca2-8a70-781a2af32872.author: Huda Kilani
f9783bd6-7a5b-5ca2-8a70-781a2af32872.description2: A cross of silver on a silver chain known with the folkloric name “heal of gazelle”, worn by Christian women. Silver was the most common jewellery; only rich people used gold. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom. This object illustrates the variegated religious composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It also demonstrates personal attire, fashion, local costumes and rites.

f9783fd3-09a2-5548-be22-593259d96e06.name: Fragment of the Parthenon frieze
f9783fd3-09a2-5548-be22-593259d96e06.description: The climax of the Greater Panathenaia, the chief festival of Athens, held in honour of Athena, was a procession which ended with the presentation of the newly woven peplos (a woman’s garment) to the tutelary goddess of the city. This is the subject of the frieze around the cella of the Parthenon, the temple on the Athenian Acropolis. This fragment shows two bearded elder citizens of Athens in conversation.
f9783fd3-09a2-5548-be22-593259d96e06.holder: Kunsthistorisches Museum, Collection of Greek and Roman Antiquities

f9788b95-591f-522c-bd57-84003553fdd9.name: *Üçetek entari*
f9788b95-591f-522c-bd57-84003553fdd9.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
f9788b95-591f-522c-bd57-84003553fdd9.description2: The attire of Ottoman women included dresses for the outdoors and the indoors. Starting from early 19th century, dresses called *üçetek* (dress with three skirts) and *dörtetek* (dress with four skirts) became fashionable. As relations with Europe increased, women in Istanbul started to use imported European textiles for their new dresses. This *üçetek entari* (dress with three skirts) is made of a soft red-coloured *canfes* (fine-textured shiny silk fabric) embroidered in the laid cord technique. The robe has a long trailing skirt, wrist-length sleeves and a stand-up collar. It fastens across the chest with button loops and plaited buttons. Along the edges of the skirt, sleeves, slits and seams are undulating floral designs embroidered in coloured silk cord.

f986df26-3b71-5c3e-8d5b-1a8c60864ea5.name: Yemeni dagger
f986df26-3b71-5c3e-8d5b-1a8c60864ea5.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
f986df26-3b71-5c3e-8d5b-1a8c60864ea5.author: Huda Kilani
f986df26-3b71-5c3e-8d5b-1a8c60864ea5.keywords: double edged blade; hilts; geometric designs; silver filigree; suspension rings; arms; armours; metalwork; fashion; accessories
f986df26-3b71-5c3e-8d5b-1a8c60864ea5.description2: A dagger with a double-edged blade, an oblong-head hilt and silver filigree work in geometric designs; it is carried on a woollen belt with leather strap-work, usually with six asymmetrical suspension rings. Yemeni and Hijazi daggers have different shapes and their diffusion on the territory of Jordan shows how population movements, trade and exchange were common in the area.

f99fda0f-bbfe-5494-9147-d4cccb13620e.name: *Théâtre du Châtelet. Germinal*
f99fda0f-bbfe-5494-9147-d4cccb13620e.description2: The thirteenth novel in the *Rougon-Macquart* series, *Germinal* (1885), is the most well-known and the most discussed of Zola's works. This naturalist writer took a new approach to depicting workers' lives, shedding light on miners' terrible working conditions and the violence and difficulty of strikes. Fearing that the adaptation of this novel for stage would trigger social unrest, the play was initially banned. It was finally performed for the first time in 1888 at the Théâtre du Châtelet. This poster highlights the most important themes of the novel - life in the mine, strikes, etc.

f9ae9656-29ab-534b-a02c-90fe95d65205.name: Three pairs of clogs
f9ae9656-29ab-534b-a02c-90fe95d65205.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
f9ae9656-29ab-534b-a02c-90fe95d65205.description2: Wooden clogs such as these have a long history in the Middle East, emerging before the Middle Ages and remaining popular for centuries to come. They were made of a variety of woods, including walnut, apricot, willow, poplar, or beech. The wood was cut into wedge shapes then moulded around the foot of the wearer. Excess wood was then shaved off, the heel attached, and the wood painted and polished. Leather girdles in a variety of colours were fixed to the heel with special nails and the wood would often be decorated with mosaics of bone or seashells organised in geometric or floral patterns. These shoes were designed to be comfortable and resistant to water, and thus were usually worn at home, particularly by women.

f9bb568b-afa8-55b3-9d37-45f6a17b547a.name: Dish
f9bb568b-afa8-55b3-9d37-45f6a17b547a.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
f9bb568b-afa8-55b3-9d37-45f6a17b547a.materials: Tin-glazed earthenware, painted in cobalt blue
f9bb568b-afa8-55b3-9d37-45f6a17b547a.description2: Fez is an important centre for Moroccan pottery and is particularly associated with a distinctive form of blue and white ceramic ware which became popular in the late 19th century. This dish, or *tabsil*, was used to serve foods with a sauce. The dish was donated to the V&A by George Maw, founder of Maw & Co., a British manufacturer of ceramic tiles. The company won many medals and awards at the international exhibitions which were a feature of the late 19th century. This dish was displayed at the 1871 Annual International Exhibition held in London. A label on its base suggests that it was loaned to the exhibition by George Maw.

f9c5a022-ba1e-5b5b-a490-3b54263c0271.name: *Daffah khachyya*
f9c5a022-ba1e-5b5b-a490-3b54263c0271.description2: This was purchased from Sheikh Sa\`ud’s family collection in 2001. The cloak is handmade and hand embroidered, made from heavy black wool. It is estimated to be older than 1960, between the 1940’s and the 1950’s. It is speculated that it was used by the Bedouins from eastern Saudi Arabia. It is called *daffah khachyya* and not *bisht*. *Khachyya* is the man who would have been involved in making the cloaks.

f9ed44c8-8799-58bf-be2f-32f20262a305.name: *The conquest of Sidon by Austrian troops, September 27th, 1840*
f9ed44c8-8799-58bf-be2f-32f20262a305.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
f9ed44c8-8799-58bf-be2f-32f20262a305.keywords: Saida; Archduke Friedrich; Austrian army; Ottoman army; war; warfare
f9ed44c8-8799-58bf-be2f-32f20262a305.description2: During the oriental crisis of 1840 – as a result of the conflict in the Eastern Mediterranean between Egypt and the Ottoman Empire – a mixed squadron of British, Turkish and Austrian ships under the command of British Admiral Sir Charles John Napier (1786–1860) bombarded the city of Sidon on September 26th. The next day, allied Austrian and British troops landed and conquered Sidon. Josef Schönbrunner, an Austrian illustrator and restorer who was an alumnus of the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, duplicated the original by Leander Russ (1809–1864) in a very dignified way.

f9ee0d73-2194-52be-a145-0cbd7e94a50f.name: Migrants waiting for embarkation at the port of Naples
f9ee0d73-2194-52be-a145-0cbd7e94a50f.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
f9ee0d73-2194-52be-a145-0cbd7e94a50f.holding_institution_org: Biblioteca di Storia Moderna e Contemporanea

f9f0db9c-6034-5d02-b5c8-8b68a3f973f3.name: Beykoz glass - cup
f9f0db9c-6034-5d02-b5c8-8b68a3f973f3.author: Mina Moraitou
f9f0db9c-6034-5d02-b5c8-8b68a3f973f3.description2: Cup decorated with a stripped band, floral motifs and in the centre a circular medallion with a basket of fruits. It was made in the workshops of Istanbul on the Asian side. The basket with the fruit motif is a known motif of the 18th century as for example in the decoration of the private chambers of sultan Ahmed III (1703–1730) at the Topkapi Palace, and on the fountains of Istanbul. Ottoman glass of the 19th century was developed in order to compete with the imported glass from Venice and Bohemia. The technique is European but the decoration Ottoman.

fa113d57-874f-5262-96a7-d769cd7f7fd8.name: Tunic (*Djellaba*)
fa113d57-874f-5262-96a7-d769cd7f7fd8.description: *Djellaba* made in tabby or plain weave, with a striped decoration from the different wefts thread colours. The origin of this design was travels by Fortuny to North Africa in the 1930s.
fa113d57-874f-5262-96a7-d769cd7f7fd8.holder: Museum of Costume, Ethnographical Heritage Research Centre
fa113d57-874f-5262-96a7-d769cd7f7fd8.author: Elvira González
fa113d57-874f-5262-96a7-d769cd7f7fd8.materials: Cotton; tabby or plain weave, printed

fa167dcd-aecd-50c2-9f06-7fb3d8cf9248.name: *Description de L'Egypte: Antiquités Planches*
fa167dcd-aecd-50c2-9f06-7fb3d8cf9248.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. The *Description de l'Égypte* was a series of publications, appearing first in 1809 and continuing until the final volume in 1829, which offered a comprehensive scientific description of ancient and modern Egypt as well as its natural history. It is the collaborative work of about 160 civilian scholars and scientists, known popularly as the savants, who accompanied Napoleon's expedition to Egypt in 1798 to 1801 as part of the French Revolutionary Wars, as well as about 2000 artists and technicians, including 400 engravers, who would later compile it into a full work.

fa5098a6-c21a-55a5-9278-ef4b943a399c.name: Arched house
fa5098a6-c21a-55a5-9278-ef4b943a399c.description: The internal layout varied from house to house: the distribution of rooms, the location of the gallery, the regularity of the plan, or the inclusion of a protruding/external central element. As the house is organised around a large central arc, the different wings open up onto a central arcade rather than directly communicating with each other. The arcade itself serves as a porch and a circulation space, facilitating transition and structuring life around the open air. During the colder months, however, a reception room indoors is used as the house's centrepiece.
fa5098a6-c21a-55a5-9278-ef4b943a399c.author: Jeff El-Msanne, David Andos
fa5098a6-c21a-55a5-9278-ef4b943a399c.history: The "arcade house" is a relatively old architectural style which was in vogue mostly before the 19th century. This style of house can be found in both rural and urban settings, and even within walled cities (?), as demonstrated by old photographs of Beirut. These houses were generally built with *ramleh* stone and a slanted roof. The house was designed on a principle of scalability, meaning it was able to grow in size without altering its internal logic.

fa8521f5-5b5a-5099-8913-7567fa1ba0ab.name: A moneylender's kit
fa8521f5-5b5a-5099-8913-7567fa1ba0ab.description2: In the first half of the 19th century, before the first banks were founded in Wallachia and Moldavia, moneylenders were the ones who dealt with money loaning and with currency exchange, in an economy which did not have yet a national coin. In Romanian they used to be called "zarafi", a term borrowed from the Turkish language. Most of them were Greek, Armenian and Jewish. They often travelled abroad to buy money, one of their main destinations being Istanbul.

faa81141-8f06-589d-906c-e5429a4e007b.name: Pipe
faa81141-8f06-589d-906c-e5429a4e007b.description: Meerschaum, sepiolite or écume de mer, is a porous mineral founded chiefly in Anatolia. Highly valued in pipe manufacturing since the late 18th century, the most famous meerschaum pipes in 19th century were those from Vienna or Paris. Due to commercial competition, new techniques were introduced. This pipe is an example of a patented French production that reproduced meerschaum pipes and cut the production price. This pipe in the shape of a young man’s head is not functional and merely decorative, and was collected by Antonio del Valle y Serrano, marquis of Villa-Huerta, in Mâcon (France), were he also collected souvenirs related to the famous poet Lamartine.
faa81141-8f06-589d-906c-e5429a4e007b.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes

fad948f2-d0c2-5464-bdb7-928c173eeccf.holder: Central Institute for Cataloguing and Documentation (ICCD)
