fb1f37eb-4321-5359-9fa3-0765c8b97a43.name: *Produits L'Algerie. Algerian products at the Paris Universal Exhibition, 1855*
fb1f37eb-4321-5359-9fa3-0765c8b97a43.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
fb1f37eb-4321-5359-9fa3-0765c8b97a43.description2: A view of the Paris Universal Exhibition of 1855 showing products from Algeria and a sign with the text 'Voir Galerie Superieure Autres Produits L'Algerie'.

fb2abd3f-4014-5c92-a525-a24db70c968b.name: Map of the 1877–1878 war
fb2abd3f-4014-5c92-a525-a24db70c968b.description2: This map shows the theatre of operations during the Russian-Ottoman war of 1877–1878, which for Romania represents her independence war. In April 1877, Romania signed a secret military convention with Russia, who was on the eve of a new war with the Ottoman Empire, allowing her troops to cross the Romanian territory in order to get south of the Danube. Because in May the Ottomans bombed some Romanian ports on the Danube without a previous war declaration, the Parliament proclaimed Romania’s independence and decided the country’s entrance in the war. By the beginning of 1878, the Russo-Romanian army was victorious. At the peace Congress of Berlin (June-July 1878) Romania’s independence was recognized, but she had to cede Russia the south of Bessarabia in exchange for a part of Dobruja.

fb46dd86-2d2c-52cf-a5c4-a7d344fc00cc.name: *The Jewish wedding*
fb46dd86-2d2c-52cf-a5c4-a7d344fc00cc.author: Dalila Orfali
fb46dd86-2d2c-52cf-a5c4-a7d344fc00cc.description2: This important painting has a very particular style, and depicts a wedding ceremony in the Jewish community of Tangier, a theme frequently revisited by the artist during his time in Morocco between 1855 and 1870. The Cabinet des Estampes also holds a pen and ink copy. The explosion of colour and the richness of its composition, where the subject is broken down into successive and perfectly coherent sequences, make this one of the most important pieces of Orientalist art. The Cabinet des Estampes at the museum also holds a beautiful pen and ink drawing by the same artist of the last King of Andalucía, Abou 'Abdallah, also known as Boabdil, turning round on his horse to take one last look at his homeland.

fb62d82c-bb0f-5b66-b3bd-e65d7480fe70.name: *Suqs*
fb62d82c-bb0f-5b66-b3bd-e65d7480fe70.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
fb62d82c-bb0f-5b66-b3bd-e65d7480fe70.history:
The *suqs* of the Tunis medina, particularly those specialising by trade, play an important economic role in the city. Some examples are:  
  
• Suq el-Chaouchiya (selling chechias, woollen hats). Founded by the community of Muslims who had been expelled from Spain in the 17th century.  
• Suq Ettrouk (Turkish *suq*)  
• Suq el-Attarine (selling perfume).  
• Suq el-Nahas (selling brass and copper).  
• Suq el-Bey, founded by Hammouda Pacha (1781–1813)  
  
Located near the Zaytuna Mosque, these are the best *suqs* in the Tunis medina. The chechia industry particularly was at its peak here in the 19th century. Today, despite the undeniable decrease in demand, chechia production has survived by adapting to a new clientele, and has become the most popular artisanal Tunisian product with tourists.
fb62d82c-bb0f-5b66-b3bd-e65d7480fe70.description2: The *suqs* have preserved their beautiful architecture to this day, with different columns, pointed arches, and dark, cool rooms lit by the natural light streaming in through the holes in the whitewashed, vaulted ceilings. Located by the great Zaytuna Mosque, these *suqs* are always busy and full of life. Each *suq* is composed of a large central street, with a number of small shops and workshops opening up onto neighbouring narrower alleys, which are covered with vaulted ceilings, made with bricks arranged in different ways to form endless geometric patterns. The woodwork on the shops and their hobnailed doors, painted in a thousand colours and decorated with calligraphic designs, add to the *suq*'s spectacular appearance.

fb86b66e-ef8d-577e-9f18-2861adbb111f.name: *The Storming of a large Storehouse near Rus al-Khyma where Capt Dancey of H. M. 65th Regt was killed. Nov. 13th 1809*
fb86b66e-ef8d-577e-9f18-2861adbb111f.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
fb86b66e-ef8d-577e-9f18-2861adbb111f.dimensions: 505 mm x 602 mm (framed); image: 215 mm x 358 mm
fb86b66e-ef8d-577e-9f18-2861adbb111f.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
fb86b66e-ef8d-577e-9f18-2861adbb111f.artist: R. Temple, HM 65th Regiment, Sixteen views; I. Clark, Sculpt.; William Haines, Publisher
fb86b66e-ef8d-577e-9f18-2861adbb111f.description2: This dramatic scene was recorded by a British soldier participating in the siege and destruction of Ras al-Khaimah, the main stronghold of the Qawasim empire in the lower Gulf. It shows a British contingent, armed with musket guns attacking a large, fortress-like building, surrounded by small dwellings, traditionally built of palm fronds and known as areesh. A soldier in the foreground is taking aim at a local fighter on the roof of the building, while he in turn is defending himself by launching a sharpened log in the attacker's direction. The actual subject of the image, however, is the striken soldier with a headwound, Captain M.M. Dansey, hit by a spear according to eye witnesses and attended to by his comrades in the centre. Nevertheless, after the attacks, the British prided themselves in their 'trifling losses' while estimating that 'from seventy to eighty' of the Qawasim Arabs were killed, and 'many must have fallen in the previous bombardment'.

fb87a426-40c2-5d5c-a3d0-e7ba69ca00e7.name: *The railway*
fb87a426-40c2-5d5c-a3d0-e7ba69ca00e7.second_name: Part of the rail transport system
fb87a426-40c2-5d5c-a3d0-e7ba69ca00e7.description2: Epinal prints take their name from the eponymous town in the Vosges region of France. These stencil-coloured lithographies with simple designs became very popular during the 19th century, thanks to their modest price and popular themes. This particular print is aimed at explaining the new railway system to rural communities, by illustrating the different jobs related to this mode of transport (station master, porter), and the types of people interested in faster transportation (soldiers, tourists, merchants). The different classes (from first to third) and their varying levels of comfort are also shown. This helped dispel and ridicule the fear transport had evoked.

fbe38383-2f88-5cc9-89b2-35902a5954d3.name: Celebrations for the 50 years of the Female Workers Friendly Society of Pavia (Italy), and inauguration of a new standard
fbe38383-2f88-5cc9-89b2-35902a5954d3.author: Angela Bellardi
fbe38383-2f88-5cc9-89b2-35902a5954d3.archival: ASCr, Società di mutuo soccorso femminile di Cremona
fbe38383-2f88-5cc9-89b2-35902a5954d3.third_name: *Festa cinquantenaria della Società operaia femminile di M. S. Inaugurazione del vessillo sociale. Madrina S.E. Donna Elena Cairoli. Padrino Ill. Sig. Comm Franchi-Maggi*
fbe38383-2f88-5cc9-89b2-35902a5954d3.description2: During the second half of the 19th century, “friendly societies” flourished in Italy (especially in Central and Northern Italy). They predated trade unionism and were an important element of Italian social life. From this picture we can infer that the Female Workers Friendly Society of Pavia had been created in 1854.

fbf36d0e-1c98-5536-895f-1b9eff88b55c.name: *The Place du Gouvernement in Algiers*
fbf36d0e-1c98-5536-895f-1b9eff88b55c.author: Dalila Orfali
fbf36d0e-1c98-5536-895f-1b9eff88b55c.description2: Albert Marquet spent 1904 and 1907 in the company of Fauve, and in 1913 he lived in Tangier with Matisse and Camoin. Seven years later in 1920 he visited Algiers for the first time, and went on to spent a few months there every year henceforth. He also lived in Algiers for the duration of the Second World War. Marquet was friendly with most of the artists from the Algerian school, and exhibited his paintings in galleries in the centre of town. Many of his paintings were on the theme of Algiers' harbour. In 1939, his friends from the Salle Bordes organised his first solo exhibition. His style, which was characterised by the luminosity and clarity he saw in North Africa, was an important early influence on the Algerian painter Mohamed Temam.

fbf3f354-9bf0-5444-bf1c-c67f39eba7dc.name: Saint Louis Capuchin Church
fbf3f354-9bf0-5444-bf1c-c67f39eba7dc.description: Saint Louis Capuchin Cathedral is a Latin Catholic cathedral located in downtown Beirut, north of the Grand Serail. The church was built in 1864 by capuchin missionaries and is named after King Louis IX of France. It is recognisable by its sandstone facades, rose-coloured wooden windows, and the new towering bell tower.
fbf3f354-9bf0-5444-bf1c-c67f39eba7dc.author: Julien El Khoury, Jeff El-Msanne
fbf3f354-9bf0-5444-bf1c-c67f39eba7dc.history: When the capuchin missionaries first arrived in Lebanon in 1628 they worshipped at the old Saint George Church (where today's Maronite cathedral stands) in downtown Beirut. In 1732, they built the first church of their own near today's Riadh al-Solh square, dedicated to King Louis IX of France. In 1868 they relocated to Bab Idris and inaugurated the current cathedral. This cathedral was used for official celebrations during the French Mandate period. The church was raided in December 1975 and was a site of fierce fighting during the Lebanese civil war, during which time it was severely damaged by fire. The cathedral was the first landmark to be rebuilt in Downtown Beirut following the war, and was reopened in 2002.
fbf3f354-9bf0-5444-bf1c-c67f39eba7dc.keywords: Church; Crusader; Religion; Catholic; Mass; Beirut

fbf96292-13dd-5f75-85ae-0dae3b1fb7f8.name: Madrasa Slimaniya
fbf96292-13dd-5f75-85ae-0dae3b1fb7f8.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
fbf96292-13dd-5f75-85ae-0dae3b1fb7f8.history: The *madarasa* has many functions, combining prayer with education and providing accommodation for students who have come to the capital to pursue their studies. The role of the *madrasa* in the medina was important not only for spreading knowledge, but also for enabling social mobility by providing education free of charge. The Husainid princes built a great number of madrasas in the city.
fbf96292-13dd-5f75-85ae-0dae3b1fb7f8.description2: Located in the medina on the eponymous street, the Madrasa al-Slimaniya was built by 'Ali Pacha Bey in memory of his son, Sliman. Architecturally, it is can be distinguished by its great elevated porch resting on columns which are topped by Turkish capitals, crowning a green-tiled cornice. The square-shaped oratory is covered in barrel vaults and the walls are decorated with ceramic tiles and panels. The beautiful carved stucco, as well as the elegant dome and the beauty of the *mihrab*, make the Slimanya oratory one of the most magnificent *madrasas* in Tunisia.

fc0202a4-85ca-5193-af7d-ee6857a9426b.name: Arabi, Sayed Ahmed Pasha (1841–1911), Colonel Ali Fahmi Bey, Colonel Abdellal Hilmi Bey
fc0202a4-85ca-5193-af7d-ee6857a9426b.description2: Portrait of minister Arabi (Urabi) together with two officers. In 1882, the war minister took power in Egypt and demanded an end to the financial control imposed by the UK and France. This led to an intervention by the British Navy under Admiral Seymour, who defeated the Egyptian army.

fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.name: Portrait of the Marquess of Cerralbo in a Turkish Garment
fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.description: The Marquis of Cerralbo and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This vignetted bust shot albumen portrait of Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, marquise of Cerralbo, shows the playful and aesthetic use of typical Turkish costume in the Abdullah Frères studio, perfect to satisfy the European desire of exoticism.
fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes
fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.third_name: Retrato de la marquesa de Cerralbo a la turca

fc5492b4-b79e-5ab6-acf3-8e4d44f66cbc.name: The villa of Paul Draneht in Oggebbio (Verbania, Italy)
fc5492b4-b79e-5ab6-acf3-8e4d44f66cbc.author: Massimiliano Cremona, Ignazio Galella
fc5492b4-b79e-5ab6-acf3-8e4d44f66cbc.archival: Intra: Tipografia Intrese, no date (but postal stamp of 1906)
fc5492b4-b79e-5ab6-acf3-8e4d44f66cbc.description2:
In 1872, Paul Draneht Bey bought a Villa on the Lago Maggiore (Italy), which he remodelled, mixing oriental and European architectural styles. From this postcard, one can see a tower with an Arabic flavour.  
In the interior, there was an “Egyptian hall”, modelled according to the style of an ancient Upper-Egypt temple. The furniture was made by one of the shops in Paris that was making the scenes for the opera *Aida*.

fc6ac8e2-2fed-5243-b1e6-1e00ea0b5928.name: Hôpital Charles Nicolle
fc6ac8e2-2fed-5243-b1e6-1e00ea0b5928.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
fc6ac8e2-2fed-5243-b1e6-1e00ea0b5928.history: The first great hospital to be built following the establishment of the protectorate, the Hôpital Charles Nicolle initially accepted only French patients. Having been established initially by a beylical decree on 9 June 1897, it was renamed after the doctor Charles Nicolle, the director of l'Institut Pasteur in Tunis from 1903 to 1936 and 1928 Nobel Prize for Physiology winner, in 1944. The Hôpital Charles Nicolle became known for its pioneering work and specialism in virologic diagnosis, congenital illnesses and paediatric nephrology.
fc6ac8e2-2fed-5243-b1e6-1e00ea0b5928.keywords: Charles Nicolle; Institut Pasteur; Nobel prize
fc6ac8e2-2fed-5243-b1e6-1e00ea0b5928.description2: This hospital was built over 12 hectares, at the foot of the Rabta Hill just outside the ramparts of the city. It was designed by the architect Resplandy, with the help of Dr Bastide. The hospital initially provided two different kinds of general medicine services and surgery, and had 190 beds. Two more buildings were added during the 20th century. Today, the Hôpital Charles Nicolle is a renowned university hospital.

fc95a324-d1b6-5cb0-852e-73608ea38c07.name: *Marco Polo in front of the Khan of Tartars*
fc95a324-d1b6-5cb0-852e-73608ea38c07.author: Marina Minozzi
fc95a324-d1b6-5cb0-852e-73608ea38c07.keywords: Orientalism; painting; Orientalist paintings; artistic exchange; travel; imaginary trips; reinvention; historical events in painting; history painting; neo-Gothic; architectural trends in painting; exoticism; Italian painters; travel
fc95a324-d1b6-5cb0-852e-73608ea38c07.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
fc95a324-d1b6-5cb0-852e-73608ea38c07.description2:
Tranquillo Cremona studied at the Academy of Fine Arts in Venice and then at Brera Academy in Milan. He is considered the “grand bohémien of Italian painting”. This painting was the artist’s first public success. He was fascinated by history paintings and Hayez’s manner as shown in his placement of Marco Polo in front of the Khan of Tartars.  
The artist’s hope to join the Italian embassy – which never happened – was the reason for his interest in the oriental theme. In the ideal recreation, oriental ideas, which were internationally shared, are linked to neo-gothic themes which were fashionable in Italy from the beginning of the 19th century.
fc95a324-d1b6-5cb0-852e-73608ea38c07.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

fcc8f922-ec2a-5d70-8123-eab8d9f5b00c.name: Photo showing the Institute of Medicine
fcc8f922-ec2a-5d70-8123-eab8d9f5b00c.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
fcc8f922-ec2a-5d70-8123-eab8d9f5b00c.keywords: Faculty; Medicine; Pharmacy; USJ; SJU; University; Education
fcc8f922-ec2a-5d70-8123-eab8d9f5b00c.description2: The Medical school at the Université Saint Joseph (USJ) was established by the French state in 1883. The French state provided funding, a curriculum, and professors. Later that same year, following an agreement between the Jesuits and the French government, the Institute of Medicine opened on the university's campus. This was later followed by the opening of many other institutes, such as the faculties of law, economics and management, and literature. On 6 October 1888, the French government recognized the institute as part of a Faculty of Medicine. In 1889, when the school of pharmacy was founded, it was renamed as the Faculty of Medicine and Pharmacy.

fcdce33b-73b5-5f44-b815-567a60b30ab7.name: The Welcome to the Italian Delegation in Morocco
fcdce33b-73b5-5f44-b815-567a60b30ab7.author: Marina Minozzi
fcdce33b-73b5-5f44-b815-567a60b30ab7.keywords: Orientalism; reinvention; historical events in paintings; exoticism; diplomatic mission; Morocco; Mulay al-Hasan; travel; travelling artist; Italian travellers; Italian painters; Edmondo de Amicis; Marocco; travel book
fcdce33b-73b5-5f44-b815-567a60b30ab7.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
fcdce33b-73b5-5f44-b815-567a60b30ab7.description2: Stefano Ussi lived between Florence and Rome and studied at the Academy of Fine Arts of Florence before enrolling as a volunteer in the first Italian War of Independence, during which he was taken prisoner by the Austrian troops. In 1875 he, along with the painter Biseo and the writer De Amicis, followed a diplomatic delegation to Morocco. The painting represents the solemn meeting in Fez between the Alauita sovereign and the Italian delegation from the Consular Office in Tangier. The bright colours and the treatment of the young Sultan appealed to Italians viewers. This episode was masterly described by the writer De Amicis in his book “Marocco” published in 1876.
fcdce33b-73b5-5f44-b815-567a60b30ab7.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

fcea3c25-ab06-5b64-9498-f2354cb75232.name: Ortaköy Mosque
fcea3c25-ab06-5b64-9498-f2354cb75232.description2: The change of perception towards the role of the sultan brought about the construction of the Imperial kiosk '*hünkar kasrı*' in front of the mosques built by sultans.

fcf42d5a-d05c-5ebc-88f3-195d584999e1.name: Vase with curved handles
fcf42d5a-d05c-5ebc-88f3-195d584999e1.holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
fcf42d5a-d05c-5ebc-88f3-195d584999e1.author: Marina Minozzi
fcf42d5a-d05c-5ebc-88f3-195d584999e1.keywords: Applied arts; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; model; reproduction; motifs; collector; Spain; Islamic art; Islamic influence; Romanticism; Neo-Mudéjar style; Alhambra vase; production of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode
fcf42d5a-d05c-5ebc-88f3-195d584999e1.description2: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans. The idea was part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Spanish and Arabian motifs became fashionable in the mid-19th century. The Spanish medieval pottery showed a very strong representation of Romantic Orientalism and inspired a beautiful production of "winged vases"(18th to 19th century). The majolica vase with curved handles is painted in blue and red-brown metallic lustre over a white background. It has a long neck, imitating the Hispanic-Moorish tradition, and its decoration shows a stylised floral motif. It can be dated around mid-19th century for its form and decoration technique.

fcf825c0-6979-528e-9ead-d92db4b19652.name: Vase
fcf825c0-6979-528e-9ead-d92db4b19652.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities
fcf825c0-6979-528e-9ead-d92db4b19652.author: Huda Kilani
fcf825c0-6979-528e-9ead-d92db4b19652.keywords: Copper tin; coated; enamelled; birds; floral decoration; Arabic script
fcf825c0-6979-528e-9ead-d92db4b19652.materials: Copper, tin niello; casting, carving and niello
fcf825c0-6979-528e-9ead-d92db4b19652.description2: A copper tin-coated enamelled vase decorated with birds, floral and Arabic script on a dark blue coloured base with orange, red and green. The Jordanian economy relied on trade and crafts. New waves of people began to settle in Jordan for the purpose of trade and crafts. This object reflects the diverse population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It also demonstrates personal attire, fashion, local costumes and rites.

fd18c679-e2d9-58bf-b89d-424355f03bbd.name: Dar Bach-Hamba
fd18c679-e2d9-58bf-b89d-424355f03bbd.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
fd18c679-e2d9-58bf-b89d-424355f03bbd.history: The Bach Hamba family, a noble military family of Turkish origins, gave their name to their home which stood here until 1923. Dar Bach Hamba is therefore a reminder of Tunisia in the first decades of the 20th century. It became the home of the Bach Hamba brothers, Mohamed and 'Ali, who had been co-founders of a part of the Young Tunisians (al-Harakat al-Shabab al-Tunisi) and of the first Tunisian French-language newspaper, *Le Tunisien*. After having served as the headquarters of the Sœurs Franciscaines du Christ Roi, Dar Bach Hamba became, in the year 2000, the seat of a Mediterranean cultural centre - the Fondazione Orestiadi - whose headquarters are in Sicily. The current building also houses a museum with an impressive collection of ceramics, textiles and clothes, which are all evidence for the links between the various Mediterranean cultures.
fd18c679-e2d9-58bf-b89d-424355f03bbd.keywords: Architecture; art; painting; stucco; mosaic; marble; ceramics
fd18c679-e2d9-58bf-b89d-424355f03bbd.description2: Behind a beautiful arched door, marking the entrance to Dar Bach Hamba, lies a vestibule leading to a central patio. Today's *dar* has kept only its huge proportions, ground floor and first floor galleries and symmetrical distribution of doors and windows on the surrounding apartments. The paving, door and window frames, neo-classical columns, and central fountain in the great hall are all made from marble imported from Carrara. The wooden ceilings in the bedrooms are painted in an Italian style. A smaller courtyard on the first floor is covered by a glass roof. The bedrooms generally open out onto balconies, with magnificent wooden coffered ceilings decorated with a rich floral pattern.

fd211c5e-6b0a-584a-8a00-0307908a3402.name: Request for financial help to the Minister of the Interior by Filippo Codispoti, a former Italian migrant to Cairo, who had to flee Egypt with his family in 1882
fd211c5e-6b0a-584a-8a00-0307908a3402.author: Fortunata Chindemi, Maria Fortunata Minasi
fd211c5e-6b0a-584a-8a00-0307908a3402.archival: ASRC, Prefettura di Gabinetto, inv.34 b.212 fasc.8118
fd211c5e-6b0a-584a-8a00-0307908a3402.description2:
In this letter Filippo Codispoti explained to the Italian Minister of Interior that he was born in Reggio Calabria (a town in Southern Italy) and was 17 years old before he migrated to Egypt. After years of hard work he had been able to reach a comfortable position and was running a wine and liquor shop, while his son was working as a shoemaker, and his daily pay was five and a half lire.  
He further explained that the civil war in Egypt had forced him to flee the country together with his wife and three children, leaving all his belongings in Egypt. He was now penniless and reduced to utter misery, and asked the government for financial help.  
According to governmental statistics, in 1882 there were 18,665 Italians in Egypt. The number of foreigners in Egypt totalled 90,886.
fd211c5e-6b0a-584a-8a00-0307908a3402.holding_institution_org: Archivio di Stato di Reggio Calabria

fd4f4f6c-55c9-53ba-b261-f3fda9387dc4.description2: Universal Exhibition of Paris, 1878. The Chapel of the Mihrab is a faithful reconstruction of the Mihrab in the beautiful mosque built in Cordoba by the Amir Abd al Rahman I above the previous Christian church. The decoration was created by Giuseppe Botana, who specialised in mother-of-pearl works, and by Zuloaga's, a mosaics' maker.

fd62bb2a-82f4-581c-9414-fac77a74a469.name: Coffee pot
fd62bb2a-82f4-581c-9414-fac77a74a469.keywords: Arts and Crafts; Daily utilitarian ware; Portugal; Vista Alegre; Factory
fd62bb2a-82f4-581c-9414-fac77a74a469.description2: This coffee pot is part of a set ordered by the King Fernando of Saxe Coburg, husband of queen Maria II. The lid bears the king’s monogram “F”, positioned underneath the crown. This set was painted by Gustave Fortier, master of panting in the Factory between 1852 and 1857 and again between 1861 and 1869. He introduces a lyrical and romantic style, manifest in the painting of flowers, in the introduction of delicate patterns and pale shades, tendencies which will define the factory’s decoration during his stay.

fd93bf8a-d085-595a-a14f-c616a5d43a58.name: Gülabdan (rose water bottle)
fd93bf8a-d085-595a-a14f-c616a5d43a58.description2: It is known that there were workshops producing glass vessels around Beykoz in Istanbul in the 19th century. The first glass workshop was founded by Mevlevi Dervish Mehmed Dede during the reign of Selim III (1789-1807). There were European glass craftsmen working in those workshops as well. Cups, bottles, jugs etc. made of colourful, colourless and opal glass were among Beykoz' productions. This Beykoz-produced *gülabdan* (a small flask for sprinkling rose water) is made of green glass, in the shape of an ewer. There are cut floral decoration on the body. There are yellow, brown, blue, green and pink flower motifs.

fdae7b92-4bc6-5157-9b5e-a4cfe7c51307.name: *The Ambulance*
fdae7b92-4bc6-5157-9b5e-a4cfe7c51307.description2: Sava Henţia was a Romanian painter who studied in Rome and Paris. During the Romanian Independence War (the Russian-Ottoman war of 1877–1878), he was one of the four Romanian painters who accompanied the Romanian army on the front with the purpose of depicting scenes from the war. However, he did not only dedicate himself to painting, but also worked as a volunteer for the Romanian Ambulance Service. In the foreground of the painting The Ambulance, some Romanian doctors are attending Ottoman soldiers, while in the background can be seen medical tents of the Red Cross.

fdf4838a-7764-5f27-afc8-32377c84dfbc.name: *The interior of Mustapha Pacha's palace*
fdf4838a-7764-5f27-afc8-32377c84dfbc.author: Dalila Orfali
fdf4838a-7764-5f27-afc8-32377c84dfbc.description2: In the early 19th century this palace, located in the Algiers kasbah, housed the collections of the first library museum. It was also the home of one of the regency's most famous deys, Mustapha Pacha, who ordered many of the old town's monuments to be built during his reign. One example of these is the great palace of Menzel el-Mahalla in east Algiers, which was later partly destroyed, with the rest being used as a hospital for the French expeditionary corps. The dey was assassinated in 1805.

fe6b786f-510f-5112-b531-2e5e437342ab.name: The Empress visits the Orient
fe6b786f-510f-5112-b531-2e5e437342ab.keywords: Constantinople; Turkey; religions buildings; Hagia Sophia; Empress Eugénie
fe6b786f-510f-5112-b531-2e5e437342ab.second_name: *Her Majesty visits the Hagia Sofia in Constantinople*
fe6b786f-510f-5112-b531-2e5e437342ab.description2: The Empress Eugénie (Napoléon III's wife) stopped off in Istanbul on her way to Suez, where she was representing France at the inauguration of the Suez Canal. This visit marked the beginning of improving relations between France and Turkey. Eugénie was received with great respect and visited all the great monuments of the city. A fervent Catholic, she could not resist stopping off at the Hagia Sophia mosque, which had once been an Orthodox cathedral.

fe6cec92-b619-55f4-a18b-3a0f8fd470af.name: Palais-Musée du Bardo
fe6cec92-b619-55f4-a18b-3a0f8fd470af.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
fe6cec92-b619-55f4-a18b-3a0f8fd470af.history: The museum occupies just a part of the entire Palais du Bardo, a collection of buildings constructed from the early 15th century onwards. It was built in the style of Andalusian princely residences, but also shows traces of North African Tunisian and Italian architectural influences dating to the Husainid period when it underwent a series of modifications. The museum was opened and received its first archaeological collections on 7 May 1888 by the Bey of Tunisia and the French Resident-General. It remains, to this day, one of the most important archaeological museums in the world, and is particularly renowned for its excellent collection of Roman mosaics.
fe6cec92-b619-55f4-a18b-3a0f8fd470af.keywords: Architecture; art; painting; stucco; mosaic; marble; ceramics
fe6cec92-b619-55f4-a18b-3a0f8fd470af.description2: The Musée du Bardo receives more than 500,000 visitors each year. It is divided into three floors, each holding thousands of exceptionally valuable items, all of which tell the story of a country at the crossroads of multiple civilisations. Visitors can admire mosaics on the floors and walls, the statues, funerary steles, ceramics, jewellery, works of art and bronze and marble sculptures, ranging from the prehistoric era to Punic, Roman and Byzantine times.

fe6fa089-3083-5936-9e90-9d863dea6475.name: Osman Hamdi Bey (During the excavation of Mount Nemrut)
fe6fa089-3083-5936-9e90-9d863dea6475.archival: *Le tumulus de Nemroud-Dagh. Voyage, description, inscriptions avec plans et photographies*, İstanbul, F. Loeffler, 1883.
fe6fa089-3083-5936-9e90-9d863dea6475.keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters,; archaeological excavations
fe6fa089-3083-5936-9e90-9d863dea6475.description2: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen were exposed to Western ideas through education and travel. The museum was founded by decree in 1891 as the Imperial Museum. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi. Hamdi began construction of the main building in 1881, and it achieved its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. It is one of the prominent structures built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul. Osman Hamdi, during his tenure as museum director, launched the first Turkish scientific excavations. He carried out archaeological excavations at Mount Nemrut, Laguna and Sidon.

fe7f9cb8-4e79-503c-a1e9-e92215a81644.name: Saraya Ba'abda: the headquarters of *al-mutasarrifin*
fe7f9cb8-4e79-503c-a1e9-e92215a81644.author: Jeff El-Msanne
fe7f9cb8-4e79-503c-a1e9-e92215a81644.history: This building, completed in 1887, stands on a hill overlooking the town entrance, an example of a typical Ottoman architecture mixed with some traditional Lebanese elements. The building has four towers on each of its corners. Works began under the reign of Prince Melhem Shihabi, the son of Haydar Shihabi.
fe7f9cb8-4e79-503c-a1e9-e92215a81644.description2: This Saraya bore witness to some of the most important periods in the history of modern Lebanon. Originally a special saray for the Prince Melhem Shihabi, it later became a governmental saray following the establishment of the Ottoman governate, of *al-mutasarrifyya* of Mount Lebanon after the civil war of 1860. The palace was specifically used as the headquarters for the Mount Lebanon governate and governors, or *mutasarrifin*.

fe898d65-6a28-56fc-93fb-7e1ee70f830f.name: *A landscape of Bazaar from Istanbul*
fe898d65-6a28-56fc-93fb-7e1ee70f830f.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
fe898d65-6a28-56fc-93fb-7e1ee70f830f.description2: At the beginning of the 19th century, romantic painters who appreciated eastern mysticism brought newly discovered eastern landscapes with their paintings which contained fiery colours and interesting landscapes. One of those painters coming to Istanbul from Malta and affected by eastern mysticism was Amadeo Preziosi. He usually painted scenes from daily life, such as shops between streets, coffeehouses, baths, peddlers passing the street, a woman filling water from a fountain and figures from different ethnic groups. Like many of his contemporaries, Preziosi had been lured to the exotic city of Istanbul. He also tried to reflect the cultural diversity of the city in his paintings. Especially in his watercolour paintings he loved expressing the blue water of the Bosporus with its caïques, pavilions, palaces, boats, mansions, residences, bazaars and cemeteries.

ff0f0b5a-89b7-5bab-b342-1924a2ccdcb4.name: Rug
ff0f0b5a-89b7-5bab-b342-1924a2ccdcb4.author: Houria Cherid
ff0f0b5a-89b7-5bab-b342-1924a2ccdcb4.description2: This knotted-pile carpet is an example of a typical Anatolian rug, decorated with a *mihrab*, surrounded by three different borders. It features floral and geometric patterns in red, yellow, green and blue.

ff1cc08e-5e46-58f1-ba2a-f93481917b38.name: Waistcoat (*Yelek*)
ff1cc08e-5e46-58f1-ba2a-f93481917b38.description: This beautiful feminine traditional *yelek* (waistcoat) is a part of a women’s typical dress. The red velvet and the light vegetal pattern embroidery handwork enhance the elegance of the piece. The Marquise of Cerralbo or her daughter would be the probable admirers and purchasers.
ff1cc08e-5e46-58f1-ba2a-f93481917b38.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes

ff28cb9b-b4cd-5d7f-8616-1983d1ba7e9b.name: *The last day of the Commune, Paris 1871*
ff28cb9b-b4cd-5d7f-8616-1983d1ba7e9b.description2: The Parisians, who had spent many long months under siege, did not accept the armistice signed with Prussia in 1871. They rose up in revolt in March, as the government was hiding in Versailles. The "Commune" of Paris, which organised the city socially and politically, was thus created. Versailles fought the "communards" for two months. After a "bloody week" and the loss of thousands of lives and many deportations, the government finally regained control of the city, which continued until a general amnesty was reached in 1880. From this point onwards, the period - which had become a taboo - gradually began to be discussed. This poster from 1883 is advertising a play which enacted Paris' takeover by the Versaillais.

ff2ee02d-c01b-55f1-8514-320080faaf5a.name: Nebamun tomb paintings
ff2ee02d-c01b-55f1-8514-320080faaf5a.keywords: archaeology; Egyptomania; exploration; collection; collecting; wall painting; museums; travel; traveller
ff2ee02d-c01b-55f1-8514-320080faaf5a.description2: Salt’s excavator, Yanni d’Athanasi, discovered and removed the exquisite wall paintings from the 18th Dynasty tomb of Nebamun. Here Nebamun counts the flocks of geese being brought before him.

ff3e8256-d8ee-5d47-b909-e92dca381df5.name: Ortaköy Mosque
ff3e8256-d8ee-5d47-b909-e92dca381df5.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
ff3e8256-d8ee-5d47-b909-e92dca381df5.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Mosques; Ancient Istanbul
ff3e8256-d8ee-5d47-b909-e92dca381df5.description2: The Ortaköy Mosque was ordered by the Ottoman sultan Abdülmecid and built between 1854 and 1856. Its architects were father and son Garabet Amira Balyan and Nigoğayos Balyan (who also designed the nearby Dolmabahçe Palace and the Dolmabahçe Mosque), who designed it in the Neo-Baroque style.

ff6c9c68-5a72-5102-ad19-99345287b4be.name: Letter from Marshall Forteguerri, commander general of the navy of the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies, confirming the purchase of Tunisian slaves in Naples

ff78af46-329b-5d7b-810a-cacb6d484374.name: Umm al-Rasas
ff78af46-329b-5d7b-810a-cacb6d484374.dates: Roman-Present; identified in 1896 by J. Germer-Durand
ff78af46-329b-5d7b-810a-cacb6d484374.author: Mohammad Najjar
ff78af46-329b-5d7b-810a-cacb6d484374.history: The World Heritage Site of Umm al-Rasas (Kastron Mefa'a, Kastrom Mefa'a) is an archaeological site in Jordan which contains ruins from the Roman, Byzantine, and early Muslim periods. The most important monument in the site was the mosaic floor of the Church of St Stephen. This biggest mosaic floor in Jordan – which was built in 785 AD – depicts the most important cities in Jordan, Palestine and Egypt. The fact that the mosaic floor was constructed during the Abbasid period reflects the spirit of tolerance and co-existence of the Muslim and Christian communities during that period. Umm al-Rasas was visited by H.B. Tristram in 1872 and subsequently identified in 1896 by J. Germer-Durand with the Biblical and Late Antiquity city of Mephaath.
ff78af46-329b-5d7b-810a-cacb6d484374.keywords: World Heritage Site; frontier station; Archaeological investigations; churches; mosaic panels; Tristram
ff78af46-329b-5d7b-810a-cacb6d484374.description2: The town of Umm al-Rasas was enclosed in an almost square (app.160x155 meters) enclosure surrounded by fortification walls and 24 towers. The main gateway was from the east. Two small gates were positioned at the north and the south sides. These were blocked later. Archaeological investigations at the site were concentrated on the four churches identified inside the fortification walls, including the church of the Rivers and the church of the Palm tree. These were named after the main component of the mosaic panels on the floors. At least 11 other churches were identified outside the enclosure to the north. The most prominent of them are the church of St. Stephen with its famous mosaic panels of 15 major towns of Jordan and Palestine of the time.

ffecc84b-856d-5f87-97de-682a1d90e53d.name: *View of Istanbul: the Valide Sultan Mosque and the port*
ffecc84b-856d-5f87-97de-682a1d90e53d.second_name: Taken from the collection *Photographies Positives* by Pascal Sébah
ffecc84b-856d-5f87-97de-682a1d90e53d.description2: Pascal Sébah (1823–1886) was a French photographer working in the Ottoman capital Constantinople, where he developed a successful trade selling photographs to European tourists and lovers of Orientalism. The great changes Constantinople underwent towards the end of the 19th century are evident in this image. The Valide Sutlan Mosque dominates the Eminönü port, which had become very prosperous during the Ottoman era thanks to active trading with the West. The construction of the Galata bridge, the Orient Express railway line, and the arrival of steam-boats also contributed to its development.
